## Exec/Kernel findings reconciled into the index (2026-11-02)

**EK10163 — m68kemu formatting thunks pass a null argument stream after allocation failure:** Locale `FormatString`, Utility `VSNPrintf`, DOS `VPrintf`, and DOS `VFPrintf` can pass the failed converter allocation to a formatter that reads its argument stream. Trigger requires an argument-bearing format and temporary allocation failure; literal-only formats are excluded. See [EK10163](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10163) and the [format-stream caller census](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8572). Source-only.

**[EK10609](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10609) - m68kemu `PropChunks()`, `StopChunks()`, and `CollectionChunks()` read guest big-endian FourCC pairs as native little-endian `LONG`s.** Requested IFF chunks can be missed or registered with reversed IDs. Optional emulator target; no maintained emulated caller was found. See the [chunk-array trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#iffparse-chunk-array-endian-trace-ek10609). Source-only.

**EK10607 — HDToolBox can divide by zero when a block device reports zero partition geometry:** `OpenRootPartition()` accepts successful zero heads/sectors, which the selected HDToolBox add-partition caller uses as a zero divisor. Conditional on a non-CD device returning that geometry; no checked-in device response was established. The HDToolBox target is explicit-build only. See [EK10607](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10607) and the [geometry-validation caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#partition-root-zero-geometry-hdtoolbox-ek10607). Source-only; no operation or build was run.

**[EK8800](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8800-valid-signal-bit-31-is-shifted-through-signed-integer-expressions) — Exec and selected callers form masks for valid signal bit 31 with signed shifts.** With 32-bit `int`, `1 << 31` is undefined under the configured C standards through C17; selected source occurrences include ATA, NVMe, SCSI and AHCI timer waits, input and console tasks, the optional printer, NTFS, and the explicitly buildable `Clip GET WAIT` command; each caller still requires its task to allocate bit 31, and the `1L` callers additionally require 32-bit `long`. Other core triggers include explicit `AllocSignal(31)`, DOS packet replies waited through `internal_WaitPkt()`, and the ASL and selected More window wait loops on 32-bit-`long` targets. SD-card and VirtIO helper copies have no maintained callers. Consequences depend on compiler output. See the [caller and standard recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#exec-signal-bit-31-standard-recheck-ek8800). Source-only; no signal operation or build was run.




**[EK514](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek514) — Android-hosted cold reboot can reuse the freed KernelArgs pointer.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK9193](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9193) — m68k ASL requester allocators return native pointers without guest-handle registration; paired use/free thunks cannot resolve them, so requests fail and native requester state is retained. Optional m68kemu targets; no maintained guest caller was found. See the [lifecycle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5054). Source-only.

**[EK9194](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9194) — m68k Commodities thunks return native CxObj pointers without guest-handle mapping.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK9212](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9212) — m68k TagItem conversion does not marshal valid TAG_MORE chains into native-width arrays.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK866](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek866) — RexxSupport `portcleanup()` replies tracked messages before unlinking them, rewriting each node’s list links while `ForeachNode()` is traversing. Multiple `GETPKT` messages can be skipped and left unreplied during close. Limited to explicit `workbench-libs-rexxsupport`; source-only.**
**[EK864](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek864) — RexxSupport `CLOSEPORT` leaks successfully allocated temporary reply resources when its reply setup fails. The named port remains registered on the error return; explicit `workbench-libs-rexxsupport` only. Source-only.**

**[EK867](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek867) — AUX startup tagging can clear a valid pointer bit on Fast-BPTR targets.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK510](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek510) — Unix host clock failures feed uninitialized values into task CPU-time accounting.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK316](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek316) — QueryTaskTagList can return a timeval with one million microseconds and no seconds carry.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK9878](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9878) — pthread_barrier_wait can retain the barrier lock after cancellation.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK371](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek371) — WaitX loses the year carry when a recurring monthly date crosses December.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK373](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek373) — WaitX reports successful exit when ReadArgs rejects the command line.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK814](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek814) — Sam440 accepts IRQs 128–239 and indexes beyond its UIC enable-state array.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK816](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek816) — Efika last-handler removal can set the wrong main-IRQ disable bit, leaving IRQs 4–19 unmasked without a handler. The follow-on effect requires a pending/asserted source; no ordinary in-tree last-handler removal was established. See the [mask and caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4640). Source-only.

**[EK818](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek818) — Efika interrupt initialization computes a value preserving external IRQ configuration and clearing pending bits, then writes a constant instead. The register mismatch is certain; hardware impact depends on firmware state and controller semantics. See the [initialization trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4642). Source-only.

**[EK817](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek817) — Efika interrupt dispatch omits and misidentifies peripheral status sources, including USB.** Source details and affected configuration are in the linked finding.

**[EK285](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek285) — OpenSBI FDT register lookup can read beyond its fixed ancestor stack for a device node nested at depth 17 or greater.** The affected OpenSBI callers include I²C, UART, PCI host and RTC discovery; the explicitly buildable RISC-V DWMAC target is also affected, but is not included in the default network aggregate. Source details and trigger scope are in the linked finding.

**[EK198](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek198) — OpenSBI advertises RVV without enabling or preserving task vector state.** An RVV task's first vector instruction remains disabled and enters the ordinary illegal-instruction path; if an alternate handler enables it, later switches still do not save/restore the vector state. Trigger requires a V-capable OpenSBI system and an RVV-using task. See the [selected CPU/trap/context ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1797). Source-only.

**[EK10189](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10189) — Efika and Raspberry Pi ARM bootstrap ELF relocation diagnostics index the raw `SHN_XINDEX` sentinel instead of the resolved section-name table index, so an undefined/COMMON-symbol error can read section header 65535 out of bounds.** Source details and conditional target/input scope are in the linked finding.

**[EK10611](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10611) — `NextConductor()` returns private RealTime conductors from the shared list without filtering `CONDUCTF_PRIVATE`, although `FindConductor()` filters them. Candidate is medium-low because public enumeration does not explicitly promise privacy; no maintained direct caller was found. See the [enumeration review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#nextconductor-private-conductor-enumeration-ek10611). Source-only.

**[EK613](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek613) — OpenSBI RISC-V Zicbom helpers use a fixed 64-byte stride; on a CPU with smaller CMO blocks, alternating cache blocks are skipped. Actual DMA-coherency impact remains conditional on a non-coherent client, not established in the selected tree. See the [block-size and caller review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7960). Source-only.

**[EK626](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek626) — `CloseAsync()` discards a failed DOS `Close()` result and returns its prior successful wait/write result. RAM, FAT, PFS3, and CDVDFS provide conditional `ACTION_END` rejection paths; no maintained caller reaction is established. See the [handler-contract trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2418). Source-only.

## Graphics/Desktop findings reconciled into the index (2026-11-02)

**[GD6336](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6336) — The selected m68k Workbench VMM module omits the assembly objects defining `TrapHandler30/40/60`; the unresolved references are expected to block the m68k Workbench aggregate build. The source and active target chain are confirmed; no build/link was run.**

**[GD6068](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6068) — ExecuteStartup leaks DiskObjects for successfully loaded WBStartup icons that are neither tools nor projects.** Conditional on those icon types appearing in the startup scan; source-only.

**[GD6069](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6069) — ExecuteStartup skips MatchEnd after a successful MatchFirst when node allocation, iteration, or Ctrl-C exits the WBStartup scan.** The AChain allocations and locks remain held for the process lifetime. Source-only.

**[GD5330](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5330-vgagfx-cursor-erasure-reads-past-a-smaller-displayable-bitmap) — VGAGfx cursor erasure uses an inclusive box one pixel larger than the drawn cursor; clipping to physical display bounds can let refresh read beyond a smaller bitmap buffer. Conditional on a smaller displayable bitmap and cursor erasure at its edge. Source-only.**

**[GD4631](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4631) — Generic Gfx HIDD `MapColor()` uses a 16-bit index against an `ULONG` palette count, so a 65,536-entry indexed ColorMap makes the scan wrap and loop forever. The ColorMap constructor accepts the count and only logs the >256 condition; in-tree caller reachability is not established. Source-only.**

**[GD14484](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14484) — HIDD ColorMap `SetColors()` can wrap `firstColor + numColors`, skip growing the palette, then write at the unchecked starting index. The method exposes full-width `ULONG` arguments, but the checked-in callers found do not establish this overflow trigger. See the [range trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#colormap-setcolors-overflow-gd14484). Source-only.**

**[GD14485](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14485) — Display `Show()` ignores failures while copying a bitmap ColorMap into the framebuffer or old bitmap. If expanding the destination map fails, colors remain stale while the display transition continues. See the [palette-copy trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#display-show-palette-copy-failure-gd14485). Source-only.**

**[GD14486](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14486) — `SetRGB32()` writes `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB[n]` even when `n >= 256`, beyond the fixed-size HIDD bitmap lookup table; its ColorMap range check does not gate the write. See the [bounds trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setrgb32-pixtab-bounds-gd14486). Source-only.**

**[GD14487](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14487) — Wanderer ignores a failed destination `Close()` and can report a copy as successful. The trigger depends on the destination filesystem returning an `ACTION_END` error; removable FAT media is one conditional path. See the [close-result trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-copy-close-result-gd14487). Source-only.**

**[GD14488](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14488) — `CopyToPAR` treats a successful `DoIO()` as a complete chunk without checking `io_Actual`; with a short USB printer OUT transfer and a clean IN-stream status, it can report a successful print after omitting bytes. See the [caller and stream trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14488-copytopar-reports-success-after-a-short-parallel-device-write). Source-only.**

**[GD14489](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14489) — `Copy` ignores a failed destination `Close()`; in MOVE mode it can then delete the source and report success. A selected removable FAT close path can reject `ACTION_END`. See the [close-result and caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14489-copy-can-delete-a-moved-source-after-destination-close-failure). Source-only.**

**[GD14490](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14490) — `Copy` ignores failed protection/date/comment updates after setting its success result, so requested metadata can be missing while the command reports success. See the [metadata-result trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14490-copy-reports-success-when-requested-metadata-updates-fail). Source-only.**

**[GD14491](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14491) — `Copy NEWER` parses `$VER:` from a fixed 4096-byte buffer without a length bound or guaranteed terminator; a malformed unterminated token can make `skipnonspaces()` read beyond it. See the [version-buffer trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14491-copy-newer-version-parsing-can-scan-beyond-its-fixed-buffer). Source-only.**

**[GD14492](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14492) — `Join` ignores a failed destination `Close()` and can report a successful concatenation despite filesystem finalization failure. See the [close-result trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14492-join-reports-success-when-closing-its-destination-fails). Source-only.**

**[GD14493](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14493) — `Join` ignores a `MatchNext()` error after one or more wildcard matches, so the output can omit files while the command reports success. See the [enumeration-result trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14493-join-ignores-wildcard-enumeration-errors-after-matching-a-file). Source-only.**

**[GD14494](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14494) — `Join` prints “Error while writing” after a source read failure. See the [diagnostic trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14494-join-labels-source-read-errors-as-write-errors). Source-only.**

**[GD14495](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14495) — `DiskChange` leaves its error code at zero when required-argument parsing fails, so `PrintFault()` suppresses the diagnostic. See the [argument-error trace](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14495-diskchange-suppresses-the-missing-device-argument-error). Source-only.**

**[GD14497](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14497-makedir-all-clears-the-error-when-creating-a-path-component-fails) — `MakeDir ALL` can overwrite a failed component-creation `IoErr()` with zero during cleanup, hiding the filesystem failure from callers. See the [path-creation review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#makedir-all-path-creation-and-error-preservation-pass-gd14497). Source-only.**

**[GD14498](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14498-list-leaks-pattern-buffers-when-pattern-parsing-fails) — `List` leaks its allocated `PAT` or `SUB` parse buffer when `ParsePatternNoCase()` rejects malformed syntax. See the [full-body and error-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#list-command-full-body-pattern-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03). Source-only.**

**[GD14499](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14499-list-all-leaks-unvisited-recursion-nodes-after-a-traversal-error) — `List ALL` frees the processed-directory queue after a traversal error but leaves queued sibling nodes and path strings allocated. See the [full-body and error-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#list-command-full-body-pattern-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03). Source-only.**

**[GD5919](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5919) — `MakeVPort()` leaks `HIDD_ViewPortData` when viewport setup fails after VPD allocation; if a planar wrapper was created first, that owned bitmap can also be lost. The selected OpenScreen rollback leaks the VPD on later setup failure; if AmigaVideo allocates its per-viewport state before replacement copper-list allocation fails, that state also leaks because deinitialization is skipped. See the [failure ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L4391) and [backend qualification](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L18946). Source-only; no failure was induced.**

**[GD14460](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14460-amigavideo-setbitmapnull-dereferences-the-detached-bitmap) — AmigaVideo's PlanarBM SetBitMap override dereferences NULL after the superclass accepts a detach.** Conditional on an external HIDD client detaching an AmigaVideo bitmap; no in-tree NULL caller to that subclass was established. See the [caller and superclass trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-setbitmap-null-gd14460). Source-only; no HIDD call was run.

**[GD14470](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14470-wanderer-leaks-copy-window-tree-if-application-setup-fails) — Wanderer creates its copy Window and child objects before Application timer setup, then skips cleanup if Application construction fails before attaching that Window.** Conditional on timer setup resource failure; repeated attempts retain the unattached object tree. See the [caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-copy-display-setup-failure-gd14470). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**[GD3075](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd3075) — Wanderer leaks toolbar and status-bar per-window records because extension cleanup never frees them; toolbar and status-bar records also leak if nested MUI construction fails.** See the [construction-failure and teardown recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3071). Source-only; no allocation failure or window lifecycle was run.

**[GD9463](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9463) — MUI Application disposal dereferences its unset preferences pointer when Configdata construction fails after a valid application base is retained.** This prevents clean constructor rollback under that resource failure. The later duplicate entry GD9906 was reconciled into GD9463. Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.


**[GD9615](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9615) — `BltBitMap()` does not clip negative destination coordinates before generic software, chunky-memory and selected driver paths consume them; packaged Raspberry Pi VCGfx also writes through an unchecked destination pointer, while optional IntelGMA, Radeon and NVIDIA paths left-shift negative destination Y during command packing.** Maintained scroll and optional layer-test callers can supply the negative origin. See the detailed backend and trigger distinctions in the [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9615). Source-only; no blit was run.

**[GD14338](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14338) — TensorDescriptionARM::setStrides replaces the tensor dimension count.** Setting an empty or differently sized stride proxy overwrites the count derived from dimensions while leaving the dimension pointer unchanged; see the linked finding for specification and creation-path details.
**[GD14339](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14339) — Vulkan-Hpp display-property comparison and hashing dereference a null name.** Comparison can pass a null name to `strcmp`, and hashing the default wrapper dereferences the name; see the linked finding.
**[GD14340](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14340) — Android HIDD manifest requires absent `androidgfx_bitmap.c`.** The only matching bitmap implementation is named `androidgfx_bitmapclass.c`, so the Android module target has a missing source prerequisite.
**[GD14341](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14341) — Android mouse HIDD fails to compile with `DEBUG > 1`.** Its two `DB2` log calls access a nonexistent `pHidd_Mouse_ExtEvent.action` member.
**[GD14342](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14342) — Android input can synthesize a phantom key press after overlapping key presses.** Its single `LastKey` slot is cleared by the first key-up, so the next key-up is treated as a key-up-only device quirk.
**[GD14343](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14343) — Softpipe and LLVMpipe double-close dependencies during failed initialization.** Their init cleanup leaves closed bases stored, then the failed-init expunge hook closes them again.
**[GD14344](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14344) — Softpipe and LLVMpipe misinterpret non-BGRA display-target resources.** Their support callbacks accept every format, while presentation always passes BGRA32 (or raw destination) to `WritePixelArray()`.
**[GD14345](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14345) — Vulkan-Hpp platform handle wrappers default to OpaqueFd.** Win32, host-pointer, Metal, RDMA, and Fuchsia import/export and capability-query wrappers can pass or query the POSIX FD type bit when callers omit the type; see the linked finding for exact structures and caller paths.
**[GD14346](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14346) — Vulkan-Hpp create-info equality forms null array endpoints.** Equality on default `DeviceCreateInfo` and `InstanceCreateInfo` objects forms null-plus-zero pointer endpoints before `std::equal()`; see the linked finding for the exact expressions.
**[GD14347](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14347) — Vulkan-Hpp fixed-string equality and hashes disagree.** Four tooling, Vulkan 1.2 properties, and pipeline-executable records compare fixed arrays as C strings but hash every byte, so equal values can hash differently as unordered-container keys. See the finding for exact source and returned-value paths.
**[GD14348](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14348) — Generic truecolor-to-palette conversion can reuse pen indices cached under a prior colormap.** The base bitmap setter leaves its inverse lookup table intact when the colormap pointer changes; selected blit and scale paths temporarily attach different maps. See the finding for exact caller and trigger scope.

**[GD4608](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4608) — `ScalePixelArray()` reaches division by zero in the generic HIDD scaler.** Its zero-initialized `BitScaleArgs` never receives the four scale factors before dispatch, and the generic scaler divides by the zero destination factors. See the [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#scalepixelarray-zero-factor-gd4608). Source-only; no scaling call was run.

**[GD14337](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14337) — Vulkan-Hpp TensorCopyARM can leave a non-null offset with zero dimensions.** The enhanced constructor counts only source offsets, so a non-null destination-offset or extent array can be forwarded with `dimensionCount == 0`; see the linked finding for specification and caller-path details.

**[GD14336](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14336) — GELS clear-path recursion dereferences standalone VSprites as Bobs.** A Bob followed by a standalone VSprite can leave the latter in `ClearPath`; a later clear dereferences its NULL `VSBob`. The mixed-list caller is conditional; see the linked finding.

**[GD10011](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10011) — ActivateLayoutGadget ignores the requested child gadget ID.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10018](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10018) — ReAction Button accepts BUTTON_AutoButton but never creates or draws its glyph.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10019](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10019) — ReAction Button disposes a caller-supplied struct Image as a BOOPSI object.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10030](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10030) — FuelGauge ignores FUELGAUGE_VarArgs, leaving formatted GA_Text placeholders literal.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10031](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10031) — FuelGauge accepts and reports tick settings but never renders tick marks.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10032](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10032) — FuelGauge signed scaling arithmetic overflows for large progress values and ranges, including XAD unsigned file sizes crossing the signed `LONG` boundary.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10034](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10034) — ReAction Scroller SCROLLER_Arrows draws empty frames without arrow behavior.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10039](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10039) — TextField default TEXTFIELD_WordWrap does not wrap long lines and truncates them.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD10091](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10091) — Generic HIDD construction can publish a display with no name after StrDup failure.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD5749](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5749) — CGFX extcol_render passes pixel width as the Native32 image row modulo.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD5905](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5905) — Wanderer IconList leaks a temporary date string on an early return.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD6101](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6101) — CPUInfo dispatches GenuineIntel and GenuineTMx86 results into the Cyrix parser.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD9562](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9562) — BumpRevision copies long names through a fixed 50-byte temporary buffer.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD9674](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9674) — InstallAROS skip-list construction dereferences unchecked allocations.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD9675](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9675) — InstallAROS directory creation copies through an unchecked path allocation.** Source details and scope are in the linked finding.

**OD2298 — HID mouse tablet-range arithmetic can send Intuition an invalid zero denominator:** a reversed-by-one absolute range produces zero exactly; the full signed 32-bit interval overflows the signed calculation and cannot fit the tablet’s 32-bit range field. Scoped to selected USB HID mouse packages when the tablet event reaches Intuition. See [OD2298](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2298) and the [descriptor/range trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-full-width-tablet-range-overflow-od2298). Source-only; no descriptor or input event was used.
**EK798 — Per-core PC frequency queries sample APERF/MPERF on the caller CPU:** `GetCPUInfo()` selects the requested CPU's saved record, but standalone frequency sampling reads counters on the executing CPU; unpinned SysExplorer per-core queries can display another CPU's frequency. Scoped to APERF/MPERF-enabled standalone PC systems when execution and selected CPU differ. See [EK798](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek798) and the [selected-core sampling trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2549). Source-only; no query or MSR access was run.
**OD3522 — PCIPC publishes duplicate PCI device objects for multiple ACPI host bridges:** every registered bridge instance scans bus 0 through the discovered high bus and appends present BDFs to the shared list without deduplication. Scoped to PCIPC/ACPICA setups with multiple host-bridge instances; duplicate enumeration is the direct effect. See [OD3522](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3522) and the [PCIPC multi-bridge scan and publication trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcipc-multi-bridge-full-scan-and-duplicate-device-publication-od3522). Source-only; no firmware or PCI enumeration was run.
**OD3523 — PCIPC can leak ACPI IRQ route nodes when PCI driver registration fails:** route nodes are accumulated before PCI/PCIPC objects are created. PCI-base construction failure strands the local bridge list; per-host PCIPC driver construction failure frees the bridge node without freeing its nested route nodes. Scoped to PC builds with ACPICA and nonempty host-bridge route lists during allocation failure. See [OD3523](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3523) and the [registration failure/ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcipc-acpi-driver-registration-failure-route-ownership-od3523). Source-only; no allocation failure or ACPI enumeration was induced.
**OD3524 — PCIPC can collapse distinct ACPI host bridges to one bus identifier:** its `_BBN` helper reads the ACPI object type word instead of `Integer.Value`; without a `_CRS` bus range, same-HID roots can collide as bus 1 and the later root’s `_PRT` routes are skipped. The resulting device impact depends on firmware interrupt-line setup. See [OD3524](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3524) and the [PCIPC ACPI routing ownership and bus-number recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcipc-acpi-routing-ownership-and-bus-number-recheck-od3524).
**OD3525 — PCIPC dereferences a failed ACPI host-bridge allocation:** after ACPI identifies a host bridge, `ACPIHostBridgeCallbackA()` dereferences its unchecked `AllocVec()` result while initializing the node and hardware-ID string. Scoped to PCIPC/ACPICA host-bridge enumeration under allocation failure. See [OD3525](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3525) and the [PCIPC allocation and IRQ adapter recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#generic-pci-interrupt-adapter-and-pcipc-inheritance-recheck-od11159-type-scope-correction-no-new-finding-or-bodyloc-credit-2026-11-03). Source-only; no allocation failure or ACPI enumeration was induced.
**OD3415 — ACPI device HIDDs retain unused discovery nodes:** fan, battery, AC-adapter, power-meter and thermal drivers keep one staging node per discovered device after successful registration, and also strand nodes on namespace or registration failure. Successful paths pin the module, so these allocations persist for its lifetime. See [OD3415](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3415) and the [five-initializer ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L28209). Source-only; no firmware walk or allocation failure was run.
**GD6223 — Appearance theme preview uses a one-plane scratch bitmap on planar screens:** the offscreen render can encode only pixel indices 0 and 1, then is copied directly into the preview, so multi-pen themes lose their colors. Scoped to Appearance Preferences on classic planar screens with depth greater than one; HIDD friends take a different allocation path. Separate from GD6229's PenMode state mismatch. See [GD6223](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6223) and the [bitmap allocation and draw trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd6223-planar-preview-depth-recheck). Source-only; no GUI or bitmap operation was run.
**GD6229 — `SetRPAttrsA()` applies direct-RGB pen mode to planar RastPorts:** the setter toggles `RPF_NO_PENS` without checking bitmap type, but only writes the direct color into the GC for HIDD bitmaps. Appearance Preferences uses this combination in its theme preview; on a classic planar screen the one-plane friend bitmap stays planar and preview fills can use the default GC color. External planar callers share the API defect. See [GD6229](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6229) and the [Appearance Preview caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd6229-appearance-preview-planar-caller-recheck). Source-only; no drawing operation was run.
**GD5170 — MUI Window sleep saves `MaxWidth` as the minimum and restores the wrong resize bound:** waking an opened, slept MUI window passes the old maximum width as `WindowLimits()` minimum, or leaves the temporary sleep minimum when that maximum exceeds the current width. Application sleep forwards this to all registered windows. See [GD5170](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5170) and the [sleep/wake and Intuition limit trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-window-sleep-wake-minimum-width-gd5170). Source-only; no window operation was run.
**GD4817 — Generic JAM2 alpha-template blending misses the foreground value at full alpha:** the `/256` channel interpolation leaves each differing channel one value toward the background when alpha is 255 (or zero with inverted alpha). Applies to generic HIDD bitmaps inheriting `PutAlphaTemplate()` in non-transparent color-expansion mode. See [GD4817](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4817) and the [arithmetic/caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14611). Source-only; no rendering operation was run.
**GD5855 — IconList label clipping uses the object X coordinate as its top edge:** `DrawEntryLabel()` sets `objrect.MinY = objX` instead of `objY`; this is active in Wanderer’s default direct-display path because buffering is off by default and the only buffer-enable branch is disabled by an undefined macro. Depending on the object’s screen position, labels can be clipped out or stale. See [GD5855](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5855) and the [default rendering-path recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14459). Source-only; no GUI redraw was run.
**OD11027 — AHI_CA can leave its public screen locked when GUI construction fails:** after `LockPubScreen()`, VisualInfo/menu/layout failure returns before `UnlockPubScreen()`. The unconditional `CloseGUI()` cleanup cannot unlock it because the screen pointer is local and is not stored. The leaked visitor count prevents the screen owner from closing the public screen. Scoped to explicitly building optional `AHI_CA`, omitted from the default executable list. See [OD11027](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11027) and the [caller and visitor-count trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-ca-public-screen-lock-rollback-od11027). Source-only; no GUI or screen was used.
**OD3575 — HDAudio publishes a codec with an empty capability list:** if both the DAC and function group report no sample rates or sample sizes, initialization still publishes the card. The normal AHI requester then queries min/max rates and passes index `-1` into the unchecked frequency-table lookup; allocating the mode also indexes an empty list. See [OD3575](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3575) and the [capability and requester trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hdaudio-zero-capability-requester-caller-recheck-od3575-2026-11-01). Scoped to native HDAudio builds with a codec reporting an empty capability. Source-only; no codec or query was used.
**EK125 — task.resource can fault and retain its task-list lock after iterator allocation fails:** `LockTaskList()` obtains the shared semaphore before allocating its handle and returns NULL without releasing it; `NextTaskEntry(NULL)` dereferences NULL before its guard. Selected callers either fault in enumeration or skip unlock on NULL, leaving the semaphore held. See [EK125](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek125) and the [task-list caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9189). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**OD4442 — USB PTP cannot represent independent DOS protection bits:** mixed WRITE/DELETE restrictions are normalized to writable, and a READ-only restriction is cached as successful although `ACTION_READ` still proceeds. Scoped to the optional PTP class on devices advertising `SetObjectProtection`. See [OD4442](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4442) and the [protection/read-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L28101). Source-only; no protection change, read or device operation was run.
<a id="gd9875"></a>**GD9875 — `ChangeVPBitMap()` can dispose a planar HIDD wrapper during a concurrent view refresh:** its bitmap conversion and `MakeVPort()` run before the active-view semaphore, so a mixed planar/HIDD transition can dispose the wrapper while `LoadView()` passes that VPD to display methods. The checked-in Intuition swap/rethink routes share `LockIBase`; no maintained caller performs the mixed-representation sequence, so this remains a medium-confidence public-API concurrency candidate. See [GD9875](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9875) and the [caller/lock-boundary reconciliation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L13976). Source-only; no swap or concurrent refresh was run.
**EK9334 — RDB table serialization masks block-write failures:** table writer ignores BADB/PART/FSHD/RDSK write results, and treats the LSEG writer’s error block number as progress; it returns success and HDToolBox clears the changed flag. See [EK9334](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9334) and the [write-result/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rdb-partition-table-write-error-propagation-recheck-ek9334-2026-11-01). Source-only; no write or I/O error was induced.
**EK9333 — RDB trusts `DE_TABLESIZE` beyond fixed environment arrays:** loading and writable DosEnvec updates use the unvalidated count for copies into/out of 20-entry arrays; sufficiently large sizes exceed their enclosing allocations, and selected DOSBoot/USB callers pass the size to `MakeDosNode()`. See [EK9333](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9333) and the [copy-bound/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rdb-dosenvec-size-downstream-caller-closure-ek9333-strengthened-2026-10-26). Source-only; no malformed RDB was used.
**EK9331 — EBR traversal can loop on a nonzero link cycle:** the parser follows link blocks until a zero link or error, without tracking visited blocks or bounding the chain; nonempty entries can also allocate duplicate handles on each pass. See [EK9331](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9331) and the [EBR traversal trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no EBR media was read.
**EK9330 — EBR AddPartition dereferences a failed handle allocation:** its constructor can return NULL, but the backend immediately forms `&new_ph->ln` for insertion. See [EK9330](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9330) and the [allocation/insertion trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK9329 — EBR table-open failure orphans earlier logical-partition handles:** the backend enqueues handles while walking the chain, but a later error causes the generic wrapper to discard the table list without calling backend cleanup. See [EK9329](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9329) and the [partial-open cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no EBR disk or allocation failure was used.
**EK9328 — MBR backend trusts caller-supplied slot indices:** AddPartition and writable `PT_POSITION` paths index the four-entry array without range checks, and AddPartition can replace an occupied slot while its old handle remains live. HDToolBox’s checked path chooses a free slot, so scope is other callers or invalid API input. See [EK9328](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9328) and the [backend/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#mbr-partition-backend-full-body-and-public-caller-pass-ek9328-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no MBR edit or write was run.
**EK9327 — GPT’s maximum-length partition name lacks a NUL in `ln_Name`:** a name with 36 nonzero low bytes fills the 36-byte node-name array without termination. The generic `PT_NAME` getter is bounded and safe; direct node-name string consumers can read beyond the name. See [EK9327](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9327) and the [name termination/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-partition-name-termination-and-consumer-recheck-ek9327-2026-11-01). Source-only; no GPT media was used.
**EK9326 — GPT parser trusts unchecked entry dimensions:** entry count and size arithmetic determine the allocation, while the loop reads fixed fields and UTF-16 names without validating `EntrySize`; undersized entries or wrapped allocation arithmetic can lead to reads past the table buffer. See [EK9326](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9326) and the [entry-table bounds trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT media was read.
**EK9325 — GPT validation trusts an on-disk header size beyond its one-block buffer:** after minimum checks, the declared size is passed to CRC without checking it against the allocated block. See [EK9325](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9325) and the [header-bound trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT media was read.
**EK9324 — GPT partition handles narrow 64-bit LBAs to `ULONG`:** GPT attribute getters retain full LBAs, but handle construction narrows start/count before raw read/write offsets are reconstructed from the handle geometry. At 512-byte sectors the start wraps above 2 TiB. See [EK9324](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9324) and the [GPT-to-handle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT disk or I/O was used.
**EK9323 — Partition.library can miss 64-bit I/O capability on large disks:** its NSD probe uses a 32-bit capacity product and omits the inclusive high cylinder; if that leaves the estimate at or below 8,388,608 sectors, legacy read/write commands remain selected even when the device supports 64-bit commands. See [EK9323](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9323) and the [geometry/command trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#partition-geometry-to-nsd-command-selection-pass-ek9323-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no disk or I/O was used.
**EK9322 — DOSBoot can overrun the partition-name buffer while suffixing a duplicate:** `PT_NAME` accepts 31 characters into a 32-byte array, then the collision path appends `".1"` without checking capacity. See [EK9322](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9322) and the [name-bound trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-duplicate-partition-name-bound-recheck-ek9322-2026-11-01). Source-only; no scan was run.
**EK9321 — DOSBoot can leak its blank mouse-pointer buffer:** if the no-media window and pointer allocation succeed but animation setup returns NULL, `anim_Stop()` skips freeing the buffer because it only does so when animation data exists. See [EK9321](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9321) and the [pointer allocation/cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-no-media-animation-constructor-and-teardown-pass-ek9320ek9321-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK9320 — DOSBoot renders the no-media animation after frame storage allocation fails:** `banm_Init()` returns a non-NULL animation descriptor even when its chunky frame or planar backing allocation is missing; the caller immediately renders from that state. See [EK9320](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9320) and the [allocation-to-first-render trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-no-media-animation-constructor-and-teardown-pass-ek9320ek9321-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure or display was induced.
**EK9319 — DOSBoot leaks graphics and intuition references on quiet screen retries:** when a no-media screen cannot be opened, the quiet helper returns without closing libraries it opened; DOSBoot retries and opens them again. See [EK9319](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9319) and the [screen retry ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-quiet-screen-retrylibrary-ownership-pass-ek9319-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no display failure was induced.
**EK9318 — PPC DOSBoot leaks the Radeon HIDD open reference on setup failure:** Sam440 and CHRP standalone configurations open `radeon.hidd`; if subsequent graphics setup fails, the early return skips `CloseLibrary()`. See [EK9318](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9318) and the [PPC setup/cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-radeon-hidd-open-reference-recheck-ek9318-2026-11-01). Source-only; no driver was initialized.
**EK9317 — DOSBoot retries menu setup without a failure bound:** failed gadget population or `OpenWindow()` leaves the page result at -1, which does not satisfy the loop's exit conditions. Persistent setup failure can hold early boot indefinitely. See [EK9317](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9317) and the [setup/retry trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-menu-setup-retry-recheck-ek9317-2026-11-01). Source-only; no allocation or window failure was induced.
**EK9316 — DOSBoot leaves its Topaz font reference open:** non-m68k builds open a font while populating Boot Options but do not close that reference; GadTools releases only the separate references it opens for the listviews. Reopening the page can retain additional font references. See [EK9316](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9316) and the [font ownership recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-topaz-font-probe-lifetime-pass-ek9316-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GUI was run.
**EK9315 — DOSBoot truncates boot-list selection indices to a signed byte:** the listview returns a `WORD` selection, but DOSBoot matches it using signed `BYTE`; high rows cannot be represented, and overflow makes the result compiler-dependent. See [EK9315](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9315) and the [listview/index trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-list-index-width-pass-ek9315-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GUI was run.
**EK9314 — DOSBoot accepts a short `DosEnvec` then reads `de_DosType` past its end:** the menu accepts table index 15, while `de_DosType` is index 16; with media present this can produce an invalid displayed type or a fault. See [EK9314](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9314) and the [bound recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-variable-length-dosenvec-bound-recheck-ek9314-2026-11-01). Source-only; no device or menu was used.
**EK9313 — DOSBoot can wrap the displayed disk capacity on 32-bit builds:** `DosEnvec` geometry fields are multiplied at `IPTR` width before the result is assigned to `UQUAD`; totals above 2^32−1 sectors can therefore be shown too small or as zero. Scope is the optional Boot Options capacity display; disk I/O is not implicated. See [EK9313](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9313) and the [width recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-capacity-arithmetic-width-recheck-ek9313-2026-11-01). Source-only; no disk or menu was used.
**EK9312 — DOSBoot applies device toggles to the wrong MountList slot and does not bound the listview's no-selection code:** filtered rows can change another node's state; an empty Devices list sends code `0xffff` into an unchecked array index, which can fault. Scoped to the optional Boot Options menu and its filtered/empty device-list cases. See [EK9312](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9312), the [state-index trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-selection-index-recheck-ek9312-2026-11-01), and the [empty-list sentinel recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-empty-device-list-sentinel-ek9312-2026-11-04). Source-only; no menu or boot was run.
**EK9311 — DOSBoot leaks Boot Options label nodes on setup failure:** labels are allocated before window creation, but `freeGadgets_PageBoot()` runs only after a successful OpenWindow/message loop. A failed context or window setup therefore leaves successfully allocated labels behind. Scoped to the optional Boot Options page with row allocations followed by setup failure. See [EK9311](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9311) and the [ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-options-label-ownership-failure-recheck-ek9311-2026-11-01). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**EK9310 — DOSBoot resolves filtered boot-list rows against the full MountList:** with a nonbootable entry before bootable entries, clicking the second displayed boot option can select the first; accepting it then promotes the wrong node for boot. Scoped to the optional Boot Options menu when those list orders occur. See [EK9310](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9310) and the [selection trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-options-filtered-list-index-and-selection-recheck-ek9310-2026-11-01). Source-only; no GUI or boot was run.
**EK9309 — DOSBoot dereferences a failed Boot Options row allocation:** after the per-device `AllocVec()` fails, an open-error/no-media formatter still reads `listNode->ln_Name`. Scoped to the optional boot menu and a MountList row whose label allocation fails. See [EK9309](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9309) and the [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-allocation-failure-trace-ek9309-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no menu or allocation failure was run.
**EK9308 — DOSBoot can drop or overrun its stale USB boot-node state:** it sizes `devicesEnabled` from the initial MountList, then later processes the live list. A late USB partition can be omitted with no menu; growth beyond twice the snapshot count can make the menu index past the array. Scoped to Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 package boots with USB mass storage and insertion during DOSBoot setup. See [EK9308](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9308) and the [source recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-mountlist-snapshot-race-source-recheck-ek9308-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no menu or boot was run.
**EK9307 — i386 omits a valid memory-map entry ending at 4 GiB:** the exclusive-end sum wraps to zero, so `mmap_InitMemory()` rejects the range and does not create MemHeaders for that RAM. Scoped to an i386-PC Multiboot map with a 16-MiB-to-4-GiB entry and no replacement range. See [EK9307](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9307) and the [map-boundary trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#i386-pc-4gib-map-end-overflow-ek9307). Source-only; no boot map was exercised.
**EK9306 — `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock()` succeeds when its caller already owns the write lock:** the selected implementation routes through reentrant Exec `AttemptSemaphore()` and increments the nest count, although POSIX requires `EBUSY`. `pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock()` correctly fails in this case and is excluded. Applies to clients linking `linklibs-pthread`; no in-tree caller was found. See [EK9306](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9306) and the [corrected coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-rwlock-try-call-self-owner-contract-recheck-ek9306-corrected-2026-11-01). Source-only; no lock call was run.
**EK9305 — PFS3 reads the Exec DeviceList without its ExecSMP read lock:** its `scsi.device` lookup uses local-CPU `Forbid()` around `FindName()`, while `AddDevice()` publishes under the DeviceList spinlock. A concurrent registration can race the traversal; the handler must have `scsidevice` for the lookup path. See [EK9305](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9305) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pfs3-execsmp-devicelist-reader-and-writer-lock-recheck-ek9305). Source-only; no device-list interleaving was run.
**EK9304 — the native PC bootconsole misses `debug=serial` at the start of the command line:** its parser searches for a space-prefixed `debug` token; when this is the first token, it clears both debug flags and `con_Putc()` suppresses screen and serial output. Scoped to the shared native bootconsole initializers. See [EK9304](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9304) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1162). Source-only; no boot was run.
**EK9303 — i386 Exec startup dereferences a missing optional boot command line:** both selected Multiboot parsers can omit `KRN_CmdLine`, but priority-0 `exec_boot()` passes the zero default to `strstr()` before `RawIOInit()`. Applies to i386-PC boots without the optional Multiboot command-line field. See [EK9303](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9303) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1452). Source-only; no boot was run.
**OD10992 — PTP MODE_READWRITE can write through a NULL buffer on an existing object:** `ACTION_FINDUPDATE` leaves the file buffer empty, and an in-range `ACTION_WRITE` skips buffer allocation before copying. Scoped to optional PTP builds and writable existing files. See [OD10992](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10992) and the [write-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ptp-findupdate-existing-file-write-null-buffer-od10992). Source-only; no file operation or device was used.
**OD1946 expanded — partial first-read/write allocation failure leaves an AUDIO handle open with incomplete buffer/request state; retry can use an invalid request or make zero progress, and close can abort an uninitialized request.** See [OD1946](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1946) and the [allocation/caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-od1946-dos-error-return-and-partial-allocation-state-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or I/O was induced.
**OD1451 expanded — AHI-Handler accepts unsupported `UNIT=` values, including `AHI_NO_UNIT` and wrapped negative values, then queues ordinary file I/O through a NULL `io_Unit`.** See [OD1451](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1451) and the [parser/device caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-unsupported-unit-range-and-null-unit-io-od1451-expanded). Source-only; no device or I/O was run.
**OD10991 — AHI-Handler plays compressed AIFC data as raw PCM:** it ignores the COMM compression type and submits encoded bytes as signed PCM. Scoped to compressed AIFC input played through the documented `copy file.AIFC AUDIO:` route; Filesave emits uncompressed `NONE`. See [OD10991](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10991--ahi-handler-plays-compressed-aifc-payloads-as-raw-pcm) and the [reader cross-check](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-aiffaifc-input-reader-and-filesave-writer-cross-check-od10991-added-no-bodyloc-credit-2026-10-31). No file or audio device was used; source-only.
**OD9572 expanded — Filesave preserves a zero AHI mixing rate: recording divides by zero, and AIFF/AIFC playback hangs in header finalization when Stop waits for the worker.** See [OD9572](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9572) and the [Filesave finalization recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#filesave-zero-mix-rate-playback-finalization-recheck-od9572-expanded-2026-10-31). Source-only; no AHI call or audio operation was run.
**EK8952 — Reusing a deleted pthread TLS key exposes stale per-thread values:** key deletion leaves per-thread slots intact, and re-creation reuses an index without resetting active threads; `getspecific` and the new destructor can consume the previous value. Scoped to applications linking optional `linklibs-pthread`; no checked-in caller found. See [EK8952](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8952) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-tls-key-reuse-ek8952-rechecked). Source-only; no pthread operation or thread was run.
**OD4056 expanded — USB Audio leaves over-capacity sample rates selectable:** the selected Deneb RTIso path reserves controller-buffer slices from endpoint MaxPktSize but copies the rate-derived hook length without a slice bound, so an over-capacity mode can overwrite adjacent controller-buffer RAM. See [OD4056](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4056) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no descriptor, stream, or controller was exercised.
**OD3196 expanded — xHCI RTIso Stop can allow a completion to submit fresh periodic transfers after Stop returns:** besides leaving submitted TRBs live, the event task refills the pending-transfer target after each completion without checking a stopped state; an interleaving can rearm the supposedly stopped USB Audio stream. See [OD3196](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3196) and the [xHCI Stop/event-task trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#xhci-stoprtiso-event-task-refill-race-od3196). Source-only; no transfer or concurrent Stop was run.
**OD3192 expanded — optional AHI plus USB Audio builds can dereference a NULL current mode after ordinary unit close:** startup queues default gain and volume updates to the separate worker; the in-tree AHI-Handler opens the device on first use and closes it on last `ACTION_END`, so if that close frees the mode before the signal is consumed, the worker reads the cleared unit pointer. The finding also covers cross-mode routing and teardown clearing while another control remains live. See [OD3192](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3192) and the [AHI lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no AHI open/close or worker schedule was exercised.

**OD9548 expanded — PCIUSB can hide a failed grouped HCD and skip rollback:** later HCD initialization can overwrite an earlier failure and mark the failed controller online; a failed OHCI BAR map leaves no register base for periodic processing or teardown. If the final initializer fails, earlier and partial HCD state is also left without rollback. See [OD9548](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9548) and the [grouped-controller source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pciusb-grouped-hcd-failure-od9548). Source-only; no device or failure was induced.

**GD10101 expanded — `DamageList.c` can traverse region nodes while a refresh frees them:** its delayed `RegionRectangle` walk has no layer lock, while `EndUpdate()` clears that list under the lock. The finding also covers `CRList.c` live ClipRect traversal. See [GD10101](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10101) and the [four-file `test-layers` re-review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-damagelist-live-traversal-gd10101-expansion). Source-only; no refresh interleaving was run.

**OD10535 — WirelessManager's optional D-Bus passive scan can send probe requests:** with D-Bus New enabled, the handler converts an explicit-channel passive request into a wildcard-SSID scan, and user-space MLME decides to probe from channel regulatory flags rather than the requested scan type. Scoped to soft-MAC SANA-II interfaces and channels not marked passive-only; D-Bus New is disabled in the checked-in `.config`. See [OD10535](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10535) and the [targeted scan trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#wirelessmanager-dbus-passive-scan-trace-od10535). Optional configuration only; no scan was run.

**OD9757 expanded — deferred SANA-II completion reads `io_Unit` after `ReplyMsg()`:** both Broadcom4400 and nvidianet release the unit semaphore by rereading the request after replying it; a resumed caller may already reuse or free that request. Trigger requires a contended unit semaphore and caller scheduling before the post-reply read. See [OD9757](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9757) and the [source-order recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidianet-request-body-and-post-reply-ownership-recheck-od9757-expanded). Source-only; no request or scheduler was run.

**EK10311 — M68040 MOVEC rejects valid MMU control-register transfers:** the selected M68040 bridge uses a C68020 whitelist, so valid MOVEC encodings for TC, ITT0/1, DTT0/1, MMUSR, URP and SRP raise illegal-instruction exceptions. Scoped to explicit optional `m68kemu.library` use; guest impact depends on those registers being used. See [EK10311](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10311) and the [MOVEC coverage pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-movec-m68040-register-coverage-ek10311). Source-only; no guest instruction or build was run.

**OD10533 — PCIUSB can retain stale PCI device objects after releasing ownership:** closing a USB unit releases PCI ownership but leaves cached controller pointers; an expungeable backend can then dispose those unowned objects, and PCIUSB's scan-once path reuses them on a later open. Scoped to optional PCIUSB builds with an expungeable backend such as hosted Linux PCI. See [OD10533](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10533) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No device close, backend expunge, or reopen was run; source-only.

**EK9432 rechecked — m68k thunks mishandle guest pointers and structures:** `GetRGB32()` passes the guest ColorMap shadow as a native object; five region APIs read guest Rectangle inputs as host words; `GetDisplayInfoData()` copies native-endian and host-layout records into guest buffers; Icon `GetIconRectangleA()` and Intuition `QueryOverscan()`/`GadgetMouse()` write little-endian 16-bit coordinates into guest storage; `SetPointerBounds()` reads guest Rectangles at host byte order and keymap `MapRawKey()` reads guest `InputEvent` fields at host offsets; `GetPrefs()`/`GetDefPrefs()`/`SetPrefs()` fail to convert multi-byte fields; DataTypes DOS `GetArgStr()`/`SetArgStr()` expose unmapped process argument-string pointers; `GetDTString()` returns an unconverted host string pointer, `PrintDTObjectA()` passes a 16-byte guest `dtPrint` directly into a 32-byte native async-print path, `DoAsyncLayout()` reads guest `gpLayout` at native offsets, `GetDTAttrsA()` can return unmapped native pointers, `GetDTMethods()`/`GetDTTriggerMethods()` return native table pointers that their `Find*()` consumers cannot round-trip, `FindToolNodeA()` reads guest lists and TagItems as native structures and returns an unmapped node, `ObtainDTDrawInfoA()` passes guest tag lists to native consumers, method-table copy/free helpers pass native arrays and handles across the guest boundary, and `DoDTDomainA()` writes successful IBox coordinates in host byte order and forwards its A5 TagItem attributes without guest-to-native conversion; Utility date vectors fail to convert `ClockData`; `GetScreenData()` copies host-layout Screen data into a guest buffer; BOOPSI object/class handles are not guest-mapped and `GetAttr()` can write host-width `IPTR` values into guest slots; other Intuition output vectors write host-endian values; and HyperLayers `InitLayers()` clears 768 native bytes through a 102-byte guest `Layer_Info`. These are instances of the optional m68kemu boundary finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest API call or build was run; source-only.
**[EK9433](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9433) - m68k `FindToolType()` passes the guest string-pointer array directly to native code and returns any matched host string pointer without guest-address translation.** The array input normally fails on 64-bit little-endian hosts; the return issue applies when a native match is produced. No maintained emulated caller was found; source-only.

**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** the generated Intuition `ViewAddress()` thunk returns native `&IntuitionBase->ViewLord` directly and narrows it into guest D0 without creating a View shadow; guest code cannot reliably read it or pass it to `LoadView()`. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [ViewAddress trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9432-viewaddress-return-map-check-2026-11-02). No View operation or build was run; source-only.
**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** Graphics `TextExtent()`, `FontExtent()`, and `TextFit()` pass six 16-bit guest extent fields without byte-order conversion; outputs are corrupted and TextFit constraints are misread on little-endian hosts. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [TextExtent trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9432-graphics-textextent-endian-recheck-2026-11-02). No text operation or build was run; source-only.
**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** generated DOS `DosGetString()`, `GetArgStr()`, `FilePart()`, and `PathPart()` return native pointers without guest-address translation; Graphics `CMove()` resolves the custom-register address as an arena pointer and emits the wrong Copper destination, while `LoadRGB4()` and `PolyDraw()` consume guest big-endian word arrays as native words on little-endian hosts. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [Graphics thunk ABI trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9432-graphics-cmove-polydraw-loadrgb4-2026-11-02). No guest call, drawing, copper list, or build was run; source-only.

**EK10310 — Graphical boot consoles fail on a framebuffer shorter than one glyph:** a 1–13 pixel height becomes zero text rows. On PC, startup then assigns the NULL result of `AllocMem(0)` as the mirror and the next debug character dereferences it; the unsigned scroll row also underflows. Raspberry Pi AArch64 can scan beyond its one-row mirror or use an underflowed fallback copy if firmware echoes a nonzero sub-glyph mode. See [EK10310](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10310) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#zero-row-framebuffer-caller-pass-ek10310-added-2026-10-31). No boot or framebuffer was used; source-only.

**OD10532 — CAMD's 10-microsecond retry wait can take a VBlank interval:** AROS CAMD opens `timer.device` on `UNIT_VBLANK`, so `DoIO()` completion is tied to VBlank processing; on the PC timer's 50 Hz emulation, a retry can wait nearly 20 ms. This can slow MIDI output retries and SysEx completion polling. Applies when the explicitly buildable `workbench-libs-camd` target is used; it is not selected by the checked-in `workbench-libs-complete` edge. See [OD10532](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10532) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#camd-retry-wait-vblank-cadence-pass-od10532-added-2026-10-31). Source-only; no MIDI operation, timer request or build was run.

**OD2297 — Serial mouse PnP probing can classify no or truncated responses using uninitialized stack bytes:** the no-marker path tests uninitialized `buf[0]`, and the short PnP-frame path parses fixed fields beyond the received length, potentially matching a false product ID. Scoped to explicitly selected serialmouse with a usable serial-unit HIDD; default boot inclusion is not established. See [OD2297](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2297) and the [full-body serialmouse review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#serialmouse-full-body-and-pnp-protocol-decoder-recheck-od11045). Source-only; no serial probe was run.

**OD11045 — Serial mouse PnP accepts Mouse Systems devices but parses them as Microsoft packets:** the table maps `PNP0F04` to `P_MSC`, but the receive handler ignores the selected protocol and always groups and decodes Microsoft three-byte packets. See [OD11045](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11045) and the [full-body serialmouse review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#serialmouse-full-body-and-pnp-protocol-decoder-recheck-od11045). Scoped to explicitly enabled serialmouse with a matching PnP device; default inclusion is not established. Source-only; no serial device was exercised.

BoingIconBar final preferences-line newline handling (GD5659 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-26): traced ReadPrefs' FGets/strlen/unconditional last-byte removal to DOS FGets' EOF semantics and final category/icon consumers (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:769-818; rom/dos/fgets.c:24-36,57-75). A newline-terminated record loses its newline; an EOF-terminated final record loses its last data character. Compared BoingIconBar Preferences' separate importer, which conditionally strips newline, and exporter, which writes newline after every record (workbench/prefs/boingiconbar/prefs.c:62-66,121-141). Qualified trigger to externally edited/supplied files without a final newline. No prefs file was loaded; targeted source/caller pass only, no full-body or LOC credit.
SANA-II success WireError candidates withdrawn (OD3105, OD3114, OD3289; 2026-10-31): Revision 7 says `ios2_WireError` may be supplied when `io_Error` is nonzero and requires it when an applicable error exists; it is not a specified success output. The uninitialized-success-field findings were removed as unsupported API claims. No body credit changed. [Specification](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/SANA-II_Revision_7#Errors).
OOP_DisposeObject SysExplorer PCI caller recheck (2026-10-31): the optional PCI module disposes its temporary PCI-controller object only after synchronous enumeration returns and only on successful construction; callback device objects are borrowed. No new disposal defect or LOC credit. Source-only.

BoingIconBar focus-timer device-close trace (GD5657 confirmed; 2026-10-26): followed optional tool startup and cleanup (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:424-445,678-690), including periodic completion/rearm (:567-581,625-635), and compared Exec's CloseDevice contract with timer.device Open (rom/exec/closedevice.c:37-55; rom/timer/lowlevel.c:407-426). On successful OpenDevice the cleanup aborts/waits for any pending request then deletes the IORequest and port without CloseDevice, leaving the open reference unmatched. The workbench-tools-iconbar edge is not included in the default tools aggregate at the reviewed manifest (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/mmakefile.src:13-18); report scopes the finding to runs where this target is selected. timer.device is noexpunge, so no unload blockage is claimed. MUI input-handler timer-scale contract trace (GD5654 confirmed and caller-scoped; 2026-10-26): compared public MUI header flag definitions with Application registration and periodic re-arm (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/libraries/mui.h:597-601; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1497,1626-1655). SCALE10 and SCALE100 define hundredth-/tenth-second units and both together mean seconds, but both timer conversion sites use ihn_Millis directly as milliseconds and check only MUIIHNF_TIMER; the internal header does not define the scale bits. The checked-in Area timer uses plain milliseconds and no scale flags (classes/area.c:1591,2130-2134), so the active trigger is an MUI client using the documented scaled form. Confirmed that such intervals are scheduled too early by the scale factor; no timer request was run. Targeted API/caller pass only; no full-body or LOC credit.

GD5653 withdrawn as a duplicate of GD9493 (2026-10-31): both candidates describe the same signed-WORD delta narrowing in the generic HIDD line renderer and public Draw() path. GD5649 nullable Popstring child source recheck (retained; 2026-10-26): re-read Popstring construction and Popasl/Popscreen hooks (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popstring.c:41-57; popasl.c:108-129; popscreen.c:27-65). The string child is fetched with default NULL and conditionally omitted from the Group; both hooks initialize their output string pointer to NULL, call get() without checking the object, and subsequently pass/dereference that pointer. Existing report scope remains the optional-child construction path; maintained callers may require the child and are not claimed as triggers. No object or requester was run; source-only, no LOC credit.

GD5648 duplicate disposition (2026-10-26): compared the indexed claim with the VMM Preferences Open/Save As implementation and existing GD6027 section. Both refer to MenuOpen/MenuSaveAs in workbench/system/VMM/MUI/menus.c:7-59; GD6027 already covers the 80-byte stack buffers, unbounded fr_Drawer copies, and ignored AddPart result. MUI context-menu constructor failure cleanup trace (GD5647 confirmed; 2026-10-26): traced zune_open_menu's ZMenu allocation, GetVisualInfoA, CreateMenusA, LayoutMenusA and cleanup exits (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:1510-1558), then its selected area-class caller (classes/area.c:1862-1888). Once GetVisualInfoA succeeds, CreateMenusA failure frees zmenu but returns without FreeVisualInfo; the VisualInfo is freed only on the success path after layout. The caller stores NULL and continues handler setup, with no access to the local VisualInfo. Confirmed conditional leak; no allocation failure or context menu was run. Targeted function/caller pass only; no full-body or LOC credit.

MUI MutualExclude mouse-index/caller comparison (GD5646 confirmed; 2026-10-26): followed HandleMouseClick's selected MenuItem into HandleCheckItem and compared with Intuition's keyboard shortcut/check path (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:330-360,367-434; rom/intuition/menus.c:156-176,188-200,221-245). MUI initializes local itemnum to zero and never assigns the selected sibling index; HandleCheckItem then exempts index zero while applying the selected item's mask. Intuition computes and passes itemnum/subnum. For a nonzero selected sibling whose MutualExclude mask includes bit zero, another checked first sibling is incorrectly left checked. Source-confirmed conditional mouse-selection defect; no menu event was run. Targeted slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

MUI stale submenu selection pointer/click trace (GD5645 confirmed; 2026-10-26): re-read FindSubItem/FindItem, HandleMouseMove, HandleMouseClick, AddToSelection and KillSubMenuWin (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:223-269,330-363,558-624,1433-1454,976-985). After a submenu row is active, returning to the same parent row produces the same activeitemnum, so the parent-window branch skips KillSubMenuWin and retains the prior activesubitemnum/pointer. A click on the parent window follows HandleMouseClick's parent-item path but AddToSelection uses the stale submenu state and can queue the enabled submenu item if ItemAddress still matches. Confirmed as a conditional pointer-selection defect; no GUI sequence was run. Targeted slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

m68k Intuition configured-vector completeness pass (GD10090 expanded; 2026-10-27; no file/LOC credit): compared public `intuition.conf` function declarations with generated wrapper definitions and both Intuition dispatch tables. Confirmed `DrawBorder` (offset 108), `PrintIText` (216), `IntuiTextLength` (330), `BuildSysRequest` (360), `AllocRemember` (396), `FreeRemember` (408), `EasyRequestArgs` (588), `BuildEasyRequestArgs` (594), and `OpenScreenTagList` (612) have no generated or manual entry; neighboring table offsets verify each gap. The generic missing-LVO handler returns zero without calling native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:280-290`). Expanded GD10090 with these omissions and their API-specific no-op/zero-return consequences. `CloseScreen`, `CloseWindow`, and `AutoRequest` were excluded because the manual table has handlers; `FreeMonitorList` remains under EK9432 because its paired raw-pointer ownership failure is already documented. `BuildSysRequest()` is additionally qualified because native `FreeSysRequest()` and `SysReqHandler()` document that family as unsupported. No emulated call or requester/drawing/screen operation was run. Source-only.

Intuition/MUI temporary menu-window open-failure cleanup pass (GD5643/GD5644 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-26): traced Intuition main/submenu decorator allocation and MDM_INITMENU calls through OpenWindowTagList and the KillMenuWin/KillSubMenuWin guards (rom/intuition/menutask.c:1204-1277,1368-1430). If opening fails after decorator init, the NULL window makes kill cleanup skip MDM_EXITMENU and frees; user-buffer leak requires nonzero requested size and successful allocation. Also compared MUI MakeMenuWin/KillMenuWin and public Menu.Flags declaration: both Intuition and MUI set read-only MIDRAWN unconditionally after window open, then clear only when the window pointer exists (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:870-899; compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:159-162). No in-tree MIDRAWN readers were found, so GD5644 records an inconsistent public state with limited verified impact. GD5641/GD5642 m68kemu thunk disposition and later optional-target restoration (rechecked 2026-10-31): the 2026-10-26 check correctly found no default ROM/package edge, but treated that as excluding an explicitly buildable optional `kernel-m68kemu-library` from the candidate reports. Restored the two distinct API mismatches under Exec/Kernel IDs EK10316 and EK10317: the manual `OpenWindowTagList` thunk leaves `TAG_MORE`'s guest address untranslated and ignores its non-NULL A0/NewWindow argument. `TAG_SKIP` entries are copied and then interpreted by native tag traversal, so no `TAG_SKIP` bug is claimed. No emulator or runtime call was exercised.

GD5640 disposition (Nouveau MST fallback GUID race withdrawn; 2026-10-26): verified the package graph at the reviewed commit: Nouveau is commented out of workbench drivers and the PC graphics-driver metatarget (workbench/mmakefile.src:36-41; arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13), and the module makefile disables its inclusion metatarget (workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:14-29). picture.datatype DTM_FRAMEBOX input/output contract recheck (GD5639 confirmed; 2026-10-26): compared DT_FrameBox() and its dispatcher (workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1394-1449,2194-2198) with the public dtFrameBox field annotations (compiler/include/datatypes/datatypesclass.h:335-344) and selected callers. The structure specifies dtf_ContentsInfo as input and dtf_FrameInfo as output, but the handler writes dimensions and FIF_SCROLLABLE only through dtf_ContentsInfo, never populating dtf_FrameInfo, while returning success for a non-NULL contents record. The inspected in-tree callers pass the same record for both arguments, masking the mismatch. Confirmed GD5639 for distinct input/output records; no external client or runtime call exercised.
