PanelGroup scan/add allocation-failure trace (GD5638 confirmed and narrowed; 2026-10-26): re-read `PanelGroup__MUIM_PanelGroup_ScanPanels()`, `AddPanel()`, `OM_NEW()`, and panel-list consumers (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:175-235,408-483,523-672`). A recognized child remains in the Group child list when `mui_alloc_struct(PanelNode)` fails; `ScanPanels()` ignores the AddPanel result, overwrites `panel_count` with the accepted-child count, and returns TRUE. `OM_NEW()` ignores the scan result and returns the object. The missing list node then makes per-panel collapse/expand/toggle/state operations skip or default that child and list-wide operations omit it. Confirmed the finding is conditional on node-allocation failure; no ownership violation or runtime reproduction claimed. Replaced the placeholder with source evidence and narrowed the index title. Targeted function/caller slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

Review correction (2026-10-23): GD4853 is retained with narrowed wording. `bitpack_read_msb()` takes bytes through an unsigned pointer but shifts them as promoted `int`; at nonzero `endbit`, a valid byte with high bits set can make `b->ptr[0] << (24 + endbit)` exceed `ULONG` range, which is undefined. The sign-bit case at offset zero alone is implementation-defined.

Review correction (2026-10-23): GD6104 remains an array-bound candidate because each feature table has 31 entries while its loop can test 32 bits. Its `1 << 31` expression is not independently undefined under the applicable C rules; whether the bit test reaches `table[31]` depends on implementation-defined conversion behavior. No selected compiler result or processor response was established.

Raspberry Pi VideoCore GPU MemHeader caller/lifecycle recheck (GD9405-GD9406 added; 2026-10-23): traced the `InitMem()` extension header through `MEMF_MANAGED`, `IsManagedMem()`, `AvailMem()` and Exec's managed-header query path. `vcgfx` sets `mhe_Avail` and `mh_Free` but never sets `mhe_Magic`, so the selected availability query treats the node as an ordinary header with an empty `mh_First`. Separately traced its `SysBase->MemList` publication through graphics-library/display-driver init failures into genmodule's failed-init free; no unlink path exists. Added GD9405 for the ignored availability callback and GD9406 for the reclaimed linked node. The two findings have separate success-path versus failed-init triggers; the latter is distinct from GD6256's IRQ-node lifetime. No memory query, allocation, or failed module load was run; source-only.

ExecSMP MemList publication recheck (GD9803 strengthened, 2026-10-25): re-read VCGfx `InitMem()` and resolved the module-init phase from its selected package/configuration. `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:143` includes `hidd-vcgfx`; `vcgfx.conf:5` sets resident priority 9, which genmodule maps to `RTF_COLDSTART` (`tools/genmodule/writeinclibdefs.c:31-45`). `InitCode(RTF_COLDSTART)` calls matching resident initializers (`rom/exec/initcode.c:57-96`), after Exec's first COLDSTART resident enables multitasking (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:53-61`). The kernel `platform_PostInit()` calls `ARMI_Init()` before then on ExecSMP, and Exec's SMP init pins the boot task after secondaries are released (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:248-288`). Thus VCGfx `InitMem()` is reached in the multi-CPU coldstart phase on that package/config. The unsynchronized `AddTail()` versus Exec's `MemListSpinLock` readers is confirmed. The contemporaneous claim that no selected allocator walk was found was superseded by the selected input-device task reader traced in the correction below; interleaving remains conditional. No package was built or initialized; source-only.

# Build-selected m68k P96gfx HIDD (local C/header pass complete; external callers and hardware closure open)

`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src` selects P96gfx in the ROM/expansion and ordinary module payloads (`:187,:375`). Its module manifest selects five C translation units with 3,642 `cloc 2.06` C code lines, and five included local headers with 2,229 code lines. All selected bodies and local headers have full-body credit: 5,871 / 5,871 local C/header lines (100%). Findings GD5995-GD5999 were added for constructor cleanup of an unlinked bitmap node and unchecked allocation results in card construction, mode registration, VRAM setup and cursor-color-map setup. The unselected `p96call.c` generator adds 97 code lines and is tracked separately. External `.card` implementations, public graphics callers, m68k ABI/compiler behavior and hardware remain open; this is local source-body coverage, not subsystem completion. No build, allocation failure or graphics operation was run; source-only.

P96 card discovery/rollback reconciliation (GD4806 retained; GD6000 detailed, 2026-10-22/25; caller scope refined 2026-11-01): followed `.card` library enumeration under `Forbid()` through `P96GFX__InitCard()`, resolution population, per-card VRAM-header construction, attribute-base failure and module-init rollback (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1624-1702,1741-1817`). The selected P96 monitor deliberately keeps its requested `.card` library open (`workbench/devs/monitors/P96/p96.c:8-18,129-141`), so GD4806 requires a different already-listed card whose final reference closes during the scan, or an external caller establishing that overlap; no in-tree overlapping closer was found. No card library, mode probe, allocation failure or initialization rollback was induced; source-only.

P96Gfx HIDD constructor/mode/cursor allocation-failure pass (GD5996-GD5999 detailed, 2026-10-25): re-read `P96GFXCl__Root__New()` and traced its allocation consumers through discovered-card `AddDisplayDriver()` registration and the cursor methods (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:310-645,1145-1165,1184-1327,1369-1379,1820-1847`). These are separate failure sites and consequences; the tag-array issue occurs even on card modes whose eventual display is not used. No allocation failure, display-driver registration, cursor update, or hardware operation was run; source-only; local file bodies were already credited in the P96 inventory.

P96Gfx bitmap palette-failure cleanup recheck (GD5995 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced depth-8 palette allocation failure through the constructor's `ok == FALSE` disposal branch. The instance data was zeroed, and because allocation failed, the bitmap's node never reaches the later `AddTail()`; its `Root::Dispose()` nevertheless reaches unconditional `Remove(&data->node)`. PlanarBM FillRect write-mask caller recheck (GD5734 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced `SetWriteMask()` into `rp->Mask`, `GetDriverData()` into `GC_COLMASK` for depth-at-most-eight bitmaps, and public `RectFill()` through `fillrect_render()` to the planar override (`rom/graphics/setwritemask.c:48-49`; `graphics_inline.h:82-89`; `rectfill.c:68-101`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:330-337`; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:443-502`). ChunkyBM RGB16_LE alpha-image row-step recheck (GD5733 detailed, 2026-10-25): re-read the signed `WORD` `src_step`/`dst_step` locals and both alpha-image row loops (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:439-557`), then traced `WritePixelArrayAlpha()`'s public `UWORD srcmod` through `RenderHook()` to `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarrayalpha.c:37-47,116-128`). A 40,000-byte modulo and width 1 produce source step 39,996, which cannot be represented by signed `WORD`; supported 16-bit two's-complement targets wrap it negative and subsequent rows use the wrong source address. The destination step is subject to the same narrowing for wide rows. No operation was run; source stride and target conversion are source/API-derived; source-only.

IconList maximum-line-width input and allocation-bound recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-23): traced `MUIA_IconList_LabelText_MaxLineLen` from the Wanderer view-settings read/write and volume-list setup through `IconList__OM_NEW()`, `IconList__OM_SET()` and `IconList__LabelFunc_CreateLabel()`. No preference was imported or changed and no label was rendered. Source-only.

IconList multiline AppIcon label destination-bound pass (GD6243 added; 2026-10-23): traced the 256-byte `AllocVecPooled()` result through per-line output offsets and `strncpy()` lengths in `IconList__LabelFunc_SplitLabel()`, then followed the selected `IconWindowVolumeList` AppIcon refresh to `AppIcon_GetLabel()` and the public `AddAppIconA()` storage of its caller-supplied text pointer. At the accepted six-character minimum line width, 50 six-character runs separated by 49 spaces produce a 349-character label; the splitter skips each inter-run space but advances its destination by six copied bytes plus one line slot, so the last copy writes indices 343–348 of a 256-byte allocation. This input avoids the existing splitter's delimiter-probe overread: each six-character run exactly matches the measured line width and the shorter-than-line search does not execute. Added GD6243 for the independent output-buffer overrun. The AppIcon label is caller-provided and has no length limit in `AddAppIconA()`; the volume-list preference path supplies the minimum line length and multiline setting. No AppIcon, preference, allocation failure, or GUI operation was run; source-only.

IntelGMA solid-line signed-width recheck (GD5980 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced the accelerated `DrawLine()` method's public LONG locals and WORD deltas/error/coordinate/loop variables through each horizontal, vertical and generic branch. Confirmed the generic Bresenham recurrence narrows `2*dy` into WORD (e.g. span 20,000 makes 40,000 unrepresentable) and the axis-aligned loops extend their endpoint while using a WORD index (e.g. exclusive endpoint 32,768 for an accepted endpoint of 32,767). Clipping only configures the GPU rectangle after the CPU loop has been selected; it does not bound the iteration count. Expanded GD5980 with the separate wrong-rasterization and conditional wraparound-loop cases, explicitly qualifying compiler conversion behavior. No line draw or build was run; source-only; no body-line credit change.

The same directory's `hosted-X11-monitor` build-program target selects `disk_startup.c`; `x11keymaptable` selects the host-side `makexkeytable.c` utility plus four 256-byte raw-key mapping assets (`def-`, `mac-`, `alt-`, and `alt-nb-`). ## RISC-V OpenSBI Headless graphics HIDD and monitor loader

The OpenSBI boot manifest selects `kernel-hidd-gfx-headlessgfx` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`); the HIDD manifest also builds the `Headless` monitor loader as a dependency. Read the three module C bodies (`headlessgfx_init.c`, 79 `cloc 2.06` code lines; `headlessgfx_hiddclass.c`, 315; `headlessgfx_bitmapclass.c`, 64), the loader `disk_startup.c` (138), all three local headers (103), `headlessgfx.conf`, and the module/boot manifests: 596 C lines and 103 header lines, 699 combined. Traced initialization and rollback through `AddDisplayDriver`, object/display construction through the selected `HW_AddDriver` and display-registration callers, mode/pixel-format tags against `stdpixfmts_le.h`, and monitor tooltypes through attribute acquisition and registration. Added GD6086: after acquiring all nine OOP attribute bases, resident initialization returns failure on graphics-library open or display-driver registration errors without releasing them; the configuration has no expunge cleanup either. Added GD6087: failed display-object construction is not propagated by the graphics HIDD constructor, and graphics.library treats a driver with no display as successfully set up, retiring its boot-replay entry. The default depth/geometry bounds and tag-array capacities are internally consistent, and the selected bitmap overrides only visibility state while delegating bitmap methods to the chunky superclass. Cross-file GD5924 reachability: default 8/16/24 formats at one sync plus inherited Direct framebuffer mode makes the generic chooser select 8-bit; see the dated caller trace below and the findings report. This is 100% body-read credit for this local target slice, not Graphics/Desktop completion. The downstream VNC reader/client was not identified in the selected sources; firmware/display handover and boot-time allocation behavior remain source-only. No build, monitor load, allocation failure or display operation was run.

GD6087 caller-path verification (2026-10-23): reread `HW__HW__SetUpDriver()` and confirmed its default implementation unconditionally returns TRUE (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:418-422`). `driver_Setup()` only returns FALSE when `HW_AddDriver()` returns NULL; when a non-NULL graphics HIDD reports a NULL `DisplayDefault`, it logs and continues to its success return (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-385,414`). `driver_ReplayBootQueue()` frees the entry on that success result (`:296-323`). This confirms the report's queue-retirement consequence. No display failure was induced; source-only.

HeadlessGfx GD6086-GD6087 candidate-detail recheck (2026-10-25): for GD6086, confirmed `GetAttrBases()` rolls back only when an `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` itself fails (`headlessgfx_init.c:32-57`), while the later resident-only graphics-library open and `AddDisplayDriver()` failure paths return FALSE without calling the release helper (`:85-125`). The disk monitor loader is excluded because the auto-registration branch runs only when `FindResident(MOD_NAME_STRING)` succeeds. For GD6087, re-read the HIDD root constructor (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:288-338`): it returns the parent-created root even if default-display creation returns NULL. Followed that non-NULL object through `HW_AddDriver()` and `driver_Setup()`; base setup succeeds and the NULL default display is logged but not converted to failure (`hwclass.c:418-422`; `graphics_driver.c:369-385,414`), so boot replay frees the queue entry (`:296-323`). Expanded both report entries with the respective exact trigger and consequence. No load, object allocation, or replay failure was induced; source-only; selected-body credit unchanged.

GD5728 fast-method dispatch and constructor consequence recheck (2026-10-25): traced the selected `gfx_histogramclass.c` cache initialization through `BMHUNMAPPIXEL`, `BMHFINDCOLOR`, and `BMHADDCOLOR` (`gfx_histogramclass.c:53-80`; `gfx_intern.h:607-648`) and matched method offsets to the `Hidd_BitMap` and `Hidd_BMHistogram` method lists in `gfx.conf`. The cached UnmapPixel method is PutPixel; the cached AddColorEntry method is FindColorEntry, whose offset happens to equal PutPixel's numeric offset. The constructor starts with an empty histogram and its misdirected Add calls therefore never insert an entry. The incompatible unmap message is consumed as PutPixel coordinates/value; selected generic ChunkyBM and PlanarBM writers compute memory addresses without coordinate checks (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:107-139`; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:356-385`), so unintended writes are possible, with exact address consequences depending on runtime values and implementation. Confirmed `gfx_histogramclass.c` is in the selected GFX module manifest and found no in-tree histogram constructor caller. No histogram or bitmap operation was run; source-only.

Confirmed the Get case falls through and overwrites the picosecond result with the pixel clock; a direct nonzero `PixelClock` from 1 through 999 also makes `pixelclock / 1000` zero before the getter's division. Confirmed the PixelTime Set conversion has an unchecked `1e9 / tag->ti_Data`. Reconciled LinuxFB's selected mode producer (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:177-243`): it passes nonzero `vsi->pixclock` as PixelTime, but truncates the tags before index 9 when the pixclock is zero, matching its comment that the zero case crashes. No in-tree PixelTime getter or zero-valued parser call was found; the generic public API remains exposed to both cases. No mode was queried or constructed; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

Generic DMEnum terminal allocation and selected caller pass (GD5730 expanded, 2026-10-25): traced recursive `querymode()` to its `syncidx >= num_syncs` base case and through unwinding into `DMEnum__Hidd_DMEnum__QueryModeIDs()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:175-271,749-809`). The terminal frame allocates `numfound + 1` ModeIDs, then unconditionally adds `numfound` and writes the invalid-ID sentinel; if AllocVec fails, this invalid pointer operation occurs before the method can return. Confirmed the selected generic `graphics.library/display_Setup()` caller checks NULL only after the query returns (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:76-80`), so its cleanup cannot catch the internal write. P96 and AmigaVideo provide separate per-architecture QueryModeIDs overrides. No query or allocation failure was run; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

Graphics.library init rollback and TextFonts semaphore ownership pass (GD5762 added, 2026-10-22): read the complete `rom/graphics/graphics_init.c` body (211 physical lines; 152 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`) and traced its INITLIB failure rollback through `compiler/autoinit/functions.c` and the generated module failure path in `tools/genmodule/writestart.c`. `fontsem` is added to Exec's public semaphore list before the hash-table allocation and several other fallible steps; failure returns without `RemSemaphore()`, while the generated initializer frees the library base. GetGBuffers/FreeGBuffers full-body and caller recheck (GD5521 strengthened, 2026-10-22): read both selected graphics.library functions in full (`rom/graphics/getgbuffers.c` and `freegbuffers.c`, 91 `cloc 2.06` C code lines total), checked `VSprite` field widths in `compiler/include/graphics/gels.h`, and searched all maintained C/header callers. `GetGBuffers()` stores the depth-scaled byte count in signed `long` and passes it unchecked to `AllocMem`; on 32-bit-long code using normal wrapping arithmetic, `Width=32767`, `Height=8194`, `Depth=8` computes a 4,295,884,768-byte SaveBuffer request that wraps to 917,472 bytes after a 536,985,596-byte ImageShadow request. With successful allocations the API returns TRUE with an undersized buffer; double buffering repeats the same undersized request for `DBuffer->BufBuffer`. `FreeGBuffers()` recomputes the same size. No maintained direct caller was found, so external use and any resulting overwrite remain unverified. This qualifies the candidate to extreme, representable dimensions and 32-bit-long targets; no buffer was allocated or used. Credited 91 full-body code lines and two selected source paths, without recalculating the incomplete Graphics/Desktop denominator. Source-only.


Graphics GELS mask construction and collision traversal pass (GD5763 added, 2026-10-22): read all of `rom/graphics/docollision.c`, `initmasks.c`, and `initgmasks.c` (189 `cloc 2.06` C code lines total); traced mask size and population to `GetGBuffers()` and the `SortGList()` ordering precondition. In `DoCollision()` both shifted-word branches use a strict `>` bound after incrementing the word index, so equality admits a one-past-row read. For sorted one-word Bobs at `(0,0)` and `(1,0)`, the negative-scroll branch reads the second mask's word index 1 although `InitMasks()` and `GetGBuffers()` allocate/populate one word. Added GD5763, with the fault/false-collision consequence qualified by adjacent memory. No maintained direct callers of `DoCollision()` or `InitGMasks()` were found; the functions remain public APIs. No mask, collision list, or handler was created or run. Credited 189 full-body code lines and three selected source paths; no percentage recalculated because the Graphics/Desktop denominator remains incomplete. Source-only.

GELS AddBob/RemIBob/RemVSprite ownership pass (2026-10-22; GD5764 retained, no duplicate): read all of `rom/graphics/addbob.c`, `remibob.c`, and `remvsprite.c` (81 `cloc 2.06` C code lines total), and traced `_ClearBobAndFollowClearPath()` against Bob's waiting/drawn flags, list unlinking, DrawPath/ClearPath repair, and head/tail internal-record cleanup. A waiting/already-cleared Bob skips restoration before unlinking; a drawn Bob follows the clear/restore path first. `RemVSprite()` can dereference `vs->IntVSprite` while repairing a DrawPath reference, but that requires the already-recorded GD5764 state where AddVSprite failed to create the internal record; it is not a distinct root cause. Graphics.library `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_WIDTH)` and generic render-caller pass (GD5766 added, 2026-10-22): read the complete `rom/graphics/getbitmapattr.c` body and traced `BMA_WIDTH` through generic HIDD row-stride construction (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:849-874`) into `GetRPClipRectangleForBitMap()` (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:1062-1074`). For chunky formats, the HIDD byte stride is aligned pixel width multiplied by bytes per pixel, but `GetBitMapAttr()` multiplies that byte count by eight as if each byte represented eight pixels. Added GD5766; the generic clip helper explicitly exists to keep HIDDs without bounds checks from accessing outside the bitmap, so its inflated maximum defeats that protection on affected render paths. Reconciled additional width callers in ColorWheel, sprite conversion, and screen-buffer allocation; no runtime operation was run. The graphics.library function is selected by `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src`; the generic HIDD is selected independently. Credited the complete `getbitmapattr.c` body (40 `cloc 2.06` C lines); no whole-subsystem denominator is available. Source-only.

GD5766 graphics-library width-consumer follow-up (2026-10-22): read the complete `rom/graphics/cleareol.c`, `clearscreen.c`, and `setrast.c` bodies (59 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and followed `SetRast()` through `fillrect_pendrmd()`/`do_render_with_gc()`. These public operations also treat BMA_WIDTH as a pixel extent; ClearEOL and ClearScreen pass it as RectFill's right edge, while SetRast passes width minus one as its full-bitmap fill bound. The selected `OpenScreen()` path calls SetRast during screen initialization (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2235-2241`), and other consumers include screen buffer and font rendering. This strengthens GD5766's selected callers and consequence; no separate root cause was added. No render or screen open was run. Credited all three function bodies, bringing the scoped source pass to 99 `cloc 2.06` C lines across four files; no whole graphics.library denominator is asserted. Source-only.

Intuition CloseScreen full-body and GD5179 cleanup-caller pass (2026-10-22): read all 425 physical lines of `rom/intuition/closescreen.c` (253 `cloc 2.06` C code lines). Traced public-screen visitor refusal, public-node/resource-list removal, screen-chain and active/default screen repair, display teardown, bitmap/ColorMap/pointer/font ownership, and final object disposal. Workbench launch CreateNewProc failure resource ownership recheck (GD5831 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `WB_LaunchProgram()` message ownership into the handler, then followed `LoadSeg()`, `DupLock(lock)`, `CreateNewProc()`, and both error/done labels. Confirmed the NULL-process case bypasses `UnLoadSeg()` and `DestroyWBS()` and never unlocks `home`; the outer handler frees only `WBCommandMessage`, and its destructor does not free the nested startup. Checked `CreateNewProc()` failure cleanup: it releases its internal locks but the supplied `NP_HomeDir` and segment remain caller-owned. No launch or process-creation failure was run; source-only; no body credit change.

Workbench handler readiness handshake/port allocation recheck (GD5832 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `CreateNewProc()` return through `WBOpen()` and the handler entry. `WBOpen()` sets `wb_Initialized` and increments the library open count solely on non-NULL process return; handler `Initialize()` can subsequently fail any of its three `CreateMsgPort()` calls, deinitialize the public command port to `PA_IGNORE`/NULL task, and return. Confirmed later `PutMsg()` calls enqueue without signaling under PA_IGNORE and OpenWorkbenchObjectA reports success after enqueue. No startup-ready handshake or open-count rollback is present on this handler exit. No process or allocation failure was run; source-only; no body credit change.

Workbench IDCMP open/close relay allocation ownership recheck (GD5833 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `__HandleIntuition_WB()` for WBENCHOPEN/WBENCHCLOSE through `CreateIWBHM()`, the optional WorkbenchPort send, and original IntuiMessage reply. When the port is absent, the relay is not queued or sent and this branch does not call `DestroyIWBHM()`; only a successfully forwarded and replied relay is freed by the reply loop. Scoped the leak to successful relay allocation with no registered app port. No event was sent; source-only; no body credit change.

GetNextAppIcon list synchronization caller recheck (GD5837 confirmed, 2026-10-25): compared the complete traversal with `AddAppIconA()` and `RemoveAppIcon()` locking. AddAppMenuItem command-key check/insert interleaving recheck (GD5840 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `keyUsed()` lock acquisition/release and the later independent lock around `AddTail()`. DiskInfo GD6053 arithmetic recheck (2026-10-25): traced both `FormatBlocksSized()` call sites in initial display and notification refresh (`diskinfo.c:274-276,637-638`) into its signature and calculation (`support.h:15`; `support.c:65-75`). <a id="gd6053"></a>**GD6053 — DiskInfo truncates 64-bit block counts and overflows usage percentages.** `FormatBlocksSized()` accepts `ULONG` counts and multiplies `100 * blocks` in 32-bit arithmetic, so sufficiently large volumes display incorrect sizes/percentages. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6053) and [selected helper/caller review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskinfo-main-support-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.

InjectIcon GD6109 normalization branch arithmetic recheck (2026-10-25): re-evaluated both copies in `main()` (`workbench/tools/IconInject/main.c:35-65`) with exact suffix and boundary cases. A `.info` name longer than five bytes reaches the `else` branch and copies `len-5`, correctly removing the suffix. An unsuffixed name longer than five bytes enters the other branch, allocates `len-4`, but copies `len-5`, leaving a NUL-terminated prefix with its final five input bytes omitted. Each iteration advances four pixels, loads two 128-bit source vectors at `3*x` and `3*x+12`, shuffles/combines them into a 256-bit result, and stores eight 32-bit pixels. Confirmed x86-64 installs this function for RGB24-to-XRGB32 when the AVX2 check enables the AVX group. A width-four row therefore provides 12 source bytes/four destination pixels but the vector block reads up to byte 27 and stores eight pixels; width≥8 repeats overlapping eight-pixel stores every four pixels. ILBM HAM row-start candidate disposition (GD5305 qualified, 2026-10-23): re-read `ReadRGBPic()`'s scanline state initialization and first-pixel HAM modification path (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbmclass.c:274,294-323`), then searched local mode definitions, format documentation and checked-in HAM producers. The code proves state starts at zero, but this local source set does not establish the required HAM line-start color or that an input row may begin with a modify command. ILBM parser/decoder caller and row-storage recheck (GD5290-GD5294, GD5291-GD5292, GD5302 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-23): reread `UnpackByteRun1()`, both bitmap conversion routines, palette setup and all of `ReadILBM()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbmclass.c:79-602`), then traced the constructor caller `ILBM__OM_NEW()` (`:831-846`) and the selected IFFParse `ReadChunkBytes()` contract. Confirmed the short uncompressed BODY allocation is followed by dimension-derived row copies (GD5291); ByteRun1 control and literal/repeat bytes have no compressed-source bound despite the scratch output allocation (GD5292); RGB/HAM row advancement omits `mskHasMask` data (GD5302); `ReadILBM()` accepts palette sizes beyond Picture's embedded arrays before `CopyColRegs()` writes (GD5290); and HAM direct-color lookup is not capped to the base CMAP length, while HAM depths 1-5 reach negative shift counts (GD5293/GD5294). Constructor disposal handles the failed `ReadILBM()` return; no separate object-lifetime issue established. No new defect promoted. This closes the parser/decoder slice only; raw writer, remaining caller behavior, and whole-file line credit remain open. No image, truncated chunk, or allocation failure was exercised; source-only.


ILBM indexed mask-plane retention and Picture renderer caller pass (GD6165 added; 2026-10-23): compared the indexed `ReadBitMapPic()` allocation and both row decoders with `mskHasMask` accounting (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbmclass.c:118-185`), then traced publication into the selected Picture `PDTA_MaskPlane` getter, `CreateMaskPlane()`, and `render_on_rastport()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:464-467,630-648`; `colorhandling.c:579-635`). Confirmed the color-depth bitmap omits the mask plane, the reader only skips it, and the Picture helper synthesizes a mask only for `mskHasTransparentColor`; the renderer's `mskHasMask` branch does not draw when the getter returns NULL. Added GD6165 for indexed masked ILBM rendering, separate from GD5302's RGB/HAM row-stride defect. Both compression paths were source-traced; no image was loaded or rendered. This is caller-path evidence only; full ILBM writer and whole-file review remain open. Source-only.


ILBM class DTM_WRITE dispatch and raw-helper reachability correction (GD5295-GD5297/GD5299-GD5301/GD5303 withdrawn, 2026-10-23): traced the active ILBM class construction and dispatcher (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/libfunc.c:115-155,165-177`) against `ilbm.conf` and the selected Picture superclass method manifest (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbm.conf`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/picture.conf:42-47`). The live ILBM `DT_Dispatcher()` handles only `OM_NEW`; every other method, including `DTM_WRITE`, is sent to `DoSuperMethodA()`. `IFF__DTM_WRITE()` in `ilbmclass.c` is not referenced by that dispatcher, and `ilbm.conf` does not register it. Therefore `SaveILBM()`, `Save_BitMapPic()` and `WriteBytes()` are unreachable from the selected ILBM DTM_WRITE path; withdrew the associated handle-close, error propagation, allocation, BMHD, padding and 24/32-bit raw-save findings from the detailed report and index. The selected Picture superclass does register `DTM_WRITE` as `DT_Write`; its writer uses the Picture color registers, so the prior EHB claim that pixel colors necessarily lose their half-bright appearance is also unsupported and withdrawn. Retained parser/read-path findings GD5290-GD5294, GD5298 and GD5302, which are reachable through `ILBM__OM_NEW()`. No save or image operation was run; source-only.

Hyperlayers XOR clipping failure caller trace (GD6186 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` through all selected `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` and `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` callers. The helper ignores `XorRegionRegion()`/`XorRectRegion()` and the subsequent `AndRegionRegion()`/`AndRectRegion()` results, then toggles `invisible` and constructs the next cliprect pass (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:389-476`). `XorRegionRegion()` preserves its destination when its temporary allocations fail (`rom/graphics/xorregionregion.c:58-105`); the rectangle wrapper propagates that failure (`xorrectregion.c:52-74`). Thus the second pass may be formed from a region that was never complemented, and the cliprect partition can misclassify or duplicate area. Expanded existing GD6186 to include this path; this is the same unchecked region-operation failure class, not a separate ID. `basicfuncs.c` already has focused review evidence, so no whole-body line credit is added. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only.

VESA boot-console takeover caller recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-23): traced the two `RawPutChar(0x03)` sites in `vesaDoRefreshArea()`/`ClearBuffer()` through the selected bitmap `UpdateRect`/scroll and display `Show` methods (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_bitmapclass.c:159-161,214-216`; `vesagfx_displayclass.c:188-218`). Both normal display paths hold `framebufferlock` while the first takeover and `HWData.owned` update occur; initial `initVesaGfxHW()` clearing is before the HIDD is published. Thus duplicate takeover through these normal callers is serialized. The separate registered `ResetHandler()` calls `ClearBuffer()` without that lock (`vesagfx_hiddclass.c:25-35`). The subsequent reset-path recheck establishes the selected ExecSMP cross-CPU overlap and is recorded as GD6316. No screen, reset, or framebuffer operation was run; source-only.

VESA reset-callback framebuffer race added as GD6316 (2026-10-23): traced registration/disposal in `VESAGfx__Root__New/Dispose()` (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_hiddclass.c:45-74,83-89`) to Exec `ShutdownA()`/`ColdReboot()` and `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()` (`rom/exec/shutdowna.c:58-60`; `coldreboot.c:51-53`; `doresetcallbacks.c:65-184`). In the non-supervisor path, callbacks run serially in a support task; this does not stop tasks on other CPUs. The selected x86-64 PC package includes VESA and supports an ExecSMP target (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:63-75`; `configure.in:1650-1670`). Therefore a cross-CPU display update can overlap the reset callback's unlocked `ClearBuffer()` even though ordinary Show/UpdateRect paths share `framebufferlock`. This establishes the unsynchronized clear/draw overlap and the conditional inconsistent framebuffer consequence; GD6316 records it with medium confidence for any lasting visible effect because reset is underway. No reset, screen update or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

Hosted X11 and WinGDI input-registration caller reconciliation (GD6317 added and expanded, 2026-10-23): traced the selected MinGW32 package and complete `gdi_Startup()` setup/failure path (`arch/all-mingw32/boot/mmakefile.src:9-13`; `startup.c:66-93`) against the legacy input wrapper and selected keyboard/mouse class manifests (`rom/hidds/input/include/input.h:102-134`; `rom/hidds/kbd/keyboard.conf:25-37`; `rom/hidds/mouse/mouse.conf:29-48`). WinGDI constructs `CLID_HW_Mouse`, whose hierarchy exposes `HW_Input` and `HW` but not `Hidd_Input`, then calls the consumer-side legacy registration wrapper. X11 constructs `CLID_Hidd_Kbd/Mouse` consumers but calls `HW_AddDriver()`, whose `IID_HW` method is absent on that hierarchy (`rom/hidds/hidd/hiddclass.conf:55-100`; `rom/hidds/kbd/keyboard.conf:1-13,25-37`; `rom/hidds/mouse/mouse.conf:1-14`). the dispatcher finds no requested-interface bucket and returns zero (`rom/oop/metaclass.c:752-800`), so both normal paths abort before display registration; WinGDI also calls the consumer-side remover on `CLID_HW_Kbd` in its keyboard rollback. Added GD6317 and its index entry. No source body lines were newly credited; caller closure for these hosted startup paths is recorded, while broader platform/runtime review remains open. No build or startup was run; source-only.

GD6317 WinGDI rollback consequence expansion (2026-10-25): rechecked the exact class interfaces and registration order after detailing the report entry. `CLID_HW_Kbd` and `CLID_HW_Mouse` both derive from `CLID_HW_Input` (`rom/hidds/kbd/keyboard.conf:25-37`; `mouse.conf:29-48`); `InputHW__HW__AddDriver()` injects the normal event callback and consumer list before calling the generic hardware registry (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:204-237`). Therefore WinGDI's first `HW_AddDriver(kbd, ...)` can register its keyboard object; its next legacy `HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver(ms, ...)` uses an `IID_Hidd_Input` method on the wrong hierarchy and fails. The subsequent legacy remover is likewise sent to the wrong receiver and does not unlink the prior keyboard driver. Expanded GD6317 to state the stranded registration without assuming how the failed module loader handles class-code lifetime. X11's exact mismatched calls are `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/startup.c:75-77`. No startup or rollback was run; no code-line credit change; source-only.

WAV common G.72x decoder and block-boundary recheck (GD6318 added; 2026-10-23): re-read all 275 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `g72x/g72x.c` and traced `SetupG72x()` through `ConvertWAVE()`, `DecodeBlocks()`, `DecodeG72x()`, the G.721 decoder and `bitpack_read_msb()`. SDL event-batch focus-state follow-up (GD6357 added; GD2620 retained, 2026-10-23): reread the complete 108-code-line `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c` worker and the selected mouse HIDD event callback. The `active` flag is initialized to true inside each VBlank loop iteration, while focus-loss state is only applied to mouse events in the same `SDL_PeepEvents()` batch. A later poll therefore forwards mouse motion/button input even if the SDL window remains unfocused, on host backends that report such events. Added GD6357 with that host-delivery condition; this is independent of GD2620's stale stack-local interrupt node after failed startup. Wanderer view-settings aligned-offset width follow-up (GD3069 expanded; arithmetic corrected 2026-10-26): re-read import, export, the standard Workbench/Drawer row construction, the type-0 image-spec change hook, and Zune's `MUIA_Imagedisplay_Spec` duplication path. The four-byte-aligned `strlen(spec)+1` offset reaches 256 at a 252-character spec and wraps to zero when stored in `UBYTE` in both parser and exporter. Recounting the selected non-`DEBUG_MULTLINE` type-0 export path gives 17 tags (136 bytes), not all 20 slots in the fixed-capacity tag array; export allocates those 136 bytes at wrapped offset zero, then `sprintf()` writes the 253-byte NUL-terminated spec, 117 bytes past the allocation. `DEBUG_MULTLINE` adds two tags but does not make the allocation large enough. A <=1,024-byte imported view-settings payload can set the long spec and trigger the selected Save path; import option decoding also uses the wrapped offset. Restored the detailed GD3069 report entry and corrected its arithmetic. This extends existing `wpeditor.c` body credit; no new body-line credit or runtime reproduction. Source-only.

Traced page-table invalidation through `MakeTableInvalid()` and `MarkPage()`, then checked the selected handler manifest and callers. In `__AROS__` builds, `MakeTableInvalid()` leaves local `TableStart` unassigned because its only assignment is excluded by the conditional, then passes it to `MarkPage()`; `MarkPage()` dereferences descriptors derived from that address. The ordinary replacement path can choose `PT_TABLE` frames. A second selected path is a requested frame removal: `HandlePageFault()` sends zero-address requests to `RemFrame()`, and `RemFrameFinish()` can select a page-table frame and call the same `MakeTableInvalid()` path (`fault.c:716-725,779-780,817-832`). Its operational trigger remains uncertain because the optional AROS handler has a separate broken address-range initialization (GD9419); the manager launches the page handler before reaching the later NULL-base publication failure, so startup ordering alone does not prove the eviction path unreachable. The VMM app and handler have active Workbench:System aggregate edges (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/mmakefile.src:18-21`; `workbench/system/VMM/mmakefile.src:47-52`). The app must still be launched and the documented AROS paging-range limitation leaves the fault trigger unestablished. Rechecked fault queues, waits and the earlier config-reduction caller; no further independent issue established. This earns full-body credit for `fault.c`; the common VMM handler body set is complete, while optional-target support and hardware/MMU runtime behavior remain open. No VMM build, page fault, disk I/O, lock, eviction, frame-removal request or MMU operation was run; source-only.


## AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` fallback HIDD (local source/header pass complete; lifecycle and hardware review open)

The AArch64 Raspberry Pi package includes `fbgfx` in its HIDD package list and describes it as the fallback framebuffer driver when `vcgfx` declines the board (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`). The selected module manifest builds five C translation units; `cloc 2.06` reports 604 C code lines. The five local headers add 137 code lines. All 741 local C/header code lines were read in full, and the config and module/package manifests were checked. Traced `FBGfx_Init()` and AddDisplayDriver registration into graphics.library's queued boot-driver replay, the graphics HIDD's nested display construction, bitmap visibility and refresh calls, reset callback registration/removal, and selected Exec/OOP implementations. Added GD9392 for cleanup removing the reset callback before it is registered on display-construction failure. Firmware framebuffer validity, display-mode/runtime behavior, pixel-format hardware semantics and allocation-failure execution remain unverified; this is not a Graphics/Desktop completion claim. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` returned-depth contract recheck (GD9421 added; 2026-10-24): traced the firmware's framebuffer allocation response through boot-tag publication, native kernel storage, `KrnGetSystemAttr()` and the selected fallback HIDD. `vcfb_init()` accepts a nonzero returned depth and passes it through `KRN_FrameBufferDepth`; `initFBGfxHW()` ignores that attribute and hardcodes 32-bit/4-byte pixels. The display mode advertises that hardcoded format, while `fbDoRefreshArea()` copies four bytes per pixel using the returned pitch. Added GD9421, conditional on firmware returning a depth other than the requested 32; the generated config requests 32, and no supported-board mismatch or exact allocation overrun was established. No framebuffer operation was run. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` UpdateRect contract and caller pass (no additional finding; 2026-10-24): traced the override's `(x,y,width,height)` endpoint construction through the shared renderer and graphics.library callers. The rectangle convention is half-open: selected `UpdateBitMap()` forwards the requested extent unchanged, full bitmap refresh uses `(0,0,width,height)`, and the generic HIDD path intersects with the bitmap's visible rectangle before translating to display coordinates. `fbgfx` applies the equivalent display offset and clips destination coordinates to the physical framebuffer; for in-bounds bitmap updates, clipping adjusts the source origin consistently. Scroll-triggered full refresh likewise uses the bitmap extent. No independent off-by-one or source-edge defect was established for valid in-bounds requests; arbitrary out-of-bitmap HIDD rectangles and actual framebuffer behavior remain untested. No line credit. Source-only.

WAV PCM decoder and selected parser-loop recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-23): re-read the complete selected `wave_pcm.c` body (`SetupPCM()` and `DecodePCM()`; 30 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and traced the `WAVE_FORMAT_PCM` registration through `GetDecoder()` and `ConvertWAVE()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/decoders.c:18-43`; `wave_class.c:294-311,350-414`). `SetupPCM()` rejects zero bit depth and calculates the decoder's byte stride; `ConvertWAVE()` rejects channel counts outside 1..`MAX_CHANNELS` before entering the data loop, derives complete blocks by `chunk.size / blockAlign`, and checks each `Read()` for the requested byte count before decoding. The 8-bit path applies the unsigned-to-signed offset; wider byte-aligned samples select their most-significant byte from little-endian PCM. No independent local decoder/input-loop defect established for supported PCM layouts. This is a recheck only: later entries already close the earlier WAV checkpoint at 1,720 / 1,720 selected C lines across 17 / 17 bodies. Public datatype callers, optional-target package inclusion, and runtime audio behavior remain open. No WAV was loaded or decoded; source-only.

SAGA boot-time input-device request and CPU-variant caller pass (GD9404 added; 2026-10-23): followed `SAGA_Init()`'s Shift-override probe through `OpenDevice()` and the selected `input.device` Open vector (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/sagagfx/sagagfx_hw.c:6644-6665`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:94-116`; `rom/devs/input/input.c:84-101`). Reconciled this against the Amiga m68k configure path: its minimum CPU is 68000 but `--with-cpu` permits later variants, while the SAGA module's suggested 68020 override is commented. Animation task-name collision exact-match recheck (GD9403 retained; 2026-10-23): traced `GenTaskName()`'s candidate into `FindTask()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:113-128`; `rom/exec/findtask.c:64-99`) and then into `FindName()`'s exact `strcmp` comparison (`rom/exec/findname.c:68-82`). `FindTask()` searches ready and waiting lists, plus running and spinning lists on ExecSMP; it does not normalize or suffix-match the candidate. An existing worker with the generated name therefore repeatedly satisfies the collision test while local `id` stays zero. This supports the documented duplicate-basename constructor loop; no independent issue or whole-file body credit resulted. No task or datatype object was created; source-only.

SAGA CPU-configuration boundary recheck for GD9404 (2026-10-23; retained, trigger wording unchanged): traced m68k target configuration through `configure.in:2865-2901,4134-4155`. The common m68k configuration sets the default minimum CPU to 68000 and accepts `--with-cpu`; the chosen CPU selects the matching `ISA_MC<CPU>_FLAGS`, with the compiler flag set defined as `-march=<CPU>` (`configure.in:1341-1347`). The SAGA module inherits target ISA flags and its local `-m68020` override is commented (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/sagagfx/mmakefile.src:1-18`). This confirms that the target can be built for later CPU variants, but the checkout does not explicitly define `__mc68000` for the Amiga target; whether its selected compiler defines that compatibility macro for each `-march` remains compiler/toolchain behavior, so GD9404 correctly scopes the input-device check as conditional. No build or compiler macro probe was run; source-only.

AmigaVideo GD5993 init-result and module-rollback boundary recheck (retained; no new finding, 2026-10-23): traced `AmigaVideo_Init()` from `Init_AmigaVideoClass()` through `AddDisplayDriver()` and `driver_Setup()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/startup.c:23-52`; `rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:263-294`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:326-383`). Recheck found that AmigaVideo expunge callbacks only release attribute bases or do nothing; they do not remove the previously installed VBlank/CIA servers or restore the blitter vector. GD5993 is therefore reinstated with this distinct dangling-interrupt consequence; GD6169 still covers the separate per-driver configuration leak. Confirmed the HIDD is selected in both m68k-Amiga ROM and ordinary module lists (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`) and by its six-source local manifest. No build, OOP allocation failure, driver registration or display operation was run; source-only.

Intuition ScreenBuffer allocation/free ownership and caller census (2026-10-23; GD4763 retained, no new finding): reread `AllocScreenBuffer`, `FreeScreenBuffer` and `CloseScreen`, following caller-provided versus internally allocated bitmap ownership, both `AllocDBufInfo` allocations, cleanup on failed bitmap allocation, the per-screen `RestoreDBufInfo` lifetime, and active-buffer restore before free (`rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c:88-165`; `freescreenbuffer.c:65-112`; `closescreen.c:183-191`). ScreenMode Preferences IFF export candidate recheck (GD6341 confirmed, scope clarified; 2026-10-23): reread the complete `Prefs_ExportFH()` body and its GUI/CLI callers (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/prefs.c:122-198,218-257`; `smeditor.c:233-245`). Traced the selected IFFParse write contract: `WriteChunkBytes()` returns the requested count on success and an error when the DOS stream hook detects a short/error `Write()` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:58-82`; `basicfuncs.c:392-423`; `dosstreamhandler.c:41-49`); `PopChunk()` can also fail during seek, chunk-size write, pad write, or buffered flush (`popchunk.c:53-155`). ScreenMode Preferences IFF import candidate recheck (GD6340 confirmed and trigger tightened; 2026-10-23): reread `Prefs_ImportFH()` with the selected IFFParse `OpenIFF`, `ReadChunkBytes`, `ReadStream` and DOS stream-hook implementations, then followed its GUI and CLI callers. GD6340 OpenIFF-error cleanup recheck (no additional finding; 2026-10-23): traced the valid non-composite top-level input through `OpenIFF()`'s `PopContextNode()` path and `Prefs_ImportFH()`'s `FreeIFF()`/caller `Close(fh)` cleanup (`workbench/libs/iffparse/openiff.c:103-115`; `basicfuncs.c:75-115`; `freeiff.c:45-66`; `prefs.c:108-117,36-47`). Region relative-span boundary and point-query pass (GD9412 added; 2026-10-23): traced the empty-destination fast path of `OrRectRegion()` through WORD rectangle storage and `IsPointInRegion()`'s coordinate translation. A non-evil public rectangle may span more than 32,768 pixels while each endpoint remains a valid WORD; its relative maximum is then narrowed to an unrepresentable positive WORD. On low-16-bit signed narrowing, the resulting inverted local rectangle makes even its left/top endpoint fail the point test. Added GD9412 with compiler behavior and lack of maintained large-dimension callers qualified. `orrectregion.c` and `ispointinregion.c` already have full-body credit; this adds no new body-line credit. Wider region-operation semantics, other producers, external callers, and selected compiler conversion behavior remain open; no region or point query was run. Source-only.

Region-span sibling API reconciliation (GD9412 expanded; 2026-10-23): extended the prior empty-region `OrRectRegion()` boundary trace to `XorRectRegion()` and `XorRectRegionND()` (which directly store the relative rectangle span in WORD fields) and `OrRectRegionND()` (whose shared band output is normalized through `_TranslateRect`, also storing WORD deltas/endpoints). Kept the concrete `IsPointInRegion()` false-negative example scoped to `OrRectRegion()` on an empty destination. The methods share the same accepted-endpoint versus signed-relative-span limit, so this remains one candidate rather than duplicate IDs. No additional line credit; the bodies and helper were previously reviewed. No region operation or point query was run. Source-only.

Intuition WaitPort caller-family census and decorator unload follow-up (GD9413-GD9414 added; 2026-10-23): classified all six direct `WaitPort()` call sites in `rom/intuition`: `sysrequest_intern.c` has the previously traced private requester port/GetMsg consumer; `menutask.c` retains GD5818's unchecked startup port; `screennotifytask.c`'s dedicated task drains its private port; `wbtasktalk.c` uses a stack-local single-waiter reply port; `intuition_misc.c` creates, waits on, dequeues and deletes its private screen-notification reply port; and `decoration.c` waits for its one destroy-message reply. No new WaitPort multi-consumer issue was established in these callers. The decoration path exposed two separate unload problems: queued `int_removedecorator()` mutates/frees the ScrDecorSem-protected list without the semaphore or a reference-count recheck (GD9413), and ignored action-record/reply-port allocation failures suppress destruction of a zero-reference decorator (GD9414). Full repo-wide WaitPort caller inventory remains open; this is Intuition-only caller coverage. No port, screen, task, or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.


ScrollRegion NULL-rectangle contract correction (GD9415 added, 2026-10-23): revisited the earlier no-finding conclusion against `IsPointInRegion()`'s absolute-bounds check plus relative-rectangle lookup (`rom/graphics/ispointinregion.c:51-70`). `TranslateRect(Bounds(region), dx, dy)` shifts the represented pixels by changing the origin; it does not clip the translated pixels to the saved original bounds. The API comment explicitly says NULL uses the region bounds as the rectangle (`scrollregion.c:28-37`), and the explicit-rectangle branch clips translated contents back to its rectangle (`:68-88`). Corrected the prior ledger claim that bounds-only translation was consistent. Direct caller census found only `MoveRaster()` and it passes a non-NULL rectangle (`gfxfuncsupport.c:861`), so the candidate is limited to external/public NULL-rectangle calls. Added GD9415; no region or caller was run. Source-only.

Animation and tapedeck are selected through active `workbench-datatypes-complete` edges (`workbench/classes/datatypes/mmakefile:4-21`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/mmakefile.src:6`; `workbench/classes/gadgets/tapedeck/mmakefile.src:9`). Intuition converted cursor allocation-failure caller recheck (GD5824 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()` through the selected `AllocBitMap()` failure return and `BltBitMap()` implementation. Generic software cursor save-under failure recheck (GD9417 added, 2026-10-23): traced `cursor_AllocBackup()` through `Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()`, the `cursor_Draw()` guard, Intuition's pointer-shape method, and LinuxFB's selected class definition. When the target/PixFmt are valid but backup `AllocVec()` fails, the setter ignores FALSE and returns TRUE after replacing the cursor image; `cursor_Draw()` immediately returns on the missing backup. LinuxFB subclasses `CLID_Hidd_Display` and does not override `SetCursorShape`, so the generic implementation is inherited (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:43-60`). Added GD9417 for accepted-but-invisible cursor state on this allocation failure. Other HIDD descendants and the pointer-dimension size limits remain to be reconciled. No allocation failure or cursor operation was run; source-only.


Generic software cursor dimension/allocation bounds pass (GD9418 added, 2026-10-23): traced HIDD bitmap dimensions through `PointerClass__OM_NEW()` and `AllocSpriteDataA()` to the generic display cursor setter, ARGB extraction and save-under use. The public `AllocSpriteDataA()` path also accepts ULONG `SPRITEA_Width` without a cursor-size maximum, allocates the HIDD output bitmap at that width, and passes it through `ChangeExtSpriteA()` to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorShape()` (`allocspritedataa.c:85-95,141-167,240-253`; `changeextspritea.c:60-88`). i386 `IPTR` is unsigned 32-bit. For 65,536 × 16,385 pixels, the ARGB and 4-byte save-under products each wrap from 4,295,229,440 to 262,144 bytes. The HIDD GetImage call’s signed WORD width prevents asserting that the ARGB extraction writes all source pixels; the independent framebuffer save-under write is the supported overrun. Confirmed the selected i386-PC package includes VESAGfx and its display class inherits the generic `SetCursorShape()` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75-79`; `rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx.conf:27-43`). VESA routes non-displayable friends of its bitmap class to generic ChunkyBM (`vesagfx_displayclass.c:150-167`), whose backing allocation is `height * bytesperrow` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:65-78`); the stated 8-bit pointer bitmap/output each requires about 1.07 GB, representable on i386 if sufficient memory is available. Added GD9418, qualified on a very large source bitmap and available memory. No large bitmap or cursor operation was created; source-only.


GD9418 HIDD `GetImage` dimension-type correction (2026-10-23): the generic image method's width/height are signed `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:525`; `gfx_bitmapclass.c:2632-2633`), so the earlier note's 65,536-pixel example does not establish a full-dimension write by `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` during ARGB extraction. Corrected GD9418 to rely on the independent save-under path: the cursor retains the original IPTR width/height, `cursor_AllocBackup()` allocates the wrapped `width*height*bpp` size, then `cursor_Draw()` calls GetImage with the clipped framebuffer rectangle (e.g. 640×480, representable as WORD), which writes 1,228,800 bytes into a 262,144-byte backup for the stated 32-bpp/dimension case. No runtime operation was performed; source-only.


GD5743 failed-scaler caller and output-state follow-up (2026-10-23): expanded the previously summary-only report after tracing `AllocSpriteDataA()`'s BMF_CLEAR destination through `BitMapScale()`'s void HIDD dispatch and the generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__BitMapScale()` three-buffer setup (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:242-253`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:454-459`; `rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:125-131,211-220`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4937-4965`). Scaler setup/scratch allocation failure returns without populating the cleared bitmap, but the sprite is still returned; selected PointerClass accepts that result and creates a shared pointer (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:103,119-149`). The default pointer palette leaves index 0 transparent (`:128-139`), supporting a blank pointer consequence. No allocation failure or pointer was induced; source-only.
Workbench Edit public-port sender follow-up (GD5184 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced the second-instance `find_janoed()` path from `FindPort(JANO_PORT)` through private reply-port allocation and `PutMsg()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:437–456`), against `close_port()` and normal cleanup (`:495–500`). This is the same borrowed-public-port lifetime defect already identified for Preferences Editor senders: owner cleanup removes/frees the port, while a client may be preempted between lookup and enqueue; queued-message draining cannot cover a sender not yet enqueued. No IPC or shutdown overlap was induced; source-only.
Workbench Edit `send_pref()` public-port lifetime cross-check (GD5184 expanded, 2026-10-23): followed `send_pref()` from `FindPort(JANOPREFS_PORT)` through request copy, `PutMsg()` and private reply wait (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:479–493`), then classified its selected callers. `setup_winpref()` issues `CMD_SHOW` (`Prefs.c:529`), while `CloseMainWnd()` issues `CMD_KILL` (`Gui.c:579–581`). The target handles `CMD_KILL` by closing its window and replying, not deleting the public port (`workbench/prefs/Editor/PrefsPort.c:121–128`; `JanoPrefs.c:341–360`); therefore that command alone is not a shutdown trigger. Updated GD5184's detail; no separate finding. No IPC or shutdown overlap was induced; source-only.
GD9401 BltTemplate direct-caller closure recheck (2026-10-23): traced all maintained direct C callers (`rom/graphics/text.c:381-388`, `rom/graphics/bltpattern.c:115-189`, `workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:290-306`) and compared coordinate/size derivation. The normal Font Manager glyph-builder target is its private bitmap, with accepted output dimensions strictly below 32,000 (`fontbitmap_class.c:152-156`), so this caller does not establish the endpoint-crossing case. `Text()` does: its template-based renderer forwards the RastPort cursor plus glyph extent and the measured raster width without clipping the request first (`text.c:381-388`); a WORD cursor at 32,000 and a 125-character 8-pixel fixed-font string yield a 1,000-pixel request crossing `WORD_MAX`, while the visible prefix remains in range. Whether the narrowed maximum becomes negative depends on implementation-defined signed-`WORD` conversion; no selected compiler result was checked, so the report now states this dependency explicitly. Expanded GD9401's maintained-caller evidence and affected scope; no new ID. `BltPattern()` callers remain constrained by their own pattern/source-derived geometry in the checked paths. No text draw, bitmap allocation, or graphics operation was run; source-only.

GD9401 bitmap-to-RastPort GELS caller closure (2026-10-24): traced `AddVSprite()` through `_ValidateIntVSprite()` and the `DrawGList()` Bob/VSprite renderer (`rom/graphics/addvsprite.c:54-67`; `rom/graphics/gels_internal.c:101-123`; `rom/graphics/drawglist.c:146-166`). The public fields are signed WORD `X`/`Width`, and GELS documents/uses `Width` as words; a positive width of 63 therefore builds a 1008-pixel backing bitmap and reaches either bitmap-to-RastPort wrapper with `xDest = VSprite.X` and `xSize = 1008`. At `X=32000`, that request crosses the signed-WORD right endpoint while retaining a visible prefix. No AddVSprite-side width or coordinate clamp precedes the draw call. This establishes a maintained caller path for the existing GD9401 condition, subject to the same implementation-defined narrowing behavior already called out; no new finding ID. The generic draw and mask wrappers share the pre-clipping endpoint construction, so the Bob `ImageShadow` branch is also covered by this caller trace. No VSprite, Bob, bitmap or render was created; source-only.

GD9401 Intuition `DrawImageState()` caller-family check (2026-10-24): inspected the planar-image branch and its selected bitmap blit (`rom/intuition/drawimagestate.c:187-211`) against the public `struct Image` layout (`compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:744-757`) and all maintained direct C call sites. The path forwards `leftOffset + image->LeftEdge` and `image->Width` to `BltBitMapRastPort()`; both are signed WORD fields, so it can reach the same endpoint-narrowing wrapper condition when the destination is near the signed coordinate limit. This is consistent with GD9401 and adds no independent mechanism. The call-site census found ordinary gadget, menu, requester, and frame rendering users, but did not establish a checked-in instance with the required near-limit destination; the demonstrated `Text()` and GELS callers remain the concrete maintained examples. Boopsi-image drawing, external `DrawImageState()` clients, and actual high-coordinate rendering remain open. No image was drawn; source-only.

VMM GD9629 active-paging reachability qualification (2026-10-24): re-read `AllocAddressRange()` and its selected startup callers after the full `fault.c` pass. In AROS builds, the function's `#else` only emits a TODO and returns `SUCCESS` without assigning `VirtAddrStart` or `VirtAddrEnd` (`workbench/system/VMM/mmu_table.c:908-929`); later managed-region publication dereferences the resulting NULL base (`VM_Manager_Init.c:742-780`). A follow-up sequencing check found that `Init_VM_Manager()` launches and waits for `PageHandler` before that publication (`VM_Manager_Init.c:701-711`; `:88-130`); the page handler installs its trap handler before reporting successful initialization (`workbench/system/VMM/pagehandler.c:114-176,535-570`). Therefore the eventual startup failure does not prove that page-fault activity is impossible in the interval. The uninitialized `TableStart` remains definite, while whether AROS reaches a `PT_TABLE` eviction before the later NULL dereference is uncertain. The detailed report now says so. No extra finding or body-line credit; no handler was built or started.

VMM AROS address-range startup caller pass (GD9419 added, 2026-10-24): rechecked the AROS conditional in `AllocAddressRange()` through `Init_VM_Manager()`, `InitPageHandler()`, support-task launch, and managed-memory publication. Confirmed the function's only assignments to `VirtAddrStart`/`VirtAddrEnd` are excluded by `#if !defined(__AROS__)`, but the AROS branch returns `SUCCESS`; `VirtAddrStart` is zero-initialized with no other assignment, and the later `VirtAddrEnd` assignment is derived from that zero base. The page handler consequently indexes `RootTable` from address zero and calls `MarkAddress()`, whose implementation is compiled out on AROS but still returns `SUCCESS`. On the manager's later publication path, the standard-starter branch calls `AddMemList()` with base NULL (whose selected implementation immediately dereferences it), while the library-start branch writes through `VirtMem == NULL`. Since the page handler is launched and reports initialization before managed-region publication, the eventual failure does not prove that it cannot handle faults in the interval (see GD9629). The VMM target is optional and its aggregate edge is disabled; the path requires the target to build and reach this startup stage. No handler, memory map, or page table was run or modified; source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi fbgfx reset-callback failed-construction cleanup recheck (GD9392 detailed, 2026-10-24): traced `FBGfx__Root__New()` through nested display construction and its failure Dispose call, then compared callback registration with `FBGfx__Root__Dispose()`. The reset interrupt is registered only after the nested display exists; failed nested construction instead disposes the outer object, whose unconditional `RemResetCallback()` reaches `Remove()` on the reset node before it was linked. Exec OOP root allocation clears the instance (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-120`), so both list links are NULL; `Remove()` dereferences `ln_Pred`/`ln_Succ` without membership validation (`rom/exec/remove.c:51-62`). Confirmed the AArch64 Raspi package includes `fbgfx` as the fallback after `vcgfx` declines the board. Expanded GD9392 with this direct cleanup consequence and package scope. No allocation failure or object construction was induced. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi fbgfx returned-depth/pitch consequence qualification (GD9421 detailed, 2026-10-24): followed the actual firmware-returned `fb_depth` and pitch from `vcfb_init()` into the kernel attributes and `initFBGfxHW()`. The HIDD ignores the returned depth, hardcodes four-byte pixels, and `fbDoRefreshArea()` copies `w * 4` bytes per row while advancing destination rows by firmware pitch. The checked-in boot config requests depth 32; no supported-board mismatched response was established. Narrowed GD9421's memory-overrun consequence to incompatible layouts with `pitch < width * 4`, while retaining the unconditional hardcoded-format assumption and conditional trigger. No framebuffer or firmware operation was run. Source-only.

CyberGraphX no-match result contract recheck (GD5747 retained; 2026-10-24): reconciled the API's `NULL if there are none` result comment with the constructor's allocate-before-enumeration/unconditional-return path (`workbench/libs/cgfx/alloccmodelisttaglist.c:53-57,129-135,172-235`). The only maintained reference outside the implementation is the direct m68k-emulator ABI thunk, which returns the pointer unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:368-373`); `FreeCModeList()` accepts an empty initialized list and safely frees it (`workbench/libs/cgfx/freecmodelist.c:40-62`). `SetRegion()` and rectangle-list allocation-failure recheck (2026-10-24; GD4662/GD6181 retained, no new finding): reread the complete `_LinkRegionRectangleList()` failure path and `SetRegion()` caller. Raspberry Pi VideoCore shared bitmap palette-fallback caller recheck (GD9420 added; 2026-10-24): corrected the prior note that treated the selected truecolor display mode as closing all palette behavior. The on-screen framebuffer is truecolor, but `VideoCoreGfxOffBM::New()` also accepts displayable/friend bitmap requests and, with GPU placement disabled, zeroes `BitmapData` before returning its ChunkyBM-backed object. Its shared `SetColors()` method delegates to the generic superclass and then range-checks against the still-zero `data->bpp`; valid palette updates above entry zero therefore report FALSE after mutating the generic colormap. Added GD9420 with the `AllocBitMap()` internal caller qualification: it issues one-entry calls and ignores the status, while direct HIDD clients can observe the false failure. No separate palette-memory corruption was established because the selected offscreen path has `VideoData == NULL` and does not use the subclass cmap cache. Full body credit remains 276 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; no palette or bitmap operation was run. Source-only.


VideoCore `SetColors()` direct-caller census for GD9420 (2026-10-24): repository-wide `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` search found five maintained C call sites. `AllocBitMap()`, `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`, the generic display colormap-copy helper, Intuition pointer-color initialization, and SDL framebuffer copy-back all discard the returned Boolean. The internal caller paths therefore do not demonstrate a visible error response to GD9420; only direct HIDD clients that inspect the documented result can observe the false failure after colormap mutation. No new root cause or line credit. Source-only.

MUI ARexx argument-buffer lifetime check (2026-10-24; no additional GD): checked whether freeing the temporary input string before `CallHookPkt()` leaves parsed string arguments dangling. DOS `ReadArgs()` copies `RDA_Source.CS_Buffer` into its own `strbuf` (`rom/dos/readargs.c:453-466`) and returns string argument pointers into that owned result storage (`:620-624,804-868`); the MUI hook runs before `FreeArgs(rdargsret)` releases it (`application.c:1746-1759`; `rom/dos/freeargs.c:50-64`). Thus freeing the original `arguments` buffer at `application.c:1749` does not invalidate parsed strings. No ownership finding added. This verifies only that lifetime concern; remaining `application.c` code and callers stay open.

MUI Area background-spec replacement failure-path check (2026-10-24; no additional GD): traced `MUIA_Background` replacement in `Area__OM_SET()` through `zune_image_spec_duplicate()`, old-spec/resource cleanup, `zune_imspec_setup()`, show, and draw (`classes/area.c:482-521,1338-1377`; `imspec.c:463-572,719-743`). If duplication fails, the old spec and initialized image are retained. If runtime setup fails after a successful replacement, the new spec remains and `mad_Background` becomes NULL; `zune_imspec_show()` and cleanup accept NULL, while the draw method falls back to `MUIM_DrawParentBackground` when there is no image. This is graceful loss of the selected background under allocation/setup failure, with no distinct correctness defect established by these paths. The `area.c` row remains targeted-only; this check is not whole-body credit.

# Hyperlayers visibility-query failure follow-up (GD6186 expanded; no new ID; 2026-10-24)

Traced `IsLayerHiddenBySibling()`'s bounding-box prefilter and region query (`rom/hyperlayers/islayerhiddenbysibling.c:79-96`) against `SetRegion()` and `AndRegionRegion()` failure semantics (`rom/graphics/setregion.c:46-82`; `rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:53-87`). MUI Group 2D min/max allocation and layout caller pass (GD9438 revised; 2026-10-24): traced `group_minmax_2d()` allocation/free/early-return behavior through `Group__MUIM_AskMinMax()`, `Group__MUIM_Layout()`, `group_layout_2d()` and its array-null guard (`group.c:1740-1753,1853-1959,2701-2707,2819-2855`). MUI Group Setup rollback and selected Window failure-caller pass (GD9439 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced Group superclass Setup into `Area__MUIM_Setup()` and the child-failure cleanup loop (`group.c:1027-1079; area.c:1526-1595`), then followed failure through WindowOpen and `Window__MUIM_Cleanup()` (`window.c:3757-3772,4046-4059`). Area Setup publishes `muiRenderInfo`, creates configured Area background resources, registers its event-handler node with the Window, and sets `MADF_SETUP` before Group attempts child Setup. On a child FALSE return, Group cleans only earlier children and omits Cleanup on itself; Window failure cleanup releases shared render-info resources but does not clean the root or clear the Window handler list. Area Cleanup is the only traced path that clears the flag/pointer, removes Area handlers, and releases Area setup backgrounds (`area.c:1601-1645`). Expanded GD9439: those Area obligations survive the failed open; on retry, Setup can repeat before matching cleanup, with resource replacement/leak effects conditional on configured resources and child behavior. Read `DoSetupMethod()` to confirm it assigns the render-info pointer then dispatches Setup without an already-setup guard (`support.c:72-78`), and Window event-handler registration/removal (`window.c:3992-4020`). Repeated-open effects remain source-inferred; exact list behavior on re-enqueue was not promoted. Other Group lifecycle paths and concrete resource-bearing caller configurations remain open; targeted slice only, no full-body credit. No failed Setup or Window open was induced; source-only.

MUI Group row-count allocation-boundary, allocator and caller pass (GD9441 rechecked; 2026-10-24): traced `MUIA_Group_Rows` from its public LONG declaration and constructor storage through empty-group grid derivation, unchecked `rows * sizeof(layout2d_elem)` allocation and the indexed row pass (`group.h:93-94`; `group.c:380-383,1714-1753,1587-1634`). Confirmed 32-bit `ULONG`/`size_t`, the 12-byte record on four-byte-alignment ABIs, and that `AllocVec` accepts a nonzero wrapped small size (`exec/types.h:38-43`; `aros/systypes.h:24`; `rom/exec/allocvec.c:52-73`). Specified the empty-Group value 715,827,883 (`0x2AAAAAAB`): multiplying by 12 wraps to a four-byte `mui_alloc()` request; AllocVec reserves four additional header bytes, leaving four user bytes, while the first row pass writes `row_infos[0].weight` at offset eight. Rechecked that the value is representable by the LONG tag and the constructor stores it as ULONG. Searched checked-in Workbench C/header sources for setters/call sites; only the implementation, declarations and convenience macros were found, so no maintained in-tree trigger is claimed. The failure depends on the stated 32-bit ABI, a public/custom client supplying the large row count, and the tiny allocation succeeding. No object construction or allocation was performed; source-only.

MUI String selection-range width pass (GD9445 rechecked; 2026-10-24): traced `ULONG` `NumChars`/`BufferPos`/`MarkPos` and the configurable `MUIA_String_MaxLen` into `Buffer_GetMarkedRange()` and `Buffer_KillMarked()` (`classes/string.c:60-65,363-413,424-462`; `string.h:38-39`). This is a focused caller check only; broader direct removal callers remain open. No MUI event or object replacement was run; source-only.

MUI legacy Application Input handler-mask recheck (GD5083 strengthened; 2026-10-24): compared `Application__MUIM_Input()` with `Application__MUIM_AddInputHandler()` and the `NewInput` callback gate (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1504,1564-1586,1826-1835,1861-1889`) and the public node layout/flag definition (`application.h:315-339`). GD2719 async-layout startup failure caller-path recheck (2026-10-24): traced the generic `DoAsyncLayout()` helper and its ASCII, binary, HTML, and picture subclass callers. The helper initializes `retval=FALSE`; if `AllocVec(LayoutMessage)` fails or `CreateNewProc()` fails, it frees any message, clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT|DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC`, and returns FALSE (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:146,172-213`). It does not send `DTA_Busy=FALSE` on either failure; that notification is in `AsyncLayouter()` after a worker actually runs (`:83-94`). Each of the four subclass GM_LAYOUT handlers notifies DTA_Busy TRUE before `DoAsyncLayout()` (`ascii/asciiclass.c:169-180`; `binary/binaryclass.c:175-191`; `html/htmlclass.c:357-373`; `picture/pictureclass.c:848-858`). Their superclass `datatypes.class` GM_LAYOUT sets `retval=TRUE` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/class.c:411,890-934`), and subclasses add the helper's FALSE result, so the dispatch still returns success while busy remains set and no layout runs. Retained GD2719, high-confidence source candidate for allocation or process-creation failure in any affected subclass. No failure was induced; module/default aggregate reachability remains configuration-dependent.

GD9520 async worker shutdown/restart flag race (new, 2026-10-24): traced the worker and API state transitions in `workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c`. The worker clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT` under `SEM_ASYNC` and clears `DTA_LayoutProc` before releasing that semaphore (`:58-78`), then releases the object semaphore and performs completion notifications before clearing `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` under `Forbid()` (`:81-100`). A second layout request in this window enters the `DTSIF_LAYOUT`-clear branch because `DoAsyncLayout()` tests only `DTSIF_LAYOUT` (`:152-168`); it sets both flags, creates a second worker and publishes its process pointer (`:170-207`). The first worker then unconditionally clears the shared `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` bit, even though the second worker is active or waiting for `si_Lock`. `RemoveDTObject()` and `DisposeDTObject()` wait only on that bit (`removedtobject.c:68-79`; `disposedtobject.c:53-66`), so they can proceed while the second worker still references the object. The async subclasses in ASCII, binary, HTML and picture call the helper; MultiView's Word Wrap menu issues another `GM_LAYOUT` through `DoLayout(TRUE)` (`main.c:1681-1692`; `misc.c:593-617`). Candidate trigger is a repeated layout request during the worker's exit/notification window. Consequence is an unprotected async reference across remove/dispose, with possible use-after-dispose or task failure. Confidence medium-high from source ordering; no interleaving or runtime was exercised.

GD9520 synchronization-scope recheck (2026-10-25): compared the worker's terminal flag clear with the second worker's `SEM_ASYNC`-protected publication. The prior worker has already released `SEM_ASYNC` before the completion notification and its final `Forbid()`/`DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` clear (`doasynclayout.c:78-100`); the new request sets the same flag while holding `SEM_ASYNC` (`:152-207`). Thus the final clear is not ordered by the semaphore. On single-CPU targets a task switch before `Forbid()` permits the second publication; on ExecSMP, `Forbid()` is explicitly processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-59`) and cannot protect the shared flag from another CPU. The waiters still observe only the cleared bit and can proceed while B's queued/active message retains the object pointer. This strengthens the existing source-level synchronization premise without claiming a reproduced schedule; no new finding ID or body-line credit.


GD9520 maintained repeated-layout caller timing confirmation (2026-10-24): ASCII `GM_LAYOUT` calls `DoAsyncLayout()` and returns its result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:165-181`); successful helper startup only queues the message with `PutMsg()` and returns TRUE without joining the process (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:201-218`). MultiView's `HandleAll()` returns from the Word Wrap case after `DoLayout(TRUE)`, then resumes its outer event loop (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:1299-1306,1681-1693,1770-1772`). Thus a subsequent user layout request can be handled while the asynchronous worker is still in its completion window; the helper's existing in-progress branch is specifically intended to accept such repeated requests. This confirms the caller can overlap layout requests; the narrow exit-window interleaving remains source-inferred and unexercised.

HTML tag/entity length-bound recheck (GD6279 detailed; 2026-10-24): re-read `parse_tag()` and `escape_to_char()` against the table-derived `MAX_Tag_Length`/`MAX_Esc_Length`. Each VLA has `MAX + 1` bytes, while the inclusive `i <= MAX` loop can store `MAX + 1` input characters and then writes the terminator at index `MAX + 1`. A name one character longer than the longest table entry therefore reaches a one-byte out-of-bounds terminator write. Expanded GD6279 with the distinct tag/entity paths and optional HTML-target scope. `parse.c` and `tables.c` already have full-body credit; no line total changed. No input was parsed; source-only.
