GD1731 plain interleaved bitmap allocation/free revalidation (2026-10-24): recomputed the row-stride and total-block arithmetic through AllocBitMap, FreeBitMap, FreeRaster, and the selected Exec MemChunk allocator. For `(sizex,sizey,depth)=(17,5,2)`, the requested block is 30 bytes, rounded to 32; two 20-byte plane spans require 40 bytes, so plane 1's final eight bytes lie outside the allocation. FreeBitMap uses padded width 32 and requests a 40-byte free, rounded to 40 or 48 depending on MEMCHUNK_TOTAL, thus releasing beyond the original 32-byte block. Traced `BltBitMap()` row addressing to the affected plane data. The plain branch requires non-displayable depth <=8 with no HIDD friend; OpenScreen's displayable route is HIDD-backed, and no checked-in caller was established for the plain interleaved route. Expanded GD1731 with this exact public API trigger and scope. Existing allocbitmap.c/freebitmap.c body credit remains unchanged; no bitmap, raster operation, or free was performed. Source-only.

8SVX sample-count wrap candidate re-review (GD6265 confirmed with bounded consequence; 2026-10-24): verified `ULONG` is unsigned 32-bit and traced `vh_OneShotHiSamples + vh_RepeatHiSamples` through BODY comparison, allocation/read, `SDTA_SampleLength` publication, and selected Sound playback length consumers. The addition wraps modulo 2^32; e.g. 0x80000000 + 0x80000001 becomes one, which passes a one-byte BODY check and publishes a one-byte sample while the stored VoiceHeader retains both large counts. Sound playback uses `SampleLength`, establishing truncated-prefix acceptance rather than a sample-buffer overrun. ASCII trailing-CR boundary candidate re-review (GD6267 confirmed with caller scope; 2026-10-24): followed the `buffer[i + 1]` read in `Ascii__DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT()` through both Text superclass buffer paths. `LoadText()` allocates one extra byte and writes a newline sentinel; by contrast `TDTA_Buffer` and `TDTA_BufferLen` setters store the caller's pointer and exact declared length without copying or extending the allocation. Thus an exact-length caller buffer ending in CR reaches a one-byte-past-extent read, while the standard file loader does not. No checked-in exact-length custom-buffer caller was found; kept GD6267 scoped to external clients of the public Text attributes. Consequence is limited to the read and possible fault/adjacent-data-dependent CR handling; no further effect is inferred. No custom buffer or layout was run; source-only.

ASCII empty-file candidate re-review (GD6268 retained at medium confidence; 2026-10-24): traced the zero-size file path through Text `LoadText()` and the subclass `OM_NEW` check. Text accepts size zero, allocates `len+1`, reads zero bytes, writes its newline sentinel at index zero, and returns a non-NULL buffer with length zero. ASCII rejects that pair solely because its condition requires both pointer and nonzero length, reports `ERROR_REQUIRED_ARG_MISSING`, and disposes the otherwise-created object. This confirms the behavioral mismatch; no explicit source contract promises that the ASCII subclass must accept an empty document, so GD6268 is retained as a low-impact, medium-confidence compatibility candidate rather than stated as an unconditional API violation. No file load was run; source-only.

Binary datatype line-allocation abort candidate re-review (GD6269 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): reread the full expected-row calculation, initial line-list replacement, allocation loop and publication path in `binaryclass.c`; traced the resulting actual line list and published total into Text drawing and viewport calculations. The row count is computed from the full input length before construction. An `AllocPooled()` failure sets `abort`, but only the Ctrl-C signal value `bsig` gates completion; with no Ctrl-C, the method writes full `si_TotVert` and publishes full total/cleared busy despite the shorter new list. Old rows have already been removed. Expanded GD6269 with the confirmed full-height/partial-content mismatch and bounded memory-pressure trigger. No allocation failure or UI layout was run; source-only.

Binary datatype large-buffer row arithmetic candidate re-review (GD6270 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced Text's size/addressability gate and optional DOS64 initialization into the Binary row-count, offset-width and iteration arithmetic. `ULONG` is unsigned 32-bit and `LONG` signed 32-bit. For a buffer above 0x7ffffff0 bytes, the rounded row count fits `LONG` but `lines * 16` in each offset-width threshold can overflow signed LONG; the chosen width controls how many high-to-low hex nibbles are written for each row address. For lengths above 0xfffffff0, `bufferlen + 15` wraps before division and undercounts rows; at buffer lengths above 0xfffffff0 the ULONG loop counter can wrap after the final partial row if allocation succeeds throughout. Text permits up to 0xfffffffe bytes when the size is addressable, and the selected Text module optionally opens dos64.library; this requires a 64-bit IPTR build, the DOS64 dependency, and enough memory. Expanded GD6270 with explicit bounds and kept output effects conditional on compiler/runtime behavior. No multi-gigabyte file, layout, or allocation was run; source-only.

PNM dimension-truncation candidate re-review (GD6271 confirmed with concrete Picture copy path; 2026-10-24): reread the PNM header parse, all row decoders and their `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` calls, then traced Picture's first-call source-buffer allocation and row-copy method. PNM parses dimensions in `long`, assigns them without bounds checks to 16-bit `BitMapHeader` width/height, but continues iterating and passing the original dimensions. Picture allocates from the truncated fields and copies the requested width/height without rectangle bounds checks. A P3 width 1/height 65,537 case produces a one-row Picture source allocation, then the second row copy starts at its end. Expanded GD6271 with this caller-to-consumer extent mismatch and exact trigger; other PNM parser findings remain separate. No image or allocation was exercised; source-only.

PNM ASCII-sample candidate re-review (GD6272 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): reread `ReadNextInt()` and the P2/P3 loops through the successful `LoadPNM()` return. is not rejected before `c - '0'`, so the first missing sample returns -49; the loops scale/cast it into RGBBuffer and submit the row without checking stream state. A 1x1 P2 header with MaxVal 255 and no sample stores byte 207 and can complete the Picture write path. P3 applies the same unchecked conversion independently to each missing channel. The non-digit token arithmetic is noted as parser weakness but not promoted to a separate finding here. Expanded GD6272; binary P4/P5/P6 parsing is outside its scope. No file load was run; source-only.

PNM zero-MaxVal candidate re-review (GD6273 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-24): traced `MaxVal` header parsing through every PNM decoder use. The only validation rejects values above 65,535; zero is retained. P2/P3 normalize ASCII samples by dividing by `MaxVal`, and P5 does the same for one- and two-byte samples, so any nonempty input in these formats reaches integer division by zero. P6 does not use `MaxVal` in its pixel conversion and is excluded from this finding. Expanded GD6273 and corrected the master-index summary to name the affected variants. No image was loaded; source-only.

PNM P6 MaxVal candidate re-review (GD6274 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced the accepted MaxVal range into the P6 read/forward path. The header permits 1..65,535, while P6 always reads `Width*3` bytes and sends those unchanged as RGB. Values below 255 are not normalized to the full channel range; values >=256 require two-byte big-endian samples, but the code still reads only one byte per channel and groups the stream as 8-bit RGB. Expanded GD6274 with both supported-range cases and updated the master-index summary. No P6 file was loaded; source-only.

GIF decoder-initialization failure candidate re-review (GD6275 confirmed and separated from decode-result handling; 2026-10-24): traced every `DecodeInit()` return path into its caller and the first decoder consumers. Codec `AllocVec()` failure stores NULL and returns -2; `LoadGIF()` ignores the result and immediately calls `DecodeLines()`, which dereferences `d->eof_code` from that NULL pointer. A short code-size read or out-of-range minimum code size also returns before `init_table()`, leaving the allocated codec fields uninitialized while the caller continues. `DecodeEnd()` is likewise called without checking prior status. Expanded GD6275 with these exact init-failure states and updated the index summary. The subsequent decode-error/full-image publication path remains GD6276 and is not duplicated. No allocation failure or GIF load was induced; source-only.

GIF decode-result and output-extent candidate re-review (GD6276 confirmed and separated from GD6275; 2026-10-24): traced line-buffer allocation, all three decoder status returns, both normal/interlaced Picture-copy paths, and decoder output accounting. `linebuf` is allocated without clearing; `DecodeLines()` can return errors after a partial prefix, and its normal end-code return does not require `linebufbytes == 0`. `LoadGIF()` ignores DecodeInit/DecodeLines/DecodeEnd results and submits the full `width*height` image (or full rows in interlaced mode) to Picture. Confirmed this is separate from GD6275's init failure/invalid codec state. Expanded GD6276 with the incomplete-stream trigger and bounded pixel-correctness consequence. No GIF load or decode was run; source-only.

GIF raw-save result-propagation re-review (GD6277 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `SaveGIF()` from codec initialization through final buffer flush and `DTM_WRITE`. `EncodeInit()` allocation failure leaves `codecvars` NULL and the unchecked call proceeds to `EncodeLines()`; its output-buffer error can also return before the encoder table is initialized. `write_code()` signals subblock write failure, but both encoding loops discard it. The final `SaveGIF_EmptyBuf()` checks `Write()` length but its FALSE result is discarded, after which `SaveGIF()` returns TRUE and the raw method forwards that success. Expanded GD6277 to distinguish the allocation-failure NULL dereference from false success/incomplete file outcomes. No save, allocation failure, or destination I/O failure was induced; source-only.

BitMapScale scratch-allocation failure re-review (GD77 re-established, 2026-10-24): traced the function's planar and generic HIDD dispatch through each local scratch allocation and its public void signature. On planar bitmaps, failure to allocate `LinePattern` jumps to the common return before any scaled pixels are written (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:250-270,396-400`). On generic HIDD scaling, failure of `srcbuf`, `dstbuf`, or `linepattern` makes `BM__Hidd_BitMap__BitMapScale()` return without writing the destination (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4928-4949`); the graphics.library caller cannot observe that status and still calls `update_bitmap()` (`bitmapscale.c:211-220`). `BitMapScale()` returns void (`graphics.conf:155`; `bitmapscale.c:42-48`), so the caller cannot distinguish a completed scale from these allocation exits. Re-established GD77 as a conditional silent no-op / unscaled-destination result on scratch-allocation failure, including generic HIDD scaling; kept separate from GD5743's concrete pointer-construction caller consequence and GD5732's different buffered drawing operations. No allocation failure or scale call was induced; source-only.

ASL file-request multiselect allocation-failure re-review (GD2701 confirmed; 2026-10-24): followed selected-file counting and WBArg construction through the requester event loop to the public result. With `FRF_DOMULTISELECT` set and more than one list item selected, `FRGetSelectedFiles()` allocates room for the counted selections, then advances the output pointer/count only when `VecPooledCloneString()` succeeds (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.c:1802-1857`). A failed selected-name copy is silently skipped; if a prior or later copy succeeds, the method publishes only that subset via `fr_NumArgs = i` (`:1869-1876`). It then unconditionally returns `GHRET_FINISHED_OK` (`:1892`), which the file-request event hook converts to a finished event and `HandleEvents()` converts to TRUE (`filereqhooks.c:1415-1417`; `basicfuncs.c:795-804`); `AslRequest()` returns that success (`aslrequest.c:301-303,331`). `FileRequester.fr_NumArgs/fr_ArgList` are the public selected-file outputs (`compiler/include/libraries/asl.h:61-62`), and checked-in consumers iterate exactly `fr_NumArgs` (`workbench/c/RequestFile.c:179-193`). Confirmed the report summary: a temporary allocation failure while copying one or more selected names can make a multiselect request report success with a partial list. No allocation failure or requester was run; source-only.

ReadPixelArray8 clipped-offset and public-result re-review (GD2662/GD2663 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read `readpixelarray8.c`, the clipping renderer, coordinate macro and vector configuration. `do_render_with_gc()` keeps the array source offsets in signed `WORD` locals and adds the clipped-away x/y distances into them (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:110-121,123-140,169-180`); `rp8_render()` converts those offsets directly into a byte offset from the caller array (`readpixelarray8.c:21-32`; `graphics_intern.h:295-296`). For `xstart=-32768,xstop=0` on a bitmap clipped to begin at x=0, the clipped source offset is 32768 and narrows to -32768; the render therefore starts before the caller array, although the documented allocation formula reserves the full requested width (`readpixelarray8.c:54-68,100-123`). Separately, the implementation accumulates and returns a `LONG` pixel count (`readpixelarray8.c:40,95,123-127`), but the public graphics vector configuration declares the result as `WORD` (`graphics.conf:175`). A fully read 256x128 rectangle returns 32768 from the body, which is not representable in signed WORD, so public callers cannot reliably receive the documented pixel count (`readpixelarray8.c:54-71`; `graphics.conf:175`). Reconfirmed the two distinct issues: the clipped pointer offset is a WORD intermediate in renderer clipping, while the count is a public return-width mismatch. No pixel read, clip operation or ABI build was run; source-only.

DataTypes NewDTObjectA internally obtained reference lifetime re-review (GD2747 confirmed; 2026-10-24): traced each `ObtainDataTypeA()` call in `NewDTObjectA()` through datatype-class open, engine lookup, object construction, returned-object disposal, and datatype replacement. A successful `ObtainDataTypeA()` increments the selected descriptor `OpenCount` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c:213-216`). `NewDTObjectA()` releases it on the explicit GroupID-mismatch paths only (`newdtobjecta.c:183-194,228-238`); after later failures such as datatype-class `OpenLibrary()`, engine lookup, or `NewObjectA()`, the NULL-object cleanup handles the file lock/IFF state but not the acquired DataType reference (`:273-349`). On success, `DisposeDTObject()` calls `DisposeObject()` and closes the datatype class library, while the base `OM_DISPOSE` frees the data handle/name but does not call `ReleaseDataType()` (`disposedtobject.c:53-67`; `class.c:961-1033`). The retained OpenCount is read by Workbench AddDataTypes, which refuses replacement of an existing descriptor when the count is nonzero (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:1024-1034`). Confirmed GD2747 for internally obtained DataTypes passed through successful object lifetime and post-obtain constructor failures; caller-supplied `DTA_DataType` references not acquired by this function are excluded. No object construction, disposal, or datatype replacement was performed; source-only.

DataTypes NewDTObjectA class-library path boundary re-review (GD2749 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-24): traced `DTA_BaseName` from the public datatype tag definition into the local library-name assembly and checked the selected in-tree ScreenGrabber caller. `NewDTObjectA()` accepts the tag at `workbench/libs/datatypes/newdtobjecta.c:131-135`, then copies `"datatypes/"` (10 bytes), appends the base name, and appends `".datatype"` (9 bytes) into `libname[120]` without a length check (`:276-286`). A 100-byte base name fits exactly with its terminator; 101 bytes makes the final terminator land at index 120, one byte past the array. The tag is defined as the datatype class base name (`compiler/include/datatypes/datatypesclass.h:99-100`). The selected ScreenGrabber caller uses the short literal `"png"` (`workbench/tools/ScreenGrabber/main.c:177-181`), so that maintained caller is not affected; the candidate applies to a call supplying a longer base name. A registered `dth_BaseName` also flows into this buffer, but no evidence was found that checked-in descriptors exceed the threshold. Confirmed GD2749 with this qualified source/API trigger. No object construction or long-name call was run; source-only.

DiskFont tagged-list UWORD count wrap re-review (GD2815 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): followed tagged font conversion through both consumers. `ConvDiskFont()` counts each on-disk tag including `TAG_DONE` in a `UWORD`, allocates `numtags * sizeof(TagItem)`, then copies exactly `numtags` entries (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_io.c:402-440`). With 65,536 ordinary tag items plus the terminator (65,537 total), the count wraps to one; the allocation holds one tag and the copy loop omits the terminator. `AllocSegment()` allocates only the requested payload plus segment bookkeeping (`basicfuncs.c:20-39`). In the ordinary open path, `ReadDiskFont()` passes this one-item list to `ExtendFont()`, which clones it by `NextTagItem()` iteration until a terminator (`diskfont_io.c:508-525`; `rom/graphics/extendfont.c:92-103`; `rom/utility/clonetagitems.c:71-84`). In the contents path, `NewFontContents()` calls `ConvDiskFont(..., FALSE)` and then itself walks the list until `TAG_DONE` (`newfontcontents.c:152-167,190-222`). These consumers therefore read beyond the allocated tag payload when the first item is an ordinary tag. The trigger requires a very large tagged font; no valid-file maximum was found in the reviewed parser path. Confirmed GD2815 as a bounded source candidate; no font file was loaded or converted. Source-only.

DiskFont fixed-width filename parser bound re-review (GD2816 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-24): checked the format declaration and every selected `ReadFontDescr()` caller. `MAXFONTPATH` is 256, matching `FontContents.fc_FileName[256]` (`compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:22-27`); the parser's local `strbuf` is 257 bytes (`af_fontdescr_io.c:28-37`). Its byte loop has no 256-byte field limit and continues reading until NUL (`:110-124`). An unterminated filename field therefore causes parsing to consume the subsequent record fields; if no NUL occurs in the one-byte spare slot or following bytes, the loop writes past the local array. The following seek also uses the unbounded length to reposition within the record (`:136-143`). Traced the selected directory enumeration and direct lookup callers (`diskfontfunc.c:93-109,842-846,1345-1348`). Confirmed the missing parser bound as a malformed-descriptor robustness/correctness candidate; valid files are expected to NUL-terminate the fixed-width field, and no valid-file trigger was found. No font descriptor was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont NewFontContents caller filename-size re-review (GD2817 confirmed; 2026-10-24): read `NewFontContents()` from input setup through return and traced the selected Font datatype caller. The routine copies `fontName` into `name[MAXFONTNAME]` with `strcpy()` before validating the `.font` suffix (`newfontcontents.c:97-117`; `MAXFONTNAME` is 32 at `diskfont.h:52`). The Font datatype obtains `Name = FIB->fib_FileName` and passes it through `NewFC()` to `NewFontContents()` (`fontclass.c:197-209`; `otag.c:50-59`); DOS defines that FIB field as 108 bytes (`dos.h:57,81`). Thus a `.font` filename of 32 or more bytes including NUL overruns the 32-byte local array on the selected caller path. Also checked the subsequent directory-basename/child-name concatenation against the FIB field size; its combined maximum remains below the 256-byte `FontContents.fc_FileName` field, so no separate candidate was added there. No long-named file was opened; source-only.

DiskFont NewFontContents backward tag-pack boundary re-review (GD2818 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced allocation, list insertion, tag counting and packing against both ABI layouts. Each item is allocated as `contentsBuffer { Node; FontContents; }` (`newfontcontents.c:32-36,170-171`), then linked before tag packing (`:183-187`). `TagItem` has IPTR-aligned data and is 8 bytes on 32-bit, 16 bytes on 64-bit (`utility/tagitem.h:17-23`); the 256-byte pack endpoint starts at `&tfc_TagCount + 2`, and the start is moved backward by `nTags * sizeof(TagItem)` without a bound check (`newfontcontents.c:195-222`). Including TAG_DONE, 33 items on 32-bit and 17 on 64-bit first overlap Node fields; 34/18 reach the Node list links, and 35/19 start before the `contentsBuffer` allocation (Node size/layout from `exec/nodes.h:31-38`, with the FontContents member following Node). `ConvDiskFont()` supplies the converted tagged list and walks until the file's TAG_DONE (`diskfont_io.c:402-455`). Confirmed the count-dependent write and target-specific thresholds; no tag-count cap was found in the traced conversion path. No font was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont `.otag` tag-buffer end-bound re-review (GD2819 confirmed; 2026-10-24): traced `OTAG_GetFile()` from file-size acquisition through all tag scan/conversion paths and its selected `ReadFontDescr()` caller. It allocates `sizeof(OTagList)+l`, reads `l` bytes into `data`, and checks identifier/embedded size (`bullet.c:77-117`; `OTagList` layout in `diskfont_intern.h:78-83`). On 64-bit, the tag-count pass advances by tag/data pairs until TAG_DONE without comparing against `l` (`bullet.c:125-145`). Both 32-bit in-place conversion and 64-bit conversion read tag data for every non-DONE item and continue until TAG_DONE, also without checking the buffer end (`:154-180`). A matching declared-size field does not ensure a complete pair or terminating tag, so a malformed file can make these loops read past the allocated data; the 64-bit count scan does so before its converted-tag allocation. `ReadFontDescr()` uses this path for OFCH descriptors (`af_fontdescr_io.c:72-95`). Confirmed GD2819 as a malformed/truncated-file parser-bound issue. No `.otag` file was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont `.otag` indirect-offset and consumer-length re-review (GD2820 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): traced indirect relocation from the file read into concrete outline-font consumers. `OTAG_GetFile()` converts `OT_Indirect` data to `otaglist->data + offset` without checking it against the actual `l` bytes (`bullet.c:77-117,154-180`). `ReadFontDescr()` obtains `OT_AvailSizes`, reads the pointed-to count, then reads that many additional UWORD entries without a buffer-end check (`af_fontdescr_io.c:72-85,211-223`). `OTAG_ReadOutlineFont()` obtains `OT_Engine`, calls `strlen()` on the pointer, and copies the value into a library path (`bullet.c:898-920`). The file header size equality does not validate these inner offsets or lengths. Confirmed GD2820 for malformed `.otag` payload bounds; kept distinct from GD2819’s missing tag terminator. No outline font was loaded; source-only.

GD2821 finding wording precision recheck (2026-10-24): the NULL dereference occurs in FreeType’s shared `GetGlyph()` helper, not in `ObtainInfoA()` itself. `ObtainInfoA()` dispatches the two selected glyph-map tag families to that helper; after a nonzero glyph code, `GetGlyph()` stores `AllocVec()` in `ge->GMap`, conditionally renders only on non-NULL, then unconditionally reads `ge->GMap->glm_Width` (`workbench/libs/freetype2/obtaininfoa.c:34-52,94-115`). Corrected GD2821’s report and master-index summary to name the actual dereference site. Existing caller/configuration analysis remains valid; source-only.

GD2823 scaling-divisor example correction (2026-10-24): the earlier `-750..750`, point-size-1 arithmetic example is invalid: `SetInstance()` computes `alt_point = 0` after its integer split (`a=d=0`), so `FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes(face, 0, 0)` returns through the checked error path before `RenderGlyph()` reaches the later divisor. Replaced it with custom bounds `0..1500`, UPEM 2048 and point size 1: `alt_point=1`, `a=1`, `d=0`, so the engine requests one pixel; the later divisor `(x_ppem * corrected_upem) / units_per_EM` is `(1*1500)/2048 == 0` in `glyph.c:285-290`. `GetWidthList()` calls `SetInstance()` first and uses the same integer formula after successful `FT_Load_Glyph()` (`kerning.c:44-47,96-107`). The UI accepts zero and positive bounds and passes these values through the custom bbox tag path; the module remains optional. This supersedes the earlier GD2823 example in this ledger. No font was rendered; source-only.

GD5908 display-info reader/removal and selected consumer recheck (2026-10-24): re-read `FindDisplayInfo()` and `NextDisplayInfo()` in full alongside the `GetDisplayInfoData()` handle path (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:54-84`; `nextdisplayinfo.c:55-93`; `getdisplayinfodata.c:145-176`), and compared them with `display_Expunge()`'s exclusive-lock unlink, OOP disposal and `FreeVec(mdd)` (`graphics_display.c:221-275`). Icon library duplication/layout full-body and failure-cleanup pass (GD9536 added; GD9535 caller evidence retained; 2026-10-24): read the complete `dupdiskobject.c` (311 physical lines; 208 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and `layouticon.c` (637 physical lines; 464 code lines), then traced `FreeDiskObject()`'s layout teardown, `GetIconTagList()` and Wanderer's AppIcon caller. `DupDiskObjectA()`'s ordinary allocation failures reach its `FreeDiskObject()` rollback; no separate duplication-body defect was established. In `LayoutIconA()`, bitmap/pen-map/chunky-buffer/mask allocation failures can occur after screen-specific state has been acquired or allocated, but error exits do not roll that partial state back and leave `ni_Screen` NULL. The mask branch uniquely returns before `FreeScreenDrawInfo()`; the other error exits free DrawInfo but only jump to the common return. `FreeDiskObject()` then calls `LayoutIconA(icon,NULL,NULL)`, which exits at the same-screen fast path and does not free the partial layout allocations; a retry with a screen dereferences the NULL saved screen for `ReleasePen()` if a partial image has a pen map. GD9536 now covers the complete missing-rollback family, with the mask-specific DrawInfo leak called out. Credited 672 full-body C lines. No allocation failure or icon operation was run; source-only.

GetIconTagList full-body and selected Workbench launcher caller pass (GD9537 added; 2026-10-24): read all 361 physical lines / 240 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `geticontaglist.c`, then traced the `FindDefaultIcon()` executable fallback into `GetDefaultIconFromType()` and the selected `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()`/`HandleTool()` decision. The tag is initialized FALSE, but the outer call does not set it when identify fallback returns a `WBTOOL` default icon. The caller branches on that value to choose Workbench versus CLI launch when the icon has no `CLI` tooltype. Added GD9537 with this conditional behavior. Reviewed default selection, file/device lookup, lock/FIB cleanup, error propagation and final layout; did not promote ignored `LayoutIconA()` status separately because an independent API failure contract was not established. Credited 240 full-body C lines. No icon lookup or program launch was run; source-only.

Icon identification full-body and DOS device-name bound pass (GD9538 added; 2026-10-24): read all 720 physical lines / 609 `cloc 2.06` C lines of `identify.c`, then followed root-volume identification through `FindDeviceName()` into `FindDosEntry()` and default-device-icon selection. The sole maintained helper caller passes `TEXT device[MAXFILENAMELENGTH]` (108 bytes), but the helper ignores its `length` argument, copies the full BSTR name, and appends two bytes. `MakeDosEntry()` allocates by input length and stores a BSTR length capped at 255; no 106-byte device-name restriction was found. Added GD9538 for names >=107 bytes when the matched device handler is selected. Also traced the classifier and default-icon paths that return a `WBTOOL` fallback without setting the outer `ICONGETA_IsDefaultIcon` tag; that caller consequence is recorded separately as GD9537. No additional independent issue was promoted from the device-type maps, lock transitions, or FIB cleanup. Credited 609 full-body C lines. No DOS list, root lock, icon lookup, or long device name was exercised; source-only.

GD9538 DOS-list publication recheck (2026-10-25): inspected `MakeDosEntry()` allocation/BSTR construction and `AddDosEntry()` publication (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:55-80`; `rom/dos/adddosentry.c:78-115`). The former sizes storage from the input C-string length and caps only the encoded BSTR length byte at 255; the latter performs duplicate-name checks and links the entry without imposing a name-length limit. This supports the documented >=107-byte trigger for a published DOS device entry, conditional on the matching handler task. The input string itself must still be NUL-terminated and readable through its full length; this source pass does not establish which external device creators permit such long names. No report change or new candidate; `identify.c` already has full-body credit. No DOS entry was created and no root volume was queried; source-only.

OS 3.5 icon reader full-body and raw/encoded payload pass (GD9539–GD9541 added; 2026-10-24): read all 1,078 physical lines / 815 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `diskobj35io.c`, tracing `ReadIcon35()` through FACE/IMAG/ARGB chunk handling, `ReadImage35()`, `Decode35()`, palette publication and `LayoutIconA()` consumption. Added GD9539 for raw-format image/palette byte counts that are not checked against the pixel/entry counts before copy/read. Added GD9540 for ignored RLE image errors and compressed-palette errors converted into a successful read with NULL palette, then followed the latter to the selected palette dereference. Added GD9541 for file-supplied depth 32 or higher reaching a shift count at least the 32-bit `int` width in `Decode35()`; depth 31's signed-shift result is implementation-defined and is not claimed as undefined. The writer emits depth 8; the invalid-depth finding is explicitly limited to nonconforming input. No icon file, IFF operation, allocation failure or layout was run; source-only.

NewIcon reader full-body and decoded palette-index bound pass (GD9542 added; 2026-10-24): read all 252 physical lines / 177 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `diskobjNIio.c`, then followed `ReadIconNI()` from the selected serialization hook through tooltype marker handling and `ReadImageNI()` into `LayoutIconA()`'s palette mapping. `numcols` is used as the pen-map allocation/count while the derived bit width can represent values from `numcols` through the next power-of-two range; `DecodeNI()` accepts and stores those values without a palette-range check. Added GD9542 for the resulting out-of-range pen-map lookup when a decoded pixel uses an unused code. The module enables NewIcon support by default. The separate ignored `DecodeNI()` status return was recorded as incomplete coverage rather than a second finding in this pass. No icon file or layout was run; source-only.

GD4662 empty-destination partial-region rollback and caller pass expanded (2026-10-24): verified `_LinkRegionRectangleList()` saves the original destination tail once and only reclaims an appended suffix when that original pointer is non-NULL. Traced the resulting tail pointer through `SetRegion()` (local `addr` never published on failure), `_CopyRegionRectangles()` temporary-result disposal, `DisposeRegion()`/`_DisposeRegionRectangleList()` tail cleanup, and `OrRegionRegion()` empty-second-operand failure return. Reconciled selected hyperlayers unchecked callers in `DeleteLayer`, z-order helpers, `_ShowPartsOfLayer`, and `_BackFillRegion`; failures can leave snapshots/visibility/damage state incomplete, with rendering consequence geometry-dependent. Expanded the GD4662 report with exact allocation/cleanup flow and caller scope. Corrected a duplicated ID in its master-index label. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only.


Generic HIDD ColorMap count/allocation-wrap candidate revalidation (GD4682 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `aoHidd_ColorMap_NumEntries` from `CM__Root__New()` through the debug-only >256 check, count publication, allocation, SetColors reallocation predicate and GetColor/GetPixel bounds. Confirmed `HIDDT_Color` is 12 bytes (four UWORD components and one ULONG pixel), and on 32-bit size_t the admissible ULONG count 357,913,942 (`0x15555556`) makes the product wrap to 8 bytes. If that small allocation succeeds, the object retains the large logical count and a later one-color SetColors call avoids growth then writes 12 bytes. Confirmed generic gfx HIDD manifest selection and searched all checked-in ColorMap constructors; selected bitmap/P96 call sites use small counts, so trigger remains a direct external/future HIDD client. Expanded the GD4682 report with the concrete wrap, consequence, configuration and caller qualification. No large object or color method was used; source-only.


Radeon line-pattern predicate/caller revalidation (GD4696 expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read the three Radeon DrawLine/DrawRect/DrawPolygon predicates and their hardware branches (`ati_bitmap.c:444-455,538-553,643-655`). In each, `=!` parses as assignment of `!((UWORD)~0)` (zero) to the GC field. Matched the parallel Nvidia methods, which use `!=` at all three corresponding sites. Traced Graphics `Draw()` to `HIDD_BM_DrawLine()` and checked the Radeon module's PPC overlays/package selection; retained optional module scope rather than claiming default boot inclusion. Expanded the GD4696 report with exact operation effects and trigger. No graphics operation or hardware was used; source-only.


Radeon MemList-header expunge candidate revalidation (GD4700 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `BitmapInit()` after card VRAM sizing into publication of `sd->managedMem` on `SysBase->MemList`; verified the header is embedded in ATI static library-base data and its managed-memory callbacks carry `sd` as user data. Radeon timer.device successful-init/expunge lifetime check (GD9603 added; 2026-10-24): traced the successful `ATI_Init()` OpenDevice branch, all `CloseDevice()` occurrences in the Radeon source, timer `DoIO()` helper call sites, and `ATI_Expunge()` through generated module/class teardown. Boopsi `MUIA_Boopsi_Object` getter return-value confirmation (GD9584 retained; 2026-10-24): verified `rom/intuition/getattr.c:70-83` constructs an `OM_GET`, calls `DoMethodA()`, and returns that method result unchanged. Therefore `Boopsi__OM_GET()` writing `opg_Storage` before falling through does not itself make `GetAttr()` successful: the caller receives whichever result the superclass path returns, or a nested gadget result if it recognizes the same ID. The public tag is explicitly get-only (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/boopsi.h:27-28`). No in-tree caller queries this tag, so practical impact remains dependent on external callers checking the documented Boolean result; no query was run.

Boopsi show/hide pairing recheck (no additional lifecycle finding; 2026-10-24): checked the class against Group virtual-scroll and child-visibility transitions. `Group__OM_SET()` calls `Group__MUIM_Hide()` before changing virtual offsets and `Group__MUIM_Show()` after relayout when the group remains drawable (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:638-644`); those methods call `DoHideMethod()`/`DoShowMethod()` on eligible children (`:2896-2946,2949-2990`), and `DoHideMethod()` clears `MADF_CANDRAW` before forwarding while `DoShowMethod()` forwards and sets it only on success (`support.c:79-95`). Thus the Boopsi child disposed in Hide is recreated on the paired Show during this selected transition; the investigated repeated-show leak hypothesis is not supported for this path. Other externally issued lifecycle sequences remain unverified. No GUI or object lifecycle was run.

Volumelist `printSize()` capacity-narrowing pass (GD9604 added; 2026-10-24): read the complete helper and its volume-list callers (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:20-36,180-216`) and reconciled the conditional `InfoData64` fields (`compiler/include/dos/dos.h:176-203`). Both used and free capacities are UQUAD before `printSize()`; after the GiB shift, conversion to `unsigned int` loses all bits above bit 31. Thus values at or above 2^62 bytes (4 EiB) wrap, with exactly 4 EiB formatted as `0G`, provided the block-count multiplication itself remains representable. Added GD9604 with DOS64-only and extreme-capacity conditions; practical volume availability was not established. No volume, formatting call, or display was run; source-only.

Volumelist DOS64 formatter/provider closure (GD9604 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced the optional NTFS `ACTION_INFO` path into `Volumelist__OM_NEW()`: NTFS `total_sectors` and `used_sectors` are UQUAD (`workbench/fs/ntfs/ntfs_fs.h:225-226`), startup loads the boot-sector `number_of_sectors` into `total_sectors` (`ntfs.c:1092`), and `FillDiskInfo()` returns that field as `InfoData.id_NumBlocks` (`disk.c:47-71`). The NTFS module is a standalone `workbench-fs-ntfs` target (`workbench/fs/ntfs/mmakefile.src:5-10`), while Volumelist is conditionally built in or external (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:323-329`). This verifies the caller type path to `printSize()` for wide counts; successful operation on a volume at or above 4 EiB is not established because broader NTFS large-volume behavior was not audited. No volume or formatter call was run; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5993 failed-init interrupt teardown recheck (reinstated and expanded; 2026-10-24): verified `_set_libinit()` calls registered expunge callbacks on InitLib failure (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:64-69`) before genmodule frees the base (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1158-1180`). The AmigaVideo callbacks are `Expunge_AmigaVideoClass()` (attribute-base release only) and `AmigaVideoBM_Expunge()` (no-op); neither reverses `AddIntServer(INTB_VERTB)`, `AddICRVector()`/CIA enable, or `SetIntVector(INTB_BLIT)` done in `initcustom()` before `AddDisplayDriver()` (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1680-1688`; `amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:359-369`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:1915-1950`; `startup.c:34-52`). A failed `AddDisplayDriver()` path such as its `DD_NO_MEM` return (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:181-183`) therefore lets the module base/code be freed while system interrupt registrations still reference `csd` and module callbacks. Reinstated GD5993 for this separate lifetime defect; the earlier compositor-tag failure observation remains only a path to driver-init failure, not a standalone bad-display finding. No init failure or interrupt dispatch was induced; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5994 dummy interlace-list allocation and caller pass (confirmed; 2026-10-24): re-read `initvpicopper()` and both callers. `MakeViewPort()` sets `MaxCount` using a helper that returns at least 2,000 bytes and deliberately clears `CopSStart` for non-interlaced bitmaps. A later VBlank scroll reattachment or compositor stack rebuild can include that bitmap in the interlace list; the helper then allocates `MEMF_CHIP` storage, immediately calls `CopyMemQuick()` with it and derives list pointers without a NULL guard. `CopyMemQuick()` copies positive counts by dereferencing the destination. Confirmed GD5994; impact is limited to the allocation-failure and interlaced mixed-viewport condition, with the VBlank path running from interrupt context. No allocation failure, scroll, compositor rebuild or hardware update was run; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5992 startup chip-allocation failure consequence trace (confirmed; 2026-10-24): calculated the requested block as 16 sprite bytes plus 184 copper bytes (46 UWORD pairs). On `AllocMem()` failure, `sprite_null` is NULL and `copper1` becomes integer address `0x10`; the `COPPEROUT` macro writes pairs through that address before the resulting pointers are stored in `GfxBase` and custom-chip registers and DMA is enabled. `initcustom()` is a `VOID` startup call and has no failure return/rollback. Kept GD5992 separate from GD5993: the former is direct null-derived CPU writes and invalid copper publication on the allocation failure itself; the latter is interrupt-handler lifetime after any later failed module initialization. No allocation failure or hardware access was run; the exact address-mapping effect remains target-specific; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5991 VBlank reveal threshold caller recheck (confirmed and trigger narrowed; 2026-10-24): traced the bitmap position-change notification through `BitMapPositionChanged`/`setscroll` into the VBlank `gfx_vblank_doupdatescroll()` downward-move branch. Reconciled the conditions: `adjust` is assigned only for cross-interlace-mode cases, but a same-mode, higher-priority obscured bitmap can pass `toptmp < topvis`, be attached successfully, and reach `topvis = toptmp - adjust`; the indeterminate threshold can affect later hidden-screen decisions in the same loop. Narrowed the trigger to a successful same-mode reveal followed by at least one more candidate. No scroll or VBlank was run; source-only.

AmigaVideo GD5990 combined-signal and teardown recheck (confirmed; 2026-10-24): verified `DisplayServiceTask()`'s wait mask and exact-value switch against Exec `Wait()`'s returned-and-cleared mask. No task schedule, disposal, VBlank, or redraw was run; source-only.

GD1731 plain-interleaved AllocBitMap caller census recheck (candidate retained, no in-tree trigger established; 2026-10-24): re-searched every source/header `BMF_INTERLEAVED` occurrence and traced all maintained allocation call sites with that flag. `OpenScreen()` begins with `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` and preserves that flag through both bitmap allocation sites (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:156,1236-1238,1286-1302`), so these use the HIDD path. GD5908 runtime display-removal caller recheck (2026-10-24): verified the monitor Wrapper is a maintained dynamic registration path, not only a boot-time driver path. Its CLI accepts `CLASS=HIDD/A,LIBRARY=LIB`; Workbench launch reads those fields from icon tooltypes; when the class is absent it opens the requested library, finds the class and calls `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/wrapper/wrapper.c:35-100`). `graphics_driver.c` supplies the temporary `DDRVA_Handover` to the HIDD constructor, and Nouveau's constructor calls `HIDDNouveauReleaseBootDisplays()` when that tag is present (`:340-352`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:421-440`). Thus on-demand Nouveau registration through Wrapper can remove an inactive boot display while ScreenMode Preferences is querying mode handles, supporting the conditional race already recorded as GD5908. Wrapper is an explicitly buildable target with an optional aggregate edge; this does not establish that every default image ships it. No wrapper, mode query or registration was run; source-only.


## Optional Monitor Editor Preferences target

`workbench/prefs/MonEd/mmakefile.src` selects one C translation unit, `moned.c`, for the explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-moned` target; its edge from the Preferences aggregate is commented out. `cloc 2.06` counts 764 C code lines in the body. Read all 1,044 physical lines plus `moned_globals.h` and `compiler.h`; traced library startup/rollback, monitor copy/restore and icon persistence, CLI timing updates, GadTools/window construction, message dispatch, Jump reopening, and teardown. Added GD9605 for inconsistent OpenDisplay failure returns and unchecked initial/Jump callers; GD9606 for font/visual-info/gadget-list leaks on window-open failure; GD9607 for 32-bit timing-product overflow to a zero divisor from accepted CLI values. `GetVisualInfoA()` returns NULL on allocation failure and `CreateContext()` documents/implements a nullable allocation result (`workbench/libs/gadtools/getvisualinfoa.c:36-57`; `createcontext.c:30-67`). External Intuition/GadTools rendering behavior and runtime allocation/window failures remain untested. No build, GUI, CLI timing update, or allocation failure was induced; source-only.


GD5910 full-detail restoration and range-proof recheck (2026-10-24): matched the index-only GD5910 summary to the current selected bodies. `SetRGB32()` first calls the bounded `SetRGB32CM()` but then unconditionally invokes `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`; that helper calls HIDD `SetColors` and separately indexes the raw bitmap pixeltable using the original ULONG `first + i` without a bound (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53,116-124`; `setrgb32cm.c:61-76`). For displayable HIDD bitmaps, `AllocBitMap()` allocates exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` (256) pixel entries or shares that same table with a friend bitmap (`allocbitmap.c:417-426`; `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`). A request for index 256 therefore passes the ColorMap no-op guard but reaches pixeltable entry 256. `LoadRGB32()`'s normal and allocation-fallback paths both reach the same unchecked setter (`loadrgb32.c:74-103`). Restored GD5910 as a confirmed source-level out-of-bounds write and replaced the report's index-only detail-gap stub. No palette call, bitmap, allocation failure or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


GD2849 build-selection qualification (2026-10-24; no new finding): checked Picture and PNG manifests. `pictureclass.c` is selected by the directly buildable `workbench-datatypes-picture` module. Icon library optional dependency first-open concurrency recheck (GD9608 added; 2026-10-24): re-read the complete `DemandOpenLibrary()` helper and its four optional-library macros in `workbench/libs/icon/icon_intern.h:206-217`, confirmed the `IconBase` fields are initially zero from genmodule's `MEMF_CLEAR` base allocation (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1090`; fields `icon_intern.h:177-180`), and traced the helper into selected datatype-identification callers (`identify.c:89-95,499-505`). The helper has no synchronization around check/open/store, while `icon.library`'s `iconlistlock` is used only for icon-list operations. Concurrent first-use calls that both successfully open the same dependency can overwrite one stored pointer; `Expunge()` closes only that pointer (`icon_init.c:76-89`), leaving an open reference. At that checkpoint, GD9608 brought the active count to 1,732 plus three withdrawn headings; later additions must be counted separately. No library operation or build was run; source-only.

Keyboard device source-body and API failure/caller pass (GD9609-GD9611 added; 2026-10-24): read the complete 701-line `rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c` body in source order (460 C code lines by `cloc 2.06`) and its 91-line internal header (45 code lines), then traced selected base-device wiring (`rom/mmakefile.src:143-149`), keyboard HIDD open/object failure and `OpenDevice()` failure return (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:147-255`; `rom/exec/opendevice.c:109-120`), pending `KBD_READEVENT` cancellation and message reply (`keyboard.c:525-548`), `ReplyMsg()`/`InternalPutMsg()` to the reply-port signal (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:50-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-106`), pending-list writes from `beginio()`, `abortio()`, and the keyboard callback (`keyboard.c:347-372,525-548,608-690`), HIDD interrupt-context contract (`rom/hidds/kbd/kbdclass.c:27-56`), and ExecSMP `Disable()`/cross-CPU `Signal()` behavior (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`; `rom/exec/signal.c:350-385`). Added GD9609 for replying before storing the aborted IO result, conditional on the reply task running concurrently on another CPU. Added GD9610 for the allocated `KBUnit` not being freed on later Open failure; it has not yet been linked into the list searched by Close, and Exec does not call Close after failed Open. Added GD9611 because pending queue mutations use local `Disable()` without a cross-CPU lock; `kb_QueueLock` is initialized but not used. The keyboard GCC helper header, broader input/HIDD caller contracts, and runtime scheduling remain open; this pass grants only `keyboard.c`/`keyboard_intern.h` body credit. No device, HIDD failure, abort, or concurrent schedule was induced. Source-only.

Keyboard report cross-index duplicate reconciliation (2026-10-24): source recheck confirmed the 128-entry event-ring wrap candidate is already OD3683, the failed-Open `KBUnit` leak is already OD2304, the pending-read lost-wakeup race is already OD2389, and the `AbortIO()` reply-before-error race is already OD1007 (`../AROS-other-drivers.md`). WiFi Preferences `WaitPort()` reply-consumer recheck (2026-10-24; GD6150 retained, no new finding): traced all three waits in `workbench/prefs/wifi/main.c` through `Send()`, `HandleReply()`, `WifiWorker()` and the worker's `ReplyMsg()` path (`main.c:84-98,304-360,394-400,642-664`; `worker.c:1334-1388`). `Send()` refuses a second command while `busy`, and the only normal reply-port consumer is the main task: startup synchronously consumes the device-list reply; the GUI loop drains replies through `HandleReply()`; cleanup drains any in-flight reply before sending and consuming the quit reply. No second `GetMsg()`/`WaitPort()` consumer for this reply port was found, so the generic WaitPort competing-consumer concern does not add a WiFi-specific race. The separately tracked GD6150 remains: cleanup disposes the MUI application before draining an outstanding command reply, while `HandleReply()` still updates MUI objects. The WiFi Preferences target is Raspberry Pi-only and optional from the Preferences aggregate (`workbench/prefs/wifi/mmakefile.src:8-16`). No worker request or close interleaving was run; source-only.

Sound datatype `WaitPort()` startup/teardown caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new finding): traced the two `WaitPort(replyport)` sites in `Sound_NEW()` and `Sound_DISPOSE()` through both selected player implementations (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:866-892,1427-1445,PlayerProc:2927-2945,PlayerProcAHI:3727-3742`). Each handshake creates a private reply port, submits exactly one message to the child process port, waits for the child to `ReplyMsg()` that same message, and immediately dequeues it with `GetMsg()` before deleting the private port. The child receives the init message before later commands on its process port, and the player-port creation failure replies before exiting; the parent treats the NULL return data as failed startup and does not publish `PlayerPort`. The exit path replies before deleting the worker's own port and returning. No second consumer or outstanding reply on either private port was established. This closes only the WaitPort handshake caller slice; existing Sound findings and broader audio/AHI contracts remain tracked separately. The `workbench-datatypes-sound` manifest selects `dispatch.c` and `sound_init.c`, but its Workbench aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:4-13`). No player process or audio operation was run; source-only.

Each static reply message also remains queued after the shutdown wait, but no independent consequence from that state was established. Source-only.

Each worker's only `OpenLibrary()`/`CloseLibrary()` pair is for `iffparse.library`; none opens its own MCC module to retain a module reference while the worker runs (`nlist/nlisttree:175,238`; BetterString `:327,396`; TextEditor `:793,879`). GD9612 shutdown-reply queue lifetime follow-up (2026-10-24; no separate finding): rechecked the static `msg` and `replyPort` lifecycle in all four clipboard workers. `ShutdownClipboardServer()` waits for the worker's reply but does not remove the reply message; the message node and port are static module data, and `mn_Node.ln_Name` retains the address of the shutdown caller's stack `ServerData`. No path reads that parameter after the shutdown case replies. If a later startup occurs, it reinitializes `replyPort.mp_MsgList` with `NewList()` before reusing the static message, detaching the stale queue entry; normal worker requests already remove their reply before returning. Thus the queued message and stale stack address do not establish an independent defect. The worker-tail/module-unload window remains GD9612. Source-only.


`ScrollRegion()` allocation/rollback and bounds recheck (GD9415 retained; no additional candidate, 2026-10-24): reread the complete implementation and direct caller (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:56-97`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:861`). The explicit-rectangle path builds `cutRegion` before modifying it, clips in place with the documented non-failing `AndRectRegion`, and swaps into the caller region only after both `ClearRectRegionND` and `OrRegionRegion` succeed; its allocation failures therefore leave the original region unchanged. The only maintained caller passes a non-NULL rectangle. The public NULL path still translates the region bounds and its relative rectangles without clipping translated contents back to the original bounds, so GD9415 remains limited to external/public NULL-rectangle calls. No region operation was executed; source-only.

GD9615 scroll-path caller follow-up (expanded existing finding; 2026-10-24): connected the negative-screen-rectangle case from GD9613 through both public no-Layer scroll paths to `MoveRaster()` and the generic software `BltBitMap()` path. `ScrollRaster()` changes a negative upper bound to the bitmap's far edge after the signed-to-unsigned comparison (`scrollraster.c:97-109`), then invokes `MoveRaster()` (`:127-128`); `ScrollRasterBF()` repeats the same clamp and call (`scrollrasterbf.c:95-108,124-125`). Thus the reviewed public scroll APIs supply an in-tree call chain to GD9615 when the caller gives the GD9613 off-screen interval and the selected bitmap is generic planar software. PaletteExtra signed-index boundary and pen-list caller pass (GD9620 added; 2026-10-24): read the full `rom/graphics/attachpalextra.c` body (54 `cloc 2.06` C lines), reconciled `ColorMap.Count`/`GetColorMap()` allocation widths and the public AttachPalExtra contract, then traced `pe_FirstFree` and `pe_FirstShared` through the selected `ObtainPen()` and `ReleasePen()` list walks. `ColorMap.Count` and list heads are `UWORD`, but `PalExtra_AllocList_Type` is signed `WORD`; with a 32,769-entry ColorMap and bitmap depth >=16, index 32,768 is valid in the allocated arrays but casts to -32,768 when a list walk initializes its index, so the next list access is before the allocation. IntelGMA registration-failure handover trigger qualification (GD5229 retained, 2026-10-24): traced `G45_LoadState()` before `AddDisplayDriverA()` against the graphics registration return paths and IntelGMA `Root.New`. Confirmed `DD_NO_MEM` and `DD_ID_EXISTS` return before driver setup, while `DD_DRIVER_ERROR` follows failed `HW_AddDriver()`; all occur after the initial mode write. Although generic graphics registration can return `DD_IN_USE` when a driver refuses boot-display handover, IntelGMA does not consume `DDRVA_Handover` in its constructor; only the searched Nouveau class consumes this tag. Removed `DD_IN_USE` as an established IntelGMA trigger and qualified the candidate to pre-setup and class-instantiation failures. IntelGMA initial-mode allocation failure caller recheck (GD9602 retained; 2026-10-24): re-read the exact allocation fields and write paths. `initialState` is a `GMAState_t *`, and `G45_LoadState()` reads `state->htotal` before any guard, so its allocation failure reaches a definite NULL dereference independently of `G45_InitMode()` finding a PLL solution. `initialBitMap` is `intptr_t`; `AllocBitmapArea()` returns -1 on failure; `Card.Framebuffer` is a `char *`; the clear loop forms `initialBitMap + Framebuffer`, making the first 32-bit store start at `Framebuffer - 1`. Qualified the result to a likely first-store fault at the mapping edge or cross-boundary write if the preceding address is mapped, rather than claiming a general arbitrary framebuffer overwrite. The report cites these types and lines. The separate missing initial-state allocation and bitmap allocation remain in one finding because both are unchecked startup allocations on the same mode setup path; no allocation failure or hardware write was induced. Source-only.

IntelGMA caller added to graphics registration false-success finding (GD5906 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `INTELG45::Root::New()` display allocation failure through the compositor constructor and graphics HIDD getter. A NULL display makes the compositor constructor dispose and return NULL; IntelGMA ignores that result and still returns its graphics HIDD, whose `DisplayDefault` getter returns `sd->display` (NULL). `driver_Setup()` logs/skips registration but reaches its unconditional TRUE return, so `AddDisplayDriverA()` reports `DD_OK`; G45 initialization then succeeds on the already assigned PCI pointer and startup makes the class resident. Added this concrete selected IntelGMA path to existing GD5906 alongside LinuxFB; no duplicate ID was added. No object allocation failure or registration was induced; source-only.

Display callback removal argument recheck (GD5907 detailed and qualified; 2026-10-24): distinguished the callback return object from registered userdata. `display_Enable()` passes the global registered userdata on add and stores the return object in that display node. `display_Expunge()` correctly passes the stored return object as callback argument 1, but also passes it as argument 3 instead of the global registered userdata required by the `SetDisplayDriverCallback()` contract. The sole in-tree callback is Intuition `DisplayDriverNotify()`, whose removal branch ignores argument 3 and disposes argument 1; therefore no current in-tree failure is established. Replaced the placeholder with a conditional private-API contract finding, updated the master index wording, and retained high confidence in the source mismatch with impact limited to clients consuming userdata during removal. No callback or display removal was run; source-only.

Font-extension unlinked-node failure recheck (GD5911 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): re-read `ExtendFont()`, hash-node allocation/insertion/deletion and `StripFont()` cleanup. Confirmed a new node from `tfe_hashnode_create()` remains unlinked until the extension, cloned tags and required color-font buffer all succeed; the three downstream failure paths free extension resources but not the new node. `StripFont()` looks up only linked nodes, so it cannot reclaim this allocation; retrying the same font repeats the new-node allocation. Expanded GD5911 from its placeholder with exact failure edges and leak scope. Full-body credits already existed; no new line credit. No allocation failure or font operation was induced; source-only.

Region clipping head/chunk cleanup recheck (GD5912 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): traced `AndRectRegion()` unlink and head publication against RegionRectangle slot counters and `_DisposeRegionRectangleList()`. If a clipped-out first entry is followed by a retained entry in the same chunk, the retained entry becomes `RegionRectangle` with nonzero `Counter`; disposal then skips the chunk containing that start and frees only later chunks. `ClearRegion()`/`DisposeRegion()` use this list cleanup, and maintained `ScrollRegion()` applies `AndRectRegion()` to `cutRegion` before disposing it. Added the specific list-shape trigger and cleanup consequence; finding remains conditional on a region with the required multi-rectangle chunk layout. No region was built or clipped; source-only.

Cross-LayerInfo ClipBlit deadlock recheck (GD5913 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): re-read the full `ClipBlit()` lock/unlock sequence and `LockLayerRom()` wrapper. Confirmed the common `LayerInfo` ordering semaphore is taken only when both distinct layers share the exact same `LayerInfo`; distinct LayerInfo pointers skip it. Each call then blocks on source followed by destination and releases after the complete internal blit, establishing the opposite-direction two-task wait cycle for different screens. Rechecked the maintained direct ClipBlit call-site census: it does not establish an opposing cross-screen pair, so the report scopes this to concurrent public API clients rather than asserting a current in-tree trigger. No lock contention or blit was run; source-only.

TextFit extent-versus-numeric limit recheck (GD5914 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): reread the full selected implementation against its function contract. The header text specifies numeric bit width/height only when `constrainingExtent` is NULL, but the implementation always gates on `constrainingBitHeight >= tf_YSize` before inspecting extent and always applies `constrainingBitWidth` in its character loop. A sufficient non-NULL extent can therefore still yield zero or a truncated fit when numeric fields are smaller. Rechecked the direct in-tree call inventory: direct calls use NULL for `constrainingExtent`; `TextFitNew()` forwards its incoming extent and is the maintained wrapper surface, but this scan did not establish a non-NULL maintained call. Replaced GD5914 placeholder with the contract defect, concrete caller condition, and explicit no-in-tree-trigger qualification. No body or line credit added; no fit/render operation was run. Source-only.

BltClear odd-count behavior and API contract recheck (GD5915 reconstructed and qualified; 2026-10-24): compared generic and selected m68k-amiga implementations. Generic writes full ULONGs and then an optional UWORD, leaving a 1-byte tail; m68k-amiga converts to `bytecount >> 1` words and its blitter loop leaves any odd byte. The public flags description says bit 1 selects row mode, while the following bytecount paragraph reverses that mode description; documented even-byte requirement therefore makes the odd-count contract ambiguous. Reconciled all checked-in direct callers: bitmap setup uses even `RASSIZE()` row bytes, Flood uses `WIDTH_TO_BYTES()` rounded to an even byte stride, and the benchmark passes 32,000. Kept GD5915 scoped to odd counts in the implementation direct-count mode with no maintained in-tree trigger; confidence is high for behavior and medium for the public contract interpretation. No clear was run; source-only.

Color-font conversion allocation wrap and output-stride recheck (GD5916 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): recomputed the 32-bit `ULONG` product for `tf_Modulo=16385`, `tf_YSize=32767`: width 131,080, full product 4,295,098,360, allocated size after wrap 131,064. Traced that width through `InitBitMap(UWORD width)` to 8 pixels and `ReadPixelArray8(WORD xstop)` to xstop 7; its output modulo is 16 and the row callback writes 8 bytes per row. The final row writes through byte 524,263, beyond the wrapped allocation. Verified `ExtendFont()` reaches this helper only for real non-antialiased color fonts, and recorded the required roughly 512 MiB of source plane data per selected plane as a major practical reachability limitation; no maintained oversized font caller was found. Replaced GD5916 placeholder with exact arithmetic, type narrows, trigger and low-medium reachability caveat. No font, buffer or pixel transfer was created; source-only.


Compositor method-base failure-sentinel recheck (GD5917 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` bucket creation through `OOP_GetMethodID()` and `compositor_Install()`. A lower-depth 1920×1080 entry followed by a higher-depth 1280×720 entry therefore returns the lower-depth mode. WeighTAMatch size narrowing and score-penalty recheck (GD5926-GD5927 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread the matcher and reconciled `TextAttr.ta_YSize` as UWORD with its signed WORD casts, size penalty and returned WORD. Added exact cases for 65535-vs-0 collapsing to distance one and 32767-vs-32768 expanding to 65535. Recomputed GD5927: with a 511-size upward mismatch, `511 << 7` is 65,408; on two's-complement WORD conversion this becomes -128. Subtracting it raises the score; with an extra target style bit that clears bit 11, 30,719 becomes 30,847. Qualified the positive-score consequence to target narrowing behavior, the size range and an existing style penalty; without the latter, the final value may wrap negative. Traced the score into OpenFont and diskfont ranking comparisons. No font search was run; source-only.


User copper-list reinitialization and growth-failure recheck (GD5928-GD5929 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread `UCopperListInit()`, `CBump()`, `CMove()`/`CWait()` and both public macro variants. Confirmed reinit sets the first segment's Count to MaxCount, rewinds only its CopPtr, and leaves `ucl->CopList` and all extension segments' cursors/counts untouched. From the first segment, the next bump increments past capacity and misses the equality transition; from a previous extension segment, emission continues there. Separately traced both extension allocations in CBump: failure leaves Count at capacity and the current cursor on its last instruction; a later macro overwrites that instruction, then moves past the allocation without an error signal. Buffer-allocation failure additionally leaves an empty extension linked, but ordinary continuation advances the active Count past the equality check and does not select that node; FreeCopList safely traverses it and `FreeMem(NULL, 0)` is a no-op. Corrected GD5929 to remove the unsupported NULL-cursor retry consequence. No maintained C macro caller was found; both findings are scoped to external/public clients. Updated GD5928 summary in master index. No list or allocation failure was run; source-only.

Traced a checked-in keyboard focus-navigation path that sets `UPDATE_SINGLEENTRY` and requests `MUI_Redraw()`. Radeon I²C allocation and EDID transfer-result caller recheck (GD5934-GD5935 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced `RADEONDisplayDDCConnected()` through the selected I²C helper and generic HIDD. Separately, the local EDID array is uninitialized, `Hidd_I2CDevice::WriteRead` returns the generic `I2C_WriteRead()` BOOL, and Radeon ignores that return before reading `edid[0x14]`; generic address/byte failures return FALSE, including paths that leave the target byte unwritten. GD5934-GD5935 I²C failure-boundary refinement (2026-10-25): re-read generic `WriteRead()` and `GetByte()` failure exits (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:286-327,330-369`) against the Radeon caller (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_driver.c:1249-1296`). The uninitialized-byte condition is specifically a transfer that fails before the read reaches EDID offset `0x14`; if failure occurs while reading that byte, it may be only partially assembled, and if it occurs later the classification byte may already be valid although the overall operation failed. Radeon ignores the result in all three cases and always classifies from `edid[0x14]`. `RADEONQueryConnectedMonitors()` calls this routine during `RADEONInit()` (`radeon_driver.c:2422-2424`), and its discovered monitor result feeds primary/secondary monitor selection (`:1465-1515`); this pass found no separate maintained hotplug/re-detection caller. GD9625 generated relative-library cleanup qualification (2026-10-24): compared `graphics.conf`'s `rellib utility`/`rellib oop` entries with `_set_libinit()` rollback. Generic masked-blit unsupported draw-mode and public caller pass (GD4130 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread `copyboxmasked_impl()` from draw-mode save through return and traced the class wrapper and graphics.library caller (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1488-1492,1516-1590,1600-1654`; `rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:24-38,127-141`). The implementation temporarily forces Copy for `PutImage`, supports only Or, Copy and AndInverted, and for other modes logs then writes the unmodified destination buffer with Copy before returning TRUE. The public minterm-to-GC conversion maps minterm zero to Clear (`gfxfuncsupport.h:84-89`; `hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:369-385`), so a masked clear through the generic fallback is a concrete no-op despite the HIDD success result. The public library vector is void; no checked-in caller with a minterm outside those three modes was found, so the practical maintained-client trigger is not asserted. This remains a generic fallback/public API candidate; accelerated driver overrides are not covered. No copy was run; source-only.


`AreaEnd()` outline-mask geometry, narrowing, and caller recheck (GD4133 detailed; 2026-10-24): re-read `areaoutlinepolygonmask()` and the TmpRas allocation calculation in source order (`rom/graphics/areafill.c:189-220`; `rom/graphics/areaend.c:130-140`), then checked public `AreaDraw()` coordinate storage (`areadraw.c:63-75`). Refined the trigger to distinguish C semantics: with `dx=16384, dy=0`, `error << 1` promotes to `int` and 32768 is representable, but assigning it to signed `WORD twice` is out of range and implementation-defined; the later compound assignment to `WORD error` also narrows. On the usual two's-complement truncation, a horizontal edge from `(0,0)` to `(16384,0)` changes the next y step to -1; the routine then computes `ry=(UWORD)(y-bounds->MinY)` and indexes past the bounds-sized mask. This excludes an unsupported claim of signed-shift UB and scopes the memory-write consequence to the stated conversion. Repository `AreaDraw()` caller census found only small clock/colorwheel/drawlist/graph geometry and debug tests; none establishes this wide-edge trigger. The public signed-WORD interface remains the input surface. No polygon, compiler build, or TmpRas access was run; source-only.


`AreaEnd()` undersized-TmpRas error-exit and caller pass (GD5759 detailed; 2026-10-24): rechecked the function from state capture through all returns (`rom/graphics/areaend.c:71-85,101-140,259-281`). For a polygon, the MOVE record calls `Move()` before the polygon-mask size check; an undersized TmpRas returns -1 without restoring `cp_x/cp_y`, whereas normal completion and the invalid-record error restore both. The Area records are also not reset on this capacity return, consistent with retry. The ellipse branch's capacity check does not itself move the cursor. Repository `AreaEnd()` caller census includes ColorWheel, Reaction DrawList, Zune clock/graph, and graphics debug code; checked call sites ignore the result, and none established a cursor-dependent follow-up after an undersized-mask error. Kept the finding as a public RastPort state-restoration defect and limited in-tree impact claims accordingly. No error was induced; source-only.

IntelGMA dynamic graphics-memory header concurrency recheck (GD4185 detailed, 2026-10-24): traced both allocator list operations and release lifetime in `intelgma_memory.c:20-118,120-194`. `AllocGfxMem()` leaves `Forbid()` before reading the current header's successor/gap; `FreeGfxMem()` leaves its protected `Deallocate()` before removing and freeing a now-empty dynamic header. GD4200 32-bit plain interleaved raster-wrap arithmetic recheck (2026-10-24): traced the non-HIDD `AllocBitMap()` branch into `AllocRaster()` and the `RASSIZE()` macro (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:195-240,497-513`; `allocraster.c:43-57`; `compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:43`). Worked the 32-bit case `sizex=262145`, `sizey=65535`, `depth=2`: combined width 524290 gives 65538-byte aligned row stride and `RASSIZE` wraps at 2^32 to 65534 bytes; the bitmap records a 32770-byte BytesPerRow and 65535 rows, while the second plane is placed 2,147,581,950 bytes after the base. Confirmed no overflow check or dimension-range rejection in the plain path. Kept this separate from GD1731's small-width per-row padding under-allocation. No maintained large-dimension plain interleaved caller was found; no bitmap or raster operation was run. Source-only.


GD4200 public raster-consumer reachability follow-up (2026-10-24): traced a returned plain two-plane bitmap into the non-HIDD `BltBitMap()` branch (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:240-315`). Its clipping uses the bitmap's stored dimensions, then its per-plane loop uses `Planes[plane]` and `BytesPerRow` without validating allocation spans. For GD4200's geometry, a one-pixel copy with plane mask selecting plane 1 addresses the plane pointer about 2 GiB past the small wrapped allocation. This establishes an ordinary public consumer for the invalid layout; no bitmap, blit, or allocation was performed. Source-only.

Intuition `ScreenPosition()` LONG-to-WORD clipping recheck (GD9391 detailed, 2026-10-24): checked the public parameter types and clipping contract against `compiler/include/graphics/view.h`, `screenposition.c`, `ScrollVPort()`, the generic bitmap setter, and native VGAGfx setter. The public LONG value is stored into signed-WORD viewport offsets before `ScrollVPort()` widens it to `IPTR` and calls the HIDD, so both selected setters receive the already-converted `WORD` value and only then apply their bounds; the exact out-of-range conversion is target/compiler-dependent, so the report no longer asserts universal wraparound. Rechecked `ScreenPosition()`/`MoveScreen()` in-tree callers: ordinary relative deltas are used and no extreme-value caller was established. Expanded GD9391's consequence and scope; no new body-line credit beyond the existing full-body entries. No screen movement or display operation was run. Source-only.


GD77 maintained icon-resize caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced selected `LayoutIconA()` through its caller `GetIconTagList()`. The color-image scaling branch allocates the replacement with `BMF_CLEAR`, calls the void `BitMapScale()`, then frees and replaces the previous bitmap without observing scaler failure (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:82,392-454`; `geticontaglist.c:345-361`; `workbench/libs/icon/mmakefile.src:37`). The `LayoutIconA()` return remains success on this path. This makes a generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure an observable blank resized icon with the prior bitmap discarded. Caller inventory also covered the in-tree `BitMapScale()` call sites in hyperlayers, demos, graphics, printer, Wanderer, icon and cgfx; this does not close broader caller/platform review. No allocation failure or icon layout was induced; source-only.


GD77 sprite-generation caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced `AllocSpriteDataA()`'s selected resize path and Intuition pointer construction. `AllocSpriteDataA()` allocates its output `AllocBitMap()` with `BMF_CLEAR`, invokes `BitMapScale()` and then publishes a non-null `ExtSprite` without checking scaler status (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:243-271`). `pointerclass.c` calls it and consumes the returned sprite bitmap (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:103-140`). A generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure can therefore publish blank pointer image data as a successful sprite. Added this as a second maintained caller consequence of GD77; no new root cause or body credit. No pointer construction or scale was run; source-only.


GD77 printer graphics caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced the selected printer scaling path after successful `PRS_INIT` (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:544-545,601-640,668-671`). It allocates the destination with flags 0 (so `BMF_CLEAR` is not requested; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:76,193`), calls the void `BitMapScale()`, then reads every output row with `ReadPixelArray()` and transfers it. A generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure leaves that bitmap unwritten, yet the path does not turn it into a printer error and retains the `PRS_INIT` result. Expanded GD77 with this conditional printed-output consequence; no new root-cause ID or source-body credit. No print, scale, or allocation failure was run; source-only.


GD77 `ScalePixelArray()` direct-HIDD caller pass (2026-10-24): traced the selected `cgfx` path from temporary HIDD bitmap allocation through `HIDD_BM_BitMapScale()`, `DoRenderFunc()` and `RenderHook` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/scalepixelarray.c:151-205`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:88-100,119-129`). The scaler returns void; the caller copies the temporary destination to the RastPort and reports the renderer's pixel count without a scaling-success signal. On generic scratch-allocation failure, it therefore copies whatever contents the temporary HIDD bitmap has after the no-write return; initialization is class-specific and remains unverified. Expanded GD77's caller map with this return-status gap, without claiming deterministic pixel contents or adding a new root cause. No scaling or render operation was run; source-only.


Printer source-hook result propagation pass (GD9630 added, 2026-10-24): traced `Printer_Gfx_DumpRPort()`'s source-hook initialization through transfer and return (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:557-671`) and its selected device caller (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:638-659`). Printer ordinary-path allocation error pass (GD9631 added, 2026-10-24): traced the no-source-hook path after successful `PRS_INIT` through transfer-row/destination bitmap allocation, the skipped rendering loop, `PRS_CLOSE`, and return (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:544-545,590-671`). System requester MapRawKey overflow caller follow-up (GD9632 added; 2026-10-24): rechecked the one-byte `MapRawKey()` call in `rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:216-247` against the keymap return and helper behavior (`rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:140-167,263-264`; `rom/keymap/support.c:29-37`).
