ScreenMode Test RastPort allocation failure recheck (GD6342 detailed; GD6343 kept distinct; 2026-10-24): followed the user Test method through successful timer setup and `OpenScreenTags()` to `CreateRastPort()` (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:274-347`). The public helper's implementation returns NULL when its single `AllocMem()` fails (`compiler/arossupport/createrastport.c:35-43`); the next statement writes through `rp`, before any cleanup label, confirming GD6342's conditional fault and skipped normal test-screen/timer cleanup. The successful path's missing `FreeRastPort()` is the separate GD6343 allocation leak. No preview or allocation failure was run; source-only.

ScreenMode preview RastPort success-path ownership recheck (GD6343 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced `CreateRastPort()` at `smeditor.c:346` through all subsequent exits. The only successful-screen path closes the screen and timer/request/port (`:462-470`) but never calls the matching `FreeRastPort()`; the temporary RastPort is not owned by the screen, and its API explicitly requires the caller to free it (`compiler/arossupport/freerastport.c:18-46`). A successful Test action therefore leaks one RastPort allocation per preview. Kept this distinct from GD6342's failed-allocation dereference. No preview was run; source-only.

Pointer Preferences export sticky-success recheck (GD6344 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced both `MAXPOINTER` iterations through `PushChunk()` and `WriteChunkBytes()` (`workbench/prefs/pointer/prefs.c:155-212`; `prefs.h:14`). `retval` is set TRUE after any one `NPTR` write succeeds and is not cleared on later `PushChunk` or short/error write; the loop continues after a failed entry. `WriteChunkBytes()` returns actual bytes written or an error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:19-27`), and GUI `PTEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ExportFH` returns the helper result (`pteditor.c:264-276`), confirming a success report for incomplete files. CLI persistence ignores the return independently (`prefs.c:258-283`), so it is not used as this finding's caller-visible success signal. No export or I/O failure was run; source-only.

Input Preferences empty-recognized-chunk import recheck (GD6345 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced successful `StopChunks()` registration into the `ParseIFF(IFFPARSE_SCAN)` loop (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:291-356`). `retval` becomes TRUE before the loop, and a valid PREF FORM containing no recognized INPT/KMSW stop chunk reaches end-of-file without resetting it or applying either structure. The GUI import handler then refreshes unchanged globals and clears the Changed flag (`ipeditor.c:565-581`); the CLI ENV path treats the file as loaded and suppresses ENVARC fallback (`prefs.c:102-113,502-528`). No file or GUI import was exercised; source-only.

Input Preferences KMSW export failure recheck (GD6346 detailed; 2026-10-24): followed `Prefs_ExportFH()` after successful `INPT` serialization (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:443-465`). `retval` becomes TRUE on INPT success; KMSW PushChunk failure has no error branch and KMSW write failure skips the `retval = retval && TRUE` assignment, leaving TRUE unchanged. `CloseIFF()` is unchecked (`:479`), and the GUI export method returns the stale helper result (`ipeditor.c:584-597`). Thus an INPT-only/incomplete file is reported successful after the specified KMSW failure. CLI save callers discard the result (`prefs.c:530-555`); no export or failure was run. Source-only.


System requester default-keymap trigger verification (GD9632 strengthened; 2026-10-24): checked the requester-synthesized `InputEvent` field values and the initialized default-keymap path (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:216-230`; `rom/keymap/keymap_init.c:47-60`). The requester supplies `ie_Qualifier=0`; selected built-in keymap code `0x4c` is `ST|S`, and the unqualified string-table slot selects descriptor zero with length two (`rom/keymap/defaultkeymap.c:105-110,631-640,905-912`). Therefore cursor-up reaches the exact one-byte `MapRawKey()` overflow without relying on a hypothetical custom keymap. `WriteToBuffer()` rejects before copying, `MapRawKey()` returns -1, and the caller treats that as truth before reading `rawbuffer[0]`. Updated GD9632 with this concrete selected-input trigger. No requester or key event was run; source-only; no body-line credit.

System requester raw-key address handoff recheck (GD9632 retained; 2026-10-25): traced the `IntuiMessage.IAddress` pointer used to rebuild `ie_EventAddress` against the selected input-handler producer (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:223-229`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:144-170,189-212`). For `IDCMP_RAWKEY`, both message producers copy the original event address into the embedded `prevCodeQuals` field and set `IAddress` to that field's address; the requester dereference therefore restores the original pointer and is not a separate bad-indirection candidate. The `MapRawKey()` overflow/unwritten-byte defect remains confined to the one-byte capacity and truth-test described by GD9632. Message storage remains live while the handler processes it and is replied by its caller after dispatch. No input event or requester was used; source-only.

GD4228 HAM row-stride consequence narrowing (2026-10-24): checked the computed source-byte offset against the planar row allocation for non-byte-aligned widths. Because `bmh_Width <= BytesPerRow * 8`, `(i * bmh_Width + x) / 8` does not by itself advance beyond the allocated plane extent for valid dimensions; it does start later rows too early and reads wrong pixel bits. Removed the unsupported overread consequence from GD4228; the incorrect HAM output remains. No frame was decoded or accessed at runtime; source-only.

Also traced `windecor_windowshape()`'s `BarRounded` result through the selected default shape hook (`:1867-1960`; `rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:1192-1222`) into `ChangeWindowShape()`/layer shape update. WinGDI native event-thread shutdown recheck (GD9637 added, 2026-10-25): traced `GDI_Init()`'s `CreateThread()`/immediate handle close through `gdithread_entry()`'s message loop and post-loop keyboard-hook removal, then followed `GDI_Shutdown()` from the selected HIDD expunge (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c:241-264,364-454`; `wingdi_hiddclass.c:759-770`). Confirmed shutdown only posts `WM_QUIT` and then closes shared acknowledgement events and frees IRQs; no worker handle is retained or joined. The keyboard hook and event callbacks can still be active until the worker processes the quit message, so added GD9637 for the conditional teardown/resource race. The exact manifestation depends on host event timing and was not reproduced. No WinGDI shutdown or event was run; source-only; local WinGDI bodies already have full-body credit.

GD9637 failed-init trigger confirmation (2026-10-25): followed the selected WinGDI initializer priorities (`gdigfx_init` at 0, `gdi_Startup` at 10) and failure unwind (`wingdi_hiddclass.c:736-777`; `startup.c:66-102`). `gdi_Startup()`'s current GD6317 mouse-registration call returns NULL, causing its initializer to return FALSE; the common `_set_libinit()` stops the init set and invokes the expunge set for rollback (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:50-69`). This confirms the graphics expunge and `GDI_Shutdown()` are reached on the selected startup-failure path after `GDI_Init()` has created the worker. Expanded GD9637's trigger evidence; no event/thread interleaving or runtime behavior was induced. No line credit change; source-only.

GD9637 early worker shutdown-post race recheck (2026-10-25): re-read the host worker startup and cleanup in source order (`gdi_native.c:241-264,376-425,444-454`). `GDI_Init()` closes its thread handle without a readiness handshake; `gdithread_entry()` does not reach `GetMessage()` until after `SetWindowsHookEx()`. `GDI_Shutdown()` ignores the `PostThreadMessage(WM_QUIT)` result and immediately closes both acknowledgement events and frees all three IRQs. The Windows API contract says posting fails if the target thread has not created a message queue; thus the selected init rollback can lose the quit message if shutdown wins the worker-start race, leaving the worker and hook alive after teardown. This strengthens GD9637's documented trigger/consequence with an explicit lost-shutdown path. Updated the finding in `AROS-graphics-desktop.md`; its index link/ID is unchanged. The API contract is documented by [Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/api/winuser/nf-winuser-postthreadmessagea). No message queue, shutdown race, or host event was run; no body-line credit changed; source-only.

MUI font-preference parser and Configdata setter follow-up (2026-10-25; no new finding): traced `zune_font_get()`'s custom font string from `MUI_ConfigdataData.prefs.fonts[]` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/font.c:26-108`; `classes/configdata.c:305-342`) to the eight font fields and Zune Prefs `MUIM_Configdata_SetFont` callers (`classes/configdata.c:1056-1096`; `workbench/prefs/Zune/{windowp,listviewsp,groupsp,buttonsp,slidersp}.c`). The accepted string comes from Dataspace/IFF or the font requester; `zune_font_get()` allocates a private copy, parses the final path component with `StrToLong()` without checking its return, narrows the resulting `LONG` to `TextAttr.ta_YSize` (`UWORD`), then opens the corresponding `.font`. Non-numeric sizes become zero and overlarge values can narrow or overflow; an unsuccessful custom open follows the existing screen/system-font fallback path. No concrete in-tree malformed preference, independent user-visible consequence, or supported size contract violation was established, so this remains a parser follow-up rather than a finding. Also checked the apparent `MUIM_Configdata_SetFont` synchronization omission: Zune Prefs calls it on a temporary Configdata object solely to save its Dataspace; live applications obtain `mgi_Prefs` from their own initialized/reloaded Configdata object, so the omitted `Configdata_SynchronizeString()` call does not establish stale live font pointers. No preference was edited or font opened; source-only.


MUI gradient renderer angle/geometry follow-up (GD9657 corrected; 2026-10-25): re-derived the denominator from the actual quadrant setup in `FillPixelArrayGradient()`. The earlier 315-degree claim was incorrect: in quadrant four `yw = -height` and `vx = vy = -180`, making `t = -180 * (height + width)`, which cannot be zero for a nonempty rectangle. At 135 degrees, `vx = vy = 180`, quadrant two retains `yw = height`, and a square gives `t = 180 * (width - height) = 0` before the first pixel's `y1_mul_t_accu / t`. Confirmed the selected Zune Prefs slider permits 135 and serializes it into the image spec via `Gradient_Function()`; mode-0 scaled/tiled drawing on CyberGraphX truecolor reaches the division. Corrected GD9657 to the reachable 135-degree square case. No gradient was rendered; source-only; no file-body line credit.

On a native icon, HasRealImage2 stores its boolean result but omits the processed-count increment. CursorFB whole-operation bracket coordinate recheck (GD5731 detailed; 2026-10-25): re-read `CFB_REMOVE_ALL`, all six callers, and `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:60-67,303-359`; `gfx_displayclass.c:294-307`), plus the public `InputEvent` and stored cursor-position types (`compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:34-42`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_display.h:50-55`). The helper tests only `[-16384,16383]`, although signed `WORD` coordinates extend through 32767. Polygon draw/fill, text draw/fill, bitmap clear, and bitmap scale can therefore skip cursor removal when the cursor rectangle lies beyond that bound, then modify its pixels without the bracket restoring it. The consequence remains conditional on the selected display accepting those coordinates and the operation touching the cursor. No mode or drawing operation was run. Source-only.

WAV decoder input-span proof for GD6202 (2026-10-25): rechecked the retained zero/undersized `blockAlign` finding against the exact batch allocation and decoder loop. `SND_BUFFER_SIZE` is 16 KiB (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/include/wave_class.h:10`); mono float32 with `blockAlign=1` makes `numBlocks=16384`, allocates and reads 16,384 bytes, then the decoder processes the same 16,384 frames while advancing four bytes per frame (`wave_class.c:367-412`; `wave_ieee_float.c:28-40`), exceeding the allocation by 49,152 bytes. Stereo 8-bit A-law at the same alignment consumes two bytes per frame. This confirms a heap-buffer overread for sufficiently large data chunks; smaller partial batches may read zero-filled bytes within the oversized allocation instead. Zero alignment still divides by zero at the same parser sizing expression. Expanded GD6202's consequence with these exact spans. PCM has separate setup that recalculates alignment; no additional PCM issue established. No WAV was loaded or decoded; source-only.

GD5744 coordinate-family trigger validation and promotion (2026-10-25): rechecked `AllocBitMap()` and the generic HIDD bitmap width attribute against the CyberGraphX entry points. `AllocBitMap()` accepts ULONG dimensions and `BMF_SPECIALFMT` forces HIDD allocation; HIDD width/height attributes are UWORD, so 32,769 pixels are representable. A one-row LUT8 bitmap at that width needs a 32,769-byte row, within `BytesPerRow`'s UWORD range. `WritePixelArray(RECTFMT_LUT8)` forwards x=32,768 through `WritePixels8()`'s signed-WORD coordinates; the bitmap clipping bound `width-1` also narrows to a negative WORD, causing the valid request to be rejected before drawing and returning zero. Promoted GD5744 from conditional/unconfirmed to a confirmed public API range mismatch; no maintained caller or large display mode is needed for this explicitly allocated offscreen HIDD bitmap. The ABI conversion and allocation were not run; source-only.

CGFX `DoCDrawMethodTagList()` no-direct-access fallback recheck (GD5754 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): reread `RenderHook()` and the public `CDrawMsg` layout. The fallback computes `max_tocopy_h` and `tocopy_h` from `PIXELBUF_SIZE / bytesperrow`, but passes `lines_todo` (the entire remaining height) to both `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` and `HIDD_BM_PutImage()`; it also leaves `cdm_ysize` at the original rectangle height for the hook. Thus a rectangle taller than the buffer capacity overruns the shared scratch buffer on the first `GetImage()`, with the hook and writeback also given oversized dimensions. Generic graphics renderer cached-GC draw-mode recheck (GD5755 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `int_bltbitmap()`, its `BltBitMap()` cache caller, and the pen-conversion fallback. The general CopyBox path saves `old_drmd`, sets `drmd`, then writes `drmd` again instead of the saved value; the special truecolor Clear path sets Copy and never applies its saved mode back. `BltBitMap()` returns the object to the shared GC cache. `bltbitmap_pens()` precomputes minterm results, then calls `HIDD_BM_PutImage()` without resetting the GC mode, so cache reuse can apply stale draw-mode semantics to those results when the selected HIDD honors that GC state. The source defect is confirmed; practical corruption depends on cache reuse and HIDD behavior. No blit or cache reuse was run; source-only.

`ClipBlit()` same-RastPort overlap minterm recheck (GD5756 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): reread the overlap branch and `MoveRaster()`. The selected overlap optimization calls `MoveRaster()` when either absolute displacement is less than half the requested width or height; `MoveRaster()` uses hard-coded `0xc0` Copy for unlayered and per-ClipRect blits and does not accept the caller's minterm. The other overlap route passes `minterm` into `internal_ClipBlit()`. The entry point documents non-Copy minterms, but the prior caller census found only maintained same-RastPort Copy uses, so the trigger is public/external API use. No blit was run; source-only.

`ScrollWindowRasterNoFill()` duplicate-move recheck (GD5757 confirmed and trigger narrowed; 2026-10-25): re-read the full vector and traced its `ScrollRaster()` call through `MoveRaster()`'s per-ClipRect loop. When both absolute displacement components are smaller than the requested rectangle dimensions, the function first `ClipBlit()`s the retained overlap. `scroll` remains TRUE if the translated rectangle is not wholly contained by one ClipRect or the layer is already marked `LAYERREFRESH`; that branch then calls `ScrollRaster()`, which moves the layer again. If either displacement consumes the full extent, the first ClipBlit is skipped, so that case is not claimed. Reconfirmed whole-tree C search found no maintained caller of this vector. No scroll was run; source-only.

Area polygon convex-fast-path slope recheck (GD5758 confirmed and trigger bounded; 2026-10-25): reread `areafillpolygon()`'s four-edge convex branch, `AreaDraw()` coordinate storage, and `AreaEnd()` TmpRas sizing. The fast path multiplies signed `LONG` `(x2-x1)` by 65,536 before dividing by vertical delta. On 32-bit signed-LONG targets, a valid convex quadrilateral edge from x=-16384 to x=16384 over one scanline produces 2,147,483,648, outside the representable range; the TmpRas size check does not constrain this intermediate. Recorded the overflow and unreliable fill result without assuming a particular wrap or asserting out-of-bounds access. Previously reviewed in-tree AreaDraw callers do not establish this wide-coordinate trigger. No render or target compiler check was run; source-only.

Ellipse midpoint overflow cross-implementation reconciliation (GD5760 confirmed and expanded; GD4064 withdrawn as duplicate; 2026-10-25): compared generic HIDD `DrawEllipse()`, Radeon and IntelGMA overrides, shared `areafillellipse()`, their public radius types and the AreaEnd dispatch. All four implementations use the same `t7 = rx * t5; t8 = t7 << 1` signed-LONG sequence. For radius 1000, t7 is 2,000,000,000 but t8 requests 4,000,000,000, beyond signed 32-bit range; larger radii can overflow t7 too. Thus the previous GD4064 1,025 threshold was not the earliest affected radius and described the same implementation family, so it is merged into GD5760; that finding additionally tracks the independent Area-fill copy. Stated only the range overflow and unreliable raster result, not a specific wrap or memory access. No target compiler or ellipse operation was run; source-only.

`Flood()` area-pattern decoder recheck (GD5761 confirmed and consequence refined; 2026-10-25): compared `pattern_pen()` with the actual `BltPattern()` convention and its pixel loop. `BltPattern()` treats every nonnegative `AreaPtSz` as monochrome, including exponent zero; Flood's helper uses `> 0`, routing zero to multicolor. The multicolor branch initializes `pen_mask` to zero and only shifts it left, so each plane contributes zero and `pixval` remains zero; it also advances the plane pointer only after the loop. Thus zero-exponent mono patterns are misinterpreted and all multicolor fill pixels use pen zero. Traced both planar-direct and ReadPixel/WritePixel paths through shared `putfillpixel()`; the decoding error applies to both. Maintained Flood callers found previously do not demonstrate patterned fill. No fill was run; source-only.

Graphics.library failed-init semaphore lifetime recheck (GD5762 confirmed and trigger enumerated; 2026-10-25): reread `GfxInit()` publication/failure order and traced the selected generated INITLIB cleanup through `_set_libinit()`, `_set_libexpunge()` and genmodule's `__freebase()` path. `fontsem` is added to Exec's public semaphore list before hash allocation and later fallible region-pool, ROM-font, graphics-root and driver initialization; no `RemSemaphore()` or `ADD2EXPUNGELIB` exists in graphics.library. On a false init result the generated path invokes the available expunge set then frees the embedded base, leaving the public list node stale. No failure was induced; source-only.

`DoCollision()` shifted one-word mask recheck (GD5763 confirmed and trigger specified; 2026-10-25): reread both shifted-comparison branches and mask setup. For a 16-pixel VSprite, `Width >> 4` is one word per row, and `InitMasks()` fills `Height * wordsperline` collision words. In the negative-scroll path, `_curindex` increments to `wordsperline`; the guard is `>`, so equality proceeds to read the next mask word. Two sorted one-row VSprites offset by one pixel provide the boundary case with `_i == 0`. Scoped the direct finding to the one-UWORD overread and left collision/fault effects conditional on adjacent contents. No maintained direct `DoCollision()` caller was found; no collision data was constructed or run. Source-only.

`AddVSprite()` internal-record allocation rollback recheck (GD5764 confirmed and separated from GD5765; 2026-10-25): reread list insertion, `_CreateIntVSprite()` allocation, DrawGList traversal and `_ValidateIntVSprite()`. The VSprite is linked before the internal record allocation; a NULL allocation result is stored without rollback. Later saved-background rendering dereferences `IntVSprite->SaveBuffer`, and the normal path passes the NULL field into `_ValidateIntVSprite()`, which dereferences the record. This is the missing-record publication defect; GD5765 remains the later unchecked bitmap replacement case after an internal record already exists. No allocation failure or list traversal was induced; source-only.

`_ValidateIntVSprite()` replacement-bitmap failure recheck (GD5765 confirmed and allocation cases separated; 2026-10-25): reread the dimension-change path and traced each replacement to its first use. Both old buffers are freed before unchecked `AllocBitMap()` calls; dimensions and source-data identity are then updated regardless of allocation results. Failed `ImageData` allocation flows immediately into `BltBitMap()`, whose `IS_HIDD_BM(destBitMap)` macro reads `bitmap->pad`, so NULL is dereferenced. Failed `SaveBuffer` allocation remains NULL for the DrawGList SAVEBACK capture path. The helper returns TRUE; callers receive no allocation-failure indication. The changed-size metadata also prevents an automatic retry from this same predicate. No allocation failure or list draw was induced; source-only.

`GetBitMapAttr(BMA_WIDTH)` chunky-HIDD bound recheck (GD5766 confirmed and caller consequence refined; 2026-10-25): compared the public attribute body with generic HIDD row-stride construction and its documented pixel-width attribute. The public vector always multiplies `BytesPerRow` by eight; chunky `BytesPerRow` is aligned pixel width times bytes per pixel (e.g. 640-pixel RGB32 gives 2,560 bytes and is reported as 20,480 pixels). Traced this result through `GetRPClipRectangleForBitMap()` and its unlayered render/pixel callers; the helper explicitly uses bitmap bounds to keep HIDDs without their own checks from accessing outside storage. Also rechecked SetRast/ClearEOL/ClearScreen endpoint consumers. Exact memory effects depend on HIDD bounds behavior, so the report claims the generic guard is defeated and qualifies out-of-bounds effects. No bitmap operation was run; source-only.

`GetDisplayInfoData(DTAG_NAME)` zero-capacity recheck (GD5767 confirmed and address claim qualified; 2026-10-25): re-read the size validation, temporary-record copy and final name terminator. The tag-size helper ignores the caller's size; zero survives the upper-bound clamp, the zero-byte CopyMem is followed by unconditional `buf[size - 1] = 0`, and `ULONG` is explicitly unsigned 32-bit. Thus the index underflows to `ULONG_MAX` and is outside the supplied zero-length destination. Removed the platform-independent “one byte before buffer” claim because the exact pointer result depends on target pointer width and compiler arithmetic. Maintained callers use structure-sized buffers; no zero-size call was made. Source-only.

`GetRGB4()` signed-index lower-bound recheck (GD5768 confirmed and caller scope stated; 2026-10-25): reread the public vector and checked the selected ColorMap allocation layout. `entry` is signed `LONG`; the only validation rejects NULL maps and `entry >= Count`, then directly indexes `ColorTable[entry]`. `GetColorMap()` allocates the color table as its own `entries * sizeof(UWORD)` block. Negative public inputs therefore read before that allocation. Re-searched maintained callers: reqtools and Palette Preferences use nonnegative iteration indices, with no local negative call established. No invalid call was made; source-only.

The path requires a displayable bitmap and successful pixel-buffer allocation followed by failed register-state allocation; non-displayable construction returns before it. VGAGfx mode setup documents a 64-KiB VGA memory map, while its display enumerator advertises maximum dimensions 16,384. A 640×900 bitmap at 640-pixel pitch clears 80×900 = 72,000 bytes, extending 6,464 bytes past that mapped plane. A non-draggable screen without SPOS_FORCEDRAG is gated out entirely; on eligible screens the requested rectangle is not made visible and the upper-left is interpreted as a movement delta. Intuition/Layers failed-`BeginUpdate()` cleanup recheck (GD5775 confirmed and exact state sequence expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `BeginRefresh()`, Layers `BeginUpdate()`/`EndUpdate()`, and `EndRefresh()`, then followed the previously tracked screen-bar, `WindowNeedsRefresh()` and `CheckLayers()` callers. It returns without setting `WFLG_WINDOWREFRESH`; paired `EndRefresh()` therefore skips EndUpdate but still unlocks the layer(s) and LayerInfo. Auto-knob minimum/track boundary recheck (GD5805, 2026-10-25): re-derived endpoint coordinates from `CalcKnobSize()` using public 6x4 minimum constants, post-border `CWidth/CHeight`, and MAXPOT interpolation. A borderless 4-pixel horizontal track with HorizPot zero gives a 6-pixel knob extending 2 pixels past the track; the standard `RefreshPropGadgetKnob()` paints raw knob coordinates with RectFill and no gadget-sized clipping. `ObtainGIRPort()` only manages layer clipping/locking. Qualified to standard rendering, excluding custom display hooks and window-border decorator paths. No gadget was rendered; source-only.

Ctrl-W first-word underflow recheck (GD5806, 2026-10-25): re-read the backward space search and each subsequent copy/count/cursor/terminator update. With no preceding space, `pos` reaches -1 and `BufferPos` is assigned that value; a nonempty suffix copies before `WorkBuffer`, while an end-of-buffer cursor still writes the terminator to `WorkBuffer[-1]`. Traced WorkBuffer to either the application StringInfo buffer or StringGClass's optional allocated work buffer. Refined the trigger and consequence to include persistent negative cursor state. No key event was sent; source-only.

Ctrl-H overlapping-copy recheck (GD5807, 2026-10-25): derived both byte ranges from `strgadgets.c:953-954`. With `len = NumChars - BufferPos`, destination begins one byte before source and the ranges overlap exactly when `len >= 2`. The following cursor/count update assumes a one-character deletion but cannot repair an undefined overlapping `memcpy()`. Scoped to non-fixed-field Ctrl-H with a nonempty suffix of at least two bytes. No key event was sent; source-only.

StringGClass justification update recheck (GD5808, 2026-10-25): compared the OM_SET `STRINGA_Justification` assignment with the public “use one of” contract, flag values, and both renderer alignment switches. The setter ORs instead of replacing; left is zero and cannot clear existing bits; center|right matches neither explicit switch case and falls through to left. Scoped to repeated updates; one initial setting is unaffected. No gadget attribute was changed; source-only.

StringGClass default MaxChars recheck (GD5809, 2026-10-25): compared public `SG_DEFAULTMAXCHARS == 128` with OM_NEW's hard-coded 80, tag override handling and allocation sizes for application/undo/work buffers. Traced the editing limit to `MaxChars - 1` payload bytes for the NUL terminator. Scoped to gadgets that omit STRINGA_MaxChars; explicit values override the default. No gadget was created or text entered; source-only.

StringGClass TextVal length-bound recheck (GD5810, 2026-10-25): traced construction allocations to `MaxChars` bytes and both initial and OM_SET `STRINGA_TextVal` paths to unbounded `strcpy()`. Compared with the public maximum-character contract and the editing path's `MaxChars - 1` payload limit. An input of length at least MaxChars overruns by at least the NUL byte. Searched selected C callers; no overlong in-tree value was established, so consequence is conditional on caller-supplied data beyond the declared maximum. No gadget or value was supplied; source-only.

StringGClass LONG_MIN conversion recheck (GD5811, 2026-10-25): traced both construction-time and OM_SET `STRINGA_LongVal` calls into `set_buffer_str()`. Confirmed a negative `LONG_MIN` is negated in the same signed type before the `% 10`/`/ 10` digit loop, invoking undefined signed overflow. Qualified displayed characters as implementation-dependent; the MaxChars truncation occurs only after arithmetic. No LongVal was set; source-only.

DragBar/SizeButton failed activation cleanup recheck (GD5812, 2026-10-25): traced both clone-before-lock paths, confirmed USEGADGETLOCK is always defined, and compared each `AttemptSemaphore(GadgetLock)` failure branch with its fail cleanup and normal GOINACTIVE release. The fail paths release held locks but leave `data->rp`; both return GMR_NOREUSE, preventing normal activation teardown. Refined trigger to successful clone followed by gadget-lock contention and qualified resize edge prerequisites. No lock contention or activation was induced; source-only.

FindHighestScreen cross-monitor seed recheck (GD5814, 2026-10-25): confirmed the helper seeds `highest` from FirstScreen before filtering by ActiveMonitor, while OpenScreen explicitly documents that FirstScreen can remain on another monitor during activation. The loop only replaces the seed with a matching screen having a smaller TopEdge, and inputhandler uses the result as the mouse upper bound. Refined the trigger to a foreign FirstScreen whose TopEdge is smaller than every active-monitor screen; documented the conditional wrong-bound effect. No monitor switch or mouse event was run; source-only.


UAE `WBOPENA_ArgLock` ownership and caller recheck (GD5842 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): followed `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()`'s UAE-targeted 68k branch into `forward_to_uae()` and `tag_list_clone()`, then compared with the normal `WB_BuildArguments()` path, which `DupLock()`s supplied locks. `tag_list_clone()` calls `NameFromLock()` and unconditionally `UnLock()`s the original tag value before copying its path into the message pool. Rechecked Wanderer callers that unlock after `OpenWorkbenchObject()` and the multi-selection `ParentDir()` tag construction. Confirmed caller-lock consumption in UAE forwarding; consequence depends on caller using or releasing its retained reference. Expanded GD5842 with exact trigger and caller scope. No UAE launch or lock operation was run; source-only.

UAE launch forwarding result propagation recheck (GD5843 confirmed and narrowed, 2026-10-25): traced the public UAE branch in `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()` through `forward_to_uae()`. The helper returns `void`; pool-creation failure returns without sending, and a second `FindPort()` failure deletes the allocated pool without queueing the message. The caller nevertheless unconditionally sets and returns TRUE. Kept these silent no-send cases distinct from GD5830's NULL pooled-message dereference. No allocation failure, port transition or launch was induced; source-only.

Wanderer filesystem utility failure-path recheck (GD5844-GD5846 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): reviewed `DisplayIOError()`, `IsDirectoryEmpty()`, `GetFileInfoBlock()`, `ReadFileInfoBlockAndLockPath()`, `performDataCopy()` and their selected filesystem callers. Confirmed GD5844's first `strcat()` uses an uninitialized stack destination and that the reporter is called on common filesystem error paths. Confirmed GD5845's FIB allocation/examination failure can produce NULL, which is passed into a second lock/examine helper without validation when the path remains lockable; traced the `DeleteContent()` emptiness check caller. Confirmed GD5846's negative `Read()` result exits the loop as EOF with `stop == FALSE`, causing a partial destination to be reported successful and metadata to be copied. Added precise triggers and consequences to the report. No filesystem operation or error injection was run; source-only.

Wanderer file-copy/move sidecar and overwrite-path recheck (GD5847-GD5849 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): traced `infoFileSetup()`/`copySingleFile()` top-level versus recursive calls and verified that top-level overwrite checking assigns over the prior sidecar setup failure; narrowed GD5847 to top-level copies with an existing companion and allocation/FIB failure. In `checkIfAlreadyExists()`, confirmed the `FileCopyData` allocation is dereferenced immediately on the existing-target + overwrite-prompt path (GD5848). Traced `MoveContent()`'s unchecked `CombinePath()` result into `FileExists()` and its DOS `Lock()` call (GD5849); later `moveFile()` NULL checking does not protect the earlier use. No allocation failure or file operation was induced; source-only.

Workbook startup/constructor candidate recheck (GD5850 and GD5852 confirmed; GD5851 and GD5853 withdrawn, 2026-10-25): traced WorkbookMain's stored library bases through the shared error/normal-return cleanup and confirmed the Intuition branch closes the GadTools base a second time, leaving Intuition open (GD5850). In `wbIconNew()`, confirmed successful `GetIconTags()` precedes label duplication; its failure label frees the filename and calls superclass disposal instead of the class disposer, leaking the owned DiskObject (GD5852). Rejected GD5851 because `WBAppNew()` tests `my->Root == NULL` before returning failure and does not dereference it on that path. Rejected GD5853 because `wbwiAppend()` checks `AllocMem()` and disposes the icon object on failure before returning. Removed withdrawn candidates from the report and master index. No allocation or library failure was induced; source-only.

Wanderer standalone Icon target and IconList clipping recheck (GD5854-GD5855 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): compared `Icon__OM_NEW()`'s declared `struct opSet *` parameter and field accesses against the public `opSet` layout and the separate custom `MUIP_Icon_CreateEntry`; confirmed the constructor also uses `entry` without declaration. The explicit `wanderer-classes-icon` module target exists but is excluded from the default and quick class aggregates, so GD5854 is limited to explicit construction of that optional module and is a compile-time source defect; no build was run. Re-read `IconList__MUIM_IconList_DrawEntryLabel()` and its three dispatch sites; confirmed its clip rectangle uses `objX` for MinY while direct-display coordinates separately use `_mleft` and `_mtop`. Buffered rendering sets both coordinates to zero, so narrowed GD5855 to direct display rendering. No GUI operation was run; source-only.

IconList buffered-resource teardown recheck (GD5856 and GD5862 confirmed and qualified, 2026-10-25): traced the DisplayFlags transition and Hide/Show allocation paths. In the disable-buffer branch, the code changes `icld_BufferRastPort` to the display RastPort before dereferencing its bitmap for `FreeBitMap()`, confirming GD5856 targets the display bitmap and loses the off-screen bitmap reference. In Hide, `DeleteLayer()` is followed by clearing the off-screen RastPort pointer without freeing that RastPort or its bitmap; the display RastPort is separately freed, confirming GD5862's leak. Both require a caller-enabled buffer; Wanderer's compile-time enabling branch is disabled in this snapshot, so no default UI trigger is claimed. No attribute or lifecycle operation was run; source-only.

IconList entry-FIB, drop-source and multiline label candidate recheck (GD5857-GD5859 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): traced CreateEntry's optional FileInfoBlock copy through successful partial-entry publication, then through `RenderEntryField()`'s unconditional Comment-column FIB dereference and the selected list redraw path (GD5857). Re-read `MUIM_DragDrop()` source-list construction and its `MUIA_IconList_IconsDropped` publication: the per-source node allocation is unchecked before member access, and the selected notification passes the event into Wanderer's operation handler (GD5858). Re-derived the all-space splitter path: the skip loop advances to the NUL byte with zero remaining length; the `TextLength()` loop then increases its requested count from that position, eventually including bytes beyond the terminator (GD5859). Scoped labels to multiline-enabled lists and strings exceeding the configured maximum. No allocation failure, drop or rendering operation was induced; source-only.

IconList partial layout, list-view state and empty-navigation recheck (GD5860-GD5861 and GD5863 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): traced the default ByName sort flags into `IconList_Layout_PartialAutoLayout()`, confirmed its unchecked `NewRegion()` result reaches both `OrRectRegion()` and `RegionAndRect()`, and verified the latter immediately reads `a->bounds` (GD5860). Rechecked OM_NEW's optional `ListViewModeAttribs` allocation against list-mode draw and input consumers and Setup's handler registration; object construction continues on allocation failure (GD5861). Reconciled Up/Down raw-key fallback through `Node_FirstVisible()`/`Node_LastVisible()` and their empty/all-hidden returns with the drawer-open empty-list caller and Zune raw-key dispatch (GD5863). No allocation, GUI or input event was run; source-only.

IconList MakeEntryVisible and drag-image layout recheck (GD5864-GD5865 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): compared all four viewport branches and confirmed the above-viewport case tests `ie_IconY` but assigns `ie_IconX` into `icld_ViewY`; class dispatch exists but no in-tree direct call was found (GD5864). Matched `MUIM_CreateDragImage()`'s allocation type against the public `MUIP_CreateDragImage` and `MUI_DragImage` structures and the selected MUI List implementation. On 64-bit ABI layouts the former is 16 bytes and the latter 24 bytes, with `flags` ending at offset 20; confirmed the IconList allocation is four bytes short (GD5865). No build, GUI operation, or drag was run; source-only.

IconList unhandled desktop drop and no-order sorting recheck (GD5866-GD5867 confirmed and caller-traced, 2026-10-25): followed drag-event allocation through the `message->obj != obj && directory_path == NULL` desktop-drop branch; `iconMove` suppresses source construction, and the common exit does not dispose the unpublished record (GD5866). Compared Sort's visible/hidden partition with its conditional hidden-list reattachment and the selected Wanderer sort-menu handlers, which clear `MUIV_IconList_Sort_Orders` and still call Sort when sorting is disabled or an order is unchecked (GD5867). No drag or sort operation was run; source-only.

IconList keyboard-selection notification and Space-toggle recheck (GD5868-GD5869 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): traced Return/Space selection-list mutations in `IconList__MUIM_HandleEvent()` against every SelectionChanged setter and Wanderer's registered menu-state notification. Return sets DoubleClick but not SelectionChanged; Space changes selection without directly setting it, and its preceding UnselectAll only emits when an existing selected entry actually changes (GD5868). Evaluated the unshifted Space condition for same, different, and NULL last-clicked entries: with any non-NULL active entry it always clears the selection first, then the toggle sees the focus deselected and adds it again; Left Shift bypasses that clear and allows removal (GD5869). No input event or UI was run; source-only.

IconList modifier, object-state, buffered setup, and drop-worker ownership recheck (GD5870-GD5874 confirmed and detailed, 2026-10-25): compared all four arrow-key selection-clear conditions with the mouse helper's left/right Shift handling (GD5870). Matched the separately AllocMem-allocated `ListViewModeAttribs` pointer against OM_DISPOSE's full cleanup (GD5871). Traced successful temporary RastPort creation through both buffered layer-setup failure branches; bitmap/Layer_Info fallback cleanup omits the temporary RastPort (GD5872). Followed the cleared IconWindow drop attribute through action-hook ownership into `CreateNewProcTags()` and contrasted its empty NULL-process branch with the worker's normal payload cleanup (GD5873). Rechecked Show's unchecked CloneRastPort result and immediate buffered-path bitmap dereference; narrowed GD5874 to caller-enabled buffering. Wanderer's compile-time buffer switch is disabled. No key, object, allocation, drop or worker failure was induced; source-only.

IconList appended-info width and buffer-resize ownership recheck (GD5875-GD5876 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): re-read label rectangle width calculation and compared horizontal/vertical padding attributes and their preference loading. Confirmed the appended-size/date expansion uses vertical padding; narrowed underestimation to the case where vertical padding is smaller than horizontal and the extra text exceeds the current width (GD5875). Traced UPDATE_RESIZE's stale-size branch from old-buffer pointer replacement and DeleteLayer through the new buffer allocation, and compared DeleteLayer cleanup against RastPort/bitmap allocation ownership. Confirmed old off-screen RastPort and bitmap are lost without frees, whether or not replacement succeeds; scoped to caller-enabled buffering because Wanderer's compile-time switch is disabled (GD5876). No preference, rendering, resize or allocation failure was run; source-only.
IconList FmtSizeToString arithmetic candidate withdrawal (GD5879 withdrawn; 2026-10-25): rechecked `FmtSizeToString()` at `iconlist.c:328-369`. The earlier 500,000,000-byte example enters the megabyte branch (`num >= 1,048,576`), which widens multiplication to UQUAD. The kilobyte branch is restricted to 1,024 through 1,048,575, so `num * 10 + 512` remains below 10,486,262 and cannot overflow a 32-bit ULONG. The evidence does not support the alleged overflow; removed GD5879 from the candidate report and master index. No replacement example was established. No UI or file-size formatting was run; source-only.
AppIcon failed-clone candidate consolidation (GD5889 withdrawn as duplicate of GD9535; 2026-10-25): rechecked `iconwindow_volumelist.c:949-956` and the direct `LayoutIconA()` caller. This is the same unchecked `DupDiskObject()` result and NULL dereference already recorded in GD9535 (`layouticon.c:71-84`; duplication failure paths in `dupdiskobject.c:143-147,170-210,258-308`). Removed the duplicate GD5889 report section and index entry; GD9535 remains the canonical finding. No refresh or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

ScreenDepth hook notification source recheck (GD5954 confirmed; 2026-10-25): matched the public `ScreenNotifyMessage.snm_Code` contract to the `ScreenDepth()` call into `FireScreenNotifyMessageCode()`. The message-port path assigns `code`; the hook path leaves the stack message field unset before `CallHook()`. Scoped the finding to `SNA_Hook` subscribers and documented the indeterminate ScreenDepth flags; no UI/API operation was run. Source-only.

DisplayAlert encoded-record alignment candidate recheck (GD5955 confirmed; 2026-10-25): re-read `requester_makebody()` and the public DisplayAlert input layout. Its UWORD coordinate dereference is performed at each record start; parser advancement is `text length + 5`, so an even-length line makes the next coordinate odd-aligned when the first record is aligned. The m68k-amiga ROM manifest selects Intuition, and odd word access faults on classic m68k. Expanded the report with exact trigger, consequence, and architecture scope. No alert or fault was run. Source-only.

OpenScreen decorator-construction candidate recheck (GD5956 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the selected non-SKINS OpenScreen call into `int_LoadDecorator()`, where `ScrDecorObj = NewObjectA(...)` is followed by unconditional `GetAttr()`. Verified `GetAttr()` invokes the `OOP_DoMethod` macro, which obtains `o_Class` through the supplied object pointer. A NULL constructor result therefore dereferences NULL before the failure can propagate to OpenScreen. Added explicit non-SKINS and constructor-failure scope to the report. No allocation failure or screen open was induced. Source-only.

X11 hardware cursor allocation candidate recheck (GD5957 confirmed; 2026-10-25): verified `X11SOFTMOUSE=0` in the local X11 header, the matching Xcursor function table and hardware-cursor capability advertisement, then traced `SetCursorShape()` from the returned `XcursorImageCreate()` pointer directly to `image->pixels` and hotspot writes with no NULL test. Scoped the finding to the default hardware-cursor path; the software-mouse compile-time branch bypasses it. No host allocation failure or cursor update was induced. Source-only.

X11 display visual-copy allocation candidate recheck (GD5958 confirmed; 2026-10-25): distinguished the checked host `XGetVisualInfo()` result from the separate unchecked `AllocMem()` for persistent `xsd->vi`. The latter is immediately used as the `memcpy()` destination, then as the source of later display setup state. Scoped the trigger to successful host query plus failed AROS allocation during hosted X11 initialization. No X11 startup or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

X11 host-library init rollback candidate recheck (GD5959 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced libc-load failure after `x11_handle` has been installed globally. The callback manually closes the handle and leaves the global non-NULL; the generic generated init failure path calls the EXPUNGELIB set, whose X11 host-library expunge callback closes that non-NULL handle again. Verified rollback ordering in `compiler/autoinit/functions.c` and `set_call_libfuncs()` failure semantics in `compiler/libinit/libinit.c`. HostLib behavior on the second close remains external and untested. Source-only.

X11 VidMode-list ownership candidate recheck (GD5960 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the `USE_VIDMODE` query through `x11_fullscreen_supported()` and its startup caller. A successful mode-list query with count zero or one stores the allocated list in static `videomodes`, returns unsupported, and has no matching XFree path; source references show later consumption only on the supported path. Scoped the leak to successful queries returning fewer than two modes and noted repeated-check overwrite as conditional. No host VidMode query was run. Source-only.

X11 bitmap class-hint allocation candidate recheck (GD5961 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful window creation into the class-hint setup. `XAllocClassHint()` is followed by two field writes with no NULL check, before `XSetClassHint()`. Scoped the finding to successful X window creation plus failed class-hint allocation. No X11 window or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

X11 bitmap class-hint ownership candidate recheck (GD5962 confirmed; 2026-10-25): searched the complete `x11gfx_onbitmap.c` for the class-hint pointer and XFree calls. The allocated structure is populated and passed to `XSetClassHint()` but never freed. Checked the Xlib API contract: `XAllocClassHint()` storage is released with `XFree()`, and setting the property does not transfer ownership. Added the documented ownership and per-window trigger to the report. No host window was created. Source-only.

X11 framebuffer icon-pixmap ownership candidate recheck (GD5963 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `init_icon()` creation through its local return value into `XSetWMHints()`, then followed framebuffer disposal. The pixmap ID is not stored in the instance layout, and disposal destroys windows plus the framebuffer drawable/colormap but does not free the icon pixmap. Scoped the leak to nonzero icon pixmap results and disposal while the shared X connection persists. No X11 window or disposal was run. Source-only.

X11 PseudoColor icon-cell ownership candidate recheck (GD5964 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the PseudoColor icon pixel loop and checked the selected host-library function table. Successful `XAllocColor()` calls feed drawing but their pixel IDs are not accumulated or released; `XFreeColors()` is not loaded. Verified the Xlib contract that callers release allocated cells and that duplicate allocations by one client increment the shared-cell allocation count. Scoped the issue to PseudoColor icon creation and successful allocations. No host display or icon was used. Source-only.

X11 clipboard-port startup rollback candidate recheck (GD5965 confirmed, conditional; 2026-10-25): traced event-task startup ordering, clipboard `CreateMsgPort()`/`AddPort("HOST_CLIPBOARD")`, the parent `initclasses()` failure rollback, and task-exit cleanup. The worker signals ready before publishing the clipboard port; if the port is published before the parent signals kill, exit deletes only the notification port and leaves the named clipboard port in the system list. Recorded the race window and conditional no-consumer consequence in the report. No startup failure or client request was induced. Source-only.

X11 clipboard large-selection candidate recheck (GD5966 confirmed and refined; 2026-10-25): traced both XA_STRING and UTF8_STRING selection-request branches. XA_STRING calculates an XMaxRequestSize-derived threshold but comments out the comparison and hardcodes the one-request branch; the fallback is TODO. UTF8_STRING also sends one replacement. Both paths send SelectionNotify with the property after XChangeProperty without observing asynchronous property errors. Checked ICCCM selection-owner requirements for INCR and error-confirmed SelectionNotify. Replaced the older "larger than one property request" wording with server-limit-dependent trigger and consequence; no transfer was run. Source-only.

X11 shared-memory `shmat()` sentinel candidate recheck (GD5967 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `shmget()` success into the `shmat()` result check. The code rejects NULL only, while the host API returns `(void *)-1` on failure; that value passes into `XShmAttach()` and is returned as accepted state if the server attach succeeds. Traced the stored address onward into `XShmCreateImage()`. Documented the POSIX/System V return contract and kept the final consequence conditional on XShmAttach behavior. No shared-memory failure or X11 image operation was induced. Source-only.

X11 shared-memory duplicate image-read candidate recheck (GD5968 confirmed; 2026-10-25): read `get_xshm_ximage()` and its bitmap image-read callers. Each helper call performs XSync followed by two identical XShmGetImage calls, discarding the first result; the helper is called once for each scanline chunk, including temporary-pixmap fallback. Scoped as redundant per-chunk server work and status loss; no performance benchmark or image read was run. Source-only.

X11 HIDD startup input-driver registration candidate recheck (GD5969 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `X11_Startup()` object creation and both `HW_AddDriver()` calls against keyboard, mouse, Hidd_Input, and HW class/interface declarations. The passed objects are `CLID_Hidd_Kbd`/`CLID_Hidd_Mouse`, subclasses of `CLID_Hidd_Input` exposing `Hidd_Input`, while `HW_AddDriver` belongs to `CLID_HW`; neither consumer class declares the HW interface. OOP dispatch returns zero for missing methods, so keyboard registration yields NULL, mouse registration is skipped, and startup returns FALSE before display-driver registration. No startup was run. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator auto-repeat state candidate recheck (GD5970 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): searched all `XAutoRepeat*`, keyboard-control queries and exits in `makexkeytable.c`. The generator disables repeat without saving prior state, turns it on on normal completion and in the IO-error handler, and exits on output-open/short-write errors before that normal restoration. Confirmed the `change-x11keymaptable` target invokes the tool. Report now distinguishes prior-off state corruption from error exits that leave repeat disabled. No utility or host setting was run. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator final-stream-error candidate recheck (GD5971 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the 256-byte `fwrite()` check through `fclose()` and process exit. Full `fwrite()` count is checked, but `fclose()` result is ignored before `exit(0)`, leaving delayed buffered write/flush/close errors unreported. Scoped the trigger to late stream errors after the complete count. No file error or generation was induced. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator build-target scope correction (GD5970/GD5971 retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): rechecked `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/mmakefile.src:57-82` and the selected X11 HIDD dependencies. The ordinary `x11keymaptable` prerequisite copies checked-in mapping assets; it does not run `makexkeytable`. Only the explicit `change-x11keymaptable` target invokes the interactive host utility. GD5970 and GD5971 therefore apply when a user explicitly runs that target/tool, not during routine hosted-X11 HIDD builds. Both findings remain valid for that opt-in configuration; no host utility or setting was used.

WinGDI User32 host-resource expunge candidate recheck (GD5972 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful GDI, User32 and native interface/handle acquisitions into `gdi_hostlib_expunge()`. Expunge releases GDI and native globals but omits both `user_func` interface drop and `user_handle` close; no later cleanup reference exists on the successful path. Scoped to MinGW WinGDI expunge after successful initialization. No host DLL lifecycle was run. Source-only.

Cocoa keyboard callback argument candidate recheck (GD5973 confirmed; 2026-10-25): matched the Cocoa keyboard class callback type and `cocoa_input_poll()` invocation against the public Hidd keyboard IRQ handler contract and InputHW event forwarding. The poller passes a UWORD rawkey as the callback's second argument; consumers expect a pointer to `pHidd_Kbd_Event` and receive the value unchanged through `InputHW__CallBackFunc()`. Scoped to recognized key events with registered consumers. No Cocoa event was run. Source-only.

Cocoa input-poller process creation candidate recheck (GD5974 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful driver registration through `CreateNewProc(ptags)` and startup's unconditional continuation to resident success. The returned process pointer is ignored; the poller is the only selected path draining the host event ring and calling input callbacks. Scoped to process-creation failure after driver registration. No process failure or input event was induced. Source-only.

Cocoa poller DOS-open failure candidate recheck (GD5975 confirmed; 2026-10-25): re-read the full process entry and its creation caller. The task's own `OpenLibrary()` result is tested only to decide whether to call `Delay(1)`; when NULL, the unconditional infinite poll loop has no wait/backoff/exit. The creator's earlier DOS open is a separate reference and is closed after `CreateNewProc()`, so it does not ensure the worker's second open succeeds. No DOS open failure was induced. Source-only.

LinuxFB nested-display construction cleanup candidate recheck (GD5976 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `LinuxFBGfx__Root__New()` from superclass object creation through `OOP_NewObject()` for the nested display. Failure cleanup unmaps framebuffer memory and closes the device but does not dispose the superclass-created graphics object. The nested constructor can return NULL when its input framebuffer metadata is absent or `get_pixfmt()` rejects a reported visual/storage format; OOP_NewObject propagates the method's NULL result without reclaiming unrelated partial objects, and HW_AddDriver frees only its failed DriverNode. Confirmed the leaked outer instance and conditional trigger; no framebuffer was opened. Source-only.

LinuxFB DirectColor gamma scaling candidate recheck (GD5977 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `r_step/g_step/b_step` derivation into `SetGamma()` indexing and `FBIOPUTCMAP`. Components of 9–15 bits produce a zero step and repeatedly sample source index 255; a 16-bit maximum also makes `1 << bits` truncate into the UWORD `scale_size` as zero, skipping the write loop while returning TRUE. Recorded both arithmetic cases and the conditional framebuffer-format scope. No gamma operation or ioctl was run. Source-only.

LinuxFB console-mode restore and tty-lifetime candidate recheck (GD5978 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced console open/mode changes in `LinuxFBDisplay__Hidd_Display__CreateObject()` through nested bitmap failure and the registered reset callback. The failure return has no rollback. On display removal, `LinuxFBGfx__Root__Dispose()` removes the callback before cleanup; `cleanup_linuxfb()` unmaps framebuffer memory and closes only the framebuffer fd, not the console fd or modes. Confirmed the conditional leaked tty descriptor and lost restore path. No console ioctl or display removal was run. Source-only.

IntelGMA EDID failure-path candidate recheck (GD5979 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): traced both duplicated EDID consumers, `probe_monitor()` and `G45_parse_ddc()`. Each destination is uninitialized stack storage; each ignores the `WriteRead` BOOL and checks checksum/header anyway. Verified the I2C device wrapper returns the transaction status and the I2C master reports failed transfers as FALSE. A false-valid buffer changes VGA/LVDS selection in startup; the mode enumerator can also add timings from it. Kept false acceptance conditional on residual bytes after failed/partial transfer. No I2C or display path was run. Source-only.

GD5421 detailed source and SMP scheduling recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the report entry from current source. `WaitTOF()` uses a stack node with `AddTail`/`Remove` under local-only `Disable()`; the VBlank `ForeachNode()` reads `ln_Succ` after calling `Signal()`. ExecSMP Signal can schedule an affinity-bound waiter on a different CPU, so the waiter may remove and return its stack node before CPU 0 advances the interrupt traversal. Concurrent callers can also interleave shared tail-link writes. Revalidated the selected Raspberry Pi package includes graphics.library and timer, its AArch64 kernel includes `kernel_execsmp`, and the BCM2711/2712 timer causes VBlank only on CPU 0 while other cores are schedulable. Kept default packaging of portable Workbench callers unconfirmed; the finding is scoped to public API use on this selected SMP configuration. No VBlank or schedule was run; source-only.


GD5422 pending DBufInfo queue interleaving recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the candidate from `internal_QueueDBufInfo()` and `TOF_VBlank()`. Queue insertion stores `dbi_Link1` then publishes the head; VBlank independently unlinks the head through `link`, clears its link/count, and replies both messages. Local-only `Disable()` does not serialize CPU 0 with another ExecSMP CPU. Traced Intuition `ChangeScreenBuffer()` into `ChangeVPBitMap()` and `FreeScreenBuffer()` waiting for `dbi_SafeMessage` before freeing the screen buffer. Identified interleavings that can overwrite the new head (losing its replies) or publish a new head linked to an already replied/cleared DBufInfo (allowing repeat traversal). SDL `Native32` image-pitch caller reconciliation (GD9693 disposition: no new finding; 2026-10-25): re-read SDL bitmap `PutImage()` pitch construction and `Native32` post-creation `BytesPerPixel` override (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:376-449`), the public HIDD `PutImage` contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:2781-2818`), and all in-tree `HIDD_BM_PutImage()` expressions. ExtractColor output-origin source recheck (GD5751 promoted, 2026-10-25): verified the public minimum mask-size contract (`extractcolor.c:40-58`), source-coordinate writes (`extractcolor_renderfunc.c:71-100`), one-row raster size (`RASSIZE(1,1) == 2`; `gfx.h:43`, `allocraster.c:57`) and bit index (`graphics_intern.h:292-293`). A 1x1 analyzed rectangle at source x=16 therefore writes at byte offset 2, beyond a 1x1 output raster. The docs do not explicitly describe coordinate origin, and no checked-in C caller was found, so the report qualifies confidence on that semantic edge. No extraction was run; source-only. Numbered headings and active link counts are unchanged (1,809 and 1,769); GD5751 remains indexed, not an unlinked disposition.


Graphics Area scanline upper-bound follow-up (GD9698 added, 2026-10-25): rechecked the already body-read `areafillpolygon()` loops and `AreaEnd()` caller. `WORD` is signed 16-bit (`exec/types.h:58-62`); both scanline loops compare this variable with inclusive `bounds->MaxY` (`areafill.c:105-111,167-170`). `AreaEnd()` closes a four-vertex polygon, computes inclusive bounds, verifies TmpRas capacity, then calls the fill (`areaend.c:88-90,115-140`). A 2×2 rectangle spanning y=32766..32767 reaches the convex path with a 4-byte mask; after y=32767, increment conversion remains representable only as a `WORD`, so the inclusive comparison cannot become false. Added GD9698 for nontermination; no in-tree caller at this boundary was found. No Area operation was run; source-only. No body line credit added.

AreaEnd WORD_MAX finding reconciliation (GD9698 withdrawn as duplicate of GD5708; 2026-10-26): compared both report sections and index anchors; they describe the same inclusive `WORD` scanline loops at `areafill.c:118,151` and the same `AreaEnd()` boundary. Removed the later duplicate GD9698 and retained canonical GD5708, strengthening it with exact 2×2 coordinates, TmpRas gating, the post-fill BltPattern path, and medium confidence for target/compiler-dependent signed narrowing. The source uses integer promotions for `y++`, followed by an out-of-range conversion back to `WORD`; this is implementation-defined, so the nontermination claim is limited to the project's ordinary two's-complement behavior. No new body credit or runtime/build was involved.

GD6174 ClipRect pool failure path recheck and detail restoration (2026-10-25): inspected `_AllocClipRect()` and its consumers in source order. When no per-layer spare node exists, `_AllocClipRect()` returns `AllocPooled()` directly; `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` writes fields through that result without checking it. Separately, `_ShowLayer()` calls `AllocPooled()` directly and immediately writes bounds/visibility fields. Confirmed the pool is checked at initialization only, and later failure paths are reachable through the shared builder's four callers (`BeginUpdate()`, `_BackupPartsOfLayer()`, `_ShowPartsOfLayer()`, `_InternalInstallClipRegion()`) and `_ShowLayer()` during layer creation. Traced the selected layer/layer-info lock spans and distinguished this ClipRect-node failure from GD6175's backing-BitMap failure. Restored GD6174 as a detailed, high-confidence source candidate; exact allocation failure was not induced. No body-line credit added.


GD6175 refresh backing-bitmap failure detail restoration (2026-10-25): revalidated both existing source traces. For simple refresh, `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` stores an unchecked `AllocBitMap()` result as the destination and calls `BltBitMap()`; selected `ChangeLayerShape()` and `MoveSizeLayer()` callers request this backup mode. For smart refresh, hidden ClipRect construction in `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` and `_ShowLayer()` leaves a NULL `BitMap` on allocation failure; the list-copy path can use a failed result immediately or install a hidden node whose bitmap is later selected for reveal. Confirmed selected `BltBitMap()` evaluates `IS_HIDD_BM()` on both bitmap arguments before any NULL guard, and the macro dereferences the bitmap. Replaced the indexed stub with a detailed finding, preserving the distinction from GD6174's ClipRect-node allocation. No failure or blit was run; no body-line credit added; source-only.


GD6176 screen-background callback detail restoration (2026-10-25): rechecked the final uncovered-region loop in `CollectPixelsLayer()` against the public `CollectPixelsLayerMsg` structure and the selected in-tree Lens callback. The path writes MinX and then MinY into `xSrc`, leaves `ySrc` unset, writes MaxY into `yDest`, and leaves `minterm` unset. The message declaration confirms these fields are separate. Lens ignores the callback when `bm` is NULL, so documented the impact as conditional on external/public clients consuming screen-background callbacks rather than claiming an in-tree failure. Replaced the indexed stub and corrected the master-index title. No callback or pixel operation was run; no body-line credit added; source-only.

GD6177 superbitmap omission detail restoration (2026-10-25): revalidated the empty `IS_SUPERREFRESH(l)` branch in the fully reviewed `CollectPixelsLayer()` body against its public function description and selected Layers export. GD6182 layer-construction shape ownership failure detail restoration (2026-10-25): traced `NewRectRegion()` ownership through `CreateLayerTagList()` allocation and cleanup. GD5692 is therefore retained at medium confidence, conditional on a transient lock failure coinciding with successful default-screen window creation. ### Zune Preferences Save As filename bound and helper pass (GD5690 re-established; 2026-10-25)

A near-capacity selected path can therefore overrun the 1,000-byte static destination; this append precedes the configdata allocation check. With caller size 998, output can be 997 path characters plus NUL. `main_saveas_menu()` then appends the six-character `.prefs` suffix and NUL into the 1,000-byte array, requiring up to 1,004 bytes. This confirms a concrete 4-byte overrun at the helper's maximum successful output; GD5690 confidence is raised to high. No requester was run.

### QuickPart Delete/AddFree allocation-failure caller pass (GD5689 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Reconciled selected `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src`, `QP_ccApp.c`'s Delete action and `QP_ccPartitionContainer.c`'s AddFree method. Delete checks allocation of its bookkeeping node but not the free-space MUI object stored in `PCCN_ChildObj`, then passes the node into AddFree. In the non-merge case AddFree links the node and calls `OM_ADDMEMBER` with that possibly NULL object; the operation is still queued. ### Generic gfx HIDD buffered-operation scratch sizing and caller pass (GD5687 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Re-read `DoBufferedOperation()` in `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c` and traced all five call sites. It sets 4,096 rows from `PIXBUFBYTES >> 2`, clamps only to request height, and multiplies rows by full-width 32-bit row size. Thus 1,920x1,080 requests allocate 8,294,400 bytes (7.91 MiB) in one scratch buffer, and 3,840x2,160 requests allocate 33,177,600 bytes (31.64 MiB), despite the nominal 16,384-byte constant. Allocation failure retries one row; the duplicate correctness effect when both allocations fail remains in GD5732. GD5687 is retained for avoidable large per-call memory consumption, high confidence in calculation and medium workload impact. No graphics operation or allocation was run.

### Text datatype CHRS growth-allocation failure and subsequent-chunk pass (GD5683 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Re-read the full `LoadTextAsIFF()` CHRS loop and traced its DTF_IFF load caller. A later CHRS iteration then allocates only its own `add_size` but uses the stale nonzero `pre_size` as the destination offset and records the combined length. If that later allocation succeeds, `ReadChunkBytes()` writes past its end. ### BoingIconBar oversize-icon range mutation and menu caller pass (GD5679 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Reconciled selected BoingIconBar target and `SetWindowParameters()` with `Show_Selected_Level()`/menu selection. A width overflow truncates the current range and assigns the next level's beginning to the current icon index. If that icon is first in its range, the next level begins on the same too-wide icon; its pass repeats the failure and moves the next boundary back to that index. This can propagate across later levels, leaving them empty; current-level display uses adjacent level beginnings as its bounds. GD5679 is retained at high source confidence. ### Picture datatype chunky-buffer/PDTA_BitMap cache consistency pass (GD5672 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Traced selected `PDT_WritePixelArray()`, `PDTA_BitMap` OM_GET, and `ConvertChunky2Bitmap()`. Same-format writes update only `SrcBuffer` and set `Layouted = FALSE`; a prior lazy `SrcBM` is neither freed nor refreshed. The getter returns existing `SrcBM` without reconversion. Thus the supported sequence write → get source bitmap → same-format write → get source bitmap exposes stale bitmap pixels, while layout/read-pixel code uses current source buffer. ### Picture bitmap-to-chunky width narrowing and consumers (historical GD5671; consolidated into GD9804; 2026-10-25)
Traced AROS `ConvertBitmap2Chunky()` through `ReadPixelLine8()` to `ReadPixelArray8()` and its early invalid-range check. The source bitmap header width is ULONG/UWORD-sized at the caller, while the API width is signed WORD. At width 32,769 on the supported 16-bit signed representation, it narrows to -32,767; endpoint calculation produces -32,768 from xstart 0, so ReadPixelArray8 returns zero. The converter ignores the result, advances the destination offset, and returns success; its `AllocSrcBuffer()` allocation is not cleared. Both asynchronous layout and PDTM_READPIXELARRAY consume that buffer. This same picture caller was later included in GD9804 along with animation and MUI bitmap callers; GD5671 was a duplicate ID and has been removed from the report/index. No wide bitmap was converted.


### BoingIconBar preference notification wakeup recheck (GD5670 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Traced preference `StartNotify()` setup, `BIBport` draining at the top of the main loop, both visible-window and no-window branches, optional focus-timer setup failure, and timer rearming (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:368-397,425-446,518-635`). The visible-window `Wait()` omits the preference port signal; if timer setup fails, the application still starts with `FocusMask == 0`, and no other event is required to arrive. A queued preference notification therefore remains pending until an unrelated selected event wakes the loop. Kept GD5670 with the timer-failure condition and unbounded idle delay stated explicitly; with the timer active the delay is ordinarily bounded by its 100 ms tick. No timer failure, notification or GUI event was induced. Source-only.

Traced the click-inside assignment to `data->nlistviewobj`, the outside-click comparison to the NList child `obj`, the parent NListview raw-key handler registration and forwarding method, and MUI's active/default/other handler dispatch order (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc.c:1286-1297`; `NList_mcc2.c:992-1032,1154-1161`; `nlistview_mcc/NListview.c:119-132,673-680`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:2240-2304`). ### NList core constructor full-body and failed-superclass ownership pass (GD9720 added; 2026-10-25)

Read all 1,659 physical lines / 1,283 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c`, including construction, setup, failed-setup cleanup, cleanup and disposal. Traced `mNL_New()`'s precreated image and nested group through the selected `MUIC_Group` superclass constructor (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/library.c:50-56`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:304-326,335-351,415-418,457-467`). If the Group's internal Family allocation fails, its constructor disposes only the partial Group before it parses/adopts the supplied `Child` tag. NList returns immediately when `DoSuperNew()` fails (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:352-380`) and does not dispose the locally created `grp`; the nested image is likewise not owned by the failed outer Group. The same occurs if creation of the nested group fails after the image was created. Added GD9720, conditional on those allocation failures. Other constructor allocation failures checked after object ownership transfer route through `OM_DISPOSE`; no additional independent finding established in this body. No class construction or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

### NList temporary wrap-line insertion failure-path pass (GD9721 added; 2026-10-25)

Reviewed `NL_InsertTmpLine()` in `NList_func2.c` and its selected caller `NL_DoWrapLine()` in `NList_mcc4.c`. In-capacity insertion shifts pointers before `AllocTypeEntry()`; failure returns without restoring the array or changing the active count, so the active list can contain a duplicate and omit its former final row. Capacity-growth insertion likewise publishes `NList_First`/`LastEntry` before the entry allocation and leaves those values changed when the new pointer array is freed. Added GD9721 for this non-transactional failure path. This is a targeted function/caller pass only: no full-file line credit is claimed, and all other `NList_func2.c` methods and broader target coverage remain open. No allocation failure or GUI operation was run; source-only.


### NList insertion allocation-loop and temporary-row deletion recheck (GD9722 added; 2026-10-25)

Read the complete `NL_List_Insert()` body and traced `MUIM_NList_Insert`, single/wrap method dispatch, and public tag callers. Both the grown-array and spare-capacity loops advance `ent3` only after a successful `AllocTypeEntry()`; a failed pool allocation leaves the loop condition unchanged and spins forever. Both paths also mutate list state before entering the loop. Added GD9722. Rechecked `NL_DeleteTmpLine()`'s active-row selection boundary: its `ent+1 <= NList_Entries` access occurs before the pointer shift, when that endpoint is the old final entry, and subsequent active-index clamping keeps the shifted array index in range; rejected the suspected sentinel dereference. This targeted pass adds no full-translation-unit line credit. No allocation failure or GUI operation was run; source-only.


### NList entry-record cleanup on rejected construction (GD9723 added; 2026-10-25)

During the full `NL_List_Insert()` body review, traced each TypeEntry allocation through the selected `MUIM_NList_Construct` dispatcher and both success/failure branches. If construction returns NULL, insertion counts the item as rejected but loses the allocated TypeEntry without returning it to the EntryPool; repeated rejected items leak one record each. Added GD9723. Also checked the related `NL_List_Replace()` NULL-construction branch; it removes the old row, but the documented replacement contract does not define failed construction semantics, so this behavior remains an unpromoted candidate pending broader contract/caller review. This targeted source review adds no whole-file credit. No hook, insertion, replacement, or allocation failure was run; source-only.

CursorFB fixed-range candidate platform/mode recheck (GD5731 retained and qualified; 2026-10-25): traced hosted SDL and X11 mode construction into generic sync/display setup. SDL_ListModes() entries are rejected only when wider/taller than the current host mode, then their w/h values are copied directly into sync tags (arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:235-268); generic Sync defaults HMax/VMax to HDisp/VDisp (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:133-144). This supports an in-tree hosted configuration if the host exposes dimensions above 16,384 and within signed-WORD cursor-coordinate range. The selected headless HIDD clamps both dimensions to 16,384 (headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:37-38,234-241), so it cannot trigger the range. Kept GD5731 conditional on host mode availability and cursor overlap; no runtime display query/drawing was run.

GD9658 display-edge threshold correction (2026-10-25): rechecked CursorFB's caller condition against cursor_Draw() clipping (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:158-173) and generic PutImage's pixel loop (gfx_bitmapclass.c:2852-2893). The earlier ledger wording implied a bitmap/display width of at least 32,776 pixels, but this is unnecessary: with a 32,768-pixel bitmap and cursor top-left at 32,760, cursor_Draw clips the cursor to the visible final eight pixels. PutImage at x=32,760 with width 16 writes those eight representable positions before later x values narrow. Corrected GD9658's trigger to require bitmap width/height >=32,768, a cursor at 32,760, and an overlapping positive extent reaching at least 32,768. The mode availability and target-specific narrowing remain conditional; no display operation was run.

Graphics font-support helper full-body/caller pass (GD5916 expanded; no new finding; 2026-10-25): read all 166 physical lines / 102 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/graphics/fontsupport.c`, confirmed it is selected by `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:15`, and checked each helper. `CalcHashIndex()` is used with power-of-two table sizes 16 and 8; its byte-sum truncation preserves the low bits used by those masks. `tfe_hashlookup()` returns an entry after releasing its table semaphore, but its only callers (`ExtendFont()` and `StripFont()`) hold the outer `fontsem`; insertion/removal likewise occur under that font semaphore, so no independent hash-node lifetime race was established in the selected uses. GD9805 bitmap-size trigger confirmation (2026-10-25): traced MUI's LONG dimension tags through selected `AllocBitMap()` to the plain-bitmap metadata assignment. `struct BitMap.Rows` and `.BytesPerRow` are UWORD; `AllocBitMap()` stores the requested row count and computes byte stride from width. Thus a 16x32,768 bitmap is representable at 64 KiB per plane, and a 32,768x1 bitmap is also a modest-area case; both cross the corresponding signed-WORD loop bound in `remap_bitmap()`. This sharpens the previous broad availability caveat: trigger still requires successful source/destination allocation and target signed narrowing, but not a high-area bitmap. No body credit or finding ID changed; no allocation or remapping was run. Source-only.
