GD5366 IntelGMA `PutImageLUT` detail restoration and caller-scope recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the missing detailed entry from the surviving coverage note and re-read `GMABM__Hidd_BitMap__PutImageLUT`, its method-table registration, generic superclass implementation and the checked-in graphics route (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_bitmapclass.c:1571-1695,2197-2199`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3924-3991`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:67-85,696-731`). The IntelGMA override dereferences `msg->pixlut->pixels` on `fbgfx` bitmaps before its allocation fallback; for a NULL LUT structure this faults immediately, while the generic superclass handles a missing LUT/table as raw pixel values. A checked-in `WritePixelArray8()` on a plain bitmap obtains the generic cached PlanarBM object, and HIDD `AllocBitMap()` allocates the per-bitmap pixel table for displayable bitmaps; these paths do not establish the null-LUT call into IntelGMA. Searched all in-tree `HIDD_BM_PutImageLUT` call sites; no IntelGMA call with a missing LUT was found. Restored GD5366 with external HIDD callers as the remaining trigger and medium caller confidence; updated the master-index summary. The x86-64 PC monitor aggregate selects IntelGMA through active MetaMake dependencies. No HIDD call or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

GD5367 `WritePixelArray8()` maximum-row width recheck (2026-10-25): re-read the public vector, `wp8_render()`, bitmap clipping and generic `PutImageLUT` method (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:16-45,64-76`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:101-140,680-731,1064-1088`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3892-3893,3924-3940`). A 32,768-pixel row on a bitmap of that width can be requested with WORD endpoints 0 and 32767 and satisfies the documented array width. After clipping, `wp8_render()` computes 32768 but stores it in signed WORD before passing it to an HIDD method whose width is also WORD; that type cannot represent the positive extent. On low-word conversion targets the result is negative and the generic method returns without writing; exact conversion/manifestation is target-dependent. No in-tree call uses a bitmap this wide; PNG remap and FTManager dimensions are WORD-limited and their checked paths do not establish the trigger. Restored GD5367 from source with medium manifestation confidence and added the master-index summary. No wide bitmap or call was created; source-only.

ReadPixelArray8 width-boundary paired-path recheck (GD4030 retained; no duplicate; 2026-10-25): re-read `rp8_render()` and the generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImageLUT()` implementation against the corresponding WritePixelArray8 boundary candidate GD5367. A clipped inclusive rectangle x=0..32767 on a bitmap at least 32768 pixels wide retains a 32768-pixel row; `rp8_render()` stores that width in signed `WORD` before the HIDD call (`rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:21-32`; clipping in `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140,1064-1085`). The inherited generic reader stores its x loop index in `WORD` and tests `x < msg->width` in both the temporary-line and allocation-fallback loops (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4163-4214`); when the width narrows to -32768, neither loop copies row pixels. This is already GD4030's exact root and consequence, so no additional ID was added. The direct `ReadPixelArray8()` caller census finds `rom/graphics/fontsupport.c` and the `ReadPixelLine8()` wrapper; the generated m68k emulator entry is an ABI thunk, not a native C caller. No transfer or target-specific signed-conversion behavior was tested; source-only.

Graphics boot-display hardware-range pointer/caller pass (GD5918 retained with existing reachability limit; 2026-10-25): traced the only checked-in `DDRV_HWRanges` producers. EFI framebuffer stores its one-entry range in static `efifbgfx_ranges`, explicitly retained for the graphics driver lifetime (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_init.c:68-84,114-145`). Nouveau constructs a seven-entry local array in `HIDDNouveauReleaseBootDisplays()` and passes it only to the handover `dho_FindDisplay()` callback (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:265-307,314-315`); graphics.library consumes it synchronously in `driver_FindBootDisplay()`/`driver_RangesOverlap()` and does not retain that caller pointer (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:176-248`). These callers therefore establish neither a dangling range-array pointer nor the exact-address-space-end overlap trigger in GD5918. The hardware-range argument is used only during New-time handover; external callers must keep it valid through the synchronous registration call. No handover, range mapping or driver registration was run; source-only.


GD9803 selected MemList reader caller correction (2026-10-25; candidate strengthened): the previous VCGfx ledger note said no selected allocator walk concurrent with initialization had been found. A cross-resident pass now traces the actual reader: Raspberry Pi boot selects `kernel-input` and `hidd-vcgfx` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:122,143`); `input.device` has resident priority 30 versus VCGfx 9 and the initial resident array is sorted descending by `krnRomTagScanner()` while building `ResModules` (`rom/devs/input/input.conf:4`; `vcgfx.conf:5`; `rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:311-339`; assigned in `rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:51`). `InitKickTags()` only sorts again if it adds KickTags (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:273-275`). Input's init hook starts `ProcessEvents()` on a new task (`rom/devs/input/input.c:66-80`), whose pre-Wait setup allocates MsgPorts and I/O requests via AllocMem (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:157-194`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:48-52`; `createiorequest.c:59-69`). On ExecSMP the boot task stays on CPU0 while secondary cores are already released before COLDSTART (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107`), allowing that task's shared-lock MemList walk to overlap the VCGfx unlocked AddTail. Updated GD9803's report evidence and qualification: the in-tree reader route is source-confirmed, but the exact simultaneous dispatch remains conditional and was not exercised. No boot, allocation, or scheduler operation was run; source-only.


GD9803 selected reader limitation and resident-order correction (2026-10-25; supersedes prior reader-overlap claim): the initial resident list is sorted in `krnRomTagScanner()` (`rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:311-339`) and installed as `SysBase->ResModules` (`rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:51`); `InitKickTags()` re-sorts only when it adds non-NULL KickTags (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:273-275`). This confirms input priority precedes VCGfx, but does not prove a concurrent reader: the input worker inherits the creating boot task's CPU-0 mask (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:126-164`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:260-280`), and so cannot overlap VCGfx initialization on that same CPU. No other in-tree reader on another active CPU during `InitMem()` has been identified. GD9803 is retained only as a conditional lock-protocol candidate; its writer-side omission is certain, but a selected execution trigger and inconsistent read remain unestablished. No scheduling was run; source-only.

Screen `SA_ShowPointer` platform-selection follow-up (GD5826 strengthened; 2026-10-25): re-read tag parsing and pointer installation in `openscreen.c:738-740,2263-2277`, `ScreenClass__OM_GET/OM_SET` (`screenclass.c:817-819,911-984`), and active monitor pointer dispatch (`misc.c:69-115`, plus `rethinkdisplay.c:180-198`). Repository-wide `ShowPointer` search found no behavioral consumer beyond getter/setter/storage. On SKINS, OpenScreen always installs the monitor's invisible shared pointer regardless of the tag; without SKINS it always installs `DefaultPointer`. Screen activation only toggles monitor-level `MA_PointerVisible`. Therefore the observable mismatch is configuration-specific: `FALSE` fails to hide under non-SKINS, `TRUE` fails to show under SKINS, and later SetAttrs never switches the screen pointer. Updated GD5826's trigger/configuration to these concrete cases. No GUI/pointer action was run; no body-line credit.

The caller successfully loads the segment and duplicates the home lock, then calls `CreateNewProc()` with both values. On NULL, the handler skips its `error:` block, which alone calls `UnLoadSeg()` and `DestroyWBS()`. DOS's error path frees its own temporary resources and unlocks only `homedir` when DOS itself duplicated an omitted `NP_HomeDir`; it does not unload the caller-provided segment or unlock the supplied home lock. `DestroyWBS()` owns the startup arguments and their duplicated locks/names. This confirms GD5831's distinct failed-process-creation cleanup leak; no new ID or body-line credit. No process creation failure or launch was induced; source-only.

On a range merge, `AddFree()` updates the existing free node and clears both `addFree` and `addObj` (`QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:371-403`), so it neither links the supplied `FSNode` nor calls `OM_ADDMEMBER` for its child (`:405-412`). The caller has no post-call `FreeVec(newSpaceNode)` or object-disposal path (`QP_ccApp.c:438-449`). This confirms a normal successful merge leaks the temporary struct; if its child object was created, it is also orphaned. Retained the separate failed-child-allocation/non-merge path as qualified because MUI's `OM_ADDMEMBER(NULL)` behavior was not established. Reframed GD5689 around the high-confidence merge-path ownership leak. No GUI or allocation failure was induced; source-only.


BoingIconBar remap/cache invalidation and second screen-lock caller recheck (GD5692 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced `ReadPrefs()`'s successful lock and per-icon `LayoutIcon()` calls before `UnlockPubScreen()` (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:767,820-837,863-867`), then the separate lock and NULL-screen `LayoutIcon()` loop in `OpenMainWindow()` (`:1405,1497-1505`). The selected `LayoutIconA()` path frees image bitmaps/remap resources and clears `ni_Screen` when passed NULL (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:97-129`). Confirmed `OpenWindowTags()` is a third operation: its `WA_PubScreenName,NULL` is resolved by a distinct `LockPubScreen(pubScreenName)` in Intuition (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:581-603`), failing only if that attempt also has no screen (`:640-643`). Thus the exact conditional sequence can preserve successful window creation after the intervening cache invalidation. Added the two-attempt screen availability condition and reset-restore caller to GD5692; no lock failure or rendering was induced. Source-only.


MUI Window snapshot-to-configdata value-flow recheck (GD5694 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced `Window__MUIM_Snapshot()`'s duplicate `winp.x2 = 0` and missing `winp.y2` initialization (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:4444-4469`) through `MUIA_Application_SetWinPos`, which copies all eight coordinate fields (`application.c:1024-1060`), and the configdata save path, which copies the counted window-position array into the dataspace (`configdata.c:884-906`; `application.c:1273-1290`). No config save was run; source-only.


AmigaGuide asynchronous resize completion recheck (GD5696 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced GM_LAYOUT's `DTSIF_LAYOUT`/`DTSIF_NEWSIZE` producer under `ag_ASyncLayout` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/amigaguideclass.c:614-636`) against AGMT_LAYOUT's worker loop and final flag clear under `si_Lock` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:268-286`). The worker does not hold the producer semaphore at its final NEWSIZE test or LAYOUT clear, so a resize in that interval can set NEWSIZE after the worker's last check without causing another layout iteration. Traced the resulting layout's viewport metric calculations (`amigaguideclass.c:844-953`) and qualified the consequence to potentially stale metrics/scrollbar state until another layout request; timing and UI effect were not reproduced. Source-only.


Intuition timer setup retry-path recheck (GD5698 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): re-read `IntuitionOpen()`'s timer block (`rom/intuition/intuition_init.c:427-449`). `TimerMP` and `TimerIO` are assigned before the failing `CreateIORequest()`/`OpenDevice()` returns; those returns do not release the newly allocated resources, and `TimerBase` remains NULL until `OpenDevice()` succeeds, so a later library-open attempt enters the block again and overwrites stored pointers. Qualified the leak to timer setup failure followed by retry (or a later successful attempt that strands prior resources); no device-open failure or retry was induced. Source-only.
Exec open-vector failure semantics cross-check for GD5698 (2026-10-26; no additional body credit): `OpenLibrary()` invokes the library open vector and returns its result directly (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:89-99`); no close vector is invoked when `IntuitionOpen()` returns NULL. This confirms failed timer allocations remain live for a later retry rather than being released by the library caller. Source-only.

Picture source-buffer overflow and PNG scanline caller recheck (GD5707 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): verified `AllocSrcBuffer()` stores the 16-byte-aligned row stride and multiplies it by height for `AllocVec()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-331`). On 32-bit builds, width 65,535, four-byte pixels and height 16,385 produce stride 262,144 and a wrapped allocation request of 262,144 bytes. PNG publishes those UWORD-compatible dimensions into the Picture BMHD and sends decoded full-width scanlines through `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` (`pngclass.c:245-260,413-415,515-538`); Picture writes each row at the aligned destination stride without checking buffer extent (`pictureclass.c:1093-1150,1185-1207`). The second row begins at the end of the undersized allocation and writes past it. Confirmed both Picture and PNG are in the i386 PC floppy package (`arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:55-60`). No image or allocation was exercised; source-only.


AreaEnd polygon WORD_MAX loop recheck (GD5708 qualified; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced `AreaDraw()` coordinate narrowing (`rom/graphics/areadraw.c:67-75`), AreaEnd bounds and TmpRas size gate (`areaend.c:106-110,130-155,185-195`), both `WORD y <= bounds->MaxY` loops (`areafill.c:118,151`), and the final BltPattern caller (`areaend.c:149-169`). For MaxY 32767, signed-WORD increment is out of range; on ordinary two's-complement narrowing the counter wraps and the inclusive loop does not terminate. Since BltPattern follows the rasterizer return, the old claim of writing past the planar destination is unsupported and removed. No in-tree max-coordinate caller was found; public API boundary retained conditionally by compiler behavior. No AreaEnd or target build was run; source-only.


OS 3.5 icon chunk-finalization result path recheck (GD5709 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced native non-PNG icon selection through `__WriteIcon_WB()`/`WriteStruct()` and `ProcessIcon35()` to `WriteIcon35()` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:396-405`; `diskobjio.c:966-999`). `WriteImage35()` returns its payload-derived `ok` after ignoring `PopChunk()` (`diskobj35io.c:863-893`); `WriteIcon35()` sets overall success from successful image writes, then ignores outer FORM finalization and returns `ok` (`:998-1015,1059-1068`). IFF `PopChunk()` reports failed size-backpatch seeks/writes, end seeks, and pad writes (`workbench/libs/iffparse/popchunk.c:77-131`); the icon stream hook maps short DOS writes and failed seeks to errors (`diskobj35io.c:71-78`). `WriteStruct()` propagates the special hook return (`compiler/arossupport/writestruct.c:274-287`). Traced the Boolean to `PutIconTagList()` and its MODE_NEWFILE target (`puticontaglist.c:124-155`). Confirmed conditional false-success report; no save or I/O failure was induced. Source-only.


OS 3.5 icon IFFHandle ownership recheck (GD5710 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced `WriteIcon35()`'s early returns and `AllocIFF()` success into all later exits (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:898-955,1059-1068`); no `CloseIFF()`/`FreeIFF()` occurs in the writer. DiskFont short `.otag` header boundary recheck (GD5711 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): `OTAG_GetFile()` allocates `sizeof(OTagList)+l` for `l` file bytes and reads the two header words unconditionally (`workbench/libs/diskfont/bullet.c:85-112`). On 32-bit, `OTagList` has two pointers plus `data[1]` (`diskfont_intern.h:78-83`), so `data[1]` begins at the requested allocation end; a 0–3 byte file leaves the second 4-byte word outside the allocation. The identifier mismatch sets `ok` false but does not skip the next independent header comparison, so the read still occurs before failure cleanup. Traced the selected outline-font caller (`af_fontdescr_io.c:72-95`) and scoped this separately from GD2819's tag-pair scan after the header. No malformed font descriptor was loaded; source-only.


GD5712 `.font` entry-count wrap caller trace (2026-10-26): re-read `ReadFontDescr()` and traced its `UWORD` count through `ReadFileEntry()`, the disk-font directory iterator, and `AvailFonts()`. The maximum outline count plus two bitmap entries wraps only when the 65,535-size list includes the two bitmap sizes and all other `UWORD` sizes; the allocation still accommodates the original counts. `ReadFileEntry()` copies zero entries and supplies one zero-initialized special outline attribute, which the directory iterator exposes to `AvailFonts()`. Corrected GD5712 to describe omitted declared sizes and a zero-size enumeration entry; removed any implication of an allocation overrun. Trigger in installed fonts is unverified. No font file was loaded; source-only.


FreeType glyph allocation failure split (GD5713 detailed; GD9835 added; 2026-10-26): traced `RenderGlyph()` bitmap allocation through `GetGlyph()` and diskfont’s `OTAG_GetGlyphMaps()`, `OTAG_CalcMetrics()`, and `OTAG_MakeCharData()`. Bitmap-buffer failure leaves a zero-width map, which is returned as unknown and silently omitted; a proportional font can therefore retain zero advance and no pixels for that character. Separately, failure to allocate the `GlyphMap` structure leaves `ge->GMap == NULL`, after which `GetGlyph()` unconditionally dereferences it. Added GD9835 for this distinct null dereference. Exact FreeType-engine selection depends on the font’s `.otag`; no font, allocator failure, or rendering was exercised. Source-only.

At width 524,304, the computed 65,538-byte stride narrows to 2 while plane allocation retains the full row size; the selected example is `AllocBitMap(524304, 2, 1, 0, NULL)`. No checked-in caller with this width was found, so scope remains direct public API use of the generic plain path. Picture.datatype source-bitmap cache invalidation/caller recheck (GD5672 retained and caller-scoped; 2026-10-26): traced the public PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY message fields in compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h through pictureclass.c dispatch, pixel-format initialization and source-buffer copy, then through PDTA_BitMap OM_GET into ConvertChunky2Bitmap. NListtree OM_NEW pre-superclass failure cleanup pass (GD9837 added; 2026-10-26; partial body/path credit only): traced both pool-creation branches and the common failure cleanup (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5110-5135,5164,5306-5312`) through `NewObjectA()` and rootclass construction (`rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:139-143`; `rom/intuition/rootclass.c:72-91`). NewObjectA supplies the class pointer as the initial OM_NEW object; failure of either private pool creation therefore reaches `CoerceMethod(..., OM_DISPOSE)` with that class pointer. Failure of `DoSuperNew()` leaves `obj == NULL` and reaches the same cleanup. `_Dispose()` immediately computes instance data and uses `obj` in `DoMethod()` (`NListtree.c:5316-5329`; `compiler/include/intuition/classes.h:64`), so these values are not valid partial instances; added GD9837. This is separate from GD9742, where a superclass object already exists but the old-version path returns it without disposal. The second-pool failure also abandons the first pool. No allocation failure or object creation was run. NListtree remains partial; source-only.

CGXVideo OOP attribute-descriptor failure-path closure (2026-10-26; no new GD, no body/LOC credit): resolved the `cgxvideo_init.c` row's open terminator/caller question by tracing its one active `IID_Hidd_BitMap` descriptor (`workbench/libs/cgxvideo/cgxvideo_init.c:11-16`) through `struct IntCGXVBase::attrbases[3]` (`cgxvideo_intern.h:32-37`), `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()`'s sentinel loop and failure cleanup (`rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:49-65`), and `MakeLibrary()`'s `MEMF_PUBLIC|MEMF_CLEAR` base allocation (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:126-145`). If the sole `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` call returns zero, the helper advances to that terminator and skips its non-advancing cleanup loop; therefore existing OD2399's multi-descriptor infinite-loop trigger does not apply to CGXVideo. `cgxv_init()` returns the obtain result directly, and its expunge hook releases bases through the same one-entry descriptor list. NListtree CopyToClip truncated-escape bounds pass (GD9843 added; 2026-10-26; targeted method/caller pass, no whole-body/LOC credit): re-read `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10030-10085`) and traced its input through public Insert and the built-in context-menu choice (`:7064-7119,6568-6578`). Insert copies accepted node names to exactly `strlen(name)+1` bytes by default and performs no ESC validation. The clipboard parser skips two source bytes after every ESC, then advances again and reads/copies without checking for NUL. A name ending in ESC or ESC plus one byte therefore places the next read beyond the node-name allocation. Added GD9843, distinct from GD9816's valid bracketed-sequence mutation and GD9746's documented Active sentinel dereference. The custom CopyToClipHook path bypasses the built-in parser. No name or clipboard operation was run; source-only. The 10,702-line NListtree translation unit and broader Graphics/Desktop goal remain partial.

GD6251 report-detail restoration and failure/caller recheck (2026-10-26; existing finding, no new ID or LOC credit): re-read `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()` and `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` around both ignored calls. `AndRegionRegion()` computes into a temporary region and returns FALSE before clearing/replacing its destination when rectangle allocation fails; its caller has just seeded the destination with the full bitmap rectangle, then continues to treat any remaining rectangles as visible and redraw them. `ClearRegionRegion()` likewise leaves its destination unchanged on allocation failure; after the ignored subtraction, the redraw path enumerates the remaining display region and fills/backfills it, so bitmap-covered pixels can be repainted. Traced the stack-change dispatch through `graphics_compositor.h` and confirmed the monitor target is optional. Replaced the report's ledger-only placeholder with the two concrete triggers, consequences, target scope and confidence. No allocation failure or display operation was run; source-only.

GD6251 ignored region-operation inventory expansion (2026-10-26; existing root cause, no new ID or LOC credit): scanned all region-helper calls in the compositor's visible-region construction and redraw path. In addition to `AndRegionRegion()` and `ClearRegionRegion()`, it ignores `OrRectRegion()` results while seeding display, bitmap and alpha regions and `ClearRectRegion()` results while subtracting opaque/edge rectangles. The corresponding helpers return FALSE on temporary rectangle allocation failure without committing a replacement destination (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:64-101`; `clearrectregion.c:58-105`). Expanded GD6251's detail to include these same-state failures; no separate defect ID was added because they share the ignored allocation-failure contract and are consumed as one visibility/backfill calculation. No allocation failure or rendering was run; source-only.

GD6251 fallback reachability recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): traced ignored visibility-helper results to the normal `BitMapStackChanged()` error path. `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()` and `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` return void; `BitMapStackChanged()` updates `ok` from stack-node allocation and `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()`, not from any region operation. It calls `HIDDCompositorReset()`/`HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` only when that independent flag is false. Thus the region-allocation failure is not automatically converted to the documented single-bitmap fallback. Direct redraw callers likewise receive no region-operation result. Added this recovery-boundary evidence to GD6251; no allocation failure or view change was run; source-only.

NListtree Move KeepStructure destination-path allegation recheck (GD9846 withdrawn; 2026-10-29; method/caller pass, no whole-body or LOC credit): re-read `_NListtree_Move()` and `CreateParentStructure()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2561-2585,2660-2701,8233-8357`). `rom/graphics/areamove.c` explicit full-body, buffer-boundary and caller pass (GD9849 withdrawn as non-observable; 2026-11-01 recheck): the complete 130-line body / 51 `cloc 2.06` C code lines were already credited in the 198/198 graphics.library subtotal. GD9412 empty-region span and point-query recheck (2026-10-26; existing candidate qualified; no LOC credit): re-read the `OrRectRegion()` empty-destination branch and `IsPointInRegion()` comparisons (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:62,85-101`; `rom/graphics/ispointinregion.c:55-77`) against the public signed-WORD rectangle layout (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:45-51`; `regions.h:19-30`). The API copies valid absolute endpoints but stores their difference into signed-WORD local maxima without a span-range guard. Such a conversion is implementation-defined when the span exceeds WORD_MAX; under low-16-bit narrowing, the local max becomes negative and the point query rejects points that passed the absolute bounds check. Kept the finding as a public API boundary issue because no maintained in-tree large-span caller was established, and qualified exact visible behavior by compiler conversion. Expanded GD9412 with these limits and source locations; no geometry operation was run and no body-line credit changed. Source-only.

GD9413 decorator removal lock/reference recheck (2026-10-26; existing candidate detailed; no LOC credit): traced `int_UnloadDecorator()`'s caller-held `ScrDecorSem` contract through `DoASyncAction()` and the input-device action queue (`rom/intuition/decoration.c:129-138`; `inputhandler_actions.c:642-674,678-712`). In the synchronous input-task branch the callback runs inline while the caller's lock is held; for ordinary callers the request is copied and queued, and the caller subsequently releases `ScrDecorSem`. The queued `int_removedecorator()` then unlinks the node and frees its pattern without taking that semaphore or rechecking the zero-reference condition (`decoration.c:103-126`). A later `int_LoadDecorator()` can find/increment the node under the lock before that callback executes, so removal can proceed despite the new reference; the callback also races the protected list traversal. Expanded GD9413 with the async-only trigger and conditional impact. No schedule or decorator operation was run; source-only.

If queued, `int_removedecorator()` creates its reply port before `Remove()` or the `MAGIC_DECORATOR` message; if `CreateMsgPort()` fails, the callback exits without unlinking or notifying the service. GD9428 Group nested-disable propagation recheck (2026-10-26; both conditional imbalances retained; no LOC credit): reread Group's OM_SET tag rewriting and child dispatch (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:473-505,560-633,1004-1020`) against Area's high-bit local disabled flag and low-bit nested count (`classes/area.c:559-590,740-748`). Group suppresses the original local tag during superclass handling, restores it, then forwards every supplied `MUIA_Disabled` value as a child `MUIA_NestedDisabled` without comparing the previous local bit. Thus repeated TRUE increments each descendant's count even though setting the local high bit is idempotent; one later FALSE decrements only once. A Group receiving `MUIA_NestedDisabled=TRUE` from an ancestor retains a positive low count while its local high bit remains clear; a redundant local FALSE still forwards a child decrement and can remove the child's inherited contribution while the Group itself remains disabled. `Group_DispatchMsg()` visits children without an effective-state transition check. Reconfirmed Appearance Preferences uses runtime Disabled updates but does not establish either redundant sequence. No object state was changed; source-only.

GD9429 selected-state export failure and Area-derived settings caller recheck (2026-10-26; candidate retained; no LOC credit): re-read Area Export/Import, Dataspace Add, Window/Group export propagation, and Application Save (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:2092-2121`; `dataspace.c:93-126`; `window.c:4535-4541`; `group.c:3259-3277,3471-3474`; `application.c:2474-2479,2488-2535`). Dataspace allocation failure returns zero before adding the selected-state record; Area discards the result, parent export methods do not propagate it, and Application Save still writes the remaining Dataspace. Import leaves selection unchanged if that record is absent. Refined the maintained example: `developer/debug/test/Zune/settings.c:58` gives an ObjectID to a StringObject, and `String` directly subclasses Area (`classes/string.c:2299-2305`); the test invokes Application Save (`settings.c:14-22`). This confirms an Area-derived identified control and save caller, but does not show it selected during an allocation failure, so the finding's selected-state trigger remains conditional. No settings file, selection or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.
ColorWheel small-size palette fallback check (2026-10-26; no finding/no LOC credit): rechecked `RenderWheel()`'s accepted unframed 8x8 minimum against `GM_DOMAIN`, `ClutWheel()`'s no-pen path, and the selected `AreaEllipse()`/`AreaEnd()` implementation (`workbench/classes/gadgets/colorwheel/support.c:386-423,589-663,738-743`; `colorwheelclass.c:606-636`; `rom/graphics/areaellipse.c:58-110`; `rom/graphics/areaend.c:199-212`). If exact palette pens cannot be allocated and the fallback radius is below four, `data->wheelrx - 4`/`wheelry - 4` underflows as UWORD before conversion to the WORD API. The resulting ellipse has inverted bounds and AreaEnd rejects its TmpRas-size calculation; the later smaller ellipses are rejected as well. The regular outer outline still uses the original valid radius and is clipped to the gadget bitmap, so this establishes degraded/missing interior decoration at the minimum size, but not an independent correctness failure beyond this tiny-widget fallback limitation. No defect added. The full ColorWheel bodies were already credited in the prior target pass; counts unchanged. No palette allocation or rendering was run; source-only.

NListtree Open/Close Active-list selector contract boundary (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the complete `_NListtree_Open()` and `_NListtree_Close()` selectors and their method documentation (`NListtree.c:6670-6734,6866-6918`; `MCC_NListtree.doc:1158-1220,2423-2495`). Both methods can dereference `ln` before the later `if (ln && tn)` guard when callers combine `ListNode_Active` with Head/Tail; Close's Parent selector also reads `data->ActiveList->ln_Parent` directly. The general ActiveList attribute documentation explicitly returns `MUIV_NListtree_ActiveList_Off` when there is no active entry (`MCC_NListtree.doc:189-206`), and construction leaves `ActiveList` zeroed (`NListtree.c:5104-5115,5217-5222,5260-5268`). However, the Open/Close method contracts define which active list/node is used without defining behavior when none exists; their documented examples pair Active list with Active tree node, which safely no-op through the final guard. The selected keyboard Open/Close calls are additionally guarded by `data->ActiveNode` (`NListtree.c:5685-5715`). Thus this pass does not promote a defect based solely on an undocumented invalid selector combination. Keep Open/Close as an explicit contract/caller follow-up; no public caller using Active+Head/Tail or Parent without a selection was found in this search. No method or GUI was run; source-only.

NListtree Open/Close active-selector boundary recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD/LOC credit): re-read the full selector dispatch and API docs for `_NListtree_Open()`/`_NListtree_Close()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:6670-6715,6858-6892`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:1158-1220,2423-2495`) against constructor initialization. `_New()` zeroes the temporary instance; neither the normal no-active case nor an initial `MUIA_NListtree_Active=Off` publishes `ActiveList`, because the only assignment in `SetAttributes()` is guarded by `!initial` (`:5104-5139,4362-4458`). NListtree no-active lookup and relative-entry helper follow-through (GD9848 candidate recheck; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): read complete `_NListtree_FindName()`, `_NListtree_FindUserData()`, `_NListtree_GetEntry()`, `FindTreeNodeByName()`, `FindTreeNodeByUserData()`, and `GetEntryByTotalPos()` bodies (`NListtree.c:1307-1335,2391-2429,2476-2514,8799-8840,8936-8977,9076-9147`). For FindName/FindUserData with the Active list selector, the public Active-Off state maps to `data->ActiveList == NULL`; each helper immediately forms `&ln->ln_List` for `GetHead()` (unless StartNode, which casts the NULL list as a node), so the NULL does reach an invalid list/node access. GD9836 compositor-construction failure caller/registration recheck (2026-10-26; retained; no LOC credit): traced both setup orderings again through `display_Register()` and `compositor_Install()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:366-404`; `graphics_compositor.c:23-59`). If the class is already registered, `display_Register()` calls the unchecked `compositor_Setup()` before `display_Enable()`; if the display registers first, it is enabled and inserted without an object, and later `compositor_Install()` ignores the failed object creation while returning `DD_OK`. In either order the failed compositor does not veto enabling/retaining the eligible display. Rechecked `display_LoadViewPorts()`'s fallback: when `ShowViewPorts` returns FALSE and `display_compositor` is NULL, the code submits only the front viewport bitmap with `HIDD_Display_Show()` (`graphics_display.c:511-565`). The concrete implementation provider is the optional Nouveau HIDD's `CLID_Hidd_Compositor` class (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau.conf:121-134`); this confirms the report's optional-module qualifier, not a default-image claim. No additional issue or caller path established. No allocation failure or display load was run; source-only.

GD9839 software-bitmap implementation path qualification (2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): followed the signed `WORD` extent from `bltpattern_render()` through both software HIDD paths. The base `BM__Hidd_BitMap__PutPattern()` rejects nonpositive dimensions (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3811-3822`); the generic chunky-bitmap class forwards those same signed fields to `HIDD_BM_PutMemPattern*()` (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:832-918`), and every pixel-width helper rejects a nonpositive width or height (`gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:829,974,1122,1328,1474,1736,1999,2332`). LinuxFB's bitmap class derives from `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` and overrides only `SetColors` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:25-35`), confirming the clipped 32,768-pixel span is also dropped on that selected software path. Other accelerated HIDD overrides may differ; no runtime draw or bitmap allocation was performed. Updated GD9839's target/consequence qualification; no finding count or body credit changed. Source-only.


GD9428 Appearance Preferences import sequence recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD): re-read the actual Theme option group construction and every runtime `MUIA_Disabled` setter in `appearanceeditor.c` (`:133-212,368-402,568-700,1028-1111`). DiskFont ReadFontDescr buffered-seek error-path trace (GD9852 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-body/LOC credit): followed both ignored `Flush()`/`Seek()` pairs through DOS read-mode `Flush()` and `Seek()` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/af_fontdescr_io.c:136-145,174-187`; `rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`; `rom/dos/seek.c:68-91`). `Flush()` clears the read-ahead bounds before its cursor-restoration seek can fail; `ReadFontDescr()` then ignores that failure and issues a relative seek with no buffer offset left to correct the physical cursor. It also ignores the relative seek result and continues parsing. Traced the returned descriptor into directory enumeration and direct font lookup callers (`diskfontfunc.c:93-145,842-860,1345-1370`). Added GD9852 for conditional mispositioned descriptor reads; retained the trigger on a failed restoration followed by subsequent I/O, without claiming a default-image module edge. No font file or I/O failure was used; source-only.

AmigaGuide node-position read-ahead error-path follow-up (GD9853 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced both AROS-only `Flush()` calls in `ScanFile()` through `ParseNodeLine()` and `CMD_ENDNODE` into `agn_Pos`/`agn_Length`, then followed those fields into `AllocAGObjectNode()`'s absolute seek and node-body read (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/file.c:109-115,403-410`; `util.c:383-407`). DOS read-mode `Flush()` can clear the buffered unread range and then fail to restore the logical cursor (`rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`); the ignored failure lets the subsequent position query observe the advanced underlying position, so the stored node range is wrong. Added GD9853, separate from GD9852's DiskFont parser consequence and GD6284's unterminated macro scan. The datatype is explicitly buildable but no parent aggregate edge is claimed. No guide or I/O failure was used; source-only.

NListtree clipboard escape parser recheck (GD9816 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): reread `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` and compared its pointer movement with NList's documented simple `ESC`+character formatting codes and built-in copy-hook contract (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10051-10072`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:415-445,466-481,656-665`). For an unbracketed code such as `ESC b` followed by `Hello`, the `s += 2` followed by unconditional `s++` drops the first ordinary character (`H`) before copying. The bracketed `ESC P[...]` case remains as documented in GD9816: `++*s` changes the opening bracket in the stored name and leaves sequence payload in clipboard text. Updated GD9816 to include the simple-code truncation; it is the same parser and finding, not a distinct defect. No name was copied or modified; source-only.

NListtree Exchange second-list selector consequence recheck (GD9813 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or body-line credit): reread the complete `_NListtree_Exchange()` selector and mutation path (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7970-8125`) against the method contract (`:7838-7930`) and helpers `NLRemoveFromTable()`/`NLFindInTable()` (`:1080-1112`). AmigaVideo GD4763 repeated-swap rollback state recheck (2026-10-26; existing finding expanded; no body/LOC credit): traced `HIDD_ViewPortData.PreviousBitmap` through initial wrapping, successive `MakeVPort()` swaps, the failure rollback and `ChangeVPBitMap()` reload (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:130`; `rom/graphics/makevport.c:120-169,222-232`; `changevpbitmap.c:66-105`). `PreviousBitmap` is populated only while NULL and is not cleared on a successful swap; a later swap can dispose the currently wrapped bitmap while retaining the original saved bitmap. If that later `MakeVPort()` fails, rollback restores the original saved object instead of the bitmap that was displayed immediately before the request. The generic caller ignores the failure, reloads from VPD state and queues both DBufInfo replies; Intuition also updates its RastPort and returns TRUE. Expanded GD4763 with this stale-state sequence and kept the visible image consequence at medium confidence because backend behavior after failed rebuild was not exercised. No viewport, buffer swap, allocation failure or VBlank was run; source-only.


ChangeVPBitMap full-body and safe-reply/queue recheck (2026-10-26; GD4763/GD5422 retained; no new finding or LOC credit): reread all 109 lines of `rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c`, then followed `internal_QueueDBufInfo()` and `TOF_VBlank()` in `rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:163-212`, the DBufInfo allocation/free contracts, and `FreeScreenBuffer()`'s wait-before-free caller. Confirmed `ChangeVPBitMap()` publishes `RasInfo->BitMap` and calls `MakeVPort()` before acquiring the viewport semaphore; it discards the rebuild result, reloads VPD state under the semaphore, and queues both replies if displayed. The non-displayed path replies immediately. The queue's local `Disable()`/`Enable()` critical section remains the already tracked GD5422 ExecSMP enqueue/removal race; the AmigaVideo failed-rebuild and stale `PreviousBitmap` path remains GD4763. `AllocDBufInfo()` is the documented constructor and `ChangeVPBitMap()` accepts a DBufInfo pointer; this pass did not treat invalid/null arguments as a separate defect. No allocation, swap, VBlank, or concurrent operation was run; source-only.


MUI Frameadjust preview allocation failure first-dereference correction (GD9512 refined; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): checked the exact macro expansion after the earlier note established that `SetAttrsA()` rejects a NULL object. In `MakeFrameDisplay()`, `set(NULL, ...)` therefore returns safely, but each preview loop next calls `DoMethod(obj, MUIM_Notify, ...)` before `OM_ADDMEMBER`. The selected `DoMethod` macro evaluates `OCLASS(obj)` after `ASSERT_VALID_PTR(obj)`; muimaster's `debug.h` defines the assertion as empty. Thus the allocation failure reaches the invalid-object dereference at the notification call, and normally cannot reach `Group__MUIM_AddObject()`. Corrected GD9512 and the file row to describe this first failure site; Group's separate non-NULL assumption is not claimed as this caller's consequence. No failure was induced; source-only.


MUI Popframe/Popimage stale-popup candidate withdrawal (GD9513; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the missing `OM_REMMEMBER` in the owner `OM_DISPOSE` handlers against the normal selected owner teardown. `Application__OM_DISPOSE` removes the main Window before disposing it (`application.c:862-870`); `Family__MUIM_Remove` sends `MUIM_DisconnectParent` before unlink (`family.c:274-287`); Window propagates disconnect to its root Group and Group sends it to every child (`window.c:3595-3620`; `group.c:832-849`). Popframe/Popimage disconnect handlers call their CloseWindow methods, which remove and dispose the popup while the Application reference is still available (`popframe.c:156-185`; `popimage.c:180-211`). Therefore the normal application/window teardown path cannot leave the popup in the Application family for its later dispose loop. Directly disposing a still-connected owner could bypass this, but that lifecycle is outside the established parent-removal contract and no selected in-tree caller was found. Marked GD9513 withdrawn, removed it from `AROS.md`, and corrected the current file rows; older dated notes are superseded by this disposition. No GUI or window lifecycle ran; source-only.

NListtree selection-table allocation failure metadata/return recheck (GD9735 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read `NLCreateTable()`, `NLAddToTable()`, and every `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` caller. On `AllocVecPooled()` failure, `NLCreateTable()` has already enlarged `tb_Size` and the failed assignment sets local `newtable` to NULL; `NLAddToTable()` returns FALSE while leaving the stale enlarged capacity paired with the prior table pointer. Initial-table failure leaves NULL plus size 64, so the next add can skip allocation and write through NULL; growth failure can make a later add pass the old allocation's end. Selection callbacks ignore insertion failure and publish `TNF_SELECTED`, preserving GD9735's existing state mismatch. Corrected an initial misread: `newtable` is initialized by the assignment expression and is NULL on failure; no indeterminate-return claim remains. Expanded the finding to cover the exact subsequent-insert failure; no new ID, body or LOC credit. No allocation failure or selection was run; source-only.

NListtree Insert destination-failure cleanup trace (GD9861 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-file/LOC credit): traced the default duplicate-name flag through `_NListtree_Insert()` allocation, destination selector resolution, list insertion and failure cleanup (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7111-7119,7129-7144,7284-7294`; `docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2080-2090`). NListtree backing-row insertion and inherited construct-hook failure trace (GD9862 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-file/LOC credit): traced `_NListtree_Insert()` through `InsertTreeNodeVisible()`/`InsertNListEntry()`, the NList InsertSingle wrapper and both `NL_List_Insert()` construction branches (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1271-1285,1375-1380,1804-1828,7121-7252`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:626-682,775-827,1798-1806`). The NListtree superclass constructor receives the caller's original tags through `TAG_MORE` (`NListtree.c:5165-5186`), so an inherited NList construct hook can reject a row by returning NULL. NList then reports zero inserted entries; NListtree ignores the result, marks the node visible, and GetEntryInfo(-3) can bind its direct-entry pointer to the previous NList row. Added GD9862 for the resulting tree/NList state and position mismatch, distinct from GD9722/GD9723 in the NList insertion implementation. Trigger is scoped to a rejecting inherited construct hook and an already-populated list; no hook or insertion was run. NListtree remains a partial translation-unit review.

NListtree InsertStruct token-buffer allocation/result pass (GD9863 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-file/LOC credit): re-read the complete `mystrtok()` helper and `_NListtree_InsertStruct()` loop, then compared initial `lasttn`, allocation skip, returned value, root sentinel and public result contract (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7378-7451`; `include/mui/NListtree_mcc.h:543`; `docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2180-2194`). Added GD9863 separately from GD9812's later-component continuation after a node allocation failure. The optional in-tree demo calls the method but discards its result; external result consumers remain untraced. No allocation failure or method call was run; the NListtree translation unit remains partial.

NListtree InsertStruct delimiter-boundary disposition (2026-10-26; no new GD or LOC credit): re-read `mystrtok()` against the public InsertStruct path/splitting description and the optional demo. A leading or repeated delimiter yields an empty token; the insertion loop treats that token as a list node when more input follows. The checked-in docs describe splitting but do not state that leading/repeated delimiters are normalized or rejected, and the optional demo uses only ordinary single separators. This is therefore retained as an API semantics question, not reported as a confirmed defect. No path string was inserted; source-only.

NListtree InsertStruct existing-leaf path continuation pass (GD9864 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-file/LOC credit): traced the existing-component FindName branch in `_NListtree_InsertStruct()` into `_NListtree_Insert()`'s non-list ListNode normalization (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7154-7165,7434-7443`). A matched nonterminal leaf is reused as `lasttn`, but the next insertion redirects to that leaf's parent list, placing the remaining path component as a sibling. This conflicts with the documented hierarchy-building/reuse behavior (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2162-2173`). Added GD9864 with the existing-leaf condition and a medium API-contract qualification; distinct from GD9812/GD9863 allocation-failure returns. The in-tree demo's paths create intermediate nodes during the same call and do not establish this preexisting-leaf case. No insertion or GUI operation was run; NListtree remains partial.

NListtree GD9862 stale-last-row and default direct-entry validation (2026-10-26; no new finding or path/LOC credit): rechecked the NListtree `OM_NEW` handoff of the original `MUIA_NList_ConstructHook` through `TAG_MORE` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5165-5186`), and confirmed the class unconditionally enables `NLTF_NLIST_DIRECT_ENTRY_SUPPORT` after creation (`:5229`). NListtree GD9864 existing-leaf contract recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): reread the `InsertStruct` public contract and implementation (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2148-2185`; `NListtree.c:7154-7165,7415-7444`). GD9855 framebuffer-callback detach versus queued fallback-instantiation recheck (2026-10-26; candidate strengthened, no body/LOC credit): verified `AddDisplayDriver(..., DDRV_BootMode, TRUE)` queues `gfxdriver_data` and reports success on queue allocation without instantiating the HIDD (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:225-226`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:397-412`). The actual attempt is deferred until `NextDisplayInfo()` or `BestModeIDA()` invokes `driver_ReplayBootQueue()` (`nextdisplayinfo.c:60-66`; `bestmodeida.c:250-255`); a failed `HW_AddDriver()` causes the entry to be requeued rather than reporting failure back to `FBGfx_Init()` (`graphics_driver.c:326-327,369-388`). The selected FBGfx `Root::New` can fail at superclass or display-object construction (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_hiddclass.c:59-84`). Since `initFBGfxHW()` has already detached `ARMI_PutChar` and the successful library initializer sets its open count, a later queued-instantiation failure leaves framebuffer debug output detached while no fallback display was created. Expanded GD9855 to include this deferred failure route; no new ID or body credit. No boot queue, driver construction, or allocation failure was run; source-only.

NListtree quiet-counter setter and internal pairing audit (2026-10-26; no new GD or LOC credit): checked `DoQuiet()` and every non-commented caller against the public `MUIA_NListtree_Quiet` contract (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1143-1169,4895-4910`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:968-990`). Graphics `ClearScreen()` cursor-origin boundary recheck (GD9870 added and expanded; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): re-read the complete body and compared its unsigned `ymin` calculation with `Move()`'s signed-WORD cursor assignment, RastPort/font field types, the public documentation, and the preceding `ClearEOL()`/`RectFill()` path. ReAction DrawList full local source pass (GD9869 added; 2026-10-26): reconciled the explicit drawlist module manifest, class definition, public directive header and ReAction link-library auto-open entry; read all local C bodies and definitions (309 `cloc 2.06` C/header code lines). In `IM_DRAW()`, the local buffer is 320 bytes and `InitArea()` receives `320 / 5 = 64` vectors. A nonclosed polygon that fills all 64 records reaches `AreaEnd()`; its unconditional `areaclosepolygon()` violates the helper's `Count < MaxCount` precondition. At full capacity `VctrPtr` aliases the start of `FlagTbl`, so two closure coordinates overwrite flag bytes, and `FlagPtr[0]` writes one byte past the 320-byte array. DrawList ignores the AreaMove/AreaDraw and AreaEnd results; the ReAction autoinit set names the image library. Added GD9869; the earlier GD9849 repeated-MOVE candidate was later withdrawn because it has no established observable effect. No build, image render, allocation failure or stack-layout observation was performed; source-only.

AreaEnd selected-caller trigger narrowing (GD9869 retained; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC increment): closed the previously open Clock and Graph caller checks. Clock's `DrawHand()` emits four DRAW points after one MOVE and ends the polygon (`clock.c:253-286`); its setup supplies 12 vectors (`clock.c:385`; `clock_private.h:20`), so this caller cannot fill the vector list. Graph allocates `EntryCount + 5` records and initializes `EntryCount + 4` (`graph.c:657,673`); its fill path emits the starting baseline point again as the final point before `AreaEnd()` (`:701-719`), so at capacity `areaclosepolygon()` recognizes the already closed polygon and does not append a record. GD9869 remains limited to DrawList's nonclosed full-capacity polygon, with debug samples and external public-API callers not exhaustively proven safe. Graphics OrRegionRegionND empty-input and allocation rollback recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD or coverage credit): re-read the implementation (`rom/graphics/orregionregionnd.c`, 36 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), its only maintained direct caller in `XorRegionRegionND()` and `_DoOperationBandBand()`'s empty-list and failure exits (`intregions.c:611-778`). `NewRegion()` initializes an empty result to zero bounds and NULL rectangles; the OR helper copies the surviving input bands, updates bounds only when output rectangles exist, and the wrapper translates only the produced result. GD9620 constructibility/public-count recheck (retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): revalidated that the 32,769-entry setup is representable end to end rather than merely a malformed `ColorMap`: `GetColorMap()` takes `ULONG entries`, allocates both tables using that count, and stores 32,769 in the UWORD `ColorMap.Count` without truncation (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:43-81`; `compiler/include/graphics/view.h:148-153`). `AttachPalExtra()` limits `sharablecolors` to bitmap depth only below eight planes; a 16-plane bitmap leaves all 32,769 entries shareable and sets `pe_FirstFree` to 32,768 (`rom/graphics/attachpalextra.c:69-115`). `ObtainPen()` takes the fast path only when the requested exclusive pen equals that head; another valid requested index enters the list walk after converting the UWORD head to signed WORD (`rom/graphics/obtainpen.c:82-120`), confirming the negative array index recorded in GD9620. The API path is source-constructible, though no checked-in high-entry caller exists. No map or pen was created; source-only.

ASL ActivateAslRequest window lifetime and nested semaphore trace (2026-10-26; no new finding): completed the caller cross-check for the 71-line / 22-code-line `activateaslrequest.c` body. `AslRequest()` publishes and clears `rn_ReqWindow` under the same exclusive `ReqListSem` (`workbench/libs/asl/aslrequest.c:220-223,323-325`) before `FreeCommon()` closes the window; activation keeps the semaphore while using that pointer (`activateaslrequest.c:52-67`). Its nested `FindReqNode()` shared acquisition is supported for the current exclusive owner: `InternalObtainSemaphore()` increments `ss_NestCount` when `ss_Owner == ThisTask` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:102-116`). Thus the pointer cannot be cleared/freed during `ActivateWindow()` on the checked path. The public vector has no maintained direct C caller. No window activation or close interleaving was run; source-only.

The implementation body and master index were already credited; no build or file operation was performed; source-only.

ASL FontRequester large-font-count caller pass (GD9912 added; 2026-10-26; no new body/LOC credit): traced selected `FOGetFonts()` setup and rescan callers (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:427,1292-1294`) through its repeated-buffer `AvailFonts(AFF_MEMORY | AFF_DISK)` request and `SortAvailFonts()` (`fontreqsupport.c:153-165,182-222`). The returned `afh_NumEntries` is UWORD (`compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:90-93`), and diskfont increments the field for every fitting entry (`workbench/libs/diskfont/availfonts.c:210-219`); no 32,767-entry cap is present. At 32,768 entries the signed-WORD conversion in `SortAvailFonts()` is implementation-defined; under the conventional GCC/Clang AROS conversion, -32,768 is converted to a huge `size_t` for qsort, whose selected implementation computes out-of-array pointers (`compiler/crt/stdc/qsort.c:73-80`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__qsort.h:87-120`). If that returns, the WORD outer/grouping indices in `FOGetFonts()` cannot represent the remaining valid entries. Wanderer Examine-error propagation through recursive copy (GD9917 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `ReadFileInfoBlockAndLockPath()`'s `Examine()` failure branch and its recursive-delete/copy callers. Wanderer Examine-error candidate withdrawal (GD9917 withdrawn; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced the recursive-copy caller's `sourceFib` origin. `CopyContent()` obtains it through a successful `GetFileInfoBlock()` on the same source directory before `ReadFileInfoBlockAndLockPath()`; therefore the later helper Examine failure does not prove the buffer is uninitialized. Although the helper returns a lock after reporting failure, source evidence did not establish wrong ExNext results or silent incomplete copy. Removed GD9917 from the master index and retained a withdrawal disposition in the detailed report. No I/O error was induced; source-only.

Wanderer move-path allocation ownership trace (GD9918 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `MoveContent()` from its `CombinePath()` allocation through the collision check, move and cleanup exits. The allocated `nextTargetFile` is never released; the selected drag/drop handler calls `MoveContent()` per entry (`filesystems.c:642-665`; `wanderer.c:345-349`). Added GD9918 for one retained path allocation per move invocation. No move or memory-pressure scenario was run; source-only.

Wanderer standalone `.info` move destination-name trace (GD9919 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): followed `infoFileSetup()`'s base-missing/sidecar-present case into `MoveContent()`. The helper changes `localSourcePath` to the `.info` file, but the preliminary destination collision check uses `FilePart(sourcePath)` and can stop before `moveFile()` performs its correctly suffixed destination check. Added GD9919 for the false collision when a target base file exists but the target sidecar does not. No files were moved; source-only.

Wanderer sidecar-copy allocation failure propagation trace (GD9920 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `copySingleFile()`'s sidecar target/FIB setup into the top-level collision check and `performDataCopy()`. The FIB failure sets `stop`, but the `!inDir` collision check overwrites it; top-level `CopyContent()` passes `inDir = !first`, so an initial file copy can then copy the main file and pass null `infoFib` to `performDataCopy()`, which dereferences `fib->fib_Size`. Added GD9920 with the destination-not-already-present condition. No allocation failure or copy was induced; source-only.

Wanderer file-copy Read() return-contract trace (GD9921 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): compared `performDataCopy()`'s `Read()` loop and completion result (`filesystems.c:197-253`) with DOS `Read()` documentation (`rom/dos/read.c:40-43`). The implementation exits the loop on `clen <= 0` without distinguishing EOF (`0`) from error (`-1`), leaves `stop` false, closes the partial destination, and returns success. Added GD9921 for mid-transfer read errors; no I/O error or copy was induced. Source-only.

Wanderer move destination-allocation error path (GD9922 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced `moveFile()`'s `CombinePath()` result through the existence check and rename guard. On null, `FileExists()` calls `Lock(NULL, ACCESS_READ)`; DOS Lock explicitly returns BNULL for a null name (`rom/dos/lock.c:66-68`), so the collision check is false. The `to && !stop` guard then skips Rename without marking failure. Confirmed the in-tree `MoveContent()` callers pass `newDir == FALSE`. Added GD9922. No allocation failure or move was induced; source-only.

Wanderer destination Close() status trace (GD9923 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): compared `performDataCopy()`'s output-close/result sequence (`filesystems.c:227-253`) against DOS Close's documented error contract (`rom/dos/close.c:27-36`) and implementation (`close.c:68-79`), which returns the destination handler's `ACTION_END` status. The Boolean is ignored and metadata copy/completion proceeds using the earlier write-loop result. Added GD9923 with handler finalization failure as the trigger and qualified resulting data state by filesystem behavior. No close error or copy was induced; source-only.

Wanderer initial copy-progress callback state trace (GD9924 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): followed the initial `performDataCopy()` callback, which sets `totallen=0`, `actlen=0`, and `filelen=fib_Size` but not `difftime`, into the selected `Wanderer__HookFunc_DisplayCopyFunc()`. The hook computes speed using `difftime` and gauge progress by dividing total bytes by file length; for a zero-byte file this is `0/0`, and the loop reaches EOF without later initializing elapsed time. Traced the drop handler's selected progress-hook setup. Added GD9924. No file was copied; source-only.

Wanderer recursive child-path allocation failure traces (GD9925/GD9926 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): compared both callers of `CombinePath()` in recursive directory traversal. `deleteDirectoryContents()` silently skips a child when path construction returns null and can complete enumeration with `stop == FALSE`, leaving the nonempty parent in place while reporting success. `copyDirectory()` passes a null child path into `CopyContent()`; `infoFileSetup()` then reaches `ConstructInfofileName(NULL)`, which calls `strlen(NULL)`. Added separate GD9925/GD9926 for silent incomplete deletion and null-string copy failure. No allocation failure, copy, or deletion was induced; source-only.

MUI Application constructor/base-name and disposal pass (GD9927 added; 2026-10-26; targeted slices only): read `Application__OM_NEW()` and `Application__OM_DISPOSE()` in full (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:379-774,781-983`), plus application lookup/config-notify helpers (`:296-374`) and Configdata preference initialization (`classes/configdata.c:560-621`). Traced generated base-name selection through `find_application_by_base()`'s semaphore-protected list scan and the later tracking-node insertion. Added GD9927: non-single-task constructors can select the same suffix because neither reserves it during the search nor publishes until after resource setup; traced the per-Base preference paths and the selected Wanderer copy caller (`wanderer.c:2508-2511`). Rechecked partial constructor rollback and disposal ordering; GD9463's missing Configdata/preferences guard remains confirmed (duplicate GD9906 reconciled into it). Reconciled timer request creation/removal with the existing GD9422/GD9908-GD9909 findings; no duplicate timer candidate added. This does not grant full-body credit for the 2,682-line `application.c`: OM_SET/GET, input processing, configuration update, save/load, pushed-method and other methods/callers remain open. No application construction, concurrent startup, preference write or allocation failure was run; source-only.

MUI Application OM_SET/OM_GET attribute and iconify pass (GD9928 added; 2026-10-26; targeted slices only): read `Application__OM_SET()`/`OM_GET()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:989-1431`) and traced window-position tags through Configdata (`:1009-1065,1273-1315`; `classes/configdata.c:861-906`), rechecking GD9907's embedded-length and destination-capacity issue without duplicating it. Rechecked single-task duplicate notification: Application forwards the queued DoubleStart Set to its Notify superclass, whose `Notify__OM_SET()` matches the incoming tag/value and dispatches registered notifications (`application.c:457-459,1255-1257`; `notify.c:397-455`); checked DiskImage and LogView notification clients, so no missing-notification finding is added despite the stale TODO comment and empty Application getter case. Added GD9928 after tracing iconify state/hide ordering through default DiskObject lookup, AddAppIconA failure handling, the window iconify gadget and `MUIM_Window_ActionIconify` (`application.c:1076-1148`; `window.c:2493-2496,4393-4400`). `application.c` remains a focused-slice review, not full-body credit; other methods and broader callers/configuration remain open. No malformed preferences, failed icon lookup, AppIcon allocation failure, notification, or GUI action was run; source-only.

MUI Application method-queue/ReturnID/UData slice (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): read `Application__MUIM_PushMethod()`, `UnpushMethod()`, `ReturnID()`, and Find/Get/SetUData methods (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1896-2059`) with queue-node allocation/deletion and dispatch (`:199-294`). The queued parameter count is masked to its 4-bit MUI count before allocation/copy; Push/Unpush protect queue links with `app_MethodSemaphore`, and the consumer detaches a node before invoking its method so reentrant queue mutation does not invalidate traversal. ReturnID enqueue/dequeue has no corresponding lock or wake signal; the sampled direct call sites are GUI notifications and app-flow callbacks, and no selected cross-task producer was established in this slice; a complete caller census is still open. `GetUData` returns a match indicator independently of the nested Get result, consistent with identifying the matching object; SetUData recurses through the Family after updating the application itself. The source's 64-bit big-endian PushMethod caveat has no selected 64-bit big-endian target in the checked manifests. Wider external task/caller contracts and the remaining Application methods stay open; no queued method, return ID or UData operation was run. Source-only.

Zune Application Load/Save/OpenConfigWindow/Execute/menu/refresh continuation pass (GD5755/GD5756 rechecked; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): read `Application__MUIM_OpenConfigWindow()`, `Application__MUIM_Execute()`, `Application__MUIM_UpdateMenus()`, `Application__MUIM_Load()`, `Application__MUIM_Save()`, and `Application__MUIM_CheckRefresh()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2320-2610`), plus the dispatcher. Reconfirmed the explicit Load/Save pathname termination candidate already documented in GD5755 and the Save truncation/error-reporting candidate GD5756; the selected implementations use `strncpy(..., sizeof(name)-1)` without explicit termination for caller paths and discard the IFF write/finalization result after opening with `MODE_NEWFILE`. Traced all checked-in direct Load/Save calls in the selected source search: maintained callers use ENV/ENVARC special values; no in-tree long explicit pathname trigger was established. Checked the open-config command assembly and its `/A,/N` Zune CLI consumer; found no maintained Base with whitespace in the direct caller sample, so no new candidate was elevated. Execute delegates to NewInput and waits on its reported signal mask; menu and refresh methods walk the application window family and dispatch to each child. Constructor-established family lifetime is assumed on these methods; no additional source-supported defect was established. No file, preferences, GUI, IFF write, or signal operation was run. This closes this method slice only; the application translation unit, its full caller closure, and aggregate Graphics/Desktop coverage remain open; source-only.

Zune Application configdata/window-family continuation (GD5636/GD5637 rechecked; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `Application__MUIM_AboutMUI()`, `Application__CloseWindows()`, `Application__MUIM_SetConfigdata()`, `SetConfigItem()`, and `OpenWindows()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2070-2318`). Confirmed both config-change callers close windows before applying the update and queue the snapshot reopen without checking `MUIM_Application_PushMethod()`; on queue-node allocation failure the list and nodes are leaked and saved windows stay closed (GD5637). Confirmed separately that a failed snapshot-list allocation returns NULL, causing `OpenWindows(NULL)` to open every family window, while per-window node allocation failure omits only that previously-open window from restoration (GD5636). Traced `MUIM_Configdata_SetString()`; it always returns zero and ignores `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()` failure, but the already-reviewed Dataspace Add/Configdata import findings cover this allocation-failure behavior, so no duplicate is added here. AboutMUI lazily creates and caches its window, checks for constructor failure before opening, and no separate lifecycle defect was established in this slice. No allocation failure, config change, preference update or window operation was run; source-only. This closes the identified Application configuration/window-family method slice; full translation-unit and application caller/configuration coverage remain open.

Zune Application input, timer and ARexx dispatch continuation (GD5277/GD5278/GD9909 rechecked; GD9929 added; 2026-10-26; no LOC credit): re-read `Application__OM_ADDMEMBER()`, `OM_REMMEMBER()`, Add/RemoveInputHandler, InputBuffered, NewInput, and legacy Input (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1427-1895`), plus the command/message declarations and selected Exec timer/message paths. Reconfirmed that `UseRexx` creates and publishes the port independently of the optional command table, leaving GD5277's NULL-table dereference on message arrival; retained GD9909's unchecked argument-buffer/RDArgs allocation and hook-on-parse-failure paths; and confirmed GD5278's parse-failure invocation is distinct from RDArgs allocation failure. Traced timer completion to rearm-before-callback, with the callback-removal ordering guarded by detaching completed requests into a local list; previously tracked timer rearm/removal candidates remain separately scoped. Added GD9929: when an enabled app receives a first-token command absent from its command table, dispatch replies without setting `rm_Result1`; standard `CreateRexxMsg()` starts that field at zero, while the interface defines `MUI_RXERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND`, so the caller can receive false success. No new command-prefix issue was retained because this source slice did not establish whether abbreviated names are part of the public command contract. The legacy `Input()` signal-mask mismatch remains GD9908. No ARexx request, allocation failure, timer, port or GUI was exercised. This completes the cited dispatch slice only; full application caller closure and the broader subsystem inventory remain open; source-only.

Zune Application membership/parent propagation recheck (2026-10-26; no new candidate or LOC credit): traced `Application__OM_ADDMEMBER()`/`OM_REMMEMBER()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1435-1465`) through the selected `Family` OM_ADDMEMBER/OM_REMMEMBER aliases and the `Window`/`Notify` connect/disconnect implementations (`classes/family.c:178-286,464-490`; `window.c:3574-3622`; `notify.c:768-800`). Family insertion connects a non-NULL child when already attached to an application; the Application wrapper then repeats the same parent connection. For Window and Notify the connection is an idempotent GlobalInfo propagation, so the duplicate dispatch does not establish a separate state defect. Removal similarly invokes disconnect in both wrapper and Family, but the first Window call closes and disconnects descendants; the second sees the window already closed, and Notify's disconnect intentionally retains GlobalInfo under its documented compatibility behavior. Family rejects a NULL child, but the application wrapper's subsequent method call would receive NULL; callers are required to pass a valid member object, and no selected in-tree NULL caller was found, so this was not elevated. No member mutation, window close or application tree was run. The membership slice is rechecked; full caller/build-variant coverage and the broader subsystem remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library AreRegionsEqual full-body and selected-vector caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 71 physical lines / 22 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/areregionsequal.c`, confirmed the vector is selected by `FUNCTIONS` in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:49` and declared in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:229`. The implementation compares absolute region bounds, then each normalized RegionRectangle bound and list termination; the region-operation writer merges adjacent horizontal spans and vertically adjoining identical bands (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:280-358,432-465,611-746`), supporting the representation comparison for library-produced regions. Full-tree C search found no direct maintained caller; the generated m68kemu compatibility thunk forwards the two region pointers to the vector (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4287-4293,7679`). No null/malformed public structure case was elevated because no such input contract is established. No region, graphics call, build or emulation was run. This adds one previously unrepresented selected vector body to the source ledger; external callers and broader graphics region-operation closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library AskFont full-body and selected-caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 56 physical lines / 15 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/askfont.c`, confirmed it is selected by `FUNCTIONS` in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:50` and declared in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf`. The vector copies the current `RastPort->Font` name/size/style/flags into the caller's `TextAttr`. Both maintained callers establish a non-NULL font first: `OpenScreen()` calls `SetFont()` with its successfully selected `dri_Font` before AskFont and stores the resulting common-prefix layout as its `TTextAttr` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2124-2132`; `intuition_intern.h:726`; `graphics/text.h:72-88`); ASL sets its dummy RastPort to `GfxBase->DefaultFont` before the fallback AskFont (`workbench/libs/asl/basicfuncs.c:699-704`). Full-tree C search found no other direct caller; generated m68k vector dispatch is not a separate caller. The public routine assumes valid RastPort/font/output pointers, and no selected caller violates that precondition. No font or screen/requester operation was run. This adds one selected vector body to the Graphics ledger; wider public caller, ABI and subsystem closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library AskSoftStyle full-body and SetSoftStyle/public-caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 59 physical lines / 12 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/asksoftstyle.c`, confirmed manifest selection (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:51`) and the vector ABI (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:54`). It returns zero for a RastPort with no Font and otherwise the complement of intrinsic `tf_Style`, matching the API note that undefined style bits are set. Traced the direct companion use in `SetSoftStyle()` (`rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c:63`): its `enable & AskSoftStyle()` mask is stored into the UBYTE `AlgoStyle`, so high undefined bits are discarded by the instance field; supported style bits are filtered as intended. Searched all maintained C calls; they pair the query with initialized/window RastPorts or use the query as the `SetSoftStyle()` support mask. `InitRastPort()` installs `GfxBase->DefaultFont`, and `SetFont(NULL)` also selects that default (`rom/graphics/initrastport.c:34-49`; `setfont.c:53-72`). No selected caller with an uninitialized RastPort or null Font was established. No font or rendering operation was run. This adds one selected graphics vector body; exhaustive API clients and broader graphics/text closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library GetAPen/GetBPen paired vector bodies and consumer pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read both selected implementations in full (11 `cloc 2.06` C lines each), confirmed `FUNCTIONS` inclusion (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:104,106`) and vector definitions (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf`). Each getter casts the signed-byte RastPort field to `UBYTE` before returning `ULONG`, preserving pen values 0..255 despite the storage type (`compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:63-64`); paired SetAPen/SetBPen vectors accept `UBYTE` and store those values. Searched direct callers, including `AreaEnd()` save/restore (`rom/graphics/areaend.c:79-80`), `Flood()` and GetRPAttrsA; their use is consistent with the byte-valued pen API. No independent conversion or ownership issue established. No rendering or pen operation was run. This adds two previously unrepresented selected vector paths; external clients and full graphics-library caller closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library GetDrMd/SetDrMd paired vector bodies and state-restore caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read both selected implementations in full (13 `cloc 2.06` C lines combined), confirmed their manifest entries (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:109,175`) and ABI declarations. `DrawMode` is a signed byte in RastPort, but all defined public modes/flags occupy low positive bits (`compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:66,99-105`); getter promotion therefore preserves supported values, and setter accepts the same UBYTE-width value, updates `linpatcnt`, and recomputes minterms. Traced selected save/restore uses in `graphics/text.c`, `bltpattern.c`, and `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c`; these save the returned value in ULONG/UWORD and restore only documented low-bit draw modes. `graphics_misc.c` and `GetRPAttrsA()` consume the getter directly. No signed-width defect was established for valid public draw modes. No draw or RastPort operation was run. This adds two selected vector bodies; external invalid-mode callers and wider graphics drawing paths remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library GetOutlinePen/SetOutlinePen pair and previous-value contract pass (GD9930 added; 2026-10-26): read both selected vector bodies (28 `cloc 2.06` C lines combined), confirmed manifest inclusion (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:112,178`) and ABI declarations in `graphics.conf`. The RastPort field is signed `BYTE`, the getter casts it to `UBYTE`, but the setter assigns it directly to `ULONG oldPen` before storing the new value. Because the public setter documents “Previous outline pen” and its pen parameter is `ULONG`, a valid stored byte 128–255 is returned sign-extended rather than as its unsigned pen number. Added GD9930, scoped to callers consuming the return value; selected `SetRPAttrsA()` and the maintained Icon drawing caller ignore it.
