Graphics.library SetMaxPen/GetRPAttrsA pen-mask contract recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD or LOC credit): re-read both complete vector bodies and compared SetMaxPen's stated maximum-index contract with its mask calculation and `GetRPAttrsA(RPTAG_MaxPen)`'s power-of-two result. For a positive maximum pen `p`, SetMaxPen stores the low-bit mask through the next power-of-two boundary; the getter reports that boundary (256 when the mask is zero). This is consistent with the representable pen range implied by the mask, while SetMaxPen(0) intentionally leaves the mask unchanged. `SetRPAttrsA(RPTAG_MaxPen)` is a no-op, but the setter documentation does not list that tag as supported. The maintained C search found no SetMaxPen or RPTAG_MaxPen caller; only the public vectors are exposed. The wording does not establish a precise getter round-trip contract, so no off-by-one finding is promoted. ### Graphics RGB4 palette vector recheck (GD5910 expanded; 2026-10-26)

| Selected source | Status and evidence |
|---|---|
| `rom/graphics/getrgb4.c` | Full 16 `cloc 2.06` C code lines reread. `entry` is signed `LONG`; the invalid-entry guard rejects only `entry >= colormap->Count`, then indexes `ColorTable[entry]` (`:53-61`). Negative indices therefore bypass the guard and read before the table. Checked-in GetRGB4 loops in `workbench/libs/reqtools/general.c:295` and `workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:344,388` use nonnegative loop indices; no maintained negative-index caller was found. Retain as the existing external-invalid-index candidate; no in-tree trigger established. |
| `rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c` | Full 50 `cloc 2.06` C code lines reread. Positive signed `WORD count` controls both allocation and loops. On successful allocation the routine calls `internal_SetRGB32Colors(vp,...,0,count,...)` after converting every input color; on allocation failure it calls `SetRGB32(vp,t,...)` for each index (`:64-99`, `setrgb32.c:63-124`). Both paths reach GD5910's unchecked HIDD pixel-table write. `AllocBitMap()` creates exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` entries for displayable HIDD bitmaps (`allocbitmap.c:423-424`; constant 256 in `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`); counts above 256 therefore include index 256. Expanded GD5910 to include LoadRGB4's direct and allocation-fallback routes. |

Caller check: maintained Palette Preferences obtains `data->count` from its screen palette setup and uses it in the save/restore loops (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:344-407`); the 2View demo uses image-derived `numColors` or a fixed 16 (`developer/demos/2View/Misc.c:235,465,480`). No checked-in call with count above 256 was established. Finding scope remains the public LoadRGB4 API on a displayable HIDD viewport when caller-provided `count > 256`; source-only, no palette operation or allocation failure induced. These are explicit path/body rows for the two RGB4 vectors; no subsystem completion is implied.

Graphics.library shared-pen reference-count overflow pass (GD9931 added; 2026-10-26; no new file/LOC credit): re-read the complete `obtainpen.c`, `obtainbestpena.c`, and `releasepen.c` bodies, including the selected PaletteExtra locking and list transitions. `PalExtra_RefCnt_Type` is signed `WORD` (`graphics_intern.h:71,74`); both shared acquisition paths increment without saturation while holding the PaletteExtra semaphore (`obtainpen.c:135-145,185-191,230-256`; `obtainbestpena.c:92-106,119-154`). At 65,536 outstanding successful references on the 16-bit two's-complement target representation, the stored count wraps to zero. `ReleasePen()` tests zero as the exclusive case and links the pen into the free list without removing its still-live shared-list entry (`releasepen.c:57-85,147-155`). Added GD9931 for the resulting premature reuse, qualified to this high-count public-API condition; no checked-in individual caller establishes 65,536 live references. Existing lock recursion and regular list-membership checks remain as previously audited. Source-only; no pen operations or concurrency were run.

Graphics.library LoadRGB32 table/fallback pass (GD5910 retained; 2026-10-26; body/path already credited): reread all of `rom/graphics/loadrgb32.c` and `setrgb32.c`, the shared `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` helper, the RGB32 vector declarations, and all direct maintained C callers. The top-word count is at most 65,535, so the temporary `HIDDT_Color` byte-size multiplication itself does not overflow on the fixed 32-bit ULONG ABI; `first + count` likewise cannot overflow ULONG. The table format has no separate byte-length argument, so each nonzero record's three-component source extent remains the caller's responsibility. In both successful-allocation and allocation-fallback branches, a record range beyond the 256-entry HIDD pixel table reaches GD5910; the ColorMap setter's per-entry upper-bound rejection does not bound the subsequent HIDD translation-table write. Checked-in calls are OpenScreen initialization and ColorWheel's bounded palette table; no additional independently triggered defect was established. No table, allocation failure or display was exercised; source-only.

Graphics.library HIDD color-update backend consistency pass (GD9932 added; 2026-10-26; existing bodies/path credit, no LOC increment): traced `SetRGB32()`/`LoadRGB32()` through `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` and the generic HIDD bitmap SetColors method into the VESA, EFI framebuffer and SM502 overrides. Each override invokes the generic superclass first (which can update/extend its software ColorMap), then checks the mode palette limit and returns FALSE on an excessive range. The graphics helper ignores that result and still updates the 256-entry pixel translation table. OpenScreen's minimum 32-entry ColorMap combined with a 4bpp target supplies valid ColorMap indices 16-31 that exceed the 16-entry hardware limit. Added GD9932 for the resulting software/hardware palette divergence. The three backend paths are separately selected modules; no device or display operation was run. Source-only.

Graphics HIDD SetColors backend census follow-up (GD9932 expanded; SDL GD9933 added; 2026-10-26): searched all checked-in implementations of `Hidd_BitMap_SetColors`, then traced range checks and superclass ordering for each. Confirmed the capacity-reject/ignored-return pattern in VESA, EFI framebuffer, SM502, Raspberry Pi framebuffer, VGA, VideoCore, VMware SVGA and LinuxFB; the LinuxFB implementation rejects before its superclass update, while the others in this set perform or delegate generic color-map mutation first. This expands GD9932 to cover software translation-table divergence across those selected backend implementations where the HIDD bitmap range is narrower than the ColorMap. X11 and SDL do not use the same explicit `1 << bpp` rejection path. The SDL indexed-color path separately allocates an `SDL_Color` array, dereferences it without a NULL check, and omits freeing it after `SDL_SetColors()`; added GD9933 for optional hosted SDL builds. No HIDD or SDL display was run and no allocation failure was induced; source-only.

SDL HIDD selection and color-array ownership scope note (GD9933; 2026-10-26): checked `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/mmakefile.src:3-20` and `arch/all-unix/boot/mmakefile.src:42-44`. The `kernel-hidd-sdl` target builds a standalone `SDL` monitor program; its option-controlled parent edge is commented in the Unix boot aggregate. GD9933 therefore applies to builds that explicitly select the SDL HIDD target, not by default to all hosted Unix images. The `SDL_Color` array is an implementation-local scratch buffer passed to `SDL_SetColors()`; the AROS function retains no pointer to that local array, and no free appears on the success path. SDL API documents `SDL_SetColors` as setting a portion of the surface colormap, consistent with synchronous palette update semantics ([SDL 1.2.15 SDL_SetColors documentation](https://www.libsdl.org/release/SDL-1.2.15/docs/html/sdlsetcolors.html)). No SDL target was built and no palette operation was run.

MonEd display-open failure contract recheck (GD9605/GD9606 retained; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read the full `OpenDisplay()`, `CloseDisplay()`, initial GUI entry and Jump reopen paths (`workbench/prefs/MonEd/moned.c:580-780,860-870,1018-1030`). Confirmed three distinct false-success/stale-window routes behind GD9605: failed `GetVisualInfo()` returns nonzero `2` before creating a window; failed `CreateContext()` skips all window construction but falls through with success `1`; and Jump ignores the reopen result after `CloseDisplay()` closes but does not clear `sp_Wnd`. Confirmed GD9606 remains separate: once visual info/context/gadgets were acquired, `OpenWindowTagList()` failure returns `0`, causing the initial caller to skip its `CloseDisplay()` call. The current findings distinguish these routes and do not rely on one failure being proof of another. No GUI or allocation/window failure was induced; source-only.


Intuition monitor-list snapshot lifetime pass (GD9934 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read `getmonitorlist.c`, `freemonitorlist.c`, `monitorclass.c`, and the graphics display expunge notifier (`rom/intuition/getmonitorlist.c:69-86`; `freemonitorlist.c:24-52`; `monitorclass.c:55-75,1080-1108`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:228-252`). `GetMonitorList()` protects both list traversals and pointer copying with `MonitorListSem` but returns after releasing it; the array contains unretained BOOPSI pointers, and `FreeMonitorList()` frees only the array. The selected display-expunge path invokes Intuition's removal callback, which disposes the listed monitor object; OM_DISPOSE's list lock serializes removal against the copy but cannot protect a client using a returned entry afterward. Direct C search found only the debug monitorclass test as a maintained client; public external clients are the relevant lifetime case. Added GD9934 with the undocumented post-return object lifetime and conditional concurrent-removal impact explicit. No display or monitor query was run; source-only.

GD9934 OOP/API lifetime-contract follow-up (2026-10-26; finding retained with conditional impact): checked `rom/intuition/intuition.conf` public vectors and `GetMonitorList()`/`FreeMonitorList()` function documentation, then searched the selected OOP API for an object retain/release operation. The only list cleanup is `FreeVec(list)` (`freemonitorlist.c:51`); OOP exposes `OOP_DisposeObject()` but no object retain/obtain counterpart in its selected vector set (`rom/oop/oop.conf:14-35`). Disposal dispatches the object's root Dispose method (`rom/oop/disposeobject.c:55-72`), while the graphics display expunge path directly disposes the Intuition monitor through `DisplayDriverNotify(FALSE)`. Intuition SetIPrefs palette caller recheck (GD9937 added; 2026-10-26; no new body/LOC credit): retraced `IPREFS_TYPE_PALETTE_V39`/`V37` through the selected IPrefs palette handler into the Workbench update branch. `SetIPrefs()` uses `lastcol + idx` for indices 4–7, while `OpenScreen()` maps preference colors 4–7 to `lastcol + 0..3`; on an 8-bit screen the former produces 256–259. The selected generic `SetRGB32()` path writes those indices into the 256-entry displayable-bitmap translation table without a bound check (existing GD5910). ReadPixelLine8 32,768-pixel boundary refinement (GD9804 strengthened; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the width-32,768 call through `ReadPixelLine8()` endpoint arithmetic, `ReadPixelArray8()` renderer callback, `rp8_render()` signed-WORD inclusive-width conversion, and the selected PlanarBM `GetImageLUT()` implementation (`rom/graphics/readpixelline8.c:59-66`; `readpixelarray8.c:21-32,97-123`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:662-704`). At this exact boundary, endpoint conversion may yield the valid stop coordinate 32,767, but the renderer and planar-reader signed WORD widths become negative and the selected `WORD x` loop copies no pixels; the returned count may itself be negative. Picture/animation callers ignore that result and consume the uncleared row. For widths 32,769–65,535, the wrapper can instead produce a stop before xstart and `ReadPixelArray8()` returns zero. Updated GD9804 to include the 32,768 boundary and distinguish the two paths. No build, bitmap, or pixel transfer was run; source-only.

Intuition pointer-color palette-base encoding trace (GD9938 added; 2026-10-26; no source-body/LOC credit): followed OpenScreen's depth-four `spritebase` calculation and packed `VTAG_SPEVEN_BASE_SET` value (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1406,1585,1588-1590`) through OpenScreen’s displayable HIDD bitmap allocation, VideoControl storage, SetPointerColors decoding, SetRGB32 and the HIDD bitmap translation-table allocation (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1225-1238`; `rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:128-130`; `rom/intuition/misc.c:267-271,331-358`; `rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:43-52,116-124`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:423-426`). For depth four, base 8 is packed as `0x0800`, but the unmasked decoder returns `0x8008`, and the pointer update writes entries `0x8009..0x800B` past the 256-entry table even though SetRGB32CM rejects them against OpenScreen's minimum 32-entry ColorMap. Traced the maintained IPrefs pointer-preference caller (`setiprefs.c:176-178`). Added GD9938 as a caller-produced index defect distinct from GD5910's generic unchecked index and GD9937's separate palette offset error. Trigger requires pointer preference loading/update with a four-plane HIDD-backed screen on a mode with `dimensions.MaxDepth <= 8`; no pointer, screen, or palette operation was run. Source-only.

OpenScreen one-/two-plane sprite-base underflow trace (GD9939 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): checked the declared `UWORD spritebase`, low-depth calculation, bitmap mode/depth selection, and screen-initialization pointer-color loop (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:175,896,1225-1238,1585,1661-1683`). For one- and two-plane `ns.Depth`, `(1 << ns.Depth) - 8` is -6/-4 and converts to UWORD 65530/65532. When the selected mode maximum depth is at most eight, OpenScreen chooses minimum depth eight for mode lookup but requests the bitmap at `ns.Depth`, then calls SetRGB32 on `spritebase + 1..3` because those values exceed `numcolors`. Traced the `BMATags_DisplayID` request into HIDD allocation and the unchecked 256-entry translation-table write (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226,242-250,423-426`; `rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:43-52,115-124`; `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`). Intuition failed OpenScreen publication/list cleanup recheck (GD5179 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): retraced the complete failure chain in `openscreen.c` and the selected screen-class/close callers (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2303-2310,2317-2399,2433-2500`; `screenclass.c:46-79`; `closescreen.c:331-351`). `int_openscreen()` inserts `pubScrNode`, links `FirstScreen`/`ActiveScreen`, may publish `DefaultPubScreen`, and adds the embedded screen resource hash node before reporting `MakeVPort()` failure. CloseScreen compositor bitmap lifetime recheck (GD9941 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced screen unlinking in `int_closescreen()` through the ignored `RethinkDisplay()` status and immediate `FreeVPortCopLists()` call (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:188-191,360-407`). On a surviving viewport's `MakeVPort()` failure, `RethinkDisplay()` skips `MrgCop()`/`LoadView()` (`rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c:138-158,212-217`), so the `MrgCop()` → `display_LoadViewPorts()` → `ShowViewPorts()` path that invokes `BitMapStackChanged()` is skipped (`rom/graphics/mrgcop.c:113-120`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-525`; `amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1494-1523`). This stale-node trigger requires the closing screen to be in the previously published compositor stack; `BitMapStackChanged()` removes old visible/obscured nodes before rebuilding (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:130-164`). `FreeVPortCopLists()` disposes the removed viewport's wrapped HIDD bitmap after driver deinit (`rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c:57-78`); AmigaVideo deinit does not remove that bitmap's embedded node, while its VBlank path traverses compositor bitmap records (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1319-1344`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:1806-1813`). Added GD9941 for the conditional stale intrusive-node lifetime. The AmigaVideo package is selected on m68k Amiga (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`). No screen close or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

CloseScreen/OpenWindow private-screen serialization recheck (GD9942 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced CloseScreen's initial `FirstWindow` check before `WindowLock`, its later locked screen-membership-only check, and the private-screen close branch through screen unlink and resource teardown (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:105-163,331-407`). Compared OpenWindow's ordinary-task `WindowLock` scope, final `FirstWindow` publication and lock release (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1048-1085,1618-1622`): an open that publishes after CloseScreen's initial check can complete first, after which CloseScreen acquires the lock but does not recheck `FirstWindow`. `int_closescreen()` checks `FirstWindow` only inside the `pubScrNode` branch, so private custom screens lack that guard. Confirmed `WA_CustomScreen` sets the supplied screen as `CUSTOMSCREEN` without a visitor lock (`openwindow.c:341-344,604-625`), while OpenScreen defaults `dowindowlock` true for ordinary tasks (`openscreen.c:146,2223-2231`). Added GD9942 for the conditional close/open serialization race; public-screen visitor protection is excluded from its scope. No screen or window operation/interleaving was run; source-only.

Private custom-screen CloseScreen/OpenWindow serialization recheck (GD9942 retained; 2026-10-26; no LOC credit): verified the precise ordinary-task interleaving against lock acquisition and publication: CloseScreen reads `FirstWindow` before `LOCKWINDOW` (`closescreen.c:108-124`); OpenWindow acquires that same semaphore, runs `int_openwindow()`, publishes `screen->FirstWindow`, then releases it (`openwindow.c:1048-1085,1621-1622`). CloseScreen subsequently owns the semaphore but its validation checks only that the screen remains in `FirstScreen` (`closescreen.c:125-143`); `int_closescreen()` repeats the `FirstWindow` guard only for screens with `pubScrNode` (`:331-346`), so a private custom screen still proceeds to unlink and teardown (`:360-407`, then `CloseScreen():168-253,273-300`). This confirms the race is not prevented by the global WindowLock; it requires the stated ordering and an ordinary task path that participates in the lock. Public-screen visitor references remain a separate guard. No window/screen operations were run; source-only.

GD9896 large-list reachability and consumer consequence recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the selected `FRGetDirectory()` `Examine`/`ExNext` loop and node insertion (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqsupport.c:444-628`), `CountNodes()` (`basicfuncs.c:959-969`), list-view `ASLLV_Labels` count and `makenodetable()` (`listviewclass.c:149-174,493-518`), and file requester multi-select sizing/copy (`filereqhooks.c:1805-1860`). Multi-select uses the same narrow result to choose its `WBArg` capacity and stop the copy loop, while the public count field is `LONG`. This confirms the existing GD9896 candidate's two distinct caller consequences. No large directory, selection or allocation behavior was exercised; source-only.

GD9912 selected-qsort behavior recheck (2026-10-26; finding retained and mechanism confirmed; no LOC credit): followed ASL's `WORD numentries` assignment into the selected C library `qsort()` implementation. `qsort` is present in the common and static function sets in `compiler/crt/stdc/mmakefile.src:500-540,840-865`; `qsort.c` emits the shared algorithm from `__qsort.h` (`compiler/crt/stdc/qsort.c:73-80`). On the stated GCC/Clang conversion, 32,768 becomes -32,768, then conversion to `size_t` yields a very large element count; the selected algorithm's `n < 7` test does not reject it and its midpoint/last-element pointer calculations use that count (`compiler/crt/stdc/__qsort.h:89-112`). This supports the report's out-of-array sort consequence on the affected conversion behavior. The count conversion remains implementation-defined, so the report's compiler qualification is retained. No font scan, sort, build, or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

ASL GD9894 constructor-failure caller recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): reread `AslCycle__OM_NEW()` and its dispose override (`workbench/libs/asl/cycleclass.c:215-257`), then followed the selected public `NewObjectA()` callers in font and mode requester construction (`fontreqhooks.c:980-983`; `modereqhooks.c:635-638,711-714,736-739`). When the superclass returns a gadget but `NewObjectA(NULL, FRAMEICLASS, ...)` fails, `CoerceMethod(..., OM_DISPOSE)` reaches `GadgetClass__OM_DISPOSE()` and the root disposer, which frees the object; `AslCycle__OM_NEW()` then returns the unchanged non-NULL local pointer. Wanderer GD9924 initial-progress callback scope correction (2026-10-26; finding retained, trigger broadened; no LOC credit): reread `performDataCopy()`'s first `CallHook()` before `Open()`/`Read()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:172-180`) against the selected `Wanderer__HookFunc_DisplayCopyFunc()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:162-178`). The callback computes non-delete speed from `obj->difftime` unconditionally, while `performDataCopy()` has not initialized that field; this affects any copy invoking the progress hook, not only empty files. Later loop iterations set `difftime` before update callbacks, but cannot undo the initial read. For `fib_Size == 0`, initial `totallen` and `filelen` are both zero, so gauge progress additionally evaluates `0/0` and converts the result to `ULONG`; the read loop then reaches EOF without setting timing. Expanded GD9924's trigger and separated the general indeterminate speed from the empty-file progress calculation; updated its index label. No file copy or UI was run; source-only.

Wanderer GD9925 delete-success propagation recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the `CombinePath()` failure branch in `deleteDirectoryContents()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:352-377`) through `DeleteContent()` (`:807-830`) and `IsDirectoryEmpty()` (`filesystems_utilities.c:93-107`). A NULL child path is skipped without setting `stop`; subsequent `ExNext()` reaches normal end and leaves `stop == FALSE`, which is the helper's success value. The parent checks the directory, sees the skipped entry remains, avoids `deleteSingleFile()` on the nonempty parent, and returns `FALSE` as successful completion. `CombinePath()` returns NULL on its allocation failure (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). This confirms GD9925's false-success consequence at the public operation boundary, not only the helper. No allocation failure or deletion was run; source-only.

Wanderer GD9926 recursive-copy null-path contract recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced `copyDirectory()`'s unchecked `CombinePath()` result into `CopyContent()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:487-495,634-640`). Zune GD9927 suffix-exhaustion boundary recheck (finding expanded; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): reread the non-single-task base-name loop (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:435-446`). GD9598 relaunch ordering recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced Find's Stop/Start path into Process.mui (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:768-787`): Stop's Kill writes `data->kill = 1` and does not clear it on worker exit; the worker only clears `data->task` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:41-53,152-185`). Relaunch calls `CreateNewProc()` before writing the returned task pointer and before resetting `data->kill` (`:193-220`). DOS process creation publishes the child through AddTask while Forbid is held, then calls Permit before returning; Exec documents that the child can finish and be freed before the creator resumes (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-564`). The execution window therefore permits the relaunched worker to read the stale kill flag and exit, with parent/worker writes racing on `data->task`. GD9598 already describes this ordering and the SMP/scheduling-dependent scope; no separate finding established. No process, stop/restart sequence or schedule was run; source-only.


FTManager pushed-method shutdown/entry ownership trace (GD9948 added; 2026-10-26; targeted cross-caller pass, no full-body or LOC credit): traced Application NewInput's final pushed-method drain and ReturnID return through FTManager's quit loop into Application disposal (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1839-1852,781-982`; `workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:281-282,360-368`). The destructor disposes child windows, whose FontList disposal signals and waits for scan workers (`fontlist_class.c:169-190`), but Application disposal has no method-queue cleanup. The still-running scanner can push font-entry payloads after the final event-loop drain (`fontlist_class.c:286-297`); successful payloads are freed only by the queued `flAddEntry()` method (`:371-375`), and queue nodes are freed only by dispatch/Unpush (`application.c:222-242,278-290,1940-1963`). No scan or shutdown interleaving was run; source-only.

Graphics.library `InitBitMap()` full-body and caller-range pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read the complete selected body (`rom/graphics/initbitmap.c`, 17 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and confirmed it is generated into the graphics library by `FUNCTIONS` in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src`. Graphics.library `CloseFont()` full-body and nested font-lock pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read the complete selected body (`rom/graphics/closefont.c`, 22 `cloc 2.06` C lines), confirmed its graphics-library manifest vector, and traced the last-accessor path through `RemFont()` and `StripFont()`. `CloseFont()` holds `fontsem` while `RemFont()` obtains it again; this is not a self-deadlock in the selected Exec implementation because `InternalObtainSemaphore()` recognizes the same exclusive owner and increments `ss_NestCount` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:84-103`), with the nested `ReleaseSemaphore()` balancing that level. Graphics `OpenMonitor()`/`CloseMonitor()` lifetime versus Sync/display teardown (GD9949 added; 2026-10-26): traced public open-count acquisition and close through generic Sync `MonitorSpec` allocation/removal, Display/DMEnum teardown, and graphics.library boot-display handover (`rom/graphics/openmonitor.c:74-85`; `rom/graphics/closemonitor.c:54-64`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:132-149,295-315`; `gfx_displayclass.c:463-471`; `gfx_dmenumclass.c:332-341`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:262-282`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:245-252`). A 2026-10-30 recheck also confirmed the display-ID branch gets `MonitorInfo.Mspc` through `GetDisplayInfoData()` and increments the count only afterward; neither that reader nor `FindDisplayInfo()` takes `displaydb_sem`, which the removal path holds. Scoped to generic Sync/Display specs and the external API/teardown overlap. No runtime operation or line credit was claimed; the selected graphics vector bodies were previously reviewed. Source-only.

GD9949 named-MonitorSpec lookup-to-pin race refinement (2026-10-26; same finding, no new ID): verified the separate named-spec path in `OpenMonitor()`: it releases `MonitorListSemaphore` after `FindName()` and only increments `ms_OpenCount` afterward (`rom/graphics/openmonitor.c:64-85`). Generic `Sync__Root__Dispose()` removes the MonitorSpec under that same semaphore, releases the lock, then frees the spec without checking the count (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:295-315`). A disposal between lookup and increment therefore makes the open path itself increment freed storage, in addition to the retained-reference-across-handover path already recorded. Graphics.library `XorRectRegionND()` full-body and empty-rectangle allocation-failure pass (GD9890 confirmed; 2026-10-26): read the complete selected body (`rom/graphics/xorrectregionnd.c`, 29 `cloc 2.06` C lines), confirmed `FUNCTIONS` selection in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src`, and traced the `IS_RECT_EVIL(Rect)` branch through `NewRegion()` and `_CopyRegionRectangles()` to `_LinkRegionRectangleList()`. `NewRegion()` returns NULL on either pooled or direct allocation failure; the unchecked NULL destination is dereferenced by the copy helper. Graphics non-destructive rectangle-region allocation guard comparison (GD9890 confirmed; 2026-10-26; targeted branch pass, no LOC credit): compared `AndRectRegionND`, `OrRectRegionND`, `ClearRectRegionND`, and `XorRectRegionND` at their `NewRegion()`/empty-rectangle paths. `AndRectRegionND` safely returns its possibly NULL allocation result for empty rectangles; `OrRectRegionND` guards its copy inside `if (Res)`; `ClearRectRegionND` explicitly returns NULL before any copy; only `XorRectRegionND` passes an unchecked NULL result into `_CopyRegionRectangles()`. `IS_RECT_EVIL` is active under `CHECK_EVIL_RECTS=1` in `intregions.h`, so the branch exists in the selected graphics build. Graphics.library `ReleasePen()` complete-body and shared-reference-count audit (GD9955 added; 2026-10-27): read the complete selected `rom/graphics/releasepen.c` body (66 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), confirmed it is selected by `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:159`, and followed its free/shared-list mutation against `ObtainPen()` and `ObtainBestPenA()`. Region rectangle operator selected caller pass (2026-10-27; no new GD or body/LOC credit): enumerated maintained callers of `AndRectRegionND`/`OrRectRegionND` and compared their copy-returning contracts with the destructive public wrappers. `ScrollRegion()` is the sole checked-in native C caller of `AndRectRegionND`; it checks the returned copy, clips the translated cut with non-failing `AndRectRegion()`, checks `ClearRectRegionND()` and `OrRegionRegion()` before swapping, and disposes temporary regions on all paths (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:58-92`; `andrectregion.c:48-145`; `clearrectregionnd.c:54-110`). No ownership or failure-path mismatch was established in that caller. `OrRectRegionND` has no checked-in native C caller; its maintained generated m68k-emulation thunk forwards the returned region pointer without changing semantics (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4330-4335`). External callers and malformed/null API arguments remain outside this pass. No region operation was run; source-only.


Region band-operation one-sided and allocation-unwind recheck (2026-10-27; no new GD or body/LOC credit): read `_OrBandBand`, `_AndBandBand`, `_ClearBandBand` and `_DoOperationBandBand()`'s result cleanup (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:432-760`) against `AndRectRegionND`, `OrRectRegionND`, and `ClearRectRegionND` source ordering. Union copies either surviving band; intersection emits no rectangle when either operand is absent; clear preserves the minuend when only the region band remains, matching `ClearRectRegionND()`'s argument order (`:76-107`). On destination-node allocation failure, the band operation returns FALSE and `_DoOperationBandBand()` disposes the constructed output list before propagating failure; callers retain ownership of inputs. No mismatch established in these paths. Extreme coordinate behavior remains tracked separately under GD9412; no region operation or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

NListtree table-growth failure caller recheck (GD9736 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `NLCreateTable()`/`NLAddToTable()` and traced both relevant callers (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1053,2561-2586,7064-7253`). `InsertTreeNode()` ignores `NLAddToTable()`; `_NListtree_Insert()` likewise ignores the result after linking and adding visibility, then increments `NumEntries` and returns the node. This confirms failed growth does not roll back the inserted node or stop later insertions. At 64 allocated slots, a failed attempt to grow to 128 leaves `tb_Size == 128` with the original 64-slot `tb_Table`; the next insertion writes at index 64. GD9736 remains distinct from GD9735, which covers selected-state/table inconsistency on the `SelectedTable` path. The target is explicitly buildable via `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src`; no default inclusion is claimed. The `NListtree.c` full-body credit already exists, so this targeted caller recheck adds no path or LOC credit. No allocation failure or tree mutation was run; source-only.


NListtree full-table removal impact recheck (GD9734 qualified; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `NLRemoveFromTable()` and its public Remove/RemoveNodes plus move/exchange callers (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1078-1107,2286-2293,7543-7665,8053-8062,8326-8328`). At full capacity the final shift iteration reads `tb_Table[tb_Entries + 1]`, one pointer beyond the allocated table; the copied value lands in `tb_Table[tb_Entries]` and is immediately overwritten by the explicit NULL clear. No persistent table corruption follows from this iteration. GD9734 is retained as a source-level out-of-bounds read, with observable impact qualified low because the dead load may be optimized away and no caller consequence was found. Full-body credit for `NListtree.c` already exists; no additional path/LOC credit. No removal, move, or exchange was run; source-only.


NListtree selected-table allocation-failure caller recheck (GD9735 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-27; no new GD or LOC credit): traced `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` through `_NListtree_SelectChange()`, `_NListtree_Select()`, and `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1053,1492-1498,1513-1562,9710-9754,9828-9870,10510-10518`). Generic chunky `PutTemplate` final-word overread recheck (GD9833 retained; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `BltTemplate()` endpoint/modulo setup, `blttemplate_render()` clipping callback, `CBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutTemplate()` dispatch, and the final-pixel mask advancement in all four 8/16/24/32-bit helpers (`rom/graphics/blttemplate.c:17-27,93-110`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:756-817`; `gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:819-1463`). A 16-pixel row begins at bit 15 and the sixteenth iteration consumes that bit, advances the `UWORD *`, then loads the next word before the loop exits. `RASSIZE(16,1)` allocates two bytes (`rom/graphics/allocraster.c:48-53`), and the public `srcMod` contract permits a two-byte row. The direct `Text()` fallback uses `raswidth_bpr = raswidth16 / 8`, `RASSIZE(raswidth,rasheight)`, and calls `BltTemplate()` with `raswidth` (`rom/graphics/text.c:137-154,381-388`); a two-character fast-font run supplies the exact 16-pixel boundary. GD9833 remains supported across all four generic pixel-width helpers and this maintained caller. No drawing or allocation was run; source-only.

Graph per-source capacity multiplication overflow recheck (GD9781 expanded; 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): re-read `Graph__UpdateSourceEntries()`, `Graph__OM_SET()`, the timer consumer, `IPTR` typedef and CPU pointer-size fallback (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:76-100,357-373,924-963`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:83-85`; `compiler/include/aros/cpu.h:88-90`). MUI Application config-change window-state failure-path caller recheck (GD5636/GD5637 retained; 2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): re-read `Application__CloseWindows()`, both configuration-change callers, `OpenWindows()`, and `PushMethod()` allocation/queue handling (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2106-2143,2146-2164,2261-2268,2276-2316,1893-1925`). Confirmed the list-allocation NULL is ambiguous: it means either no child list or snapshot allocation failure, while each open window is still closed; OpenWindows(NULL) then opens every child, including ones previously closed. If a per-window node allocation fails, the non-NULL list reopens only the successfully recorded windows. Separately, after a successful snapshot, both callers ignore PushMethod's return; CreateMQNode failure means no callback is queued, so OpenWindows cannot reopen/free the snapshot. SetConfigdata has already disposed the old configdata and installed the new one before this queue attempt. These are the distinct state and ownership consequences already tracked by GD5636 and GD5637; no additional defect established. No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only.

StringGadget numeric input conversion boundary recheck (2026-10-29; no new GD or body/LOC credit): followed the complete `DoSGHKey()` numeric-edit branch in `rom/intuition/strgadgets.c:1148-1225` through `atol()` to the selected C runtime `compiler/crt/stdc/atol.c:48-50` and `strtol.c:106-147`. The input filter permits only a leading minus and decimal digits for `GACT_LONGINT`; `strtol()` detects `ULONG` accumulation overflow and returns the signed LONG endpoint, including negative overflow, so long digit strings do not wrap into an unrelated in-range value in this implementation. VGAGfx cursor aperture consequence recheck (GD6140 retained and narrowed; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): rechecked the fixed VGA mode table and cursor address calculation in `arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:37-42,338-389` against `vgaRefreshArea()` clipping in `vgagfx_support.c:445-480`. The selected 640×480 mode uses an 80-byte planar row, so active display rows occupy 38,400 bytes of the standard 64 KiB VGA aperture. The cursor loop lacks a `disp_height` guard and erasure clips at that height, establishing writes/stale contents beyond the active framebuffer. The checked-in code does not establish an ordinary cursor shape large enough to reach beyond the VGA aperture; narrowed GD6140 to stale off-screen aperture memory and removed the unsupported implication of host-memory/aperture overrun. No cursor, VGA memory, or hardware operation was run; source-only.


VGAGfx cursor hotspot and physical-versus-bitmap dimension contract recheck (GD6141–GD6142 retained; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `PointerClass__OM_NEW()` and `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()`/`SetPointerPos()` (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:48-169`; `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:81-100,1916-1960`) against the public display method contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:461`). Intuition creates the pointer bitmap from the supplied bitmap dimensions, passes the pointer x/y hotspot offsets to `SetCursorShape()`, then sends the logical pointer position unchanged to `SetCursorPos()`. The VGA shape method consumes bitmap width/height and pixels but not the offsets; its position method clamps against the visible bitmap width/height. The VGA bitmap constructor stores requested bitmap dimensions separately from the selected mode dimensions and does not require equality (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:48-91`); its displayable-buffer setup also clears physical rows/columns outside a smaller bitmap (`:265-317`). This supports the stated nonzero-hotspot and dimension-mismatch triggers for GD6141/GD6142. The public method text says hotspot offsets are generally needed for hosted cursor implementations, so GD6141 remains framed as ignored supplied hotspot data and visual displacement, without asserting a universal hit-test consequence. No new independent defect or body credit; no pointer, bitmap, or display operation was run. Source-only.


VGAGfx nested `HW_acc` acquisition recheck (no new finding; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `SetCursorShape`, `SetCursorPos`, `SetCursorVisible`, and the `Show`/bitmap-refresh callers into `draw_mouse()` (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:228-385`; `vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:300-321`). Several callers hold `HW_acc` while invoking `draw_mouse()`, which obtains the same semaphore. This is not a self-deadlock: Exec `InternalObtainSemaphore()` treats an already-owned semaphore as recursive and increments `ss_NestCount` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:90-113`); each nested `ReleaseSemaphore()` decrements the count, and only the final release clears ownership (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:80-88`). No lock-reentrancy finding is added. The independent unsynchronized `mouseVisible` assignment in `SetCursorVisible()` was inspected, but no selected concurrent reader/writer interleaving with a distinct user-visible consequence was established beyond the subsequent semaphore-serialized erase/draw; not promoted. GD6229 embedded-GC initialization consequence recheck (existing finding strengthened; 2026-10-29; no new ID or coverage credit): traced `RPTAG_PenMode=FALSE` and color tags through `SetRPAttrsA()`, `GetDriverData()`, `InitRastPort()` and `WritePixel()` (`rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c:128-160`; `graphics_inline.h:68-89`; `initrastport.c:59-68`; `writepixel.c:65-69`). <a id="vulkan-funcs-pipeline-partial-creation"></a>Vulkan-Hpp batch pipeline partial-success ownership trace (GD10225 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): compared the enhanced compute-pipeline wrappers (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:3764-3802,3846-3898`), graphics-pipeline wrappers (`:4916-4954,4998-5050`), and beta AMDX execution-graph wrappers (`:16561-16605,16652-16708`) with the Khronos Multiple Pipeline Creation contract. The nearby `getQueueFamilyPerformanceQueryPassesKHR()` local `numPasses` is passed to a `void` API command whose specified purpose is to write the required pass count (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:15230-15244`; [Vulkan reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyPerformanceQueryPassesKHR.html)); it is not an error-result candidate. `acquireProfilingLockKHR()` itself has no output local and simply forwards its input structure (`:15249-15269`). Vulkan-Hpp memory-map pointer error-contract follow-up (GD10223 rechecked; targeted only, no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced enhanced `Device::mapMemory()`, core `mapMemory2()`, its KHR alias, and `getMemoryMetalHandleEXT()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:1110-1129,8465-8480,22599-22613,31976-31993`). Each declares an uninitialized local pointer, passes its address to dispatch, calls `detail::resultCheck()`, and then moves the pointer into `createResultValueType()`. `ResultValue<T>` construction stores/copies that value before the caller can inspect the result (`vulkan.hpp:7527-7544`). The official Vulkan `VkResult` reference states that output parameters have undefined contents for runtime errors unless a command specifies otherwise; `vkMapMemory` and `vkMapMemory2` document memory-map, host-memory and device-memory failures ([vkMapMemory](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory.html), [vkMapMemory2](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory2KHR.html), [VkResult](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). With `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and assertions disabled, `resultCheck()` continues on those errors and the wrapper moves the undefined output. This directly corroborates the existing GD10223 pointer-output case; it does not establish a separate root cause or broaden the finding to unrelated commands. The wrapper header remains partial and receives no file/LOC credit. No API call or build was run; source-only.

**EK10213 — m68k Utility pack-table endianness (2026-10-30):** both generated Pack/UnpackStructureTags thunks pass guest big-endian `ULONG` table words directly to native host code; little-endian hosts decode the entries incorrectly. The native pack/unpack implementations also use host-endian typed loads/stores on multi-byte guest structure fields. Scoped to optional m68kemu guest calls and kept distinct from EK9203's output-width issue. See [EK10213](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10213) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1804). No path/LOC credit changed.
**GD10268 — DataTypes startup leaks a held NamedObject on a global name collision:** if an existing global `DataTypesList` object has no user area, `GetDataTypesList()` retains its `FindNamedObject()` reference while the replacement is rejected as a duplicate; DataTypes initialization fails and the old object's use count remains elevated. Conditional on a prior exact-name collision. See [GD10268](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10268) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L10226). No path or LOC credit changed.

**GD10269 — AddDataTypes updates shared datatype lists without their semaphore:** its initial built-in list population occurs before it takes `dtl_Lock`, while DataTypes API readers traverse those lists under the shared lock. Concurrent readers or another AddDataTypes invocation can observe/interleave list changes. Applies when AddDataTypes is included and run; no path or LOC credit changed. See [GD10269](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10269) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
**OD10268 — Nouveau RAM reclocking loses a PMU script-submission error:** GF100/GF108, GK104/GM107/GM200, and GT215 RAM programming ignore failed MEMX script submission and continue with RAM register work. Trigger is a PMU FIFO that remains full for the two-second send timeout with `NvMemExec` enabled. See [OD10268](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10268) and the [MEMX error-propagation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-memx-exec-error-propagation-od10268). Combined represented body coverage is now **4,367/4,855 files (89.9%)** and **1,661,877/2,205,403 C/header code lines (75.4%)**, leaving 488 files and 543,526 code lines without full-body credit. Source-only; no PMU, RAM transition, firmware, or build was exercised.

**OD10288 — synchronous Falcon command timeouts consume sequence IDs:** a queued command reply timeout returns without releasing/cancelling its sequence; a late synchronous reply also leaves it allocated. See [OD10288](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10288) and the [Falcon sequence-timeout recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-falcon-sequence-timeout-recheck-od10288). **EK9101 — OpenSBI FDT missing `#size-cells` default (2026-10-30):** restored and rechecked the conditional interoperability finding. The parser defaults a missing root size-cell property to two, skips ordinary one-cell-size memory tuples, and may fall back to an EFI scalar range or 128 MiB; a later EFI region list can replace the missed regions. DTSpec requires compliant boot programs to provide the property but tells clients to assume one when it is absent. No matching in-tree DTB was found. See [EK9101](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9101) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9867).


**EK9100 — ExecSMP exception-handler snapshot cap (2026-10-30):** restored the missing detail and rechecked registration/dispatch. Registration accepts more than eight handlers for a vector, but ExecSMP dispatch snapshots only eight and logs/skips the rest; the maintained selected caller set does not reach the cap. See [EK9100](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9100) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9864).


**EK9102 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi mailbox transmit wait (2026-10-30):** restored and rechecked the unbounded transmit-full spin in `vcmb_write()`. Eight `vcmb_write()` call sites outside `vc_mb.c`, plus the wrapper’s ninth internal call, can block before any read timeout/fallback; `serInit()` reaches it before the first console output on pre-Pi-5 models. The sibling mailbox resource bounds its corresponding wait. See [EK9102](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9102) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1001).

**Exec/Kernel hosted Unix BootMsg lifetime pass (2026-10-30):** traced the successful hosted handoff and found its tag array, memory map, host interface, debug records, command-line and BSS tracker remain backed for the running process. No dangling pointer was established on that normal path; Android same-process retry state remains EK514, and other producers/contracts remain open. No path or LOC totals changed. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**Exec/Kernel Sam440 BootMsg payload pass (2026-10-30):** traced Parthenope tags through Sam440 startup. The kernel copies the tag list to static storage, duplicates command-line/boot-loader strings and debug data, and clears the debug-info tag before publication. The retained BSS tracker pointer has only an early in-tree consumer; its later storage lifetime and external readers remain unresolved, so no new bug was claimed. Existing command-line findings remain separate. No path or LOC totals changed. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**Graphics/Desktop NList replacement-failure reconciliation (GD9773 withdrawn as duplicate; GD9954 retained; 2026-10-30):** consolidated the duplicate report entries for the same construct-hook failure path. GD9954 remains the sole active finding: the replacement failure deletes the old row and returns success, with intended rollback semantics qualified as medium confidence. No path or LOC credit changed. See [GD9954](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9954) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**EK10214 — Parthenope RDB partition length is one block short (2026-10-30):** the Sam440 bootloader stores the inclusive geometry's block count minus one in `disk_partition_t.size`, whose local contract is a block count. The ext2 callback receives the undersized partition descriptor; downstream effects are qualified because that callback is external. Reconciled stale EK9332/EK9337 placeholders to their existing DISK-296/DISK-302 findings. No path or LOC credit changed. See [EK10214](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10214) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L839).

**Graphics/Desktop GD10233 continuation (2026-10-30):** added Vulkan-Hpp's enhanced `setVertexInputEXT()` as another use site for the existing ArrayProxy `size_t`-to-`uint32_t` narrowing. The optional API has no checked-in caller. Corrected the latest coverage notes to reflect that `vulkan_funcs.hpp` already has full source-body credit; consumer and configuration closure remain open. No path/LOC totals changed. See [GD10233](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10233) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**EK10215 — RISC-V large-range unmap can exhaust the page-table pool (2026-10-30):** the OpenSBI unmap walker splits each touched 2 MiB leaf into an L0 table; a 256 MiB unmap needs 128 such tables, exceeding the fixed pool once existing root/intermediate tables are counted. Exhaustion halts in the allocator. No in-tree `KrnUnmapGlobal()` caller was found, so the finding is limited to public/external API use. No path or LOC totals changed. See [EK10215](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10215) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**EK10205 — task launch callback duplicate scope and caller path confirmed (2026-10-30):** manifest reconciliation limits the generic-scheduler/architecture-dispatcher pair to Sam440 and RISC-V OpenSBI. The selected `RemTask()` → `KrnDispatch()` → trap/syscall → `cpu_Dispatch()` routes reach that duplicate sequence. ARM-native, AArch64-native, and native RISC-V use their own scheduler implementations; Efika uses its custom scheduler. The only checked-in callback assignment is Efika's and remains outside the affected paths, so the trigger is external/future use on the two affected targets. No path or LOC totals changed. See [EK10205](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10205) and the [dispatch coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9885).
**EK10216 — truncated PC Multiboot2 EFI64 tag supplies a bogus system-table pointer (2026-10-30):** x86-64 parsing reads the 64-bit pointer even when the tag declares only its 8-byte header. If the end tag follows, its type/size bytes become the pointer, which is published to the selected EFI resource and dereferenced during initialization. Conditional on malformed external boot metadata; no in-tree producer was found. No runtime boot test was performed. See [EK10216](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10216) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9886).

**EK10217 — i386-PC dispatcher skips pending task exceptions (2026-10-30):** Exec sets TF_EXCEPT and forces scheduling, but i386-PC cpu_Dispatch has its Exception() call commented out. Tasks with an exception callback resume without delivery, leaving the flag set for later scheduler decisions. Applies to the explicit pc-i386 kernel target; the current boot aggregate edge is commented out. No build or runtime test was performed. See [EK10217](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10217) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).
**EK10218 — concurrent BOOPSI class registration can publish duplicate IDs (2026-10-30):** MakeClass checks for an existing ID under a shared lock, but publication occurs later through AddClass, which unconditionally inserts under the exclusive lock and documents duplicate IDs as undefined. Two overlapping registrations for the same public class ID can both succeed; later FindClass selects by list order. Conditional on client ID collision and overlapping registration; no in-tree duplicate-ID pair was found. See [EK10218](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10218) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).
**EK10219 — m68k `AllocNamedObjectA()` leaks its native allocation if shadow creation fails:** the thunk allocates the native object, then returns NULL from failed guest-shadow allocation/registration without freeing the native object. Conditional on shadow heap/table exhaustion on the optional 64-bit-host m68k emulator. See [EK10219](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10219) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK10224 — detached-stream conversion failure loses I/O and can leak its copied lock (2026-10-30):** `detach.o` passes unchecked `OpenFromLock(DupLockFromFH(...))` results to `CreateNewProc()`. NIL is accepted, so the child can start without inherited I/O and null input suppresses argument injection; if lock duplication succeeded but filehandle conversion failed, the unconsumed lock is not freed. Conditional on filesystem/allocation failure. See [EK10224](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10224) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no handle failure was induced.
**EK10223 — TLSF uses undefined signed shifts in bitmap search and updates (expanded 2026-11-02):** bucket search shifts signed `~0`, and `SetBit()`/`ClrBit()` can shift signed `1` into bit 31 for valid second-level classes (for example, a 1008-byte free block maps to second-level index 31). These operations occur on TLSF-backed allocation/free paths; effects depend on compiler behavior. See [EK10223](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10223) and the [bitmap-shift caller recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tlsf-bit31-bitmap-shift-ek10223). Source-only; no build or allocator operation was run.
**EK10222 — 32-bit TLSF rounding can map large requests to zero or invalid buckets (2026-10-30):** near-4-GiB aligned sizes wrap during `MAPPING_SEARCH()`: one maps the request to zero and can return a zero-size block after managed-pool autogrowth; a nearby value produces a negative first-level index and negative shift count. Applies to 32-bit TLSF configurations such as i386-PC and ARM-native; no in-tree near-limit request was found. See [EK10222](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10222) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation or runtime operation was performed.
**EK10221 — 64-bit TLSF pooled allocations can index past the bucket tables (2026-10-30):** a request near 126 GiB maps to first-level bucket 31, but the tables contain indices 0–30. `AllocPooled()` forwards its `IPTR` size into a TLSF-managed pool before any bounds check. Applies to TLSF-backed 64-bit configurations such as default x86-64 PC and RISC-V64 OpenSBI startup; no literal near-boundary call appeared in a 503-call source census; dynamic sizes remain untraced. See [EK10221](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10221) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation or runtime test was performed.
**EK10220 — m68k `RawDoFmt()` returns output length instead of the remaining DataStream pointer:** guest callers receive a character count where the API promises the unconsumed stream cursor. Applies to the optional m68k emulator when the result is used. See [EK10220](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10220) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10351). Source-only; no guest call was run.
**OD10293 — VMware SVGA failed probe leaks its initialized DRM device:** `devm_drm_dev_alloc()` relies on managed `drm_dev_put()` cleanup, but the AROS action stub registers nothing and the post-allocation probe failure paths do not put the device. See [OD10293](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10293) and the [failed-probe cleanup recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vmware-svga-failed-probe-cleanup-od10293). This is distinct from OD4211's partial `drm_dev_init()` cleanup. No allocation failure, probe or build was run; source-only.
**GK20A IOMMU map-failure finding-ID reconciliation (OD10294 → OD11151; 2026-11-03):** OD10294's multi-page/noncontiguous AROS `vmap()` trigger and its cleanup consequences are the same root defect as [OD11151](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11151). Updated OD11151 with the exact compatibility-layer constraint and removed the duplicate ID. See the [instance-memory source review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L29946). No IOMMU operation or build was run; source-only.
**OD10296 — GK20A partial instance-memory cleanup dereferences a NULL owner:** DMA or IOMMU construction can fail after publishing the object but before `gk20a_instobj_new()` sets `node->imem`; common error cleanup then calls a destructor that dereferences the unset owner. See [OD10296](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10296) and the [partial-constructor recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gk20a-partial-constructor-cleanup-od10296). No allocation failure, IOMMU operation or build was run; source-only.

**OD9573 SD-card SDHCI SMP lock recheck (2026-10-30):** traced selected BCM2711/2712 GIC IRQ targeting and Exec task-affinity inheritance. Both the SDHCI peripheral IRQ and its created bus worker are routed/affined to CPU 0, confirming that an interrupt can preempt the task while it holds the shared spinlock and deadlock in the IRQ callback. The affected configuration remains AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP; no hardware or IRQ was exercised. See [OD9573](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9573) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No path/LOC credit; the full review remains open. Source-only.

**[OD3313](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3313) — Raspberry Pi SD-card delay checks fail at the 32-bit timer wrap.** `sdcard_Udelay()` can skip a requested delay when its absolute deadline wraps; on AArch64 BCM2711’s Arasan fallback, the 64-bit inter-write deadline can exceed every 32-bit timer sample and trap the bus worker in an endless loop. Conditional on timer rollover; hardware effects of skipped delays remain unverified. Source-only.
**GD10275 — Buffered IconList setup leaks its RastPort on layer setup failure:** if buffering is selected and bitmap/RastPort allocation succeeds but layer-info or layer creation fails, fallback overwrites the new RastPort pointer without freeing it. Conditional on the optional buffered path; Wanderer’s default enable switch is disabled. See [GD10275](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10275) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only.
**GD10274 — Vulkan-Hpp latency timing wrappers can return unwritten records:** RAII and enhanced vector helpers return storage sized from the first maximum-count query without trimming it to the fill call's actual `timingCount`. Conditional on fewer records being written on the second call; no non-generated in-tree consumer was found. See [GD10274](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10274) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No Vulkan query or build was run; source-only.
**GD10273 — Generic bitmap row alignment wraps at the UWORD width limit:** with default 16-pixel alignment, widths 65,521–65,535 round to 65,536 in a `UWORD` and wrap to zero. Generic chunky bitmap creation requests a zero-byte buffer; generic planar creation requests zero-byte planes, so both fail for positive height and planar depth. A framebuffer switched to a custom mode of that width also receives a zero row stride, but the resulting generic display-copy behavior is unverified at these dimensions. The mode-change trigger depends on a driver exposing such a mode; no allocation or mode switch was run. See [GD10273](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10273) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). Full-body source credit recorded; source-only.
**GD10272 — AddDataTypes can lose a refresh after scan setup fails:** `DateScan()` stores a changed `DEVS:DataTypes` timestamp before `ScanDirectory()` allocates traversal state. If that allocation fails, the command still reports success and a later refresh sees the stored timestamp and skips retrying. Conditional on low-memory failure during `REFRESH`; applies when the optional command is built and run. See [GD10272](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10272) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No path or LOC credit changed.

**GD10271 — AddDataTypes can silently omit built-in datatypes on allocation failure:** `CreateDTList()` ignores all four `CreateBasicType()` results, then returns a valid shared list; `AddDataTypes` can report success with missing ASCII/binary/IFF/directory fallback entries. Subsequent datatype examination can return NULL for content with no more specific match. Conditional on low-memory allocation failure; applies when the optional command is built and run. See [GD10271](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10271) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No path or LOC credit changed.

**GD10270 — Vulkan-Hpp `UniqueDisplayKHR` has a destroy-based default deleter although `PhysicalDevice` only provides display release:** direct use of the public unique alias fails to instantiate its destructor; generated unique-result methods avoid this with an explicit release deleter. Scoped to copied Vulkan-Hpp smart-handle clients; no in-tree consumer was found. See [GD10270](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10270) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No path or LOC credit changed.


**OD10297 — Nouveau R535 display control paths leak reply RPCs:** unsupported output-type returns omit `ctrl_done()`, and R535/R570/R580 backlight callbacks leak still-owned replies on RM-status errors. See [OD10297](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10297) and the [display-control cleanup recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-control-rpc-cleanup-od10297). No RM request, display operation, GPU access or build was run; source-only.

**OD10298 — R535 display constructor dereferences NULL after display allocation failure:** `nvkm_disp_new_()` leaves `*pdisp` NULL on `-ENOMEM`, but `r535_disp_new()` then initializes a mutex through it. Conditional on allocation failure in the GA102/TU102 GSP/RM path. See [OD10298](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10298) and the [constructor-allocation recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-constructor-allocation-recheck-od10298).


**OD10299 — RM control-read helper leaks reply RPCs on RM status errors:** `nvkm_gsp_rm_ctrl_rd()` returns `ERR_PTR` without releasing a reply retained by selected R535/R570/R580 control push paths; transport failures that clear the pointer are excluded. See [OD10299](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10299) and the [control-read cleanup recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-rm-control-read-cleanup-od10299).


**OD10300 — R535 BAR2 initialization dereferences a missing flush-page mapping (2026-10-30):** on the selected GSP/RM BAR path, BAR2 setup logs but ignores a zero-page wrap or map error, then calls `nvkm_kmap()` with a NULL object. See [OD10300](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10300).


**OD10301 — R570/R580 FBSR initialization errors leak the RM memory-list object:** control allocation or submission failure returns before freeing the successfully created object. See [OD10301](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10301) and the [FBSR error-path recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fbsr-error-path-recheck-od10301od10304).

**OD10302 — R570/R580 FBSR errors can leave channel scheduling disabled:** later save/init failures return without restoring scheduling after it was disabled. See [OD10302](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10302) and the [FBSR error-path recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fbsr-error-path-recheck-od10301od10304).

**OD10303 — Nouveau suspend failures leak earlier instance-memory snapshots:** applies to R570/R580 FBSR and native NV04/NV50/GK20A instmem suspend paths; a later save failure retains earlier buffers and retry overwrites them. See [OD10303](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10303), the [FBSR error-path recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fbsr-error-path-recheck-od10301od10304), and the [native instmem trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-native-instmem-snapshot-retry-od10303).

**OD10304 — R535 FBSR region-list allocation failures leak collected entries:** early `-ENOMEM` returns bypass the cleanup loop. See [OD10304](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10304) and the [FBSR error-path recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fbsr-error-path-recheck-od10301od10304).


**OD10306 — Nouveau GSP FIFO setup trusts unchecked RM table counts:** device-info pagination ignores `bMore` and loops trust counts against fixed arrays; oversized counts can read past replies and later pages can be omitted. See [OD10306](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10306) and the [FIFO count recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-fifo-table-count-recheck-od10306). No RM response, FIFO init, GPU operation or build was run; source-only.

**OD10254 — Nouveau LOAD-timeout recovery skips nonzero CGIDs:** the shared Turing decoder passes the LOAD field without shifting it to the CGID table index, so native TU102/GA100 lookup rejects it and skips runlist recovery; GSP-delegated FIFO is excluded. See [OD10254](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10254) and the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-load-timeout-cgid-lookup-od10254). **OD10305 was withdrawn and merged into OD10256** to avoid duplicate partial-channel cleanup findings.

**OD10307 — ATA identify timeout can spin forever with BSY set (2026-10-30):** the one-second fake-IRQ timeout loop repeatedly invokes the PIO-read handler with an unchanged BSY status; the handler refuses to clear while busy, leaving local interrupts disabled indefinitely. See [OD10307](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10307) and the [IDENTIFY fake-IRQ trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ata-identify-fake-irq-busy-loop-od10307).


**EK9436 — m68k graphics initializers write native-width records into guest-sized structures (detail restored, 2026-10-30):** restored the source-backed trigger, exact 76/32/14/12-byte overwrite extents for RastPort/ViewPort/View/AreaInfo, the InitBitMap exclusion, and optional 64-bit m68kemu scope. See [EK9436](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9436) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).


**EK9437 — m68k `AllocBitMap()` shadows omit Depth, Flags, and plane pointers (detail restored, 2026-10-30):** restored the exact three-field shadow map and native population paths, while qualifying impact to direct guest structure access because `GetBitMapAttr()` is the documented accessor and no maintained guest caller is established. See [EK9437](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9437) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).


**EK9438 — m68k Graphics free thunks retain guest shadow mappings:** restored after rechecking all three allocation/free pairs and the bounded shadow allocator. Repeated `NewRegion`/`DisposeRegion`, `GetColorMap`/`FreeColorMap`, or `AllocBitMap`/`FreeBitMap` cycles retain guest heap blocks and shadow slots; at table exhaustion, a subsequent native allocation is not released when shadow creation fails. No in-tree emulated guest caller was found. See [EK9438](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9438) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9439 — m68k `GetColorMap()` guest shadows lose palette-table pointers:** restored after checking the native allocator, shadow layout and pointer-conversion path. The native ColorMap has ColorTable and LowColorBits arrays, but both fields become NULL in the guest shadow; direct guest structure access is affected, while native accessor vectors still resolve the native object. No maintained emulated caller was found. See [EK9439](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9439) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No palette operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9440 — m68k Region mutations are not reflected in the guest shadow:** restored after checking the layout and generated/native mutator paths. The layout omits `bounds`, and wrappers do not synchronize `RegionRectangle` after mutation; direct guest structure inspection can therefore be stale, while calls that resolve the native shadow remain functional. No maintained emulated guest caller was found. See [EK9440](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9440) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No Region operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9891 — m68k generated lifecycles retain guest shadow mappings:** restored and reconciled against the current wrappers/native owners. Confirmed cases cover MsgPort, DevProc, GadTools Menu and messages, Utility NamedObject, and borrowed DrawInfo. Repeated successful calls retain guest heap blocks and bounded table entries; only native-free cases are described as leaving mappings to freed storage. DeleteIORequest and Graphics free pairs remain separately tracked. See [EK9891](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9891) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9441/EK9442 — console completion counter wrap and ignored scan errors:** restored after rechecking the match counter, chooser branch, `ExNext()` contract, DOS error propagation and selected FAT handler. EK9441 is conditional on a 32,768+ match set and compiler narrowing; EK9442 can mis-insert one result as unique only when a scan error follows it and another matching entry remains. Both are selected in ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi packages. See [EK9441](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9441), [EK9442](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9442), and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No scan or build was run; source-only.


**EK9443 — Unix-hosted and MinGW reject Wanderer’s warm-only shutdown action:** restored after rechecking both `ShutdownA()` switches and the selected Ctrl-Reboot caller. The call returns before dispatching warm reset, so Wanderer reports unsupported; Unix and MinGW have separate `ColdReboot()` restart paths, whose actual host behavior remains untested (MinGW RAM marker caveat: EK9517). See [EK9443](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9443) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No reboot was run; source-only.


**EK9444 — Unix startup continues after `core_Start()` fails:** restored after tracing the early failure returns, signal setup, startup caller and HostLib cleanup contract. `kernel_startup()` ignores FALSE and proceeds into cold-start residents without the signal/trap/IRQ/syscall setup; unresolved-symbol failure also leaks the allocated interface array. Later failure is conditional and untested. See [EK9444](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9444) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No boot or build was run; source-only.


**EK812 — `ChildStatus()` has an unlocked live-child scan on ExecSMP:** restored after rechecking both list mutations and the POSIX `waitpid(pid, ...)` caller. A scan can miss a notifying child between list transfer and return `ECHILD`, or race an unnotified sibling's removal/free while traversing. Both require cross-CPU overlap. See [EK812](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek812) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No task or wait was run; source-only.

**EK10341 — POSIXC `waitpid()` counts exited children without the message-port lock:** its unconditional `ListLength()` walk can overlap the ExecSMP child-exit publisher's locked append. Scoped to ExecSMP builds selecting POSIXC `waitpid()`; the unlocked exited-list walk is separate from EK812's live-child reader. See [EK10341](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10341) and the [caller/lock trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-waitpid-exited-child-count-list-lock-pass-ek10341). Source-only; no wait or interleaving was run.

**EK10342 — POSIXC `wait()` and `waitpid(-1)` omit `ECHILD` when no children exist:** `waitpid(-1, ..., WNOHANG)` returns 0; the blocking forms enter `ChildWait(0)` and wait indefinitely. The no-child result differs from the POSIX `ECHILD` contract. See [EK10342](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10342) and the [no-child path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-waitpid-any-child-no-child-echild-pass-ek10342). Source-only; no wait call was run.

**EK10343 — POSIXC `WEXITSTATUS` mishandles compound arguments:** the public macro masks an unparenthesized argument, so conditional or bitwise expressions may leave selected high bits unmasked. No in-tree precedence-sensitive caller was found; scope is external or future clients. See [EK10343](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10343) and the [macro/caller census](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-wexitstatus-precedence-and-caller-census-ek10343). Source-only; no caller or build was run.



**EK427/EK9907 — VMM Rexx `MEMTYPE` dispatch and syntax:** restored after rechecking the command switch, numeric parser, cache resize path and guide. Numeric low-bit values fall through into `WRITEBUFFER` and can replace a nonzero write cache with a zero-size cache; documented FAST/CHIP/ANY tokens instead fail parsing and return an argument error. Both findings are scoped to an operating optional VMM loop; the checked-in startup limitation EK9906 remains relevant. See [EK427](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek427), [EK9907](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9907), and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No command or cache resize was run; source-only.


**EK428 — optional VMM library startup dereferences null `CxParams`:** restored after tracing the library's `StartupParams = 0` message through manager initialization. `Init_VM_Manager()` then evaluates `PrefsPath` through the null pointer before the manager replies, so the `OpenLibrary()` handshake can fail to complete. This is an optional library path, not a default-image finding; it precedes the separate EK9906 MUI-start failure. See [EK428](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek428) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No library open was run; source-only.


**EK429 — VMM `ShowGUI()` formats a 198–199-character path into a 200-byte command buffer:** restored after tracing the MUI path builder through `AddPart()` and the manager formatter. Quote wrapping requires 201–202 bytes including NUL, so the write exceeds the buffer by one or two bytes when the preferences process is not running and console open succeeds. Optional VMM targets only; EK9906 remains a startup caveat. See [EK429](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek429) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No GUI process was run; source-only.

**EK05 — `ChildWait()` can clear the child signal after a child has already queued its completion (ExecSMP):** the SMP predicate check and signal clear are not atomic together; a child can publish and signal between them, leaving a queued completion with no wake signal. The configured triggers are x86-64 PC SMP and ARM32/AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP; POSIX `wait()`/`waitpid()` provide maintained callers for notifying children. Earlier coverage notes call this EK811; it is the same finding. See [EK05](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek05) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No task or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

**OD10308 — PoPo GUI cleanup aborts an unsubmitted timer request after MUI startup failure:** if MUI class or application construction fails after timer.device opens but before the first SendIO, cleanup calls AbortIO on the never-enqueued request; timer AbortIO calls Remove on zeroed list links and dereferences NULL. Conditional on the optional Poseidon GUI startup failure path. See [OD10308](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10308) and the [PoPo cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#popo-unsubmitted-timer-abort-od10308). No allocation failure, GUI, timer request, or build was run; source-only.

**EK8875 — Historical duplicate identifier for EK10363:** this earlier entry describes the same `Cause()` duplicate-enqueue race and is retained only because existing ledger notes cite it. The complete finding and reconciled conditional caller examples are under canonical [EK10363](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10363), including optional RTL8139, PCIUSB, and USB Audio paths. It is not counted as a separate bug.


**EK8799 — `WaitIO()` can return while `ReplyMsg()` is still publishing a timer completion:** On selected ExecSMP `C:Wait` and reset-callback paths, an independent signal can expose the reply state before reply-port insertion completes, letting cleanup or reuse race the publisher. The same pattern occurs in explicit optional `C:Logger`, Bluetooth, Poseidon, and PPP/serial targets. Conditional on a narrow cross-CPU timing window; source-only.

**EK9883 — Exec `WaitIO()` and DOS `EndNotify()` can remove messages without the shared port lock on ExecSMP:** the selected AHI-Handler path gives `WaitIO()` a shared reply port with a concrete concurrent completion producer; `EndNotify()` has the same unlocked-removal pattern on a caller-shared notification port, though no maintained in-tree overlap was established. See [EK9883](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9883) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No I/O, port operation or interleaving was run; source-only.

**EK8877 — PC startup ignores required exception-handler allocation failures:** the i386/x86-64 syscall and common PC APIC error/IPI registrations discard KrnAddExceptionHandler() results. If node allocation fails during startup, the gate remains installed without its handler; later delivery reaches cpu_Trap()'s unhandled-exception halt path. The spurious vector is excluded. See [EK8877](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8877) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No allocation failure, boot or trap was induced; source-only.


**EK8883 — Raspberry Pi boot LED diagnostics read a third GPIO cell from an eight-byte property:** both ARM32 and AArch64 loops accept two cells, then print data[2]. Their GPIO behavior separately checks for a third cell, so the confirmed impact is limited to an out-of-property diagnostic read and misleading log output. Requires firmware to supply an enabled LED gpios property with one argument; no checked-in DTB establishes that input. See [EK8883](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8883) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No boot or DT input was exercised; source-only.
