**EK9129 — debug-enabled btserial can read its freed base during concurrent expunge:** on ExecSMP, class expunge can free the base after `devClose()` decrements its count but before its debug `KPRINTF` reads the count. `KPRINTF` compiles away unless `DEBUG` is enabled, so no ordinary-build consequence is established. See [EK9129](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9129) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1866). Source-only; no lifecycle race was run.

**EK9130 — x86-64 PC assumes xAPIC MMIO after firmware handoff:** the APIC base helper ignores x2APIC mode, then early setup accesses local-APIC registers through MMIO. A handoff with x2APIC enabled can prevent APIC setup. See [EK9130](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9130) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4510). Source-only; no APIC hardware or boot was used.

**EK9131 — Native RISC-V dispatch waits the wrong task after an invalid stack:** it removes the rejected task from Ready but enqueues the previous task's node in Wait, potentially leaving one node linked in two queues. The checked-in SiFive U boot path currently does not reach the kernel. See [EK9131](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9131) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4518). Source-only; no scheduler operation was run.

**EK9132 — i386 PC same-ring exception dumps misreport SS:** the 32-bit same-ring frame does not save SS, but the page-fault log and context dump read that slot from the interrupted stack. Diagnostic-only; x86-64 is excluded. See [EK9132](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9132) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1444). Source-only; no trap was run.

**EK9133 — Efika exception backtrace trusts the faulting stack chain:** MMU fault diagnostics follow saved GPR1 and read backchain/return-address words without stack bounds or progress checks; a damaged stack can trigger another fault or loop before exception handling completes. See [EK9133](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9133) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1611). Source-only; no exception was run.

**EK9134 — Efika protection changes do not synchronize hashed PTEs or invalidate TLB entries:** the selected PCI allocator requests cache-inhibited memory, but the Efika `KrnSetProtection()` update omits the cache/TLB sequence used by `mmu_map_page()`, so cached mappings may retain old attributes. See [EK9134](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9134) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1611). Source-only; no MMU or DMA operation was run.

**EK9135 — Efika IRQ registration truncates 32-bit IDs before range validation:** inputs above 255 can wrap into valid IRQs 0–62 and register on the wrong source; the checked-in timer and ATA callers use valid values. See [EK9135](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9135) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1612). Source-only; no IRQ was registered.

**EK9136 — Efika startup copies metadata past its unchecked seven-MiB workspace:** command-line, BSS, OpenFirmware tree and debug symbols grow `memlo` from physical `0x07100000` toward the loaded image at `0x07800000` without a boundary check. Oversized cumulative metadata can overwrite kernel sections. See [EK9136](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9136) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1613). Source-only; no oversized boot metadata was supplied.

**EK9141 — Hyper-V debugger Backspace underflows an empty input index:** the optional NMI debugger writes `cmndbuff[-1]` and reads `cmndbuff[-2]` when Backspace is first at the prompt. Requires explicitly enabling and booting the Hyper-V debugger. See [EK9141](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9141) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2250). Source-only; no input was generated.

**EK9142 — a full Hyper-V debugger line ignores its terminator:** at 1,023 ordinary characters, the optional NMI debugger stops storing input and keeps testing the unchanged last character, so CR/Ctrl-X/Escape cannot end the prompt. See [EK9142](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9142) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2250). Source-only; no input was generated.

**EK9190 — x86-64 PC nested interrupts can fault on an unaligned XMM save area:** a nested IRQ at the re-enabled SoftInt callback entry leaves `FXSData` 8-byte misaligned, but `core_IRQHandle()` stores with `movaps`. See [EK9190](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9190) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1748). Source-only; no interrupt was induced.

**EK9191 — x86-64 PC IRQ callbacks can clobber unsaved interrupted XMM state:** only XMM0–3 are saved on the no-task-switch path, while ordinary C callback code may use caller-saved XMM4–15; the private preservation comment omits XMM4. No selected in-tree callback clobber was established, so reachability is conditional. See [EK9191](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9191) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1205). Source-only; no interrupt was run.

**EK9201 — m68k `FreeNamedObject()` leaves freed guest shadows registered:** the generated vector frees the native object but omits shadow-table removal and guest-heap release, so repeated guest lifecycles leak slots and retain stale mappings. Applies to optional m68k emulation on 64-bit hosts; no checked-in guest lifecycle was established. See [EK9201](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9201) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8521). Source-only; no guest sequence was run.

**EK9202 — m68k `RemNamedObject()` treats a guest Message as the larger native structure:** the raw thunk passes the 20-byte guest buffer to native code expecting the 48-byte selected x86-64 layout; writing `ln_Name` overruns the guest object and reply handling reads the wrong `mn_ReplyPort`. Checked-in callers pass NULL, so the trigger is limited to guest calls with a non-NULL message. See [EK9202](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9202) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4945). Source-only; no message was sent.

**EK9203 — m68k tag-output thunks use native-width `IPTR` stores:** DataTypes `GetDTAttrsA`, GadTools `GT_GetGadgetAttrsA`, DOS `GetSegListInfo`, Utility `UnpackStructureTags`, and Graphics `GetRPAttrsA` can write eight-byte host values through four-byte guest output slots, overwriting adjacent guest data and leaving host-endian values. Limited to optional m68k guest calls with matching output tags on 64-bit hosts; native checked-in callers use native-width storage. See [EK9203](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9203) and the [TagItem output-thunk recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68kemu-tagitem-output-thunk-recheck-ek9203-2026-11-02). Source-only; no guest buffer was used.

**EK9205 — m68k `RawDoFmt()` can write and copy past its 1,024-byte stack buffer:** if formatting requires at least 1,024 characters, `snprintf()` returns the required size, which advances the output pointer beyond the buffer before the NUL store and copy. The trigger is conditional on long formatted output through the optional m68k emulator. See [EK9205](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9205) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4955). Source-only; no formatter was run.

**EK9206 — m68k formatter conversion uses four-byte slots for `%i` and `%p`/`%P`:** native 64-bit RawDoFmt consumes eight-byte IPTR values, so negative `%id` values are zero-extended and following arguments can be misaligned. Applies to optional m68k guest formatting thunks on 64-bit hosts. See [EK9206](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9206) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8614). Source-only; no guest output was produced.

**EK9209 — m68k Locale `FormatString()` mishandles positional arguments:** its bridge ignores `$` indexes and string-pointer conversion, but native Locale reads by positional offsets. A positional format can read the wrong slot or dereference guest memory as a host pointer. Conditional on guest use; its Hook callback has a separate bridge defect. See [EK9209](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9209) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4961). Source-only; no guest format was run.

**EK9204 — the m68k `RawDoFmt()` thunk ignores `PutChProc` and delegates conversions to host `snprintf`:** serial/count modes and custom guest callbacks are not dispatched; unsupported `%n` can invoke host count-store behavior through an untranslated guest value. Applies to guest use of the optional m68k emulator; string mode is only approximated. See [EK9204](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9204) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4953). Source-only; no callback was run.

**EK9200 — m68k NamedObject lookup/name vectors return native pointers:** successful `FindNamedObject()` increments the native use count but returns an unmapped host pointer; `NamedObjectName()` likewise returns a raw host string. Guest code cannot reliably dereference the results or release the lookup reference. Applies to optional m68k emulation on 64-bit hosts; no checked-in guest reproducer was established. See [EK9200](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9200) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8521). Source-only; no guest call was run.

**EK9182 — Android-hosted kernel alerts lose their final character:** JNI `GetString()` allocates `strlen()` bytes but copies `strlen()-1`; the selected alert producer always prefixes a title and newline. See [EK9182](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9182) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L996). Source-only; no Android alert was sent.

**EK9181 — m68k `OpenWindow` omits IDCMP and size limits from its guest Window shadow:** native Intuition initializes these public fields, but the thunk writes only selected fields, leaving guest reads stale. See [EK9181](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9181) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no window was opened.

**EK9180 — m68k `OpenScreen()` leaves public ViewPort fields unsynchronized:** `ColorMap` is zero in the guest shadow, so passing it to `GetRGB32()` resolves to NULL and native color lookup dereferences it; dimensions and offsets are also stale. Conditional on guest field use in the optional m68k emulator; no in-tree reproducer is known. See [EK9180](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9180) and the [OpenScreen/GetRGB32 trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#open-screen-viewport-field-state-ek9180-continuation). Source-only; no emulated call or build was run.

**EK9179 — m68k Window/Screen RastPort shadows do not track native graphics calls:** SetAPen/Move update native fields while the guest RastPort remains uninitialized or stale, so later guest reads see old values. See [EK9179](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9179) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no graphics call was run.

**EK9178 — m68k window/screen teardown leaks child shadows and mishandles CloseScreen results:** repeated lifecycles leak guest allocations and shadow slots; once full, a returned object may not be closable through its guest handle. CloseScreen also frees the guest shadow when native closure fails and reports FALSE even when it succeeds. See [EK9178](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9178) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no GUI lifecycle was run.

**EK9177 — m68k record-lock arrays use a 16-byte guest stride but native x86-64 code advances 32 bytes:** native `LockRecords`/`UnLockRecords` misread fields and can scan beyond the guest array. See [EK9177](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9177) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no record lock was acquired.

**EK9176 — m68k `WaitPkt` returns a native packet pointer/layout through guest D0:** if a packet reaches the runner's native process port, the guest receives a narrowed host address and cannot interpret the native packet fields. See [EK9176](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9176) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no packet wait was run.

**EK9175 — 64-bit hosts zero-extend negative m68k `DoPkt` arguments:** a guest `-1` becomes positive `4294967295` in native `SIPTR` packet fields. Only signed packet arguments are affected. See [EK9175](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9175) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no packet call was run.

**EK9174 — m68k packet thunks read D-register packet arguments from A registers and pass guest packet storage directly to native code:** packet/port values can be unrelated, and native field/queue operations do not match guest packet layouts. See [EK9174](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9174) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no packet operation was run.

**EK9173 — m68k formatted output does not translate guest `%b` BSTR addresses:** native `RawDoFmt` shifts and dereferences the raw guest value in host memory, so output can read unrelated bytes or fault. This affects optional m68k DOS and Utility formatting thunks. See [EK9173](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9173) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no formatter was run.

**EK9172 — m68k pattern matching passes a smaller guest `AnchorPath` directly to native DOS:** native 64-bit pointer fields and embedded FIB use a different layout, so matching and cleanup can misread guest fields or follow invalid native pointers. See [EK9172](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9172) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no pattern search was run.

**EK9171 — m68k `ExAll`/`ExAllEnd` use A2/A5 instead of declared D2/D5 and pass guest structures as native layouts:** on 64-bit hosts the 32-bit guest record/control layouts also differ from native DOS. See [EK9171](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9171) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no call was run.

**EK9170 — m68k `AllocDosObject` returns native pointers and `FreeDosObject` reads A2 instead of its declared D2 pointer:** non-FIB objects have no guest shadow, and cleanup may leak or pass the wrong pointer. See [EK9170](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9170) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no object was allocated.

**EK9169 — 64-bit hosts can truncate native DOS BPTR handles at the m68k boundary:** returned file/lock handles are narrowed to 32-bit D0 and later passed back to native DOS without a handle map, so paired operations can use an invalid BPTR. Optional m68k emulator only. See [EK9169](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9169) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1803). Source-only; no DOS operation was run.

**EK9168 — the optional m68k `ReadArgs` handle can be truncated before `FreeArgs`:** native `RDArgs *` is returned through 32-bit guest D0, then cast back to a host pointer. On 64-bit hosts, a guest using D3=0 may pass an invalid handle to `FreeArgs`. Caller-owned structure layout is separate (EK9432). See [EK9168](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9168) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1799). Source-only; no guest call was run.

**EK9167 — m68k `ReadArgs` writes native string/number/vector pointers into guest array slots:** pointer-valued results are narrowed but not copied or translated into guest memory, so guest dereferences use invalid guest addresses. See [EK9167](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9167) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1799). Source-only; no guest call was run.

**EK9166 — repeated opens can exhaust the optional m68k emulator’s fake-library table:** after its 16-name cache fills, generated libraries are allocated a fresh base on each open; `CloseLibrary()` does not reclaim them, and the 64 KiB jump-table region fills before the 32-entry array limit. Requires repeated opens after map saturation; no maintained workload found. See [EK9166](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9166) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1793). Source-only; no guest was run.

**EK9165 — the optional m68k startup scan can mistake unrelated data for an auto-open table:** if a generated-library name follows a zero longword in the inferred pattern, it writes a fake library base into that slot. No colliding maintained workload was found. See [EK9165](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9165) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1793). Source-only; no guest image was run.

**EK9164 — the optional m68k Hunk loader silently skips four recognized relocation record types, then returns the entry as success:** relocated guest code can run with unadjusted addresses; direct `RunFile()` callers are developer utilities and runtime-library fallback is conditional. See [EK9164](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9164) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1793). Source-only; no Hunk image was loaded.

**EK9163 — runtime-loaded m68k Hunk BSS can retain previously freed guest data:** the parser skips the BSS size assuming the hunk allocation is zeroed, but reused guest heap blocks are not cleared. Requires a disk-loaded Hunk library and block reuse. See [EK9163](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9163) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1793). Source-only; no library or guest was loaded.

**EK9162 — the optional m68k runner continues after guest argument allocation fails:** it enters the guest with A0=0 and D0 holding the nonzero argument length, so the guest receives inconsistent arguments. Requires nonempty arguments and an exhausted guest heap. See [EK9162](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9162) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1796). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.

**EK9161 — the optional m68k runner ignores the requested guest stack size:** guests always receive a fixed 64 KiB region; a guest needing more can grow into the adjacent guest heap. This fixed-stack limit is in the README but conflicts with the API documentation and DOS callers. See [EK9161](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9161) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1796). Source-only; no guest was run.

**EK9160 — emulated AllocMem/AllocVec can return stale data despite `MEMF_CLEAR`:** the thunks ignore or drop the clear requirement, and freed guest blocks are reused without clearing. Requires guest allocation reuse in the optional emulator. See [EK9160](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9160) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4854). Source-only; no allocation sequence was run.

**EK9159 — oversized m68k emulator allocations can return pointers in the guest stack:** near-4-GiB sizes wrap during alignment/header arithmetic and are accepted as tiny blocks at the heap boundary. Affected callers are the optional emulated AllocMem/AllocVec/AllocPooled vectors; no ordinary workload trigger was found. See [EK9159](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9159) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6424). Source-only; no guest allocation or write was run.

**EK9158 — m68k Hunk relocation offsets can wrap their bounds check:** a near-`ULONG_MAX` offset passes the `offset + 3` test, then wraps the guest address to just before the hunk and can overwrite heap allocation metadata. Requires a malformed Hunk file and the optional emulator. See [EK9158](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9158) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4852). Source-only; no file or emulation was run.

**EK9157 — the optional m68k Hunk loader copies code/data past the declared guest allocation:** it checks payload bounds against the input file but not against the hunk allocation, allowing adjacent guest-heap data to be overwritten. Requires a malformed Hunk file and the optional emulator path. See [EK9157](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9157) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4852). Source-only; no file or guest code was loaded.

**EK9156 — the generic linear allocator uses an uninitialized region semaphore unless `mm_Protect()` runs first:** `mm_Init()` does not initialize it, while allocation/free paths use it. No maintained selected path currently establishes the trigger because generic page size is unset and `mm_Protect()` has no checked-in caller. See [EK9156](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9156) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4864). Source-only; no allocation was run.

**EK9155 — BCM2712 GIC dispatch can index beyond the 384-entry IRQ table:** valid SPI IDs above 383 pass the dispatcher and reach an unchecked table index. The RP1 MSI route is firmware-DTB-dependent; actual board ranges are not in-tree. See [EK9155](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9155) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1055). Source-only; no interrupt or device was exercised.

**EK9153 — CHRP resident scanning can omit Efika’s RTAS resource on allocation failure:** the scanner silently skips a resident when its temporary list-node allocation fails; without `rtas.resource`, Efika shutdown requests return without calling firmware. See [EK9153](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9153) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4749). Source-only; no allocation failure or shutdown request was induced.

**EK9151 — optional `FindAddr` accepts a valid numeric prefix followed by junk:** the diagnostic can attribute the prefix address to a module without flagging trailing text. The developer command is optional and no in-tree invocation was found. See [EK9151](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9151) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L675). Source-only; no command was run.

**EK9150 — PC SMP AP startup wraps its loop index at 256 registered CPUs:** `apic_count` is wider than the `apicid_t` loop variable, so after slot 255 the counter wraps to zero and startup keeps iterating. Requires all 256 xAPIC IDs to be enabled. See [EK9150](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9150) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1244). Source-only; no AP startup was run.

**EK9146 — the optional emergency-console handler dereferences failed allocations:** name and FileLock allocation results are used without NULL checks, so low memory during selected DOS actions faults the handler instead of replying with an error. Requires the optional ECON handler and emergency-console boot option. See [EK9146](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9146) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1163). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.

**EK9145 — big-endian `INITSTRUCT` expands to one comma expression instead of two initializer words:** static initializer use is not a constant expression, and runtime use omits the opcode word expected by `InitStruct()`’s decoder. No in-tree use was found; the defect affects external/future big-endian clients. See [EK9145](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9145) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1931). Source-only; no compile or initialization was run.

**EK9144 — concurrent ExecSMP task creation can assign duplicate task/process IDs:** the shared ID counter is advanced and checked without cross-CPU reservation, and tasks are published only afterward. Concurrent initializers can accept the same ID, making ID-based lookup or child waits ambiguous in applicable cases. See [EK9144](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9144) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1903). Source-only; no task creation or interleaving was run.

**EK9143 — alert formatting indexes past the specific-alert tables for unknown subsystem values:** the generic formatter accepts subsystem values through `0x7f` but its table ends at `0x43`; the optional m68k hook has a shorter table and an ineffective masked-value check. Checked-in producers use defined constants, so malformed/custom input is required. See [EK9143](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9143) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1834). Source-only; no alert was generated.

**OD10283 — NV40 RAM PLL calculation treats “no solution” as success:** `nv04_pll_calc()` returns zero when it finds no valid divider, but `nv40_ram_calc()` only rejects negative results and then uses uninitialized divider outputs to form the memory PLL values. The generic P-state path can proceed to programming. Applies to selected NV40-derived RAM backends when a requested frequency has no valid PLL solution. See [OD10283](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10283) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L27265). Source-only; no invalid frequency or reclock was run.

Graphics.library `MrgCop()` full-body and selected-caller pass (no new GD; GD9941 path rechecked; 2026-10-30): read all 145 physical lines / 59 `cloc 2.06` C code lines, confirmed selection in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src`, and traced visible ViewPort grouping, display callbacks, error propagation and semaphores through `DoViewFunction()` and Intuition `RethinkDisplay()`. The checked-in MakeVPort/MrgCop/LoadView sequence is serialized; no additional selected-path defect was established. GD9941 remains the separate conditional CloseScreen path. Graphics/Desktop represented-body coverage advances to **1,097/1,183 paths** and **431,210/572,682 C/header code lines (75.3%)**. See the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No display operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9432 update — m68k Utility `SetMem()` returns the resolved host pointer through guest D0:** the public result should be the guest destination address, so guest code consuming it cannot rely on a valid m68k pointer. Added as another instance of the existing optional guest/native pointer-boundary finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10360). The adjacent Utility thunk recheck retained existing EK9200/EK9206/EK10213 findings and found no additional issue in `Strlcpy`/`Strlcat`. Source-only; no emulated API call or build was run.



**EK8839 restored — ARM32 Raspberry Pi high-window virtual-to-physical translation uses TagItem record addresses instead of `ti_Data`:** a caller translating an address at or above `0xf8000000` receives an incorrect physical address. Selected Raspberry Pi boot code supplies distinct virtual/physical bases; checked-in callers do not establish that their allocator buffers enter this range. See [EK8839](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8839) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10368). Source-only; no mapping or DMA operation was run.


**[EK8838](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8838) — m68k AC68080 AMMX context save predecrements from the AMMX member base:** the 256-byte save lands in the preceding FPU context while restore reads the AMMX member. A task with live AMMX state loses it across switches; if `AFF_FPU` is also set, the save overwrites saved FP/FSAVE data. Applies to maintained m68k-Amiga builds on detected AC68080 hardware. The address/layout defect is source-confirmed; hardware behavior and in-tree AMMX clients remain unverified. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1498). No build or task switch was run; source-only.


**EK8861 restored — OpenSBI FDT readers do not bound property-name strings:** invalid `off_dt_strings`/`nameoff` values can make early boot parsing read outside the supplied DTB before its EFI/default fallback; the optional `dumpdt` walk also reads names of otherwise ignored properties. The trigger requires a malformed or truncated firmware FDT; the diagnostic path additionally requires `dumpdt`. See [EK8861](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8861) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10370). Source-only; no malformed blob or boot was exercised.


**EK8862 restored and expanded — the OpenSBI EFI retry reuses the prior actual map size as buffer capacity and keeps stale collected regions:** after a failed first `ExitBootServices`, map growth can make the refresh fail with `EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`, whose status is ignored; even a successful refresh does not rebuild the arrays consumed by kernel startup/MMU mapping. The trigger depends on firmware map changes. See [EK8862](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8862) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10375). Source-only; no EFI boot was run.


**EK8863 restored — the OpenSBI EFI stub silently drops firmware descriptors after its 24-region table fills:** if a needed ACPI root or child table lies in an omitted range, the post-MMU ACPI/PLIC path may fault unless another mapping covers it. The descriptor and table placement trigger remains firmware-dependent. See [EK8863](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8863) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10378). Source-only; no EFI/ACPI boot path was run.


**EK8864 restored — the RISC-V OpenSBI UEFI path collects up to 16 usable ranges but startup only maps and publishes the first eight:** any later non-coalesced ranges in that retained window are unavailable to the normal allocator. The trigger depends on firmware presenting more than eight distinct usable ranges. See [EK8864](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8864) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10381). Source-only; no EFI map or boot was used.


**EK8845 restored and qualified — on ExecSMP, child cleanup can report through a cached former parent after `ChildOrphan()`:** if the process requested notify-on-death, cleanup can still enqueue/signal its completion; a later repeated removal can also bypass a newly head-inserted sibling in the specified single-child interleaving. No maintained direct `ChildOrphan()` caller was found. See [EK8845](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8845) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10384). Source-only; no child operation or SMP schedule was run.


Exec/Kernel report/index reconciliation (updated 2026-11-04): the report now has 1,224 numbered finding headings and 9 additional legacy anchor-only entries with explanatory text; the prior 355/433/9 recovery recount is obsolete. This index contains 974 unique Exec/Kernel IDs across 1,017 link occurrences. Numeric heading links lacking stable anchors were repaired. These counts describe report structure, not source coverage or subsystem completion; see the coverage ledger for reviewed/remaining source.

**Efika OpenFirmware bootstrap build-manifest pass (2026-10-30):** audited the complete selected `mmakefile.src`, confirming its six source inputs, dependency generation, linker inputs/entry, and explicit normal and quick targets. The aggregate boot edge remains commented; no default-image inclusion is claimed. No separate build-graph issue established. **OD10321 — Poseidon can drop a completed pipe reply at the hardware-shutdown timeout:** on the 300th poll, the shutdown task clears the pending count and exits before draining the HCD reply port. A completion queued during that final interval is never forwarded to the pipe caller. This ordinary completion path is selected by the 32-bit ARM Raspberry Pi package's USB2OTG controller, which does not advertise QuickIO. See [OD10321](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10321) and the [shutdown drain trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#poseidon-hcd-final-drain-shutdown-recheck-od10321). Source-only; no shutdown or I/O was run.

SDL GD5721 class-metadata lifetime recheck (2026-10-30): confirmed successful input registrations remain in the shared `HWData.drivers` list when SDL's subsequent `AddDisplayDriverA()` fails; the startup rollback then disposes their SDL class objects without `HW_RemoveDriver()`. BaseMeta frees class dispatch tables and Root disposal frees class storage, while `HW_EnumDrivers()` can still return the retained driver instances. Expanded GD5721 to describe the conditional stale-class dispatch consequence. GD2620's VBlank server/task lifetime remains separate. No registration failure, class disposal, enumeration, or method call was run; source-only.



**EK9275 strengthened — repeated m68k borrowed-object lookups can exhaust the shared 256-entry shadow map:** successful `FindResident`, `FindPort`, `FindSemaphore`, `FindTaskByPID`, `FindName`, `WhichLayer`, `DeviceProc`, `FindCliProc`, `GetConsoleTask`, `GetFileSysTask`, `SetConsoleTask`, or `SetFileSysTask` calls, and repeated `ViewPortAddress()` calls for a live Window, can allocate fresh shadows without releasing prior borrowed-result entries; after capacity is reached, the wrapper returns zero for a native object it found or returned. Limited to the optional m68k emulator and external guest calls; no maintained guest workload was established. `GetDeviceProc` and manual `FindTask` have separate lifecycle findings. See [EK9275](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9275) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L175). Source-only; no lookup or build was run.


**OD10324 — Nouveau can map host pages above a GPU's DMA address limit:** the AROS DMA shim ignores the NV04 MMU's `GFP_DMA32` request and accepts direct-bus addresses above 32 bits, then NV04 stores the address in a 32-bit PTE. Conditional on an NV04 host-page mapping receiving a page above 4 GiB. Limited to the explicit Nouveau target; the PC graphics aggregate edge is disabled. See [OD10324](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10324) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no GPU mapping or build was run.
**GD10286 — VulkanProbe leaves `radeonsi.hidd` open:** after a successful `OpenLibrary()`, no exit path calls `CloseLibrary()`, so each run retains a shared open reference. The probe is selected through an active `workbench-hidds` virtual edge; successful-open runtime reachability requires a separately supplied provider, absent from this snapshot. See [GD10286](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10286) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-library-reference-lifetime-pass). Source-only; no library load or probe was run.
**GD10287 — Softpipe and LLVMpipe dereference a failed RastPort allocation:** their per-cliprect `DisplayResource` methods assume `CreateRastPort()` succeeded; allocation failure faults during presentation and bypasses displaytarget unmap. Applies when the active aggregate selects Softpipe (`AROS_TARGET_TOOLCHAIN=yes`) or LLVMpipe (`AROS_TOOLCHAIN=llvm` and `AROS_TARGET_TOOLCHAIN=yes`), and to explicit module builds. See [GD10287](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10287) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#softpipe-and-llvmpipe-local-source-pass). Source-only; no presentation or allocation failure was run.
**GD10288 — `SetRGB4()` has signed overflow for valid component values 8–15:** it multiplies a promoted `UBYTE` by signed `0x11111111` before conversion to `ULONG`; C leaves the overflowing result undefined, so a compiler may produce an incorrect channel value. Applies on signed 32-bit-`int` targets; visible miscompilation is compiler-dependent. See [GD10288](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10288) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setrgb4-component-expansion-pass). Source-only; no palette operation or build was run.
**GD10289 — `DrawGList()` uses copy minterm for unmasked transparent sprites:** `0xc0` copies zero-valued sprite pixels over the destination even though the source FIXME identifies `0xe0` as intended. Limited to external bare-VSprite or shadowless-Bob clients; a checked-in caller census found no maintained GELS client, and Graphics animation helpers route ImageShadow Bobs through the separate masked branch. See [GD10289](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10289) and the [Graphics/Desktop caller census](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#drawglist-public-caller-census). Source-only; no sprite or build was run.
**GD10290 — TextEditor MCP displays vanilla `')'` as Space:** KeyToString maps 0x29 to the "space" token, while the parser maps that token to 0x20; acknowledging the displayed key can silently rewrite the binding. Requires a saved or user-created ')' binding in the explicitly selected optional MCP. See [GD10290](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10290) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-keystorage-roundtrip-pass). Source-only; no preferences UI or build was run.
**GD10291 — TextEditor MCP over-reads command buffers while saving spell settings:** serialization always reads 256 bytes from dynamically sized command contents (including the default empty command), and commands longer than 255 bytes also make Dataspace read past a 260-byte stack record. Requires the explicitly selected optional MCP. See [GD10291](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10291) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-command-serialization-pass). Source-only; no preferences save or build was run.

**GD10292 — NBalance test program leaks OS4 library references on interface failure:** the standalone test closes Utility, Graphics, Layers, and DataTypes only inside successful `GetInterface()` branches, leaving a base open if its interface lookup fails. Limited to the explicitly selected test target on AmigaOS 4. See [GD10292](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10292) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nbalance-test-startup-interface-failure-pass). Source-only; no interface failure or launch was run.
**GD10285 — TextEditor MCP initialization leaks partially created MUI subclasses:** a later subclass allocation failure leaves earlier classes allocated when selected MCP initialization fails. `Preference.c` contains a similar path, but the checked-in target does not select it, so it remains an external-build lead. Applies to the explicitly selected optional TextEditor MCP target; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See [GD10285](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10285) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-subclass-setup-and-rollback). Source-only; no failure or build was run.

**TextEditor MCP startup implementation full-body pass (GD10285 rechecked; 2026-10-30):** completed exact-path body coverage for `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcp/library.c` (210 physical lines / 124 `cloc 2.06` C code lines). Traced Locale/NBitmap ownership and `ClassInit()`/`ClassExpunge()` against shared failed-init cleanup; confirmed the existing GD10285 partial-subclass leak and found no independent startup defect. Graphics/Desktop represented body coverage advances to **1,101/1,183 paths (93.1%)** and **431,468/572,682 C/header code lines (75.3%)**. The optional MCP target is not claimed as default-image content. No module load, allocation failure, GUI operation or build was run; source-only.

**OD10325 — NVIDIA accelerated bitmap operations compute ROP masks with a negative signed left shift:** `CopyBox` and other selected bitmap methods evaluate `~0 << depth`, invoking undefined behavior for ordinary depths (and a width-sized shift at 32 bpp). The exact mask/output is compiler-dependent; the NVIDIA HIDD is an explicit optional target. See [OD10325](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10325) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidia-hidd-class-copybox-mask). Source-only; no build or hardware operation was run.
**OD10326 — NVIDIA on-bitmap allocation rollback frees an invalid sentinel:** if VRAM allocation fails, constructor cleanup passes the encoded failure value to `Deallocate()`, which alerts under consistency checks or may corrupt the card-memory allocator without them. Applies to explicit optional NVIDIA HIDD builds. See [OD10326](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10326) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidia-onbitmap-failed-allocation-rollback). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**OD10327 — NVIDIA HIDD initialization dereferences a failed state allocation:** pool exhaustion after adapter setup leaves the `CardState` pointer NULL, then `InitMode()` writes through it before initialization can roll back. Applies to explicit optional NVIDIA HIDD builds. See [OD10327](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10327) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidia-initialization-and-map-failure-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**OD10328 — NVIDIA HIDD initialization disables interrupts and spins forever on failure:** missing hardware or another returning initialization failure reaches an unconditional `Disable()` plus infinite loop instead of returning FALSE; a non-final attribute-base acquisition failure hangs earlier under OD2399. On a single-CPU build this prevents normal interrupt-driven progress. Applies to explicit optional NVIDIA HIDD builds. See [OD10328](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10328) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidia-initialization-and-map-failure-pass). Source-only; no load failure was induced.

**OD10329 — Atheros5000 unsupported wireless band reaches configuration with an uninitialized HAL mode:** `SetOptions()` stores public A/N or unsupported band values, while `ConfigureAdapter()` initializes `hal_band` and rates only for B/G before using them. An external SANA-II client can therefore cause indeterminate HAL mode/rate configuration during `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` or online reconfiguration. Normal WirelessManager advertises only B/G. See [OD10329](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10329) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#atheros5000-unit-band-selection-pass). Source-only; no request or radio was used.


**OD3657 — Generic I²C `WriteWord` drops the low byte of a 16-bit value:** it constructs subaddress + high byte + low byte but sends a two-byte transaction, so the low byte never reaches the device even when the method reports success. Applies to packages selecting generic `hidd-i2c` (including RISC-V OpenSBI and PPC Sam440) when a client calls `WriteWord`; no in-tree caller was found. See [OD3657](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3657) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no bus transaction was run.


**OD1151 — Generic bit-banged I²C can poll forever when `RiseFallTime` is zero:** SCL polling does not reduce its timeout counter and retains the bus semaphore. Requires explicit bit-banged HIDD use, a direct client setting zero, and SCL remaining low; no default packaged trigger is established. See [OD1151](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1151) and the [reachability/restoration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L35315). Source-only.

**GD10235 — Vulkan-Hpp typed output helpers can pass too little storage:** enhanced/RAII `writeMicromapsPropertyEXT()` forwards a multi-micromap count and stride with one `DataType` buffer; enhanced/RAII NV acceleration-structure-handle helpers can provide less than the API’s fixed eight-byte output when instantiated with a smaller type. Applies to downstream use of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp APIs; no checked-in C++ caller was found. See [GD10235](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10235) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**EK10226 — OpenSBI RISC-V executes relocated modules without instruction-fetch synchronization:** the boot ELF loader writes and relocates module code, then boot-package resident initializers run without `fence.i`/SBI remote-fence synchronization. On systems whose instruction fetch is not coherent with stores, a module may execute stale or unsynchronized bytes. Coherent systems are unaffected; no boot-time failure was reproduced. See [EK10226](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10226) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).


**OD2355 — KMS leaks loaded keymap segments on rejection and conversion:** `OpenKeymap()` returns without unloading a rejected non-HUNK segment, and converter builds lose the original LoadSeg pointer on both failed and successful conversion. Repeated loads retain segment memory. Applies to KMS when those loader paths occur. See [OD2355](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2355) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.
**OD2356 — KMS duplicate keymap cleanup passes a raw AllocMem block to UnLoadSeg:** conversion output is a raw allocation, but duplicate-name cleanup treats it as a DOS LoadSeg list. It can corrupt memory or fail to free correctly. Applies to converter builds on concurrent duplicate short-name loads or repeated full-path loads. See [OD2356](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2356) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no duplicate cleanup was run.
**OD2357 — KMS converter omits high-key descriptor padding from allocation sizing:** odd-sized high-key descriptors advance the copy cursor beyond the extent included in `kmsegsize`, potentially overlapping the stored keymap name or exceeding the allocation. Applies when a converter-enabled build loads a map with the stated descriptor layout; no shipped example is established. See [OD2357](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2357) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.
**OD2358 — KMS converter reads keymap fields and descriptors without segment bounds:** malformed HUNK payloads or relocated pointers can make fixed-field and descriptor reads exceed the loaded segment. Applies to converter-enabled builds with malformed keymap data. See [OD2358](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2358) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no malformed map was loaded.

**OD10330 — Poseidon can free endpoint state while client pipes remain open after removal timeout:** after about 15 seconds, hardware removal forces the device use count to zero, frees its endpoint/configuration objects and later frees the hardware record. A later close of a still-open endpoint pipe dereferences its freed endpoint. The 32-bit ARM Raspberry Pi package selects Poseidon and USB2OTG; the trigger requires a client to retain its pipe through forced hardware removal. No in-tree timing sequence is established. See [OD10330](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10330) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no removal, pipe close, HCD or build was run.

**OD4094 — USB2OTG reports `CMD_FLUSH` success without cancelling transfers:** its handler returns success without touching pending or active requests. Poseidon's selected hardware-shutdown task calls this command and then waits for request completions; the 32-bit ARM Raspberry Pi package selects both Poseidon and USB2OTG. This is distinct from OD10321's final-poll lost reply. See the [Other Drivers report](AROS-other-drivers.md) and [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no transfer or shutdown was run.

**OD10331 — CAMD USB-MIDI port open can race interface release and use a freed binding:** on ExecSMP, the optional embedded CAMD driver's port-open callback reads a Poseidon binding without a lifetime pin while release can remove it, stop its worker and free it. The candidate is downstream of OD4300's format rejection and OD4301's callback-register mismatch; no normal unmodified-path reachability is claimed. See [OD10331](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10331) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#camd-usb-midi-openrelease-binding-lifetime-pass). Source-only; no callback, release, or build was run.


**OD10332 — WinGDI cursor conversion can overrun wrapped scratch buffers:** on 32-bit MinGW, a very large pointer bitmap can wrap the four-byte area calculation to a small allocation, after which mask creation loops over the full pixel area. The trigger requires a huge bitmap and successful wrapped allocations; current normal display registration is gated by GD6317. This is the WINGDI-specific path, separate from generic-display GD9418. See [OD10332](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10332) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mingw-wingdi-selected-target-reconciliation). Source-only; no large bitmap or cursor operation was run.

**EK869 — Amiga SAD can lose UART input to serial.device:** `KrnObtainInput()` claims success without taking the UART, while the optional Amiga serial HIDD installs a receive interrupt that reads the same register as SAD. A byte arriving between SAD polls can be diverted to serial.device. Limited to explicit m68k-Amiga serial HIDD/device targets; their aggregate edges are disabled. See [EK869](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek869) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1576). Source-only; no debugger or UART was used.

**PPP target-selection correction (OD4135 and OD4256; 2026-10-30):** the active MetaMake chain is `AROS` → `workbench-complete` → `workbench-devs` → `workbench-devs-common` → `workbench-devs-networks` → `workbench-devs-networks-ppp`. The m68k-Amiga boot chain also selects the serial HIDD. Updated the two detailed findings to reflect standard full Workbench and m68k-Amiga package selection; no source-body or LOC credit. See [OD4135](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4135), [OD4256](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4256), and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No target was built or device exercised; source-only.

**BWFM package-selection correction (OD4404, OD4409, OD4475, OD9669, OD9873, OD9875, OD9876 and OD9965; 2026-10-30):** traced both Raspberry Pi ARM32/AArch64 roots through `AROS_TARGET_ARCH=raspi`, the active `workbench-devs-networks-soc-raspi` aggregate and boot `PKG_RSRC` lists. The standard full build selects `bwfm.device` and packages `bwfm.resource`; AROSTCP is also selected through `workbench-network`. Corrected stale optional/disabled-edge qualifications in the affected report entries. No code-body or LOC credit. See the [Other Drivers report](AROS-other-drivers.md) and [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No build, scan, or radio was used; source-only.

**Network-driver aggregate selection correction (OD4135, OD4256, nForce findings; 2026-10-30):** MetaMake's active `#MM-` declarations include PPP unconditionally in `workbench-devs-networks` and include `workbench-devs-networks-nforce-$(AROS_TARGET_CPU)`. The active full Workbench chain reaches `workbench-devs-common` and its network aggregate; on i386, the CPU-specific edge selects `workbench-devs-networks-nforce-i386`. The m68k-Amiga boot package also selects its serial HIDD, confirming OD4135's concrete backend. Earlier coverage-ledger statements describing PPP or i386 nForce as absent from the default aggregate are superseded. No build or device operation was run; source-selection evidence only. See the [Other Drivers report](AROS-other-drivers.md) and [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md).


**EK10227 — Moira division overflow can leave C set:** selected DIVS.W, DIVU.W, and 64-bit-dividend signed/unsigned DIVL overflow paths set V but omit the documented C clear. A prior set carry survives. Limited to explicit `m68kemu.library` builds. See [EK10227](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10227) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1768). No instruction or build was run; source-only.


**EK10228 — Moira dump-format setter updates the wrong style:** `setDumpNumberFormat()` changes instruction disassembly formatting, while data dump routines continue using the unchanged data style. The checked-in AROS bridge has no call to this public C++ setter, so current product impact is unconfirmed. See [EK10228](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10228) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1762). Source-only; no output was generated.


**EK9473 — m68kemu guest word/long accesses can wrap the 32 MiB arena bounds:** both the inline width helpers and Moira's selected word callbacks use overflow-prone `addr + width` checks. At `0xFFFFFFFF`, the word check wraps; selected Moira disables alignment faults, so the guest access reaches the callback and indexes outside the arena. Limited to explicit m68kemu builds. See [EK9473](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9473) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8566). This corrects an earlier caller review; no guest access was run.


**EK10229 — reading the m68kemu return sentinel stops the guest:** `read16()` ends the run for any access to `0x00DEAD00`, although the address lies inside guest RAM and is not reserved from heap use. An ordinary data read can therefore terminate emulation before the guest returns. Limited to explicit m68kemu runs. See [EK10229](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10229) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8557). No guest access was run.


**EK10230 — the m68k disk-library loader truncates tables above 1,000 vectors:** it stops counting at 1,000 without requiring the function-table terminator, builds only those slots, then returns the base as successful. Higher guest vectors can jump through unrelated guest memory. Limited to explicit m68kemu disk fallback; no in-tree library of this size was found. See [EK10230](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10230) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1791). Source-only; no library was loaded.


**EK10231 — Moira misses signed 32-bit DIVSL.L overflow:** with dividend `0x80000000` and divisor −1, the quotient exceeds signed 32-bit range, but the selected helper leaves V clear and writes the quotient/remainder registers. This follows the selected M68040 DIVL path in explicit `m68kemu.library` builds. See [EK10231](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10231) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1768). No instruction or build was run; source-only.

**OD10264 — Bluetooth removal events queue invalidated object pointers:** `REMHARDWARE`, `REMCLASS`, and `REMERRORMSG` queue pointers after freeing their objects; `REMDEVICE` queues a retained outer pointer after child state and its lock are torn down. No checked-in listener dereferences these payloads, and the public API does not define their lifetime; this remains a conditional external-subscriber contract candidate. See [OD10264](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10264) and the [event-payload lifetime trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-removal-event-payload-lifetime-od10264). Source-only; no event or removal was run.
**OD9737 — Bluetooth error-log list races on ExecSMP:** writers use processor-local `Forbid()` without a list lock, while readers use only a shared base lock; BTErrorLog's `DEBUG/S` mode traverses the list without taking even that lock. Overlapping add/remove/read operations can corrupt or misread the list. See [OD9737](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9737) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no concurrent schedule was run.
**OD10333 — BTCtrl reports discovery finished when `SCAN WAIT` setup allocation fails:** message-port or event-hook allocation failure skips the wait, while the scan can continue and BTCtrl still prints completion with success status. Applies when the BTCtrl shell command and Bluetooth library are available and a scan starts successfully. See [OD10333](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10333) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-btctrl-wait-allocation-failure-pass). Source-only; no allocation or scan was run.

**OD2744 — Envy24 AHI Start leaks partial buffers after allocation failure:** failed Start returns without unwinding allocations or setting the active flag; AHI does not call Stop on that error, and a repeated play/record request overwrites the retained pointers. AHI FreeAudio's Stop path also skips inactive directions. Applies to selected AROS Envy24 AHI builds under the documented allocation-failure/retry sequence. See [OD2744](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2744) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#envy24-start-error-and-retry-caller-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or audio operation was run.

**OD10334 — BTCtrl `SCAN WAIT` can miss discovery completion and wait indefinitely:** the event handler is registered only after discovery starts, and registration does not replay earlier events. If discovery stops in that gap, the first state check never runs unless another signal wakes the task. Applies to BTCtrl with a scan that completes in the narrow start-to-registration interval. See [OD10334](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10334) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-btctrl-discovery-stop-lost-wakeup-pass). Source-only; no scan or task schedule was run.

**OD10335 — BTCtrl silently skips requested remote-name lookup on setup allocation failure:** message-port or channel allocation failure skips the request without an error and leaves the command status successful. Applies when BTCtrl and the Bluetooth library are available for a found device. See [OD10335](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10335) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#btctrl-remotename-allocation-failure-pass). Source-only; no allocation or device request was run.

**OD10336 — forgetting a device can strand its active remote-name request:** removal moves the device out of the list used by completion lookup; the handler then skips replying to the channel and clearing the request slot. Applies when a remote-name request overlaps BTCtrl or Preferences forget. See [OD10336](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10336) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#btctrl-remotename-device-retirement-pass). Source-only; no device request or interleaving was run.

**EK9213 — m68k TagItem conversion mistakes in-range numeric data for pointers:** scalar values such as `TAG_SKIP` counts, task stack sizes, ASL dimensions, and CyberGraphX mode dimensions can be replaced by host pointers. Applies to optional 64-bit-host m68kemu callers using the generic converter. See [EK9213](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9213) and the [ASL scalar-tag pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10514). Source-only; no guest tag list or API call was run.
**EK9215 — m68kemu returns an unshadowed native Task pointer from `NewCreateTaskA()`:** the 64-bit native pointer is narrowed into guest D0, but subsequent task APIs resolve only registered shadows or guest-arena pointers. A guest using the returned handle may not address the created Task. Optional m68kemu only; no maintained guest caller found. See [EK9215](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9215) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5034). No guest task was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel m68k Commodities list-marshalling pass (EK9432 expanded; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-30): traced `CopyBrokerList()` and `FreeBrokerList()` guest `List *` arguments through the generated thunks into native `RemHead()`/`FreeVec()`. Native traversal uses incompatible host pointer width and byte order for guest list links, including during the initial free of an empty list. Added this case to the existing guest/native boundary finding, separate from EK9893's `NewBroker` mismatch. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest call or build was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel CLI synthesized-stream failure re-review (EK9875 restored; 2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): confirmed that `internal_CliInitAny()` can successfully open a local stdout stream, then return early when stderr synthesis fails without closing or publishing that stdout handle. Narrowed the trigger to streamless/BNULL output and error inputs; ordinary inherited live streams are excluded. Rebuilt the detailed candidate from the caller and process-cleanup paths. See [EK9875](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9875) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7444). No failure or CLI startup was induced; source-only.


Exec/Kernel PC bootstrap framebuffer capacity re-review (EK9876 restored; 2026-10-30; no body/LOC credit): re-traced graphical Multiboot1/2 and VESA initialization: `fb_Init()` clears the text-cell mirror before `AllocFB()` attempts to reserve it from the fixed 16 MiB workspace, and the reservation result is ignored. Restored EK9876 for exceptionally large valid modes exceeding workspace capacity, while keeping EK344's separate mirror-reuse allegation withdrawn. See [EK9876](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9876) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7363). No boot or framebuffer operation was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel candidate disposition (EK9879 withdrawn as duplicate of OD3527; 2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the ARM processor-frequency mailbox buffer against the selected BCM2708 mailbox contract. See [OD3527](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3527) and the [Exec/Kernel disposition](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9879). No clock query or cache operation was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel m68k cache-unit candidate re-review (EK9880 restored; 2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): confirmed the public processor API specifies kB while the m68k initializer stores byte counts and its `GetCPUInfo()` writes them unchanged. A 68040 therefore returns 4,096 per L1 cache where the documented value is 4; the developer diagnostic labels the raw output as kB. The m68k ShowConfig formatter labels it in bytes and is consistent with the provider. See [EK9880](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9880) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7433). No query or diagnostic was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel optional PC IPI diagnostic re-review (EK9882 restored; historical EK749 alias; 2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): confirmed both `TEST_SMP_IPI` calls pass four arguments to the six-argument `core_DoCallIPI()` API. The local define is commented out and no build option enables it, so this affects only manually enabled diagnostic builds, not the default PC kernel. See [EK9882](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9882) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3837). No compile or IPI was run; source-only.


Exec/Kernel AArch64 cache-sentinel candidate re-review (EK9884 restored; 2026-10-30; no path/LOC credit): confirmed the public `$FFFFFFFF` length sentinel is documented to clear all addresses, but the native AArch64 helper takes its whole-cache route only when the start is NULL. A non-NULL start falls through to a 4 GiB virtual-address loop and may fault on unmapped ranges; no maintained caller uses this form. See [EK9884](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9884) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7653). No cache operation was run; source-only.

**EK9885 — pthread exposes 18 scheduling, concurrency, and process-sharing functions with no in-tree definitions:** calls compile from the copied public header but cannot link against the selected pthread archive. Source-only; no link was run.

**EK9886 — m68k GadTools bridge omits `CreateGadgetA` (LVO −30) and `CreateContext` (−114):** emulated calls to the unregistered vectors return D0=0, so guest gadget construction fails. **EK9887 — m68k diskfont bridge omits `OpenDiskFont` (LVO −30) and `NewScaledDiskFont` (−54):** emulated calls to either unregistered vector return D0=0, so guest font requests fail. **EK9888 — m68k Utility bridge omits `NextTagItem` (LVO −48):** emulated calls return zero, which looks like normal end-of-list and can silently skip a nonempty tag list. Applies to Utility clients running under m68kemu.
