See [GD10413](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10413-copy-can-dereference-a-null-device-procedure-while-examining-a-soft-link) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-shell-command-full-body-mode-and-error-path-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10414 — AmigaGuide navigator installs an empty clip region after rectangle allocation failure:** `InstallClipRegionSafe()` ignores `OrRectRegion()` failure and proceeds to install the empty region before drawing. See [GD10414](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10414-amigaguide-navigator-installs-an-empty-clip-region-after-rectangle-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-library-clearregion-full-body-and-amigaguide-caller-pass). Optional AmigaGuide datatype caller; allocation-failure path is source-only.

**GD10415 — Compositor dereferences a missing alpha region after allocation failure:** it calls `OrRectRegion()` after `NewRegion()` can fail without checking the result. See [GD10415](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10415-compositor-dereferences-a-missing-alpha-region-after-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor monitor with alpha bitmaps; allocation-failure path is source-only.

**GD10416 — Compositor treats a failed display-region build as an empty display:** it ignores the initial `OrRectRegion()` failure, then removes all bitmap nodes from visibility and redraws the display void. See [GD10416](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10416-compositor-treats-a-failed-display-region-build-as-an-empty-display) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor monitor full redraw under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10417 — Failed alpha-region expansion suppresses later alpha recomposition:** a failed union leaves the alpha tracking region incomplete, so incremental opaque bitmap updates can skip overlapping alpha redraws. See [GD10417](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10417-failed-alpha-region-expansion-suppresses-later-alpha-recomposition) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor alpha regions under allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10418 — Compositor can paint the display background over a bitmap after region subtraction fails:** it ignores `ClearRegionRegion()` failure, then treats the still-unsubtracted bitmap area as display void and backfills over it. See [GD10418](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10418-compositor-can-paint-the-display-background-over-a-bitmap-after-region-subtraction-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor opaque bitmap redraw under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10419 — Compositor redraws an unclipped bitmap region when display intersection fails:** `AndRegionRegion()` failure leaves the full bitmap region in place, which is later passed to a CopyBox API requiring in-bounds coordinates. See [GD10419](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10419-compositor-redraws-an-unclipped-bitmap-region-when-display-intersection-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor partially off-display opaque bitmap under region allocation failure; backend consequence varies; source-only.

**GD10420 — Failed opaque-region subtraction lets lower Compositor bitmaps overwrite upper ones:** ignored `ClearRectRegion()` failure leaves overlapping pixels visible in lower layers, which draw later in the same top-to-bottom traversal. See [GD10420](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10420-failed-opaque-region-subtraction-lets-lower-compositor-bitmaps-overwrite-upper-ones) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor overlapping opaque bitmaps under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10421 — NList demo image drawing loops can wrap at the signed coordinate limit:** signed `WORD` loop counters advance by two through inclusive coordinates; on wrapping targets, the optional custom-image renderer can fail to terminate at the coordinate limit. See [GD10421](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10421-nlist-demo-image-drawing-loops-can-wrap-at-the-signed-coordinate-limit) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nlist-demo-custom-image-renderer-full-body-and-caller-pass). Optional NList demo/custom image tag and extreme geometry; medium confidence, source-only.

**OD10421 — DRM EDID-to-SAD helper returns descriptors from only the first audio block:** it stops after the first CTA audio block, omitting any later SADs. See [OD10421](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10421-drm-edid-to-sad-helper-returns-descriptors-from-only-the-first-audio-block) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-sad-extraction-pass). Optional VMware/Nouveau DRM cores; no in-tree caller found, so impact is limited to external/future clients; source-only.

**OD10422 — DiskImage Expat allocator can wrap the private-header size:** adding its `size_t` header to a near-maximum allocation request can wrap to a small `AllocPooled()` size while recording the original large request. Affects the default allocator in x86-aros and ppc-aros `expat.library` when the public `XML_MemMalloc()` API receives such a request; undersized-allocation consequence depends on the wrapped small allocation succeeding. See [OD10422](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10422-diskimage-expat-allocator-can-wrap-the-private-header-size) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-expat-pool-allocator-full-body-and-size-overflow-pass). Source-only.

**OD10423 — MountHDF divides by zero for zero geometry parameters:** `BLOCKSPERTRACK` or `SURFACES` can be supplied as zero, making the computed cylinder size zero before the DOS-node cylinder-count division. Affects the x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage `MountHDF` commands. See [OD10423](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10423-mounthdf-divides-by-zero-for-zero-geometry-parameters) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-tooltypes-and-mounthdf-geometry-parameter-pass). Source-only.

**OD10424 — MountHDF leaks its DOS node when a duplicate name is rejected:** `MakeDosNode()`'s allocation is not freed when `AddBootNode()` fails because `IHD<unit>` already exists. Repeated attempts retain one allocation each in x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds. See [OD10424](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10424-mounthdf-leaks-its-dos-node-when-a-duplicate-name-is-rejected) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-tooltypes-and-mounthdf-geometry-parameter-pass). Source-only.

**OD10425 — DiskImage AROS fallback truncates 64-bit file offsets:** the AROS DOS64 stub falls back to `Seek()` after narrowing a `QUAD` offset to `LONG`. Selected DMG parsing passes 64-bit plist/resource offsets through this path, so sections above `LONG_MAX` can be read from the wrong position or fail. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds; source-only. See [OD10425](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10425-diskimage-aros-fallback-truncates-64-bit-file-offsets) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-dos64-helper-and-dmg-offset-caller-pass).

**OD10426 — DiskImage image-name allocation failure is reported as success:** `DITAG_GetImageName` checks the non-NULL output-slot address instead of the `ASPrintf()` result, so allocation failure leaves the returned name NULL and does not set `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE`. The optional Zune list then displays “no disk” for the still-mounted image and treats the entry as empty for eject/double-click behavior. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds; source-only. See [OD10426](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10426-diskimage-image-name-allocation-failure-is-reported-as-success) and the [DiskImage GetImageName caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-getimagename-error-result-and-gui-caller-reconciliation-2026-11-06).

**OD10428 — DiskImage reply port signals reserved bit zero:** the custom reply port leaves `mp_SigBit` zero, then synchronous operations set it to `PA_SIGNAL`; Exec signals the caller on `SIGF_ABORT`, and `WaitPort()` consumes that bit while waiting. A pending or concurrent abort signal can therefore be swallowed during the synchronous call. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage device/library builds; source-only. See [OD10428](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10428-diskimage-reply-port-signals-reserved-bit-zero) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-no-signal-port-reply-signal-bit-and-callers-pass).

**OD10429 — CUE CDDA byte swapping uses unaligned word accesses on PowerPC:** the Motorola-track path passes the caller's `scsi_Data` buffer to `swab2()`, which dereferences it as `ULONG *`/`UWORD *`. Affects ppc-aros CUE CDDA reads with unaligned buffers; source-only. See [OD10429](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10429-cue-cdda-byte-swapping-uses-unaligned-word-accesses-on-powerpc) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-swab2-alignment-and-cue-cdda-caller-pass).

**OD10430 — DiskImage extraction overwrites a predictable temporary-file collision:** DMS/XAD/XPK extraction writes `unit_<unit>.<ext>` with `MODE_NEWFILE` in the configured temp directory or `T:`; an existing same-named file is replaced, then normal cleanup deletes it. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage plugin builds; source-only. See [OD10430](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10430-diskimage-extraction-overwrites-a-predictable-temporary-file-collision) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-temporary-file-name-collision-and-extraction-callers).

**OD10431 — DiskImage reports successful abort for a request already in progress:** `LibAbortIO()` searches only the queued requests and defaults to success; once the unit worker dequeues a request, abort reports success without setting `IOERR_ABORTED`, while the operation continues to normal completion. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage device requests; source-only. See [OD10431](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10431-diskimage-reports-successful-abort-for-a-request-already-in-progress) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-beginio-abortio-queue-and-completion-pass).

**OD9710 — USB HID report-descriptor debug dump reads past the final partial line:** `nDebugMem()` always evaluates 16 byte arguments, even when the final row contains fewer bytes, so a descriptor length not divisible by 16 causes reads beyond its exact-sized report buffer. The binding GUI and selected parser-error paths reach this diagnostic. Affects explicit builds selecting Poseidon's ROM USB HID class; source-only. See [OD9710](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9710) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-error-dump-and-partial-source-pass).

**OD10433 — USB HID report parser reads truncated item bytes past the descriptor:** short-item payload bytes and incomplete long-item header bytes are dereferenced without checking the remaining descriptor length. A declared long-item payload is skipped without validation, and the parser may report success after advancing past the end. Affects builds selecting the standalone Poseidon ROM USB HID class when a report descriptor ends partway through an item; source-only. See [OD10433](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10433-usb-hid-report-parser-reads-truncated-item-bytes-past-the-descriptor) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-report-parser-item-boundary-pass).
**OD10434 — CDFS closes the I/O-request pointer slot instead of its request:** normal device teardown passes the address of `bp_IOStdReq` to `CloseDevice()` and leaves the successful request/port allocations unreleased. Affects optional CDFS builds; source-only. See [OD10434](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10434-cdfs-buffer-cache-deletion-closes-the-pointer-slot-instead-of-its-io-request).

**OD10435 — ISO9660 volume dates use the wrong ASCII digit base:** decimal conversion subtracts `'9'` instead of `'0'`, so mounted volume dates do not reflect the descriptor. Affects optional CDFS builds mounting ISO9660 media; source-only. See [OD10435](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10435-iso9660-ascii-date-conversion-subtracts-the-wrong-digit-base).

**OD10436 — Rock Ridge NM names and AS comments are mishandled:** fitting fields are skipped, and a long ISO identifier can make the NM copy size negative before conversion to unsigned `IPTR`. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with those extensions; source-only. See [OD10436](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10436-rock-ridge-nm-names-and-as-comments-are-skipped-unless-they-exceed-remaining-capacity).

**OD10437 — ISO9660 locate leaks a lock record on a non-directory intermediate component:** one failed multi-component path shape returns without freeing the allocated lock. Affects optional CDFS builds; source-only. See [OD10437](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10437-iso-path-traversal-leaks-a-lock-record-for-a-non-directory-intermediate-component).

**OD10438 — ISO9660 unmount leaks path-table storage:** normal unmount frees the volume structure but omits its separately allocated table bytes and entry array. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with a path table; source-only. See [OD10438](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10438-iso9660-unmount-leaks-separately-allocated-path-table-storage).

**OD10439 — ISO9660 directory lookup applies its offset twice:** after selecting the cache block for a directory offset, the code indexes that block using the full directory offset. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with directories spanning multiple blocks; source-only. See [OD10439](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10439-iso9660-directory-lookup-applies-the-full-directory-offset-twice).

**OD10440 — ISO9660 path-table lengths and parent indexes are unchecked:** incomplete entries can be retained and invalid parent indexes later address beyond the table. Affects optional CDFS builds using ISO path tables; source-only. See [OD10440](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10440-iso9660-path-table-entry-lengths-and-parent-indexes-are-not-validated).

**OD10441 — ISO9660 directory and Rock Ridge record lengths are not bounded:** declared record and extension sizes are consumed before being checked against their enclosing record and block. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with inconsistent directory records; source-only. See [OD10441](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10441-iso9660-directory-and-rock-ridge-record-lengths-are-not-bounded).

**OD10442 — DiskImage READ CD output is not bounded by `scsi_Length`:** the SCSI dispatcher passes the caller buffer and CDB frame count to the plugin without passing its declared capacity; CCD, CUE, MDS, and NRG write the requested CDDA bytes directly or through an audio decoder. An undersized `scsi_Length` can be overrun. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros builds selecting those plugins; source-only. See [OD10442](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10442-diskimage-read-cd-paths-do-not-bound-audio-output-to-scsi_length).

**OD10443 — DiskImage INQUIRY truncates its vendor, product, and revision identifiers:** the fixed-width response helper replaces each field's final character with NUL. Affects DiskImage device builds; source-only. See [OD10443](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10443-diskimage-inquiry-strings-overwrite-the-final-byte-of-each-identifier).

**OD10444 — DiskImage reads the SCSI opcode before validating CDB length:** a zero-length or missing CDB is dereferenced before the opcode switch's length checks. Affects DiskImage `HD_SCSICMD`; source-only. See [OD10444](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10444-diskimage-reads-the-cdb-opcode-before-checking-its-declared-length).

**OD10445 — DiskImage retains the prior caller's error-output pointer:** a later failing UnitControl request can write through a stack pointer saved by an earlier synchronous wrapper call. Affects DiskImage public UnitControl APIs; source-only. See [OD10445](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10445-diskimage-retains-a-callers-error-pointer-after-unitcontrol-returns).

**OD10446 — DiskImage READ CAPACITY underflows for sub-block Generic images:** a 0–511-byte image is accepted with zero sectors, but the SCSI handler subtracts one and reports last LBA `0xffffffff`. Affects DiskImage builds with the built-in Generic plugin; source-only. See [OD10446](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10446-diskimage-read-capacity-underflows-for-a-generic-image-smaller-than-one-block).

**OD10447 — DiskImage persists an invalid path if `NameFromFH()` fails:** successful image open is followed by saving the unchecked canonical-path buffer. Affects x86-aros/ppc-aros DiskImage filename-tag mounts; source-only. See [OD10447](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10447-diskimage-saves-an-invalid-path-when-namefromfh-fails).

**OD10448 — DRM mode validation accepts modes without a compatible CRTC:** when an attached encoder accepts a mode but no registered CRTC matches its `possible_crtcs` mask, the generic probe helper leaves the mode status at `MODE_OK`. No selected in-tree trigger was established; optional VMware/Nouveau DRM core candidate. Source-only. See [OD10448](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10448-drm-mode-validation-accepts-modes-without-a-compatible-crtc) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vmware-drm-mode-validation-with-no-compatible-crtc-pass).
**GD10422 — NList demo custom images discard inherited Area attribute updates:** the custom `OM_SET` drops unhandled tags, so NList's selected `MUIA_Disabled=FALSE` attachment update does not reach `MUIC_Area`. See [GD10422](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10422-nlist-demo-custom-images-discard-inherited-area-attribute-updates) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nlist-demo-custom-image-renderer-full-body-and-caller-pass). Optional NList custom-image path with a disabled object; source-only.
**GD10424 — NList demo abandons caller-created image objects during shutdown:** image cleanup detaches the NLI and two button objects without disposing them; the still-live NLI instance makes custom-class deletion fail, and the demo ignores that result. See [GD10424](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10424-nlist-demo-abandons-caller-created-image-objects-during-shutdown) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nlist-demo-custom-image-renderer-full-body-and-caller-pass). Optional demo; allocations persist only until process exit; source-only.
**OD10449 — CDFS does not reject a negative `Read()` length:** at a nonzero file offset the signed length can bypass the EOF clamp, then mix with unsigned copy lengths; on 64-bit targets a negative value can become a near-4-GiB `CopyMem()` size, while 32-bit targets can copy whole block chunks. Invalid-argument candidate only; no maintained negative-length caller was found. Optional CDFS target. See [OD10449](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10449-cdfs-treats-a-negative-read-length-as-the-remainder-of-the-file) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#cdfs-negative-read-length-pass). Source-only.
**OD10450 — CDFS negates the minimum signed seek offset:** on 32-bit builds, `-LONG_MIN` is undefined even when seeking backward 2 GiB from a sufficiently large file position is valid; the result can be a rejected or compiler-dependent seek. Optional CDFS target and large files only. See [OD10450](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10450-cdfs-negates-the-minimum-signed-seek-offset) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#cdfs-negative-seek-offset-pass). Source-only.

**GD10425 — VGAGfx changes VGA mode without the shared hardware lock:** showing a bitmap restores VGA registers and clears display memory without `HW_acc`, while drawing uses that semaphore around its own register and aperture writes. Concurrent view switching and bitmap updates can interleave those operations. Affects native PC sessions when VGAGfx is selected; the PC package manifests also list VESAGfx. Exact display effect is hardware/interleaving dependent. See [GD10425](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10425-vgagfx-changes-vga-mode-without-the-shared-hardware-lock) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vgagfx-show-mode-restore-hardware-lock-pass). Source-only.

**EK8785 — task.resource leaks per-task storage when a task removes itself:** the RemTask wrapper frees the per-task slot array only after calling Exec, but Exec's self-removal path switches away without returning; ETask and service cleanup do not free that separate allocation. Repeated short-lived tasks using task storage can leak memory. Applies to task.resource builds and self-removing tasks that created task slots. See [EK8785](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8785) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage row](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2140). No task exit was run; source-only.

**GD10426 — PopupMenu transition can blit an uncleared bitmap after RastPort allocation failure:** if the offscreen bitmap succeeds but the copied RastPort fails, rendering remains on the window while animation still blits the bitmap; P96 backing storage is not cleared. Affects explicit PopupMenu builds with animation enabled, with the backing-allocation path verified for M68k-Amiga P96; source-only. See [GD10426](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10426-popupmenu-transition-can-blit-an-uncleared-bitmap-after-rastport-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-offscreen-buffer-failure-pass).

**GD10427 — PopupMenu dereferences a missing input-event port after allocation failure:** handler setup returns a non-NULL partial record when a required port is missing, and the popup loop dereferences that port. Explicit PopupMenu builds under event-port allocation failure; source-only. See [GD10427](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10427-popupmenu-dereferences-a-missing-input-event-port-after-setup-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-main-implementation-full-body-pass).

**GD10428 — PopupMenu dereferences a failed root-menu allocation:** popup setup uses the `PM_SetupSubWindow()` result without checking for NULL before tag handling and menu dispatch. Explicit PopupMenu builds under root-window allocation failure; source-only. See [GD10428](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10428-popupmenu-dereferences-the-root-menu-after-its-allocation-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-main-implementation-full-body-pass).

**GD10429 — PopupMenu silently drops shadow-map regions after allocation failure:** list cloning, topography/shadow rectangle splitting, and generated-shadow copying can omit regions without propagating allocation failure. Nested menus may render missing or overlapping shadows. Optional PopupMenu builds with shadow mapping enabled under allocation failure; source-only. See [GD10429](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10429-popupmenu-silently-drops-shadow-map-regions-after-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-linked-list-full-body-and-submenu-shadow-map-pass).

**GD10430 — PopupMenu setters free getter-returned values before reusing them:** round-tripping internal title, string, submenu, or owned exclusion pointers through `PM_GetItemAttrsA()` and `PM_SetItemAttrsA()` frees the storage before the setter copies or stores it. Conditional on a client passing the same owned pointer back; source-only. See [GD10430](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10430-popupmenu-setters-free-getter-returned-values-before-reusing-them) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-item-attribute-full-body-and-aliasing-pass).

**GD10431 — Clearing a PopupMenu exclusion list leaves its freed pointer installed:** setting `PM_Exclude` to NULL frees an owned list but skips clearing the field, which later selection/destruction paths still traverse or free. Explicit PopupMenu library builds; source-only. See [GD10431](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10431-clearing-a-popupmenu-exclusion-list-leaves-its-freed-pointer-installed) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-item-attribute-full-body-and-aliasing-pass).

**GD10432 — Centered titleless PopupMenu items fault during drawing:** `PM_NewDrawItem()` calls `strlen(pmtitle)` in its centering branch without checking for NULL, although titleless items and `PM_Center` are independently accepted. Explicit PopupMenu builds with a centered item that has no normal title; source-only. See [GD10432](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10432-centered-popupmenu-items-call-strlen-on-a-missing-title) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-graphics-full-body-and-null-title-caller-pass).

**GD10433 — PopupMenu does not render the documented `PM_Object` item title:** the setter stores the BOOPSI object, but layout and drawing never measure or invoke it, leaving the item blank. Conditional on clients using `PM_Object`; source-only. See [GD10433](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10433-popupmenu-accepts-a-boopsi-title-object-but-never-measures-or-draws-it) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-full-body-and-object-tag-caller-pass).

**GD10434 — PopupMenu “insert before” places new items after a submenu's first child:** recursive predecessor lookup returns the target first child itself, and insertion links after that pointer. Affects `PM_Insert_Before` and `PM_Insert_BeforeID` on nested submenu heads; source-only. See [GD10434](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10434-popupmenu-insert-before-places-new-items-after-a-submenus-first-child) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-search-and-insertion-full-body-pass).


**OD10174 — CUE AIFF/WAVE reads can exceed the final partial-sector buffer:** both readers use the whole stream length instead of bytes remaining from the requested offset; rounded final CDDA sectors can consume trailing chunks, overwrite the caller buffer, and wrap zero-fill size. Optional CUE plugin; source-only. See [OD10174](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10174) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md).

**OD2167 — SB128 Stop can race playback and record soft interrupts on ExecSMP builds:** Stop frees DMA/mix buffers without synchronizing across CPUs with queued or active callbacks. Scoped to x86_64-PC ExecSMP configurations where SB128 is selected; no uniprocessor race established. See [OD2167](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2167) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sb128-execsmp-softint-stop-race-scope-pass).

**OD2168 — SB128 leaks partial playback allocations after combined-start failure:** when record-buffer allocation fails after playback allocations succeed, AHI returns without Stop rollback; a retry overwrites the only cleanup pointers. Affects combined play/record starts followed by retry before Stop/FreeAudio. See [OD2168](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2168) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sb128-combined-start-rollback-recheck).

**EK10244 — CDFS cache teardown passes the address of its request pointer to `CloseDevice`:** closing a successfully opened CDFS device supplies a pointer-field address as an `IORequest`, so Exec reads unrelated cache state as request/device fields; the separately allocated request and message port are also not destroyed. Applies to builds selecting `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10244](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10244) and the [CDFS BCache teardown pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-bcache-teardown-pass). Source-only; no close was run.


**EK10245 — CDFS decimal volume dates subtract the wrong digit base:** `ascdec()` subtracts `'9'`, so valid ASCII digits wrap through unsigned arithmetic and produce an invalid volume timestamp. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` ISO mounts. See [EK10245](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10245) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no image was mounted.

**EK10246 — CDFS indexes a sector buffer with the absolute directory offset:** after reading the correct sector, `isoReadDir()` uses the full directory offset into that 2048-byte buffer. Multi-sector directories can yield invalid entries or fault the handler. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10246](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10246) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no directory was read.

**EK10247 — CDFS omits fitting Rock Ridge names and Amiga comments:** NM and AS comment payloads are copied only when they exceed available space, leaving fitting extension data unreported. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` images using these extensions. See [EK10247](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10247) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no image was read.

**EK10248 — CDFS leaks parsed path tables on ISO unmount:** the raw path-table data and pointer array are not freed by `ISO9660_Unmount()`, so repeated mount/eject cycles can retain memory. Applies when optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` successfully parses a path table that is not discarded earlier. See [EK10248](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10248) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no media cycle was run.

**EK10249 — CDFS misadvances after ignored directory records:** lookup and enumeration can skip later visible entries in the sector; enumeration resumed with a nonzero disk key can also advance by an uninitialized record size. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10249](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10249) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no directory operation was run.

**EK10250 — CDFS accepts truncated ISO path-table records:** the parser publishes entries without validating the fixed header and padded record extents, then lookup reads extent/parent fields beyond short table data. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` with malformed path-table metadata. See [EK10250](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10250) and the [CDFS ISO9660 body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-body-pass). Source-only; no malformed image was used.

**EK10251 — CDFS leaks a temporary lock on a path from a file:** `ISO9660_Locate()` allocates its result lock, then returns `ERROR_DIR_NOT_FOUND` for a slash component on a file without freeing it. Repeated invalid locate requests can accumulate allocations. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10251](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10251) and the [CDFS ISO9660 Locate cleanup follow-up](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-iso9660-locate-cleanup-follow-up). Source-only; no packet was sent.

**GD10435 — Oversized generic software pointers can draw uninitialized ARGB pixels:** cursor bitmap dimensions are unsigned 16-bit but generic `GetImage` extents are signed 16-bit; a width of 32768 can produce no extracted pixels, after which the generic cursor still accepts and draws from the unwritten buffer. The ordinary `SetPointer()` raw-data path cannot request this size; the trigger requires the private `PointerA_BitMap` path or an external HIDD caller. See [GD10435](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10435) and the [cursor dimension-contract follow-up](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-software-cursor-dimension-contract-follow-up). Source-only; no cursor operation was run.

**OD10451 — Nouveau can write past its fixed DCB output array:** BIOS DCB iteration follows a count or table-pointer extent, but `new_dcb_entry()` appends unchecked into a 16-entry array. An over-capacity pre-Tesla PCI ROM table can overwrite subsequent BIOS state. Applies to explicit optional Nouveau PCI builds; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See [OD10451](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10451) and the [Nouveau DCB capacity follow-up](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-dcb-capacity-follow-up). Source-only; no ROM or GPU was used.

**GD10436 — PopupMenu varargs wrapper frees an indeterminate pointer after allocation failure:** on `NO_LINEAR_VARARGS` targets, `PM_ExLst()` unconditionally calls `FreeVec(values)` even when its `AllocVec()` failed before initializing `values`. Applies to explicit static PopupMenu link-library clients; no default-image inclusion or in-tree caller is claimed. See [GD10436](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10436) and the [static PopupMenu varargs wrapper pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#static-popupmenu-varargs-wrapper-full-body-and-allocation-failure-pass). Source-only; no failure or API call was run.

**GD10437 — PopupMenu's exported layout entry point does nothing:** `PM_LayoutMenuA()` is a configured vector, not a skipped slot, but its implementation ignores the arguments and returns zero. No public semantic documentation or maintained caller was found, so it remains a low-confidence API-completeness candidate, not a confirmed behavior defect. Applies to explicit PopupMenu clients using this API; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See [GD10437](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10437) and the [layout-vector contract recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-vector-contract-recheck-gd10437). Source-only; no call or build was run.

**EK10252 — Overlapping reset calls overwrite shared callback-completion state:** task-context reset calls share one waiter, signal mask, and running-handler pointer, so one chain can wake another early or demote the other chain’s handler. Applies only to selected reset vectors that call `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()`; MinGW32 is excluded. ExecSMP permits cross-CPU overlap; on one CPU a callback must yield. The supervisor-only path is excluded. See [EK10252](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10252) and the [reset-vector selection pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#reset-callback-vector-selection-pass). Source-only; no reset was run.

**GD10438 — Generic bitmap stride calculation conflicts with alignment and explicit-stride contracts:** bit-mask rounding only works for power-of-two alignment values, and the constructor rejects explicit `BytesPerRow` values smaller than the padded default even though documentation says the explicit stride overrides alignment. Checked-in driver alignment values found here are powers of two; direct use of these generic HIDD contracts remains the trigger. See [GD10438](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10438) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-bitmap-alignment-contract-follow-up). Source-only; no bitmap or build was run.

**GD10439 — Generic masked blits truncate mask rows for sub-byte alignment:** `CopyBoxMasked` rounds source width to the bitmap alignment, then truncates to bytes; width 9/alignment 4 yields a one-byte stride for a 12-pixel mask row that needs two bytes. Later rows consume neighboring-row bits and masked output is wrong. The generic HIDD contract includes aligned mask extent, while the legacy bridge passes the mask without a stride and its autodoc leaves padded rows implicit. In-tree triggering requires a sub-byte-alignment caller supplying aligned mask rows; none was found, including in the expanded Picasso96 producer census (16/32). See [GD10439](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10439) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#masked-blit-alignment-follow-up). Source-only; no blit or build was run.
**GD10440 — Clipboard MCC initialization leaks its semaphore when worker creation fails:** each NList-family/TextEditor `StartClipboardServer()` retains the semaphore allocated before a failed `CreateNewProcTags()`; generated failed `LibInit()` skips `ClassExpunge()`, so repeated failed opens leak the object. Separate from GD9697's worker-startup hang. See [GD10440](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10440) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#clipboard-worker-create-failure-pass). Source-only; no process failure was induced.


**EK10253 — CDFS trusts ISO path-table parent indices:** a complete entry with parent index zero or beyond the table count is used as an unchecked pointer-array index during lookup and `..` traversal. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` with malformed path-table metadata. See [EK10253](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10253) and the [CDFS parent-index follow-up](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-path-table-parent-index-follow-up). Source-only; no malformed image was used.


**EK10254 — CDFS can resolve a directory name from the wrong branch:** path-table name lookup scans every directory entry instead of only direct children of the current directory, so a name elsewhere in a non-Rock-Ridge ISO can satisfy a missing-child lookup. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` when a path table is retained. See [EK10254](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10254) and the [CDFS child-lookup follow-up](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-path-table-child-lookup-follow-up). Source-only; no image or locate request was run.


**EK10255 — CDFS trusts Rock Ridge record lengths:** malformed directory or extension lengths can make the parser read beyond the record and, at a sector boundary, beyond the cache buffer. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` reading malformed ISO9660/Rock Ridge metadata. See [EK10255](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10255) and the [Rock Ridge extent-validation follow-up](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-rock-ridge-extent-validation-follow-up). Source-only; no malformed image was used.


**EK10256 — CDFS does not reject negative read lengths:** after a nonzero seek, a negative `Read()` byte count can enter the copy loop and copy beyond the requested/file range. This is conditional on an invalid caller argument; no maintained caller was found. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10256](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10256) and the [negative-length caller pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-negative-read-length-follow-up). Source-only.


**EK10257 — CDFS mishandles EOF-relative seeks:** it rejects valid negative offsets from EOF and accepts some positive offsets that move beyond EOF, where later read-length clamping can underflow. Applies to optional `kernel-fs-cdfs`. See [EK10257](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10257) and the [EOF-relative seek pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-offset-end-seek-pass). Source-only; no seek or read was run.


**GD10441 — Say reports success when WAV finalization fails:** after successful synthesis, `EndWav()` ignores failure to seek back and rewrite the RIFF header and ignores `Close()` status. The command can therefore return success with stale lengths or incomplete output. Applies to the explicit `workbench-c-say` target; default inclusion is not claimed. See [GD10441](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10441) and the [Say full-body/WAV finalization pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#say-command-wav-finalization-and-full-body-pass). Source-only; no WAV or failure was exercised.


**GD10442 — Say maps intermediate text-mode cancellation to hard failure:** `FeedWords()` converts a `RETURN_WARN` from Ctrl-C during an intermediate segment flush into `RETURN_FAIL`; `FeedFile()` preserves the warning. This makes command-text cancellation report a different shell status. Applies to the explicit `workbench-c-say` target. See [GD10442](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10442) and the [Say full-body/WAV finalization pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#say-command-wav-finalization-and-full-body-pass). Source-only; no cancellation was run.


**OD10453 — DiskImage READ TOC reports the wrong last-track number after filtering:** a nonzero start track reduces the descriptor count, which the handler incorrectly writes as the disc’s last track number. Explicit DiskImage device target; source-only. See [OD10453](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10453-diskimage-read-toc-reports-the-wrong-last-track-number-after-filtering) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-scsicmd-full-body-and-toc-caller-pass).

**OD10454 — MountHDF underflows the high cylinder for images smaller than one cylinder:** with valid nonzero geometry, a nonempty image smaller than one cylinder makes the cylinder-count-minus-one expression underflow; the generated DOS node reports an all-ones `DE_HIGHCYL`, so filesystems can derive an invalid, oversized extent. Explicit x86-aros and ppc-aros MountHDF targets; source-only. See [OD10454](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10454-mounthdf-underflows-the-high-cylinder-for-images-smaller-than-one-cylinder) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-mounthdf-command-full-body-and-cylinder-boundary-pass).

**EK10258 — Hosted ELF load failures leak the open module and relocation buffer:** section-read and relocation failures return from `LoadKernel()` without closing the current module stream; rejected relocations also retain the temporary relocation block. Repeated Android pre-start retries can accumulate these resources. See [EK10258](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10258) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#hosted-elf-loader-error-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no load or retry was run.
**EK10259 — udis86 accepts register-form VSIB gather encodings:** a ModRM register form leaves the required VSIB operand empty without setting a decode error, so the PC debug disassembler reports a successful but incomplete gather instruction. Applies to the optional PC `udis86` library. See [EK10259](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10259) and the [udis86 VSIB decoder pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udis86-vsib-decoder-pass). Source-only; no decode or build was run.
**EK10260 — udis86 AT&T output omits operand-width suffixes:** the selected AT&T translator never sets the width used to print `b`/`w`/`q`, leaving some memory operations ambiguous in the i386 debugger. See [EK10260](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10260) and the [udis86 syntax backends pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udis86-syntax-backends-pass). Source-only; no disassembly or build was run.
**EK10261 — udis86 reports incorrect operand access modes:** final decode handling overwrites generated access metadata, reporting read-only for read/write operands such as the VSIB mask in `vgatherdpd`. Applies to optional PC `udis86` clients inspecting operand metadata. See [EK10261](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10261) and the [header and operand-access pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udis86-header-and-operand-access-pass). Source-only; no decode or client was run.

**EK10262 — udis86 does not validate required VSIB addressing forms:** gather operands are accepted without a SIB byte or with a 16-bit effective address, despite the selected ISA constraints; the latter can also leave the decoder at the wrong next-byte position. Applies to optional PC `udis86` and its x86 debug consumer. See [EK10262](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10262) and the [udis86 VSIB decoder pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udis86-vsib-decoder-pass). Source-only; no instruction stream or decoder was run.

**EK10263 — udcli disables access reporting after a no-operand instruction:** the per-instruction printer clears its global `-access` flag and restores it only when an operand exists; if the first instruction has none, later access metadata is omitted. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-c-pc-udcli` target. See [EK10263](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10263) and the [udcli full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udcli-full-body-pass). Source-only; no CLI or build was run.

**EK10264 — udcli does not propagate invalid input and option errors:** malformed `-x` input and invalid numeric values are diagnosed, file read errors are treated as EOF, and unknown `-v` values silently select AMD; these paths do not report failure. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-c-pc-udcli` target. See [EK10264](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10264) and the [udcli input/error-path recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#udcli-input-error-path-recheck). Source-only; no CLI or I/O error was induced.

**OD10455 — Unix hostdisk automount probes geometry through an uninitialized structure:** the Unix backend reads `dg_SectorSize` before setting it and leaves the other geometry fields untouched; automount can divide by zero or publish arbitrary drive geometry. Scoped to the resident hostdisk automount path on hosted Unix. See [OD10455](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10455-unix-hostdisk-automount-probes-geometry-through-an-uninitialized-structure) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hostdisk-automount-full-body-and-geometry-caller-pass). Source-only.

**OD10456 — Hostdisk automount copies indeterminate DOS geometry words:** `MakeDosNode()` copies unset `DE_SECORG`, `DE_PREFAC`, and `DE_INTERLEAVE` values into the published environment; filesystems can see invalid geometry or unintended options. Applies when the hosted hostdisk automount hook runs. See [OD10456](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10456-hostdisk-automount-copies-indeterminate-dos-geometry-words) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hostdisk-automount-full-body-and-geometry-caller-pass). Source-only.

**OD10457 — Hostdisk automount ignores a rejected boot node and leaks it:** a duplicate generated `HD*` DOS name makes `AddBootNode()` reject the node, but automount ignores the result and loses the allocation. Applies when DOS is already active during hostdisk automount. See [OD10457](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10457-hostdisk-automount-ignores-a-rejected-boot-node-and-leaks-it) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hostdisk-automount-full-body-and-geometry-caller-pass). Source-only.

**OD10458 — Hostdisk leaks its per-unit message port when opening the host file fails:** if the worker creates its message port but `Host_Open()` then fails, the worker exits without deleting the port and the parent frees the unit without freeing that port. Each failed open leaks the port structure and signal bit. Applies to hosted hostdisk implementations using the shared worker. See [OD10458](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10458-hostdisk-leaks-its-per-unit-message-port-when-opening-the-host-file-fails) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hostdisk-device-full-body-startup-and-request-pass). Source-only.

**OD10459 — MinGW hostdisk rejects a valid 64-bit seek when the low offset word is `0xFFFFFFFF`:** it treats `SetFilePointer()`'s ambiguous sentinel as unconditional failure without checking `GetLastError()`, so the requested I/O is skipped. Applies when a MinGW32 request has a positive high word and all-one low word. See [OD10459](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10459-mingw-hostdisk-treats-a-valid-0xffffffff-seek-position-as-an-error) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mingw-hostdisk-backend-and-unix-geometry-shim-pass). Source-only.

**OD10460 — MinGW hostdisk rejects valid image sizes whose low word is `0xFFFFFFFF`:** it treats `GetFileSize()`'s ambiguous return as failure even when `GetLastError()` reports success. Applies to image geometry in the MinGW32 hostdisk target. See [OD10460](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10460-mingw-hostdisk-rejects-valid-image-sizes-with-low-word-0xffffffff) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mingw-hostdisk-backend-and-unix-geometry-shim-pass). Source-only.

**OD10461 (withdrawn):** duplicate of [OD9898](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9898). The stale BAR/ROM export path is already covered there; no separate finding is counted.
**OD2471 — FLAC signed bitreader has undefined sign-extension shifts:** one helper defect covers undefined shifts both for negative samples narrower than 32 bits and for legal zero-width escaped residuals. It is conditional on use of the selected decoder; ordinary AHIRecord recording does not invoke that API. See [OD2471](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2471) and the [FLAC bitreader review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-record-flac-bitreader-declaration-dynamic-width-reconciliation). OD2863 is withdrawn as a duplicate. Source-only.

**OD10462 — DiskImage AbortIO can deadlock when a synchronous `PA_CALL` callback submits same-unit `DoIO`:** AbortIO replies while holding the unit semaphore; a reentrant synchronous request waits for the worker, which needs that semaphore to dequeue it. Conditional on an AROS `PA_CALL` client using this sequence in an explicitly selected DiskImage build. See [OD10462](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10462-diskimage-abortio-callback-can-deadlock-synchronous-io-on-the-same-unit) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-beginio-abortio-queue-and-completion-pass). Source-only; no callback or request was run.
**OD10463 (withdrawn):** duplicate of [OD10430](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10430-diskimage-extraction-overwrites-a-predictable-temporary-file-collision), which already covers the shared `CreateTempFile()` collision, truncating open, and cleanup deletion across DMS, XAD, and XPK. The XAD/XPK initialization and tempfile source-body coverage remains credited in the [coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-temporary-file-ownership-and-initialization-pass).

**OD10464 — DiskImage Zune GUI retains one leading space in the custom window title:** with exactly one leading whitespace character in a nonempty `CX_POPKEY`, `TrimStr()` does not shift the string, so the Zune title includes the extra space. Reaction’s Commodities hotkey caller is not selected by the x86-aros/ppc-aros targets; overlapping `strcpy` behavior is not retained as an active defect. See [OD10464](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10464-diskimage-zune-gui-retains-one-leading-space-in-the-custom-window-title) and the [caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-trimstr-selected-zune-caller-recheck). Source-only.

**OD10465 — MountHDF accepts a nonnumeric `UNIT` tooltype as unit zero:** `TTInteger()`/`atol()` turn a no-digit value into zero, bypassing MountHDF’s missing-unit check and targeting unit 0. See [OD10465](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10465-mounthdf-accepts-a-nonnumeric-unit-tooltype-as-unit-zero) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-tooltype-helper-full-body-and-caller-pass). Source-only; no icon or device was used.


**OD10467 (withdrawn):** duplicate of [OD10429](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10429-cue-cdda-byte-swapping-uses-unaligned-word-accesses-on-powerpc), which already covers the same CUE Motorola-track buffer passed to `swab2()` and the PPC alignment condition. The `swab2.c` full-body credit remains in the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-swab2-alignment-and-cue-caller-pass).


**OD10469 — DiskImage persists an uninitialized path when NameFromFH fails:** `InsertDisk()` ignores path lookup failure, then successful image insertion persists an uninitialized stack buffer as a string. See [OD10469](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10469-diskimage-persists-an-uninitialized-path-when-namefromfh-fails) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-unit-worker-full-body-and-tag-caller-pass). Source-only.

**OD10470 — CISO block-index allocation size can wrap:** an oversized CISO block count wraps the 32-bit index-table byte size, then image-open initialization iterates the original count and writes past the undersized allocation. Applies to optional CISO plugin builds. See [OD10470](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10470-ciso-block-index-allocation-size-can-wrap) and the [coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-ciso-index-table-overflow-pass). Source-only; no image or plugin was run.

**OD10471 — DAA chunks crossing volume boundaries reuse the wrong file offset:** a compressed chunk split across DAA volumes seeks the continuation at the first volume’s offset, so reads fail or feed the wrong bytes to decompression. Applies to optional multi-volume DAA plugin builds. See [OD10471](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10471-daa-chunks-crossing-volume-boundaries-reuse-the-wrong-file-offset) and the [coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-daa-multivolume-read-pass). Source-only; no image or plugin was run.

**OD10472 — IPF and DAX reads ignore the high half of 64-bit offsets:** the legacy m68k IPF plugin and optional DAX plugin map 64-bit read requests using only the low offset word, so an out-of-range high offset can return data from a low sector. Not claimed for the default AROS package. See [OD10472](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10472-ipf-reads-ignore-the-high-half-of-64-bit-offsets) and the [cross-plugin caller review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-ipf-dax-64bit-offset-recheck-od10472). Source-only; no device or image was used.
**OD10473 — eGalax GUI uses an invalid signal mask when tracking-signal allocation fails:** if `AllocSignal(-1)` returns `-1`, the GUI and input worker shift by a negative count, so tracking notifications use an undefined mask. Applies to the explicitly built optional eGalax USB class. See [OD10473](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10473-egalaxtouch-gui-shifts-by-an-invalid-signal-index-when-signal-allocation-fails) and the [coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#egalaxtouch-full-body-and-tracking-signal-pass). Source-only; no GUI or signal exhaustion was induced.

**OD10474 — LAN78xx aliases the LAN7500 RX and TX FIFO end registers:** initialization writes both FIFO boundaries to register `0x098`, so the TX write overwrites the RX boundary and never reaches the TX register at `0x09C`. Applies to the selected LAN78xx class on LAN7500/7505 devices; exact hardware impact is conditional. See [OD10474](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10474-lan78xx-aliases-the-lan7500-rx-and-tx-fifo-end-registers) and the [coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#lan78xx-register-map-and-fifo-end-pass). Source-only; no hardware was used.

**GD10443 — Mesa compatibility allocator returns undersized blocks on size overflow:** unchecked `size_t` multiplication/header addition can wrap before `AllocMem()`, returning a small non-NULL block for an unrepresentable request. Applies to graphics targets selecting `emul_arosc.c`. See [GD10443](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10443) and the [coverage review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-emulation-allocator-and-time-fallback-pass). Source-only; no allocation was run.

**GD10444 — Mesa gettimeofday fallback reports success when it did not set the time:** allocation or timer-device open failure leaves the output untouched but returns success. Applies to graphics targets selecting `emul_arosc.c`; no direct in-tree caller was found. See [GD10444](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10444) and the [coverage review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-emulation-allocator-and-time-fallback-pass). Source-only; no timer call was run.

**GD10445 — HostGL TLS allocation failures are dereferenced:** allocation failure for the shared TLS object or a per-task TLS node reaches an unchecked NULL dereference in the hosted X11 GL context manager. Applies to the optional hosted `hostgl` library. See [GD10445](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10445) and the [coverage review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-tls-allocation-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.


**OD10475 — Nouveau VBIOS indirect-register INIT opcode targets the BIOS offset:** full interpreter and selected devinit POST caller pass added; optional Nouveau script containing opcode `0x5a` writes the BIOS source offset instead of the decoded destination register. See [OD10475](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10475) and the [Nouveau BIOS INIT interpreter pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-bios-init-interpreter-full-body-pass). Other Drivers advances to 1,993/2,017 paths (98.8%) and 936,245/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.3%); subsystem review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS, GPU, register write, or build was used.


**Nouveau NVKM DCB parser pass (no new finding):** reviewed the selected DCB table decoder and its I²C, GPIO, connector, extdev, MXM, and display consumers. OD10451 remains scoped to the separate legacy fixed-array parser. Other Drivers advances to 1,994/2,017 paths (98.9%) and 936,421/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.3%); review remains open. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvkm-dcb-table-full-body-pass). Source-only; no BIOS or hardware behavior was exercised.


**OD10476 — GT215 RAM-map record length check is one byte short:** version 0x10 parsing reads through byte 9, but the selected GT215 RAM caller accepts a nine-byte stride and can program the next record’s byte into `0x10f804`. Scoped to explicit GT215/GT216/GT218 Nouveau builds with the stated BIOS table. See [OD10476](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10476) and the [RAM-map decoder pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-rammap-decoder-full-body-pass). Other Drivers advances to 1,996/2,017 paths (99.0%) and 936,660/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.3%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10477 — Nouveau short performance rows can supply a clock state from adjacent BIOS bytes:** version 0x25 decoding reads the memory-frequency field without checking the row length, and the clock state accepts the parsed value. Scoped to optional Nouveau consumers of short version 0x25 records. See [OD10477](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10477) and the [performance parser pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-performance-table-parser-full-body-pass). Other Drivers advances to 1,997/2,017 paths (99.0%) and 936,842/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**Nouveau RAM timing parser pass (no new finding):** reviewed the selected timing-table decoder and GT215/NV50/GK104/GF100 consumers. Their accepted record lengths cover the fields used by each parser branch; short decoded rows are rejected before RAM configuration use. Other Drivers advances to 1,998/2,017 paths (99.1%) and 936,983/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-memory-timing-table-full-body-pass). Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**Nouveau RAM strap mapping pass (no new finding):** reviewed the selected BIT-M translation and M0203 strap/group helpers and traced them through BIOS INIT and RAM backends. Selected RAM consumers validate returned indices against the table counts before indexing. Other Drivers advances to 2,000/2,017 paths (99.2%) and 937,123/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-ramcfg-strap-mapping-full-body-pass). Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10478 — Nouveau boost records can be decoded past their declared lengths:** the selected parser reads six-byte main and per-domain records without validating each declared stride, then the clock path uses the decoded bounds and percentages. Scoped to optional Nouveau consumers of short version 0x11 records. See [OD10478](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10478) and the [boost-table parser pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-boost-table-parser-full-body-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,001/2,017 paths (99.2%) and 937,217/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10479 — Nouveau CSTEP rows can be decoded past their declared lengths:** version 0x10 main entries and nested steps have fixed four- and five-byte reads without corresponding length checks; selected clock code uses the resulting C-state index, frequency and voltage. Scoped to optional Nouveau consumers of short CSTEP rows. See [OD10479](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10479) and the [CSTEP parser pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-cstep-parser-full-body-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,002/2,017 paths (99.3%) and 937,307/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10480 — Nouveau VPSTATE lookup can use a row past the table:** the version 0x10 parser accepts index `ecount`, although that is the first row after the table; clock initialization can install its adjacent BIOS bytes as base/boost thresholds. Scoped to optional Nouveau with a VPSTATE 1.0 BIOS ID equal to the entry count. See [OD10480](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10480) and the [VPSTATE parser pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-vpstate-parser-full-body-and-clock-constructor-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,003/2,017 paths (99.3%) and 937,362/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10481 — Nouveau M0205 can read a RAM training clock past a short BIOS header:** the v1.0 parser reads the frequency at bytes 6–7 without verifying the declared header covers them; selected GT215 RAM training uses a nonzero value as its target clock. Scoped to GT215-family RAM training with `NvMemExec` and a short M0205 header. See [OD10481](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10481) and the [M0205 parser pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-m0205-nested-ram-training-table-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,004/2,017 paths (99.4%) and 937,465/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10482 — Nouveau M0209 training data can divide by zero:** a BIOS `modulo` value is used directly as the divisor while unpacking RAM-training words; the selected GK104 caller reaches the decoder for matching training metadata. Scoped to GK104-family RAM initialization with `modulo == 0`. See [OD10482](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10482) and the [M0209 decoder pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-m0209-training-data-decoder-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,005/2,017 paths (99.4%) and 937,569/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10483 — Nouveau BIOS image scan can stall on a zero-sized image:** a non-final, non-0x70 image with decoded size zero leaves BIOS image traversal on the same image; shadow-source recursion can exhaust the stack, and for non-0xe0 image types the constructor index scan also cannot progress. Zero size can come from PCIR fallback or accepted NPDE data. See [OD10483](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10483), the [NPDE enumeration pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-npde-image-size-parser-and-enumeration-pass), and the [PCIR caller pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-pcir-table-parser-and-image-chain-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,007/2,017 paths (99.5%) and 937,680/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%) at the initial finding entry; review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10484 — Nouveau BIOS address validation can overflow:** the shared accessor checks `addr + width` in 32-bit arithmetic, so an extreme BIOS pointer can wrap past the bounds test before indexing the BIOS buffer. Scoped to selected Nouveau readers of 32-bit BIOS offsets; VPSTATE provides a concrete path. See [OD10484](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10484) and the [BIOS address accessor pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-bios-address-accessor-and-pointer-caller-pass). Other Drivers advances to 2,009/2,017 paths (99.6%) and 937,893/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.4%); review remains open. Source-only; no BIOS or hardware was used.


**OD10485 — Rejected explicit Nouveau BIOS sources leak their candidate buffers:** a score-zero explicitly selected built-in source loses its copied image when fallback retries and overwrites the data pointer; a failed custom-firmware source is lost when its sentinel slot is excluded from cleanup. Scoped to optional Nouveau NvBios selection that loads an image, scores zero, and falls back. See [OD10485](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10485) and the [BIOS source ownership pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-bios-source-scoring-and-ownership-pass). Other Drivers stands at 2,016/2,017 paths (99.95%) and 938,501/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.5%); review remains open. Source-only; no firmware or hardware was used.

**OD10486 — Nouveau clock cleanup can hide a failed core-clock transition:** a successful voltage or fan cleanup overwrites a failed core-clock `calc()`/`prog()` result; the worker reports success although the requested P-state was cached before programming. Scoped to optional Nouveau clocks with attached voltage/thermal cleanup and a core-clock failure. See [OD10486](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10486) and the [shared clock base pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-clock-base-full-body-and-transition-error-pass). This adds 571 code lines and advances the Other Drivers body-credit checkpoint to 2,017/2,017 paths and 939,072/1,259,999 C/header lines (74.5%); caller/configuration review remains open. Source-only; no failure injection or hardware operation.


**EK10265 — m68k `ExamineFH()` leaves the guest FileInfoBlock stale:** the generated thunk mutates a native FIB shadow but does not copy successful examination results back to guest memory. Scoped to the optional 64-bit hosted m68kemu bridge when using `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)`. See [EK10265](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10265) and the [ExamineFH shadow-output recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#generated-dos-examinefh-shadow-output-pass). Source-only; no guest call or build was run.

**EK9432 rechecked — DOS and Commodities guest/native boundary cases expanded:** the generated `SetFileDate()` path passes a guest-endian DateStamp into native packet handlers, and `ErrorReport()` forwards overloaded `arg1` values without translating guest volume records or strings. The generated Commodities `CxBroker()` thunk also lets native code write nonzero `CBERR_*` values directly into big-endian guest storage on selected little-endian hosts. These are conditional on the optional 64-bit hosted m68kemu bridge and remain instances of EK9432's shared marshalling boundary; see [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432), the [DOS thunk recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#generated-dos-examinefh-shadow-output-pass), and the [CxBroker output recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cxbroker-error-scalar-output-ek9432). No guest call or requester was run; source-only.

**EK9203 rechecked — `GetSegListInfo()` output width:** its generated DOS thunk converts output-tag storage to guest backing memory, while native DOS writes an 8-byte `IPTR` into the guest's 4-byte slot. The overwrite requires a guest-visible BPTR matching a DOS-tracked segment; no in-tree emulator caller establishes that route. See [EK9203](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9203) and the [DOS segment-info body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dos-segment-info-assign-list-full-body-pass). The full `GetSegListInfo()` and `AssignAddToList()` bodies are now credited; no DOS operation or build was run.

**EK10266 — `AssignLate()` and `AssignPath()` read one byte past the path string:** both include an extra byte beyond the NUL in their `CopyMem()` length; a terminator at the end of a readable mapping can make the read fault. The copied byte is after the stored NUL, so no ordinary path corruption is claimed. See [EK10266](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10266) and the [assign helper full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#assign-helpers-full-body-and-caller-pass). Source-only; no boundary access or build was run.

**GD10444 extended to optional EGL:** the EGL module compiles a duplicate `gettimeofday()` fallback that also returns success without writing `timeval` when request/port allocation or timer-device open fails. No direct caller is established because the configured Mesa EGL core sources are absent here. The local EGL support files are reviewed; imported core coverage remains open. See [GD10444](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10444) and the [EGL local-support pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#egl-local-support-full-body-pass). Source-only; no EGL or timer operation was run.

**GD10446 — GL override removal leaves a freed library name installed:** after a notified removal of `ENV:SYS/GL` with no ENVARC fallback, `GetGLVar()` leaves the freed implementation string in `glb_GLImpl`; the next `LibOpen()` passes it to `OpenLibrary()`. Optional GL library target; source-only. See [GD10446](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10446) and the [GL coverage pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gl-pass-through-library-full-body-and-notification-setup-gd14813).

**GD10447 — GL library passes a missing implementation name to `OpenLibrary()`:** opening the optional pass-through library with no implementation configured forwards NULL into library-name lookup instead of failing cleanly. See [GD10447](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10447) and the [GL configuration review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gl-pass-through-library-full-body-and-notification-setup-gd14813). Source-only.

**GD10448 — CursorFB direct access bypasses the software-cursor bracket:** direct framebuffer locking returns a pixel address without hiding the software pointer or taking its cursor semaphore; writes under the visible cursor can overwrite it and later cursor removal can overwrite the client update. No in-tree active-framebuffer caller was established. See [GD10448](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10448) and the [CursorFB direct-access review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cursorfb-direct-access-cursor-lifetime-pass). Source-only.

**EK10267 — Moira watchpoints miss byte accesses at `0xffffffff`:** the watchpoint range's exclusive end wraps to zero, so the guard does not match and the callback is skipped. This is in the optional m68kemu target; no maintained AROS watchpoint caller is established. See [EK10267](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10267) and the [watchpoint boundary pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-watchpoint-boundary-pass). Source-only.

**EK10268 — M68040 STOP raises a spurious privilege exception when the immediate clears S:** after checking the pre-instruction supervisor bit, Moira loads the immediate SR and sets STOPPED, but its next loop iteration raises vector 8 if the new S bit is clear. With no eligible interrupt, STOP should remain stopped in user state; the erroneous frame saves the changed SR and points at the immediate word. Optional m68kemu M68040 path. See [EK10268](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10268) and the [STOP state-transition recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-stop-state-transition-recheck-ek10268). Source-only.

**EK10269 — security.library rollback uses uninitialized task tracking after early init failure:** failed INITLIB setup runs cleanup before the task tracking hook, semaphore, and lists are initialized; pool-creation failure can make cleanup remove a never-linked hook. The selected boot order normally initializes `task.resource` first; a missing-resource trigger requires its init to fail or security.library to be initialized outside that cold-start order. Applies to the selected x86-64 PC and RISC-V OpenSBI packages when security.library's initial pool allocation fails. See [EK10269](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10269) and the [security library initialization pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-library-initialization-and-rollback-pass-ek10269). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**EK10270 — C:Partition reports success after table-write errors:** all three `WritePartitionTable()` results are ignored, so the optional command can return success after failed or partial table updates. See [EK10270](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10270).

**EK10271 — C:Partition leaks successful ReadArgs allocations:** its `FreeArguments()` wrapper is never called, so repeated runs in one Shell process retain each parsed argument block. See [EK10271](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10271).

**EK10272 — C:Partition treats unknown SCHEME values as MBR:** unsupported values silently fall back to MBR/EBR and can write a different layout than requested. See [EK10272](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10272).

**EK10273 — C:Partition silently skips unsupported BOOTTYPE values:** only `fat32` creates the requested boot partition; other paired values fall through and can still report success after writing the remaining layout. See [EK10273](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10273).

**EK10274 — security.library logout can fail to restore the saved owner:** if cloning the saved owner fails, `PopOwner()` discards the saved snapshot but reports success, leaving the current effective owner installed while restoring only some UID/GID fields. The selected `Logout` command then reports that owner as the restored identity. Conditional on allocation failure during logout with a saved non-NULL owner. See [EK10274](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10274) and the [security task-owner restore pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-task-owner-restore-failure-pass-ek10274). Source-only; no login/logout or allocation failure was run.

**EK10275 — security.library global logout skips grandchildren:** global login pushes saved credentials recursively, but logout restores only the selected task and its direct children. In a task tree at least two levels deep, grandchildren remain under the globally applied owner after `Logout GLOBAL`. See [EK10275](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10275) and the [global owner-stack restore pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-global-owner-stack-restore-pass-ek10275). Source-only; no task tree or login/logout was run.

**EK10276 — security.library can apply a login after failing to save the prior owner:** `ApplyOwner()` ignores `PushOwner()` failure, so login can report success without a saved credential snapshot; later logout cannot restore the prior owner. With `GLOBAL`, this can affect only part of the task tree. Conditional on snapshot allocation failure followed by successful application of the new owner. See [EK10276](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10276) and the [owner-stack allocation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-owner-stack-allocation-pass-ek10276). Source-only; no login/logout or allocation failure was run.

**EK10277 — security.library can report login success without changing the owner:** `ApplyOwner()` ignores `SetNodeOwner()` failure; `secLoginA()` then returns the task’s existing non-nobody owner, which the `Login` command treats as success. The `PARENT` path can similarly report success when applying the caller’s owner fails. Conditional on owner-clone allocation failure and a previously non-nobody task. See [EK10277](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10277) and the [owner-application failure pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-owner-application-failure-pass-ek10277). Source-only; no login or allocation failure was run.

**EK10278 — security.library remains active after its login server fails to start:** after-DOS initialization sets its ready flag before server startup and ignores failure, while DOS considers the library active from resident presence alone. A configured security boot can then enter a login loop that has no server to authenticate requests. See [EK10278](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10278) and the [Security.library after-DOS server startup pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-library-after-dos-server-startup-pass-ek10278). Source-only; no startup failure or boot was induced.

**EK10279 — security plug-in context sizes can wrap into undersized allocations:** `secContextLocate()` and its allocator add context/header sizes without checking whether the total fits the `ULONG` allocation limit. A sufficiently large plug-in context request can return a smaller block than the API promises. See [EK10279](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10279) and the [security plug-in source pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-plugin-memory-and-context-pass-ek10279-ek10281). Source-only; no plug-in or allocation was run.

**EK10280 — security plug-in header search reads beyond short loaded segments:** the loader scans a fixed 4 KB in every segment even though the HUNK loader allocates each according to its encoded size. A short candidate segment without a header can be read past its allocation during rejection. See [EK10280](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10280) and the [security plug-in source pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-plugin-memory-and-context-pass-ek10279-ek10281). Source-only; no plug-in was loaded.

**EK10281 — unloading an encryption plug-in races in-flight callbacks:** crypto code reads the callback table and pins the module in separate unsynchronized steps, while unload checks its reference count after releasing the module semaphore. A root-authorized unload can overlap password operations and unload code while a callback is starting. See [EK10281](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10281) and the [security plug-in source pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-plugin-memory-and-context-pass-ek10279-ek10281). Source-only; no plugin or concurrent unload was run.

**EK10282 — DOS continues setuid execution when owner setup fails:** load, command, and process creation paths ignore failed setuid metadata/owner setup and continue with the caller's owner. Conditional on a setuid executable and an allocation failure. See [EK10282](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10282) and the [security DOS hooks pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-dos-setuid-hooks-pass-ek10282-ek10283). Source-only; no allocation failure or setuid execution was run.

**EK10283 — SMP CreateNewProc can run a setuid child before assigning its owner:** the child is published as ready before the creator calls the owner setter, and ExecSMP `Forbid()` blocks scheduling only on the current processor. Another CPU can start the child in that interval. See [EK10283](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10283) and the [security DOS hooks pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-dos-setuid-hooks-pass-ek10282-ek10283). Source-only; no process or SMP schedule was run.

**EK10284 — Aborted console password check leaves partial input in its stack buffer:** if console input ends or is interrupted after partial entry, `secCheckPasswdA()` returns before clearing its password buffer. The residual bytes remain in the caller's stack storage until overwritten. See [EK10284](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10284) and the [password-check vector pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-password-check-vector-full-body-and-server-call-pass). Source-only; no password input was run.

**EK10285 — DOS protection limit is bypassed if existing protection cannot be read:** `secLimitProtection()` returns the requested bits unchanged after a lock, FIB allocation, or Examine failure, and DOS continues to issue `ACTION_SET_PROTECT`. Conditional on the later DOS operation succeeding, a non-root caller can change GROUP/OTHER or set-ID bits while the limit is enabled. See [EK10285](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10285) and the [protection-limit hook review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-limit-protection-hook-full-body-pass-ek10285). Source-only; no failure or protection change was induced.

**EK10286 — Failed password persistence can truncate the password database:** the server changes the in-memory hash, then rewrites the live file with `MODE_NEWFILE`; a post-open write/close failure can leave the database partial, with no rollback. See [EK10286](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10286) and the [password API and persistence pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#security-password-api-and-database-persistence-pass-ek10286). Source-only; no file or I/O failure was induced.

**[EK9418](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9418) — Experimental CEBoot exits with status 0 when its fixed boot-information arena fills.** The kernel is not handed off, but the launcher sees success. See the [arena trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6073). Source-only; no boot was run.
