**OD10525 — IntelGMA i915 maps a NULL vertex buffer after allocation failure:** the selected AROS winsys returns NULL on allocation failure, but the vbuf renderer maps it before checking. Conditional on the optional `DBG_VBUF` path. See [OD10525](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10525) and the [i915 primitive-vbuf review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or draw was run.
**OD10526 — IntelGMA i915 dereferences a failed vbuf-render allocation:** the optional `DBG_VBUF` context path initializes the newly allocated renderer without a NULL check. See [OD10526](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10526) and the [i915 primitive-vbuf review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or context creation was run.





**GD10466 — V3D can keep a framebuffer page as its render target after scanout detach allocation fails:** the detach helper clears scanout bookkeeping even when its private replacement BO allocation fails, so later windowed rendering can continue through the framebuffer-backed resource. Applies to the optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 V3D Gallium target; default-image inclusion is not claimed. See [GD10466](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10466-v3d-can-keep-a-framebuffer-page-as-its-render-target-after-scanout-detach-allocation-fails) and the [targeted presentation-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-scanout-detach-allocation-failure-gd10466). Source-only; no allocation failure or GPU operation was run.

**GD10467 — V3D can display a render job discarded by timeout recovery:** the sequence wait ignores its failure result, and overlay presentation continues after recovery has dropped the queued job. The queued BO can be shown with stale or incomplete pixels. Applies to the optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 V3D Gallium target; default-image inclusion is not claimed. See [GD10467](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10467-v3d-can-present-a-frame-discarded-by-timeout-recovery) and the [timeout/recovery caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-wait-recovery-overlay-result-gd10467). Source-only; no GPU timeout or display was induced.

**EK10299 — Moira bit-field width calculation overflows signed `int`:** a valid register-width operand with its high bit set can become `INT_MIN`, then overflow on subtraction before modulo-32 width handling. Results depend on compiler/optimization. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` builds, not default ROM inclusion. See [EK10299](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10299) and the [bit-field arithmetic pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-register-width-bit-field-signed-overflow-ek10299). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.


**EK10300 — Moira executes MOVES with nonzero reserved extension bits:** the selected handler ignores the extension's zero-required low eleven bits and performs the transfer instead of taking an illegal-instruction exception. Conditional on malformed MOVES encodings in an explicit M68040 `m68kemu.library` build. See [EK10300](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10300) and the [MOVES extension validation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-moves-reserved-extension-validation-ek10300). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.

**EK10302 — CHRP Exec bootstrap cannot preprocess its `InitETask` call:** the architecture override passes three arguments to the only checked-in two-argument macro, so explicit CHRP PPC `kernel-exec` builds fail before link. Default Efika image inclusion is not claimed. See [EK10302](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10302) and the [CHRP macro-arity pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#chrp-exec-bootstrap-source-and-macro-arity-pass-ek10302-and-ek8842-reconciled-no-pathloc-credit-2026-10-31). Source-only; no build was run.

**EK8842 — CHRP Exec continues after required allocation failures:** several bootstrap allocations only log failure before null dereferences or publication, risking early boot failure under memory exhaustion. It is conditional on the CHRP override being made buildable; no default-image claim. See [EK8842](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8842) and the [CHRP allocation-failure review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#chrp-exec-bootstrap-source-and-macro-arity-pass-ek10302-and-ek8842-reconciled-no-pathloc-credit-2026-10-31). Source-only; no allocation failure or boot was run.


**GD10468 — V3D job state is not serialized against interrupts in ExecSMP:** the optional AArch64 RasPi driver registers GIC SPI 74, which BCM2711 targets at CPU 0, while SMP tasks without affinity can run on any CPU; local interrupt disabling and the task-side semaphore do not serialize the IRQ handler against task service on another core. Limited to an explicit `raspi-aarch64` `smp` build of the optional V3D HIDD; default UP and default-image inclusion are not claimed. See [GD10468](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10468-v3d-job-state-is-not-serialized-against-interrupts-in-execsmp) and the [IRQ-route confirmation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-smp-irq-route-confirmation-for-gd10468). Source-only; no IRQ interleaving or build was run.


**OD3228 — USB Audio capture reuses one buffer for multiple in-flight isochronous IN requests:** xHCI, OHCI and UHCI can have two input transfers targeting the same recording buffer, so a later packet may replace an earlier packet before its completion callback consumes it. EHCI is excluded because it calls the completion hook before scheduling the next one-packet request. The USB Audio class is optional; default RasPi package inclusion is not claimed. See [OD3228](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3228) and the [host-controller callback reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-audio-capture-buffer-overlap-build-graph-and-host-controller-reconciliation-od3228-retained-2026-10-31-no-new-finding-or-pathloc-credit). Source-only; no device or transfer was exercised.

**OD4300 reachability recheck:** the legacy m68k `CAMDDriver.c` array also stores `Flags=0` in its `MDEV` record; AROS CAMD would reject it through the same format gate if that branch were packaged. The class manifest has no m68k CPU alias, so the affected selected targets remain the declared i386, x86_64, ARM, AArch64 and PPC variants. See [OD4300](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4300) and the [embedded-driver loader reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-midi-embedded-camd-bridge-loaderbuild-gate-reconciliation-od4300od4301od4459-rechecked-2026-10-31-no-new-od-or-loc-credit). Static source only; no binary was loaded or build performed.

**OD3521 — OpenSBI PCIDT can report success after allocating fewer MSI vectors than requested:** the backend always programs one vector and ignores the requested minimum. Checked-in callers request one vector; the defect is conditional on a future or external PCIDT client requiring more. See [OD3521](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3521) and the [PCIDT contract and caller census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#opensbi-pcidt-vector-contract-and-caller-census-refresh-od3521-retained-conditionally-2026-10-31-no-new-finding-or-fileloc-credit). Source-only; no vector request or interrupt was run.

**OD1409 — OpenSBI PCIDT leaks its MSI target page when virtual IRQ allocation fails:** the FDT DesignWare path allocates a target page and programs the bridge before reserving software vectors; if every reservation size fails, it clears `msiReady` but loses the page. The selected endpoint method then refuses vector acquisition, so no current endpoint fanout is established on that path. Conditional on virtual-range exhaustion; source-only.

**OD1411 — OpenSBI PCIDT advertises MSI after kernel controller registration fails:** the kernel supports four MSI controller records, but PCIDT accepts up to eight bridges and ignores `KrnModifyIRQA()` failure. A fifth distinct FDT MSI bridge can still configure endpoints and report vector acquisition success without an interrupt fanout. Conditional on the bridge topology; source-only.

**OD1412 — OpenSBI PCIDT can assign the same MSI vector to concurrent clients:** the free-bit scan and bitmap update are not serialized across endpoints on one bridge, so interleaved direct requests can select the same vector. Conditional on concurrent direct clients; source-only.

**OD10527 — OpenSBI PCIDT can report successful initialization after a bridge registration fails:** its init loop uses the legacy PCI registration method, which discards generic `HW_AddDriver()`'s NULL failure result. A failed bridge may therefore be absent from PCI enumeration, and successful later registrations can repeat an earlier bridge. Conditional on allocation or setup failure during RISC-V OpenSBI PCIDT startup. See [OD10527](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10527--opensbi-pcidt-reports-initialization-success-when-a-bridge-driver-was-not-registered) and the [bridge-registration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#opensbi-pcidt-bridge-driver-registration-failure-trace-od10527-added-2026-10-31-no-pathloc-credit). No boot or registration failure was induced.

**OD10528 — PCI enumeration silently omits devices whose HIDD object construction fails:** `InsertDevice()` returns NULL, but `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver()` ignores the result and reports setup success. On PCIDT, the constructor masks endpoint interrupts before the failed superclass construction. Conditional on selected device-object construction failure during PCI scanning. See [OD10528](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10528--pci-bus-setup-succeeds-after-a-discovered-device-object-failed-to-construct) and the [PCI device-construction failure pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pci-bus-device-construction-failure-od10528). No allocation failure or enumeration was induced.
**LDDemon Open serialization review correction (2026-10-31):** OD9568, OD9923, OD9931 and OD9965 are withdrawn because their triggers require concurrent same-name public `OpenDevice()` callbacks, which LDDemon serializes through each device's Open vector. OD3115 is narrowed to Open overlapping final Close, because the `CloseDevice()` wrapper does not take the per-name semaphore. See the [corrected findings](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3115) and [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md).

**GD10469 — ChangeLayerShape ignores custom-shape intersection failure:** if region allocation fails during `AndRegionRegion()`, the rectangular destination survives, and the update proceeds with a bound broader than the requested custom shape. See [GD10469](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10469-changelayershape-ignores-custom-shape-intersection-failure) and the [intersection failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changelayershape-custom-intersection-failure-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or shape update was induced.


**GD10470 — Palette Preferences cannot restore a client-installed very large color map through LoadRGB4:** its unsigned `ColorMap->Count` snapshot narrows to signed `WORD`; 32,768 entries become a nonpositive count and `LoadRGB4()` skips restoration on affected targets. `SA_ColorMapEntries` cannot produce this size because OpenScreen narrows it to signed `WORD`; the scoped trigger requires a client-installed map returned by `GetColorMap()`. See [GD10470](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10470-palette-preferences-cannot-restore-very-large-color-maps-through-loadrgb4) and the [caller and count-type trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-large-colormap-restore-recheck). Source-only; no screen or palette update was run.
**GD10472 — OpenScreen reduces large `SA_ColorMapEntries` requests to 32 entries:** the tag is stored in signed `WORD numcolors`; on affected targets, 32,768 becomes negative and the minimum-size expression selects 32. No checked-in caller was found; the trigger is external-client use, and the undocumented maximum keeps reachability confidence medium. See [GD10472](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10472-openscreen-reduces-large-sa_colormapentries-requests-to-32-entries) and the [tag-to-ColorMap trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#openscreen-large-colormap-tag-narrowing-gd10472). Source-only; no screen was opened.


**OD3298 — keyboard.device clears a freed open-unit flag after replying the final queued read:** on ExecSMP, the reply owner can consume the message and close the unit before `kbdSendQueuedEvents()` clears `KBUF_PENDING` through the replied request. See [OD3298](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3298) and the [keyboard handler lifetime recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#keyboard-final-queued-read-unit-lifetime-od3298-recheck). Source-only; no request or device was used.


**OD2389 — keyboard.device can leave a read queued after publishing its event:** on ExecSMP, a key callback can publish an event and skip draining the queue just before BeginIO inserts its pending request, leaving input blocked until another key arrives. See [OD2389](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2389) and the [empty-check/enqueue recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#keyboard-pending-read-empty-check-enqueue-race-od2389-recheck). Source-only; no event or interleaving was run.

**OD10529 — VMware's in-process DRM shim rejects property-blob create/destroy requests:** the core handlers exist, but the selected `drmIoctl()` switch omits both ioctl cases, so callers receive `-EINVAL`. Scoped to optional VMware DRM builds and callers using this shim; no in-tree call was found. See [OD10529](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10529--vmwares-in-process-drm-ioctl-shim-cannot-create-or-destroy-property-blobs) and the [full property-core review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vmware-drm-property-core-full-body-and-ioctl-dispatch-pass-od10529-2026-10-31). Source-only; no ioctl or build was run.
**OD10530 — DiskImage Zune device-type dialog uses a freed drive entry after a disk-change refresh:** the modal handler retains a `DriveEntry *`; its disk-change wait path refreshes the List, whose destruct hook frees that entry, and the confirm hook later dereferences it. Conditional on a disk-change notification while the dialog is open and then confirming. Scoped to the explicitly buildable optional DiskImageGUI target. See [OD10530](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10530--diskimage-zune-device-type-dialog-uses-a-freed-drive-entry-after-a-disk-change-refresh) and the [drive-list lifetime pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-zune-drive-list-lifetime-pass-od10530). Source-only; no device or GUI sequence was run.
**OD10531 — DiskImage Zune list refresh leaks entries when MUI insertion fails:** drive and plugin row allocations are treated as transferred even when MUI list growth fails; unadopted records (and drive strings) are left in the GUI pool. Conditional on internal List allocation failure during refresh. Scoped to the optional DiskImageGUI target. See [OD10531](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10531--diskimage-zune-list-refresh-leaks-entries-when-mui-insertion-fails) and the [list insertion failure pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-zune-list-insertion-failure-pass-od10531). Source-only; no allocation failure or GUI refresh was run.

**EK10304 — Moira's separate-model disassembler treats valid M68030 coprocessor instructions as illegal:** while `setModel(cpuModel, dasmModel)` builds the opcode table using `dasmModel`, CPI handler registration checks `cpuModel`; with an M68000 core and M68030 disassembler, `cpGEN` stays on the illegal handler and reports a two-byte instruction. Scoped to optional Moira C++ consumers of the documented two-model API; no in-tree caller uses that overload. See [EK10304](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10304-moira-disassembler-uses-cpu-cpi-model) and the [model-selection trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-disassembler-cpi-model-selection-ek10304). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.

**EK9432 rechecked — DOS list, LocalVar and path helper pointer results:** generated `LockDosList`/`AttemptLockDosList`, `FindDosEntry`/`NextDosEntry`, `FindVar`, `FilePart`, and `PathPart` return native pointers without guest-address/shadow translation. Added these optional m68kemu DOS instances to the existing guest/native boundary finding; see [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [generated DOS thunk coverage notes](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest call or build was run.

**EK9432 rechecked — generated Exec list primitives:** m68kemu's `Insert`/`AddHead`/`AddTail`/`Remove`/`RemHead`/`RemTail`/`Enqueue` thunks operate on guest `List`/`Node` layouts as native structures; 64-bit native pointer writes do not match the 32-bit guest fields. Added as an Exec instance of the existing guest/native marshalling finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [generated thunk coverage notes](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest list operation or build was run.

**EK9432 rechecked — generated Exec memory-list APIs:** the optional m68kemu `Allocate`/`Deallocate` and `AllocEntry`/`FreeEntry` thunks pass guest `MemHeader`/`MemList` layouts to native code without shadow conversion; the listed guest/native sizes differ on 64-bit hosts, and `AllocEntry` also returns an untranslatable native handle. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [generated thunk coverage notes](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest call or build was run.


**EK10308 — m68kemu manual Intuition/Graphics thunks index past the guest arena for byte fields:** `OpenWindow`, `OpenScreen`, `AutoRequest` and `OpenFont` directly read guest structure bytes without validating the arena extent. A truncated structure at the arena end can cause an out-of-bounds host read. Scoped to the optional m68kemu vectors; no default-ROM or checked-in guest caller is claimed. See [EK10308](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10308) and the [manual thunk bounds pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11831). Source-only; no guest call or build was run.

**m68kemu `GetDrawInfoAttr` output-width mismatch (EK10305, 2026-10-31):** generated thunk passes a guest four-byte `IPTR` result slot directly to native 64-bit `GetDrawInfoAttr()`, whose unconditional status store writes eight bytes and overwrites the following guest word. Source-only; no guest call or build was run. See [EK10305](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10305) and the [GetDrawInfoAttr thunk pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11808).


**m68kemu Utility tag-list thunk recheck (2026-10-31):** reconciled the just-inspected `FindTagItem()`, tag mutators, and `FilterTagItems()` filter-array path against existing EK9196–EK9198 and EK10177. Those reports already cover the temporary-array use-after-free, discarded mutations, allocator handle/double-free behavior, and host-endian Tag arrays. No duplicate IDs or text were retained. Source-only; no guest calls or builds. See [EK9196](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9196), [EK9197](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9197), [EK9198](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9198), and [EK10177](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10177).


**GD10471 expanded — Vulkan-Hpp dynamic dispatch can erase EXT fallbacks for four KHR commands:** constructor-level reconciliation confirmed that three of the four affected EXT/KHR pairs also occur in `DeviceDispatcher` and `DispatchLoaderDynamic`; the same root cause is tracked once under GD10471 (GD10546 withdrawn as a duplicate). The optional headers have no found in-tree C++ client. See [GD10471](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10471--vulkan-hpp-dynamic-dispatch-loses-the-ext-fallback-for-vkcmdendrendering2khr) and the [dispatch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-end-rendering2-dispatch-fallback-gd10471). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.


**Graphics/Desktop Vulkan-Hpp dynamic-dispatch continuation (2026-10-31):** reconciled the 843-field dynamic-dispatch member table against global/instance/device initialization. Found no duplicate members, type/name mismatch, or missing active initializer; the disabled-platform placeholders account for the uninitialized platform slots. This structural pass adds no file or LOC credit and does not complete the header review. GD10471 remains recorded. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-dynamic-dispatch-member-table-reconciliation). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.


**GD10220 rechecked — ignored Vulkan-Hpp device lookup callback confirmed for layered loaders:** `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init(instance, gipa, device, gdpa)` discards `gdpa` and reloads through GIPA. Khronos Vulkan-Hpp issue #2578 documents the next-layer callback case; later Vulkan-Hpp release notes require the callback for device-level initialization. Confidence raised to high and scope narrowed to optional downstream Vulkan-Hpp clients using such layers. See [GD10220](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10220) and the [source and upstream-contract recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-gd10220-layered-device-callback-recheck). No Vulkan callback or build was run; source-only.


**GD10221 rechecked — no-exceptions loader failure requires `init()`:** the default constructor does not initialize. The convenience `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init()` hides the failed static loader, forwards a null procedure pointer past a disabled assertion, then calls it. A caller-owned `init(dl)` can check `dl.success()` first. Retained and narrowed to initialization calls whose procedure lookup returns null with assertions disabled. See [GD10221](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10221) and the [loader-failure recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-gd10221-no-exceptions-loader-failure-recheck). No runtime loader call was made.


**GD10219 withdrawn — empty Vulkan-Hpp proxy `end()` is not a bug:** the null pointer is offset by zero, which is defined in C++11 and later. The stride member is also initialized for empty strided proxies. See the [disposition](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10219) and [standards/source recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-gd10219-withdrawal). No file or LOC credit changed.


**EK10309 — m68kemu disk-library Resident scan can bind the wrong hunk file:** the scan starts at only the first hunk and continues across the whole arena, although later hunks allocate below it. A later-hunk Resident can be missed or a previously loaded library's Resident can be mistaken for the requested library, producing the wrong base and vectors. Scoped to optional m68kemu disk-library fallback. See [EK10309](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10309) and the [loader scan pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68kemu-disk-library-resident-scan-ek10309). Source-only; no guest library or build was run.

**OD9917 expanded — AROS SANA-II cookie wrappers also misroute the TX-copy fallback after a NULL DMA-copy result.** When an external opener supplies `S2_DMACopyFromBuff32` and it returns NULL, the DMA wrapper leaves `ios2_Data` set to the caller's packet pointer; the ordinary TX fallback then passes that pointer where the AROS `TXFunction` wrapper expects an `IOSana2Req *`. Scoped to the corresponding AROS network targets selected by the active platform aggregates (Atheros5000 with GNU; Broadcom4400, Etherlink III, Intel Pro/100, nvidianet, Prism2 and Rhine through the cards group; Realtek8180 for PC architecture); no in-tree opener using the DMA-copy tag was found. See [OD9917](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9917), the [SANA-II fallback caller audit](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sana-ii-s2_dmacopyfrombuff32-null-result-fallback-audit-od9917-expanded-no-new-od-or-bodyloc-credit-2026-10-31), and the [full finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9917). Source-only; no request, DMA callback or build was run.

**GD10473 — VideoCore cursor setup leaks firmware memory after partial allocation.** `InitCursor()` does not free its firmware allocation when cursor locking fails or the returned address fails validation; its caller ignores the failure and continues initialization. See [GD10473](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10473-videocore-cursor-setup-leaks-firmware-memory-after-partial-allocation) and the [cursor setup review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#videocore-cursor-setup-failed-lockmem-allocation-leak-gd10473). Source-only; no firmware allocation or cursor setup was run.

**GD10474 — Vulkan-Hpp RAII Context can call a null loader entry point in no-exceptions builds.** If dynamic loading is enabled, `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` is set, and the failed library/proc lookup yields null, the default Context passes that result to `ContextDispatcher`, which invokes it during construction without an exposed status check. Scoped to downstream clients of the optional copied headers; no in-tree RAII Context client was found. See [GD10474](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10474) and the [loader failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-context-loader-failure-gd10474). Source-only; no loader failure or build was run.

**GD10475 — Vulkan-Hpp constructs a device dispatcher after failed device creation.** In downstream `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds with `NDEBUG`, if `vkCreateDevice()` fails and leaves its output handle untouched, `PhysicalDevice::createDevice()` still constructs `DeviceDispatcher`, which queries commands with the null device before returning the error result. See [GD10475](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10475) and the [failed device-creation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-device-create-failure-gd10475). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.

**OD3733 — Bluetooth class scan reads an uninitialized service-binding flag.** `bDeviceClassScan()` reads `hassvcbinding` on a scan with no existing or successful service binding; this is undefined behavior and can suppress a configured or automatic device-level binding. The missed-binding consequence requires an external/custom class implementing device-binding methods; checked-in BTHID, btserial, and btpan do not. See [OD3733](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3733) and the [class-scan reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od3733-hassvcbinding-reconciliation). Source-only; no device scan was run.

**OD3736 — Overlapping Bluetooth scans can bind two HID services from one device.** BTHID checks for a device binding before starting its worker but publishes the binding only after worker startup; the event task and Preferences Class Scan action can overlap, and separate 16-service batches can reach two HID services. Scoped to Bluetooth builds selecting BTHID and Preferences with the stated service layout and overlap. See [OD3736](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3736) and the [selected-caller overlap confirmation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-bthid-duplicate-binding-selected-caller-overlap-confirmation-od3736-strengthened-no-body-or-loc-credit). Source-only; no scan or schedule was run.

**GD10476 — SysExplorer retains removed HIDD objects:** its tree stores borrowed controller and graphics-display pointers; ATA removal and graphics boot-display handover can dispose those objects, while later properties actions dispatch through the cached pointers. Scoped to the optional Storage/ATA or Gfx modules and removal/handover while the app remains open. See [GD10476](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10476-sysexplorer-keeps-removed-hidd-objects-in-its-hardware-tree) and the [ownership/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sysexplorer-cached-hidd-object-removal-gd10476). Source-only; no removal, handover, or runtime operation was performed.

<a id="ek10313"></a>EK10313 — POSIXC `dup2()` or racing `dup()` can mistake another process's globally reserved descriptor for its own, overwrite shared owner data, and free the reservation while that process still has a local descriptor. See [EK10313](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10313-dup2-can-replace-another-processs-global-posixc-descriptor-reservation) and the [caller/ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-dup2-cross-process-target-reservation-ek10313). See [EK21](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek21) and the [source/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#unix-hosted-krnfreepages-width-ek21). Source-only; no mapping or release was performed.

<a id="gd10484"></a>**GD10484 — Vulkan-Hpp RAII physical-device enumeration can return null entries after the device inventory shrinks between its count and fill calls.** Returned `PhysicalDevice` wrappers then contain null handles. Conditional on downstream use of the optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII API and a device-set change during enumeration. See [GD10484](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10484-vulkan-hpp-raii-physical-device-enumeration-can-return-null-entries-after-device-removal) and the [source/spec trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-raii-physical-device-enumeration-count-fill-race-gd10484). Source-only; no device or Vulkan call was exercised.
<a id="gd10485"></a>**GD10485 — software composition can skip CyberGraphX updates for bitmap regions wider or taller than 32,768 pixels:** `UpdateBitMap()` accepts `UWORD` extents, but the compositor message stores them in signed `WORD` fields; a full-bitmap update from the maintained unlock path can become an inverted rectangle and miss recomposition. Conditional on an oversized displayable bitmap and active optional software compositor. See [GD10485](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10485-software-compositor-drops-updates-wider-than-signed-word) and the [width/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-updatebitmap-signed-width-caller-trace-gd10485). Source-only; no bitmap or display operation was run.

**[EK10316](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10316) — m68kemu `OpenWindowTagList()` scans beyond a `TAG_MORE` list and passes its guest address to native Intuition.** A valid `TAG_MORE` ends the current list, but the thunk scans for `TAG_DONE`, copies the extra span, then leaves the continuation address untranslated. Conditional on explicitly building/loading the optional m68kemu library; the default ROM does not include it. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10316) and [tag-chain recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openwindowtaglist-tag-more-translation-recheck-ek10316). Source-only; no emulated call or window operation was run.

**[EK10317](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10317) — m68kemu `OpenWindowTagList()` ignores its non-NULL `NewWindow` argument.** Settings supplied in that structure are lost unless repeated by the tag list. Conditional on the explicitly built optional m68kemu library; no default ROM inclusion or checked-in guest caller is claimed. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10317) and [argument trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openwindowtaglist-newwindow-argument-recheck-ek10317). Source-only; no emulated call or window operation was run.

<a id="ek10318"></a>
**[EK10318](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10318) — TaskTrace can show stale registers and stack data for an x86-64 PC task running on another CPU.** The command reads the last context saved at switch-out without stopping or snapshotting a remote running task. Conditional on ExecSMP and the explicitly built optional TaskTrace shellcommand. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10318) and [saved-context trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tasktrace-live-task-context-snapshot-ek10318). Source-only; no trace or schedule was run.

**[OD4404](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4404) — BWFM's long-lived RX and association workers inflate `lib_OpenCnt`, so AROSTCP can report an interface offline without sending BWFM `S2_OFFLINE`.** Conditional on Raspberry Pi ARM32/AArch64 builds with BWFM and AROSTCP, successful firmware startup, and AROSTCP as the sole external opener. BWFM then remains logically online. AROSTCP's teardown aborts its parked event request, so no teardown hang is claimed. See the [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4404) and [caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od4404-sana-unrun-teardown-qualification). Source-only; no device or teardown was run.


<a id="compositor-od2399-caller-recheck"></a>Compositor monitor shared OOP-base failure caller pass (OD2399 expanded; 2026-10-31): traced its seven-entry list and startup rollback; failures in the first six entries reach the shared non-advancing cleanup loop, while final-entry failure returns after releasing acquired bases. The optional module has an explicit target but a commented parent aggregate edge, so no default-package inclusion is claimed. No new finding or path/LOC credit; see [OD2399](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2399) and the [coverage note](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#compositor-monitor-oop-attribute-base-caller-pass). Source-only.


**[OD2399](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2399) — OOP_ObtainAttrBases can spin forever after a non-final attribute-base lookup fails:** its cleanup loop does not advance the descriptor pointer, so multi-entry callers hang on an allocation failure before the final IID; already obtained bases are not released. Single-entry lists and final-entry failures are excluded. See the [direct-caller census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od2399-direct-caller-census-and-multi-entry-descriptor-reconciliation). Source-only.

<a id="od2399-direct-caller-census"></a>OD2399 direct-caller census (2026-10-31): enumerated 65 checked-in `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()` call sites and reconciled multi-entry lists; expanded OD2399 with omitted SDL, X11, WinGDI, VGA, i8042/IPMI, platform input, USB tool, graphics HIDD, VMware, and SysExplorer callers. Their reachability is conditional on the corresponding target selection and a non-final interface-name allocation failure; one-entry callers are excluded from this hang. No new defect ID or file/LOC credit. See [OD2399](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2399) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od2399-direct-caller-census-and-multi-entry-descriptor-reconciliation). Source-only.


<a id="acpi-attrbase-init-order-disposition"></a>ACPI HIDD attribute-base ignored-result recheck (2026-10-31): rejected a suspected continuation with zeroed bases. Generated module class initialization runs before InitLib and registers each ACPI module's final custom IID bucket before its `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()` call, excluding the final-descriptor allocation-failure return path; earlier missing-IID failures remain covered by OD2399. No new finding or LOC credit. See the [coverage record](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#acpi-hidd-ignored-attribute-base-result-generated-init-order-disposition). Source-only.


GD4755 exponent-16 report qualification (2026-10-31): replaced the stale one-line index entry with exact `BltPattern()` consequences and the API contract limitation. `SetAfPt()` stores the signed-byte value without validation; ±16 can narrow the computed 65,536-row height to zero before modulo, while +16 with a mask skips the zero-row validation loop and is treated as solid. No checked-in caller uses exponent 16, and the public header does not state the valid range, so support for that input remains unresolved and confidence is conditional. The canonical finding is in `AROS-graphics-desktop.md` under GD4755; source-only.


VideoCore cursor scope and dormant-helper reconciliation (2026-10-31): GD10473 remains scoped to BCM283x/BCM2711 because `InitCursor()` runs on BCM2711 after HVS setup is skipped; BCM2712 returns before it. The analogous lock-failure leak in `vc4_gpumem_alloc()` is under `VC4_GPUBM_ENABLE`, currently defined as zero, and is not reported as active at this revision. Details are recorded in the Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger; no runtime operation was performed.


OD9782 USB HID LowLevel caller qualification (2026-10-31): refined the reload-race trigger: default configuration maps rumble to LowLevel port 2, which the hook matches from port argument 1; the relevant setters are `SJA_RumbleSetSlowMotor` and `SJA_RumbleSetFastMotor`. The HID module is explicitly buildable and its parent class aggregate is disabled. The canonical Other Drivers finding and coverage ledger record this conditional path; no device or runtime operation was used.


OD9783 maximum-array input qualification (2026-10-31): confirmed a one-bit, one-count Output array can generate a 65,536-entry logical-value map while using only one bit in the report; a four-byte Logical Maximum avoids the separate two-byte signed-shift case. Documented the exact UWORD sequence and later-item alias in the canonical Other Drivers finding and coverage ledger. Map allocation and descriptor parsing remain conditional; no descriptor or device was used.


**[EK10319](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10319) — Generated handlers can be installed without their DOS/filesystem registrations.** On initialization-time resource or allocation failure, generated handler init can ignore the failed registration (including a false `AddBootNode()` result) and return a non-NULL resource base, preventing the cold-start resident walk from retrying. Applies to generated handlers with configured registrations, including boot-selected `con` on AArch64 Raspberry Pi and SiFive U. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10319) and [genmodule writer review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#genmodule-writestart-handler-init-error-propagation-recheck-ek10319). Source-only; no failure or boot was run.

**Current Graphics/Desktop + Exec/Kernel + Other Drivers coverage checkpoint (2026-10-31):** summing the latest regional ledgers gives **4,657/5,057 area entries (92.1%)** and **1,674,337/2,213,401 C/header code lines (75.6%)** with full-body credit; **400 entries and 539,064 code lines** remain without full-body credit. Area entries may duplicate paths, and full-body credit does not imply caller/configuration/platform closure. This supersedes earlier combined checkpoints in the dated ledger notes; source-only.

<a id="gd10486"></a>**GD10486 — `GetColorMap()` truncates large entry counts and leaks both tables when freed:** `Count` is a `UWORD`, so a 65,536-entry request returns a map with count zero; `FreeColorMap()` then passes zero sizes to `FreeMem()` and leaves both tables allocated. No checked-in caller requests this count. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10486-getcolormap-truncates-an-unrepresentable-entry-count-and-leaks-its-tables-on-free) and [API/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#getcolormap-count-representation-and-free-size-trace-gd10486). Source-only; no map or allocation was run.

<a id="gd10487"></a>**GD10487 — Wanderer dereferences a failed root-path allocation:** the root Workbench-window path allocates five bytes for `"RAM:"` without checking `AllocVec()` before `sprintf()`. If the allocation fails after the icon-window object was created, Wanderer faults before adding/opening the root window. The standalone target is explicit; parent aggregate edges are commented. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10487-wanderer-dereferences-a-failed-workbench-path-allocation) and [root-window allocation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-root-window-path-allocation-failure-gd10487). Source-only; no failure was induced.

<a id="gd10488"></a>**GD10488 — Wanderer runs copy/delete after its progress window fails to open:** `CreateCopyDisplay()` returns success after an unchecked window-open request; the callers continue copy/delete, while the only writer of the Stop flag is a gadget in that unavailable window. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10488-wanderer-continues-copydelete-operations-when-its-stop-window-fails-to-open) and [progress-window caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-copy-delete-progress-window-open-failure-gd10488). Explicit Wanderer target only; no default-packaging claim. Source-only; no file operation or window failure was induced.

<a id="od10980"></a>**OD10980 — Poseidon can dereference a failed formatted device-ID allocation:** the enumeration path passes unchecked `pd_IDString` to configuration lookup; `pMatchStringChunk()` dereferences it when a device configuration entry exists. Conditional on allocation failure plus either a matching `DEVID` entry or a nonempty config tree that takes the save path. See [OD10980](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10980--poseidon-passes-a-failed-device-id-allocation-into-string-matching) and the [allocation/configuration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#poseidon-formatted-device-id-allocation-and-config-lookup-pass-od10980). Source-only; no USB operation or failure was induced.


ARM-native raw SC_STI startup caller census (2026-10-31; no new EK): the only raw `SC_STI`/`SC_SUPERSTATE` sites are secondary-CPU startup and `IdleTask()`. Both are linked into the bounded `core.elf` text region, so the syscall address gate admits them; their saved-mode/mask transition is consistent with the intended privileged idle context. This closes that caller-scope gap only. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#arm-native-raw-sc_sti-startup-caller-census-2026-10-31-no-new-ek-or-bodyloc-credit). Source-only; no build or runtime operation.

<a id="gd10489"></a>**GD10489 — Wanderer misreports progress above 32,767 copy/delete items:** both item counters are signed 16-bit `WORD` values then become the gauge's unsigned maximum; the wider operation counter continues independently. Scoped to exceptionally large lists and the explicit Wanderer app target; exact narrowing is compiler-dependent. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10489) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-large-operation-count-truncation-gd10489). Source-only; no large list was created.


**GD5849 expanded — Wanderer can report a failed move as successful after destination-path allocation failure:** `moveFile()` passes a NULL combined path to `FileExists()`, whose DOS `Lock(NULL)` returns no lock; it then skips `Rename()` and returns the success value. The sole maintained drop caller ignores the returned status. A later companion `.info` allocation can succeed and move only the sidecar. See [GD5849](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5849) and the [recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-move-allocation-failure-false-success-gd5849-expanded). Source-only; no move or allocation failure was induced.

<a id="gd10490"></a>**GD10490 — Wanderer can dereference a failed source-directory lock during recursive copy:** `CopyContent()` passes the unchecked second `Lock()` result to `copyDirectory()`, whose `ExNext()` path dereferences the lock. Trigger requires the directory to be examined successfully, then the later read lock to fail. Scoped to explicit Wanderer app builds. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10490) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-recursive-copy-failed-source-lock-gd10490). Source-only; no filesystem race or lock failure was induced.

<a id="gd10491"></a>**GD10491 — Wanderer reports an empty-directory copy successful when the target name is a file:** after overwrite acceptance, `CreateDirectory()` returns no lock for an existing non-directory, but the empty-source enumeration leaves `stop` false and `CopyContent()` returns success. Scoped to the explicit Wanderer app target and a file/directory name conflict. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10491) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-empty-directory-copy-target-type-conflict-gd10491). Source-only; no filesystem operation was performed.

<a id="gd10492"></a>**GD10492 — Wanderer reports recursive copy success after `ExNext()` errors:** it shows an enumeration error but leaves the helper's failure result clear, so partial copies without a later sidecar-copy failure return success and a multi-item drop continues. Scoped to filesystem enumeration errors during recursive copy. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10492) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-recursive-copy-enumeration-error-gd10492). Source-only; no copy or filesystem error was induced.


EK10318 caller reachability recheck: TaskTrace enumerates `LTF_ALL`, which explicitly includes `LTF_RUNNING`/`TS_RUN`, and reads registers before printing task state. This confirms the live remote-task route; the finding remains about stale snapshot accuracy, not an invalid read. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tasktrace-ltf-all-running-task-caller-recheck-ek10318). Source-only; no task trace was run.

<a id="ek10320"></a>**EK10320 — TaskTrace checks only the start of an x86-64 frame record before reading two words:** a malformed RBP near an allocation boundary can pass `TypeOfMem()` while the second word crosses the allocation. Normal configured x86-64 code preserves frame pointers; the trigger requires malformed/corrupted state or a nonstandard producer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10320) and [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tasktrace-frame-record-extent-check-ek10320). Source-only; no malformed task was used.

<a id="ek10321"></a>**EK10321 — `DecodeLocation()` returns module/symbol name pointers after releasing the database lock:** concurrent unload can free their storage before a caller formats the result. Applies to `debug.library` callers that consume names after return; selected Exec alert formatting and optional TaskTrace are confirmed callers. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10321) and [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#decodelocation-returned-name-lifetime-ek10321). Source-only; no unload or lookup was run.

<a id="ek10322"></a>**EK10322 — The kernel backtrace resolver traverses debug module metadata without synchronizing with unload:** an ExecSMP fatal backtrace can overlap DOS freeing records when allocator locks do not serialize the two paths. Scoped to x86-64 PC with TLSF and debug.library active; memory-header reachability is unresolved. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10322) and [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#kernel-backtrace-resolver-module-lifetime-ek10322). Source-only; no trap or unload was induced.

<a id="ek10323"></a>**EK10323 — Private RealTime conductor sentinel is treated as a name pointer:** the documented `~0` private-conductor value is stored in `ln_Name`; later `FindName()` can pass it to `strcmp()` while scanning the global list. Triggered by an unmatched named lookup after a private conductor is created; the explicit Animation datatype target creates private conductors; a follow-up lookup is caller-dependent. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10323-private-realtime-conductor-sentinel-is-later-treated-as-a-name-pointer) and [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#realtime-private-conductor-name-sentinel-ek10323). No lookup was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10493"></a>**GD10493 — GadTools faults if a menu-bar-label image cannot be created:** `makemenuitem()` sets its item pointer to NULL after `NewObjectA()` fails, then dereferences it before `CreateMenusA()` can take its intended `GTMENU_NOMEM` cleanup path. Maintained Wanderer menus use `NM_BARLABEL`; scoped to image/class creation failure. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10493-gadtools-dereferences-a-failed-menu-bar-label-image-during-menu-creation) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-barlabel-image-construction-failure-gd10493). Source-only; no allocation failure or UI operation was induced.

<a id="gd10494"></a>**GD10494 — GadTools can report success when submenu layout fails:** `layoutsubitems()` ignores a failed submenu `layoutmenuitems()` result; a font-open failure in text subitems under an image parent can therefore be hidden by successful parent layout. Scoped to the exported GadTools API and font-open failure; no maintained direct `LayoutMenuItemsA()` caller was found. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10494-gadtools-reports-submenu-layout-success-after-a-child-layout-error) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-submenu-layout-error-propagation-gd10494). Source-only; no font or menu operation was induced.

<a id="gd10495"></a>**GD10495 — GadTools attaches subitems of a trimmed menu entry to the prior entry:** after the 64-item limit is reached, `CreateMenusA()` skips the next top-level item but leaves `curitem` unchanged; its following subitems are attached to the previous retained item. Scoped to over-limit NewMenu input accepted with `GTMENU_TRIMMED`. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10495-createmenusa-attaches-submenu-entries-from-trimmed-items-to-the-previous-item) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-trimmed-menu-item-submenu-parenting-gd10495). Source-only; no over-limit menu was created.

<a id="gd10496"></a>**GD10496 — GadTools leaks the menu block when rejecting an invalid full menu:** `CreateMenusA()` allocates its backing block before checking the first item/title relationship; the invalid-input path calls `FreeMenus(NULL)`, which performs no free. Scoped to `GTMN_FullMenu=TRUE` with invalid NewMenu ordering. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10496-createmenusa-leaks-its-allocation-when-rejecting-an-invalid-full-menu) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-invalid-full-menu-allocation-cleanup-gd10496). Source-only; no invalid menu was submitted.

<a id="gd10497"></a>**GD10497 — GadTools closes a borrowed RastPort font after requested-font lookup fails:** the label helper falls back to `rport->Font`, then `closefont()` treats that borrowed pointer as an opened reference and calls `CloseFont()`. A last reference to a non-ROM font can be removed while still installed in the RastPort. Scoped to GadTools IntuiText rendering when `OpenFont()` fails. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10497-gadtools-closes-the-rastports-borrowed-font-after-an-openfont-failure) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-label-font-fallback-ownership-gd10497). Source-only; no font operation was run.

<a id="gd10498"></a>**GD10498 — GadTools palette color count depends on tag order:** `makepalette()` lets a later `GTPA_Depth` overwrite a previously supplied `GTPA_NumColors`, despite the palette class implementing NumColors precedence. A palette with both tags can therefore use the wrong count. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10498-gadtools-palette-color-count-depends-on-tag-order) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gadtools-palette-depth-and-color-count-tag-order-gd10498). Source-only; no palette was created.

GD5775 list-view caller expansion (2026-10-31; no new GD or body/LOC credit): rechecked the GadTools list-view `GREDRAW_UPDATE` refresh-layer branch (`workbench/libs/gadtools/listviewclass.c:1136-1147`). Its `BeginUpdate()` FALSE branch explicitly calls `EndUpdate(FALSE)`, but failed `BeginUpdate()` has already unlocked and left `cr2` aliased to the active ClipRect list (`rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:68-92`). On the affected non-smart-refresh layer state, EndUpdate frees and republishes that list, then unlocks again; the caller also proceeds to render without a successful update lock. Folded this exact caller into GD5775 rather than opening a duplicate. No layer failure or rendering was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd10506"></a>**GD10506 — GadTools palette layout divides by zero for zero colors:** `GTPA_NumColors=0` is accepted, then layout computes zero columns and divides by that value. <a id="gd10507"></a>**GD10507 — GadTools palette treats an unmapped pen as a color-table index:** if a selected pen is absent from the supplied table, the class keeps the pen value and later indexes the table with it. <a id="gd10508"></a>**GD10508 — Graphics double-buffer reply queue can lose an entry on ExecSMP:** CPU 0’s VBlank handler can race a `ChangeVPBitMap()` insertion, and concurrent direct callers can also race each other because they release the viewport semaphore before the queue insertion. Local-only `Disable()` does not serialize these CPU paths; a head insertion can be overwritten, leaving buffer reply messages unsent. Scoped to x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi 2/3 32-bit and Pi 4/5 AArch64 ExecSMP with a displayed double-buffered viewport; explicit PC IRQ affinity may change the producer CPU. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10508-graphics-double-buffer-reply-queue-can-lose-an-entry-on-execsmp) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-double-buffer-reply-queue-execsmp-gd10508). No queue interleaving was run; source-only.

**[EK8910](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8910) — `sem_timedwait` can return timeout while a permit is available:** the condition wait gives a simultaneous timer signal priority, and the semaphore wrapper returns before rechecking a permit already published by `sem_post`. Requires a timed waiter and the stated signal overlap; the maintained in-tree `sem_wait` call uses no deadline. Source-only. See the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sem-timedwait-timeout-with-available-permit-ek8910).

<a id="ek10324"></a>**EK10324 — PosixC pthread exit can unload its leave-hook code before it returns:** if delayed expunge is requested and the worker's PosixC base is the last reference, its leave hook's `CloseLibrary()` can unload the module while that hook is executing. Requires an explicit expunge request and final-reference ordering; no in-tree PosixC caller found. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10324) and [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-thread-exit-hook-self-expunge-ek10324). No thread exit or expunge was run; source-only.
<a id="gd10510"></a>**GD10510 — SDL bitmap image methods use 3-byte surfaces for 4-byte pixel formats:** `PutImage()` and `GetImage()` pass depth 24 to SDL for `0RGB32` and related formats whose arrays store four bytes per pixel, so reads and writes use the wrong pixel boundaries. Reachable through CyberGraphX `ReadPixelArray()`/`WritePixelArray()` on the explicitly buildable hosted SDL HIDD. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10510-sdl-hidd-treats-four-byte-32-bit-pixel-formats-as-three-byte-surfaces) and [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sdl-32-bit-pixel-array-format-trace-gd10510). No pixel-array operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10511"></a>**GD10511 — Negative Decoration `BarHeight` can produce a zero system-image height:** a custom theme can set a negative bar height, causing the window decorator's unsigned scaled image height to become zero; Intuition then divides by that height while creating a system gadget image. Separate from GD6008's direct divide by zero for a zero `BarHeight`. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10511--negative-decoration-barheight-can-produce-a-zero-system-image-height) and [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#negative-decoration-barheight-system-image-path-gd10511). Custom-theme and system-gadget path; source-only, no window was opened.

<a id="od10983"></a>**OD10983 — AArch64 post-DMA clean can overwrite device data in a shared cache line:** after a device-to-RAM transfer, clean-and-invalidate writes back a dirty cache line; if CPU activity dirties a partial edge line during DMA, stale bytes can overwrite the device result. The Raspberry Pi package manifest includes PCI xHCI, whose source passes byte-granular buffers through this helper; its optional low-address bounce buffer is only guaranteed 16-byte alignment. The AArch64 kernel target also lists absent architecture-local source prerequisites (EK8902), so current checkout buildability/reachability is unverified. If the target is made buildable, manifestation still requires CPU writes to adjacent data in the same 64-byte line during DMA. Medium confidence in the interleaving; source-only. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10983--aarch64-post-dma-clean-can-overwrite-device-data-in-a-shared-cache-line) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#aarch64-partial-line-dma-cache-trace-od10983).

<a id="od10985"></a>**OD10985 — USB class debug dumps pass promoted `int` bytes to `%lx`:** identical helpers in ASIX Ethernet, ethwrap, moschipeth, PTP, and stir4200 have active in-tree `dumpmem()` callers. With `DEBUG` enabled this is undefined variadic behavior and may misformat bytes on wider-`long` ABIs; ordinary builds omit the diagnostic. High confidence in the mismatch; source-only. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10985--usb-class-debug-dumps-pass-promoted-int-bytes-to-lx) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#asixeth-debug-dump-format-type-od10985).

<a id="ek10325"></a>**EK10325 — `SaveTaskStorage()` fails to compile with task.resource debug logging:** its `D(...)` log refers to undeclared `size` instead of local `slots`; enabling `DEBUG` expands the statement and breaks that build. The manifest’s local debug define is commented, so the ordinary build is unaffected. High confidence; source-only. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10325) and [trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2150).

<a id="ek10326"></a>**EK10326 — Darwin AArch64 hosted kernel has an undefined `VFPContext` in signal save/restore:** the selected Unix context-switch source expands macros that apply `sizeof` to this missing type, so the macOS arm64 kernel translation unit cannot compile. Other Darwin CPU targets are unaffected. High confidence from source selection and definitions; no build was run. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10326) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#darwin-aarch64-signal-context-header-ek10326).

<a id="ek10327"></a>**EK10327 — Darwin x86-64 signal switching copies 576 bytes into a 512-byte FXSAVE buffer:** the selected hosted task context reserves only the legacy FXSAVE structure plus alignment slack, but both signal macros use the larger XSAVE structure size. The restore reads beyond the context allocation and the save overwrites at least 49 bytes past it. Scoped to Darwin hosted x86-64; high confidence from source sizes and selected callers, no build or dispatch run. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10327) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#darwin-x86-64-signal-context-header-ek10327).

<a id="ek10328"></a>**EK10328 — Darwin AArch64 hosted tasks do not preserve NEON state:** generic contexts contain no trailing FP buffer, leave `fpuContext` null and start with `ECF_FPU` clear, so the selected signal save/restore macros skip vector state on every task switch. Scoped to macOS arm64; high confidence from selected allocation and guards. Independent of EK10326's compile blocker; no runtime switch was tested. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10328) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#darwin-aarch64-fpu-context-lifecycle-ek10328).

<a id="ek10329"></a>**EK10329 — `TASKTAG_TCBEXTRASIZE` can wrap the task allocation size:** `NewCreateTaskA()` adds the requested extra size to `sizeof(struct Task)` in 32-bit `ULONG` without overflow checking, then initializes the task through the undersized allocation. Applies when a caller supplies a wrapping value and the allocation succeeds; no checked-in tag caller was found. High confidence in the size-wrap path; source-only. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10329) and [trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tasktag-tcbextrasize-allocation-overflow-ek10329).

<a id="ek10330"></a>**EK10330 — Unix SAD changes shared stderr flags:** while SAD polls, it sets `O_NONBLOCK` on descriptor 2, so a scheduled Unix emulation-handler write can fail with `EAGAIN` on a full pipe and is returned as `ERROR_UNKNOWN`; on exit, release clears a pre-existing nonblocking flag. Conditional on Unix-hosted SAD and the stated stderr/handler state. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10330) and [trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#unix-sad-shared-stderr-status-flags-ek10330). Source-only; no debugger or write was run.

<a id="ek153"></a>**EK153 — ARM32 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP inserts the bootstrap MemList into a zeroed task list:** `AddHead()` dereferences the still-null list head before the later `NEWLIST()`. The secondary can fault or corrupt low memory and never release the startup lock, leaving the ARM32 primary waiting. High confidence in the invalid list operation; exact memory effect is target-map dependent. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek153) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1393). Source-only; no secondary was started.

<a id="ek726"></a>**EK726 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP inserts the bootstrap MemList into a zeroed task list:** the secondary calls `AddHead()` before `NEWLIST()`, so it writes through the null list head and cannot complete registration. The BCM27xx primary has a bounded startup wait and can continue after logging the nonreporting CPU; no whole-system hang is claimed from this defect alone. High confidence in the source ordering; exact memory effect is target-map dependent. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek726) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1070). Source-only; no secondary was started.


<a id="od10986"></a>**OD10986 — Poseidon’s “Ignore” popup action can use a removed device’s ID string:** after an unlocked validity check, concurrent removal may clear `pd_IDString` before the preference update; Poseidon’s config matcher/creator dereferences the cleared pointer. Scoped to an ExecSMP overlap between PoPo “Ignore” and device removal. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10986--poseidons-ignore-popup-action-can-use-a-removed-devices-id-string) and [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#popo-shut-up-device-removal-id-string-race-od10986). No popup or removal was run; source-only.

<a id="od10987"></a>**OD10987 — AHIRecord dereferences a failed FLAC encoder allocation:** FLAC encoder creation can return NULL, but the saver passes it to setters before signaling startup success. On allocation failure the saver can fault before its ready signal, leaving the master blocked after the destination is opened. Applies to optional AHIRecord FLAC output. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10987--ahirecord-dereferences-a-failed-flac-encoder-allocation) and [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahirecord-flac-encoder-allocation-startup-pass-od10987). No recording or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

<a id="od10988"></a>**OD10988 — FLAC encoder buffer resize dereferences a failed allocation:** the selected FLAC init path records an aligned-buffer allocation failure but immediately `memset`s its output pointer, which is still NULL on first initialization. AHIRecord can fault during setup instead of returning an encoder-init error. Applies to optional AHIRecord FLAC output under buffer-allocation failure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10988--flac-encoder-buffer-resize-dereferences-a-failed-allocation) and [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahirecord-flac-buffer-resize-allocation-pass-od10988). No allocation failure or recording was induced; source-only.

<a id="od10989"></a>**OD10989 — AHIRecord ignores FLAC stream initialization failure:** the saver sets `FileOpen` and signals readiness regardless of the encoder init result. After a later workspace allocation failure, sampling continues with incomplete encoder state; a fixed-subframe path can dereference the missing residual buffer. Applies to optional AHIRecord FLAC output under the stated failure/input path. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10989--ahirecord-ignores-flac-stream-initialization-failure) and [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahirecord-flac-init-result-caller-pass-od10989). No recording or allocation failure was induced; source-only.
<a id="od10990"></a>**OD10990 — AHIRecord truncates 32-bit samples in its 16-bit FLAC path:** it copies signed S32 samples unchanged although FLAC is configured for 16-bit input; a constant sample of 65536 is serialized as zero. Applies to optional AHIRecord FLAC output when S32 values use bits above the low 16. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10990--ahirecord-truncates-32-bit-samples-in-its-16-bit-flac-path) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahirecord-flac-sample-conversion-contract-od10990). Source-only; no recording was run.
**OD3271 — USB keyboard modifier count exceeds its fixed array:** the descriptor parser retains an over-limit count for an eight-entry array; report and worker paths index beyond it, and the 8-bit count wraps to a write before the array at 256 fields. On 32-bit-int targets, sufficiently large counts also reach an undefined signed shift. Applies to the optional HID keyboard class with an over-capacity report descriptor. High confidence in the source-level bounds and wrap behavior; descriptor reachability is conditional. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3271) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-modifier-count-od3271). No descriptor, report, device, or build was used.
**OD4091 — USB keyboard key-array count narrows before allocation:** the 32-bit descriptor count is stored in an 8-bit field for buffer sizing, while the callback copies the full-width byte count. A 257-byte report can allocate two bytes and then copy 257 bytes past the destination when UHCI dispatches a successful one-byte completion. Applies to the optional USB HID keyboard class with an over-width key array. High confidence in narrowing/copy; descriptor and completion conditions are conditional. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4091). No descriptor, report, device, or build was used.
**OD10997 — USB HID report length narrows to zero before UHCI queue setup:** a 256-byte parsed report becomes a zero `uint8_t` AddInterrupt length; UHCI queues no transfer descriptors then dereferences its NULL tail pointer. Applies to explicitly selected optional HID and UHCI modules. High confidence in the source path; descriptor reachability is conditional. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10997-usb-hid-addinterrupt-length-narrowing). No descriptor, device, registration, or build was used.
**OD2971 — UHCI does not dispatch some TD errors to transfer clients:** error-only status is acknowledged without queue processing; synchronous callers can wait or falsely succeed on another completion path, and interrupt-pipe callbacks can stop. Consolidated duplicate OD10998 into this entry. Applies to an explicitly selected UHCI HIDD and compatible hardware; stock boot-package reachability is not established. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2971). Source-only.
**OD10994 — USB HID keyboard and mouse workers do not check their event-buffer allocations:** after `AllocVec()` fails, the next translated key or mouse event writes through the NULL batch pointer. Scoped to either optional USB HID input class under memory pressure with `input.device` available. High confidence in both unchecked allocations and event-writing paths; source-only. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10994) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-keyboard-event-buffer-failure-od10994). No allocation failure, report, device, or build was used.
**OD10995 — USB HID keyboard worker can call `OpenDevice()` with a NULL request:** message-port or I/O-request creation failure is unchecked; the selected `OpenDevice()` dereferences the request before validating it. Scoped to the optional USB HID keyboard class under setup allocation/signal failure. High source confidence; source-only. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10995--usb-hid-keyboard-worker-passes-a-null-io-request-to-opendevice) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-keyboard-iorequest-allocation-failure-od10995). No failure, worker, device, or build was induced.

**OD3142 rechecked — USB HID 31/32-bit field extraction also left-shifts a negative signed value:** the existing full-width mask shift is undefined; for a 32-bit field with its high bit set, sign extension then shifts a negative `int32_t` even by zero, which is also undefined. Scoped to the generic USB HID mouse's valid wide X/Y fields. See [OD3142](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3142) and the [HID parser trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-field-width-and-signedness-review-od3142-od3143-rechecked). Source-only; no descriptor or report was used.

**OD2312 — USB HID worker event buffers leak if opening input.device fails:** both keyboard and mouse allocate their event batch before OpenDevice() and omit its free on the failure return. This restores coverage-only keyboard OD2312 and consolidates mouse OD2806. Scoped to selected USB HID classes when batch allocation succeeds but input-device open fails. High source confidence; source-only. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2312--usb-hid-workers-leak-event-buffers-when-inputdevice-open-fails) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-worker-open-failure-event-buffer-leak-od2312). No allocation or device-open failure was induced.

**OD2184 restored — USB HID workers can lose their one-shot detach signal during DOS readiness:** keyboard always defers Ctrl-C processing on a wake that begins before DOS is ready; mouse also loses it if DOS remains unavailable. The worker can stay blocked with input.device and its worker resources retained after hub disposal. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2184) and [trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-worker-detach-before-dos-init-od2184). Source-only; no worker or detach was exercised.

These targets are selected through the active network aggregate in the standard workbench build; the consequence remains conditional on PCI-driver removal. nForce is excluded because OD3080 prevents its unit publication. OD3745 expanded — PCIUSB and PCI xHCI also retain unclaimed PCI objects between enumeration and first ownership; the selected PCIPC and RISC-V PCIDT expunge paths can remove unowned devices during that gap.
