OD3745 expanded — optional Prometheus also caches enumerated PCI object pointers for direct-bus boards and later dereferences unclaimed entries; backend removal can leave its board wrappers stale. Conditional on the library being open during expunge. See [OD3745](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3745) and the [Prometheus lifetime trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#prometheus-pci-wrapper-lifetime-od3745).
**OD11471 — Prometheus leaves unsupported board-attribute outputs unchanged:** `Prm_GetBoardAttrsTagList()` promises zero for unknown tags but does not write the output slot. Conditional on an optional library caller supplying an unsupported tag. See [OD11471](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11471) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#prometheus-library-pci-lifetime-body-pass).

**OD11472 — PCNet32 loses earlier workers when PCI enumeration finds multiple adapters:** each matching PCI device creates a worker, but the base retains only the last unit; expunge stops one and waits indefinitely for the others. Requires two supported adapters and successful initialization. See [OD11472](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11472) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcnet32-multi-adapter-enumeration-expunge-od11472).

**EK9217 — Parthenope CD boot can mistake an uninitialized cache tag for block 16:** `cdrom_create()` does not initialize `sector_in_buf` before the first volume-descriptor read, and `cdrom_read()` skips the device read if stale allocator data equals the requested block. The descriptor then comes from uninitialized `tmpbuf`. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only; default-image inclusion is not claimed. See [EK9217](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9217) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5039). No media or boot was used; source-only.

**EK9216 — Parthenope CD factory dereferences a failed boot-object allocation:** after `get_dev()` allocates a copied descriptor, failure to allocate `cdrom_boot_dev_t` skips the guarded setup but reaches `return &boot->dev`. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only; no default-image inclusion claim. See [EK9216](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9216) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5332). No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.

**EK9218 — Parthenope CD teardown leaks its copied block-device descriptor:** `get_dev()` allocates/copies `block_dev_desc_t`, but the registered destroy callback frees only the enclosing boot object. Reached on successful CD backend teardown in the explicit optional Sam440 target. See [EK9218](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9218) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5039). No boot or device operation was performed; source-only.

**EK9219 — Parthenope CD discovery copies into a failed descriptor allocation:** `get_dev()` calls `memmove()` on the result of `malloc()` as soon as it finds a CDROM scan entry. An allocation failure faults before `cdrom_create()` can return NULL. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9219](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9219) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5039). No scan or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

**EK9220 — Parthenope CD factory dereferences an absent or unread SUSP area:** root-record lengths can yield a zero-size SUA on plain ISO; `cdrom_create()` ignores allocation/read results and immediately reads the signature. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9220](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9220) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5039). No media or boot was used; source-only.

**EK9221 — Parthenope SUSP scans leak their current buffer on failed media reads:** both the initial SUA read and a CE continuation read return without freeing the allocated buffer; `get_entry()` discards the error and treats it as no match. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only; repeated exhaustion is not established. See [EK9221](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9221) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5043). No media error or boot was induced; source-only.

**EK9222 — Malformed Parthenope SUSP data can hang CD lookup:** a zero-length entry leaves the iterator cursor unchanged, while a cyclic CE continuation repeats without a progress or cycle check. This can stall factory setup or filename lookup on malformed ISO media. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9222](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9222) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5178). No image or boot was used; source-only.

**EK9223 — Parthenope copies matching SUSP entries beyond the allocated SUA:** `my_iteration()` copies the on-media `e->len` without checking the bytes remaining in the current buffer; root RR and filename NM lookups reach this callback. Malformed matching records can make the copy read past the SUA allocation. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9223](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9223) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5047). No malformed image or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9224 — Parthenope dereferences a failed SUSP-entry allocation:** when a matching RR/NM entry is found, `my_iteration()` does not check `malloc(e->len)` before copying to the result. Applies only to explicitly built optional `parthenope-sam440`. See [EK9224](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9224) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5049). No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.
**EK9225 — Parthenope CD lookup dereferences unchecked path/name allocations:** the requested path copy is passed to `memcpy`, and an ISO directory-name buffer is passed to `cdrom_read`, without checking allocation success. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9225](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9225) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4994). No low-memory condition or boot was induced; source-only.
**EK9226 — DOS concurrent `InternalFlush` calls can duplicate writes and corrupt `fh_Pos`:** the flushing flag check/set is not atomic, and competing cleanup can subtract an old position from an already reset cursor. The overlapping animation children have not been established to share and concurrently flush the handle. See [EK9226](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9226) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5053). No task interleaving or handler write was run; source-only.

**EK10333 — ARM `GetCPUInfo()` returns incomplete or mismatched model/version/vendor identity fields:** its ARM32 display clients show zero model/revision data and cannot match the numeric implementer ID because the getter writes a string pointer. Scoped to ARM32 processor.resource users. See [EK10333](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10333) and the [caller/source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#arm-processor-identity-tags-ek10333). Source-only; no processor query was run.


**EK10334 — AArch64 `processor.resource` leaves ARM model/version/vendor outputs untouched:** scoped to external or future callers on Raspberry Pi AArch64; no maintained caller was found. See [EK10334](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10334) and the [selection/tag trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#aarch64-processor-identity-tags-ek10334). Source-only; no processor query was run.

**GD10513 withdrawn — duplicate of [GD10280](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10280).** Both entries covered the enhanced and RAII pipeline-properties convenience overloads passing the same wrong, undersized output object; GD10280 remains canonical. Source review and coverage credit remain in place.
**EK10335 — The selected pthread library accepts asynchronous cancellation but does not deliver it asynchronously:** with the default build, `pthread_cancel()` only leaves CTRL-C pending because the async exception handler is compiled out; a target running code without cancellation checks can continue indefinitely. Scoped to `linklibs-pthread`; high confidence in the source path, with manifestation depending on the target not reaching a cancellation check. See [EK10335](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10335) and the [cancellation path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-asynchronous-cancellation-delivery-ek10335). Source-only; no thread or build was run.

**[EK10337](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10337) — m68kemu window thunks mishandle initial gadget lists.** `OpenWindow()` drops `NewWindow.FirstGadget`; `OpenWindowTagList()` forwards `WA_Gadgets` as a raw guest pointer that native Intuition traverses using the incompatible host Gadget layout. Conditional on explicitly building/loading the optional m68kemu library and a guest caller supplying an initial gadget list; no default ROM inclusion or checked-in caller is claimed. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10337) and [direct field trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openwindow-firstgadget-field-recheck-ek10337) plus [WA_Gadgets trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openwindow-tag-gadgets-recheck-ek10337). Source-only; no emulated call or window operation was run.
**[EK10338](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10338) — m68kemu `OpenScreen()` drops `NewScreen.ViewModes`, `Font`, and `CustomBitMap`, masks `SCREENBEHIND`, `SCREENQUIET`, and `AUTOSCROLL` out of `NewScreen.Type`, and forces `SHOWTITLE`.** A guest request can select the wrong HAM/EHB mode, default screen font/bitmap, bring a background screen to front, draw a bar on a quiet screen, fail to autoscroll at screen edges, or show an unwanted title bar. Conditional on the optional m68kemu library and a guest using those fields. The native `2View` demo uses `SCREENBEHIND` and `ViewModes`, but no in-tree m68k guest caller was established. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10338) and [NewScreen-field trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openscreen-newscreen-field-recheck-ek10338). Source-only; no screen or emulator call was run.
**[EK10339](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10339) — m68kemu `AutoRequest()` discards `IntuiText.ITextFont`.** Converted requester text uses the requester font instead of a guest-specified font, which can change its appearance and fit. Conditional on explicitly building/loading the optional m68kemu library and a guest supplying a font; no checked-in guest caller was established. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10339) and [font-conversion trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#autorequest-intuitext-font-recheck-ek10339). Source-only; no requester or emulator call was run.
**[EK10340](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10340) — m68kemu `AutoRequest()` silently truncates `IntuiText.NextText` chains.** The thunk caps body/button chains and also ignores recursive node-allocation failure, then displays the partial chain. Conditional on a long guest chain or allocation failure through the optional m68kemu library; no checked-in caller was established. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10340) and [chain-length/allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#autorequest-intuitext-chain-recheck-ek10340). Source-only; no requester, allocation failure, or emulator call was run.
**GD10514 — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap constructor accepts both usage-count array forms:** equal-length nonempty `usageCounts` and pointer-array arguments pass the enhanced constructor, leaving both mutually exclusive Vulkan pointers set. Scoped to downstream clients of the optional `VK_NV_displacement_micromap` wrapper; high confidence in the source and valid-usage mismatch, no in-tree caller found. See [GD10514](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10514) and the [wrapper review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-displacement-micromap-usage-count-validation-gd10514). Source-only; no Vulkan command or build was run.

**GD10233 continuation — NV acceleration-structure geometry count:** `AccelerationStructureInfoNV` narrows the enhanced geometry proxy size to `uint32_t` in its constructor and setter, then the NV build wrapper forwards that count with the original pointer. This is the existing large-container narrowing issue, gated by `VK_NV_ray_tracing`; no in-tree C++ caller found. See [GD10233](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10233-vulkan-hpp-array-proxies-truncate-large-container-sizes).

**GD10515 — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap constructor ignores the pointer-array length:** supplying only the `ppUsageCounts` array leaves the shared count at zero because the enhanced constructor derives it from the empty alternative proxy; the entries are omitted from the native record. Optional Vulkan-Hpp downstream caller; no in-tree use found. See [GD10515](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10515) and the [constructor and dispatch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd10515-caller-and-configuration-reconciliation). Source-only; no command or build was run.

**GD10516 — Vulkan-Hpp `ApplicationInfo` comparisons can dereference null names:** default construction leaves both name pointers null, but equality and C++20 three-way comparison call `strcmp` when only one side is null. Comparing a default value with a named value can therefore fault. Optional Vulkan-Hpp client comparison; no in-tree comparison use found. See [GD10516](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10516) and the [comparison review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-applicationinfo-nullable-string-comparison-gd10516). Source-only; no comparison or build was run.

**GD4656 — `CloseMonitor()` can lose a concurrent `OpenMonitor()` count update:** on ExecSMP, its semaphore-protected plain decrement can overwrite the atomic increment because the opener does not take that semaphore. This can undercount the public monitor open count and make a later close report failure despite an outstanding reference; no maintained lifetime consumer was found. See [GD4656](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4656) and the [monitor open/close review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L11471). No concurrent monitor call was run; source-only.

**OD11000 withdrawn:** the selected 8SVX/IFF/DOS path uses signed `LONG` sizes and read results and does not establish a published near-`ULONG_MAX` sample length; see the withdrawal note in [Other Drivers](AROS-other-drivers.md).

**OD2373 — CharMap scrollback frees a line still referenced by the active selection:** at the history cap, a `C_SCROLL_UP` trim can free the selected oldest line without updating its stored selection pointer; Right-Command+C then traverses that stale line. Applies to selected `CONU_CHARMAP` and `CONU_SNIPMAP` paths. See [OD2373](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2373-charmap-scrollback-frees-a-selected-line) and the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L26748). Source-only; no console sequence or clipboard copy was run.
**OD11001 withdrawn:** `genmodule` does not emit the `.conf` attribute type into the generated interface header, and the only in-tree caller uses the returned Task correctly. The stale config annotation has no evidenced caller-visible effect; see the [withdrawal rationale](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11001-acpi-button-servicetask-attribute-has-the-wrong-pointer-type).
**OD11002 — DOSBoot MountList snapshot races AddBootNode on ExecSMP:** a USB mass-storage BootNode added after DOSBoot counts the list can be treated as disabled and dropped from MountList on the no-menu path; larger growth can overrun the selection array. Conditional on early USB enumeration during DOSBoot; source-only. See [OD11002](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11002-dosboot-mountlist-snapshot-races-addbootnode).
**OD3922 — Poseidon can mark preferences saved after an incomplete write:** a short `Write()` is treated as success; an ENVARC open failure followed by a successful ENV write can update the shared saved hash despite the overall failure; and a USB hub task can create a new device config record after serialization but before the save publishes the hash. The GUI disables Save based on hash equality. Conditional on storage errors or the stated task interleaving. See [OD3922](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3922) and the [save-result/hash caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#poseidon-save-hash-update-after-envarc-failure-od3922-expanded). Source-only; no file write or concurrent task schedule was run.

**GD10517 — Graph.mcc leaves skipped source slots uninitialized:** when a client requests a source index beyond the next slot, growth initializes only the final record but raises the count across the gap. Later drawing or resizing can read an uninitialized entry-buffer pointer from an intermediate slot. Optional Graph.mcc downstream caller; checked-in SysMon uses sequential indices. See [GD10517](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10517) and the [source trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graph-sparse-source-index-growth-gd10517). Source-only; no graph operation or build was run.

**GD10518 — Graph.mcc ignores `MUIA_Graph_Aggregate` while drawing:** the public attribute sets `GRAPHF_AGGR`, but the draw method never reads it and continues to plot every source independently. Optional Graph.mcc downstream API; no in-tree caller found. See [GD10518](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10518) and the [implementation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graph-aggregate-attribute-gd10518). Source-only; no graph draw or build was run.

**GD10519 — VBlank may traverse a freed `DBufInfo`:** on ExecSMP, `FreeScreenBuffer()` can free its per-buffer record while it remains queued behind the screen Restore record; a prompt `CloseScreen()` can also free the Restore record before the Disp reply. The handler then reads or replies through freed storage. Scoped to x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi 2/3/4/5 SMP with the described cross-CPU overlap. Distinct from GD10508's queue-head mutation. See [GD10519](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10519) and the [DBufInfo owner-lifetime trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vblank-dbufinfo-reply-lifetime-gd10519). Source-only; no screen or VBlank operation was run.

**GD10520 — V3D BO page-rounding overflow retains an empty arena on failed creation:** a `UINT32_MAX` CREATE_BO size rounds to zero, then the failed allocation path leaves a new 32 MiB mapped arena in the list until session teardown. Repeated requests can consume memory. Scoped to explicit downstream ioctl requests on the optional AArch64 Raspberry Pi V3D target; no checked-in request producer was found. See [GD10520](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10520) and the [UAPI/allocation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-bo-size-rounding-overflow-and-failed-allocation-arena-retention-gd10520-added-prior-size-narrowing-wording-corrected-2026-11-01). Source-only; no ioctl or allocation failure was induced.
**GD10521 — system requester sizing ignores per-line `IntuiText.ITextFont`:** requester text is measured with the screen font but rendered with each entry's requested font, so larger custom fonts can exceed the calculated box or be clipped. No checked-in caller using custom fonts in this path was found. See [GD10521](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10521) and the [requester font-metrics trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#system-requester-ignored-itextfont-metrics-gd10521). Source-only; no requester or custom-font operation was run.
**GD10522 — `int_PrintIText()` carries a custom entry's soft style into following plain text:** after a custom-font line, the original font is restored but its `AlgoStyle` is not, so subsequent entries with no `ITextFont` can inherit the prior line's bold/italic style. Conditional on a mixed-font chain; no matching checked-in caller was established. See [GD10522](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10522) and the [soft-style trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#itext-custom-font-soft-style-carries-forward-gd10522). Source-only; no rendering was run.
**GD10523 — Vulkan-Hpp `StridedArrayProxy` iterator is not stride-aware:** its exposed raw `T*` `begin()`/`end()` pair makes range iteration step by `sizeof(T)` even when records are spaced by a larger stride, so iteration visits padding or the wrong elements. Scoped to downstream users of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API; no in-tree caller was found. See [GD10523](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10523) and the [proxy review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-strided-proxy-utility-and-commandbuffer-declaration-pass-gd10523gd10524-added-gd10279-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no iteration or build was run.
**GD10524 — Vulkan-Hpp `StridedArrayProxy` offset products wrap at 4 GiB:** `size()` and `m_stride` are `uint32_t`, so `end()` and `back()` calculate their byte offsets with 32-bit unsigned multiplication; on a 64-bit client a representable count spanning over 4 GiB can produce an early end or wrong last element. Scoped to large downstream buffers using the optional copied API; no in-tree caller was found. See [GD10524](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10524) and the [proxy review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-strided-proxy-utility-and-commandbuffer-declaration-pass-gd10523gd10524-added-gd10279-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no large buffer or build was used.

# Hyperlayers BeginUpdate shape-mask caller pass (GD6186 expanded; no new ID; 2026-11-01)

Traced both ignored in-place `AndRegionRegion()` shape masks in `BeginUpdate()` to active ClipRect construction. Allocation failure preserves the pre-mask damage intersection, so drawing may proceed outside the visible/custom layer shape; expanded GD6186 and the coverage record. This is distinct from GD6172's nullable `AndRegionRegionND()` failure. No allocation failure or drawing operation was run; source-only.

**Graphics/Desktop progress (2026-11-01):** continued the RAII source-order pass through `vulkan_raii.hpp:8405`, completing the remaining `CommandBuffer` declarations and reviewing `CommandBuffers`, `CuFunctionNVX`, `CuModuleNVX`, and the start of beta `CudaFunctionNV`. Rechecked GD10263 at `Device::allocateCommandBuffers()`: host allocation for the owning wrapper vector follows native handle allocation, leaving the already documented exception cleanup window. No new finding or coverage credit; the copied RAII header and broader callers/configurations remain open. See the [coverage record](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-commandbuffer-and-cuda-handle-continuation-gd10263-rechecked-no-new-gd-or-bodypathloc-credit-2026-11-01). Source-only; no Vulkan allocation, exception, handle, command, or build was exercised.

**Graphics/Desktop progress (2026-11-01):** continued the RAII source-order pass through `vulkan_raii.hpp:9005`, completing CUDA and data-graph session handles and reviewing debug-report/debug-utils messenger ownership through the start of deferred-operation handling. Device/instance, allocator, dispatcher and native-handle state remained paired across move, clear, release and destruction; no new issue was established. The optional copied header, its callers and configuration remain open, with no file/LOC credit. See the [coverage record](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-cudadata-graphdebug-handle-source-order-pass-no-new-finding-or-fileloc-credit-2026-11-01). Source-only; no Vulkan object, callback, device, build or runtime behavior was exercised.

**[EK10347](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10347) — Console `Write()` reports the requested count after a device allocation failure:** when a pending incomplete CSI sequence requires a merge buffer and that allocation fails, the console device records zero bytes accepted; the handler ignores `DoIO()`'s result and returns the original requested length. Conditional on the pending sequence and allocation failure. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10347) and [caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#console-handler-short-write-result-propagation-ek10347). Source-only; no failure or write was induced.
**EK10346 — Console handler fails to handle signal-allocation failure:** if the handler task has no free signal bits, it stores `AllocSignal()`'s failure value as a byte and later shifts by that invalid number when waiting for device reads or synchronous writes. I/O completion may be missed or remain blocked. See [EK10346](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10346) and the [console signal-allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#console-handler-read-signal-allocation-failure-ek10346).

**EK705 — Shifted console-history keys select the wrong entries after ring wrap:** once 32 command slots are full, Shift-Up and Shift-Down still choose physical slots 0 and 31 instead of the oldest/newest slots relative to the ring cursor. See [EK705](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek705) and the [history-ring source-order recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2483). Applies to cooked input in `kernel-fs-con`; source-only, no console interaction was run.

By ledger: Graphics/Desktop 1,368/1,460 files (93.7%), 470,498/634,467 lines (74.2%); Exec/Kernel 1,554/1,804 files (86.1%), 164,397/185,071 lines (88.8%); Other Drivers 1,934/2,390 files (80.9%), 569,935/697,711 lines (81.7%). This counts explicit full-read status, not caller/configuration/lifecycle closure or goal completion; 144 distinct ledger labels did not map unambiguously to tracked paths, explicitly unselected rows were excluded, and `cloc` did not emit per-file rows for two mapped paths. The ledger inventory still needs build-selection and status reconciliation before these can serve as an ETA denominator. **Other Drivers progress (2026-11-01):** rechecked timer VBlank registration and dispatch on Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 and MinGW32 against `timer.conf`, which marks timer.device `noexpunge`. Normal runtime removal is therefore out of scope; a MinGW failed-`StartClock` rollback remains externally dependent. The generic concurrent VBlank walk/removal case is already EK629, with realtime.library as the selected owner; no timer-specific defect was added. The one-line VBlank declaration is now explicitly marked read. See the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no timer or interrupt ran.
**EK10345 — Public OOP class lookup can race final class expunge:** `OOP_FindClass()` drops the class-list lock before returning, `OOP_NewObject()` pins the class afterward, and generated expunge unlinks and disposes it without waiting on the count. A concurrent external lookup can therefore touch freed class metadata. The optional Workbench MonWrapper target also borrows a found class without opening its provider before AddDisplayDriverA(); final-expunge overlap remains timing-dependent. See [EK10345](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10345) and the [lookup-to-pin lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#oop-public-class-lifetime-detailed-restoration-gd4254-2026-10-17). Source-only; no class or expunge was run.


**EK9002 — Sam440 stack-probe alert copies beyond the saved CPU context:** the Sam440 saved frame is 424 bytes, while the supervisor alert formatter copies the 968-byte generic PPC `ExceptionContext`. Scope is an explicitly selected Sam440 target reaching the common scheduler stack-probe alert; the checked-in default package edges are commented, so no default-image route is claimed. See [EK9002](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9002) and the [Sam440 manifest/context trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sam440-scheduler-selection-and-stack-probe-context-pass-ek9002-scope-qualified-2026-11-01). Source-only; no exception or alert was induced.

**OD11003 — HDAudio mono mode overruns its AHI and DMA buffers:** a custom mode can replace shipped AudioID `0x003E0001` with `AHIDB_Stereo=FALSE`; AHI then allocates mono frames, but HDAudio keeps stereo hardware format and its interrupt copies stereo-sized words. See [OD11003](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11003) and the [mode-file/build/caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od11003-hdaudio-mode-pass). Conditional on custom mode registration and playback; source-only, no playback was run.
**OD11006 — Concurrent Atheros unit setup can expose a partial shared rate table:** the helper marks the table initialized while its reverse map is still being cleared/populated; another unit can then use `0xff` as an index into a 32-entry rate array. Scoped to GNU-toolchain builds, which select `atheros5000.device` through the active network aggregate: SMP permits cross-CPU overlap, and single-CPU PC scheduling can preempt between same-priority unit tasks at a quantum boundary, with a TX lookup before initialization completes also required. See [OD11006](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11006) and the [UP preemption trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#atheros5000-up-task-preemption-route-for-od11006). Source-only; no adapter, preemption or TX operation was run.
**[EK292](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek292) — Hosted ARM `GetCPUInfo()` maps feature tags to the wrong Linux feature bits:** the public tag order inserts VFPv3D16 and VFPv4 between Linux feature positions, so capability queries can report Neon, Thumb, ThumbEE, or another feature under the wrong label. Scoped to hosted ARM Linux processor.resource clients, including the selected ShowConfig and SysExplorer pages. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek292) and the [feature tag mapping audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#hosted-arm-cpu-feature-tag-order-ek292). Source-only; no host query or build was run.
**[EK10352](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10352) — Hosted ARM `GetCPUInfo()` leaves the FPU feature output untouched:** the Linux provider omits `GCIT_SupportsFPU`, so the optional diagnostic hides FPU support and other callers can receive a stale value. See [EK10352](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10352) and its [provider/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#hosted-arm-fpu-feature-output-ek10352). Source-only; no host query or build was run.
**[EK10353](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10353) — GPT writer subtracts backup table bytes from an LBA:** the backup entry-array size is calculated in bytes but subtracted directly from the final LBA, placing the array too early and potentially overwriting a partition's tail during HDToolBox save. See [EK10353](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10353) and the [GPT write-unit trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-backup-entry-array-byte-lba-mismatch-ek10353). Source-only; no disk or write was used.
**[EK10349](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10349) — Hosted ARM processor initialization leaks earlier model strings:** every matching `Processor:` line duplicates a string into one field without freeing the previous value. Conditional on repeated records in the host's `/proc/cpuinfo`; bounded to startup. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10349) and the [ownership recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#hosted-arm-processor-initializer-ownership-ek10349). Source-only; no host file or initialization was used.

**OD11004 — HID output array strings skip an element after a comma:** quoted strings consume one report slot per character, then their comma consumes another slot; later values are shifted in output/feature reports. See [OD11004](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11004) and the [parser/caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-output-array-string-parser-od11004). Requires a configured output/feature array action with a quoted string followed by another value; source-only, no HID report was sent.
**OD11007 — HID array parsing overflows its signed 32-bit accumulator:** high-bit decimal/hex values for 32-bit output or feature array fields exceed `LONG` during parsing, so the intended report bits are not reliable. Scoped to configured USB HID array actions using those values. See [OD11007](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11007) and the [parser and encoding trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-array-high-bit-value-overflow-od11007). Source-only; no report was sent.
**OD11008 — HID syntax errors still submit partially updated arrays:** the parser mutates valid prefix values, returns on a later syntax error, and the action caller still marks the report touched; the worker then submits the partial output/feature report. Requires a configured malformed array action and a triggering input event. See [OD11008](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11008) and the [parser/flush trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-array-syntax-error-report-flush-od11008). Source-only; no report was sent.
**OD11009 — Short HID descriptors are parsed past their allocation:** descriptors shorter than the six-byte fixed header are logged but parsing continues, reading the descriptor-count field out of bounds and potentially walking beyond the allocation. Conditional on a truncated HID descriptor reaching the class. See [OD11009](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11009) and the [function-level bounds pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-short-descriptor-bounds-pass-od11009). Source-only; no transfer was run.
**OD11010 — RTL8139 link-down can bypass S2_OFFLINE cleanup:** the interrupt path clears `IFF_UP`, which the offline handler uses to decide whether to stop the unit. A carrier return can re-enable Tx/Rx despite administrative offline; if online arrives before that link-up state update, restart can overwrite and leak the old DMA-buffer pointers. See [OD11010](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11010) and the [link/offline ordering review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8139-link-offline-restart-refinement-od11010). Source-only; no NIC or request was run.

**OD11011 — USB MassStorage narrows allocated unit numbers to eight bits:** the persistent identity cache assigns 32-bit unit ranges but never reclaims them; each worker stores `base + LUN` through a `uint8_t`. After enough distinct multi-LUN identities have accumulated, IDs wrap. Reattaching an earlier cached identity while a later wrapped identity is active republishes both sets with duplicate IDs, and Open returns the first match. Scoped to selected Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 USB MassStorage packages. See [OD11011](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11011) and the [unit-number width and reattachment trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-unit-number-width-pass-od11011). No USB device or build was exercised.
**OD11024 — USB MassStorage cache aliases simultaneously active devices with identical descriptors:** after the first device's cache entry is published, a later same-model device without a serial descriptor matches that active entry, publishes no distinct LUNs, and shares its numeric unit IDs; device Open resolves those IDs to the first matching active unit. Selected Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 packages; requires matching USB identity strings. Simultaneous discovery on separate controllers may bypass this exact path and remains an unconfirmed race. See [OD11024](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11024) and the [cache identity and construction-order trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od11024-usb-massstorage-duplicate-identity-construction-order).
**OD9575 — BCM PCI indexed configuration windows can select the wrong function under SMP:** the shared index/data sequence is protected only by local-CPU `Disable()`/`Enable()`, so concurrent config calls through one bridge on separate CPUs can redirect a read or write. Applies to BCM2711 and BCM2712 PCI HIDDs on ExecSMP; requires overlapping calls through the same bridge instance. The source caller census did not establish an in-tree overlapping caller pair, so platform occurrence remains unproven. See [OD9575](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9575) and the [indexed-window SMP pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L22054). Source-only; no PCI operation or hardware was exercised.
**OD11025 — BCM2712 PCI `MapPCI()` does not bound the requested span to its outbound window:** only the start address is checked, then the entire caller length is mapped; a crossing tail can address outside the PCI window. Scoped to the selected Raspberry Pi 5/BCM2712 PCI HIDD; in-tree MSI-X callers depend on BAR/window placement. See [OD11025](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11025) and the [BCM2712 PCI span check](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2712-map-pci-outbound-window-span-od11025). Source-only; no endpoint or mapping was used.
**OD11026 — BCM2712 MSI-X setup can leave the endpoint Function Mask set:** it enables MSI-X while preserving the capability-wide mask, then reports success; the selected RP1 caller accepts the returned interrupt IDs and attaches xHCI even though the endpoint remains masked. Scoped to selected `pcibcm2712` when firmware or prior device state leaves that bit set. See [OD11026](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11026) and the [MSI-X vector setup/release pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2712-msi-msix-vector-setup-release-od11026). Source-only; no endpoint or interrupt was used.
**OD2988 — PCI BAR sizing uses only the low dword for 64-bit apertures of 4 GiB or larger:** the generic PCI HIDD reports truncated/zero sizes, and BCM2712's trained-link endpoint setup can leave a large BAR0 unassigned. See [OD2988](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2988) and the [PCI BAR sizing trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L1477). Source-only; no BAR was probed.
**OD11012 — USB MassStorage uses the last LBA as a sector count and cylinder number:** READ CAPACITY(10) supplies a last LBA, but `TD_GETGEOMETRY` reports it as the total sector count and the whole-disk BootNode puts it in `DE_HIGHCYL`. FAT multiplies that cylinder value by heads and sectors per track, producing an inflated or wrapped extent. Scoped to selected Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 MassStorage builds and the whole-disk FAT fallback. See [OD11012](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11012) and the [capacity-to-DosEnvec trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-last-lba-geometry-unit-pass-od11012). No device or filesystem operation was run.
**OD11058 — USB MassStorage decodes READ CAPACITY with a signed left shift:** `capacity[0] << 24` is evaluated as signed `int`; a returned last-LBA high byte of `0x80` or above overflows that type and makes the expression undefined before assignment to `uint32_t`. A compiler may still emit the expected bit pattern, so resulting capacity errors are implementation-dependent. Scoped to USB MassStorage devices reporting at least 2^31 blocks. See [OD11058](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11058) and the [capacity decode trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-read-capacity-signed-shift-od11058). Source-only; no device or build was used.
**OD11059 — USB MassStorage splits large writes with the wrong data pointer and length:** each WRITE CDB covers at most 1,024 blocks, but its BOT data phase uses the original buffer and full request length; later chunks also reuse the first buffer address. Writes above 1,024 blocks therefore mismatch command and payload, and the DirectSCSI path ignores the data-transfer result. Scoped to selected USB MassStorage builds when a caller submits a larger TrackDisk write. See [OD11059](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11059) and the [READ/WRITE chunking trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-write-chunking-buffer-length-od11059). No device or write was run.
**OD11060 — USB MassStorage narrows TrackDisk transfer counts to 16 bits:** a 32-bit byte length becomes a 32-bit sector count, then the HIDD API truncates it to `uint16_t`; an exact 65,536-sector request reaches the transfer loop as zero, performs no I/O, and is reported complete. Other oversized requests transfer only their low 16-bit count. Applies to both 32-bit and 64-bit TrackDisk read/write vectors on selected USB MassStorage builds. See [OD11060](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11060) and the [transfer-count narrowing trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-trackdisk-count-narrowing-od11060). No device or I/O request was run.
**OD11061 — USB MassStorage derives its block shift from the least set bit, assuming every reported block size is a power of two:** a device reporting 520-byte blocks is treated as 8-byte blocks, turning a one-block request into 65 SCSI blocks and a 33,800-byte transfer. Scoped to selected MassStorage builds with a non-power-of-two block-size device. See [OD11061](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11061) and the [capacity-to-I/O trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-nonpoweroftwo-blocksize-od11061). No device, request, I/O or build was used.

**OD11062 — USB MassStorage logs the uninitialized eight-byte READ CAPACITY buffer when the CBW transfer fails:** the source enables `DEBUG` and emits all eight local bytes even when `DirectSCSI()` returns before the data phase. See [OD11062](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11062) and the [failure-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-read-capacity-failure-debug-buffer-od11062). No device, transfer, debug console or build was used.
**OD11222 — RTL8029 failed unit discovery clears an out-of-range unit slot:** `InitializeUnit()` reaches cleanup with a zeroed, unnamed unit when no board is found; cleanup subtracts `'0'` from that zero byte and writes through a negative `dd_Units[]` index, outside the device-base allocation. Scoped to selected RTL8029 builds and opens for units with no matching hardware. See [OD11222](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11222) and the [failed-discovery cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8029-failed-unit-discovery-cleanup-od11222). No device or build was used.
**OD11223 — RTL8029 never releases Prometheus board ownership:** last-close cleanup frees the unit without releasing the PCI device obtained by `FindHardware()`. The board remains unavailable to later claimants. If another client keeps Prometheus loaded while RTL8029 expunges, its board record also retains a pointer to the freed device base; if Prometheus expunges too, its cleanup frees that wrapper without releasing the HIDD owner. See [OD11223](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11223) and the [board-owner lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8029-prometheus-owner-release-od11223). No board or device operation was run.
**OD11224 — RTL8029 uses a board when its Prometheus ownership claim fails:** `FindHardware()` ignores the zero result from `Prm_SetBoardAttrsTags()` and returns the board I/O base, so initialization can reset/program a PCI device already owned by another client. Conditional on a competing owner of a matching board; no in-tree competing owner was found. See [OD11224](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11224) and the [board-claim result trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8029-prometheus-owner-claim-od11224). No board or device operation was run.
**OD11225 — Prometheus releases the PCI device attribute base twice:** library cleanup releases `IID_Hidd_PCIDevice` for both stored bases, leaving the acquired `IID_Hidd_PCIDriver` reference unreleased and potentially consuming another client's device-base reference. See [OD11225](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11225) and the [attribute-base teardown trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#prometheus-attribute-base-release-od11225). No library load or expunge was run.
**OD11226 — PCI ATA failure cleanup frees an interrupt-registration object twice:** after `HIDD_PCIDevice_AddInterrupt()` rejects the handler, the constructor frees the allocation but retains its pointer; the ensuing dispose path unregisters and frees that stale pointer. Scoped to probed PCI ATA buses whose interrupt registration fails. See [OD11226](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11226) and the [constructor/dispose trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pci-ata-interrupt-registration-failure-cleanup-od11226). Source-only; no device or interrupt operation was run.
**OD11013 — DOSBoot can drop the disk BootNode when partition registration produces no replacement:** partition-table open success is treated as registration success, so the source whole-disk node is removed even if every partition is skipped or node creation fails. Confirmed on Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI package routes with selected SDCard/NVMe/VirtIO whole-disk node producers. See [OD11013](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11013) and the [boot-scan target/provider trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dosboot-partition-scan-targetprovider-matrix-for-od11013-scope-narrowed-no-new-finding-or-bodypathloc-credit-2026-11-01). No partition table or allocation failure was used.
**OD3547 — HID analog joystick scaling overflows signed `LONG`:** a 32-bit axis value can overflow when rebased and shifted eight bits before normalization. Covers optional Bluetooth HID and the explicitly selected ROM USB HID class; both install analog joystick mappings for X/Y usages. See [OD3547](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3547) and the [USB action-path recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od3547-usb-hid-analog-joystick-normalization-recheck). Source-only; no descriptor or report was used.

**OD9466 — Bluetooth HID default joystick thresholds overflow for wide ranges:** the default Game Pad/Joystick mapper computes quarter-range cutoffs using signed `LONG` arithmetic; for logical bounds 0..0x7fffffff, adding one to the span overflows before the thresholds are saved. This affects the generated digital direction actions; OD3547 separately covers the analog scaling operation. Scoped to the optional Bluetooth HID class when no saved action overrides the mapper. See [OD9466](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9466). No descriptor or report was used; source-only.
**OD3459 — HID saved action configuration can load partially after allocation failure:** Bluetooth HID and Poseidon's USB HID can skip saved actions or string data yet report success, suppressing default mappings. See [OD3459](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3459) and its [USB loader trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-saved-action-load-allocation-failure-od11005). Source-only; no allocation failure or configuration was used.
**GD10526 — Radeon cursor visibility and mode activation can race:** cursor visibility updates the hardware bit and shared `cursorVisible` state without the Radeon `HWLock`, while display activation takes the lock and reapplies that state. A concurrent pointer change and activation can leave hardware and software state inconsistent. Scoped to explicit `hidd-radeon` builds; concurrency is conditional. See [GD10526](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10526) and the [Radeon cursor lock trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#radeon-cursor-visibility-and-display-activation-lock-trace-gd10526). Source-only; no interleaving or build was run.
**GD10527 — Radeon cursor positioning overflows at the minimum signed x coordinate:** for x = -32768, negating into a `WORD` cannot represent 32768, and the horizontal register expression may left-shift a negative signed value. Scoped to explicit `hidd-radeon` builds and callers that supply the boundary through `MoveSprite()` or the HIDD method; a maintained Intuition pixel-position route is possible if selected screen geometry permits that coordinate. See [GD10527](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10527) and the [cursor coordinate trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#radeon-cursor-word-min-coordinate-trace-gd10527). Source-only; no cursor call or build was run.

**GD10528 — `MUIO_ImageButton` truncates long image paths:** the helper validates the full path with `Lock()`, then ignores `strlcat()` truncation while building a fixed 512-byte image spec; the image class later loads the shortened path. Affects public MUI callers with paths over 509 bytes; maintained callers use short fixed paths, so in-tree reachability is not established. See [GD10528](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10528) and the [path-length trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-imagebutton-path-length-recheck-gd10528). Source-only; no path or GUI was exercised.

**EK10351 — `NewCreateTaskA()` reads a nonexistent name entry for unnamed tasks:** if both `TASKTAG_NAME` and `TASKTAG_TASKMSGPORT` are omitted, the allocation contains only Task and stack entries, but the constructor still reads `ml_ME[2].me_Addr` into `tc_Node.ln_Name`. The ARM-native SMP processor probe does this for secondary CPUs; an optional m68kemu bridge also forwards guest task tags without adding either tag. A nonzero uninitialized value bypasses NewAddTask's NULL-name fallback and may be dereferenced by later name lookup. See [EK10351](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10351) and the [allocation/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#newcreatetaska-unnamed-task-entry-read-ek10351). No task or build was run; source-only.
**GD10529 — AmigaVideo `UpdateRect()` leaves cached pixels unwritten:** `PutPixel()` queues planar writes, but both the bitmap update method and selected AmigaVideo compositor rectangle-change method are empty. A later `ChangeVPBitMap()`—including the maintained `ChangeScreenBuffer()` route when given a caller-supplied same-layout classic bitmap—can replace the wrapped planes before the cache drains, causing the queued pixel to be lost from the old bitmap and written into the new one on a later flush. Scoped to selected m68k Amiga AmigaVideo HIDD bitmaps; disposal or buffer switching before another flush is required. See [GD10529](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10529), the [update-boundary trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-pixel-cache-update-boundary-gd10529), and the [buffer-swap caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-pixel-cache-changevpbitmap-trace-gd10529). Source-only; no draw, swap or build was run.
**GD10530 — AmigaVideo pixel-cache mask shifts signed `1` into bit 31:** a valid write at cache slot 31 reaches `1 << 31`, undefined for signed `int`; if the high mask bit is not set, the subsequent cache flush skips the pixel. Scoped to selected m68k Amiga AmigaVideo bitmaps; compiler manifestation is unverified. See [GD10530](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10530) and the [cache-mask trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-pixel-cache-mask-bit31-gd10530). Source-only; no build or pixel operation was run.
**EK19 — Boot panic formatting can overrun its fixed buffer:** the selected Unix and Android panic formatters append unbounded `vsprintf()` output after a fixed header; selected host error strings are passed without a local length bound, though a string long enough to overrun the 1,024-byte buffer is not established. See [EK19](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek19) and the [Android caller/header recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#android-kernel-alert-header-ek19-recheck). Source-only; no host error or boot was induced.
**GD10531 — nested `ObtainGIRPort()` on a different layer skips that layer's clip/scroll setup:** the shared `BackupLayerContext.nestcount` is nonzero during a nested cross-layer acquisition, so it skips clearing that layer's clip region and scroll offsets. Scoped to public/custom gadget clients that nest renders across layers; no checked-in reproducer was found. See [GD10531](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10531) and the [GIRPort nesting trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#girport-nested-layer-context-gd10531). Source-only; no nested render or build was run.

**GD10532 — V3D can use BO addresses inconsistent with MMU state:** partial page-table/scratch allocation makes mapping trust an uninstalled table; allocation failure can also leave a previously enabled firmware MMU active while the fallback masks addresses. Scoped to optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 hidd-v3d; the firmware-state branch depends on board startup state. See [GD10532](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10532) and the [hardware-service source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-source-order-and-mm-mapping-findings-gd10532-gd10533). Source-only.
**GD10538 — V3D recovery can orphan successful MMU scratch allocations:** page-table allocation failure with scratch success leaves a live scratch block; retry overwrites its handle, and session cleanup cannot reclaim the pinned arena. Scoped to optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 hidd-v3d recovery after a GPU hang. See [GD10538](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10538) and the [V3D hardware-service source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-source-order-and-mm-mapping-findings-gd10532-gd10533). Source-only.

**GD10533 — V3D submission sequence wrap skips overlay completion waits:** the persistent 32-bit submission counter wraps to zero, which the wait helper treats as “no sequence”; queue readiness also uses non-wrap-safe ordering. Scoped to optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 hidd-v3d after 2^32 accepted submissions. See [GD10533](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10533) and the [hardware-service source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-source-order-and-mm-mapping-findings-gd10532-gd10533). Source-only.

**GD10534 — TextEditor leaks a temporary export-state record on output allocation failure:** after the hook allocates its `Buffer` record, failure of the initial output allocation leaks it; failure of a grown output allocation leaks it when it occurs on a non-final line. A final-line growth failure is cleaned up. Info is one selected caller. Small leak per failed attempt; no failure was induced. See [GD10534](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10534) and the [ExportHook coverage pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-exporthook-full-body-and-export-caller-pass-gd9992-corrected-and-gd10534).

**GD10535 — Info leaks the allocated TextEditor export string for an empty tooltype list:** the default editor export returns a non-NULL empty buffer, but `BuildToolTypes()` deletes its pool and returns without freeing that buffer. Saving an icon with an empty tooltype editor leaks one export buffer. This differs from GD6043's actual export-failure path. See [GD10535](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10535) and the [Info/TextEditor export coverage pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-exporthook-full-body-and-export-caller-pass-gd9992-corrected-and-gd10534). Source-only; no save was run.
**GD10536 — Nouveau destroys an MST manager after initialization fails:** the manager pointer is published before topology-manager initialization, and a later encoder teardown unconditionally destroys it even when helper initialization returned early. A workqueue or topology-state allocation failure can leave work items or the DRM private object uninitialized. Scoped to explicit optional Nouveau builds with a non-eDP MST output and later teardown. See [GD10536](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10536) and the [display/MST initialization trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv50-display-full-body-and-mst-init-failure-gd10536). Source-only; no allocation failure or teardown was run.


**[EK10354](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10354) — Graphics manual thunks are registered at the wrong vectors:** `ScrollRaster` shadows `ReadPixel` at LVO 318 and `SetABPenDrMd` shadows `GetBPen` at LVO 864; calls to the two intended functions fall through to zero-return handling at their actual offsets. Scoped to the optional m68kemu library. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10354) and [vector reconciliation](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#graphics-m68kemu-manual-vector-reconciliation-ek10354). Source-only; no guest call or build was run.

**[EK10355](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10355) — m68kemu omits the public Graphics `WeighTAMatch()` vector:** LVO 804 has a native implementation but no manual or generated thunk, so guest calls return zero instead of the font-match score. No maintained guest caller was found. Scoped to optional m68kemu. See the [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10355) and [Graphics vector reconciliation](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#graphics-m68kemu-manual-vector-reconciliation-ek10354). Source-only; no guest call or build was run.

**OD11014 — DOSBoot can divide by zero on an RDB partition with zero cylinder geometry:** the RDB handler accepts the partition DosEnvec without validating its surfaces or blocks per track, then DOSBoot computes their product and uses it as a modulo divisor. A checksum-valid RDB entry with a DosType and either field zero can fault the startup partition scan. Confirmed package routes include Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI. See [OD11014](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11014) and the [partition geometry data-flow review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dosboot-rdb-zero-geometry-modulo-pass-od11014). No table or boot was used.

**OD11015 — RTL8029 unit-open cleanup hangs or leaks after partial worker startup:** if the worker cannot create its public message port, cleanup waits forever for a lifetime-port reply the worker never sends. If `CreateNewProc()` itself fails, cleanup leaks the lifetime port and signal already allocated. Scoped to the optional RTL8029 device target. See [OD11015](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11015) and the [startup-timeout cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8029-startup-timeout-cleanup-od11015). No task, allocation failure or device open was run.

**OD11016 — ISA PnP nonblocking multi-lock failure can corrupt a semaphore and strand earlier locks:** both card and device lock helpers have a stray semicolon after their rollback loop, so failure releases the semaphore that was not acquired and leaves earlier locks held after freeing the only result handle. This is scoped to the explicitly enabled optional ISA PnP resource and external/future nonblocking callers; it is disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11016](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11016) and the [multi-lock rollback caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-nonblocking-multilock-od11016). No contention or resource build was run.
**OD11017 — ISA PnP device allocation failure crashes during cleanup:** if the device structure is allocated but its initial resource-group allocation fails, cleanup drains an uninitialized zeroed resource list and `RemHead()` dereferences its NULL head. Scoped to explicitly enabled `kernel-isapnp`; disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11017](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11017) and the [allocation cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-device-allocation-cleanup-pass-od11017). No allocation failure or build was induced; source-only.**
**OD11018 — ISA PnP multi-lock sorting uses undefined pointer subtraction:** `ComparePtr()` subtracts pointers to separately allocated objects and narrows the result to `int`; valid multi-object calls therefore lack a portable, guaranteed ordering, which can undermine consistent lock order. Scoped to explicit `kernel-isapnp`; no checked-in caller passes multiple objects. See [OD11018](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11018) and the [sort and lock-array review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-pointer-ordering-review-od11018). No multi-object lock or build was run; source-only.**
**OD11019 — ISA PnP silently ignores memory-range descriptors:** the parser consumes `PNPISA_RDN_MEMORY_RANGE` as unknown data, so conflict selection and configuration omit the memory requirement while `ProgramConfiguration()` can still activate the device without writing memory registers. Scoped to explicitly enabled `kernel-isapnp`; disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11019](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11019) and the [memory-resource configuration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-memory-resource-configuration-od11019). No hardware or build was used; source-only.**
**OD11020 — ISA PnP retains partial resources after an alternative allocation fails:** if allocation fails after some resource records were appended, the selector tries later alternatives without rolling back the prefix. A later successful selection can then program the failed option’s entries along with the chosen one. Scoped to explicitly enabled `kernel-isapnp`; disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11020](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11020) and the [alternative-resource rollback trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-alternative-resource-allocation-od11020). No allocation failure or build was induced; source-only.**
**OD11021 — ISA PnP I/O range search wraps past `0xFFFF`:** a conflicting last candidate wraps the 16-bit iterator base to zero, which may be accepted outside the descriptor and disables the I/O range when programmed; repeated wraps can also prevent configuration search from terminating. Scoped to explicit `kernel-isapnp`; disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11021](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11021) and the [I/O range exhaustion trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-io-range-wrap-od11021). No resource or build was used; source-only.**


**EK10356 — OpenSBI's early FDT parser does not bound structure tokens, node names, or property values:** a truncated or inconsistent structure can make startup read beyond its declared extent before EFI/default fallback. See [EK10356](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10356) and the [structure-extent audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#opensbi-fdt-structure-extent-pass-ek10356). No FDT or boot was used.
**EK10357 — AArch64 `KrnMapGlobal()` can leave partial mappings after reporting allocation failure:** the range walker publishes earlier 2 MiB entries before a later table allocation fails; selected BCM2711/BCM2712/RP1 DMA allocators can then free backing memory and BCM2712 PCI mapping can return failure without rollback. See [EK10357](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10357) and the [AArch64 mapping failure/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#aarch64-global-map-partial-allocation-failure-and-v3d-arena-cleanup-ek10357). Source-only; no mapping or allocation failure was induced.


**D34 — DOS64 position operations fail on NTFS because unsupported 64-bit packets return `DOSFALSE` with no error:** `Seek64()` and `GetFilePosition64()` treat the zero-error response as a valid 64-bit query and do not fall back to ordinary `ACTION_SEEK`, which NTFS supports. Applies when the optional NTFS handler is installed alongside dos64.library. See [D34](AROS-dos.md#d34). Source-only; no seek or NTFS volume was used.

**D35 — DOS64 reports file-size changes successful on read-only NTFS:** the handler returns the positive `ERROR_DISK_WRITE_PROTECTED` value in `dp_Res1`, but DOS64 treats any non-`DOSFALSE` change result as success. `ChangeFileSize64()` reports true; `SetFileSize64()` also returns a non-error value, with its result additionally affected by D36. Applies when dos64.library is used with the optional NTFS handler. See [D35](AROS-dos.md#d35). No resize or NTFS volume was used.

**D36 — NTFS returns the address of its file-size field to DOS64:** `ACTION_GET_FILE_SIZE64` sets `dp_Res1` to `&fl->gl->size`, while DOS64 interprets `dp_Res1` as the size value. `GetFileSize64()` therefore returns an address-like value (truncated on 32-bit packet transport); `SetFileSize64()` inherits the bad query result. Applies when dos64.library is used with the optional NTFS handler. See [D36](AROS-dos.md#d36). No query or volume was used.

**GD10537 — SDL may dispatch through disposed keyboard/mouse HIDD objects during startup failure:** the event task outlives input-object cleanup, but whether host SDL can deliver an event before video setup is not established in this checkout. Retained as a conditional candidate for the optional hosted SDL HIDD. See [GD10537](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10537) and the [SDL event lifecycle review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sdl-event-task-startup-input-object-disposal-pass-gd10537). No registration failure or event was induced; source-only.
**EK8837 — pthread accepts stack sizes below `PTHREAD_STACK_MIN`, including zero:** a zero size with no custom stack is accepted but causes `pthread_create()` to omit `NP_StackSize` and use the default; a positive undersized custom stack reaches below-bound argument writes in the selected x86-64 `NewStackSwap()`. Applies to builds selecting the pthread link library, with the concrete write traced on x86-64. See [EK8837](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8837) and the [pthread stack attribute recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-stack-attribute-zero-size-recheck-ek8837-strengthened-2026-11-01). No thread or stack switch was run; source-only.
**OD4006 — Sam440 serial HIDD overwrites its IRQ vector and adjacent unit pointers:** `GetIRQs(int *)` writes four PPC32 integers through a four-byte `UBYTE` IRQ array, corrupting the IRQ bytes and the first three unit-pointer slots before registration. Scoped to explicit builds of the optional Sam440 serial HIDD after its compile errors are fixed. See [OD4006](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4006) and the [IRQ-array reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sam440-serial-irq-array-and-handler-context-reconciliation-od4006-od4008). No IRQ or build was run.
**OD4008 — Sam440 serial IRQ handlers keep pre-unit context:** the library init hook registers handlers before serial.device creates HIDD unit objects, and does not re-register them later. The current IRQ-array overrun also corrupts three context slots; correcting only that overrun still leaves stale pre-unit data. Scoped to explicit optional-target use after compile blockers are fixed. See [OD4008](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4008) and the [IRQ-array reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sam440-serial-irq-array-and-handler-context-reconciliation-od4006-od4008). Handler-data mapping and runtime behavior were not exercised.
**OD2536 — Serial HIDDs advertise baud rates their setters reject and can ignore the built-in 9600 preference:** the Sam440 constructor also passes legacy selector value 5 to a setter requiring 50 or more, ignores the failure, and serial.device publishes the unit without retrying the configured rate. The Sam440 extension is limited to explicit use after its existing compile errors are fixed; it is absent from the checked default package. See [OD2536](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2536) and the [Sam440 baud preference recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sam440-default-baud-preference-recheck-od2536). No serial I/O or build was run.
**OD2509 — Direct serial-unit construction can index beyond the four supported ports:** PC and Sam440 expose `CLID_Hidd_SerialUnit` Root.New paths that accept caller unit IDs beyond 0–3 before indexing `bases[]`; the factory guards only protect serial.device-created units. The Sam440 case is gated on fixing its current compile errors and is not in the checked default package. See [OD2509](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2509) and the [Sam440 constructor bounds pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sam440-direct-serial-unit-root-new-bounds-pass-od2509). No object or build was used.

**OD11022 — ISA PnP greedily rejects valid resource lists:** a later descriptor can conflict with an earlier descriptor's first candidate, causing list construction to fail before it backtracks to another valid base. A failed base list makes card configuration fail. Scoped to optional `kernel-isapnp`, disabled in the checked-in i386 PC package. See [OD11022](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11022) and the [iterator/backtracking pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#isapnp-iterator-full-body-and-internal-list-backtracking-od11022). No card or build was used.


**GD10539 — DoGadgetMethodA drops inherited RastPort pen state during GM_RENDER:** reusable rendering RastPort initializes `FgPen`/`BgPen` defaults and copies only layer/bitmap/font, unlike the prior full RastPort clone. Custom render methods that rely on inherited pens can draw with incorrect colors. See [GD10539](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10539) and the [DoGadgetMethodA render RastPort review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dogadgetmethoda-render-rastport-pen-state-pass-gd10539-added). Source-only; no rendering test was run.
**Graphics/Desktop progress (2026-11-01):** reread the complete WBRename source and reconciled the recent WBNewDrawer/ExecuteStartup passes with older findings. The WBNewDrawer observation duplicated GD6042; the two ExecuteStartup observations duplicated GD6068 and GD6069. Removed duplicate IDs GD10540-GD10542. Rechecked WBRename's GD6036-GD6041 and expanded GD6039 to include the borrowed device-name pointer used after releasing the DOS-list lock. Verified that the volume/device filter flags release the same shared DOS-list semaphore, so the mismatched filter spelling does not establish a separate lock leak. See the [Graphics/Desktop report](AROS-graphics-desktop.md) and [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No GUI, filesystem operation, DOS-list mutation or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Graphics/Desktop progress (2026-11-01):** read the complete Clock utility bodies and local headers (193 C/header code lines) and traced its argument, catalog and MUI lifecycle. Its unchecked window-open result is already covered by GD10451; no separate issue was established. Clock is an explicitly buildable optional target whose parent aggregate edge is commented. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No GUI, argument parse, catalog open or build was run; source-only.

**Graphics/Desktop progress (2026-11-01):** completed source-order review of the four C files and four selected local headers in the build-selected ExecuteCommand tool (483 C/header code lines); no independent finding established. Traced asynchronous stream and search-path ownership into the selected DOS and Workbench APIs. The coverage ledger has the per-file body credits and active Workbench target dependency. No build, command, process or GUI was run; source-only.
**GD10544 — Workbook dereferences a missing GadTools VisualInfo during window construction:** `GetVisualInfo()` may return NULL on allocation failure, but Workbook passes it directly to `LayoutMenus()`, which dereferences it; the failed construction also bypasses menu/window cleanup. Scoped to the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-system-workbook` target. See [GD10544](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10544) and the [VisualInfo failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#workbook-gadtools-visual-info-failure-gd10544). Source-only; no allocation failure or GUI operation was run.


**GD5859 expanded — Wanderer multiline label splitting can measure past the NUL after skipping leading spaces:** the proportional/kerned `TextLength()` path reads the explicit count; coverage now includes the exact-size AppIcon and drawer-name caller routes, while GD9402 is withdrawn as a duplicate. See [GD5859](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5859) and the [IconList split-label trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-iconlist-leading-space-split-textlength-overread-gd5859). Source-only; no label or GUI was exercised.
**GD10547 — VulkanProbe can miss a compute queue after family 16:** it caps the reported family count at 16 and searches only that prefix, so a device with a later compute family is falsely reported as having none. Scoped to the explicitly buildable diagnostic target; occurrence depends on the device family layout. See [GD10547](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10547) and the [Probe queue-family bound recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-queue-family-prefix-bound-gd10547). Source-only; no device or build was exercised.

**GD10548 — VulkanProbe can mislabel a different GPU as the 9060:** if the requested ID is not found, it tries `physdev[0]` but emits a success line naming the 9060. Its eight-device enumeration also accepts `VK_INCOMPLETE` without retrying, so a later 9060 can be missed. Scoped to the optional diagnostic target and a successful device-zero compute path. See [GD10548](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10548) and the [Probe fallback-identity recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-fallback-device-identity-gd10548). Source-only; no device or build was exercised.
**GD10543 — WBRename can overflow its 128-byte relabel-path buffer:** volume or device names of 127 bytes or more are concatenated with `strcat()` without bounds checks; DOS `MakeDosEntry()` does not impose a shorter maximum. Scoped to the build-selected WBRename target and relabeling long-named volumes. See [GD10543](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10543) and the [name-length trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wbrename-relabel-path-buffer-length-pass-gd10543). Source-only; no long-name entry or relabel was used.
**EK10358 — Unix hosted task CPU usage is never sampled:** the selected Unix scheduler accumulates CPU time but does not update `iet_CpuUsage`; `QueryTaskTagList()` returns that field, which SysMon and `C:TaskList` display; SysMon sorting also uses the value. Scoped to Unix-hosted builds running either caller; SysMon is selected by the active `#MM- workbench-system` virtual-target dependency, and `TaskList` is in the common command target. See [EK10358](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10358) and the [writer/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#unix-task-cpu-usage-query-and-sysmon-caller-pass-ek10358). Source-only; no hosted target or GUI was run.
**EK10359 — Generic hosted bootstrap fallback does not compile:** `support.c` omits the semicolon after its `parts` initializer and calls undeclared/unimplemented `join_strings()` instead of `join_string()`. Scoped to explicitly building the generic unoverridden `kernel-bootstrap-hosted` fallback; Unix and MinGW substitute support implementations. See [EK10359](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10359) and the [target-selection trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#generic-hosted-support-fallback-selection-and-buildability-ek10359). No build was run.
**EK10360 — ARM32 SMP processor probes can record the wrong core when affinity-mask allocation fails:** `Processor_Init()` continues after `KrnAllocCPUMask()` returns NULL, and ARM treats the resulting NULL task affinity as “run anywhere.” A probe can therefore write the running core’s MPIDR into another logical CPU’s record, which `Processor_FillTopology()` later publishes under that record’s index. Scoped to selected ARM32/ARMeb ExecSMP processor-resource initialization, with the wrong mapping conditional on allocation failure and cross-core scheduling. See [EK10360](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10360) and the [probe affinity trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#arm-processor-probe-affinity-mask-failure-ek10360). Source-only; no allocation failure or boot was induced.
**EK9472 — Hosted and Windows CE bootstrap basename scans can read before pathless names:** hosted Unix and MinGW `namepart()` helpers scan backward without a lower bound; a custom config with a pathless module name reaches the helper when `AROS_MODULES_DEBUG` is disabled. Optional Windows CE also scans bare `argv[0]`/module names. The generic hosted fallback has the same runtime flaw but is currently unbuildable under EK10359. See [EK9472](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9472) and the [basename and target-override trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#generic-hosted-support-fallback-selection-and-buildability-ek10359). Source-only; no bootstrap was run.

**OD11030 — USB Audio programs its endpoint before choosing the actual mix rate:** allocation sends `SET_CUR` with the requested rate, then replaces AHI `MixFreq` with a nearby advertised rate without programming it. A rejected discrete-rate request is logged but allocation succeeds, so playback packet sizing can use a rate the endpoint did not adopt. Scoped to explicitly buildable optional `kernel-usb-classes-usbaudio`. See [OD11030](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11030) and the [allocation-rate ordering trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-audio-endpoint-rate-programming-order-od11030). Source-only; no USB device or transfer was used.
**OD11029 — a stale Bluetooth inquiry completion can finish a newer discovery:** an old `INQUIRY_COMPLETE` event may remain queued while the hardware task handles stop/start control messages first; its handler then clears the new session’s shared active flag. An old command’s five-second timeout callback has the same cross-session effect. Premature finish requires a Classic-only new session with no pending name-resolution work. Scoped to stop/restart overlapping an old queued completion or command timeout. See [OD11029](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11029) and the [cross-session callback trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-inquiry-callback-cross-session-state-od11029). Source-only; no controller or discovery was run.

**OD11028 — AHI_CA omits the mode annotation from its properties list:** the translated properties labels include Annotation and the API provides `getAnnotation()`, but ClassAct fills only six values, so its list ends at Version. Scoped to optional AHI_CA, omitted from the default executable list. See [OD11028](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11028) and the [ClassAct GUI source pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-ca-public-screen-lock-rollback-od11027). Source-only.

**OD4000 — RPiI2S replays stale samples beyond AHI's current mix length:** it DMA-copies the maximum buffer, while the selected AHI mixer clears only the current-size region after a player-frequency change. The remaining tail contains prior or uninitialized data. Scoped to selected ARM/AArch64 RPiI2S with timing enabled and current mix frames below the configured maximum. See [OD4000](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4000) and the [mixer and DMA-buffer trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rpii2s-short-mix-mixer-clear-and-dma-copy-recheck-od4000). Source-only; no stream or hardware was used.


**OD3898 expanded — queued remote-name discovery can submit for a forgotten device and then stall the name queue:** Forget can retire a device after name-resolution nodes are queued but before `bNextNameRequest()` submits; the class retains the object allocation but removes it from the active list and deletes its lock. The later completion cannot find the device and leaves the request slot occupied. This is the same liveness root as the active-request and malformed-completion paths, not a separate finding or a proven freed-memory access. See [OD3898](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3898) and the [Bluetooth name-request coverage trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-discovery-name-queue-retirement-recheck-od3898-expanded). No path or LOC credit changed; source-only.

**Bluetooth hardware-task body coverage (2026-11-01):** completed body review of the manifest-selected `rom/bluetooth/bluetooth/hwtask.c` (3,100 physical lines; 2,613 `cloc 2.06` C code lines). This advances combined Graphics/Desktop, Exec/Kernel and Other Drivers body coverage to **4,691/5,078 entries (92.4%)** and **1,684,205/2,219,811 C/header code lines (75.9%)**, leaving 387 entries and 535,606 lines without full-body credit. Area entries may overlap physical paths. Bluetooth transport-specific behavior, external clients/devices, and broader caller/lifecycle checks remain open. See the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-hwtask-current-file-full-body-reconciliation). Source-only; no device, event, or build was used.

**EK9432 rechecked — Intuition `NextObject()` pointer slot:** reconciled the existing case with the generated thunk and native cursor access: selected little-endian 64-bit hosts use native pointer width/byte order on a 32-bit big-endian guest slot, so iteration state and the adjacent guest word can be corrupted. Caller reachability remains limited to an emulated guest; no new finding was added. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest call or build was run.


**OD2708 expanded — keypad raw-key mismatch also affects optional USB/Bluetooth HID raw-key actions:** the action editors label and inject the mismatched raw codes unchanged, so a keypad `/` action can fire for physical keypad `*` on the affected PC/Linux keyboard paths. This is caller evidence for the same root, not a new finding. See [OD2708](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2708) and the [caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od2708-usb-bluetooth-hid-keypad-action-caller). Source-only.


**BWFM transmit-hook caller check:** traced the selected AROSTCP queued-mbuf path into the BWFM copy hook. It supplies `m_pkthdr.len` alongside that same packet chain; no selected mismatch was established, while external SANA-II caller bounds remain open. See the [caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bwfm-arostcp-tx-buffer-hook-caller-recheck). No new finding or coverage credit. Source-only.


**`GetDataStreamFromFormat()` `%b` width recheck:** the formatter consumes `%b` as an `IPTR` BSTR pointer; `BPTR` is `APTR` or `IPTR` depending on `AROS_FAST_BPTR`, so the packed slot width agrees on both representations. Sparse positional format validity remains unestablished and is not reported as a defect. See the [coverage note](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#getdatastream-bptr-slot-width-target-reconciliation). No new finding or coverage credit. Source-only.


**EK10361 — Workbench `Info` masks initialization failure:** allocation/pool failures print an error and return from `doInfo()`, but `main()` always returns `RETURN_OK`.
