This is separate from EK9060's leaked `InfoData` allocation on pool failure. See [EK10361](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10361) and the [caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#info-command-status-caller-pass-ek10361). Source-only.


**EK10362 — DOSBoot retries indefinitely on persistent VisualInfo allocation failure:** with the early boot menu requested, the failed page returns `-1`, but its loop exits only on page codes 5 or 6. The selected m68k boot path can therefore remain in menu setup instead of continuing boot. See [EK10362](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10362) and the [caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-visualinfo-retry-loop-ek10362). Source-only.


**OD11031 — PC i8042 drops Print Screen/SysRq:** E0 scan `0x37` maps to `NOKEY`, so the key named by `K_Sys_Req` is filtered before keyboard-event dispatch despite the public `RAWKEY_PRTSCREEN` code. See [OD11031](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11031) and the [mapping trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pc-i8042-printscreen-event-map-od11031). Source-only.


**OD11032 — PC i8042 does not recognize standard Scroll Lock:** ordinary `0x46`/`0xC6` scans miss the E0-only lock-state case and map to `NOKEY`; the E0 form toggles software state but also maps to `NOKEY`, so clients receive no raw key. This narrows OD2336, whose signal-mask problem applies only after a lock case is reached. See [OD11032](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11032) and the [scan-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pc-i8042-standard-scrolllock-sequence-od11032). Source-only.

**OD11033 — USB HID keyboard can lose a key press when reports coalesce:** the report callback overwrites shared current/previous state and signals with a bit, so a press and release received before the worker runs collapse into an unmatched release. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional USB HID keyboard class; does not require SMP. See [OD11033](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11033) and the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-keyboard-report-coalescing-od11033). Source-only.

**EK10363 — Concurrent `Cause()` calls can corrupt an ExecSMP soft-interrupt queue:** the already-queued check is outside the per-priority spinlock and is not repeated under it. Two CPUs can append one node twice, self-linking it so dispatch can repeatedly invoke the same callback and stall that priority list. Scoped to ExecSMP-enabled x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi SMP configurations when the same interrupt object is caused concurrently. Optional USB Audio has two maintained `Cause()` callers for the same player interrupt across output-request and release hooks. Synchronous stop does not join a completion callback on another CPU, so overlap during device removal is a possible in-tree trigger on optional ExecSMP USB builds; its timing remains conditional. See [EK10363](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10363) and the [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cause-smp-duplicate-enqueue-ek10363). Source-only.

**OD9889 expanded — SiS900 leaks descriptor rings and per-open TX/RX packet buffers:** each accepted shared open allocates new buffers, close drains without freeing them, and unit deletion omits both packet buffers and descriptor rings; early ring setup returns also bypass cleanup. Scoped to selected SiS900 builds on shared opens, expunge, or ring setup failure. See [OD9889](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9889) and the [ring allocation and cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sis900-ring-ownership-follow-up-od9889-expanded). Source-only; no device lifecycle or allocation failure was run.

**OD11034 — VIA Rhine dereferences a failed unit-name allocation:** `CreateUnit()` passes an unchecked `AllocVec()` result to `sprintf()` during PCI enumeration. Scoped to an explicitly built normal/debug VIA Rhine module when a matching card is found and name allocation fails; default inclusion is not claimed. See [OD11034](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11034) and the [constructor/expunge trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#viarhine-unit-name-allocation-and-expunge-ownership-od11034-od11036). Source-only; no allocation failure or enumeration was run.

**OD11035 — VIA Rhine leaks its allocated unit name:** `DeleteUnit()` frees the unit but never the `AllocVec()`-owned name, on expunge and constructor cleanup paths. Scoped to explicit VIA Rhine targets when a unit reaches cleanup. See [OD11035](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11035) and the [constructor/expunge trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#viarhine-unit-name-allocation-and-expunge-ownership-od11034-od11036). Source-only; no unit lifecycle was run.

**OD11036 — VIA Rhine debug enumeration dereferences a failed `CreateUnit()` result:** its debug-only log reads unit fields without checking for NULL when BAR mapping, allocation, or startup setup fails. Scoped to the explicitly built debug target with a matching device; default inclusion is not claimed. See [OD11036](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11036) and the [constructor/expunge trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#viarhine-unit-name-allocation-and-expunge-ownership-od11034-od11036). Source-only; no device or failure was exercised.


**OD11037 — USB HID mouse report callbacks can overwrite one another on ExecSMP:** the interrupt callback can be requeued while running and dispatched by a second CPU; overlapping callbacks can read the same ring head and overwrite one slot, losing or mixing input reports. Scoped to explicitly built optional OHCI/UHCI/HID modules on x86-64 PC ExecSMP, not the default boot package. See [OD11037](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11037) and the [dispatch and ring trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-mouse-ring-execsmp-reentrant-callback-od11037). Source-only; no interrupt, device, build, or SMP schedule was run.

**OD11038 — USB HID disposal can free keyboard or mouse state during report processing:** on ExecSMP, disconnect can signal a worker running on another CPU, then free keyboard buffers and the OOP object without waiting. An active report branch continues using that state before checking Ctrl-C at the next wait. The hub task runs at priority 10 after initialization, below the HID workers at 20, so the reported same-CPU reschedule rules out this overlap on uniprocessor systems. Scoped to explicitly built optional USB HID keyboard/mouse and OHCI/UHCI modules on x86-64 PC SMP; default boot inclusion is not claimed. See [OD11038](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11038) and the [disposal/worker trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-dispose-during-report-od11038). Source-only; no device, detach, or worker schedule was run.

**OD11039 — input.device button swapping leaves qualifier state unchanged:** with InputPrefs button swapping enabled, the selected character-map console receives the swapped left/right event code with physical button qualifiers and therefore starts/stops text selection from the wrong logical button. See [OD11039](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11039) and the [InputPrefs/input.device/console event path](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#input-device-swapped-button-qualifier-state-od11039). Source-only; no event or preference change was run.


**OD11040 — USB and Bluetooth HID usage tables contain incorrect displayed labels:** Generic Desktop usage 0x45 repeats the Y-axis label instead of identifying Z, and Keyboard/Keypad usage 0x34 is labeled as backtick/double quote instead of apostrophe/double quote. Both copies feed parser diagnostics and Control GUI labels; no report/action impact established. See [OD11040](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11040) and the [USB-IF table comparison](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-generic-desktop-usage-label-od11040). Source-only; no descriptor or GUI was used.


**OD11041 — USB MassStorage large-block emulation passes unaligned request buffers to `CopyMemQuick`:** a 512-byte request against a 1,024-byte-block device can reach the emulation copy with caller `io_Data` unaligned; m68k 68000/010 `move.l` may fault. See [OD11041](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11041) and the [request/copy contract trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-large-block-unaligned-iobuffer-copyquick-od11041). Source-only; no device or request was exercised.

**OD11042 — USB MassStorage Bulk transport uses `CopyMemQuick()` on an unaligned-capable SCSI command:** a valid byte-aligned `scsi_Command` can be odd, and the packed CBW's CDB field starts at offset 15; a 16-byte Bulk-Only command may fault on m68k 68000/010. See [OD11042](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11042) and the [CDB/copy contract trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-bulk-cdb-copyquick-alignment-od11042). Source-only; no request was exercised.


**GD10549 — MUI Register title counting wraps its signed 16-bit index:** a custom Register with 32,768 or more title pointers can wrap `numitems` negative and read before the title array while seeking its terminator. No maintained large-title caller found. See [GD10549](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10549) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). Source-only; no object or GUI was created.


**GD10224 scope update (2026-11-03):** expanded the borrowed-allocation-callback lifetime candidate from unique deleters to ordinary RAII owners, traced through `Device::allocateMemory()` → `DeviceMemory` storage → `vkFreeMemory`. Cross-checked the Vulkan allocator-lifetime contract: confidence is now high for temporary/short-lived `AllocationCallbacks` structs and remains medium for temporary/short-lived custom dispatchers. The no in-tree caller caveat remains. See [GD10224](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10224) and the [RAII owner allocator-retention pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-raii-owner-allocator-retention-gd10224).


**EK10364 — `NewCreateTaskA()` can accept a smaller stack after size-rounding overflow:** on maintained 4- and 16-byte-alignment targets, a near-4-GiB `TASKTAG_STACKSIZE` can wrap during upward alignment, then be clamped to the architecture's minimum stack size. The legacy `CreateTask()` wrapper forwards its caller's stack size without validation; no checked-in caller supplies a near-limit value. See [EK10364](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10364) and the [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#task-stacksize-align-overflow-ek10364). Source-only; no task was created.

**EK10365 — `CreateIORequest()` can record zero for a successful 65,536-byte allocation:** `size` is `ULONG` but is stored in 16-bit `Message.mn_Length`; `DeleteIORequest()` then calls `FreeMem(ptr, 0)`, which returns without freeing. The optional m68k emulator forwards the guest-supplied size to this API. See [EK10365](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10365) and the [size-width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#deleteiorequest-size-width-ek10365). Source-only; no allocation was run.

**EK10366 — m68k allocation thunks leak native resources if guest-shadow creation fails:** `CreateIORequest()`, `CreateMsgPort()`, graphics allocators, GadTools `CreateMenusA()`, Utility `AllocNamedObjectA()`, and Intuition `LockPubScreen()`/`ObtainGIRPort()` leave native allocations, visitor locks, or layer locks behind when shadow allocation/registration fails; the port case also leaks its signal bit. Four Hyperlayers constructors show the same rollback omission, but a usable guest `Layer_Info` input route is not established (EK9432), so they are excluded from confirmed triggers. See [EK10366](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10366) and the [shadow rollback trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek10366-m68k-creatiorequest-shadow-rollback). Source-only; no guest call or allocation failure was induced.

**EK358 — `WaitForPort` can free a timer request and reply port before timer completion finishes:** Ctrl-C/D cleanup can free a still-queued VBlank request; on ExecSMP, it can also race while the timer interrupt is still executing `ReplyMsg()`/`InternalPutMsg()`. See [EK358](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek358) and the [timer/cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9543). Source-only; no command, timer or interleaving was run.


**EK633 — OpenSBI boot self-tests use unchecked signal allocations and leak a signal when task creation fails:** boot-task signal exhaustion shifts `-1`; on ordinary RV64 lowering the high-bit result truncates to a zero `ULONG` mask, so the optional handshake can wait forever (the shift is undefined in C). The new FPU worker starts with the reserved mask `0xFFFF`, so its unchecked allocation is available on the selected path. If child-task creation fails after allocation, the boot task's signal bit is not released; repeated matching substrings plus repeated creation failures can exhaust its 16 allocatable bits before a later test invocation. Ordinary startup exhaustion was not established. See [EK633](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek633) and the [self-test signal trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L351). Source-only; no signal exhaustion or task failure was induced.

**EK8775 — OpenSBI boot arguments match optional self-test names as substrings:** unrelated values containing `testsched` or `testfpu` start a test, whose worker then sleeps indefinitely. Repeated matches can leave multiple extra tasks. See [EK8775](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8775) and the [self-test dispatch trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L351). Source-only; no bootargs or task was used.


**OD9806 — `FreePotBits()` can erase a newly reacquired POTGO configuration:** the resource clears its allocation mask before clearing shared output state and writing the hardware register. Concurrent same-port `ReadJoyPort()` calls can interleave a reacquisition/configuration in that gap; checked-in debug joystick and optional RocketTool loops provide caller paths, but the overlap remains conditional. See [OD9806](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9806) and the [Potgo caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#potgo-release-reacquire-caller-topology-od9806). Source-only; no interleaving or hardware access was run.


**OD9803 — concurrent `AllocPotBits()` calls can return the same potgo lines:** the free-mask read/compute and reservation write are unprotected. The debug joystick utility and optional RocketTool can call `ReadJoyPort()` from separate tasks on the same port, though duplicate ownership still depends on the allocator interleaving and overlapping use. See [OD9803](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9803) and the [caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#potgo-allocator-same-port-caller-recheck-od9803). Source-only; no interleaving or hardware access was run.


**OD10154 — concurrent m68k `ReadJoyPort()` calls can overwrite each other’s CIA direction state:** each game-controller poll saves and restores the whole CIA direction byte, so a poll on port 0 can clear port 1’s output direction during an overlapping transaction. The debug joystick command and optional RocketTool can run as separate tasks on opposite ports; the timing and controller path remain conditional. See [OD10154](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10154) and the [cross-port caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#lowlevel-cross-port-caller-topology-od10154). Source-only; no task overlap or hardware access was run.


**OD11043 — AGP bus disposal skips superclass cleanup and leaks the temporary object:** `AGP__Root__Dispose()` frees the bridge-class nodes but omits `OOP_DoSuperMethod()`, so the selected optional Nouveau lookup's `OOP_DisposeObject()` never reaches the root allocator. The temporary object and its class object count remain live per lookup. Scoped to explicitly built Nouveau plus AGP HIDD when AGP lookup runs; default-package inclusion is not claimed. See [OD11043](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11043) and the [AGP disposal trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#agp-root-dispose-superclass-leak-od11043). Source-only; no object or bridge operation was run.

**OD11044 — Raspberry Pi USB2OTG shares DATA toggle state across same-number IN and OUT endpoints:** after an odd packet count in one direction, the opposite direction can start with the wrong DATA PID, causing a receiver to discard data as a duplicate; halt-clear also resets both directions. Scoped to Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 USB2OTG builds and devices using same-number non-control endpoints in both directions. See [OD11044](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11044) and the [toggle-state trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb2otg-directional-data-toggle-state-od11044). Source-only; no USB device or transfer was exercised.

**GD10550 — Nouveau drawing can report success after partial acceleration setup failure:** scratch-buffer or NV50/NVC0 2D-object setup failure returns from acceleration initialization without tearing down the channel/push buffer; the HIDD continues in software mode, but Tesla and NVC0 drawing wrappers can still accept the incomplete GPU path and suppress software fallback. Scoped to explicitly enabled Nouveau builds. See [GD10550](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10550) and the [full-body/caller review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv50-exa-full-body-partial-init-caller-pass-gd10550). Source-only; no GPU operation or build was run.

**GD10551 — Nouveau GART image transfer can loop forever when a row exceeds its scratch buffer:** on an explicitly enabled Nouveau HIDD with a non-NULL GART BO smaller than one packed row, upload/download clamp the chunk height to zero; every selected M2MF/copy-engine dispatch route returns success for zero height, so the caller's height never decreases while engine, bitmap and GART locks remain held. See [GD10551](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10551) and the [EXA source/caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-exa-full-body-gart-row-bound-gd10551). Source-only; hardware allocation behavior was not exercised.

**GD10552 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha uploads discard 3D prepare failures:** the GART upload path ignores prepare/validation failures across NV10–NV40, allowing callers to suppress the bitmap superclass fallback and leave a chunk undrawn. See [GD10552](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10552) and the [NV10–NV40 EXA body/caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv10-exa-full-body-alpha-upload-caller-pass). Source-only; no failure or GPU operation was induced.

**GD10553 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha uploads omit GPU-dirty synchronization state:** successful NV10–NV40 GART/3D alpha uploads do not set the bitmap dirty flag; for an already mapped BO, subsequent CPU reads skip the wait and disposal skips the queued-work kick. See [GD10553](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10553) and the [NV10–NV40 EXA body/caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv10-exa-full-body-alpha-upload-caller-pass). Source-only; no mapped bitmap or GPU operation was used.

**GD10554 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha-image upload writes past its GART chunk:** the chunk loop computes a bounded row count, but the conversion/copy call is given the full remaining image height. Large `PutAlphaImage()` requests can write beyond the mapped GART BO before only one chunk is submitted. Scoped to explicitly built Nouveau with NV10–NV40 GPUs and dimensions exceeding the scratch-buffer row capacity. See [GD10554](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10554) and the [NV10–NV40 EXA body/caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv10-exa-full-body-alpha-upload-caller-pass). Source-only; no upload or build was run.
**GD10555 — Generic HIDD alpha blending left-shifts a negative signed value:** the shared alpha helper shifts `alpha * (source - destination)` by eight; with nonzero alpha and a lower source channel the operand is negative, which is undefined in C. Affects generic HIDD alpha-image and JAM1 alpha-template paths in checked-in builds, whose configs do not define `EXACT_ALPHA`. See [GD10555](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10555) and the [generic alpha caller/arithmetic pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14615). Source-only; no blend or build was run.
**GD10556 — `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` ignores `globalalpha`:** the function forwards source pixels unchanged, despite the public contract and its own BUGS note; the explicitly buildable MUI Pixmap class accepts configurable global alpha and passes it through, but it is not applied. See [GD10556](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10556) and the [parameter/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14623). Source-only; no pixel array was rendered.
**GD10557 — MUI Pixmap ignores global alpha on low-depth screens:** its <=8-bit renderer builds a mask from per-pixel alpha alone, then blits without consulting `MUIA_Pixmap_Alpha`; a zero global alpha can still draw opaque source pixels. This is separate from GD10556's truecolor `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` parameter omission. See [GD10557](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10557) and the [low-depth draw-path pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14627). Source-only; no display or draw was run.

**GD10558 — AROS VMM treats a nonresident page-table marker as a pointer:** the table-fault path passes an address derived from a `PAGED_OUT` root descriptor to `MarkPage()`, while the AROS-compiled table-installation block is excluded. This can walk invalid descriptor memory and leave the original page fault unresolved. Optional x86/x86-64 VMM only; practical startup reachability is uncertain because of GD9419. See [GD10558](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10558) and the [table-fault trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#aros-vmm-table-fault-gd10558). Source-only; no VMM fault was run.

**GD9747 — NListtree Move/Exchange can create parent/list cycles:** the class omits descendant checks; the demo's Move/Exchange guards fail, and its KeepStructure Move has no guard. Rendering an affected node can recurse indefinitely through its parent cycle. See [GD9747](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9747) and the [current caller census](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nlisttree-gd9747-move-exchange-caller-census). Source-only; no tree mutation or render was run.
**GD5733 — ChunkyBM alpha-image row skips can overflow signed `WORD`:** source and destination row skips are stored in `WORD`; a valid large row stride can narrow to a negative step and make later rows use the wrong address. Confirmed for RGB16_LE and for BGR032 inherited by the selected Raspberry Pi VCGfx bitmap classes. See [GD5733](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5733) and the [ChunkyBM/VCGfx stride recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14619). Source-only; no bitmap operation or build was run.

**OD11046 — PC keyboard tables emit the wrong Num Lock raw-key code:** standard Num Lock scan `0x45` is translated to `0x5A`/`0xDA` rather than public `RAWKEY_NUMLOCK` `0x6D`/`0xED`. Applies to selected PC i8042 and optional MinGW WINGDI tables. See [OD11046](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11046) and the [lock-key table recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pc-keyboard-numlock-raw-code-od11046). Source-only.
**OD11047 — VCGfx can skip horizontally disjoint same-bitmap copies after DMA failure:** its DMA-failure guard checks vertical aliasing but omits horizontal overlap, so a valid large same-bitmap copy can return before the NEON fallback. Raspberry Pi ARM-native VCGfx only; source-only. See [OD11047](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11047) and the [fallback predicate recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vcgfx-copybox-horizontal-nonoverlap-od11047).

**OD11048 — Bluetooth service-ID allocation failure applies a device-level forced class to a service:** a NULL service ID is interpreted by `btGetForcedBinding()` as a request for the device-level setting. If the device already has a service binding, this can suppress normal class attempts for a newly discovered service. Scoped to Bluetooth SDP or GATT service-ID allocation failure with an existing service binding and a device-level forced-class setting. See [OD11048](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11048) and the [selector recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-sdp-service-id-allocation-failure-selector-recheck-od11048). Source-only.

**OD11049 — x86-64 PCIPC leaves high PCI BAR mappings installed after `UnmapPCI`:** qualifying BARs above 128 GiB receive global mappings, but selected PCIPC inherits an empty `UnmapPCI`; the selected generic `KrnUnmapGlobal` is also a no-op and is not reached by current dispatch. Selected ATA, AHCI, e1000, lpe32002, pcnet32, rtl816x, and sis900 release paths are affected when their BAR range crosses the threshold. Distinct windows can retain mappings and page-table allocations. See [OD11049](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11049) and the [caller-selection trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcipc-above-window-map-unmap-caller-recheck-od11049-expanded). Source-only.

**OD11050 — Android keyboard callback narrows the event pointer to UWORD:** the Android HIDD declares the callback data as 16-bit, then passes an event pointer to keyboard.device. Default warning-as-error mode is expected to reject the build; if suppressed, the consumer dereferences a narrowed address. Scoped to Android `kernel-hidd-androidgfx`. See [OD11050](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11050) and the [callback type trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#android-keyboard-callback-pointer-width-od11050). Source-only; no build or callback was run.

**OD2304 caller recheck (2026-11-01):** enumerated all seven checked-in `OpenDevice("keyboard.device")` callers. They cover input.device, DOSBoot, VMM, PFS3 and optional USB/Bluetooth HID reset handlers; no automatic retry after failed Open was found. OD2304 remains valid, with repeated leak accumulation qualified as requiring a later independent or external open attempt. See the [caller census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#keyboard-device-open-failure-caller-census-od2304).

**GD10559 — Sound.datatype uses an uninitialized MaxPlaySamples result:** continuous AHI playback ignores the fallible `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` result and uses `playsamples` for buffer sizing. A concurrent `AddAudioModes REFRESH` can remove the selected mode after allocation and before the query. See [GD10559](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10559) and the [caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-ahi-attribute-query-failure-gd10559). Source-only; no audio operation was run.
**GD10560 — FTManager GUI can install fonts in the wrong directory after a destination-lock failure:** a failed initial `Fonts:` lock falls through to DOS's boot-process namespace; a failed later destination change leaves the old lock active while the GUI shows the rejected path. The CLI uses an explicit destination and is not in scope. See [GD10560](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10560) and the [destination-lock caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14661). Source-only; no font or file operation was run.
**GD10561 — BHFormat leaks a DOS device-list read lock on a volume without a device entry:** the Workbench GUI path on `RAM:` finds no matching `DLT_DEVICE`, exits without unlocking, and leaves later exclusive DOS-list operations able to wait indefinitely. Optional Workbench Format target only; source-only. See [GD10561](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10561) and the [RAM-volume lock trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#bhformat-volume-handler-dos-list-lock-gd10561).
**GD10562 — QuickPart writes past a 64-byte DOS device-name buffer:** a valid device BSTR of 64 or more characters causes the partition view to write the colon and terminator out of bounds. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10562](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10562) and the [full partition-class review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-class-full-body-review).
**GD5689 — QuickPart loses free-space nodes when ranges merge:** the AddFree helper can leak a merged node/object, and during partition-table scan it can merge a tail spacer into a free node already marked for removal, hiding the tail region. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD5689](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5689) and the [partition-container source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-container-full-body-review).
**GD10563 — QuickPart dereferences a failed selection-region allocation:** selected-partition drawing passes a failed `NewRegion()` result to `OrRectRegion()`. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10563](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10563) and the [full partition-class review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-class-full-body-review).
**GD10564 — QuickPart does not handle failed partition-node allocations:** failure to allocate the initial or inserted bookkeeping node can lead to a NULL dereference; failure to allocate the trailing free-space node omits that region from the UI model. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10564](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10564) and the [partition-container source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-container-full-body-review).

**GD10565 — QuickPart leaves each discovered disk device open once after scanning:** construction opens the device, scan opens the same request again and closes once, and disposal deletes the request without balancing the first open. For AHCI-backed disks this leaks the counted unit use and can leave AHCI teardown waiting for that use to close. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10565](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10565) and the [disk-class lifecycle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-class-full-body-review).
**GD10566 — QuickPart mishandles disk-scan allocation and construction failures:** unchecked message-port, I/O-request, handler-name, and drive-name allocations can lead to NULL dereferences; failed device or superclass construction leaks temporary resources, and failed supplied-name replacement loses the old pointer. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10566](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10566) and the [disk-class lifecycle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-class-full-body-review).

**GD10567 — QuickPart leaks per-disk strings and localization allocations:** each disposed disk object leaves its copied handler/name/display strings, hook, and hook data allocated after normal MUI teardown. Repeated QuickPart launches can accumulate them per discovered disk. Selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; source-only. See [GD10567](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10567) and the [disk-class ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-class-full-body-review).


**EK10367 — m68k GadTools can lose a message when shadow creation fails:** `GT_GetIMsg()` has dequeued it or `GT_PostFilterIMsg()` has consumed its wrapper, but the thunk returns NULL before the guest receives a replyable original message. See [EK10367](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10367) and the [message/shadow trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek10367-gt-getimsg-shadow-failure). Source-only; no guest message or shadow failure was induced.


**EK10368 — m68k GadTools reply paths leak consumed message shadows:** `GT_ReplyIMsg()` and direct `GT_FilterIMsg()`/`GT_PostFilterIMsg()` cycles release or reuse native wrappers without removing their guest shadows; repeated event handling eventually exhausts the fixed shadow table. See [EK10368](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10368) and the [reply-shadow lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek10368-gt-replyimsg-shadow-lifetime). Source-only; no message loop was run.


**EK10369 — m68k `GT_FilterIMsg()` can strand its extended message state on shadow failure:** the native filter allocates or reserves a wrapper before the thunk creates its guest shadow; failure skips required post-filter cleanup. See [EK10369](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10369) and the [filter-shadow trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek10369-gt-filterimsg-shadow-failure). Source-only; no filter call or allocation failure was induced.
**GD10568 — MUI_MakeObject may ignore Menuitem_CopyStrings:** the public flag is declared but ignored; the constructor borrows title/shortcut pointers. This remains a medium-confidence API candidate because the tree has no explicit copy/lifetime contract or checked-in caller. See [GD10568](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10568) and the [contract/caller review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-makeobject-maintained-caller-census-gd10568). Source-only.
**GD10570 — MUI localized NewMenu mode dereferences NULL labels:** optional MiamiPanel passes NULL-labeled menu items with `MUIO_MenustripNM_CommandKeyCheck`; the constructor reads `label[1]` without a NULL check during app construction. See [GD10570](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10570) and the [caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-commandkeycheck-null-label-caller-gd10570). Source-only.
**GD10571 — SMP-SmallPT does not handle startup task/port failures:** a missing main port can fault; failed renderer/worker startup can leave a parent waiting indefinitely for a message or port that will never arrive. Scoped to the optional explicitly buildable test program. See [GD10571](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10571) and the [startup failure pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-startup-failure-gd10571). Source-only; no task or GUI was run.
**GD10572 — SMP-SmallPT leaks a public-screen lock if window opening fails:** it unlocks only after a successful `OpenWindowTags()`, then exits when window creation fails. Scoped to the optional SMP-SmallPT target. See [GD10572](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10572) and the [full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575). Source-only; no window failure was induced.
**GD10573 — SMP-SmallPT mishandles timer.device failure and teardown:** failed `OpenDevice()` leaves `TimerBase` NULL for later `GetSysTime()` calls; successful runs never close the device or free its request/port. Scoped to the optional target. See [GD10573](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10573) and the [full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575). Source-only; no timer operation was run.
**GD10574 — SMP-SmallPT dereferences a failed presentation RastPort allocation:** it writes the bitmap field without checking `CreateRastPort()`'s nullable result. Scoped to the optional target under memory pressure. See [GD10574](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10574) and the [full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**GD10575 — SMP-SmallPT dereferences failed rendering allocations:** unchecked renderer arrays, the shared pixel buffer, and per-worker ports, tile buffer, and message pool can fault before or during rendering; the GUI or renderer can then wait for a message from a worker that has stopped. Scoped to the optional target under memory pressure. See [GD10575](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10575) and the [workspace-allocation recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-workspace-allocation-recheck-gd10575-2026-11-01). Source-only; no allocation failure or build was induced.
**EK8946 — Reset timeout priority demotion can race callback-task teardown:** on ExecSMP, the handler can clear and retire its task between the launcher's pointer check and `SetTaskPri()`'s pre-lock dereference. See [EK8946](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8946) and the [timeout boundary trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#reset-timeout-callback-task-lifetime-ek8946). Source-only.)

**GD10576 — SMP-SmallPT RAYDEPTH can overflow its worker stack-size calculation:** `RAYDEPTH/N` has no upper bound and is used in signed arithmetic before conversion to the worker stack-size tag, causing overflow on x86-64 at 2147443 and above. See [GD10576](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10576) and the [full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575). Source-only; no target run or build.

**GD10577 — SMP-SmallPT parses HEIGHT after its minimum-height clamp:** values under 128 bypass the intended clamp and are rounded down to a 32-pixel multiple by window setup (for example, 127 becomes 96). See [GD10577](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10577) and the [full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575). Source-only; no window was opened.

**EK10577 — SMP-SigRace worker tasks can outlive stack-local state:** timeout and partial-startup returns can leave workers holding `TASKTAG_USERDATA` pointers into phase-local `SigWorker` records after the phase returns. Scoped to explicitly built `test-smp-sigrace` on ExecSMP. See [EK10577](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10577) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-sigrace-full-body-and-timeout-lifetime-pass-ek10577). Source-only; no task or build was run.

**EK10578 — SMP scheduler and I/O tests can leave workers using expired stack records:** partial task-creation failures in SMP-Sched and SMP-DoIO return without stopping previously started workers that retain pointers to phase-local records. Scoped to those explicitly built ExecSMP tests. See [EK10578](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10578) and the [SMP-Sched](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-sched-full-body-and-worker-cleanup-pass-ek10578-ek10579) and [SMP-DoIO](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-doio-full-body-timer-request-pass) passes. Source-only; no build or task was run.
**EK10579 — SMP-Sched priority-wake phase can pass without saturating all CPUs:** its four-slot spinner array and loop cap leave CPUs idle on systems with more than four cores, so the high-priority waiter can run without preempting a busy core. See [EK10579](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10579) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-sched-full-body-and-worker-cleanup-pass-ek10578-ek10579). Source-only; no scheduler run was performed.

**EK10580 — SMP-Sem can leave workers using expired stack records:** partial task-creation failures return while already-started workers retain `TASKTAG_USERDATA` pointers into automatic phase arrays. Scoped to explicitly built SMP-Sem on ExecSMP under allocation/task-creation failure. See [EK10580](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10580) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-sem-full-body-and-partial-startup-lifetime-pass-ek10580). Source-only; no task or build was run.

**EK10581 — SMP-DoIO timeout removal leaves timer requests/resources unsettled:** a timed-out worker can still be in DoIO/WaitIO when the parent removes it, without aborting/draining the request or closing its device/request/port. Scoped to the optional SMP-DoIO timeout path. See [EK10581](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10581) and the [timer request pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-doio-full-body-timer-request-pass). Source-only; no request or task was run.

**EK10582 — SMP-Lists leaks its private library on timeout:** the library-sum phase returns on `collect()` failure without freeing the allocation made by `MakeLibrary()`. Scoped to an explicitly built SMP-Lists timeout. See [EK10582](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10582) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-lists-full-body-and-timeout-cleanup-pass-ek10582). Source-only; no library operation or build was run.

**EK10583 — SMP-Proc can exit successfully after partial or zero child creation:** allocation failure breaks creation, but final status checks only created children and can report `0 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 INVALID`. Scoped to explicit SMP-Proc under process/mask allocation failure. See [EK10583](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10583) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-proc-full-body-result-lifetime-pass-ek10583-ek10584). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK10584 — SMP-Proc and SMP-Affinity children can access parent records after completion is observed:** children set their done flags before the final `Signal()` reads parent/signal fields; parents may return from the phase and free the signal with no child join. See [EK10584](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10584), the [SMP-Proc pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-proc-full-body-result-lifetime-pass-ek10583-ek10584), and the [SMP-Affinity pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-affinity-full-body-lifecycle-pass). Scoped to the stated interleavings on ExecSMP. Source-only; no task was run.

**EK10585 — SMP-Affinity can leave a target spinner running after setup failure:** the target starts before both masks are validated; a failed mask allocation takes an exit path without stopping it, leaving it to use a phase-local record. See [EK10585](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10585) and the [full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#smp-affinity-full-body-lifecycle-pass). Scoped to explicit SMP-Affinity on ExecSMP under partial allocation failure. Source-only; no task was run.


**GD10233 continuation (2026-11-01):** added four `VkWriteDescriptorSet` pNext wrappers for KHR/NV acceleration structures, NV partitioned acceleration structures, and ARM tensor views. Their `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` payload count can be narrowed while retaining the full pointer; these are exceptionally large invalid descriptor extents and add no new root cause. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. See [GD10233](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10233-vulkan-hpp-array-proxies-truncate-large-container-sizes) and the [source-order review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-nested-descriptor-write-array-extent-recheck-gd10233-expanded-2026-11-01). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.


Rhine/Prism2 signal-failure candidate withdrawn before promotion (2026-11-01): their unit tasks start with the 16 general signal bits available from Exec's `TaskSigAlloc` default and consume only three/four signals before entering the wait loop. The unchecked `AllocSignal` shifts therefore have no exhaustion trigger on these startup paths. No OD or body/LOC credit; see the [caller-state trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rhine-prism2-unit-signal-pool-failure-recheck-2026-11-01). Source-only.


**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-01):** added Exec `PutMsg()`'s guest-owned Message input: the thunk passes unshadowed 20-byte m68k memory to the 48-byte native 64-bit implementation, which writes queue links and node state at incompatible offsets. This extends the existing guest/native marshalling finding; no maintained in-tree emulated caller was found. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [Exec thunk slice](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-exec-thunk-signal-message-and-device-vector-slice-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-01). Source-only; no guest or build was run.

**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-01):** rechecked the handwritten m68k Exec message thunks. `GetMsg()` creates an `IntuiMessage` shadow for its generic `Message *` result, and `WaitPort()` returns a native message pointer without guest mapping. These affect generic-message returns and callers that consume WaitPort's return, respectively; both remain conditional instances of the existing bridge-boundary finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [GetMsg/WaitPort recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-exec-getmsg-waitport-result-contract-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-01). No guest call or build was run; source-only.

**EK10586 — m68k Exec public-port thunks are no-ops:** registered `AddPort()` and `RemPort()` handlers return without changing the native public-port list. Guest publication/removal therefore does not match the API result expected by native clients. Scoped to guest use of these vectors through the optional m68k emulator; no in-tree guest caller was found. See [EK10586](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10586) and the [thunk check](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-exec-public-port-noop-thunks-ek10586-2026-11-01). Source-only; no port operation or build was run.

**EK10587 — m68k `FindName(NULL, name)` always misses:** the thunk rejects a NULL list instead of using Exec's public port list as native `FindName()` does. Scoped to guest callers using that supported default-list form. See [EK10587](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10587) and the [null-list recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-findname-null-list-default-ek10587-2026-11-01). No guest lookup or build was run; source-only.

**EK9387 — m68k guest `AvailMem()` always reports the full heap span:** it ignores current free-list usage and the `MEMF_LARGEST` request, so callers can overestimate available memory. Scoped to guest calls through the optional m68k emulator. See [EK9387](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9387) and the [AvailMem/heap rechecks](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5828). No guest allocation or query was run; source-only.

**EK10588 — m68k `DeletePool()` does not free outstanding pooled allocations:** the pool thunks allocate blocks from the shared guest heap but do not track them for pool deletion. Repeated pool lifecycles can consume containment heap until context teardown. Scoped to optional m68k emulator guests using pooled allocation. See [EK10588](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10588) and the [pool lifecycle recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-heap-pool-delete-lifecycle-ek10588-2026-11-01). No pool operation or build was run; source-only.

**EK9204 continuation (2026-11-01):** expanded the manual m68k `RawDoFmt()` finding: `%%` is excluded from the argument count but consumes the output loop's argument index, so a later conversion such as `%d` is emitted literally. This shares the existing callback/parser replacement root cause. See [EK9204](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9204) and the [escaped-percent recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-rawdofmt-escaped-percent-index-recheck-ek9204-2026-11-01). No format or build was run.

**EK10589 — m68k `TypeOfMem()` accepts out-of-arena addresses:** the manual thunk always reports `MEMF_PUBLIC`, including addresses beyond the 32 MiB guest arena where native Exec reports no memory. Scoped to guest callers using this pointer check. See [EK10589](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10589) and the [arena-bound recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-typeofmem-arena-bound-ek10589-2026-11-01). No query or build was run; source-only.

**EK10590 — RISC-V feature flags miss versioned multi-letter ISA extensions:** the legacy `riscv,isa` parser exact-matches lowercase, unversioned tokens, so valid case variants or suffixes such as `Zba1p0` can be displayed in the ISA string but reported unsupported by `GCIT_SupportsZba`. Scoped to RISC-V64 firmware using the legacy property with those spellings. See [EK10590](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10590) and the [ISA feature parser recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#riscv-legacy-isa-versioned-multiletter-feature-flags-ek10590-2026-11-01). Source-only; no firmware tree or build was used.

**EK10591 — Android bootstrap retains a JNI local object reference after `Load()` returns:** `Load()` stores its `this` local reference globally, then Java returns from `Load()` before `Kick()` or the child-exit callback uses it. Later `DisplayError()`/`HandleExit()` JNI calls therefore receive an expired reference. Scoped to the selected Android hosted bootstrap. See [EK10591](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10591) and the [JNI callback lifetime recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#android-bootstrap-jni-object-reference-lifetime-ek10591-2026-11-01). Source-only; no Android runtime was exercised.

**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-01):** added the handwritten `ReplyMsg()` path: it silently ignores a generic guest-owned `Message` with no registered shadow, rather than delivering it to its reply port. This is another conditional instance of the existing guest/native message-boundary finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [ReplyMsg recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68k-replymsg-unshadowed-generic-message-ek9432-2026-11-01). No message or build was run.

**GD10578 — WinGDI keyboard HIDD has an incompatible callback type cast:** its `InputIrqCallBack_t` field is assigned a function pointer cast to `(APTR, UWORD)`, so default warning-as-error compilers are expected to reject the module. The interrupt path itself passes the event pointer through the correctly typed field; no runtime truncation is claimed. See [GD10578](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10578) and the [WinGDI callback type recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wingdi-kbd-callback-type-gd10578). Source-only; no build was run.

**EK8853 — DynModule RemoveModule reverses its message-port allocation check:** the normal success path invokes the exit hook without sending the dispose request; allocation failure with a module port present sends a NULL reply port and then calls `GetMsg(NULL)`. Scoped to explicit `linklibs-dynmod` clients; no in-tree caller was found. See [EK8853](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8853) and the [RemoveModule recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dynmodule-removemodule-create-port-result-ek8853). Source-only; no module or allocation failure was exercised.

**GD10579 — AmigaVideo accepts a missing display-rethink task:** if compositor housekeeper task allocation fails, construction still succeeds. A later mixed-interlace stack update cannot queue the `RethinkDisplay()` call and leaves that attach attempt incomplete. Scoped to selected m68k Amiga AmigaVideo and the conditional transition; see [GD10579](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10579) and the [task-creation/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-housekeeper-task-creation-result-gd10579). Source-only; no task failure or display update was induced.

**OD11051 — Console handler may close a caller-supplied `WINDOW0x...` window:** the handler stores the supplied `Window *` and later unconditionally calls `CloseWindow()` during teardown. This is an ownership candidate because the source does not define whether the option transfers ownership; no in-tree pointer-form caller was found. Scoped to explicit `kernel-fs-con` builds and callers that pass an existing window. See [OD11051](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11051) and the [source/ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#console-handler-supplied-window-lifetime-candidate-od11051). Source-only; no window or build was used.

**OD11052 — Console handler ignores timer setup failure:** a failed `timer.device` open is not reported, and a later timed `WaitForChar()` sends I/O through a request with no device. Scoped to explicit `kernel-fs-con` builds, timer acquisition failure, and a timed wait with no buffered input; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See [OD11052](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11052) and the [file/caller coverage trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#console-handler-and-completion-file-roster-od11052). Source-only; no timer or build was exercised.

**OD11053 — Console completion count is too narrow for large match sets:** the optional completion code counts distinct matches in signed 16-bit `WORD` and has no cap. On ordinary narrowing behavior, 32,768 matches make Tab completion skip both auto-expansion and the chooser. Scoped to explicit `kernel-fs-con` builds and unusually large directory match sets; impact is limited to completion. See [OD11053](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11053) and the [match-count trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#console-completion-match-count-width-od11053). Source-only; no large directory or build was used.

**OD11054 — Generic bit-banged I²C mishandles 10-bit reads:** the generic address helper resends the second address byte after a read header, and read-only transfers omit the initial write-format address phase. Scoped to clients using a 10-bit address on a generic bit-banged backend, including Sam440; no checked-in 10-bit caller was found. See [OD11054](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11054) and the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#generic-i2c-10-bit-read-sequence-od11054). Source-only; no I²C transaction or build was run.


**EK10593 — MinGW emulation handler leaks host IRQ and reader-thread resources:** native event/thread creation failures leave a reserved host IRQ, and AROS IRQ-registration failure or later expunge does not stop the native reader before closing its DLL. Repeated failures can exhaust the finite host IRQ pool. Scoped to explicitly built MinGW emulation-handler targets; aggregate package edges are commented. See [EK10593](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10593) and the [lifecycle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#mingw-emulation-handler-native-reader-lifecycle-ek10593). Source-only; no failure, thread, or build was exercised.

**EK10595 — Efika ARM package omits its declared I²C HIDD:** the package makefile declares `PKG_HIDDS := i2c` but passes misspelled `PKD_HIDDS`, so the optional `kernel.pkg` recipe omits `Devs/Drivers/i2c.hidd`. Its `#MM` edges actively connect the package to the Efika image target; no upstream aggregate dependency on `arosboot-efika` or direct in-tree Efika client was found. See [EK10595](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10595) and the [Efika package trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L13147). Source-only; no package or build was produced.

**EK10594 — The console handler can signal an exited writer through its stale break target:** a shared input/output handler stores the most recent reader/writer task, but does not clear it when that task exits; a later Ctrl-C can pass the stale pointer to `Signal()`. Scoped to explicit `kernel-fs-con` builds with shared interactive handles and the write/exit/read overlap. See [EK10594](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10594) and the [shared-stream caller/lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#console-shared-stream-stale-break-target-ek10594). Source-only; no console, signal, or build was run.


**OD11055 — HID extended raw-key actions do not send key events:** USB and Bluetooth HID expose the action as implemented, but its event injection is disabled; USB only handles the power-key special case through a requester. Scoped to explicit builds of the optional HID class modules. Source strongly establishes the no-op; intent is less certain because the code marks it as unfinished. See [OD11055](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11055) and the [action-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-extended-raw-key-action-no-op-od11055). No report, event, GUI or build was run.


**OD11056 — USB and Bluetooth HID usage-name maps omit or mislabel defined usages:** Game Controls `0x3A`, Consumer `0x0C:0x00CF`, Generic Device Controls entries, LED `0x4E`–`0x56`, Camera Control `0x20`–`0x21`, several Auxiliary Display usages, and standard usage pages `0x20`, `0x41`, `0x59`, `0x91`, `0x92`, and `0xF1D0` lack names; Auxiliary Display `0x02` has a stale label. Numeric usages remain intact, so this is a low-confidence descriptive-catalog candidate, not a decoding defect. Scoped to explicit builds of the optional USB HID or Bluetooth HID classes. See [OD11056](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11056) and the [map comparison](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-current-usage-table-name-map-omissions-od11056). No descriptor, GUI, or build was used.

**OD11057 — WirelessManager leaks the SANA-II scan pool on teardown:** if an interface is removed while a hard-MAC `S2_GETNETWORKS` request is outstanding, deinit aborts/waits for the request but does not destroy the pool held in `ios2_Data`. Scoped to `CONFIG_DRIVER_SANA2`, devices advertising `S2_GETNETWORKS`, and teardown before scan-result dispatch. See [OD11057](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11057) and the [scan-pool teardown trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sana2-scan-pool-teardown-od11057). Source-only; no interface removal, scan or build was exercised.


**EK10596 — ARM and AArch64 `KrnSpinLock()` ignore its documented failure hook:** both implementations retry without invoking the hook documented to let a lower-priority lock owner run. Scoped to external or future ARM-native/AArch64 callers passing a non-NULL hook; maintained Exec callers checked here pass `NULL`. See [EK10596](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10596) and the [architecture/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#arm-aarch64-spinlock-failhook-contract-ek10596). Source-only; no contention or build was exercised.


**GD10580 — Vulkan-Hpp latency timing helpers return unused timing slots:** the default, custom-allocator and RAII vector helpers allocate using the preliminary maximum count but ignore the actual count written by the fill call. If fewer records are written, callers receive zero-initialized tail entries as if they were valid timings. Scoped to downstream C++ clients using optional Vulkan-Hpp with `VK_NV_low_latency2`; no in-tree C++ caller was found. See [GD10580](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10580) and the [API/count trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-low-latency-timing-result-count-gd10580). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.

**GD10581 — Nouveau GH100 recovery can access board-specific GPIO/UART addresses on other targets:** configured reset mode bits call fixed-address MMIO helpers without a matching platform guard. On a different hardware map, recovery can fault or access unrelated registers. Scoped to optional Nouveau GH100 configurations with GFW timeout and the affected reset bit enabled; intended-board reachability is not established. See [GD10581](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10581) and the [source/platform trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-gh100-fixed-address-recovery-gd10581). Source-only; no reset or build was run.

See [GD14329](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14329) and the [API/caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#obtaindatatypea-named-ram-group-filter-gd14329). Source-only; no query or build was run.

See [GD14330](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14330) and the [Read-to-classifier trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#datatypes-file-probe-read-result-gd14330). Source-only; no I/O error or build was induced.

See [EK9147](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9147) and the [m68k Utility arithmetic pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4777). Source-only; no arithmetic was run.
**EK9148 — m68k software `SMult64` chooses sign correction from the product high word:** the `-1 * 1` case returns +1, and some positive products can be negated. Applies to the 68000/68010/68060 fallback; no maintained direct in-tree caller was established. See [EK9148](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9148) and the [m68k Utility arithmetic pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4777). Source-only; no arithmetic was run.
**EK8969 — POSIXC ordinary `execve()`/`execv()` preserves descriptors marked `FD_CLOEXEC`:** the regular RunCommand handoff copies descriptor flags but skips the close-on-exec pass. See [EK8969](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8969) and the [POSIXC close-on-exec trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3446). Source-only; no program was executed.
**EK779 — OpenSBI FDT register-size arithmetic can wrap and admit a too-short `reg` property:** unchecked cell-count and byte-size arithmetic can then make `FDT_ReadCells()` read beyond the property. Conditional on malformed firmware data and a matching selected device node. See [EK779](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek779) and the [FDT tuple recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8054). Source-only; no firmware was used.
**EK144 — an empty ROM resident scan dereferences its NULL terminator during sorting:** the unsigned `num - 1` bound wraps before the missing-`exec.library` panic path. Conditional on an empty resident scan with a successful pointer-array allocation. See [EK144](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek144) and the [RomTag scanner inventory](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2103). Source-only; no boot was run.
**EK9019 — PC task exception callbacks are not dispatched:** i386 leaves `Exception()` commented and x86-64 compiles it out, so matching exception signals remain pending. Conditional on an i386-PC or x86-64-PC task with a configured callback and matching signal. See [EK9019](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9019) and the [PC exception-callback pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3703). Source-only; no task switch was run.
**EK318 — TaskList displays a rounded fraction of 100 without carrying into seconds:** `C:TaskList` and SysMon both turn valid CPU-time remainders from 995,000 to 999,999 microseconds into `.100` while leaving the seconds field unchanged. See [EK318](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek318) and the [TaskList caller pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L944). Source-only; no boundary display was run.
**EK9195 — m68k Commodities thunks pass guest `CreateCxObj()` pointers as native addresses:** filter strings, ports, tasks, events, and custom callbacks are not translated; scalar A1 arguments and the separate broker-layout issue are excluded. Applies to optional 64-bit-host m68kemu clients. See [EK9195](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9195) and the [Commodities pointer/caller pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7646). Source-only; no guest call was run.
**EK8803 — queued `task.resource` hooks link the caller Hook instead of their wrapper:** traversal reads the Hook node’s successor as the callback pointer, skips the intended callback, and leaves the wrapper unlinked. Requires an external queued-hook registration; immediate `THF_ROA` mode is unaffected. See [EK8803](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8803) and the [task-hook reconciliation](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4968). Source-only; no hook was run.
**EK9196 — m68k Utility TagItem allocators return unmapped native pointers:** `AllocateTagItems()` and `CloneTagItems()` results are unusable guest addresses; the paired free thunk also frees its converted temporary twice if reached with a guest-resolvable list. See [EK9196](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9196) and the [Utility TagItem lifecycle pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4993). Source-only; no guest allocation was run.
**EK9197 — m68k `FindTagItem()` shadows an element after freeing its temporary array:** success shadows freed storage, and the TagItem map treats scalar `ti_Data` as a pointer. See [EK9197](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9197) and the [TagItem thunk reconciliation](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5039). Source-only; no guest list was used.
**EK9198 — m68k Utility TagItem mutators discard caller-visible changes:** five wrappers mutate converted native copies and free them without updating guest lists. See [EK9198](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9198) and the [TagItem thunk reconciliation](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8553). Source-only; no guest list was used.
**EK473 — `RemTask()` frees a task while its CPU can still be executing it:** ExecSMP removal updates state locally, then immediately releases the target’s context and task memory; the selected PC scheduler may continue running a tombstoned task. Intuition’s selected screen-notify and menu-handler startup tasks signal failure before parking, while their parents wake and call `RemTask()`; on a cross-CPU schedule this is a maintained production caller. AHIRecord force-removes its level-meter task after a shutdown timeout, which can overlap a running worker on ExecSMP. Explicit `test-exec-public` and `test-exec-private` callers remove workers without a completion handshake. See [EK473](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek473), the [Intuition failure-startup caller recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek473-intuition-failure-startup-callers), and the [optional caller and network-driver recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek473-ahi-and-network-caller-recheck). No task, allocation failure, or schedule was run.
**EK830 — concurrent `RemTask()` calls can both clean up the same task:** the terminal-state check precedes serialized state transitions, but both callers proceed into context, ETask, and memory cleanup. Conditional on two concurrent removers passing the check. See [EK830](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek830) and the [cleanup-owner audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2931). Source-only; no task or interleaving was run.
**EK9138 — Realtime alarm fields are published without synchronization:** `SetPlayerAttrsA()` races Pulse’s locked reads, allowing an early signal or a mixed task/bit destination. Conditional on an external API update overlapping Pulse on ExecSMP. See [EK9138](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9138) and the [Realtime alarm publication checks](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4617). Source-only; no alarm was run.
**EK9139 — POSIXC socket `F_SETFD` reports success without storing `FD_CLOEXEC`:** AROSTCP’s foreign-descriptor path hard-codes success for `F_SETFD` and zero for `F_GETFD`. Conditional on POSIXC/AROSTCP fd.library integration and caller use. See [EK9139](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9139) and the [descriptor-flag contract recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4621). Source-only; no socket call was run.
**EK8881 — default AUX startup includes the BSTR length byte in the device name:** on `AROS_FAST_BSTR` targets the console handler copies `0x0d` as the first character, so `OpenDevice()` does not receive `serial.device`. The ordinary `Startup=0` path is affected when its separate BPTR tag survives. See [EK8881](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8881) and the [AUX BSTR follow-up](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2958). Source-only; no startup was run.
**EK9154 — POSIXC socket `F_SETFL` silently ignores `O_ASYNC`:** the AROSTCP fd hook forwards only `O_NONBLOCK`, despite the stack supporting `FIOASYNC`; `F_GETFL` also omits the flag. Applies to POSIXC/AROSTCP socket integration and callers using `O_ASYNC`. See [EK9154](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9154) and the [socket-flag dispatch pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4829). Source-only; no socket notification was used.
**EK9513 — conditional native-RISC-V SMP init callback lacks a return:** if a manually enabled `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` callback yields zero, initlib skips later Exec callbacks. Maintained native-RISC-V variants do not enable it and SiFive U does not hand off to the core. See [EK9513](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9513) and the [native-RISC-V initlib pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7066). Source-only; no build or boot was run.
**EK8848 — i386-PC dispatch unconditionally uses Pentium-only `RDTSC`:** the selected i386 dispatcher executes the instruction for every task without checking TSC support, although this target is compiled with an i486 ISA baseline. A no-TSC 486-compatible system that reaches dispatch traps with #UD. Scoped to the explicit `pc-i386` target; whether every i486 is a supported runtime target remains conditional because the hardware minimum is undocumented. See [EK8848](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8848) and the [CPU-floor/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#i386-pc-rdtsc-cpu-floor-ek8848). Source-only; no CPU or build was used.
**GD14331 — m68kemu `GetRPAttrsA()` writes host-width results into 32-bit guest slots:** the generated thunk maps the guest result address to guest memory, then native `GetRPAttrsA()` stores an eight-byte `IPTR` on the 64-bit target. A four-byte guest result is overwritten, and pointer results are not translated to guest handles. Scoped to optional x86-64 m68kemu when guest software calls this API. See [GD14331](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14331) and the [thunk/native output-width trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#m68kemu-getrpattrsa-output-width-gd14331). No emulator, guest program, or build was run.
**EK10598 — AArch64 SMP exception-stack watchdog compares frames against a single shared ceiling:** each secondary uses its own SP_EL1 stack, but `krnCheckExcStack()` has one function-static baseline. A core with a higher stack address can trigger a false warning and reset it; a higher baseline from another CPU can mask upward movement on a lower stack. Diagnostic-only; limited to multi-core AArch64 native builds. See [EK10598](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10598) and the [per-core stack trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#aarch64-smp-exception-stack-watchdog-ek10598). Source-only; no exception was run.
**OD1832 — Amiga mouse HIDD changes port-1 POTGO direction bits without reserving them:** its constructor allocates only port-0 POTGO lines, then writes `0xff00` to the shared register, changing port-1 direction state as well. A port-1 input client can consequently be affected. See [OD1832](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1832) and the [POTGO ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#m68k-potgo-writepotgo-caller-census). Source-only; no hardware access was performed.

**OD82 — Serial and parallel final close can free a unit after a concurrent shared open:** LDDemon serializes same-name Open calls, but Close uses only processor-local `Forbid()` and can race a cross-CPU Open after the final opener-count check. The newly published request can retain a unit pointer that Close then frees. Scoped to ExecSMP builds selecting serial.device or parallel.device and the relevant HIDD. See [OD82](AROS-other-drivers.md#od82) and the [open/close lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L292). Source-only; no device or concurrent operation was run.

**Current Graphics/Desktop + Exec/Kernel + Other Drivers body-coverage checkpoint (2026-11-02):** full-body credit is **4,756/5,088 area entries (93.5%)** and **1,694,858/2,221,484 C/header code lines (76.3%)**; **332 entries and 526,626 lines** remain without full-body credit. This updates the 2026-11-01 arithmetic reconciliation after five shared Exec/Keyboard files received complete body credit in the Graphics/Desktop ledger. Area entries may duplicate physical paths. These totals measure source-body review only; caller, build/configuration, platform contracts and candidate disposition remain open. Source-only.

**GD14333 — Reaction Label ignores the documented pen mapping for its embedded image:** `LABEL_Mapping` is stored and returned but never applied when `DrawImageState()` draws the child image. Scoped to explicitly built Reaction Label class users setting a non-default pen map; no in-tree caller was found. See [GD14333](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14333) and the [tag/draw-path trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#label-mapping-pen-map-contract-gd14333). Source-only; no image or build was run.

**GD14334 — Reaction Label omits the public `LABEL_Key` OM_GET attribute:** the getter has no case and its ImageClass fallback returns FALSE for unknown attributes. Scoped to explicitly built Reaction Label users querying the documented underscore key; no in-tree query was found. See [GD14334](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14334) and the [getter/superclass trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#label-key-om-get-contract-gd14334). Source-only; no object query or build was run.


**OD11063 — USB Audio can publish a NULL mode name after formatting allocation failure:** a later AHI name query passes that NULL tag value to `stccpy()`, which dereferences it; the AHI mode requester provides an in-tree caller. Requires the name allocation to fail while the AHI database node allocation succeeds. See [OD11063](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11063) and the [allocation and query trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-audio-null-mode-name-after-allocation-failure-od11063). No allocation failure, requester, mode query, or build was run.


**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** m68kemu's generated Intuition `SetPointer()` thunk passes guest legacy cursor bitmap bytes directly; on little-endian hosts `AllocSpriteDataA()`'s old-format word conversion rearranges asymmetric cursor rows before `BitMapScale()` reads them. Added as a conditional input-byte-order instance; no maintained guest caller was found. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [SetPointer cursor-data trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68kemu-intuition-setpointer-cursor-data-byte-order-trace-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-02). No guest call or build was run; source-only.


**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** the generated m68kemu `DrawImageState()` thunk passes guest-owned `Image` records directly to native Intuition; m68k and 64-bit host offsets for `ImageData` and `NextImage` differ, and this thunk creates no shadow. Added as a conditional structure-marshalling instance. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [DrawImageState layout trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68kemu-intuition-drawimagestate-image-layout-trace-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-02). No maintained emulated caller was found; no GUI call or build was run.


**EK9432 continuation (2026-11-02):** the m68kemu `NextPubScreen()` thunk returns the host pointer to its guest-backed name buffer without translating it to the guest address. The in-tree caller only checks for NULL; the consequence is limited to guest code consuming the returned pointer. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [NextPubScreen return mapping trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#m68kemu-nextpubscreen-return-pointer-mapping-recheck-ek9432-expanded-2026-11-02). No maintained emulated caller was found; no guest call or build was run.

**OD11064 — USB MassStorage consumes REQUEST SENSE data after command failure:** startup and polling ignore a failed REQUEST SENSE result and classify media from an uninitialized or partial buffer. The separate data-phase/residue success-accounting bug is DISK-029. See [OD11064](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11064) and the [REQUEST SENSE failure trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-request-sense-failure-od11064). No USB transfer or build was run.
**OD11065 — USB MassStorage can report a reinserted medium with stale capacity:** the poller sets `MSF_DiskPresent` before READ CAPACITY and does not undo it or invalidate the previous medium's geometry on failure. See [OD11065](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11065) and the [reinsertion/capacity trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-reinsertion-capacity-failure-od11065). No media swap or build was run.
**OD11066 — USB MassStorage 64-bit range checks can wrap for one-byte blocks:** a zero block shift leaves the 64-bit block and count unchanged, allowing the inclusive-end sum to wrap before the HIDD narrows the LBA to 32 bits. Scoped to out-of-range 64-bit requests on media reporting one-byte blocks; device behavior is conditional. See [OD11066](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11066) and the [64-bit interval trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-64bit-range-wrap-od11066). No device, request, or build was used.
**OD11072 — USB MassStorage constructs an invalid DOS sizeblock when capacity is unavailable:** its cleared unit retains block shift zero, but volume setup still evaluates `1 << (shift - 2)`, a negative shift count, and passes the resulting environment to `MakeDosNode()`. Conditional on a unit starting with no media or failed initial capacity. See [OD11072](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11072) and the [zero-shift volume setup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-zero-shift-dosenv-od11072). No device, no-media event, DOS node, or build was used.
**OD2859 — USB MassStorage does not validate the SCSICmd pointer or minimum CDB length before reading it:** a NULL command structure, NULL/zero-length CDB, or short opcode-specific CDB reaches unchecked pointer/index reads in `cmd_DirectSCSI()`. Conditional on a malformed direct `HD_SCSICMD` request; ordinary selected class callers use full-length CDBs. See [OD2859](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2859) and the [short-CDB and pointer validation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-short-cdb-validation-od2859). Source-only; no request was issued.
**EK8860 — OpenSBI maps and reserves only 2 MiB for the firmware device tree:** the parser accepts the DTB's declared size, but startup maps 2 MiB and the extra-bank allocator excludes only that fixed extent while selected clients retain the original blob. Larger trees can leave later data unmapped or available for allocation, conditional on firmware size and placement. See [EK8860](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8860) and the [FDT extent trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#opensbi-fdt-extent-map-and-reservation-ek8860). No DTB, allocation, or build was used.


**OD11069 — CAMD `PutSysEx()` can race ordinary live input while inserting a completed SysEx message into the same receive ring:** both paths reach `PutMidi2Link()`, but only the ordinary receiver takes the node queue semaphore; the shared cluster lock allows concurrent producers. This can lose or corrupt queued messages under overlapping activity. No checked-in direct client was found. See [OD11069](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11069) and the [producer/queue lock trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#camd-putsysex-receive-queue-producer-race-od11069). No MIDI operation or concurrency was run.



**OD9658 — CAMD `GetMidiErr()` can erase a concurrently raised error:** the public accessor reads then clears `MyMidiNode.error` without synchronization. Receiver updates can be lost in that window; `PutSysEx()` also reaches error writers without `receiversemaphore`, so all writers need a shared lock or atomic bit operations. No checked-in direct caller was found. See [OD9658](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9658) and the [caller/lock recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#camd-getmidierr-putsysex-caller-recheck-od9658). No MIDI input or concurrent call was run.




NListtree no-active Sort optional-demo caller confirmation (GD9848 strengthened; no new ID/body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): corrected the earlier caller census that found no in-tree no-active Sort trigger. In the explicitly buildable demo, `DrawSampleTree()` inserts rows without `MUIV_NListtree_Insert_Flag_Active` (`NListtree-Demo.c:191-237`; insert-active is bit 13 while the sample flags are `TNF_OPEN`/`TNF_LIST` bits 0/1), and NList initializes its active row to Off (`NList_mcc.c:401-402`). The Sort hook initializes `lastactive` to zero, reads `MUIA_NListtree_Active`, then passes it directly as the Sort `ListNode` (`NListtree-Demo.c:745-756`); the Sort button invokes that hook (`:1009,1110-1112`). Before a user selects a row, the class Active value remains NULL/zero (`NListtree.c:5138-5139,5006-5010`); the class Sort method treats NULL as an ordinary node argument and `ListNode_Sort()` dereferences it on the flag-zero path (`:9369-9400,3112-3116`). Expanded GD9848’s affected configuration/trigger and raised confidence for this demo caller path; public API no-active selector combinations remain conditional. No GUI, sort operation or build was run; source-only.


Apple Silicon CreateSegList ignored-protection-result caller pass (EK712 expanded; no new EK or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): followed the successful page-allocation branch of `CreateSegList()` through its R/X request into the selected Unix `KrnSetProtection()` implementation (`compiler/arossupport/createseglist.c:87-99`; `arch/all-unix/kernel/setprotection.c:15-35`). The host `mprotect()` result is discarded and the vector returns void, so a host rejection is invisible to the caller; `CreateSegList()` then returns the generated jump segment. Confirmed `__AROSPLATFORM_WXSEG__` is selected for Darwin AArch64 (`configure.in:1805-1811`) and the DOS bootstrap creates and launches the segment (`rom/dos/cliinit.c:177-197`). Expanded EK712 to include this transition-failure route alongside the previously recorded allocation-failure fallback. The trigger requires an otherwise successful page allocation and a host rejection of the R/W-to-R/X change; host entitlement/policy outcomes remain unverified. Existing bodies and line totals were already credited. No allocation failure, protection change, or boot was induced; source-only.

**OD3067 — PCNet32, nForce and SiS900 worker tasks use unchecked message-port allocations:** a failed reply/input port can fault the task or let the parent publish a unit with no worker. The active network aggregate selects these x86-family device targets in standard i386-PC/x86_64-PC workbench builds; nForce unit publication remains separately blocked by OD3080. See [OD3067](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3067) and the [worker port caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sis900-worker-port-finding-deduplication-od3067). No allocation failure, task, device or build was induced.
**OD11073 — USB HID parses its shared DMA report buffer after the controller has rearmed it:** OHCI and UHCI defer parsing through `Cause()` but requeue the same transfer buffer first. A following periodic transfer can overwrite bytes while the selected keyboard or mouse parser reads them, producing mixed or skipped input state. Conditional on callback overlap; applies to explicitly selected HID and OHCI/UHCI targets, which are not included in the USB aggregate dependencies. See [OD11073](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11073) and the [rearm/deferred-parse trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-shared-report-buffer-rearm-before-deferred-parse-od11073). Source-only; no transfer was run.
