**OD11075 — PCIUSB teardown does not quiesce deferred callbacks:** OHCI/EHCI completion soft interrupts can outlive HCD private-state teardown on ExecSMP. A queued NAK-timeout callback can also resubmit its timer after close's abort; if the device is expunged before timeout, the request remains linked in timer.device's list after its containing unit is freed. See [OD11075](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11075) and the [deferred-callback trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pciusb-deferred-completion-softint-versus-close-od11075). Source-only; no close, interrupt, or expunge was run.
**OD11076 — USB HID passes a length one byte too large to `ParseReport` after removing a report ID:** a subclass that bounds reads with the supplied length can treat one byte beyond the payload as valid. The checked-in keyboard and mouse handlers ignore the length, so no current in-tree effect is claimed. Conditional on a multi-report HID device and a subclass that consumes the field; the HID class is optional in the default USB aggregate. See [OD11076](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11076) and the [caller/extent trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hid-multi-report-parser-length-caller-boundary-od11076). Source-only; no transfer or parser was run.
**OD11078 — BTSerial `CMD_RESET` leaves active writes and buffered input intact:** an active multi-chunk write can continue transmitting, and pre-reset ring-buffer data remains visible to later reads. See [OD11078](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11078) and the [reset/write-state trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#btserial-reset-active-write-od11078). Source-only; no request or device was run.
**OD11079 — BTSerial shutdown races request admission:** on ExecSMP, a request can pass admission before shutdown and enter queue insertion after the final drain; read/write requests can dereference the deleted task port while signaling, and other commands can remain queued after the unit-port drain. See [OD11079](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11079) and the [shutdown-admission trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#btserial-shutdown-admission-race-od11079). Source-only; no request or schedule was run.
**OD11080 — Mesa3DGL leaks Gallium pipe-driver objects:** `CreatePipe()` creates a driver OOP object, but Mesa’s normal context teardown and post-creation error paths never call the matching `DestroyPipe()`. Repeated context lifecycles retain those objects. See [OD11080](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11080) and the [pipe-object lifetime trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#gallium-createpipe-object-lifetime-od11080). Source-only; no GL context was run.

**[OD2372](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2372) — Embedded reset-callback nodes can outlive their owners:** VMware SVGA, VirtIO, AHCI, and PCIUSB OHCI/UHCI/EHCI cleanup paths free callback-node owners without unlinking the nodes from Exec. A later reset can traverse stale callback state. Conditional on owner teardown before reset; optional backends and no default hot-removal sequence is claimed. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2372) and the [PCIUSB expunge trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pciusb-ohci-uhci-ehci-reset-node-expunge-follow-up-od2372-expanded-2026-11-02). Source-only.


## Other Drivers findings reconciled into the index (2026-11-02)

**[OD3225](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3225) — BCM GENET RX traverses tracker, opener, and pending-read lists without synchronization against `S2_UNTRACKTYPE`, `CMD_READ`, `AbortIO()`, or `Close()` mutations. High-confidence overlap on the explicit Raspberry Pi ExecSMP variant; conditional higher-priority preemption on single-CPU ARM32. Source-only; no schedule was run.**

**[OD3110](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3110) — BCM GENET marks its kernel IRQ as registered even when `KrnAddIRQHandler()` could not allocate a handler; later teardown passes the NULL token to a remover that dereferences it. Conditional on low memory during explicit Raspberry Pi GENET startup; source-only.**

**[OD3027](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3027) — BCM GENET request-port allocation failure leaks the task, stack, and `MemList` allocated earlier in `CreateUnit()`. Trigger requires low-memory failure during explicit Raspberry Pi GENET startup; source-only.**

**[OD2934](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2934) — PCIUSB’s composed OHCI/UHCI/EHCI root hub caps at 16 ports but stores and returns only 16 change bits, so port 16 cannot be signaled; its hub descriptor also allocates only two mask bytes. Conditional on a 16-port PCIUSB root hub; source-only.**

**[OD2939](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2939) — BCM GENET `DeleteUnit()` never closes/releases the unit-level timer.device request and message port allocated by `CreateUnit()`, leaking them on expunge and later initialization failures. Explicit Raspberry Pi GENET target; source-only.**

**[OD2928](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2928) — BCM GENET `CMD_FLUSH` drains unit queues but omits pending reads on each opener’s private port, then reports success. Conditional on a direct/external client flushing with reads outstanding; explicit Raspberry Pi GENET target. Source-only.**

**[OD2926](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2926) — BCM GENET ignores PHY RX/TX delay-register write failures, then completes PHY initialization; with a mismatched `phy-mode`, the link can receive but fail to transmit correctly. Explicit Raspberry Pi GENET target only; source-only.**

**[OD2925](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2925) — BCM GENET accepts unchecked device-tree cell counts; arithmetic can wrap tuple-length validation and make the parser read beyond `reg`/`ranges` properties. Conditional malformed firmware tree and explicit Raspberry Pi GENET target; source-only.**

**[OD2924](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2924) — BCM GENET Close frees per-opener packet-stat baselines without decrementing unit tracker references; AROSTCP tracks IP/ARP and closes without untracking, so tracker nodes persist across interface lifecycles. Conditional on explicitly selecting Raspberry Pi’s `workbench-devs-networks-soc-raspi` target; not claimed in the checked default boot packages. Source-only.**

**[OD2920](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2920) — DWMAC returns link-up with guessed 10-half settings when PHY advertisement reads fail after negotiation; the caller programs those settings into the MAC. Explicit RISC-V64 target only; source-only.**

**[OD2919](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2919) — DWMAC and BCM GENET `NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY` handlers write the full result structure without checking `io_Length`; a short declared buffer can be overwritten. Explicit RISC-V64 DWMAC and Raspberry Pi GENET targets; source-only.**

**[OD2918](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2918) — USBDevice accepts a successfully transferred string descriptor shorter than its two-byte header, then computes a negative character count and uses it for allocation/indexing. Conditional malformed-descriptor path; source-only.**

**[OD2917](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2917) — USBDevice construction ignores failure of the language-table request and reads `langid` from the untouched local descriptor; later name lookups use that indeterminate value. Conditional; mainly affects displayed device names. Source-only.**

**[OD2916](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2916) — USBDevice construction writes decoded or fallback product/manufacturer/serial strings through unchecked pooled allocations. Low-memory failure reaches a NULL write or `CopyMem()`; selected USB subclasses; source-only.**

**[OD2915](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2915) — `USBDevice::New()` accepts a NULL per-device timer; a later failed configuration-descriptor request passes it to `USBDelay()`, which dereferences it. Conditional on timer setup and descriptor-transfer failure; selected USB hub/HID/MassStorage paths; source-only.**

**[OD2908](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2908) — USB enumeration and base device construction use an OHCI control pipe without checking whether `CreatePipe()` returned NULL; the selected control-transfer path dereferences it. Conditional on outer pipe allocation failure and OHCI selection; source-only.**

**[OD2909](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2909) — After USB `SET_ADDRESS`, failure to allocate the replacement OHCI pipe returns before releasing the controller lock or freeing the reserved address. Other tasks can remain blocked on that controller; conditional on OHCI and low-memory failure. Source-only.**

**[OD2864](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2864) — During USB startup scanning, failure of either class-name allocation reaches `CopyMem()` with a NULL destination. Because the scan precedes the startup reply, the selected explicit USB stack target can fail to complete startup when this occurs; HID and MassStorage `AddClass` calls normally deduplicate against scanned names. Optional-target and low-memory conditional; source-only.**

**[OD2910](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2910) — USB address allocation returns `0xff` on bitmap exhaustion, but `NewDevice()` treats any nonzero result as a valid device address and attempts enumeration with the out-of-range value. Trigger requires exhaustion of one controller’s address map; source-only.**

**[OD2911](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2911) — If USB enumeration reserves an address but no class object is created, `NewDevice()` returns without freeing it. The hub retries failed creation every ten seconds, so a persistently unsupported device can exhaust the controller address map. Conditional on the selected hub path; source-only.**

**[OD2912](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2912) — For a USB hub-class device, failure of `OOP_NewObject()` is followed by `HIDD_USBHub_OnOff(NULL, TRUE)`; the selected OOP dispatch reads the object header. Conditional on hub object construction failure; source-only.**

**[OD2913](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2913) — `NewDevice()` ignores failed descriptor transfers; a failed initial device read feeds zero max-packet size into the next OHCI pipe, while a failed configuration-header read leaves `config` fields indeterminate before allocation and interface processing. Conditional on transfer failure in the optional USB stack/OHCI path; source-only.**

**[OD2914](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2914) — USB device disposal frees its pipe and timer but never returns the allocated address to the controller bitmap. Repeated disconnects exhaust available addresses on the selected Sam440/Efika USB package paths; source-only.**

**[OD10031](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10031-nouveau-nvif-edid-error-skips-pm-release-and-preserves-old-edid) — A failed NVIF EDID read on a connector without an I²C adapter returns before releasing the runtime-PM usage reference or replacing a previously published EDID. The stale-EDID effect requires an earlier successful read. Source-only.**



**[OD11229](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11229-nouveau-connector-continues-after-drm-connector-init-failure) — Nouveau ignores a failed `drm_connector_init()`; if initial DRM mode-object allocation fails before `connector->funcs` is set, construction continues and the later reset call dereferences the NULL function pointer. Conditional on that allocation failure in the selected Nouveau DRM path. Source-only.**



**[OD1602](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1602) — Poseidon's private read/write semaphore updates its owner/count fields and waiter/borrow lists under `Forbid()` only, which does not serialize other CPUs on ExecSMP. Nested hub scans provide a selected concurrent path; overlapping updates can lose a lock record or desynchronize its count. Conditional on ExecSMP with Poseidon/hub support; source-only.**

**[OD10155](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10155) — USB and Bluetooth HID report-descriptor parsing left-shifts negative signed bytes when decoding two-byte short items, so negative logical bounds depend on undefined C behavior. The adjacent four-byte promotion is documented separately as implementation-defined, not included in the UB claim. Optional HID targets; source-only.**

**[OD9424](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9424) — LowLevel `ReadJoyPort()` frees its full requested POTGO mask in `llPortClose()` even after `AllocPotBits()` failed, clearing another client’s reservation and POTGO state. The selected AmigaMouse HIDD persistently reserves port 0 mask `0x0f00`, so `ReadJoyPort(0)` supplies a concrete conflicting owner. See the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#potgo-failed-allocation-unowned-free-od9424). Source-only; no joystick or hardware operation was run.

**[OD9887](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9887) — IntelGMA continues after a failed PCIPC MMIO or GATT mapping.** The GATT path can write page-table entries through the failed mapping when later graphics-memory allocation needs a non-stolen block. The finding remains conditional on an explicitly selected IntelGMA target and x86-64 PC PCIPC mapping failure; see the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#intelgma-pcipc-mapping-failure-caller-trace-od9887-expanded-no-body-path-loc-credit-2026-11-02).

**[OD9900](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9900) — PCIUSB EHCI leaves PCI memory decode enabled if its selected x86-64 PCIPC BAR mapping fails.** The driver enables MEM decode before mapping, and its failure path releases ownership without restoring the PCI command bit. Conditional on an above-128-GiB BAR mapping failure and memory decode initially being clear. Source-only.


**[EK10599](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10599-kernel-clocksource-generated-header-disconnected) — Kernel clocksource header generation is disconnected from normal kernel and SDK include targets; a clean generated-header state can leave `registerclocksource.c` without `proto/clocksource.h`, and edits to `clocksource.conf` do not invalidate the custom stamp.**

**[EK10600](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10600-riscv64-backtrace-scans-past-task-stack) — RISC-V64 OpenSBI backtrace scans up to 4 KiB from saved SP without checking task-stack bounds; invalid or near-boundary SP can make fatal diagnostics read outside the stack.**

**[EK10601](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10601-opensbi-dumpdt-clamps-nested-cell-sizes) — OpenSBI `dumpdt` clamps depth tracking at 24 and can format deep `reg` entries using the wrong parent address/size cell counts.**

**[OD3807](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3807) — LE Secure Connections Just Works and Numeric Comparison omit the initiator Pairing Confirm and time out; scoped to optional `btlesc` pairings.**

**[FS-082](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-082) — SFS buffered transfers route odd caller buffers through `CopyMemQuick`; on m68k this can raise an address error.** Affected when the default DMA mask forces a bounce transfer for a block-aligned read/write. See [the DOS mask and bounce-buffer trace](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-082). Source-only; no file I/O or build was run.

**[FS-083](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-083) — SFS dereferences a failed cache-buffer acquisition before callers can handle exhaustion.** If an operation needs a new cache entry while all cache buffers are pinned, the handler can fault instead of returning the cache-exhaustion error. See [the allocator and caller trace](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-083). Source-only; no exhaustion or filesystem operation was induced.

**[FS-084](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-084) — NTFS does not check `CreateMsgPort()` for its notification port before dereferencing its signal bit during handler startup.** If that allocation fails but subsequent setup succeeds, the handler faults instead of reporting startup failure. See the detailed path in [FS-084](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-084). Source-only; no allocation failure or mount was induced.

**[FS-085](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-085) — NTFS replies successful startup when required initialization fails.** DOS then accepts the dead handler's message port as a successful startup result. See the [startup reply trace](AROS-filesystems.md#fs-085). Source-only; no initialization failure or mount was induced.

**[EK8962](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8962) — Caller-supplied stack sizes can leave the swapped C stack misaligned.** In addition to selected pthread and AArch64 Shell cases, `Stack 40961` misaligns the PPC Efika workbench Shell path by four bytes and produces a 4- or 8-byte misalignment on explicitly built RISC-V32/RV64 Shell targets. RISC-V boot manifests do not include Shell by default. See the [stack-size arithmetic and PPC/RISC-V switch traces](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8962). Source-only; no stack switch or build was run.

**[GD14349](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14349) — AmigaVideo can write user copper instructions beyond its fixed 500-instruction destination buffer.** The public list can grow across linked `CBump()` segments, but the HIDD appends to a fixed-capacity copper allocation without checking remaining space; the aggregate count also narrows to signed `WORD` at very large list sizes. Scoped to m68k AmigaVideo viewport rebuilds with an oversized external/future list; no active checked-in producer reaches the limit. See the [count and copy trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-copperlist-aggregate-count-overflow-gd14349). Source-only.

**[GD14350](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14350) — AmigaVideo may overwrite the last user copper instruction after inserting a line-wrap wait.** If a count-bounded list omits `CEND()`, a wait crossing line 256 emits one extra instruction while the stored tail still uses the input count; later list linking writes at that tail. The graphics copper test uses a final out-of-range `CWait(10000,0xFF)`, which the parser skips and which balances the inserted instruction; no in-tree count-exhausted list without such a terminator was found. See the [output/tail trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-linewrap-wait-tail-accounting-gd14350). Source-only.

**[GD14351](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14351) — FKey submits an ARexx request with a NULL command when `CreateArgstring()` fails.** The optional FKey target still sets the one-argument flag and sends the request after allocation failure, dropping the configured command without reporting it. See the [allocation and cleanup trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#fkey-arexx-command-argstring-allocation-failure-gd14351). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**[GD14352](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14352) — The optional graphics copper test ignores failed `UCopperListInit()` and dereferences its null list/instruction cursor on the first `CWait()`.** Triggered by either copper-list allocation failing after the test header is allocated. See the [caller initialization trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-copper-test-list-init-failure-gd14352). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**[EK10605](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10605-managed-inbounds-callback-null) — `AllocAbs()` and `FreeMem()` call a managed header’s nullable `mhe_InBounds` callback without checking it. Conditional on an external/custom provider publishing a managed MemHeader without that callback; no in-tree system-list provider was found. See the [dispatch trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#managed-inbounds-callback-null-ek10605). Source-only; no provider or memory operation was run.
**[EK10604](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10604-tlsf-allocabs-scan-bound) — TLSF `AllocAbs()` scans to `MAX_FLI` although its matrix has only `REAL_FLI` rows; a request whose absolute range is not found can read beyond the matrix rather than fail cleanly. Applies to TLSF-managed memory headers. See the [allocator trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tlsf-allocabs-scan-bound-ek10604). Source-only; no allocation or build was run.
**[EK10603](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10603-tlsf-oversized-initial-region) — TLSF traps when registering a contiguous free region of at least 128 GiB on 64-bit builds: the initial block maps to bucket 31, beyond the 0–30 table range. Conditional on a firmware memory map exposing a sufficiently large contiguous free extent; x86-64 PC selects TLSF by default. See the [allocator trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#tlsf-oversized-initial-region-ek10603). Source-only; no boot or build was run.
**[EK10602](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10602) — Relative-base setup leaks tables when task-slot publication fails:** if task-slot array allocation fails after the per-task table is allocated, the result is ignored and each later relative-wrapper lookup can allocate another table and PosixC open reference. Scoped to startup-linked relative-library clients; no current checked-in standalone client was established. See the [failure-path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#relative-base-slot-publication-failure-ek10602). Source-only; no failure or build was run.
**[EK10155](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10155) — OpenSBI drops ACPI PLIC contexts for nonzero controller IDs.** The ACPI parser accepts only RINTC entries whose controller ID is zero and does not match contexts against the selected PLIC record; on an ACPI-only nonzero-ID system, no context is retained and PLIC initialization is skipped. No checked-in firmware topology establishes this case. See the [ACPI PLIC parsing trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8577). Source-only; no interrupt or boot was exercised.
**[EK9380](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9380) — `SystemTagList()` dereferences a failed `ExtArg` allocation after creating a child process.** If `AllocMem()` fails after `CreateNewProc()` succeeds, the function writes through NULL before sending the child its startup packet, then skips normal launch cleanup. See the [failure-path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5691). Source-only; no allocation failure or launch was induced.
**[EK9381](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9381) — `SystemTagList()` writes through a failed command-buffer allocation.** A nonempty command lacking a trailing newline is copied into an unchecked `AllocVec()` result before it is injected. Scoped to the allocation-failure branch; the reviewed hosted emergency-console caller uses an empty command. See the [caller and cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5692). Source-only; no failure or launch was run.
**[EK9382](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9382) — `SystemTagList()` can launch with the wrong current directory after `DupLock()` fails.** When the caller relies on inherited `NP_CurrentDir`, an unchecked duplication failure sends NULL to the child; later relative-path opens fall back to the boot process's directory. See the [directory propagation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5693). Source-only; no lock failure or launch was induced.
**[EK9383](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9383) — `CliInitNewcli(NULL)` faults despite its documented NULL-default contract.** The vector forwards NULL to a helper that reads packet fields immediately. The selected `AROS_CLI` macro retrieves a packet itself; the optional m68kemu bridge can pass native NULL, but no guest caller was established. See the [wrapper and caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L788). Source-only; no call was run.
**[EK9385](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9385) — 130 nested `Disable()` calls can make the first `Enable()` re-enable interrupts early.** The signed-byte nesting count wraps; this is source-explicit for the selected m68k-Amiga and PC byte-counter paths. No in-tree 130-deep caller was found. See the [counter-width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5819). Source-only; no interrupt or build was run.
**[EK8827](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8827) — 130 nested m68k-Amiga `Forbid()` calls can permit a task switch early.** The signed-byte counter wraps, and the first `Permit()` can reach the scheduler’s negative-count gate while 129 forbid levels remain. No in-tree 130-deep caller was found. See the [counter and scheduling trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek8827-forbid-nesting-overflow-recheck). Source-only; no schedule was run.
**[EK9386](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9386) — InstallAROS uses its shared file buffer after allocation failure.** The stage constructor keeps the object when `AllocMem()` returns NULL, and later backup/copy paths pass that pointer to file I/O without checking it. The tool target is explicit and its aggregate edge is commented out. See the [allocation and caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5894). Source-only; no file operation or allocation failure was run.
**[EK9400](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9400) — PC SMP startup failures can leave offline CPUs eligible for task affinity.** Late AP stack, wake, readiness, or bootstrap failures do not reduce the discovered `apic_count`; affinity validation and scheduler filtering continue using it. A task pinned only to an offline CPU can remain unscheduled. See the [AP startup/count trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9400-ap-count-reconciliation). Source-only; no AP or schedule was exercised.
**[EK9401](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9401) — A failed x86-64 PC processor-query mask allocation can misattribute CPU 0 data to a secondary CPU.** A NULL affinity mask restricts the query task to CPU 0, while its CPUID results are stored in the requested secondary CPU slot. See the [query-task trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5926). Source-only; no allocation failure or query was run.
**[EK9402](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9402) — A later PC processor-query setup failure can free the resource base before earlier query tasks finish.** Previously queued tasks retain and use the base during query; failed InitLib rollback does not cancel them. See the [startup rollback trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5892). Source-only; no failure or task execution was induced.
**[EK9403](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9403) — The AArch64 Raspberry Pi loader can apply ET_EXEC relocation corrections twice.** Several additive data and branch relocations are adjusted in both sequential relocation switches; impact depends on the generated core containing an affected relocation. See the [relocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5931). Source-only; no image was built or booted.
**[EK9404](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9404) — Live m68k page-table updates can leave stale translations or permissions in the ATC.** The mapping routine updates descriptors without invalidating cached translations; normal boot setup runs before MMU enable, so the finding is limited to later live updates. See the [mapping/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1532). Source-only; no MMU operation was run.
**[EK9405](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9405) — m68k Amiga FASTREMAP ignores partial page-table failures.** After invalidating a CHIP range, it ignores failed remapping and can continue boot with a partial/unmapped range; the replacement buffer can leak. The trigger requires page-table allocation failure. See the [failure-path recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8905). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**[EK9406](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9406) — debug.library can index beyond the ELF section table for an invalid symbol section index.** DOS relocation need not reference the malformed symbol, but debug registration scans the symbol table afterward. See the [symbol-index/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8907). Source-only; no ELF was loaded.
**[EK9407](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9407) — AArch64 native page-table tables consume twice their usable size for alignment.** Each 4 KiB table reserves an 8 KiB allocation and the unused half is not reclaimed; build/runtime reachability remains conditional on the existing kernel manifest gap. See the [allocator trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8909). Source-only; no mapping was run.
**[EK9408](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9408) — m68k serial diagnostics dereference a NULL ExecBase after detecting it is invalid.** A reversed TCB-print ternary dereferences NULL on the invalid-base branch and prints a sentinel on the valid branch. See the [handler trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8911). Source-only; no fault was induced.
**[EK9409](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9409) — m68k serial diagnostics treat address-error frames as valid memory.** Address-error frame tags bypass the validity-check switch, whose default reports every address as valid. See the [frame-tag trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5954). Source-only; no memory probe was run.
**[EK9410](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9410) — m68k serial diagnostics validate only a string's first byte before printing it.** The serial printer reads to NUL without bounds or further probes. See the [string trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5957). Source-only; no exception was induced.

**GD14355 — Dir discards malformed pattern-template errors:** `ParsePattern()` errors are treated as a non-wildcard path and replaced by a later `Lock()` error. See [GD14355](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14355-dir-discards-malformed-pattern-template-errors) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD14356 — Dir's `ALL FILES` option does not recurse into subdirectories:** the `doDirs` display option also gates recursion, so file-only recursive listings omit nested files. See [GD14356](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14356-dirs-all-files-option-does-not-recurse-into-subdirectories) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD14357 — Search suppresses file-open and file-I/O errors:** `FindString()` treats failed opens and read/seek errors as no matches, and normal traversal clears the error. See [GD14357](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14357-search-suppresses-file-open-and-file-io-errors) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-command-file-io-error-propagation-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.



**GD14360 — Delete hides unmatched arguments after any earlier match:** `firstmatch` is cleared globally and never reset for later `/M` entries, so a missing later pattern can be masked by an earlier match. See [GD14360](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14360-delete-hides-unmatched-arguments-after-any-earlier-match) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#delete-command-multi-argument-match-status-pass). Selected `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD14361 — Delete reads before an empty file argument:** `ReadArgs()` accepts an empty quoted `/M` item, but `doDelete()` indexes `strlen(item) - 1` before checking it. See [GD14361](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14361-delete-reads-before-an-empty-file-argument) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#delete-command-empty-argument-bounds-pass). Selected `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD14362 — MakeDir ALL clears filesystem errors on failure:** `CreateDirAll()` overwrites Lock/CreateDir/Examine failures with its still-zero local error before the caller prints the fault. See [GD14362](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14362-makedir-all-clears-filesystem-errors-on-several-failure-paths) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#makedir-all-error-preservation-pass). Selected `workbench-c` target using ALL; source-only.

**GD14457 — AllocSpriteDataA does not bound old-format sprite height:** the output height narrows into a UWORD allocation size, then a UWORD loop counter iterates against the original ULONG height; heights above 65,535 overrun the temporary planes and do not terminate. See [GD14457](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14457-allocspritedataa-does-not-bound-old-format-sprite-height) and the [old-format sprite height pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#allocspritedata-old-format-height-boundary-pass). Public API condition reachable through SetPointer’s unchecked negative WORD height; the preferences caller uses 16-by-16 dimensions. Source-only.

**OD11081 — Printer graphics dump reports success when raster allocation fails:** failed row-buffer or scaled-bitmap allocation leaves the status at success, so the dump closes and returns success without rendering the raster. Scoped to explicitly built/loaded printer graphics segments; the Workbench aggregate edges are disabled. See [OD11081](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11081) and the [printer graphics allocation-failure pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#printer-graphics-allocation-failure-od11081). Source-only; no allocation or print request was run.

**OD11082 — Fractional printer widths are sign-extended before scaling:** the signed `LONG` destination field is shifted as signed even though `SPECIAL_FRACCOLS` and `GraphicDump` supply unsigned fractions; MEDIUM/LARGE can become negative widths and then oversized unsigned scaling values. Scoped to explicitly built printer modules. See [OD11082](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11082) and the [fractional printer-dimensions pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#printer-fractional-dimensions-od11082). Source-only; no print request was run.

**OD11083 — GraphicDump indexes past its printer error-name table:** the tool has names for codes 0–11 but indexes directly by `io_Error`; the printer API permits segment errors 32–126, so a custom error reads beyond the table before `%s` output. Scoped to explicitly built GraphicDump and printer segments returning custom errors. See [OD11083](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11083) and the [GraphicDump full-body pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#graphicdump-full-body-pass). Source-only; no print request was run.

**OD11084 — GraphicDump uses display offsets as bitmap-local source coordinates:** Intuition's screen `LeftEdge`/`TopEdge` are viewport offsets, but the tool passes them as source bitmap coordinates for the whole screen. On a positioned planar screen, printer scaling can read past row and plane bounds. Scoped to explicitly built GraphicDump/printer modules. See [OD11084](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11084) and the [GraphicDump full-body pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#graphicdump-full-body-pass). Source-only; no screen or print request was run.


**GD14363 — ShaderModuleIdentifierEXT comparison can read past its fixed identifier array:** the wrapper accepts a public `identifierSize` above 32, then uses it as the `memcmp` length and optional ordering loop bound. This requires invalid wrapper state; compliant Vulkan results are bounded. See [GD14363](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14363-shader-module-identifier-comparisons-trust-an-unchecked-identifiersize) and the [comparison bounds pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#shader-module-identifier-comparison-bounds-pass). Optional Vulkan-Hpp API; source-only.

**OD11085 — historical duplicate of OD3167:** this is the same USB Audio shared update-flag lost-update race; [OD3167](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3167) is canonical. OD11085 remains as a historical reference, not a separate bug. See the [control-update flag race pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-audio-control-update-flag-race-pass). Source-only.


**GD14364 — VCGfx skips overlapping vertical copies when DMA is unavailable:** DMA setup failure is allowed, but the large-copy path mistakes its no-channel result for a partial transfer and returns without the CPU copy. See [GD14364](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14364-vcgfx-skips-overlapping-vertical-copies-when-dma-is-unavailable) and the [VCGfx no-DMA overlapping-copy pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vcgfx-no-dma-overlapping-copy-pass). Raspberry Pi VCGfx; source-only.

**GD14365 — Generic HIDD CopyBox uses signed WORD counters and coordinates for UWORD extents:** large loops overflow signed counters, and small in-bounds rectangles crossing coordinate 32,767 can pass negative coordinates to the planar fallback. The optional Compositor can also pass a 32,768 extent from inclusive Rectangle endpoints. See [GD14365](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14365-generic-hidd-copybox-uses-signed-word-counters-and-coordinates-for-uword-extents) and the [generic CopyBox extent-width pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-copybox-extent-width-pass). Source-only.

**GD14366 — Generic HIDD CopyBox buffer fast paths ignore the GC color mask:** `BltBitMap()` applies a caller-supplied partial plane mask for palette destinations, then same-format chunky LUT8 copies overwrite the full byte. See [GD14366](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14366-generic-hidd-copybox-buffer-fast-paths-ignore-the-gc-color-mask) and the [generic CopyBox color-mask and caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-copybox-color-mask-pass). Source-only.

**GD14367 — CopyBox cursor-intersection check narrows unsigned extents to WORD:** large copy bounds can wrap negative and leave the software cursor composited during a blit. See [GD14367](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14367-copybox-cursor-intersection-check-narrows-unsigned-extents-to-word) and the [CopyBox cursor-bound pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copybox-cursor-bound-pass). Source-only.


**OD11086 — AHI RecordTest can report success after its first recording read fails:** `DoIO()` returns the device error, but the failure branch skips the loop without setting DOS `IoErr()` or a failure exit status. See [OD11086](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11086) and the [initial-read error path pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-recordtest-initial-read-error-path-od11086). Source-only; no audio device was used.

**OD11087 — AHI PlayTest turns a DOS input error into a huge playback length:** signed `Read()` error `-1` is stored as `ULONG` and passed to `CMD_WRITE` for the 20,000-byte input buffer. See [OD11087](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11087) and the [PlayTest input-error pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-playtest-input-error-length-od11087). Source-only; no input stream or audio device was used.

**OD11088 — USB HID variable-field parsing expands an unchecked `ReportCount`:** one descriptor count controls per-field allocations, and allocation failures do not stop the loop or fail parsing. Affected optional Poseidon ROM USB HID builds when a variable report declares an unusually large count. See [OD11088](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11088) and the [ReportCount expansion pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-reportcount-expansion-od11088). Source-only; no descriptor or device was used.

**OD11089 — USB HID accepts Report IDs outside its map and wire ranges:** a four-byte ID of 65,536 narrows the `UWORD` map maximum, producing a one-slot map before an out-of-range initialization write; IDs 256–65,535 fit the map but cannot be selected from the one-byte interrupt report ID. See [OD11089](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11089) and the [report-ID map width pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-report-id-map-width-od11089). Source-only; no descriptor or device was used.

**GD14369 — accelerated CopyBox paths use signed shifts to pack command fields:** NVIDIA has negative-Y and large-field shift cases; the explicitly buildable ATI Radeon override also shifts a negative destination Y. GPU clipping remains unresolved under GD9615. See [GD14369](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14369) and the [NVIDIA CopyBox pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nvidia-copybox-negative-coordinate-shift-gd14369). Source-only; no GPU operation was run.

**GD14458 — Mesa3DGL can turn a temporarily collapsed window layer into near-maximum framebuffer dimensions:** unsigned margin subtraction wraps before the negative-size clamp; the dimensions reach Gallium resource creation and failed attachments can leave buffer presentation disabled. Scoped to window-backed Mesa3DGL contexts during the collapsed-layer state documented in the source. See [GD14458](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14458-mesa3dgl-drawable-size-subtraction-underflows-for-a-collapsed-window-layer) and the [arithmetic and propagation recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa3dgl-drawable-size-arithmetic-gd14458). Optional Mesa3DGL target; source-only, no build or runtime operation.

**OD11095 — Serial and parallel device `Open()` hooks leave `io_Error` clear when their first per-unit allocation fails, so Exec reports success with `io_Unit == NULL`; both `Close()` hooks dereference that pointer. Conditional on low memory and these explicitly built device modules. See [OD11095](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11095-serial-and-parallel-devices-report-a-successful-open-when-unit-record-allocation-fails) and the [open-failure trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#serial-parallel-unit-record-allocation-failure-od11095). Source-only; no device operation or allocation failure was run.
**OD11094 — Workbench USB HID report-count overflow leaves a one-byte input buffer:** a four-byte-encoded Report ID Global item with value 65,535 wraps `max + 1` in the 16-bit count; the callback strips that byte, then the keyboard parser reads its fields past the one-byte allocation. Optional workbench USB HIDD target; malformed descriptor only. See [OD11094](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11094-workbench-usb-hid-report-count-overflow-leaves-a-one-byte-input-buffer) and the [report-count overflow pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#workbench-usb-hid-report-count-overflow-od11094). Source-only; no descriptor or device was used.

**OD11090 — USB Bluetooth can strand commands admitted during worker shutdown:** `devBeginIO()` checks the deny flag before `PutMsg()`; on ExecSMP a command can reach the queue after interface-release cleanup's final drain, with no worker left to reply. Optional USB Bluetooth target; no in-tree caller found. See [OD11090](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11090-usb-bluetooth-can-strand-commands-queued-during-worker-shutdown) and the [shutdown-admission trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-bluetooth-shutdown-admission-od11090). Source-only; no request or device was used.

**OD11091 — USB printer can admit I/O after worker shutdown drains:** a caller can pass `ncp_DenyRequests` before teardown, then enqueue after the final queue drain; read/write signaling can also use the deleted task-port object before `ncp_Task` is cleared. Optional USB printer target; no in-tree client found. See [OD11091](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11091-usb-printer-admits-requests-after-its-workers-shutdown-drain) and the [shutdown-admission trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-printer-shutdown-admission-od11091). Source-only; no printer or request was used.

**OD11092 — USB CDC ACM, CP210x and PL2303 can enqueue requests after worker shutdown:** each checks `ncp_DenyRequests` before queue insertion, then teardown drains and frees task resources; on ExecSMP a delayed request can arrive after the final drain, and CDC ACM can signal through a deleted task-port object. Optional targets; source-only. See [OD11092](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11092-usb-serial-classes-can-enqueue-requests-after-worker-shutdown) and the [shutdown-admission trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-serial-shutdown-admission-od11092).

**OD11093 — PalmPDA, STIr4200 and RawWrap can strand requests during teardown:** each checks `ncp_DenyRequests` before enqueue, then drains and frees task resources; a cross-CPU caller can enqueue after the final drain. PalmPDA read/write signaling can also access its deleted task port. Optional USB targets; source-only. See [OD11093](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11093-palmpda-stir4200-and-rawwrap-can-strand-requests-admitted-during-teardown) and the [shutdown-admission trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-palmpda-stir4200-shutdown-admission-od11093).

**EK844 — Sashimi can return a freed resource on ExecSMP:** `OpenResource()` releases the ResourceList read lock before Sashimi increments its open count; local-only `Forbid()` does not close that gap, and the count updates themselves can race. See [EK844](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek844) and the [resource lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1977). Optional debug tool; source-only, no interleaving was run.

**EK845 — Sashimi frees a resource after removal rejects it as busy:** `Off` cleanup ignores `RemoveSashimiResource()`'s in-use result and frees the still-published resource, leaving a dangling ResourceList node. See [EK845](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek845) and the [removal cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2006). Source-only; no `Off` sequence was run.

**EK846 — Concurrent Sashimi starts can add duplicate resource names on ExecSMP:** the absence check uses local `Forbid()`, then `AddResource()` locks only the later insertion, so two starts can both publish. See [EK846](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek846) and the [duplicate publication trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1848). Optional debug tool; source-only, no duplicate publication was run.

**GD14459 — `test-layers` dereferences an empty slot in `scrolllayer`:** a valid layer ID with no layer prints a warning but continues to read `layers[i]->Flags` and call `ScrollLayer()`. This is separate from GD10889's out-of-range index. See [GD14459](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14459-test-layers-scroll-command-dereferences-an-empty-layer-slot-after-reporting-it-missing) and the [source/caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-scrolllayer-empty-slot-gd14459). Optional test utility; source-only.

**EK67 — Generic Exec startup silently disables MungWall when `KRN_CmdLine` also requests StackSnoop:** the later option assignment replaces the independent MungWall flag. Conditional on a boot command line containing both options; PPC-CHRP uses a separate initializer. See [EK67](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek67-mungwall-stacksnoop-co-option) and the [co-option reachability trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L136). Source-only; no boot was run.


**EK9412 — Security filesystem interception continues after replacement DOS entries fail to publish:** ignored constructor/AddDosEntry failures can leave the intercepted volume without one or both DOS-visible aliases. See [EK9412](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9412) and the [replacement insertion trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8917). Source-only.

**EK9413 — Security volume probing uses DOS-list names and handler ports after unlocking:** concurrent unmount can invalidate the saved BSTR and handler port before probe use. See [EK9413](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9413) and the [DOS-list lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8919). Source-only; no unmount was run.

**EK9414 — A 256-byte security key-file path wraps to an empty BSTR:** on the reviewed SFS path, the empty path resolves to the root directory, so later configuration reads may use the wrong directory. See [EK9414](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9414) and the [BSTR/SFS trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8921). Source-only; no key file or filesystem was used.

**EK9415 — Security server reports ready after volume initialization fails:** a probe-list allocation failure leaves `Configured` false, which access checks treat as permission granted. See [EK9415](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9415) and the [startup/authorization trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8923). Source-only; no allocation failure or server start was induced.


**EK9388 — Parthenope dereferences failed ELF debug-metadata allocations:** a failed symbol-string or per-symbol allocation is used immediately; outer metadata allocation failures instead go unreported while ELF loading succeeds. Optional Sam440 Parthenope boot target. See [EK9388](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9388) and the [loader coverage row](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L840). Source-only; no low-memory boot was run.


**EK9395 — Quoted Exec debug-flag lists can hang startup:** the separator loop never advances after the first word. Generic runtime-debug builds only; m68k Amiga compiles the helper out. See [EK9395](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9395) and the [parser trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5857). Source-only; no boot was run.

**EK9396 — Exec debug flag names and `ALL` match prefixes:** `init` selects the earlier `InitCode` entry instead of `InitResident`, and any token beginning with `all` enables every flag. Generic runtime-debug builds only. See [EK9396](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9396) and the [parser trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5857). Source-only; no boot or logging run was performed.


**EK9397 — PPC CHRP Efika discards generic critical-alert text:** its selected kernel keeps the generic `krnPutC()` hook, which returns success without output, so `KrnDisplayAlert()` renders nothing. Pegasos and Sam440 select other output hooks. See [EK9397](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9397) and the [target-selection trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5914). Source-only; no alert was run.


**EK8832 — x86-64 PC BSP CPU-count growth can outstrip TSS storage after allocation failure:** the new CPU maximum is published before both replacement arrays succeed; AP setup can index the retained BSP-only TSS array. Partial replacements can also leak. Conditional on x86-64 PC SMP low-memory startup. See [EK8832](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8832) and the [BSP reconfiguration trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6127). Source-only; no allocation failure or AP start was induced.


**EK538 — `GetEntropy()` can fill a buffer but return a negative count:** its unsigned 32-bit request length is cast to signed `LONG` after generation; direct requests of 2 GiB or more cannot be reported accurately. Checked-in POSIX and stdc callers cap requests below this boundary; external resource clients remain unverified. See [EK538](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek538) and the [result-width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6699). Source-only; no large buffer was used.


**EK8859 — Optional Pegasos CHRP kernel startup parks before kernel-resource/Exec handoff:** its entry relocates boot data, then enters an unconditional empty loop. The architecture target has no checked-in aggregate/package edge. See [EK8859](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8859) and the [entry/target trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5995). Source-only; no build or boot was run.


**EK8932 — m68k bootstrap resident scanning can overrun its fixed table:** a scan appends every match without checking remaining slots; enough Residents overwrite the adjacent temporary ExecBase. Supported ROM density is unverified. See [EK8932](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8932) and the [table-boundary trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7182). Source-only; no ROM or boot was used.


**EK8795 — Far-past pthread condition deadlines can overflow signed 32-bit subtraction:** the absolute-time conversion subtracts current seconds before clamping a negative interval; wrong-delay effects depend on compiler handling of signed overflow. The relative helper is unaffected. See [EK8795](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8795) and the [caller/arithmetic trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8405). Source-only; no timed wait was run.


**EK9428 — VMM copies an unchecked config token into a 20-byte stack buffer:** its MMU config reader accepts up to 78-character tokens and `GetNthString()` has no destination capacity. Optional VMM target/configuration; other caller buffers are not generalized here. See [EK9428](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9428) and the [caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6175). Source-only; no config or startup was run.


**EK9424 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot diagnostics truncate high BSP addresses:** `%08x` formatting and 32-bit casts omit upper address bits in serial diagnostics only. See [EK9424](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9424) and the [format trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6151). Source-only; no boot was run.

**EK9425 — Early AArch64 Raspberry Pi diagnostics access UART before initialization:** exception and early allocation-failure logging reach `putByte()` while the peripheral/UART base is still zero-derived. Board behavior remains unverified. See [EK9425](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9425) and the [UART ordering trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6159). Source-only; no hardware access was performed.

**EK9426 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi skips initrd packages when the length wraps to zero:** the 64-bit endpoint difference is stored in 32-bit `pkg_size`; a nonempty exact 4-GiB multiple is treated as absent. See [EK9426](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9426) and the [package-gate trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6156). Conditional on an unusually large valid initrd; source-only.


**EK9429 — VMM can accept a write-buffer size without resizing the active cache:** task creation, message allocation, or replacement-buffer allocation may fail silently after the new value is committed. Optional VMM/page-handler path; default AROS reachability is separately limited by EK9906. See [EK9429](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9429) and the [resize trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6179). Source-only.

**EK9906 — AROS VMM passes a NULL paging base to `AddMemList()`:** the AROS range allocator leaves `VirtAddrStart` unset but returns success; the selected MUI starter then initializes a memory header through NULL. Optional VMM path; default package reachability is not claimed. See [EK9906](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9906) and the [range/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L67). Source-only; no VMM start was run.


**EK9430 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi trusts BSP package/member lengths beyond the initrd:** its scan and load passes do not validate embedded total/name/data extents against the firmware-provided buffer. Conditional on a truncated or inconsistent PKG initrd. See [EK9430](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9430) and the [package extent trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6181). Source-only; no package or boot was used.


**EK9431 — m68k CyberGraphX lock returns a native bitmap pointer the unlock thunk cannot resolve:** the generated lock thunk returns the native handle unchanged, while unlock maps its argument as a guest pointer/shadow. Conditional on emulated guest use of a CyberGraphX HIDD bitmap. See [EK9431](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9431) and the [handle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7648). Source-only; no guest call was run.

**EK9445 — m68k CyberGraphX base-address output can overwrite adjacent guest memory:** the native handler writes an 8-byte host `IPTR` through a 4-byte guest `LBMI_BASEADDRESS` slot on 64-bit hosts. Conditional on a guest bitmap lock requesting that tag. See [EK9445](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9445) and the [width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7648). Source-only; no guest memory write was run.


**EK9389 — Contended timed pthread locks can outlast expired deadlines:** signed 32-bit seconds are converted to unsigned timeval seconds before subtraction; a past deadline can wrap into a large timer interval. Applies to contended timed mutex and rwlock calls. See [EK9389](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9389) and the [deadline trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5839). Source-only; no lock or timer request was run.


**EK9390 — AArch64 startup silently omits device-tree RAM ranges after the eighth:** see [details](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9390).

**EK9393 — Concurrent direct RawPutChar calls race the x86-64 PC boot-console cursor and mirror:** see [details](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9393).

**EK513 — Exec bootstrap dereferences failed support-base or SMP lock-resource allocations:** see [details](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek513).

**EK422 — Supervisor-mode FindMem can race optional VMM memory-list publication on ExecSMP:** see [details](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek422).

**OD9921 — SANA-II network-device Open reads the extended request before validating its length:** Etherlink III, NVIDIA, Atheros5000, Intel Pro/100, Broadcom4400, Prism2, Realtek8180 and Rhine access `ios2_BufferManagement` before checking `mn_Length`. The selected AROSTCP request helper allocates `sizeof(*req)`, so the short-allocation trigger is limited to external or other clients that provide less than a full `IOSana2Req`. See [OD9921](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9921) and the [Open/caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od9921-short-sana2-open-request-and-arostcp-caller-recheck). Source-only; no request was opened.

**[GD14461](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14461-amigavideo-loses-the-current-sprite-when-replacement-allocation-fails) — AmigaVideo removes an existing sprite before allocating a size-changed replacement, leaving the sprite null if that allocation fails.** Applies to m68k AmigaVideo `ChangeExtSpriteA()` callers; source details and trigger scope are in the linked finding.

**[GD14462](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14462-amigavideo-selects-the-sprite-display-band-from-a-truncated-y-coordinate) — AmigaVideo truncates the sprite Y coordinate to 8 bits while selecting stacked-display settings, potentially using an earlier band's resolution or interlace mode.** Applies to m68k AmigaVideo displays with stacked bands and differing settings; see the source trace.

**[GD14463](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14463-amigavideo-shifts-negative-sprite-coordinates-as-signed-integers) — AmigaVideo left-shifts signed negative X/Y coordinates while packing sprite registers, which is undefined in C.** Applies when negative off-screen coordinates reach the m68k AmigaVideo cursor or sprite encoder; see the source trace.

**[GD14464](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14464-amigavideo-accepts-wide-sprites-while-encoding-only-16-pixels) — AmigaVideo accepts sprites up to 64 pixels on AGA hardware, but encodes only 16 pixels while AGA features are disabled.** Applies to numbered sprites before AGA mode is enabled; see the source trace.

**[GD14465](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14465-amigavideo-uses-one-sprite-fetch-mode-for-buffers-with-different-layouts) — AmigaVideo changes a shared sprite fetch mode per shape but uses it for every active sprite buffer, so mixed widths can misread or overwrite sprite data.** Applies to mixed-width numbered sprites on AGA-enabled AmigaVideo; see the source trace.

**[GD14466](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14466-amigavideo-never-publishes-numbered-sprite-buffers-into-the-copper-list) — AmigaVideo initializes every sprite channel to null but never records numbered-sprite copper pointer patch locations, so successful nonzero sprite changes remain invisible.** Applies to the selected m68k AmigaVideo HIDD; see the source trace.

**[OD11098](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11098-radeon-bitmap-pitch-wraps-out-of-the-pitch-offset-register) — Radeon bitmap creation accepts a 32-bit pitch that wraps to zero when packed into the 32-bit pitch/offset word.** Conditional on a sufficiently wide offscreen bitmap obtaining VRAM in the optional Radeon HIDD; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See the [Radeon pitch-bound trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#radeon-bitmap-pitch-wrap-od11098).

**[OD11097](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11097-etherlink-iii-frees-an-opener-while-the-rx-soft-interrupt-can-still-traverse-it) — Etherlink III can free a shared opener while another CPU’s RX soft interrupt traverses the opener list, because `Disable()` is local on ExecSMP.** Applies to explicitly built Etherlink III on ExecSMP with shared opens and overlapping close/receive activity; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See the [opener lifetime trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#etherlink3-opener-rx-softint-lifetime-od11097).

**[OD11096](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11096-usb-hid-mouse-discards-wheel-report-magnitude) — The optional USB HID mouse class turns any nonzero wheel delta into one notch, dropping additional movement encoded in larger reports.** Applies when a relative Z/Wheel report has magnitude greater than one; see the source trace.

**[EK568](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek568) — pthread timed-lock cleanup can pass an unqueued timer request to `AbortIO()`, whose timer implementation removes it as if it were linked.** The main trigger is a contended timed lock with a zero converted interval; see the [timer cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-timed-lock-cleanup-ek568).

**[GD14467](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14467-planar-bltbitmap-downward-overlap) — Generic planar `BltBitMap()` walks overlapping rows top-to-bottom even when the destination is below the source, so `MoveRaster()` can propagate overwritten rows while scrolling.** Applies to downward overlapping copies through generic software bitmaps; HIDD backends are outside the finding.

**[GD14468](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14468-findcolor-unextended-colormap) — `FindColor(..., -1)` can scan past the palette when `PalExtra` is absent because the signed sentinel becomes an unsigned loop bound.** Applies to a valid `GetColorMap()` colormap without a subsequent `AttachPalExtra()` call; no maintained in-tree trigger was established.

**[GD14469](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14469-amigavideo-dereferences-a-missing-pixel-format-descriptor-for-truecolor-sprites) — AmigaVideo truecolor cursor and numbered-sprite conversion dereferences NULL for valid `Native` pixel-format descriptors.** Conditional on the optional m68k AmigaVideo HIDD receiving a truecolor HIDD bitmap in `ChangeExtSpriteA()`.

**[EK9183](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9183) — `AddTaskHook()` dereferences its queued-hook node after allocation failure instead of returning `FALSE`.** Scoped to selected `task.resource` builds when an external or indirect client registers a queued hook under memory pressure; no in-tree producer was found.

**[OD10000](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10000) — PCI ATA can retain ownership of a claimed controller when all channels are rejected or their probe records cannot be allocated, leaving no ATA bus and preventing other drivers from claiming the PCI device.** Applies to selected i386-PC, x86-64-PC, and Sam440 PCI ATA HIDD builds.

**[OD10001](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10001) — PCI ATA's method-base failure cleanup releases the wrong four OOP attribute-base IDs, risking live PCI base-reference loss while leaking ATA/HW references.** Conditional on method-base acquisition failure in the selected PCI ATA module.

**[OD10002](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10002) — PCI ATA initialization leaks its storage-root object when a later setup step fails.** Applies to the selected module's failure rollback after root creation.

**[OD10003](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10003) — DRM EDID base-block reading leaks the raw 128-byte allocation if the parsed wrapper allocation fails.** Conditional on successful EDID read followed by wrapper-allocation failure in the optional DRM callers.

**[OD10004](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10004) — DRM EDID parsing resets accumulated color-format flags for each CTA extension, dropping formats advertised only in an earlier extension.** Applies to optional Nouveau parsing of revision 1.3 EDIDs with multiple CTA blocks; no default-image inclusion is claimed.

**[OD10005](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10005) — VMware cursor-plane setup ignores failure to create required hotspot properties and continues registering the plane.** Conditional on property-allocation failure in the optional VMware DRM target; no default-image inclusion is claimed.

**[OD10006](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10006) — The generic DRM EDID helper parses the previous EDID after a property update fails.** See the detailed finding for the conditional caller and consequence.

**[OD10007](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10007) — CRTC initialization leaves a freed display unit linked after CRC-source allocation fails.** The finding traces VMware and Nouveau callers; affected target selection is detailed in the report.

**[OD10008](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10008) — Nouveau leaks both display allocations when NV04 flip-event construction fails.** Applies to the optional Nouveau pre-NV50 display path.

**[OD10009](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10009) — Nouveau exposes an NV04 CRTC with unusable cursor state after cursor-buffer setup fails.** Conditional on cursor-buffer allocation failure in the optional Nouveau target.

**[OD10010](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10010) — Failed NV04 page flips leave scanout BO tracking and pin ownership inconsistent.** See the report for the conditional page-flip path.

**[OD10011](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10011) — Nouveau reports NV04 vblank enabled after vblank-event construction fails.** Conditional on event construction failure in the optional Nouveau target.

**[OD10012](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10012) — Nouveau NV04/NV50 encoder constructors ignore DRM encoder initialization failure.** Optional display setup can attach an unregistered encoder after allocation failure and report success; constructor-specific cleanup consequences are detailed in the report.

**[OD10013](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10013) — NV04 video overlay divides by zero for a one-pixel destination dimension.** Conditional on overlay setup with a destination width or height of one.

**[OD10014](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10014) — NV17 TV setup attaches DRM TV properties after property-creation failure.** Conditional on the optional Nouveau NV17 TV path and property-allocation failure.

**[OD10015](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10015) — NV50 head setup discards primary-plane construction failure.** The overwrite affects pre-GV100 and GV100+ constructor paths. Optional Nouveau configuration; source-only.

**[OD2642](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2642) — Raspberry Pi boot FDT metadata allocation exhaustion is unchecked, causing a boot fault or incomplete tree on selected ARM32/AArch64 targets.** Conditional on exhausting the fixed temporary metadata pool; source-only.

**[OD2643](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2643) — ARM32 Raspberry Pi boot lookup can keep walking from the wrong ancestor after a missing FDT path component, potentially mapping an unrelated node's `reg` as the local interrupt block.** Conditional on a stale/malformed local-interrupt symbol path; the AArch64 lookup rejects missing components.

**[OD2644](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2644) — ARM32/AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot parsers trust FDT section extents and terminators, so a truncated or inconsistent tree can cause out-of-bounds reads or invalid boot-tree state.** Source-only; malformed FDT required.

**[OD10016](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10016) — Optional NV50 Nouveau cursor/overlay setup ignores immediate-channel map failure and can later use the unmapped pointer.** Conditional on NVIF mapping failure followed by plane update; source-only.

**[OD10017](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10017) — Optional pre-Volta NV50 display resume ignores a failed core-channel initialization and proceeds as successful.** Conditional on a core push-channel wait error during resume/runtime reinitialization.

**[OD10018](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10018) — Optional GB202 Nouveau ignores RM mode-possible errors and rejection, then continues startup or programs the rejected mode.** Visible result depends on GSP-RM/hardware; source-only.

**[OD10019](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10019) — Optional GB202 head setup wraps exhausted tile/physical-window searches and can submit a resource already owned by another head.** Conditional on full resource exhaustion; source-only.

**[OD10020](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10020) — Optional NV50 head creation ignores CRTC registration errors and may continue with a missing or partially published CRTC.** Conditional on DRM object/name/CRC initialization failure.

**[OD10021](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10021) — Optional Nouveau underscan accepts borders larger than half the mode dimension and wraps the output viewport subtraction.** Conditional on underscan and a small active mode; source-only.

**[OD10022](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10022) — Optional Nouveau aspect scaling or underscan overflows a 32-bit 19-bit-fixed-point ratio for dimensions of 8,192 or more.** Conditional on large modes; source-only.

**[OD10023](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10023) — Optional Nouveau Turing-and-later output paths ignore a failed display-ID push and continue state changes.** Conditional on a transient push-channel reservation failure; hardware effect unverified.

**[OD10024](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10024) — Optional NV50 display output allocation failures can leave outputs missing while initialization reports success; one path also leaks its unregistered wrapper.** Conditional on allocation failure; source-only.

**[OD10025](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10025) — Optional Nouveau VRAM-backed display push buffers are published after the visibility-flush wait times out.** Pascal default or forced-VRAM configuration; stale command fetch is hardware-conditional.

**[OD10026](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10026) — Optional NV50 DP MST manager initialization can fail, then mode-config rollback finalizes its uninitialized private object.** Conditional on topology-state allocation failure after encoder registration.

**[OD10027](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10027) — Optional NV50 SPWG LVDS enable can dereference NULL EDID after the BIOS strap-mode fallback accepts the panel.** Conditional on missing EDID and the relevant VBIOS configuration.

**[OD10070](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10070) — PCI xHCI may signal worker tasks before their pointers are published, if an event arrives during startup or after worker creation fails.** Conditional on an event during the pre-worker interrupt window or worker-creation failure in selected Raspberry Pi AArch64, RISC-V OpenSBI, or x86-64 PC USB package configurations.

**[OD10071](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10071) — NV04 resume programs the hardware cursor even when its VRAM repin fails.** Conditional on the optional Nouveau target and cursor pin failure during system resume.

**OD10007 update (2026-11-02):** added the NV04 pre-publication failure route: if mode-object registration or CRTC-name allocation fails, `nv04_crtc_create()` ignores the error and can return success after allocating cursor/head/event state; because the CRTC never entered `crtc_list`, normal mode-config cleanup cannot reach its destructor. This is separate from the existing post-publication CRC-source failure.

**[OD11099](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11099-radeon-8-bit-offscreen-bitmaps-use-the-wrong-destination-datatype) — Radeon 8-bit offscreen bitmaps retain datatype zero instead of the indexed 8-bit register encoding, so accelerated copies can use the wrong pixel format.** Applies to explicitly built Radeon HIDD bitmap operations; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See the [datatype trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#radeon-8bit-datatype-od11099).

**[OD11100](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11100-designware-uart-receive-interrupt-can-overrun-its-stack-buffer) — The OpenSBI DesignWare UART receive callback can overrun its 513-byte stack buffer if it drains at least 514 bytes in one invocation.** The missing bound is clear in source, but the selected hardware path has not been shown to refill the buffer to that threshold; this remains a low-confidence candidate. See the [receive-bound trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dwuart-rx-buffer-bound-od11100).




**[OD11102](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11102-usbdevice-name-allocation-failure-is-not-checked) — USBDevice does not check pooled allocations for product, manufacturer, or serial strings, then writes through the NULL result during device construction.** Reached through hub enumeration in the Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 USB packages; conditional on pool allocation failure. Source-only. See the [name-string allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usbdevice-name-string-allocation-od11102).


**[OD11104](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11104-workbench-usb-massstorage-underreports-capacity-by-one-sector) — Workbench USB MassStorage underreports the sector count by one, so the GPT writer places its backup header one sector before the device's actual last LBA.** Included in Raspberry Pi ARM/AArch64 package class lists; a GPT write client is required. See the [capacity-field trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#workbench-usb-massstorage-capacity-od11104).

**[OD11106](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11106-ahci-rejects-full-track-format-requests) — AHCI rejects the Workbench Format utility's full-track or full-cylinder TD_FORMAT transfer because its maximum is one byte below a track's published size.** Applies to the selected AHCI driver and explicitly built Format utility; source and caller path are confirmed. See the [full-track format trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahci-full-track-format-bound-od11106).

**[OD11107](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11107-ahci-format-rejects-offsets-after-first-track) — AHCI compares a TD_FORMAT absolute disk offset with one track’s byte length, rejecting nonzero-offset requests that pass its separate length check.** Conditional on a direct client using a shorter format request; BHFormat's full-track or full-cylinder request fails earlier under OD11106. See the [format-offset trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahci-format-offset-bound-od11107).

**[OD11108](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11108-ahci-td-eject-reports-success-without-ejecting) — AHCI accepts removable-media TD_EJECT requests but completes them successfully without issuing an eject/load command.** Applies to removable AHCI units; C:Eject also attempts SCSI pass-through. See the [TD_EJECT trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahci-td-eject-no-op-od11108).

**[OD11109](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11109-workbench-load-command-ejects-media-and-masks-scsi-failure) — Workbench `Load` always sends a SCSI eject CDB after its load CDB, and then overwrites the SCSI result with the trackdisk request result.** The AHCI trackdisk request is itself a successful no-op for removable media (OD11108), so this can report success after ejecting. See the [Eject/Load trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#workbench-load-command-od11109).

**[GD14471](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14471-reqtools-shared-idcmp-port-walk-omits-smp-lock) — ReqTools’ shared-IDCMP close helper and file requester timer cleanup traverse/remove UserPort messages without the port spinlock required to serialize ExecSMP producers/consumers.** Scoped to ExecSMP ReqTools paths; source-only.

**[GD14472](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14472-rtlockwindow-reads-private-tail-of-requesters) — ReqTools `rtLockWindow()` reads its private magic and backpointer beyond ordinary public `Requester` objects while scanning a window’s requester chain.** Applies when the window already has a non-ReqTools requester; source-only.


**[OD3423](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3423-usb-printer-short-device-id-response) - USB printer class consumes the GET_DEVICE_ID length header and payload without checking actual transfer counts; short headers leave the length partly uninitialized, and lengths below two cause reads before the allocated string.** Trigger requires a short or malformed printer response; xHCI reports short packets as success. Source-only.

**[OD3424](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3424-usb-printer-port-status-reads-unreceived-byte) - USB printer PDCMD_QUERY decodes an uninitialized status byte after an error or zero-byte short success.** Trigger requires a failed or short printer status response; xHCI can report the short response as successful. Source-only.


**[GD14473](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14473-nfloattext-align-tag-accesses-instance-before-super-new) - The optional NFloattext class reads instance data from its class pointer before superclass object allocation when MUIA_NFloattext_Align is supplied, then resets the requested value to the default.** Requires a client using the public alignment attribute; no checked-in caller passes it. Source-only.


**[GD14474](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14474-nfloattext-getentry-returns-unwrapped-tail-on-allocation-failure) - NFloattext's wrapped-line getter returns the selected line's unbounded source-text tail when its temporary substring allocation fails.** Requires a wrapped entry and allocation failure in the optional class. Source-only.

**[GD14475](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14475---nlisttree-open-all-dereferences-the-table-of-an-empty-child-list) - NListtree's Open-All method indexes the first table slot before checking whether a non-root list is empty, faulting for an empty child list.** Requires an explicitly built/loaded NListtree MCC or legacy Listtree wrapper client to call Open-All on a concrete empty child list; the wrapper forwards the selector unchanged, while checked-in direct callers use the root. Both class aggregate edges are disabled. Source-only.
**[GD14477](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14477) - Vulkan-Hpp display-query wrappers (display-plane, RandR, DRM, and WinRT) create owning `DisplayKHR` objects whose destructor calls `vkReleaseDisplayEXT` even though the query did not acquire display control.** If another wrapper owns the same acquired display, its premature release can revoke that control. Optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII client path; no checked-in caller or default inclusion claimed. Source-only.
**[GD14479](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14479) - Vulkan-Hpp `getLatencyTimingsNV()` does not trim its result vector to the fill call's returned count.** A changing latency-report count can leave default entries at the end of the returned vector. Optional `VK_NV_low_latency2` RAII path; no checked-in caller claimed. Source-only.

**[GD14480](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14480) - Nouveau compatibility I²C adapter rejects single-message reads.** It advertises `I2C_FUNC_I2C` and provides `i2c_master_recv()`, but the transfer dispatcher rejects the one-message read that helper submits; CH7006 and SIL164 encoder read helpers consequently fail. Optional Nouveau HIDD, excluded from the default aggregate at this checkout. Source-only.

**[GD14481](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14481) - Nouveau compatibility I²C transfer dereferences an unallocated device.** The write and combined-transfer paths call `OOP_DoMethod()` without checking whether temporary I²C device construction succeeded. Optional Nouveau HIDD; allocation failure can fault a transfer. Source-only.

**[GD14482](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14482) - Nouveau internal I²C bit-bang truncates message lengths to eight bits.** Its 8-bit loop counter truncates the 16-bit message length and can report success without transferring all bytes. Conditional on explicitly built internal-bitbang Nouveau use; no in-tree >255-byte caller was found. Source-only.

**[GD14483](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14483) - Nouveau compatibility I²C adapter treats one-byte register reads as probes.** The common one-byte write/read pair is consumed by the address-only probe branch, which returns success without transferring either data byte; NVKM then returns stale register data. Optional Nouveau HIDD. Source-only.

**[GD9396](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9396) — LinuxFB DirectColor gamma updates ignore failed `FBIOPUTCMAP` calls and still report success, hiding partial or absent hardware updates. The host ioctl failure is conditional. Source-only.**
**[GD9397](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9397) — LinuxFB pseudocolor updates change the software colormap before unchecked host writes, then report success when `FBIOPUTCMAP` fails, allowing software and hardware colors to diverge. Source-only.**

**[GD9395](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9395) — On the LinuxFB x86 32-bpp truecolor path, the `1 << bpp` guard can reduce to one and reject nonzero `SetColors` entries; unchecked callers then store an uninitialized `pixval` in the bitmap's pen lookup table, which graphics later uses for pen-based blits. The shift is undefined in C and the trigger is architecture/compiler dependent. Source-only.**

**[GD9394](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9394) — Intuition accepts negative window minimum sizes; later size-gadget and zoom paths cast them to unsigned limits, potentially snapping the window to its maximum. The trigger depends on caller-supplied negative minima; no checked-in direct `WindowLimits()` caller was found. Source-only.**


**[OD4100](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4100) — Raspberry Pi USB2OTG ignores required AHB-idle, reset, FIFO-flush and channel-halt timeout results during initialization and recovery, then continues controller programming. The source-level omission is clear; the resulting hardware behavior is conditional. Source-only.


**[OD1522](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1522) — On Raspberry Pi ExecSMP builds using USB2OTG, an aligned bulk-IN DMA segment larger than 16 KiB can bypass the bounce buffer while ending partway through a cache line. Concurrent writes to another allocation sharing that edge line can race the controller's whole-line cache maintenance. This remains a conditional, medium-low-confidence candidate; no checked-in caller establishes the overlap. Source-only.
**[OD839](AROS-other-drivers.md#od839) — Numeric zero-length writes and empty NUL-terminated string writes can make the PC, Sam440, and OpenSBI UART HIDDs read and transmit beyond the request buffer after serial.device wraps its pending length.** Requires an explicitly built serial.device and one of those UART backends with `UART_LSR_THRE` set; source-only.
