**OD11110 — USB MassStorage's removable monitor can enqueue an internal device request after the unit worker's final drain; it then waits forever for a reply, and last-close waits forever for that monitor to exit. Conditional on cross-CPU request/teardown overlap on ExecSMP in the explicitly buildable optional class. See [OD11110](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11110) and the [shutdown/tunnel trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-internal-tunnel-shutdown-admission-od11110). Source-only; no device or schedule was run.
**OD3210 — Speech and Narrator last-close hooks skip audio release if their temporary reply port or request allocation fails, yet still report close success. Previously acquired audio.device requests and playback buffers remain allocated. Triggered when temporary port/request creation fails during last close; explicitly buildable optional devices. See [OD3210](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3210) and the [close/allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#speech-narrator-last-close-release-allocation-failure-od3210). Source-only; no allocation failure or close was run.
**OD3211 — speechcore drops each sentence's final incomplete 512-byte PCM block because it flushes only full blocks and resets the buffer for each sentence. Speech/Narrator playback and Say WAV output cannot recover those bytes. See [OD3211](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3211) and the [renderer/sink trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#speechcore-sentence-tail-pcm-drop-od3211). Source-only; no synthesis or audio output was run.
**[GD9414](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9414) — Intuition silently abandons unloading an unused decorator if async-action allocation fails or the callback cannot create its reply port.** The node remains registered and its service receives no destroy message; persistence depends on a later unload attempt. Affected configurations require an active decorator service and allocation or signal-bit exhaustion. Source-only; no failure was induced.
**[OD4180](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4180) — VMware VKMS CRC generation dereferences a NULL BO mapping when mapping fails.** Scoped to an explicitly built VMware SVGA HIDD with VKMS enabled; this target is not connected to the standard PC boot package in this snapshot. Source-only; no mapping failure or CRC operation was induced.
**[OD11111](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11111) — VMware SVGA cursor preparation ignores a failed framebuffer BO mapping, then its GB-only or cursor-MOB update can copy from NULL.** Scoped to the explicitly buildable VMware HIDD and the stated cursor capability/map-failure path; standard PC boot inclusion is not claimed. Source-only; no cursor or mapping failure was exercised.
**[OD11112](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11112) — VMware command-buffer pool setup reports success after its MOB fallback mapping fails, then submits through missing storage and tears down through the DMA branch.** Scoped to the explicitly buildable VMware HIDD with DX/MOB support and the stated allocation-failure sequence; standard PC boot inclusion is not claimed. Source-only; no failure or device was exercised.



**OD11113 — DiskImage Expat buffer growth overflows its signed capacity:** `XML_GetBuffer()` doubles a signed `int` capacity without overflow or progress checks. A positive parse request above 1 GiB can overflow the doubling loop before Expat returns an allocation error. The optional DMG plugin passes a single `ULONG` plist length to `XML_Parse()`, so a sufficiently large readable plist can reach the path. See [OD11113](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11113) and the [large plist buffer-growth trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-expat-large-plist-buffer-growth-od11113). Source-only; no large plist or allocation was used.


**EK819 — RexxSupport `OPENPORT` crashes or leaves a published port on allocation/registration failure:** it dereferences unchecked `PortNode`/name allocations, fails to roll back after reply-allocation errors, and ignores a failed Rexx cleanup-resource registration while returning success. The port can remain public and pin the library without script-exit cleanup. Limited to explicit `workbench-libs-rexxsupport` builds; default package reachability is not established. See [EK819](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek819) and the [OPENPORT failure/rollback trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rexxsupport-openport-allocation-and-publication-failure-ek819). Source-only; no command or allocation/RPC failure was run.
**OD3941 — WirelessManager Amiga event loop uses a stale timer request after timeout changes:** a SANA-II signal callback can replace or cancel the timeout-list head while an older timer request remains active. The old timer signal can invoke a new first-EAPOL timeout too early, or leave the disconnect-recovery scan waiting until the canceled 30-second keepalive deadline. Scoped to the selected `CONFIG_DRIVER_SANA2=y`, `CONFIG_ELOOP=eloop_amiga` build. See [OD3941](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3941) and the [timer/signal ordering trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#wirelessmanager-eloop-timeout-rearm-caller-trace-od3941). Source-only; no event or timer was run.
- **[EK10612](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10612)** — Selected PC and Raspberry Pi timer backends update shared clock state from IRQ and task contexts without complete cross-CPU serialization on ExecSMP. Overlapping calls can lose or double-count elapsed time. See the [PC and Raspberry Pi caller traces](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pc-timer-eclock-update-smp-race-ek10612). Source-only.
- **[EK10613](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10613)** — On AArch64 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP systems whose selected timer IRQ is delivered (BCM2837/Pi 3), timer request insertion can snapshot the queue and later overwrite a compare deadline armed by another CPU. The selected AArch64 timer initializer also omits the list-lock initialization (EK10614); BCM2711/2712 use a VBlank fallback and remain excluded from the compare-deadline consequence. See the [timer compare trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#raspberry-pi-timer-compare-reprogramming-ek10613). Source-only.
- **[EK10614](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10614)** — The AArch64 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP timer initializer never sets `tb_ExecLockBase` or `tb_ListLock`, so request insertion, tick completion and AbortIO skip the cross-CPU queue lock. Concurrent timer queue operations can lose/corrupt requests. See the [initializer and queue-lock trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#raspberry-pi-timer-list-lock-missing-ek10614). Source-only.

Coverage-link repair: GD10288's coverage link now resolves to the explicit `setrgb4-component-expansion-pass` anchor in the Graphics/Desktop ledger; this restores the previously missing full-body/caller record for `rom/graphics/setrgb4.c`. No new finding ID was added.

**[OD9920](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9920-ahci-busy-wait-uses-uncalibrated-scale) — AHCI hard sleeps can use the `~0` calibration sentinel before timer initialization or after calibration failure, producing multi-billion-iteration busy loops.** Applies to selected i386-PC and x86-64-PC AHCI builds on the stated reset/calibration paths. See the [AHCI scale and call-order trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahci-uncalibrated-hard-sleep-scale-od9920). Source-only.


**[OD2573](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2573-ata-controller-construction-leaks-on-daemon-task-creation-failure) — ATA controller construction leaks the superclass-allocated object and class instance count when daemon task creation fails.** Applies to selected PCI ATA and optional Gayle ATA controller construction. See the [ATA startup rollback trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ata-controller-startup-rollback-od2573-od2574). Source-only.
**[OD2574](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2574-ata-controller-published-after-daemon-init-failure) — ATA publishes a controller after timer/daemon initialization fails; later disposal signals a NULL daemon pointer.** Applies to selected PCI ATA and optional Gayle ATA paths on the stated timer failures. See the [ATA startup rollback trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ata-controller-startup-rollback-od2573-od2574). Source-only.

**OD11115 — Hosted Unix parallel HIDD failure cleanup treats its zero-cleared descriptor as open when UnixIO object allocation fails, then calls cleanup methods through a NULL object.** Conditional on hosted Unix parallel HIDD unit construction and the UnixIO-object allocation failure. See [OD11115](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11115) and the [constructor failure trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hosted-parallel-hidd-unixio-allocation-failure-od11115). Source-only; no allocation failure or runtime operation was induced.

**OD3064 — PCNet32 never decrements its per-unit open count, so closing an exclusive opener leaves future opens permanently busy; rejected busy opens also increment the count.** Selected by standard i386-PC and x86_64-PC workbench builds through the active network aggregate. See [OD3064](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3064-pcnet32-open-count-never-decreases) and the [Open/Close count trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcnet32-open-close-count-reconciliation-od3064). Source-only; no device operation was run.

**OD3065 — PCNet32 overwrites and leaks its RX/TX DMA rings each time another shared opener starts the already-open unit.** Selected by standard i386-PC and x86_64-PC workbench builds through the active network aggregate. See [OD3065](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3065-pcnet32-restarts-and-leaks-dma-rings-on-every-shared-open) and the [shared-open allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcnet32-shared-open-dma-ring-replacement-od3065). Source-only.

**OD3066 — PCNet32 stops the NIC on every Close, including while shared clients remain and during cleanup of a rejected exclusive Open.** Selected by standard i386-PC and x86_64-PC workbench builds through the active network aggregate. See [OD3066](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3066-pcnet32-close-stops-the-device-for-every-opener) and the [shared-close/rejected-Open trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcnet32-shared-close-rejected-open-od3066). Source-only; no request or device was run.


**OD11116 — Nouveau USERD offset range validation can wrap:** on the generic NVIF path with a no-BAR USERD backend, `ouserd + USERD_size` can wrap and pass the memory-size check, after which the offset is used for USERD initialization and RAMFC setup. The checked-in Nouveau client uses offset zero; this remains conditional on a generic caller supplying a wrapping nonzero offset. See [OD11116](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11116) and the [source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-userd-offset-range-check-od11116). Source-only; no request or hardware was run.


**OD11117 — Nouveau RM engine construction ignores the common constructor's `-ENODEV` when an engine is disabled, then publishes/registers that engine anyway.** Applies to the selected GSP-RM CE, NVDEC, NVENC, NVJPG and OFA construction paths when their per-engine configuration option disables the engine. See [OD11117](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11117) and the [constructor/publication trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-rm-engine-constructor-ignores-disabled-engine-error-od11117). Source-only; no build or GPU operation was run.

**OD11118 — Nouveau enables a GSP RM display notification before linking its callback locally; a notification delivered in that interval is logged as unmatched and dropped.** Conditional on an HPD/DP IRQ arriving during callback registration; the timing depends on RM firmware behavior and confidence is medium. See [OD11118](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11118) and the [event registration/dispatch trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-display-event-registration-order-od11118). Source-only; no display event or hardware was exercised.

**OD11120 — Nouveau can leak the original allocation when a split GSP RPC fails.** The checked-in AROS callers do not currently produce payloads above the 16-page limit; retained as a low-reachability future/internal-caller candidate. See [OD11120](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11120) and the [selected-caller census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-rpc-split-request-selected-caller-census-od11120-2026-11-04). Source-only.

**OD11121 — Nouveau R535/R570/R580 RM control writes with no output payload treat the transport's `NULL` reply as success, skipping a nonzero RM command status.** Affected callers proceed as if the control command succeeded; this includes display notification registration. See [OD11121](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11121) and the [control-reply status trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-control-reply-status-and-ownership-review). Source-only; no firmware command was run.

**OD11122 — Nouveau's x86 ACPI `_DOD` parser leaks ACPICA's output buffer when the result shape or element types are invalid.** Conditional on malformed ACPI firmware with GSP-RM and ACPI enabled. See [OD11122](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11122) and the [ACPI validation/cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-acpi-and-registry-configuration-pass).
**OD11123 — On 64-bit Nouveau, an accepted `NOUVEAU_REGISTRY` DWORD above `UINT32_MAX` is narrowed and silently stored as its low 32 bits.** See [OD11123](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11123) and the [registry parse/type trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-acpi-and-registry-configuration-pass). Source-only; no configuration or GPU operation was run.


**OD11124 — Nouveau loses PMU-only GSP diagnostics during debugfs log retention.** Conditional on debugfs log retention being enabled and the PMU log being the only populated buffer. See [OD11124](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11124) and the [GSP retention review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-suspend-and-debugfs-retention-review). Source-only.

**OD11125 — Nouveau leaks GSP suspend/resume DMA page tables when suspend setup allocation fails.** Conditional on an allocation failure after partial suspend-resource construction; rollback and final destruction omit cleanup for these partial states. See [OD11125](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11125) and the [GSP suspend/retention review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-suspend-and-debugfs-retention-review). Source-only.


**OD11126 — Nouveau R535/R570/R580 leaks the RM control allocation when an unsupported instance-memory target is used as a display pushbuffer.** Conditional on GSP display channel initialization with an instance-memory UMEM. See [OD11126](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11126) and the [display pushbuffer error-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-pushbuffer-target-error-review). Source-only.


**OD11127 — Nouveau DP link training and AUX error handling dereference the RM response pointer after transport failure clears it.** Applies to R535-family GSP display paths. See [OD11127](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11127) and the [DP control error-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-displayport-control-error-review). Source-only.


**OD11128 — Nouveau display output discovery leaks its RM response on `TYPE_NONE` and invalid output metadata.** Conditional on one of those RM responses during R535-family display initialization. See [OD11128](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11128) and the [output discovery lifetime trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-output-and-acpi-review). Source-only.

**OD11129 — Nouveau's x86 ACPI backlight `_DSM` parser does not bound copies to its 4 KiB RM buffer.** Conditional on a supported firmware method returning more than 4 KiB of packed data. See [OD11129](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11129) and the [ACPI backlight parser trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-output-and-acpi-review). Source-only.


**OD11130 — Nouveau R535 display hotplug handling skips the 32nd display-mask bit.** Conditional on display ID 31 being reported. See [OD11130](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11130) and the [HPD notification bounds trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-hpd-notification-bounds-review). Source-only.


**OD11131 — Nouveau DP AUX size is unchecked across fixed 16-byte request, RM, and legacy handler buffers.** Conditional on a request size above 16 reaching a traced AUX implementation. See [OD11131](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11131) and the [AUX bounds trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-aux-rates-and-constructor-review). Source-only.

**OD11132 — Nouveau writes DP link rates through unchecked signed indices into an eight-entry table.** The checked-in DPCD producer supplies indices 0–7; an invalid index requires another NVIF client or future caller. See [OD11132](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11132) and the [link-rate bounds trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-aux-rates-and-constructor-review). Source-only.

**OD11133 — Nouveau display creation dereferences NULL when the display object allocation fails.** See [OD11133](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11133) and the [constructor allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-aux-rates-and-constructor-review). Source-only.


**OD11134 — R570/R580 Nouveau suspend errors can leave channels stopped or BAR2 disabled.** Conditional on an RPC or later suspend failure after state changes. See [OD11134](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11134) and the [FBSR suspend/resume trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r570-r580-fbsr-complete-body-review). Source-only.

**OD11135 — R535 Nouveau suspend leaks collected FBSR descriptors when a later descriptor allocation fails.** See [OD11135](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11135) and the [FBSR allocation cleanup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r570-r580-fbsr-complete-body-review). Source-only.


**OD11136 — Nouveau R535 BAR2 setup marks the aperture ready after its GSP page-directory update fails.** Conditional on an `UPDATE_BAR_PDE` RPC error during initialization. See [OD11136](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11136) and the [BAR2 setup error trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-bar2-rpc-error-review). Source-only.


**OD11137 — Nouveau BAR1 initialization leaves its root page-table backing pointer NULL when wrapper allocation fails.** Conditional on failure of the BAR1 mapping allocation after the old backing object is released. See [OD11137](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11137) and the [BAR initialization review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-bar-complete-body-review). Source-only.
**OD11138 — Nouveau truncates the framebuffer reserved-region boundary to 32 bits.** Selected R535/R570/R580 GSP can calculate the wrong preserved-memory size when the region end exceeds 4 GiB. See [OD11138](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11138) and the [R570/R580 GSP source review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r570-r580-gsp-complete-body-review). Source-only.

**OD11139 — Nouveau does not bound FMC ELF section-name offsets.** A malformed GH100-family FMC image can make section lookup read beyond its name table. See [OD11139](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11139) and the [GH100 firmware-loader review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gh100-gsp-boot-and-firmware-validation-review). Source-only.

**OD11140 — Nouveau divides by the firmware signature count without checking for zero.** A malformed Turing-through-AD102 booter image can fault driver initialization. See [OD11140](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11140) and the [TU102 bootstrap review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-tu102-gsp-bootstrap-and-teardown-review). Source-only.

**OD11141 — Nouveau reports fini success after secure-boot status or WPR booter-unload errors.** On Turing, TU116, GA100, GA102 and AD102 paths, `tu102_gsp_fini()` warns on these two errors but returns success; `r535_gsp_fini()` errors during suspend are propagated. See [OD11141](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11141) and the [TU102 bootstrap review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-tu102-gsp-bootstrap-and-teardown-review). Source-only.

**OD11142 — Nouveau reads GA102 booter metadata without checking its offset or size.** A malformed GA102/AD102 image can make firmware parsing read beyond the loaded buffer. See [OD11142](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11142) and the [generation-selector review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-generation-selector-callback-and-firmware-version-review). Source-only.

**OD11143 — Nouveau accepts a short FSP reply and reads unfilled fields.** A truncated boot-handshake response can produce a spurious success or failure. See [OD11143](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11143) and the [GH100 FSP reply review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gh100-fsp-reply-review). Source-only.

**OD11144 — Nouveau trusts an RPC response length shorter than its fixed header.** A truncated R535-family RPC record leaves header fields unchecked before use. See [OD11144](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11144) and the [R535 RPC transport review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-rpc-ring-wrap-and-split-failure-review). Source-only.

**OD11145 — Nouveau leaks FWSEC firmware allocations when FRTS setup fails.** Post-construction initialization errors return without releasing the local Falcon firmware object. See [OD11145](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11145) and the [FWSEC initialization review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-fwsec-failure-cleanup-review). Source-only.

**OD3144 — USB HID parser and Global Push allocation failures reach unchecked pointers.** Parser-context failure can cause NULL dereferences in selected generic, keyboard, or mouse paths; Global Push stack-node allocation is also unchecked. See [OD3144](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3144) and the [HID parser review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-allocation-and-descriptor-state-reconciliation).

**OD3145 — USB HID parser reads descriptor items past the declared end.** Truncated item headers or payloads are decoded without a complete-item bounds check. See [OD3145](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3145) and the [HID parser review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-allocation-and-descriptor-state-reconciliation).

**OD3146 — USB HID variable input with no usages indexes before the usage array.** A positive-count Variable Input with no local usages reaches the `nu - 1` index. See [OD3146](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3146) and the [HID parser review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-allocation-and-descriptor-state-reconciliation).

**OD3147 — USB HID parser dereferences an empty Global Push stack on Pop.** An unmatched Global Pop is processed in the first Report ID scan. See [OD3147](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3147) and the [HID parser review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-allocation-and-descriptor-state-reconciliation).

**OD11146 — Nouveau PFN clear splits virtual-memory state at unaligned byte boundaries.** `PFNCLR` updates page-table entries at page granularity but splits the VMA at the unaligned byte range without validating alignment. See [OD11146](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11146) and the [shared VMM implementation review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-shared-vmm-pfn-clear-review-od11146).

**OD11147 — Nouveau VMM map accepts an overflowing range before splitting its VMA.** An unsigned end-address wrap can bypass the containment check and feed an oversized interval to the VMA splitter. See [OD11147](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11147) and the [NVIF VMM dispatcher review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvif-vmm-dispatcher-review-od11146-od11147).

**OD11148 — Nouveau host-memory allocation error cleanup unreferences freed storage.** A rejected RAM payload frees the partial object but leaves its pointer published for the caller's error cleanup. See [OD11148](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11148) and the [Nouveau MMU memory helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mmu-memory-helper-review-od11148-od11149).

**OD11149 — Nouveau BAR1 mapping errors retain the allocated VMA.** GF100/NV50 map helpers do not release their BAR1 VMA when memory mapping fails. See [OD11149](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11149) and the [Nouveau MMU memory helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mmu-memory-helper-review-od11148-od11149).


**OD11151 candidate — Nouveau GK20A IOMMU map failure still publishes an active CPU-map reference.** If a future AROS Tegra integration reaches the IOMMU path, failed `vmap()` leaves fallback accessors without a mapping. Current checked-in AROS cannot reach the path: its Tegra constructor stub returns `-ENODEV`, and no platform-device caller exists. See [OD11151](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11151) and the [GK20A instance-memory review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gk20a-iommu-instance-memory-review-od11151).



**OD11152 — Nouveau GT215 link training consumes results after PMU fetch failure.** An ignored PMU result-fetch error leaves the uninitialized 64-word buffer consumed as training data, potentially marking bogus timing values as valid. See [OD11152](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11152) and the [GT215 RAM controller review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gt215-ram-controller-full-body-review-od11152).

**OD11153 — Nouveau GF100 RAM script uses address zero for register 0x137300.** Its descriptor is left zeroed by a misdirected setup assignment, so the RAM clock-source read and divider write target MMIO address zero. See [OD11153](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11153) and the [GF100 RAM controller review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gf100-ram-controller-full-body-review-od11153).

**OD11154 — Nouveau wrapped VRAM allocation leaks its object on node-allocation failure.** `nvkm_ram_wrap()` publishes a memory object before allocating its node and fails without releasing it; R535 BAR callers return without cleanup. See [OD11154](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11154) and the [shared RAM helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-shared-vram-allocation-and-mode-register-calculators-od11154).

**OD11155 — Nouveau preinit succeeds while VPR remains locked without scrubber firmware.** GP102/GA102 oneinit ignores firmware-load errors, and the common unlock path returns success if VPR is locked but no scrubber image is available. See [OD11155](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11155) and the [framebuffer lifecycle review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-framebuffer-lifecycle-and-vpr-scrubber-review-od11155).

**OD11156 — Nouveau framebuffer constructors ignore common constructor failure.** NV50 and GF100-family wrappers ignore failure to allocate/map the required DMA flush page, publish the object, and later program its address as if setup succeeded. See [OD11156](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11156) and the [NV50 framebuffer constructor review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nv50-framebuffer-constructors-and-gsp-backing-review-od11156).

**OD11157 — Nouveau PFN clear does not reject overflowing or out-of-VMM intervals.** A wrapped limit can clear the current VMA remainder; a too-large range can be processed across later mapped PFN VMAs and still return success. No checked-in PFNCLR caller was found. See [OD11157](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11157) and the [shared VMM PFN clear range review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-shared-vmm-pfn-clear-range-review-od11157).

**OD11158 — Nouveau VMM constructor errors can reach destructor cleanup with an uninitialized or empty VMA list.** Partial construction is unreferenced on NVIF error paths, while the VMM destructor unconditionally removes the first list entry. See [OD11158](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11158) and the [NVIF VMM dispatcher and constructor cleanup review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvif-vmm-dispatcher-and-constructor-cleanup-review-od11157-od11158).

**OD11159 — Generic PCI DMA allocation length can wrap after alignment overhead.** On 32-bit targets, a near-`ULONG_MAX` request can wrap to a small `AllocVec` size while the caller still believes it owns the requested span; in-tree PCI DMA clients use bounded sizes, so the trigger remains an external/public HIDD caller condition. See [OD11159](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11159) and the [PCI DMA allocator recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#generic-pci-dma-allocator-public-size-contract-recheck-od11159).

**OD11160 — USB HID missing Logical Maximum can miscompute 32-bit input ranges.** The tolerated fallback shifts 32-bit `1UL` by `ReportSize` without a width guard; on 32-bit C ABIs a 32-bit variable Input field can receive an undefined, incorrect maximum and be filtered out before its action runs. Scoped to the optional USB HID class and malformed descriptors with a supplied Logical Minimum but missing Maximum. See [OD11160](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11160) and the [USB HID logical-range fallback review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-missing-logical-maximum-fallback-review-od11160).

**EK10615 — ExecSMP housekeeper can spin on a remote tombstone and delay its reclamation.** See [EK10615](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10615) and the [housekeeper queue review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#housekeeper-remote-tombstone-queue-ek10615).
**EK10616 — RexxSupport `GETPKT` inserts a null node when its port is empty.** See [EK10616](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10616) and the [GETPKT caller/contract recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rexxsupport-getpkt-empty-queue-ek10616).
**EK10617 — RexxSupport `GETPKT` strands a dequeued message when its result allocation fails.** See [EK10617](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10617) and the [GETPKT result-allocation failure trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rexxsupport-getpkt-result-allocation-ek10617).
- **[EK10618](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10618)** — The PC timer accounts for at most one 16-bit PIT rollover per update; if IRQ0 service or another sample is delayed more than about 54.9 ms, elapsed time loses complete counter periods. Conditional on a long service gap; separate from the ExecSMP update race in EK10612. See the [rollover audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pc-timer-eclock-missed-wrap-ek10618). Source-only; no timer or hardware was exercised.

**OD1574 — Efika timer clock normalization is incomplete after a long update gap (latent behind OD9941 build blocker).** See [OD1574](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1574) and the [Efika timer review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#efika-timer-ticks-full-body-review-od1574).

**OD1872 — Efika EClock update loses complete low-word timebase wraps (latent behind OD9941 build blocker).** See [OD1872](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1872) and the [Efika timer review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#efika-timer-ticks-full-body-review-od1574).

**OD9941 — Efika timer initializer has a shared-layout compile error and out-of-range queue initialization.** See [OD9941](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9941) and the [Efika timer shared-base review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#efika-timer-shared-base-header-closure-od9941).

**OD1573 — Efika timer initialization dereferences unchecked OpenFirmware data (firmware-dependent; latent behind OD9941).** See [OD1573](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1573).

**OD3352 — Efika timer reports success after IRQ registration failure (latent behind OD9941).** See [OD3352](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3352).

**OD11164 — DiskImage helper libraries do not complete delayed expunge on close.** See [OD11164](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11164) and the [helper-library lifecycle review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-helper-library-deferred-expunge-od11164).

**OD11163 — Expat dereferences a missing namespace prefix after allocation failure.** See [OD11163](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11163) and the [DTD/prolog review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#expat-dtd-prolog-special-section-od11163).

**OD11162 — Expat continues parsing after a stop in special-section callbacks.** See [OD11162](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11162) and the [content-token processing review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#expat-content-token-processing-od11162).

**OD11161 — Expat parser reset can report success after losing the requested encoding.** See [OD11161](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11161) and the [parser lifecycle review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#expat-parser-create-reset-and-free-lifecycle-od11161).

**[OD11177](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11177) — Expat parser reset retains an inflated group-stack capacity after realloc failure.** A failed growth mutates the capacity before realloc; reset preserves it, so a subsequent sufficiently deep DTD can write past the old buffer. Optional DiskImage Expat API; source-only.

**[OD11178](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11178) — DiskImage consumers ignore failed preference reads and retain partial settings.** Unit startup may apply partial ENV/ENVARC values; a persistent GUI snapshot can rewrite the saved file with only the parsed prefix. Applies to the x86/PPC DiskImage device and GUI packages; source-only.

**[OD11179](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11179) — DiskImage `WritePrefs()` reports success after output errors.** It ignores every `FPrintf()` result and marks the save successful after opening the replacement file; a failed write can leave malformed settings XML. Source-only.

**[OD11180](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11180) — DiskImage preferences writer does not escape XML strings.** Saved image paths containing `&` or `<` produce malformed XML, preventing the unit preferences from loading later. Source-only.

**[OD11181](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11181) — DiskImage snapshot leaks its loaded ENVARC preferences tree on later allocation failure.** Persistent snapshot error exits omit cleanup for the already loaded dictionary. Source-only.

**[OD11182](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11182) — DiskImage saves an uninitialized path when `NameFromFH()` fails.** After a successful image open, the caller ignores path recovery failure and copies the uninitialized fixed-size buffer into preferences. Source-only.

**[OD11183](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11183) — DiskImage preference parser silently truncates long keys and strings.** The reader clips values into fixed 64/512-byte buffers while the object model and writer allow longer data. External/imported preference values only; no in-tree long value found. Source-only.

**[OD11184](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11184) — USB MassStorage can coalesce detach and rebind into one `SIGF_SINGLE` wake.** The worker can misread the combined wake as removal, cancel its timer, and block without reconnecting the rebound unit. Conditional on rebind before the worker consumes the detach signal. Source-only.

**OD11165 — bzip2 decoder does not bound the selector count to its arrays.** See [OD11165](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11165) and the [bzip2 decoder review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-bzip2-selector-count-od11165).

**OD11166 — bzip2 run-length decoding overflows signed counters before its block bound.** See [OD11166](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11166) and the [bzip2 decoder arithmetic review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-bzip2-run-arithmetic-od11166).

**OD10196 — DAX classifies only the first non-compressed area:** `IsNCArea()` repeats its first table entry, so later raw areas are marked compressed and sent to zlib. Explicit optional DAX target; no default-image inclusion claimed. See [OD10196](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10196-dax-classifies-only-the-first-noncompressed-area). Source-only.

**OD10197 — DAX trusts the non-compressed-area count past its fixed 192-entry table:** a larger header count makes image-open classification read beyond the table. Explicit optional DAX target; no default-image inclusion claimed. See [OD10197](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10197-dax-trusts-noncompressed-area-count-past-fixed-table). Source-only.

**OD10198 — DAX passes an unchecked 16-bit frame size to `Read()` for its 9,216-byte input buffer:** a larger file-backed frame length writes past the allocation. Explicit optional DAX target; no default-image inclusion claimed. See [OD10198](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10198-dax-reads-frame-length-past-input-buffer). Source-only.

**OD10199 — DAX copies a full requested frame range after zlib successfully produces fewer bytes than requested, returning stale/uninitialized output from its uncleared frame buffer. Source-only.**

**OD11168 — z.library advertises gzip-file and inflateBack APIs absent from the built library.** See [OD11168](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11168) and the [zlib public interface review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-zlib-public-header-api-build-selection-od11168).

**OD11171 — DHCP minires update wrapper dereferences an empty update list.** See [OD11171](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11171) and the [minires update-wrapper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-update-wrapper-review-od11171).
**OD11172 — DHCP minires signed sends leak the temporary verification key.** See [OD11172](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11172) and the [minires signed-send review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-signed-send-review-od11172).
**OD11173 — DHCP minires canonicalizer reads before its buffer for a short escaped name.** See [OD11173](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11173) and the [minires name/date review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-name-and-date-review-od11173).
**OD11174 — DHCP minires signer dereferences the length before validating arguments.** See [OD11174](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11174) and the [minires signing/verification review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-signing-and-verification-review-od11174).
**OD11175 — DHCP minires query builder wraps its short-buffer check.** See [OD11175](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11175) and the [minires packet-builder review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-packet-builder-review-od11175).
**OD11176 — DHCP minires update builder's capacity macro cannot detect exhaustion.** See [OD11176](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11176) and the [minires packet-builder review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#dhcp-minires-packet-builder-review-od11175).
**OD2834 — BCM2708 I²C HIDD inherits nonfunctional bit-level methods.** See [OD2834](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2834) and the [BCM2708 I²C review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2708-i2c-hidd-startup-registration-and-findings-od2834-od2838).
**OD2835 — BCM2708 I²C byte methods do not return their required status.** See [OD2835](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2835) and the [BCM2708 I²C review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2708-i2c-hidd-startup-registration-and-findings-od2834-od2838).
**OD2836 — BCM2708 I²C reader samples the FIFO before the read completes.** See [OD2836](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2836) and the [BCM2708 I²C review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2708-i2c-hidd-startup-registration-and-findings-od2834-od2838).
**OD2837 — BCM2708 I²C byte methods can wait forever for controller DONE.** See [OD2837](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2837) and the [BCM2708 I²C review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2708-i2c-hidd-startup-registration-and-findings-od2834-od2838).
**OD2838 — BCM2708 I²C hardware initialization is not registered.** See [OD2838](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2838) and the [BCM2708 I²C review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bcm2708-i2c-hidd-startup-registration-and-findings-od2834-od2838).
