<a id="ek10640"></a>**EK10640 — POSIXC `fstatvfs()` returns success without writing the result buffer.** A valid call leaves stale or uninitialized fields looking like successful filesystem statistics. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10640) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-fstatvfs-review-ek10640). Source-only.


<a id="ek10642"></a>**EK10642 — POSIXC stat fallback writes metadata but returns `-1`.** The shared 32-bit and 64-bit path helpers leave their failure result unchanged after filling the output structure. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10642) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stat-helper-fallback-review-ek10642). Source-only.

<a id="ek10643"></a>**EK10643 — POSIXC `lseek()`/`lseek64()` ignore short or failed zero-fill writes beyond EOF.** They can return success with an offset short of the requested position. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10643) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-lseek-zero-fill-review-ek10643). Source-only.

<a id="ek10644"></a>**EK10644 — POSIXC `statfs()`/`getfsstat()` copy 90 bytes from shorter mount-name strings.** The copy reads beyond the path buffer and fills the output tail with unrelated bytes. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10644) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-mount-stat-bounds-review-ek10644). Source-only.

<a id="ek10645"></a>**EK10645 — POSIXC `select()`/`pselect()` always return 0.** They report no descriptors ready and skip the requested wait. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10645) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-select-pselect-review-ek10645). Source-only.

<a id="ek10646"></a>**EK10646 — POSIXC `sleep()` overflows large second counts when converting to DOS ticks.** A request of 85,899,346 seconds wraps to four ticks on 32-bit `unsigned int`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10646) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-sleep-time-api-review-ek10646). Source-only.

<a id="ek10647"></a>**EK10647 — POSIXC `utimes()` wraps pre-1978 modification times into far-future dates.** The unsigned epoch conversion turns historical timestamps into future DateStamps. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10647) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-utimes-time-conversion-review-ek10647). Source-only.

<a id="ek10648"></a>**EK10648 — POSIXC `utimes()` discards the supplied subsecond modification time.** Valid fractions are truncated to whole seconds despite DateStamp tick precision. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10648) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-utimes-time-conversion-review-ek10647). Source-only.

<a id="ek10649"></a>**EK10649 — POSIXC `tempnam()` reads before an empty directory string.** An empty `TMPDIR` or `dir` reaches `strlen(f) - 1` and dereferences before the buffer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10649) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-tempnam-empty-directory-review-ek10649). Source-only.

<a id="ek10650"></a>**EK10650 — POSIXC `tmpfile()` does not unlink its created file.** Closing the returned stream leaves the temporary pathname on disk. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10650) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-tmpfile-unlink-review-ek10650). Source-only.

<a id="ek10651"></a>**EK10651 — stdio output and flush failures can leave the error indicator clear.** POSIXC output and stdc/POSIXC per-stream flush failures can leave `ferror(stream)` reporting no error. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10651) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdio-error-state-review-ek10651). Source-only.

<a id="ek10652"></a>**EK10652 — stdc/POSIXC `fgets()` and direct DOS `FGets()` can overrun small buffers.** Size 1 writes the terminator past the buffer; direct DOS size 0 wraps the unsigned limit and can copy until newline/EOF. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10652) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdio-line-input-review-ek10652). Source-only.

<a id="ek10653"></a>**EK10653 — POSIXC `fopen()` leaks its descriptor on stream-node allocation failure.** It opens the file before `fdopen()` allocates the stream record and does not close on failure. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10653) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-fopen-cleanup-review-ek10653). Source-only.

<a id="ek10654"></a>**EK10654 — stdc and POSIXC `vfscanf()` ignore a failed pre-read flush.** It proceeds to parse input after `Flush()` reports failure, potentially hiding lost pending output on an update stream. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10654) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-vfscanf-flush-review-ek10654). Source-only.

<a id="ek10655"></a>**EK10655 — stdc and POSIXC `ungetc()` return the unconverted input value.** Values above 255 are stored as a byte but returned unchanged. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10655) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-ungetc-conversion-review-ek10655). Source-only.

<a id="ek10656"></a>**EK10656 — POSIXC `getpass()` leaves terminal echo enabled.** Password input is read from ordinary stdin without changing echo mode. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10656) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-identity-api-review-ek10656-ek10657). Source-only.

<a id="ek10657"></a>**EK10657 — POSIXC `getpass()` leaves excess input queued.** A line longer than its buffer is read only once, leaving the suffix for the next stdin read. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10657) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-identity-api-review-ek10656-ek10657). Source-only.

<a id="ek10658"></a>**EK10658 — POSIXC `getpgid()` and `tcgetpgrp()` always return zero.** They ignore PID/descriptor and report a success-shaped value despite no process-group query. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10658) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-terminal-control-review-ek10658). Source-only.

<a id="ek10659"></a>**EK10659 — POSIXC `sigismember()` tests the wrong signal bit.** It disagrees with the add/delete functions, producing incorrect membership results. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10659) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-signal-set-and-build-review-ek10659-ek10661). Source-only.

<a id="ek10660"></a>**EK10660 — POSIXC signal-set functions do not validate signal numbers before indexing.** Invalid values can index outside the four-word set. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10660) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-signal-set-and-build-review-ek10659-ek10661). Source-only.

<a id="ek10661"></a>**EK10661 — POSIXC build list includes signal-jump sources with unconditional `#error`.** Both listed files stop compilation and no per-CPU replacements are checked in. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10661) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-signal-set-and-build-review-ek10659-ek10661). Source-only.

<a id="ek10662"></a>**EK10662 — Default signal reporting writes an unrestricted task name into a 50-byte buffer.** `__sig_default()` uses `sprintf()` with task names copied at their full length. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10662) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-signal-implementation-review-ek10662-ek10663). Source-only.

<a id="ek10663"></a>**EK10663 — `raise()` ignores blocked signal masks and `SA_NODEFER`.** It dispatches blocked signals immediately and defers same-signal delivery even when requested otherwise. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10663) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-signal-implementation-review-ek10662-ek10663). Source-only.

<a id="ek601"></a>**EK601 — POSIXC exec preparation dereferences three unchecked pooled allocations.** PATH, argument-buffer, and script-interpreter allocations can fail before immediate writes. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek601) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-exec-wrapper-and-path-conversion-review-ek601-ek10664). Source-only.

<a id="ek10664"></a>**EK10664 — POSIXC exec paths do not check failed Unix-to-Amiga path conversions.** NULL results reach DOS `Lock()`, `Open()` and `LoadSeg()` callers. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10664) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-exec-wrapper-and-path-conversion-review-ek601-ek10664). Source-only.
<a id="ek10665"></a>**EK10665 — POSIXC environment cache leaks a name when value-buffer growth fails.** Failure to grow a cached value buffer removes the node but leaks its separately allocated name. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10665) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-environment-api-and-cache-review-ek10665). Source-only.
<a id="ek10666"></a>**EK10666 — POSIXC `uselocale()` never queries or changes the current locale.** It only returns its argument. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10666) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-locale-object-api-review-ek10666-ek10667). Source-only.
<a id="ek10667"></a>**EK10667 — POSIXC `newlocale()` discards categories not selected by its mask.** A partial mask can replace `LC_CTYPE` from the supplied base. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10667) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-locale-object-api-review-ek10666-ek10667). Source-only.
<a id="ek10668"></a>**EK10668 — POSIXC `uname()` reverses the release major and minor components.** The release string is formatted minor.major. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10668) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-uname-and-small-api-pass-ek10668). Source-only.
<a id="ek10669"></a>**EK10669 — POSIXC `mbsnrtowcs()` consumes characters after its destination is full.** It advances the source past characters it did not write. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10669) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10670"></a>**EK10670 — POSIXC `mbsnrtowcs()` counts the terminating NUL in its result.** See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10670) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10671"></a>**EK10671 — POSIXC `wcsnrtombs()` omits the output NUL terminator.** It reports the source consumed without terminating the converted destination. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10671) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10672"></a>**EK10672 — POSIXC `wcsnrtombs()` clears the source pointer when its character limit is reached.** The caller loses the unconverted suffix. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10672) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10673"></a>**EK10673 — POSIXC `wcsnrtombs()` returns zero for the NULL-destination sizing form.** Its capacity check still applies when `dst` is NULL. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10673) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10674"></a>**EK10674 — stdc `mbrtowc()` treats impossible UTF-8 lead bytes as incomplete.** Malformed one-byte prefixes return incomplete instead of `EILSEQ`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10674) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10675"></a>**EK10675 — POSIXC `wcsnrtombs()` dereferences a failed temporary buffer allocation.** A failed `AllocVec()` can leave the later output copy reading from NULL. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10675) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10676"></a>**EK10676 — POSIXC `fchown()` reports success without changing ownership.** The selected implementation is a TODO that returns zero. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10676) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-directory-ownership-and-truncate-wrapper-pass-ek10676). Source-only.
<a id="ek10677"></a>**EK10677 — POSIXC `setsid()` always fails without setting `errno`.** See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10677) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-process-id-and-session-api-pass-ek10677). Source-only.
<a id="ek10678"></a>**EK10678 — stdc multibyte conversion ignores the selected C locale.** The selected helpers always use UTF-8 despite the current locale's C encoding. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10678) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-multibyte-bounded-conversion-review-ek10669-ek10678). Source-only.
<a id="ek10679"></a>**EK10679 — POSIXC `posix_memalign()` overwrites the output pointer on failure.** A failed allocation replaces the caller's previous pointer with NULL. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10679) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-allocation-and-reentrant-prng-pass-ek10679). Source-only.
<a id="ek10680"></a>**EK10680 — POSIXC `random()` starts with mostly uninitialized default state.** The first-use setup copies bytes instead of the full word table. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10680) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-random-state-initialization-review-ek10680-ek10681). Source-only.
<a id="ek10681"></a>**EK10681 — POSIXC `initstate()` treats a negative size as the largest state buffer.** It can write state words beyond the caller's small buffer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10681) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-random-state-initialization-review-ek10680-ek10681). Source-only.
<a id="ek10682"></a>**EK10682 — POSIXC `posix_fadvise()` accepts invalid arguments for foreign descriptors.** Its socket/foreign-owner shortcut returns success before validating offset, length or advice. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10682) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-advisory-file-api-review-ek10682). Source-only.
<a id="ek10683"></a>**EK10683 — POSIXC `localeconv_l()` interprets locale handles with the wrong structure layout.** It returns the beginning of the `newlocale()` object as though it contained `struct lconv`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10683) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-locale-specific-wrapper-review-ek10683). Source-only.
<a id="ek10684"></a>**EK10684 — POSIXC `*at()` helper can use a directory descriptor after concurrent close.** `__at_enter()` drops the descriptor-table guard before it duplicates the directory lock, leaving a lifetime race with `close()` in shared pthread tables. Scoped to its explicit concurrent-close intent. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10684) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-at-directory-lock-lifetime-review-ek10684). Source-only.
<a id="ek10685"></a>**EK10685 — POSIXC `strptime()` accepts failed numeric conversions and stores an indeterminate value.** `MATCHUINT` treats `sscanf()` returning zero as success and writes its unset temporary. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10685) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-strptime-parser-review-ek10685-ek10686). Source-only.
<a id="ek10686"></a>**EK10686 — POSIXC `strptime()` returns a pointer before the input on mismatched `%%`.** A failed literal-percent match applies the negative `EOF` value to the input pointer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10686) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-strptime-parser-review-ek10685-ek10686). Source-only.
<a id="ek10687"></a>**EK10687 — Shared `gmtime()` conversion mishandles negative timestamps.** Signed division and remainder leave negative time fields and fail to move the calendar date before the epoch. Affects stdc and POSIXC GMT/local time wrappers. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10687) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-reentrant-time-conversion-review-ek10687). Source-only.
<a id="ek10688"></a>**EK10688 — `jrand48()` and `mrand48()` do not safely produce the required signed 32-bit result.** Their signed shifts overflow on 32-bit-`long` targets and fail to sign-extend on wider-`long` targets. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10688) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-rand48-family-review-ek10688). Source-only.
<a id="ek10689"></a>**EK10689 — POSIXC declares `strtol_l()` and `strtoul_l()` but exports no library vectors.** Their source files are selected and header prototypes are public, but `posixc.conf` omits both vector entries. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10689) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-wide-string-and-locale-long-api-review-ek10689). Source-only.
<a id="ek10690"></a>**EK10690 — POSIXC `getopt_long()` suppresses every requested option diagnostic.** AROS supplies a no-op `warnx()`, so malformed options return errors without the expected stderr explanation. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10690) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-getopt-implementation-review-ek10690). Source-only.
<a id="od11244"></a>**OD11244 withdrawn:** the 255-entry loop reaches index 255, where the entry helper rejects it and terminates before wraparound. See the [correction](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-8-bit-table-loop-wrap-candidate-correction-od11244-withdrawn-2026-11-03).
<a id="od11245"></a>**OD11245 — Nouveau XPIO parser always reports failure and allows a short entry.** `dcb_xpio_parse()` fills fields but returns zero on success, and a six-byte entry still triggers a read at offset 6. No in-tree caller was found, so current runtime impact is unestablished. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11245) and [coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-xpio-bios-parser-full-body-pass-od11245-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11246"></a>**OD11246 — Nouveau ICCSense initialization leaks its parsed power-rail table.** A successful BIOS-table parse allocates a rail array that one-init neither retains nor frees; the subdevice destructor cannot release it. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11246) and [coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-iccsense-parser-and-oneinit-ownership-pass-od11246-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11247"></a>**OD11247 — Nouveau thermal BIOS fallback can write fan trip points past its 10-element array.** The parser has no trip-count cap, and a `0x25` entry before a `0x24` also indexes before the array. Reached when the primary fan table is unavailable; firmware incidence is unverified. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11247) and [coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-thermal-bios-fan-parser-bounds-pass-od11247-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11248"></a>**OD11248 — Nouveau GPIO voltage parsing wraps the count for a complete 256-entry VID range.** The 256-entry array is filled, but its `u8 vid_nr` wraps to zero, so later get/set paths treat the mappings as empty. Requires a ranged table covering all VID values. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11248) and [coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-voltage-bios-parser-and-vid-consumer-pass-od11248-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11249"></a>**OD11249 — Cyclic Nouveau voltage-map links recurse without a termination check.** A VMap cycle causes common voltage/clock lookup to recurse until stack exhaustion; no affected ROM was available. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11249) and [coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-voltage-core-and-vmap-caller-pass-od11249-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11250"></a>**OD11250 — Nouveau linear fan control divides by zero for equal BIOS temperature bounds.** The legacy fallback parser accepts equal linear bounds; automatic fan interpolation divides by zero when the sampled temperature equals them. Conditional on firmware and fallback selection. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11250) and [thermal-core coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-thermal-control-core-and-pwmtoggle-implementation-pass-od11247-caller-recheck-od11250-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11251"></a>**OD11251 — Nouveau fault-buffer setup leaks partially initialized buffers on failure.** Buffer memory-allocation or BAR2-pin failure leaves the buffer slot outside the destructor’s `buffer_nr` loop; pin failure also leaks its memory reference. Scoped to selected Nouveau fault subdevices and setup failure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11251) and [fault-buffer lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fault-buffer-full-body-and-failure-lifecycle-pass-od11251-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11252"></a>**OD11252 — Nouveau interrupt registration can leak an allocation on partial failure.** If `stat` allocation fails but the following `mask` allocation succeeds, the shared helper frees only `stat`; the failed MC interrupt record is not linked for normal teardown. Scoped to MC/VFN initialization under allocation pressure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11252) and [MC interrupt registration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mc-interruptreset-implementation-pass-od11252-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11253"></a>**OD11253 — Nouveau MEMX completion drops PMU send failures and logs uninitialized reply words.** A GT215 PMU queue timeout skips script execution, but MEMX reports success and consumes untouched reply values. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11253) and [PMU/MEMX caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-pmu-shared-lifecycle-and-gt215-memxmessage-pass-od11253-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11254"></a>**OD11254 — Nouveau Falcon acquisition retains its owner after one-time setup fails.** A TOP-address lookup error leaves the Falcon marked busy, so later users receive `-EBUSY`. Conditional on Falcon setup failure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11254) and [Falcon lifecycle review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-falcon-core-and-firmware-lifecycle-review-od11254-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11255"></a>**OD11255 — Nouveau v1 secure-firmware diagnostics print the IMEM overlay count as the DMEM count.** Only debug output is affected when counts differ. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11255) and [NVFW parser/dump review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvfw-dump-accessors-pass-od11255-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11256"></a>**OD11256 — Nouveau subdevice init failure leaves it marked enabled, so a later lazy reference may succeed without initialization.** Conditional on a failed first init through a zero-refcount engine. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11256) and [subdevice lifecycle coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-core-lifecycle-and-object-reference-pass-od11256-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11257"></a>**OD11257 — Nouveau GPU-object copy-from helper writes into its source object instead of the supplied destination.** No in-tree callers were found in the pinned tree. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11257) and [GPU-object helper coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-core-lifecycle-and-object-reference-pass-od11256-od11257-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11258"></a>**OD11258 — Nouveau FSP synchronous response parsing accepts a short packet and reads uninitialized reply fields.** Conditional on a truncated response during GH100-family GSP FMC boot. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11258) and [FSP transport coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fsp-command-transport-pass-od11258-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11259"></a>**OD11259 — Nouveau MXM ROM discovery reads the two-byte structure length past its six-byte probe buffer, then trusts the unbounded value for a narrowed allocation/read and later checksum walk.** Conditional on ROM-shadow SIS discovery. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11259) and [MXM parser/ownership review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mxm-rom-and-shadow-table-pass-od11259-od11260-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11260"></a>**OD11260 — Nouveau MXM shadow-table allocations have no subdevice destructor and leak at teardown.** Conditional on successful table acquisition. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11260) and [MXM parser/ownership review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mxm-rom-and-shadow-table-pass-od11259-od11260-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11261"></a>**OD11261 — Four Nouveau generation-specific I2C bus constructors ignore adapter-registration errors and report success.** Conditional on bus adapter setup failure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11261) and [shared I2C bus lifecycle coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-i2c-shared-bus-lifecycle-pass-od11261-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.

<a id="od11262"></a>**OD11262 — Nouveau AUX transfers fail to restore the DPCD auto-read enable bit because their helper always passes false.** Conditional on selected GK110/GM200 AUX use. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11262) and [AUX implementation coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-i2c-aux-transfer-and-registration-pass-od11262-od11264-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11263"></a>**OD11263 — Nouveau G94/GF119/GM200 AUX constructors ignore I2C adapter-registration errors.** Conditional on registration failure. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11263) and [AUX implementation coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-i2c-aux-transfer-and-registration-pass-od11262-od11264-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11264"></a>**OD11264 — Nouveau AUX I2C transfers truncate message lengths to eight bits and can report partial transfers as success.** Conditional on messages of at least 256 bytes. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11264) and [AUX implementation coverage](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-i2c-aux-transfer-and-registration-pass-od11262-od11264-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11265"></a>**OD11265 — NV05 memory initialization indexes an eight-entry fallback table with a four-bit strap value.** If no BMP memory-init table is available and the strap is 8–15, fallback configuration reads go out of bounds before VRAM setup. Board incidence is unverified. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11265) and [devinit review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-devinit-memory-and-post-lifecycle-pass-od11265-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11266"></a>**OD11266 — Nouveau ACR discards WPR build and relocation errors, then continues with the image.** Conditional on selected ACR firmware callbacks reporting an error; device initialization can proceed with incomplete WPR metadata. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11266) and [ACR review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-acr-wpr-build-and-lifecycle-pass-od11266-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11267"></a>**OD11267 — Nouveau R535 VFN teardown leaks its dynamically allocated function table.** The R535 wrapper installs a destructor callback, but the common VFN destructor never calls it; one small allocation remains per successful device lifetime. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11267) and [VFN review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-vfn-usermode-and-r535-ownership-pass-od11267-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11268"></a>**OD11268 — Nouveau PCIe link negotiation turns PCIe 5.0/6.0 bus rates into a negative speed enum.** The negative value indexes before the speed-name array and reaches the generation link callback; conditional on a PCIe 5/6 bus and a link-speed request. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11268) and [PCIe review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-pci-pcie-speed-and-generation-pass-od11268-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11269"></a>**OD11269 — Nouveau R535/R570/R580 GSP callbacks trust response counts and notification payload bounds.** Oversized framebuffer/interrupt counts, malformed sequencer lengths/slots, or short LibOS-print events can cause out-of-bounds message accesses. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11269) and [GSP schema and callback review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-rm-schema-and-callback-bounds-pass-od11269-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11270"></a>**OD11270 — Nouveau GSP RPC receive trusts undersized message lengths.** A short RPC/continuation length can underflow the copied payload size. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11270) and [RPC framing review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-rpc-transport-receive-and-split-failure-review-od11270-od11271-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11271"></a>**OD11271 — Failed split Nouveau GSP RPC submissions leak the retained original request.** Conditional on an allocation, queue, or reply failure for an RPC larger than one queue element. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11271) and [RPC framing review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-rpc-transport-receive-and-split-failure-review-od11270-od11271-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11272"></a>**OD11272 — Nouveau GSP ACPI `_DOD` parsing leaks ACPICA result buffers on invalid output.** Conditional on successful `_DOD` evaluation returning a malformed package or entry. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11272) and [GSP ACPI/system-info review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r570-r580-gsp-system-info-acpi-contract-pass-od11272-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11273"></a>**OD11273 — Nouveau GSP teardown locks an uninitialized IDR after early setup failure.** The selected AROS IDR destroy routine locks its mutex, while GSP initializes the IDR only at the end of successful one-time setup. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11273) and [GSP initialization/teardown review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-oneinit-and-idr-teardown-ordering-pass-od11273-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11274"></a>**OD11274 — Nouveau R535 GSP RM ELF lookup trusts section offsets and names.** A truncated/inconsistent local RM firmware image can cause out-of-range reads or return a section range beyond the image. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11274) and [GSP RM firmware parser review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-rm-elf-section-lookup-bounds-pass-od11274-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11275"></a>**OD11275 — Nouveau GSP OS-error logging assumes a NUL-terminated firmware string.** A full 256-byte nonterminated error string can make `%s` read beyond its field/response. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11275) and [GSP notification review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r570-r580-gsp-os-error-notification-string-bounds-pass-od11275-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11276"></a>**OD11276 — Nouveau GSP radix-3 mapping can omit a firmware page at exact 2 MiB table boundaries.** Conditional on an RM firmware section ending just after a 2 MiB page-table capacity boundary. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11276) and [GSP radix-3 allocation review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-radix3-table-capacity-boundary-pass-od11276-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11277"></a>**OD11277 — Nouveau R535 GSP bootloader parsing trusts binary-header offsets.** An inconsistent local bootloader image can make descriptor reads or image copies extend past the file. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11277) and [GSP bootloader binary-header review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-bootloader-binary-header-bounds-pass-od11277-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11278"></a>**OD11278 — Nouveau GSP radix-3 mapping does not enforce its 1 GiB capacity.** An oversized firmware image can make level-2 page pointers overrun the fixed level-1 page. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11278) and [GSP radix-3 allocation review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gsp-radix3-table-capacity-boundary-pass-od11276-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11279"></a>**OD11279 — Nouveau R570/R580 GR scrubber leaks its reserved FIFO channel ID.** The retained ID is never returned when scrubber/GR resources are released, reducing the channel IDs available during that device lifetime. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11279) and [R570/R580 scrubber review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r570-r580-gr-scrubber-channel-id-lifecycle-pass-od11279-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11280"></a>**OD11280 — Nouveau GSP CPU sequencer continues after a register poll timeout.** A failed readiness poll is ignored, so later sequencer commands can run against an unmet hardware condition. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11280) and [GSP sequencer review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-cpu-sequencer-poll-timeout-pass-od11280-added-2026-11-03). Source-only; intended ABI error handling remains uncertain.
<a id="od11281"></a>**OD11281 — Nouveau GR context promotion leaks its GSP control buffer on setup errors.** Allocation or mapping failures return after creating the RPC request without freeing it; repeated failures can retain memory. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11281) and [GR context-promotion review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-gr-context-promotion-error-unwind-pass-od11281-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11282"></a>**OD11282 — Nouveau GSP control reads leak reply buffers when RM reports an error.** Error status is returned while response-bearing RPC allocations remain owned; affected paths include R570/R580 TPC queries, R535/R570/R580 SOR backlight controls and the Blackwell display mode-possibility query; repeated failures can retain memory. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11282) and [GSP control reply ownership review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r580-control-reply-error-ownership-pass-od11282-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od4343"></a>**OD4343 — printer.device reuses a command buffer while its previous write is pending.** Successive command formatting can overwrite bytes submitted asynchronously through the shared buffer. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4343) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.
<a id="od4344"></a>**[OD4344](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4344) — printer.device can return while a text buffer is still in use by an asynchronous backend.** Delayed backend continuation can retain a pointer to expired stack storage. See the [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4344) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.
<a id="od4345"></a>**OD4345 — printer.device CSI parameter index persists across sequences and writes past the parameter array.** Four semicolon-form commands in one write can make the parser store at `parm[4]`. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4345) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.
<a id="od11283"></a>**OD11283 — Nouveau FIFO recovery notification can index before the channel array.** An invalid high-bit channel ID becomes negative, bypasses the lookup's upper-bound check, and is used as an array index. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11283) and [FIFO recovery channel-ID bounds review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r580-fifo-recovery-channel-id-bounds-pass-od11283-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11284"></a>**OD11284 — Nouveau GSP FIFO initialization can succeed after a runlist allocation failure.** Engine entries for the missing runlist are skipped, and later initialization can still return success with an incomplete FIFO topology. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11284) and [FIFO runlist-construction review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-fifo-runlist-allocation-error-propagation-pass-od11284-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11285"></a>**OD11285 — Nouveau GSP FIFO drops a shared runlist when one engine entry is unsupported or fails.** Deleting the runlist for one entry causes later supported entries with the same runlist ID to be skipped. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11285) and [FIFO shared-runlist error-path review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-fifo-shared-runlist-error-path-pass-od11285-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.



<a id="gd14759"></a>**GD14759 — BMP loader decodes the third 2-bit palette index incorrectly.** The packed field is stored as 0/4/8/12 instead of 0–3, giving the third pixel the wrong color in the loader’s four-entry palette mode. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14759) and [coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#bmp-packed-pixel-index-review-gd14759). Source-only.

<a id="gd14760"></a>**GD14760 — BMP loader ignores a reduced `biClrUsed` palette.** A valid indexed image with fewer than the maximum palette entries can be rejected or have pixel bytes read as palette data. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14760) and [coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#bmp-reduced-palette-review-gd14760). Source-only.
<a id="od11287"></a>**OD11287 — Nouveau R535 retains an SOR reservation when the RM-selected output is unavailable.** A failed local SOR lookup leaves the returned reservation in the mask used by later acquisitions. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11287) and [R535 display SOR acquisition review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-display-sor-acquisition-state-pass-od11287-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11289"></a>**OD11289 — Nouveau R535 DP AUX handling can replace an RM control error with a protocol reply.** Non-retry control errors are overwritten by the response payload’s `replyType`. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11289) and [R535 DP AUX error-propagation review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-dp-aux-error-propagation-pass-od11289-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11290"></a>**OD11290 — Nouveau NVIF DP rates method reports success when driver setup fails.** The method drops the output driver callback’s error result. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11290) and [DP rates callback error-propagation review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-dp-rates-callback-error-propagation-pass-od11290-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11293"></a>**OD11293 — Nouveau ICCSense treats signed shunt-voltage readings as unsigned.** Negative current is converted to a large positive measurement before power calculation. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11293) and [ICCSense sensor-format recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-iccsense-signed-shunt-format-pass-od11293-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11294"></a>**OD11294 — Nouveau bit-banged I2C treats one-byte register reads as address probes.** The adapter returns success without reading data, so `nvkm_rdi2cr()` returns an uninitialized byte. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11294) and [coverage recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-bit-banged-i2c-single-byte-register-read-pass-od11294). Source-only.

<a id="gd14761"></a>**GD14761 — VC4 Mesa clamps NPOT repeat samples at the seam:** shader `fract()` plus forced clamp avoids POT padding but loses cross-edge blending with linear filtering, producing incorrect colors near the wrap boundary. Scoped to the optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Mesa 26 path; its parent build edge is commented out. See [GD14761](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14761) and the [patch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-26-vc4-npot-repeat-filtering-gd14761). Source-only.

<a id="gd14762"></a>**GD14762 — VC4 submission drain timeout continues with prior work pending:** after 100,000,000 spins, the code logs and proceeds to overwrite the pending render handoff and start a new submission without reset/counter recovery. Scoped to the optional Raspberry Pi VC4 target and a stuck prior job. See [GD14762](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14762) and the [VC4 submission trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vc4-submit-drain-timeout-gd14762). Source-only.
<a id="gd14763"></a>**GD14763 — VMware/Nouveau EDID parsing skips CVT 60 Hz reduced blanking:** the CVT flag loop starts at bit one, so it never adds the bit-zero mode. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14763) and [full EDID parser review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14764"></a>**GD14764 — VMware/Nouveau EDID parsing reports zero HDR minimum luminance:** integer rounding collapses the 8-bit input before the square/divide calculation. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14764) and [full EDID parser review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14765"></a>**GD14765 — VMware/Nouveau HDR maximum luminance uses MaxFALL:** the display maximum is calculated from the frame-average field rather than the desired maximum-luminance field. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14765) and [full EDID parser review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14766"></a>**GD14766 — VC4 submission logs invalid BO handles but still builds and submits GPU addresses from zero.** A malformed/stale command-list or surface handle can become a zero-based indexed-draw or render-surface address in the optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Gallium HIDD; default build inclusion is not claimed. See [GD14766](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14766) and the [command-list trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vc4-bin-cl-invalid-handle-follow-up-gd14766). Source-only.

<a id="ek677"></a>**EK677 — OpenSBI GOP framebuffer remap can leave the Sv39 lower canonical window.** A remapped GOP framebuffer span extending beyond physical 384 GiB produces a noncanonical alias range that the selected EFI HIDD later accesses. Conditional on firmware placement; see [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek677) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L277). Source-only.

<a id="ek678"></a>**EK678 — OpenSBI framebuffer/high-device aliases can overwrite RAM still offered to the allocator.** A remapped device span can replace identity RAM mappings while startup publishes the overlapping bank as allocatable. Conditional on the firmware/device/RAM layout; see [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek678) and [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L279). Source-only.
<a id="od11295"></a>**OD11295 — Nouveau R535/R570/R580 object free ignores RM failure status.** The RPC transport can succeed while RM reports FREE failure; the helper discards that status and local object cleanup proceeds. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11295) and [allocation lifecycle pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r570-r580-allocation-free-status-pass-od11295). Source-only.
<a id="od11296"></a>**OD11296 — Nouveau display notification can arrive before its callback is registered.** GSP notification delivery drops events that arrive after RM enables them but before the host adds the callback to its client list. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11296) and [event registration/dispatch pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-r535-r570-r580-event-registration-dispatch-pass-od11296). Source-only.
<a id="ek10693"></a>**EK10693 — `mktime()` miscounts pre-1970 leap days.** Signed division toward zero drops leap-day counts for negative year offsets; 1968-01-01 is returned one day late. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10693) and [mktime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdc-mktime-calendar-conversion-pass-ek10693-ek10694). Source-only.
<a id="ek10694"></a>**EK10694 — `mktime()` overflows before detecting dates outside 32-bit `time_t`.** Dates after the 2038 limit overflow signed `int` intermediates, including in WirelessManager certificate-time conversion. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10694) and [mktime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdc-mktime-calendar-conversion-pass-ek10693-ek10694). Source-only.
<a id="ek10695"></a>**EK10695 — `difftime()` overflows before converting its result.** Signed 32-bit `time_t` operands are subtracted before the `double` cast, so wide intervals overflow. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10695) and [time conversion pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdc-difftime-arithmetic-pass-ek10695). Source-only.
<a id="ek10696"></a>**EK10696 — 32-bit `clock()` wraps after about 2.7 years.** The tick count is accumulated in 32-bit `unsigned long` without range handling. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10696) and [clock review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-clock-tick-range-pass-ek10696). Source-only.
<a id="ek10697"></a>**EK10697 — `strftime()` overwrites its output prefix for `%n`, `%t`, and `%%`.** These specifiers write at `s[0]` instead of the current output position. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10697) and [strftime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-strftime-and-date-string-formatting-pass-ek10697-ek10699). Source-only.
<a id="ek10698"></a>**EK10698 — `strftime()` can place its final NUL beyond the destination.** Conversion lengths can consume or exceed all remaining capacity before the epilogue writes the terminator. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10698) and [strftime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-strftime-and-date-string-formatting-pass-ek10697-ek10699). Source-only.
<a id="ek10699"></a>**EK10699 — `strftime()` leaks current-locale references.** It calls `OpenLocale(NULL)` per conversion without balancing it with `CloseLocale()`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10699) and [locale-reference trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-strftime-and-date-string-formatting-pass-ek10697-ek10699). Source-only.
<a id="ek10700"></a>**EK10700 — stdc and POSIXC `strerror()` index before their tables for negative inputs.** Neither implementation checks the lower bound before using the error number as an array index. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10700) and [strerror source review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-posixc-strerror-error-path-review-ek10700-ek10703). Source-only.
<a id="ek10701"></a>**EK10701 — stdc `strerror()` omits the defined `EOVERFLOW` message.** stdc `perror()` consequently emits a generic message for overflow errors; the POSIXC override is unaffected. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10701) and [strerror source review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-posixc-strerror-error-path-review-ek10700-ek10703). Source-only.
<a id="ek10702"></a>**EK10702 — stdc `strerror()` can pass a NULL buffer to DOS `Fault()`.** Its unchecked lazy allocation can fail before formatting a DOS error. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10702) and [strerror source review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-posixc-strerror-error-path-review-ek10700-ek10703). Source-only.
<a id="ek10703"></a>**EK10703 — stdc `strerror()` calls DOS `Fault()` after DOS library open failure.** The open hook reports success even when its DOS base is NULL. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10703) and [strerror source review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-posixc-strerror-error-path-review-ek10700-ek10703). Source-only.

<a id="ek10704"></a>**EK10704 — stdcio `fgetc()` ignores a failed stdin synchronization.** The first read clears its one-time flush flag even when DOS cannot restore unread buffered input. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10704) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-stream-status-accessors-full-body-pass-ek10704). Source-only.

<a id="ek10705"></a>**EK10705 — stdcio append output ignores seek-to-EOF failure.** Three output functions continue writing at the previous file position when append positioning fails. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10705) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-stream-status-accessors-full-body-pass-ek10704). Source-only.

<a id="ek10706"></a>**EK10706 — stdc and POSIXC `fread()` report DOS read errors as EOF.** A buffered DOS read error becomes a short block count, and both wrappers set EOF without setting the error indicator. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10706) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-stream-status-accessors-full-body-pass-ek10704). Source-only.

<a id="ek10707"></a>**EK10707 — stdc and POSIXC `fgets()` hide read errors after partial input.** DOS `FGets()` returns partial data when a later character read fails; neither wrapper sets `ferror()`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10707) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-stdio-line-input-review-ek10652). Source-only.

<a id="ek10708"></a>**EK10708 — stdcio `fflush(NULL)` also flushes input streams.** Its file-list walk does not filter for output streams, so unread input can be discarded when the handler cannot restore position. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10708) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-fflush-and-input-stream-review-ek10708). Source-only.

<a id="ek10709"></a>**EK10709 — stdcio `fclose()` removes unlinked standard streams.** Closing a standard stream reaches `Remove()` although stdcio never inserts its embedded standard stream nodes in the open-file list. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10709) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-fclose-standard-stream-review-ek10709). Source-only.

<a id="ek10710"></a>**EK10710 — stdc `fopen("r+")` opens the DOS handle for input only.** The returned stream is marked read/write, but writes cannot update the file. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10710) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-file-open-mode-review-ek10710). Source-only.

<a id="ek10711"></a>**EK10711 — POSIXC `ungetc()` leaves EOF set after successful pushback.** `feof()` continues to report EOF although the pushed character is available. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10711) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-ungetc-conversion-review-ek10655). Source-only.

<a id="ek10712"></a>**EK10712 — stdcio shutdown leaves changed `stderr` buffering flags behind.** It snapshots and restores stdin/stdout modes but omits a distinct process error handle. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10712) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-startup-teardown-review-ek10712). Source-only.

<a id="ek10713"></a>**EK10713 — stdcio `tmpfile()` retries permanent creation failures forever.** Its loop does not distinguish name collisions from unwritable-volume or allocation failures. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10713) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-temporary-file-and-reopen-review-ek10713-ek10715). Source-only.
<a id="ek10714"></a>**EK10714 — stdcio `freopen()` leaks a newly opened file when reusing a standard stream.** It preserves `DONTCLOSE` from the embedded standard stream after transferring an owned handle. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10714) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-temporary-file-and-reopen-review-ek10713-ek10715). Source-only.
<a id="ek10715"></a>**EK10715 — stdcio `tmpfile()` can truncate a file created at its checked name.** `tmpnam()` releases the existence-check lock before `fopen("wb+")` uses truncating create semantics. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10715) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-temporary-file-and-reopen-review-ek10713-ek10715). Source-only.

<a id="ek10716"></a>**EK10716 — stdc `rename(path, path)` deletes the file.** The wrapper removes the destination before attempting to rename the now-missing source. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10716) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-file-operation-wrapper-review-ek10716). Source-only.

<a id="ek10717"></a>**EK10717 — stdc formatter negates minimum signed integers in signed arithmetic.** `%d`, `%ld`, or `%lld` on the minimum value reaches undefined signed negation. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10717) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.
<a id="ek10718"></a>**EK10718 — stdc `%a`/`%A` output a fixed zero placeholder.** The selected full-specifier formatter ignores the floating value in this branch. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10718) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.
<a id="ek10719"></a>**EK10719 — stdc floating formatting loses the sign of negative zero.** Its negative-value comparisons treat `-0.0` as nonnegative. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10719) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.
<a id="ek10720"></a>**EK10720 — stdc long-double infinity checks read the double union member.** On wider-long-double targets, `%L` special values enter the finite-number path. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10720) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.
<a id="ek10721"></a>**EK10721 — stdc formatter overflows negating `INT_MIN` dynamic width.** A valid negative `*` width is negated in signed int before widening. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10721) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.
<a id="ek10722"></a>**EK10722 — stdc/POSIXC formatted output returns a partial count after callback failure.** Shared `__vcformat()` returns its current count instead of a negative error; the POSIXC `vfprintf()` callback has the same path. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10722) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-printf-shared-formatter-review-ek10717-ek10722). Source-only.

<a id="ek10723"></a>**EK10723 — stdc `scanf("%u")` rejects negative input.** The scanner refuses the optional minus sign for unsigned conversions instead of converting the value to unsigned. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10723) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-formatted-input-scanner-review-ek10654-ek10725). Source-only.
<a id="ek10724"></a>**EK10724 — stdc `%Lf` input writes through a `double *`.** On wider-long-double targets, only part of the destination object is written. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10724) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-formatted-input-scanner-review-ek10654-ek10725). Source-only.
<a id="ek10725"></a>**EK10725 — stdc scanf lacks `%a`/`%A` hexadecimal-float input.** These conversions fall through into the integer parser and destination path. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10725) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-formatted-input-scanner-review-ek10654-ek10725). Source-only.

<a id="ek10726"></a>**EK10726 — stdc scanf's `inf`/`nan` constants use big-endian byte order.** Little-endian targets receive a different floating value. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10726) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-formatted-input-scanner-review-ek10654-ek10725). Source-only.

<a id="ek10727"></a>**EK10727 — stdcio environ refresh leaks old arrays.** Repeated environment changes leak each replaced snapshot. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10727) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-environment-support-review-ek10727-ek10728). Source-only.

<a id="ek10728"></a>**EK10728 — stdcio environ initialization reports success after allocation failure.** Setup can leave `*environptr` null while returning success. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10728) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-environment-support-review-ek10727-ek10728). Source-only.

<a id="ek10729"></a>**EK10729 — stdc `mbsrtowcs()` consumes its source during a size query.** A null-destination query updates `*src`, so a later conversion can lose the input. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10729) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-multibyte-conversion-review-ek10729-ek10732). Source-only.

<a id="ek10730"></a>**EK10730 — stdc `wcsrtombs()` applies `len` during size queries.** A common null-destination, zero-length query reports zero for a nonempty string. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10730) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-multibyte-conversion-review-ek10729-ek10732). Source-only.

<a id="ek10731"></a>**EK10731 — stdc `wcsrtombs()` does not check its temporary allocation.** Allocation failure reaches `wcrtomb()` with a null output buffer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10731) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-multibyte-conversion-review-ek10729-ek10732). Source-only.

<a id="ek10732"></a>**EK10732 — stdc `wcrtomb(NULL, wc, ...)` returns the character width, not reset length.** Multibyte characters return more than the UTF-8 reset length. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10732) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-multibyte-conversion-review-ek10729-ek10732). Source-only.

<a id="ek10733"></a>**EK10733 — stdc `fgetwc()` accepts malformed UTF-8.** Overlong, surrogate, and out-of-range code points are returned instead of rejected. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10733) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-stream-review-ek10733-ek10735). Source-only.

<a id="ek10734"></a>**EK10734 — stdc `fputwc()` does not check its temporary allocation.** Allocation failure reaches the encoder with a null output buffer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10734) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-stream-review-ek10733-ek10735). Source-only.

<a id="ek10735"></a>**EK10735 — stdc `ungetwc()` does not clear EOF after pushback.** `feof()` remains set after a successful pushback. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10735) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-stream-review-ek10733-ek10735). Source-only.

<a id="ek10736"></a>**EK10736 — stdc `wcslen()` uses a signed `int` length counter.** Strings longer than `INT_MAX` wide characters overflow before returning `size_t`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10736) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-string-primitives-review-ek10736). Source-only.

<a id="ek10737"></a>**EK10737 — stdc `wctob()` reads its buffer before checking conversion failure.** Invalid input reads an unwritten byte; allocation failure can pass a null buffer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10737) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-classification-and-byte-conversion-review-ek10737). Source-only.

<a id="ek10738"></a>**EK10738 — stdc wide signed conversions mishandle `LONG_MIN`/`LLONG_MIN`.** Their positive magnitude limits and later signed negation do not represent the minimum value safely. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10738) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10739"></a>**EK10739 — stdc wide unsigned conversions reject a leading minus.** `wcstoul()` and `wcstoull()` return zero and report no conversion instead of applying unsigned negation. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10739) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10740"></a>**EK10740 — stdc base-zero wide conversions misreport the end pointer for zero.** The consumed leading zero is not included in the parser's conversion flag. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10740) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10741"></a>**EK10741 — stdc `wcstombs()` does not terminate its output.** A converted nonempty string lacks the required trailing null byte. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10741) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10742"></a>**EK10742 — stdc wide float parsers consume incomplete exponents.** `wcstod()`, `wcstof()`, and `wcstold()` advance past `e` or `e+` without exponent digits. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10742) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10743"></a>**EK10743 — stdc `wcstombs()` does not check its temporary allocation.** Allocation failure reaches `wcrtomb()` with a null output pointer. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10743) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10744"></a>**EK10744 — stdc wide integer parsers stop `endptr` at the first overflow digit.** Remaining digits in the same numeric sequence are left unconsumed. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10744) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10745"></a>**EK10745 — stdc wide floating parsers do not recognize infinity or NaN.** Documented `inf`/`nan` inputs are treated as no conversion. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10745) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-numeric-conversion-review-ek10738-ek10745). Source-only.

<a id="ek10746"></a>**EK10746 — stdc wide scanf integer conversions assign zero.** The parser gathers digits but never converts them before storing. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10746) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-formatted-io-review-ek10746-ek10748). Source-only.

<a id="ek10747"></a>**EK10747 — stdc wide scanf does not implement scansets.** `%[...]` falls through into its numeric conversion path. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10747) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-formatted-io-review-ek10746-ek10748). Source-only.

<a id="ek10748"></a>**EK10748 — stdc wide scanf `%Lf` writes through `double *`.** Wider long-double destinations are only partially written. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10748) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-wide-formatted-io-review-ek10746-ek10748). Source-only.

<a id="ek10749"></a>**EK10749 — stdc `setlocale()` ignores the requested category.** A `C.UTF-8` change to one category also changes `LC_CTYPE` and `MB_CUR_MAX`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10749) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-locale-state-review-ek10749-ek10750). Source-only.

<a id="ek10750"></a>**EK10750 — stdc `setlocale(category, NULL)` mutates locale state.** The query form resets to `C` instead of returning the active locale. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10750) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-locale-state-review-ek10749-ek10750). Source-only.

<a id="ek10751"></a>**EK10751 — stdc `wcsftime()` uses the next weekday/month name.** Its `%a`, `%A`, `%b`, `%B`, and `%p` table indices are off by one. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10751) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-time-formatting-review-ek10751-ek10753). Source-only.

<a id="ek10752"></a>**EK10752 — stdc `wcsftime()` can terminate before the output buffer when truncated.** Its final pointer adjustment can write before the destination. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10752) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-time-formatting-review-ek10751-ek10753). Source-only.

<a id="ek10753"></a>**EK10753 — stdc `wcsftime()` maps `%c`, `%C`, and `%x` incorrectly.** The conversions omit or add fields and `%C` is not a century. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10753) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-time-formatting-review-ek10751-ek10753). Source-only.

<a id="ek10754"></a>**EK10754 — stdc `realloc_nocopy(ptr, 0)` can return the old small allocation.** This contradicts its documented free-on-zero behavior. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10754) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-allocation-family-review-ek10754-ek10755). Source-only.

<a id="ek10755"></a>**EK10755 — stdc `free()` can confuse a valid allocation size with aligned-allocation metadata.** `malloc(MEMALIGN_MAGIC)` collides with the sentinel used by `free()`. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10755) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-allocation-family-review-ek10754-ek10755). Source-only.
<a id="ek10756"></a>**EK10756 — stdc `strndup()` stores the string length in `int`.** On 64-bit builds, a multi-gigabyte length can overflow or be narrowed before allocation. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10756) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-strndup-width-review-ek10756). Source-only.

<a id="od9698"></a>**OD9698 — USB MassStorage dereferences a failed unit allocation.** If per-LUN `AllocVecPooled()` fails, `CreateUnit()` writes through NULL before its caller's check; the task cannot send the setup signal awaited by `Storage::New()`. Selected in ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi package manifests. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9698) and [allocation/setup-wait trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#massstorage-unit-allocation-null-check-od9698). Source-only.

<a id="od9699"></a>**OD9699 — USB MassStorage continues after timer setup failure.** A failed port/request allocation reaches null-unsafe `OpenDevice()`; a failed timer-device open reaches null-unsafe `SendIO()`. The worker faults before signaling the synchronous creator wait; one allocation branch also leaks its reply port. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9699) and [timer setup trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#massstorage-timer-setup-failure-od9699). Source-only.
<a id="od11302"></a>**OD11302 — Virtual Bluetooth connection setup can strand a link slot when event allocation fails.** Classic and LE setup reserve a link before silently scheduling/delivering completion; allocation failure leaves the host waiting and the slot occupied until HCI Reset. Applies to the optional `vbthci.device` simulator. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11302) and [caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#virtual-bluetooth-connection-event-allocation-failure-od11302). Source-only.
<a id="od3951"></a>**OD3951 — Virtual Bluetooth pairing replies read six address bytes from short command buffers.** Five pairing reply opcodes copy or compare a six-byte address without checking the actual parameter length. The conditional trigger is a malformed direct `BTCMD_WRITEHCI` client request to optional `vbthci.device`; no in-tree truncated caller was found. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3951) and [command-length trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#virtual-bluetooth-command-parameter-validation-od3951). Source-only.
<a id="ek10757"></a>**EK10757 — stdc `strlen()` and `strnlen()` subtract signed pointer casts.** On targets where a valid string can cross the signed-`long` address boundary, the implementation can overflow while computing its length. Reachability is platform-conditional and unverified. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10757) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-narrow-string-scan-review-ek10757). Source-only.
<a id="ek10758"></a>**EK10758 — WITHDRAWN: stdc `strncpy()` padding remains within its `n`-byte bound.** The source NUL is counted again by the remaining padding count; the highest written index is `n-1`. See [withdrawal](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10758). Source-only.
<a id="ek10759"></a>**EK10759 — WITHDRAWN: stdc ctype guards signed-byte input.** The selected `tolower()` checks the value before indexing and returns out-of-range values unchanged; the configured byte tables case-fold ASCII only. See [withdrawal rationale](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10759) and [coverage recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-narrow-string-compare-review-ek10759). Source-only.
<a id="ek10760"></a>**EK10760 — stdc `strcasestr()` reads past both strings for an empty search string.** The unsigned comparison count wraps from zero, so the loop dereferences beyond both NUL terminators. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10760) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-substring-search-review-ek10759-ek10760). Source-only.
<a id="gd14768"></a>**GD14768 — Legacy network-browser backdrop parser omits the path terminator byte.** The `sprintf()` output is one byte larger than the requested allocation; the file is not selected in the current Wanderer manifests, so this is a dormant-source candidate. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14768) and [full source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-networkbrowserlist-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14769"></a>**GD14769 — AVX RGB24 conversion reads and writes past the requested pixel width.** Its vector body handles eight pixels while the loop advances by four; current architecture registration is disabled, so this is a dormant i386 implementation defect. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14769) and [conversion kernel review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#i386-hidd-gfx-rgbconv-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14770"></a>**GD14770 — AVX RGB24 conversion duplicates a source color channel.** Its shuffle mask selects source byte 1 for two output components; registration is currently disabled. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14770) and [conversion kernel review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#i386-hidd-gfx-rgbconv-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="gd14771"></a>**GD14771 — AVX BGR15 conversions map red and blue incorrectly.** The 32-to-15-bit kernels duplicate red and lose blue; the reverse kernel swaps the BGR15 channel masks. Registration is currently disabled. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14771) and [conversion kernel review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#i386-hidd-gfx-rgbconv-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.
<a id="od11303"></a>**OD11303 — Legacy Realtek firmware parser's patch range can wrap.** A 32-bit offset-plus-length check can pass after overflow, then the loader copies outside its firmware buffer. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional `rtlv1.fwl`. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11303) and [full loader/helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#realtek-firmware-loader-full-body-review-od11303-od11305). Source-only.
<a id="od11304"></a>**OD11304 — Realtek firmware loaders accept a ROM-version response without its version byte.** Both loaders default the missing value to zero and may select the wrong patch. Applies to optional `rtlv1.fwl` and `rtlv2.fwl`. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11304) and [full loader/helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#realtek-firmware-loader-full-body-review-od11303-od11305). Source-only.
<a id="od11305"></a>**OD11305 — Realtek firmware loaders register when opening DOS failed.** A later matching load uses a null DOS base for firmware-file access. Applies to both explicitly buildable optional Realtek loader modules. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11305) and [full loader/helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#realtek-firmware-loader-full-body-review-od11303-od11305). Source-only.
<a id="ek10761"></a>**EK10761 — stdc `arc4random()` fallback does not meet its cryptographic-strength contract when `entropy.resource` is unavailable.** See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10761) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-arc4random-family-full-body-2026-11-03). Source-only.

- [EK10762 — entropy estimate maintained by `AddEntropy()` is not exposed by `GetEntropyInfo()`](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10762) (optional entropy.resource; source-only).
<a id="od11306"></a>**OD11306 withdrawn — duplicate of OD11041.** The USB mass-storage caller-buffer alignment issue is already covered by [OD11041](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11041); OD11041 is the sole active finding. [Reconciliation note](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-massstorage-quickcopy-buffer-alignment-od11306).
<a id="od11307"></a>**OD11307 — Nouveau Falcon self-boot firmware copy reads and uploads a partial word.** A non-word-aligned external image reaches a 32-bit copy loop without size validation. [Finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11307) and [review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-shared-falcon-engine-firmware-boundary-review-od11307); conditional on an external image of invalid length. Source-only.
<a id="od11308"></a>**OD11308 — Nouveau DMA objects accept ranges wider than generation descriptor fields.** The shared API accepts 64-bit bounds, while generation-specific formats encode only 32, 40, or 56 address bits. [Finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11308) and [review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-dma-user-object-generation-review-od11308); conditional on an oversized NVIF range. Source-only.
<a id="od9755"></a>**OD9755 — Broadcom4400 RX filtering can stop the Sam440 PPC system on an unaligned word load.** The aligned DMA buffer plus 30-byte RX header places the destination MAC at 2 mod 4; the selected kernel does not emulate integer alignment faults and falls into its unhandled-exception loop. Conditional on the PPC compiler emitting a word load. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9755) and [platform trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#broadcom4400-ppc-rx-alignment-handler-od9755). Source-only.

- Nouveau DMA engine wrapper full-body review: six generation/shared files, 139 C lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md` entry `nouveau-dma-engine-generation-wrappers-full-body-2026-11-03`.
- Nouveau G84 BSP generation wrapper full-body review: one selected file, 18 C lines; no new finding. Shared Xtensa implementation remains open. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-bsp-g84-generation-wrapper-full-body-2026-11-03`.
<a id="od11309"></a>**OD11309 — Nouveau Xtensa loader silently truncates non-word-aligned firmware.** It discards the last one to three bytes and still reports engine initialization success. Conditional on malformed external G84 BSP/VP firmware. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11309) and [full review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-xtensa-shared-engine-and-generation-wrappers-od11309). Source-only.
<a id="od11310"></a>**OD11310 — Nouveau GA100/GA102 copy-engine interrupts return unhandled.** The legacy callback only logs and returns `IRQ_NONE`; if no other handler claims the dispatch, the shared dispatcher masks pending sources. Conditional on a CE-only interrupt. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11310) and [full review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-ce-generation-and-interrupt-review-od11310). Source-only.
- Nouveau MPEG engine full-body review: seven selected files, 567 C/header lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-mpeg-generation-and-channel-context-full-body-2026-11-03`.
<a id="od11311"></a>**OD11311 — Nouveau NV50/GF100 software vblank methods can dereference a null display pointer.** Their constructors tolerate absent display, but the vblank-allow methods do not. Conditional on display disabled while software engine remains enabled. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11311) and [full review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-software-engine-channel-and-vblank-review-od11311). Source-only.
- Nouveau NVDEC generation full-body review: five selected files, 127 C/header lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvdec-generation-and-lifecycle-full-body-2026-11-03`.
- Nouveau NVENC generation full-body review: four selected files, 84 C/header lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nvenc-generation-and-lifecycle-full-body-2026-11-03`.
- Nouveau SEC2 generation full-body review: seven selected files, 662 C/header lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-sec2-generation-and-firmware-lifecycle-full-body-2026-11-03`.
- Nouveau G98 SEC wrapper full-body review: one selected file, 51 C lines; no new finding. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-g98-sec-engine-wrapper-full-body-2026-11-03`.
<a id="od11312"></a>**OD11312 — Nouveau legacy FIFO ignores a hash-puller timeout before invalidating state.** If HASH_BUSY persists for two seconds, the code still invalidates the hash and restarts FIFO processing, risking incorrect PGRAPH instance offsets. Applies to legacy generations sharing this helper. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11312) and [full-body review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nv04-fifo-full-body-pause-and-interrupt-review-od11312). Source-only.
- Nouveau NV10/NV17/G98 FIFO variant full-body review: three selected files, 225 C lines; cross-referenced to OD11312. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nv10-nv17-g98-fifo-generation-variants-od11312`.
- Nouveau NV40/G84 FIFO generation full-body review: two selected files, 380 C lines; cross-referenced to OD11312. See `AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nv40-g84-fifo-generation-full-body-od11312`.
<a id="od11313"></a>**OD11313 — Nouveau NV50/G84 FIFO resumes after a context-switch acknowledgment timeout.** The unbind callback ignores a two-second wait timeout, then the caller resumes channel/runlist scheduling. Applies to NV50/G84/G98 FIFO paths. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11313) and [full review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-nv50-fifo-full-body-context-wait-and-runlist-review-od11313). Source-only.

<a id="od11314"></a>**OD11314 — Nouveau GF100 FIFO runlist fault-clear callback is a no-op.** Recovery calls a zero-mask register update, which cannot change the fault register before unblocking the runlist. Repeated/stale fault behavior is unverified. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11314) and [full-body review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gf100-fifo-full-body-runlist-recovery-review-od11314). Source-only.

<a id="od11315"></a>**OD11315 — Nouveau channel creation can accept an overflowing USERD offset.** The range check adds a caller-supplied 64-bit offset and slot size without overflow validation, then uses that offset for USERD writes and the RAMFC address. Applies to non-BAR USERD with a supplied handle; behavior was not run. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11315) and [review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fifo-shared-channel-lifecycle-review-od11315). Source-only.

<a id="od11316"></a>**OD11316 — Nouveau Ampere FIFO suppresses runlist construction errors.** A failed TOP runlist is deleted and skipped, while FIFO oneinit returns success; a later channel-group request for that runlist gets `-EINVAL`. Engines assigned only to it are unavailable through that path. Applies to GA100/GA102 paths; hardware behavior not exercised. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11316) and [full-body review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-ampere-fifo-full-body-runlist-and-interrupt-review-od11316). Source-only.

<a id="od11317"></a>**OD11317 — RTL8139 TX callback failure advances an unsubmitted ring slot.** The request is rejected, but `tx_current` still advances and the ordered completion scan can stall on a slot with no completion. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11317) and [transmit loop review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8139-transmit-loop-completion-recheck-od11317-od11318). Source-only.
<a id="od11318"></a>**OD11318 — RTL8139 TX wire error can leak into the next request.** `wire_error` is initialized outside the drain loop and is not reset after a failed callback. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11318) and [transmit loop review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8139-transmit-loop-completion-recheck-od11317-od11318). Source-only.

<a id="gd14772"></a>**GD14772 — Workbench handler dereferences a failed close-relay allocation.** A `WBENCHCLOSE` relay allocation failure is immediately dereferenced; the handler can exit without replying, leaving Intuition's synchronous close wait blocked. Distinct from GD5833's successful-allocation/no-Workbench-port leak. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14772-workbench-handler-dereferences-a-failed-close-relay-allocation) and [allocation/reply-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#workbench-close-relay-allocation-failure-gd14772). Source-only.

<a id="gd14773"></a>**GD14773 — Concurrent `CloseWorkBench()` calls can dereference a disposed screen.** One caller keeps the initial Workbench pointer across an unlocked notification interval; another can close and dispose that screen before the first caller dereferences its saved pointer. See [finding](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14773-concurrent-closeworkbench-calls-can-dereference-a-disposed-screen) and [caller/lifetime trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#closeworkbench-concurrent-screen-lifetime-gd14773). Source-only.
