**[GD14774](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14774) — Workbench handler can send through a port after it is unregistered and freed.** Explicitly built Wanderer and Workbook targets unregister and delete their application ports while handler sends are unsynchronized with that lifetime; an overlapping relay or screen event can pass either NULL or a stale pointer to `PutMsg()`. Their parent aggregate edges are commented out. Conditional source-level race; no teardown was run.

**[GD14775](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14775-editor-include-path-parsing-writes-past-its-fixed-scratch-buffer-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Ctrl+Enter copies an unbounded include path into the 256-byte `BufTxt` array, overrunning it on a sufficiently long include line.**

**[GD14776](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14776-editor-selected-line-indentation-ignores-allocation-failures-explicit-optional-target) — Editor selected-line indentation silently commits only the lines whose buffer growth succeeds, then advances the active cursor as if its line changed.**

**[GD14777](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14777-editor-selected-text-deletion-keeps-failed-line-mutations-in-its-undo-count-path-explicit-optional-target) — Editor selection deletion ignores line-buffer allocation failures, decrements its line count anyway, and can record a failed join that corrupts the list on undo.**

**[GD14778](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14778-editor-case-conversion-dereferences-the-end-of-an-empty-file-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Upper/Lower/Toggle reads through a NULL line buffer on a zero-byte file; end-of-line positions also lack a character bound check.**

**[GD14779](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14779-editor-case-conversion-bypasses-undo-and-modified-state-tracking-explicit-optional-target) — Editor case conversion changes text without undo or the modified flag, so closing a clean project discards it without prompting.**


**[OD11319](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11319) — Optional DMG plugin truncates its hash-table allocation size before indexing every output MiB; sufficiently large declared sparse images can make open write past the allocated index.**

**[OD11320](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11320) — Optional DMG plugin truncates total sectors above 2^32 in geometry; TD_GETGEOMETRY and SCSI READ CAPACITY can underreport a large image.**

**[OD11321](AROS-other-drivers.md#aux-fast-bptr-startup-tag-collision-od11321) — The selected Workbench AUX handler clears address bit 30 from a stack-local startup pointer on fast-BPTR targets when that bit is set, misaddressing the startup structure.**

**[GD14780](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14780-editor-reload-clears-the-unsaved-marker-before-checking-whether-reload-succeeded-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Reload clears the modified flag and undo history before confirming the backing file loaded; a failed reload leaves old edits that can later be discarded without a save prompt.**

**[GD14781](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14781-editor-save-as-clears-the-dirty-state-before-the-save-succeeds-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Save As marks modified text clean before the write succeeds, so a failed save can be followed by closing without a prompt.**

**[GD14782](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14782-editor-save-reports-success-after-a-write-failure-explicit-optional-target) — Editor save ignores buffered write and close failures and returns success, allowing callers to clear the modified marker after a partial file write.**

**[GD14783](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14783-editor-cut-deletes-selected-text-after-a-failed-clipboard-write-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Cut ignores IFF clipboard write failures and deletes the selection after reporting success.**

**[GD14784](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14784-editor-join-and-strip-deletes-the-next-line-after-insertion-fails-explicit-optional-target) — Editor “join and strip” deletes the next line even when appending its text fails, losing that line on allocation failure.**

**[GD14785](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14785-editor-word-selection-reads-one-byte-past-an-unterminated-final-line-explicit-optional-target) — Editor word selection can read past the file buffer when its backward scan begins at the end of an unterminated final line.**

**[GD14786](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14786-editor-paste-reports-success-and-reads-uninitialized-line-counts-after-partial-insertion-failure-explicit-optional-target) — Editor multiline paste ignores partial insertion failure and may update the project using an uninitialized line count.**

**[GD14787](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14787-editor-text-rendering-can-overrun-its-fixed-scratch-buffer-explicit-optional-target) — Editor line rendering can write beyond its 256-byte scratch buffer when more than 256 text columns are visible.**

**[GD14788](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14788-editor-whole-word-search-reads-past-an-unterminated-final-line-explicit-optional-target) — Editor whole-word search reads one byte past an unterminated final line when a match reaches EOF.**

**[GD14789](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14789-editor-bracket-matching-dereferences-the-cursor-position-without-checking-line-length-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Find Bracket reads at the cursor without checking for end-of-line or an empty line.**

**[GD14790](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14790-editor-preferences-always-replace-a-selected-parent-screen-with-the-default-public-screen-explicit-optional-target) — Editor's parent-screen validation loop never iterates, so applying preferences substitutes the default public screen.**

**[GD14791](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14791-editor-preferences-parser-trusts-field-lengths-from-the-file-explicit-optional-target) — Editor preferences parsing copies file-declared lengths without checking record bounds or destination field sizes.**

**[GD14792](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14792-editor-search-window-dereferences-gadgets-after-unchecked-allocation-failures-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Search/Replace initialization dereferences unchecked gadget-allocation results and can crash under memory pressure.**

**[GD14793](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14793-editor-replace-all-can-loop-forever-when-deletion-fails-for-an-empty-replacement-explicit-optional-target) — Editor Replace All can repeatedly match the same text forever when deletion fails and the replacement is empty.**



**[GD14794](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14794-icon-35-writer-leaks-an-iffhandle-on-every-serialization-explicit-optional-target) — Icon 3.5 serialization leaks an IFFHandle on each save that uses the IFF writer.**

**[OD11322](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11322) — VMM PageHandler can acknowledge one keyboard reset more than once, decrementing the shared handler count early.**

**[GD14795](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14795-diskfont-cache-entry-count-can-wrap-its-allocation-on-32-bit-builds) — A corrupt diskfont cache can wrap a `TTextAttr` allocation and overrun it during initialization on 32-bit builds.**

**[GD14796](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14796-diskfont-iterator-allocation-failure-leaves-the-font-semaphore-held) — Diskfont iterator allocation failure leaves the font semaphore held, blocking later font operations.**

**[GD14797](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14797-diskfont-directory-enumeration-passes-failed-exall-allocations-to-dos) — Diskfont directory enumeration uses unchecked ExAll control and data-buffer allocations.**

**[GD14798](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14798-failed-diskfont-descriptor-reread-leaves-the-process-in-the-fonts-directory) — A failed descriptor reread returns before restoring the caller's current directory.**

**[GD14799](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14799) — More writes before its input buffer when a non-seekable read fails.**

**[GD14800](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14800) — More's line-array size multiplication can wrap before count-based initialization on 32-bit builds.**

**[GD14801](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14801) — More discards Escape and other non-tracking messages in its scrollbar wait loop.**

**[GD14802](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14802) — More's Find requester overflows its static search buffer by one byte at the maximum input length.**

**[GD14803](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14803) — More truncates file-requester selections longer than its 108-byte path buffer.**

**[GD14804](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14804-sound-datatype-indexes-past-its-validity-flags-when-one-shot-playback-ends) — Sound.datatype indexes beyond its two-entry validity array when non-continuous AHI playback reaches its stop branch.**

**[GD14805](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14805-stereo-sound-datatype-playback-truncates-large-cycle-counts) — Stereo Sound.datatype AHI playback truncates cycle counts above 32,767 in its 16-bit callback counter.**

**[GD14806](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14806-vc4-mesa-bo-cache-timeout-uses-adjustable-wall-time-conditional) — Raspberry Pi VC4 Mesa measures BO-cache timeout with the settable system clock.**

**[GD14807](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14807-mesa-stdc-base-resolver-races-across-concurrent-tasks-conditional) — Raspberry Pi Mesa's shared StdC base resolver can return another task's base.**

**[OD3366](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3366) — USB serial Open can consume its own setup request or wait on the wrong port; Palm PDA Close has the same-port defect.**


<a id="ek10763"></a>**EK10763 — stdc `strrev()` decrements before an empty string.** Empty input causes undefined pointer arithmetic. FKey reaches it from an accepted empty `INSERT ` tooltype and an empty Insert Text GUI value (optional target). See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10763) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-reverse-and-collation-helper-pass-ek10763-ek10764). Source-only.
<a id="ek10764"></a>**EK10764 — WITHDRAWN: `strxfrm()`'s selected `strncpy()` copy stays within `n` bytes.** See [withdrawal](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10764). Source-only.
<a id="ek10765"></a>**EK10765 — stdc `strtod()` overflows its signed exponent accumulator.** A decimal exponent above `INT_MAX` triggers signed overflow while parsing; `strtof()`, `strtold()`, and `atof()` inherit the path in FPU-enabled builds. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10765) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-floating-conversion-wrapper-pass-ek10765). Source-only.
<a id="ek10766"></a>**EK10766 — unsigned string conversions negate the overflow sentinel.** Negative magnitudes beyond the unsigned result range set `ERANGE` but return a small wrapped value instead of the maximum; `strtoumax()` delegates to the affected code. Standards confidence is medium because WG14 records ambiguity in the inherited wording. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10766) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#unsigned-string-overflow-recheck-ek10766). Source-only.
<a id="ek10767"></a>**EK10767 — stdc `strtod()` does not parse hexadecimal floating constants.** In FPU-enabled builds, `0x1p2` is parsed only as the initial zero; `strtof()`, `strtold()`, and `atof()` inherit the omission. See [finding](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10767) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdcio-floating-conversion-wrapper-pass-ek10765). Source-only.
<a id="od11323"></a>**OD11323 — Nouveau fault-buffer initialization leaks a partially initialized buffer when backing allocation or BAR2 pinning fails.** Teardown walks only the count of successfully completed buffers. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11323) and the [Nouveau fault-buffer cleanup pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-fault-buffer-oneinit-cleanup-od11323). Source-only.
<a id="od11324"></a>**OD11324 — Nouveau GSP GR context promotion leaks its allocated RPC buffer when local memory allocation or VMM setup fails.** The direct error returns bypass the RPC buffer release path. See [finding](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11324) and the [R535/R570/R580 GR promotion trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-gr-promotion-rpc-cleanup-od11324). Source-only.


<a id="od11247"></a>**[OD11247](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11247) — Nouveau thermal BIOS fan parsing writes beyond the fixed trip array.** In the legacy fallback, an 11th `0x24` record writes through the following fan settings and beyond the parsed fan structure; `0x25` before any trip indexes before the array. Conditional on malformed/unsupported legacy thermal BIOS data; no affected board ROM was examined. See the [fan parser and consumer trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-thermal-bios-sensor-fan-parser-and-fallback-caller-pass-od11247-added-2026-11-03). Source-only.


<a id="ek9152"></a>**[EK9152](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9152) — taskless pre-init semaphore attempts can leave a semaphore permanently held.** Before the bootstrap task exists, a `PREINITLIB` callback can get TRUE from either attempt API on a free semaphore, but `ReleaseSemaphore()` returns without releasing it. Later exclusive users can wait indefinitely. The only maintained callback in this snapshot does not make the call, so current startup reachability is unestablished. See the [pre-init path and release trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#taskless-preinitlib-attemptsemaphore-ek9152). Source-only.


<a id="gd14808"></a>**[GD14808](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14808) — chunky pixel writes can read before their source array after clipping.** The shared renderer stores a clipped source offset in signed `WORD`, then forms a pointer from it; offsets above 32767 can wrap negative, so `WritePixelArray8()`, `WriteChunkyPixels()`, and `WritePixels8()` can pass a pointer before the caller's data to the generic HIDD reader. No in-tree caller with this extreme clipping offset was established. See the [source-offset and HIDD trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-chunky-pixel-write-clipped-source-offset-gd14808). Source-only.
**GD14809 — Vulkan-Hpp scalar query-result helper accepts `queryCount > 1` while providing only one `DataType` object as output storage.** A scalar caller can ask the Vulkan command to write several results through that single object. Optional downstream Vulkan-Hpp clients only; no in-tree caller found. See [GD14809](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14809) and its [source/contract trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-query-pool-scalar-result-capacity-gd14809).

**[EK10768](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10768) — `SetTaskPri()`, `SetTaskAffinity()`, or `Signal()` may pass a freed affinity mask to `KrnScheduleCPU()` if a remotely running task terminates after the caller drops its lock. Conditional on ExecSMP, finite task affinity, and concurrent removal. Source-only; see the [lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#settaskpri-remote-affinity-mask-ek10768).

**[EK10769](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10769) — Efika's selected idle task and empty-ready path spin without executing their `MSR_POW` power-save instruction. Conditional on an explicit CHRP Efika build reaching idle; power impact is hardware-dependent. Source-only; see the [idle power-path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#efika-idle-power-path-ek10769).

**[EK10770](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10770) — DOSBoot formats device rows into a fixed 96-byte label without bounding the device and startup-device names. Conditional on a valid-media row whose formatted text exceeds the allocation. Applies to the optional Boot Options menu. See the [format-capacity trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-format-capacity-ek10770). Source-only.

**GD14811 — Vulkan GPU re-registration can replace callbacks and driver data behind live handles.** Conditional on a provider registering the same PCI device with a different backend after creating Vulkan objects, with that entry remaining preferred; later calls can reach the replacement callbacks with old handles. No in-tree provider caller was found. See [GD14811](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14811) and the [registry/dispatch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-registry-live-handle-reregistration-gd14811). Source-only.

**[GD14812](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14812) — MUIScreen can open an AutoClose public screen before its worker publishes the message port, silently omitting task/signal setup and AutoClose tracking. Conditional on the first screen open racing worker startup. See the [startup-readiness trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#muiscreen-autoclose-worker-startup-readiness-gd14812). Source-only.

**[GD14813](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14813) — GL pass-through library initialization formats a notification path through NULL if its allocation fails. Conditional on `ENV:SYS` lookup succeeding and allocation failure during startup. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-libs-gl` target. See the [full-body and notification setup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gl-pass-through-library-full-body-and-notification-setup-gd14813). Source-only.

**[GD14814](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14814) — Lamp passes pen 255 to `SetAPen()` when its PenSpec cannot be resolved. Conditional on PenSpec conversion/setup failure and a subsequent draw; the visible result depends on screen depth/backend. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-classes-zune-lamp` target. See the [MUI pen caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#lamp-mui-penspec-failure-caller-gd14814). Source-only.

**[GD14815](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14815) — Window stores `MUI_ObtainPen()` results in 16-bit fields, dropping the allocation marker and leaking allocated half-shine/half-shadow pens at cleanup. Conditional on `ObtainBestPenA()` allocating those RGB pens. Applies to explicitly buildable muimaster. See the [Window render-info pen ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#window-render-info-pen-ownership-gd14815). Source-only.


GD5097 refinement (2026-11-04): `PubScreenStatus()` may refuse privatization while visitor references remain, and the AutoClose worker can lose its tracking record if a new visitor arrives after the zero-count signal but before `CloseScreen()`. The screen can remain public or private depending on the path; both branches ignore close failure and discard tracking. See [GD5097](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5097) and the [MUIScreen status/worker trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#muiscreen-autoclose-worker-failed-close-race-gd5097).


**[OD11325](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11325) — Nouveau can narrow an oversized contiguous VRAM request to zero 4 KiB pages, then return a successful zero-length or one-page object for an oversized request. Conditional on a selected contiguous Nouveau VRAM path and the request size. See the [allocator and NVIF caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-zero-page-count-vram-request-od11325). Source-only.
**[OD11326](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11326) — Nouveau GSP/RM can wrap a near-4 GiB graphics MAIN context size to zero when adding subcontext headers; the resulting zero-sized VMM mapping aborts GR initialization if RM returns the boundary value. Scoped to R535/R570/R580 GSP/RM paths; firmware reachability is unverified. See the [context-size and VMM trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-gr-context-size-wrap-od11326). Source-only.
**[OD11327](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11327) — GP100 fault-buffer entry-count multiplication can wrap, allocating 4 KiB while exposing a count over 134 million entries. Conditional on the hardware count register returning the stated value; behavior beyond the mapped storage is unverified. See the [count-to-allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#gp100-fault-buffer-size-wrap-od11327). Source-only.


<a id="od11328"></a>**[OD11328](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11328) — 18 optional network-driver `S2_DEVICEQUERY` handlers write beyond a short caller-advertised result buffer; 17 clamp only the initial copy, while PPP writes the full result.** Applies when a driver target is selected and a client provides a short result area. See the [specification and driver-call-site census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sana-ii-devicequery-short-buffer-writes-od11328). Source-only.
**[OD11330](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11330) — AROSTCP unlinks an open SANA-II interface before allocating its temporary close request; if request or port allocation fails, it skips `CloseDevice()` and abandons the open interface state during teardown. Trigger is conditional on allocation failure in `sana_deinit()`. See the [teardown trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#arostcp-sana-deinit-close-request-allocation-od11330). Source-only.
**[OD11331](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11331) — AROSTCP can leave the MiamiPanel interface state at “Going Online” when request allocation fails; the device stays offline, the ioctl returns success, and no recovery state is sent. Conditional on the GUI running during low-memory interface bring-up. Source-only.
**[OD11332](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11332) — AROSTCP can queue uninitialized IPv4 destination bytes when `IFF_NOARP` skips resolution or `arpresolve()` accepts a broadcast without filling its output; the RTL8139 target copies them into the Ethernet frame; RTL8139 is selected through the active cards aggregate for i386, x86_64, m68k and ppc Workbench builds. Source-only.
**[OD11333](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11333) — AROSTCP reports success and commits an IPv4/IPv6 address after temporary-request allocation or `S2_CONFIGINTERFACE` failure leaves the SANA device not running. Source-only.

**[GD14816](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14816) — VulkanProbe may fall back to another compute-capable GPU and still report success on the RX 9060 XT. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional probe. Source-only.
**[GD14817](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14817) — VulkanProbe never closes its successful `radeonsi.hidd` open; the outstanding library reference can prevent normal close/expunge after the probe exits. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional probe. Source-only.

**[GD14818](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14818) — Gallium HIDD's public `aHidd_Gallium_WinSys` macro references an attribute enum value that is not declared. Conditional compile failure for consumers that use it; no in-tree caller found. Source-only.


**[GD14819](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14819) — `CreatePipe()` can return a stale non-NULL caller output value when all pipe-creation attempts fail. Conditional on external callers supplying pre-populated output storage; the checked-in Mesa caller zero-initializes it. Source-only.

**[GD14820](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14820) — Mesa3DGL creates Gallium HIDD driver objects but never actively calls `DestroyPipe()` during normal context destruction or later creation-failure cleanup. Repeated contexts can retain driver objects. Source-only.

**[OD10141](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10141) — Nouveau ignores thermal fan construction failure and can dereference a NULL fan during initialization. Conditional on all fan-backend allocations failing; GF119/GT215 have an additional init-time dereference. Source-only.

**[OD11334](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11334) — Nouveau MXM DCB sanitization fails to check the zero “connector entry missing” result and can overwrite the first VBIOS image byte. Conditional on incomplete MXM/DCB connector metadata and default sanitization. Source-only.

**[OD11335](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11335) — Nouveau derives the PMU boot upload size from an unchecked unsigned end-minus-start range and streams that length during GM200/GV100 post-init. Conditional on inconsistent PMU metadata. Source-only.

**[OD11336](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11336) — Nouveau GSP FWSEC dereferences a missing PMU descriptor pointer or reads its header past the validated BIOS buffer. Conditional on an invalid/truncated type-`0x85` descriptor. Source-only.

**[OD11337](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11337) — Nouveau's nonzero-index GPIO/XPIO path loses the XPIO table version before `dcb_gpio_parse()` decodes the entry. No checked-in nonzero-index caller found. Source-only.

**[GD14821](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14821) — Jano Editor can free a `CMD_NEWEDIT` request and its startup arguments after Ctrl-C interrupts the reply wait, while the request may remain queued for the running instance. Conditional; explicitly buildable optional Editor target. Source-only.

**[OD11338](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11338) — Nouveau's 32-line GPIO event path uses signed `1 << 31` in interrupt enable/disable and pending-status masks. Conditional on GPIO line 31 handling; compiler impact untested. Source-only.

**[GD14822](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14822) — Jano Editor frees its IPC request/reply port, then `CloseMainWnd()` sends `CMD_KILL` through those freed pointers if Preferences Editor is running. Applies to the explicitly buildable optional Editor target. Source-only.


**[OD3642](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3642) — IFFParse reports short clipboard reads as complete; TextEditor can import unwritten bytes from a truncated CHRS chunk. Conditional on a short backing-file read. Source-only.

**[OD810](AROS-other-drivers.md#od810) — Clipboard device ignores failed zero-padding and seek operations for sparse writes; with its RAM fallback, a payload can be stored at EOF while the device reports success and records a larger cached size. Conditional on a gap write under allocation failure; no selected in-tree sparse-write caller was found. Source-only. See the [gap-write failure trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#clipboard-gap-write-allocation-failure-od810-2026-11-04).

**[OD2464](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2464) — OpenSBI DesignWare UART accepts a unit without a working transmit IRQ.** Node-allocation failure, an absent or unmapped PLIC, or an out-of-range PLIC source can leave a successfully opened unit without interrupt delivery; deferred writes may never complete. Conditional on interrupt setup and partial-write state; source-only.

MonitorClass non-HIDD cursor-conversion candidate reconciliation (GD5823/GD5824 withdrawn; 2026-11-04): traced all in-tree shape-message producers through PointerClass shared-pointer construction. `AllocSpriteDataA()` creates output with `BMF_SPECIALFMT`, and successful `AllocBitMap()` outputs are marked HIDD; allocation failure prevents pointer publication. No selected caller can reach MonitorClass's temporary non-HIDD bitmap conversion branch, so its reported leak and failed-allocation NULL blit were implementation-only candidates without an in-tree trigger. Both IDs are withdrawn in the detailed report; full-body review credit remains. Source-only.

Efika idle-power occurrence census (EK10769 retained; 2026-11-04): checked every `MSR_POW` occurrence in the selected Efika kernel. The additional writes belong only to unhandled-exception terminal loops; they do not provide a normal idle fallback. The idle task and empty-ready scheduler loop remain non-sleeping as recorded in EK10769. No hardware or runtime state was used; source-only.

**[OD11340](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11340) — Nouveau connector events can index past the GPIO event-reference array when BIOS HPD metadata supplies a line outside the backend's 32-line range.** Conditional on an out-of-range DCB mapping and a GPIO-based PLUG/UNPLUG subscription; no BIOS incidence was verified.

task.resource lock initialization lead (EK313 retained; 2026-11-04): verified `TaskListSpinLock` starts zero because Exec `MakeLibrary()` clears the complete resource base, and selected ExecSMP spinlocks use zero as their unlocked state. The missing explicit init call is not a separate bug; EK313 remains the unsynchronized prelaunch list insertion. No task.resource load, lock or build was used.


**[GD14823](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14823) — Jano Editor leaves its global port pointer set after `CreateIORequest()` fails and frees the port; common cleanup then removes and frees the stale pointer again. In duplicate-instance mode, the NULL-named private port is also freed while still linked in Exec's port list. Conditional on optional Editor request allocation failure. See the [allocation rollback trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#jano-editor-port-allocation-rollback-gd14823). Source-only.


**[GD14824](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14824) — `clippingtest` prints setup errors but always exits with status zero, so a status-based runner can treat a test that never ran as successful. Conditional on use by such a runner; no checked-in caller was found. See the [`test-layers` re-review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-helper-re-review-gd14824). Source-only.


**[OD11341](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11341) — Nouveau decodes version-sized GPIO fields without checking the BIOS entry stride; a short record can borrow fields from following image bytes. The shared parser is used by GPIO matching and the BIOS init-script path. Conditional on inconsistent GPIO table metadata. See the [entry-length recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gpio-entry-length-recheck-od11341). Source-only.

**[OD11342](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11342) — AROSTCP routes outgoing IPv4 multicast through ARP resolution instead of applying the link-layer multicast mapping, leaving packets queued for an unresolved group address. Conditional on multicast-enabled AROSTCP and an address-based SANA-II interface; RTL8139 is selected through the active cards aggregate on i386, x86_64, m68k and ppc Workbench builds. Source-only.**

**[OD11343](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11343) — AROSTCP can program IPv4/IPv6 SANA-II multicast filters before allocating membership records; allocation failure returns without removing the filter. BCMGENET retains an orphaned range, while RTL8139 can remain in `IFF_ALLMULTI` receive mode. Conditional on provider acceptance followed by pool exhaustion; the active network aggregate selects BCMGENET on Raspberry Pi and RTL8139 through the card-driver aggregate on supported CPU families, with e1000, nForce and rtl816x providing additional all-multicast paths. Source-only.**

**[EK10771](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10771) — `stpsym()` writes two bytes into zero- or one-byte destinations and returns inside a truncated symbol rather than after its full extent. Conditional on external API input; no direct in-tree caller found. See the [SAS/C helper review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#sas-c-string-helper-review-ek10771). Source-only.

UserGroup `ioerr2errno()` caller pass (2026-11-04; no new EK): checked both selected negative-I/O-error consumers against the converter’s DOS error mappings and fallback; no separate mismatch established. This adds one full-body path and 35 C lines to Exec/Kernel coverage. Source-only.

**[GD14825](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14825) — PopupMenu waits indefinitely for IDCMP_NEWSIZE after Intuition fails to allocate the asynchronous ChangeWindowBox() action.** Conditional on resizing an existing popup from a non-InputDeviceTask, action-pool allocation failure, and an empty popup UserPort. Applies to explicitly built PopupMenu; no default-image inclusion is claimed. See the [resize failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-resize-action-failure-gd14825). Source-only.


**[GD14826](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14826) — PopupMenu sorted insertion always misses its insertion point because its unsigned string-comparison result is tested as negative; the API still reports insertion success. No in-tree caller of this tag was found; external/future clients only. Explicit PopupMenu builds only. See the [support-helper review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-support-helpers-sorted-insertion-and-shadow-list-pass). Source-only.





**[GD14829](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14829) — PopupMenu row sizing narrows custom image heights to 8 bits, underestimating images taller than 255 pixels. Explicit PopupMenu builds only. See the [layout calculation review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-and-topology-calculation-pass). Source-only.

**[GD14830](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14830) — PopupMenu pull-down layout subtracts child minimum heights from a smaller screen-bar height using unsigned arithmetic, which can wrap and assign incorrect row sizes. Explicit PopupMenu builds only. See the [layout calculation review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-and-topology-calculation-pass). Source-only.




**[GD14832](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14832) — PopupMenu’s optional real-shadow path swaps red and blue fields when shading BGR15/BGR16 pixels. Applies to non-AROS CyberGraphX builds where that path is enabled; AROS excludes it. See the [pixel-format review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-real-shadow-pixelformat-pass). Source-only.

Conditional on partial init failure with concurrent holders. See the [init rollback review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cybergraphics-library-init-rollback-pass). Source-only.

**[GD14836](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14836) — A failed file read leaves a negative byte count that TextEditor demo uses as a buffer index, writing before the input buffer. Applies to the selected optional demo. Source-only.**

**[GD14837](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14837) — TextEditor demo's SkipHeader inner scan is unbounded and reads past files with no newline. Applies to the selected optional demo. Source-only.**

**[GD14838](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14838) — TextEditor MCP's AmigaOS 4 `menu` key formatter is not matched by its parser because of a misspelled platform conditional; editing the binding loses its raw key. Optional AmigaOS 4 MCP build. Source-only.**

**[GD14839](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14839) — TextEditor MCP retains a successful Locale library open when AmigaOS 4 `GetInterface()` fails during initialization; optional AmigaOS 4 MCP build. Source-only.**


**[GD14841](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14841) — TextEditor MCP's DEBUG memory tracker truncates long allocator aliases and reports correctly released objects as unsuitable frees. Affects optional AmigaOS 4 and MorphOS MCP DEBUG builds with memory tracking enabled; the underlying allocation and release APIs remain paired. See the [debug memory-tracker review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-debug-memory-tracker-pass). Source-only.**


**[EK840](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek840) — On ExecSMP, selected `Break PROCESS`, `ChangeTaskPri PROCESS` and `Status PROCESS` can use a CLI `Process *` after `FindCliProc()` releases the list lock; local `Forbid()` does not protect it from another CPU exiting the target. Status formats the borrowed process after releasing `rn_RootLock`. See the [FindCliProc caller-lifetime review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#findcliproc-borrowed-process-lifetime-ek840). Source-only.**


**[EK10772](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10772) — `Resident REMOVE` leaves one `Forbid()` level outstanding whenever the requested segment exists, and Exec preserves the task's forbid nesting across waits. Subsequent code in that task can run without task switching until it balances the count. See the [Resident command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#resident-command-full-body-forbid-balance-ek10772). Source-only.**


**[EK10773](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10773) — `Run` can launch a `+`-continued command without its continuation when joining the text runs out of memory, leaving that text in the parent input stream. Conditional on continuation input and allocation failure. See the [Run command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#run-command-full-body-continuation-allocation-ek10773). Source-only.**


**[EK10774](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10774) — `Execute` copies script paths longer than the CLI command-name BSTR's 255-byte capacity into that fixed buffer. Conditional on an existing long path accepted by the shell's 512-byte input line. See the [Execute command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-command-full-body-name-boundary-ek10774). Source-only.**


**[EK10775](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10775) — If `Execute` cannot allocate its argument buffer, it returns failure after changing `cli_CurrentInput` to the script; the Shell continues reading from that script despite the failure. Conditional on nonempty arguments and allocation failure. See the [failure-path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-setvbuf-failure-state-retention-ek10775). Source-only.**


**[EK10776](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10776) — If `Execute` cannot allocate the buffer that joins unread `+` continuation text to explicit arguments, it still runs the script with incomplete arguments. Conditional on buffered continuation and allocation failure. See the [join-allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#execute-continuation-join-allocation-ek10776). Source-only.**


**[EK10777](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10777) — `Pipe` can launch a pipeline stage with `NIL:` input when duplicating its input handle fails; a duplicated lock can also be leaked if `OpenFromLock()` fails. Conditional on a pipeline and handle/allocation failure. See the [Pipe command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pipe-command-full-body-input-ownership-ek10777). Source-only.**


**[EK10778](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10778) — `CD` can loop indefinitely when `GetLockName()`'s initial allocation fails while DOS `IoErr()` is zero; its unsigned retry size eventually wraps. Conditional on low memory and that error state. See the [CD command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cd-command-full-body-getlockname-retry-ek10778). Source-only.**


**[EK10779](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10779) — `Path RESET` frees its successor before the loop advances into it, traversing freed list storage and leaking the original head. Requires at least two command-path entries. See the [Path command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779). Source-only.**


**[EK10780](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10780) — `Path` can pass a NULL DOS_FIB to `Examine()` after allocation failure; the successful Examine path dereferences it. Requires a DOS_FIB allocation failure during a path check. See the [Path command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779). Source-only.**


**[EK10781](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10781) — `Path ADD` stores a failed insertion as its next predecessor; a later eligible path dereferences NULL. Requires an earlier path insertion to fail and a later eligible path in the same ADD request. See the [Path command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779). Source-only.**


**[EK10782](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10782) — `Path` leaks the allocated DOS_FIB when `Examine()` fails. Requires Examine() failure after DOS_FIB allocation succeeds. See the [Path command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#path-command-full-body-list-lifetime-ek10779). Source-only.**


**[EK10783](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10783) — `Setenv` and `Unsetenv` can return success with absent or partial `ENV:` listings when FIB allocation, `Examine()`, or `ExNext()` fails. Conditional on listing mode and a DOS/filesystem failure. See the [listing error-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#setenv-command-full-body-listing-errors-ek10783). Source-only.**


**[EK10784](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10784) — `Get` and `Getenv` print local/global values longer than 255 bytes as complete after truncating them to fixed buffers; the selected `Set` and `Setenv` commands can create longer values. See the [Getenv value-bound review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#getenv-command-full-body-value-bound-ek10784). Source-only.**


**[EK10785](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10785) — `If ... VAL` ignores numeric parse failures, so invalid or partially numeric operands can be compared as zero or as a numeric prefix. Conditional on malformed numeric operands. See the [If command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#if-command-full-body-evaluation-and-error-status-ek10785). Source-only.**

**[EK10786](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10786) — `If` prints an error for use outside scripts or an unmatched false block but returns success, masking the failure from Shell result handling. Conditional on either invalid context. See the [If command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#if-command-full-body-evaluation-and-error-status-ek10785). Source-only.**


**[EK10787](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10787) — A label-less `Skip` returns success at EOF when no `EndSkip` was found, despite documenting that a missing target is an error. Conditional on an unterminated skip block. See the [control-flow command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#shell-control-flow-command-full-body-pass-ek10787). Source-only.**


**[EK10788](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10788) — `Ask` can accept the unread suffix of an overlong invalid response as a new answer; a trailing `yes` can set the yes return code. Conditional on an input line longer than 99 bytes. See the [Ask input-boundary review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ask-command-full-body-input-boundary-ek10788). Source-only.**


**[EK10789](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10789) — `Cut` adds `StrToLong()`'s unchecked -1 failure result to the bounds pointer and then dereferences before the operand. Conditional on a malformed CHAR/WORD range. See the [Cut bounds review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cut-command-full-body-bounds-pass-ek10789). Source-only.**


**[EK10790](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10790) — `PathPart DIR` allocates no byte for a terminator before calling a path helper that scans to NUL, so it reads beyond the requested buffer. Conditional on the `DIR` option. See the [PathPart review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pathpart-and-fault-command-full-body-pass-ek10790). Source-only.**


**[EK10791](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10791) — `Clip GET WAIT` ignores a failed `StartNotify()` and can wait indefinitely for a signal that will never be sent. Requires GET+WAIT and a StartNotify registration failure. See the [Clip command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791). Source-only.**


**[EK10792](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10792) — `Clip COUNT` uses an 8-bit counter and reports zero if all 256 units are present. Requires all 256 clipboard units to be counted as occupied. See the [Clip command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791). Source-only.**


**[EK10793](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10793) — `Clip COUNT` treats every open error except not-found as an occupied unit. Requires COUNT and an open failure other than ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND. See the [Clip command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791). Source-only.**


**[EK10794](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10794) — `Clip SET` reports success after writing the payload even if IFF chunk finalization fails. Requires a final IFF chunk/write/seek failure after the payload write succeeds. See the [Clip command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791). Source-only.**


**[EK10795](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10795) — `Clip GET` does not check cumulative ULONG size arithmetic while concatenating text chunks, so a wrapped allocation can be followed by an oversized copy. Requires cumulative text chunks to exceed the ULONG aggregate-size range. See the [Clip command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#clip-command-full-body-and-notification-iff-pass-ek10791). Source-only.**


**[EK10796](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10796) — `Echo` computes unsigned `l - 1` for an empty string with positive `FIRST`, then dereferences the out-of-range pointer. Conditional on that input. See the [Echo bounds review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#echo-command-full-body-bounds-pass-ek10796). Source-only.**

**[EK10797](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10797) — `Stack` can display a negative byte count after accepting a near-`LONG_MAX` stack size on 64-bit targets.** Requires 32-bit `LONG`, 64-bit `size_t`, and a large stack setting. See the [Stack command review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stack-quit-and-registration-full-body-pass-ek10797). Source-only.

**[EK10798](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10798) — embedded shell-command initialization ignores `AddSegment()` failures and can report success with commands missing after allocation failure.** Conditional on resident-list allocation failure during initialization. See the [registration review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stack-quit-and-registration-full-body-pass-ek10797). Source-only.

**[EK10799](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10799) — `Prompt` can print a stale or empty fault message when `SetPrompt()` rejects a name over 255 bytes without setting IoErr.** The Shell input limit makes the case reachable. See the [SetPrompt contract review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#prompt-command-setprompt-ioerr-contract-ek10799). Source-only.

**[EK10800](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10800) — POSIX `chdir("")`/`opendir("")` can succeed on the current directory; native path mode also lets the stat-family, `fstatat()`, and read-only `open()`/`openat()` operate on empty paths there.** Conditional on selected handlers accepting empty relative names. See the [empty-path caller pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-stat-empty-path-mode-recheck-ek10800). Source-only.

**[EK10801](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10801) — POSIX `stat`/`lstat`, `chdir`, `readlink`, and `chown` wrappers can return failure with stale errno for a NULL pathname when native path mode bypasses `__path_u2a()` validation.** See the [path validation review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-stat-null-path-mode-recheck-ek10801). Source-only.

**[EK10802](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10802) — `chown("")` can target the current directory in native path mode and change its owner on security-enabled RAMFS.** Requires sufficient rights and the selected multi-user handler configuration. See the [chown caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-chown-empty-path-ramfs-trace-ek10802). Source-only.

**[EK10803](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10803) — POSIXC `open(NULL, ...)` faults in Unix mode or leaves errno stale in native mode; `mkstemp(NULL)` dereferences its template in every path mode.** See the [NULL-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-open-null-path-review-ek10803). Source-only.

**[EK10804](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10804) — Unix path conversion treats every `/.attbin*` name as the special `/.attbin` path and returns ENOENT.** Requires a valid name sharing that prefix. See the [path-prefix filter review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posix-path-prefix-filter-review-ek10804). Source-only.

**[EK10805](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10805) — POSIX parent-path conversion expands terminal `..` by one byte but allocates only the input length, so its output NUL can exceed the requested buffer.** Conditional on a fresh or exactly sized conversion buffer. See the [parent-path conversion review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-parent-path-conversion-buffer-ek10805). Source-only.

**[EK10806](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10806) — POSIXC `realpath()` can return success for a missing final path component because it ignores `readlink()` failures.** See the [realpath error-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-final-component-error-ek10806). Source-only.


**[EK10808](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10808) — POSIXC realpath() ignores a failed fchdir() restore and may return success with the caller in a changed directory.** Requires a path traversal and restoration failure. See the [restore-error trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-restore-error-ek10808). Source-only.

**[EK10809](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10809) — POSIXC realpath() follows at most 39 links despite configuring a 40-link recursion budget.** The exact maximum-contract interpretation should be confirmed. See the [symlink-limit trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-realpath-symlink-limit-ek10809). Source-only.


**[EK8998](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8998) — POSIXC directory-stream position drifts on EOF: after `.` and `..`, a later read can return `..` again; `seekdir()` can resume past a saved entry.** Applies to POSIXC streams in `doupath` mode and position restoration. See the [iterator state audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3669). Source-only; no enumeration was run.

**[EK9239](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9239) — stdc/POSIXC `ftell()`, `ftello()` and `fgetpos()` can report a successful position after buffered output fails.** DOS clears `FHF_WRITE` when a flush write fails, and `Close()` then skips its final flush; `ftello64()`/`fgetpos64()` share the POSIXC path. See the [caller and DOS-state trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dos-ftell-failed-flush-position-ek9239). Source-only; no I/O was performed.


**[EK10812](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10812) — POSIXC can retain a usergroup.library ↔ POSIXC relative-library cycle when the caller has no StdC exit-list base.** The StdCBase == NULL branch opens usergroup without queueing the exit-time release; usergroup itself retains POSIXC. In-tree trigger reachability is unconfirmed. See the [lifecycle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-optionallibs-cycle-ek10812). Source-only; no library lifecycle was run.


**[EK10813](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10813) — POSIXC assert.h exposes assert_perror but the selected library has no __assert_perror definition.** A client using the macro with NDEBUG unset can fail to link. No checked-in caller was found. See the [symbol audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-assert-perror-missing-definition-ek10813). Source-only; no client build was run.


**[EK10814](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10814) — POSIXC failed assert calls exit(10) rather than abort().** It follows normal process-exit handling instead of the C99 assertion termination contract. See the [implementation comparison](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-assert-perror-missing-definition-ek10813) and [WG14 N1256, §7.2.1.1](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1256.pdf). Source-only; no assertion was run.

**[EK10815](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10815) — POSIXC `dprintf()`/`vdprintf()` return `-1` after a positive short write, losing the successful byte count; the selected `write()` wrapper leaves `errno` unchanged for such counts.** Conditional on a short-write result. See the [short-write pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-dprintf-short-write-ek10815). Source-only; no I/O was performed.

**[EK10816](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10816) — POSIXC `nl_langinfo()`/`nl_langinfo_l()` return `""` for most locale item constants exposed by their public headers, including weekdays, months, date/time formats and currency data.** No in-tree direct caller was found. See the [item coverage audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-nl-langinfo-item-coverage-ek10816). Source-only; no locale call was run.

**[EK10817](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10817) — stdc and POSIXC `perror()` write the optional prefix before reading `errno` for the message; a failing `fputs()` can replace the original error and produce the wrong diagnostic.** Conditional on prefixed stderr output failing before later output. See the [errno-ordering audit](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-perror-errno-ordering-ek10817). Source-only; no I/O was performed.

**[EK10818](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10818) — POSIXC `printf()` ignores an `fflush(stdout)` failure and returns the earlier formatting count.** Conditional on buffered output and a DOS handler write failure. See the [flush pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-printf-flush-ek10818). Source-only; no I/O was run.

**[EK10867](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10867) — DOS `Fault()` writes its `": "` header separator without checking remaining buffer capacity; a short header buffer is overrun.** Conditional on an undersized caller buffer and non-NULL header. Source-only; no DOS call was run.

**[EK10868](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10868) — DOS `Fault()` negates the minimum signed error value in its unknown-error fallback, invoking signed overflow.** Requires a selected `DosGetString()` replacement that returns NULL and a `LONG_MIN` input; no in-tree use of that value was found. Source-only; no DOS call was run.

**[EK10869](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10869) — DOS `SetVar()` does not check local variable allocations; under memory pressure it can dereference a NULL node or value pointer.** Conditional on allocation failure during a local/default variable write. Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.

**[EK10870](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10870) — DOS `SetVar()` returns success after unchecked global ENV writes and can silently skip a requested ENVARC copy.** Conditional on handler write, close, or persistent-file open failure. Source-only; no variable write was run.

**[GD14842](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14842) — BetterString and HotkeyString demos dereference failed custom-class creation.** Applies to the optional BetterString and HotkeyString test targets when MUI_CreateCustomClass() fails. See the [full-body test-program pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#betterstring-test-program-full-body-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**[GD14843](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14843) — BetterString and HotkeyString demos skip class cleanup after application creation fails.** Applies when custom-class creation succeeds but ApplicationObject construction fails in either optional test target. See the [full-body test-program pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#betterstring-test-program-full-body-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**[EK10819](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10819) — POSIXC pclose() always returns ENOSYS without closing the stream created by popen().** The selected API starts commands asynchronously, so pclose also never waits for or reports command completion. See the [popen/pclose full-body pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-popen-pclose-full-body-pass). Source-only; no process or stream was run.

**[EK10820](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10820) — RISC-V hard-float math routines restore an uninitialized fenv after `feholdexcept()` fails.** Selected `lrint`/`llrint` variants and positive-finite `sqrtl()` can write indeterminate state into FCSR. See the [fenv wrapper and RISC-V caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#riscv-fenv-holdexcept-lrint-ek10820). Source-only; no floating-point operation was run.

**[EK10821](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10821) — ARM and RISC-V soft-float `fegetenv()` returns success without writing its output.** AArch64 is covered by EK10852; the RISC-V soft-float case requires a nondefault ABI. Source-only; no fenv call was run.


**[EK10822](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10822) — Selected `atanh` variants report incorrect or incomplete pole/domain errors.** Double and distinct long-double wrappers raise overflow for a pole at ±1; the selected float implementation does not set errno for pole or domain errors. See the [POSIX `atanh()` contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/atanh.3p.html). Source-only; no math operation was run.


**[EK10823](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10823) — `exp()`/`expl()` report NaN and +infinity as overflow.** Their wrappers set `ERANGE` and raise `FE_OVERFLOW` for every non-finite result, including these non-error special values. Source-only.

**[EK10824](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10824) — Distinct-precision `expl()` narrows the result to `double`.** This loses long-double precision and can report overflow for values still representable as `long double`. Source-only.


**[EK10825](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10825) — `lgamma(±INFINITY)` returns infinity with a spurious pole/overflow error.** Negative infinity is misclassified as a pole; positive infinity as finite-input overflow. Source-only.

**[EK10826](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10826) — Distinct-precision `fmodl()` reports a quiet NaN dividend as a domain error.** It sets `EDOM` and raises `FE_INVALID`, unlike its double counterpart. Source-only.


**[EK10827](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10827) — Non-finite fast-forwarding skips `errno = EDOM` for out-of-domain infinities across selected math wrappers.** Affected examples include `sqrt(-INFINITY)`, `log(-INFINITY)`, `acos(INFINITY)`, and `fmod(INFINITY, y)`. Source-only.


**[EK10828](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10828) — `modf(NAN, NULL)` reaches the low-level output store before its documented null check.** It can fault instead of returning NaN with `EDOM`. Source-only.


**[EK10829](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10829) — `remquo()`/`remquol()` skip their documented NULL-output error when operands are non-finite.** They return NaN without setting `EDOM`. Source-only.


**[EK10830](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10830) — Distinct-precision `atan2l(±0, ±0)` reports a domain error.** It returns NaN and raises invalid, contrary to the POSIX signed-zero result. Source-only.


**[EK10831](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10831) — `y0(0)` and `y1(0)` return NaN with `EDOM` instead of the negative-infinity pole result.** They raise invalid rather than reporting the pole as a range error. Source-only.


**[EK10832](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10832) — Selected `exp`/`expf`/`expl` paths omit `ERANGE` when finite inputs underflow.** The double and long-double wrappers do not detect zero/subnormal results; the float IEEE body has no errno wrapper. Source-only.


**[EK10833](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10833) — Binary128 `expl(NAN)` converts NaN to its integer exponent.** The selected kernel lacks the NaN guard present in the ld80 variant. Source-only.

**[EK10834](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10834) — Double `fmod()`, `remquo()`, and `remainder()` can miscompute subnormal remainders.** A signed mantissa word skips the leading-bit count in exponent normalization; `remquo()` quotient bits can also be wrong. Source-only.

**[EK10835](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10835) — Medium trigonometric argument reduction assumes round-to-nearest.** With upward rounding it can choose the wrong quadrant and pass an out-of-range argument to sine/cosine/tangent kernels in float and double paths, including `sincos`. Source-only.

**[EK10836](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10836) — `jn`/`yn` order normalization overflows for `INT_MIN`.** The double and float kernels negate the signed order before recurrence. Source-only.

**[EK10837](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10837) — `hypot()`/`hypotf()` use a negative signed exponent in a left shift when scaling subnormals.** This is undefined C behavior in finite subnormal result paths. Source-only.
**[EK10838](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10838) — Binary128 `powl()` shifts a negative result exponent as a signed integer.** This is undefined C behavior during exponent reconstruction for some positive powers below one. Source-only.
**[EK10839](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10839) — Long-double `remquo` can overflow its signed quotient accumulator.** The distinct-precision kernel shifts signed `int q` for each quotient bit; `remainderl()` reaches the same kernel. Double and float use unsigned accumulators. Source-only.
**[EK10840](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10840) — `scalbn[f/l]` can overflow signed exponent arithmetic.** For finite nonzero normal input, `n == INT_MAX` overflows `k + n` before the range guard; the earlier `INT_MIN` scope was withdrawn. Source-only.
**[EK10841](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10841) — Low-precision `lround` variants can bypass integer-range checks.** Includes `llround[f]`, `lroundf` with either `long` width, and `lround(double)` with 64-bit `long`; same-precision `llroundl` aliases inherit the defect. Source-only.
**[EK10842](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10842) — `nearbyint` restores away `FE_INVALID` from signaling NaNs.** Saving/restoring the whole environment suppresses exceptions besides inexact. Source-only; conditional on signaling-NaN/fenv support.
**[EK10843](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10843) — POSIXC `stat64()` narrows a 64-bit DOS size through 32-bit `off_t`.** Large-file metadata truncates on 32-bit builds without large-file mode; `stat64`, `lstat64`, and `fstat64` share the path. Source-only.
**[EK10844](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10844) — POSIXC reports zero `st_blocks` for nonempty AFS OFS files on 512-byte blocks.** The AFS-reported 488-byte usable block makes the `st_blksize / 512` multiplier truncate to zero. Source-only; configuration-conditional.
**[EK10845](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10845) — `ctanl()` can convert an out-of-range range-reduction quotient to `long`.** On the near-pole path, sufficiently large finite real arguments can overflow the representable range before the quotient is cast, making the result undefined/compiler-dependent. Selected distinct-long-double configurations only; source-only.
**[EK10846](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10846) — `casin[f/l]` returns only +π/2 on the real axis for `|x| > 1`.** It omits the nonzero imaginary branch-cut value, and negative inputs get the wrong real sign; selected `cacos`, `cacosh`, and `casinh` compositions inherit incorrect outputs. Source-only.
**[EK10847](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10847) — `catan[f/l]` returns maximum sentinels for pure-imaginary inputs above one.** These have finite principal values; selected `catanh` inherits the error for real inputs above one. Source-only.
**[EK10848](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10848) — `cpow[f/l]` returns zero for every zero base, including negative powers.** This turns a pole into an ordinary zero result. Source-only.
**[EK10849](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10849) — `ctanhl()` overflows its hyperbolic intermediates for large finite inputs.** `Inf/Inf` produces NaN where the real result should approach ±1; distinct long-double targets only. Source-only.
**[EK10850](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10850) — `cexpl(+Inf + i0)` returns a NaN imaginary part.** The long-double body evaluates `Inf * sinl(0)` instead of preserving the input zero. Distinct long-double targets only; source-only.

**[OD11344](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11344) — Nouveau GSP message work can outlive device teardown.** A queued/running R535 message worker is not cancelled or drained before its mutexes and shared memory are destroyed; conditional on device teardown overlapping pending work. Source-only.


HEIC short-header bounds and selected DOS result contract recheck (GD6308 fleshed out; no new ID or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): re-read `HEIC_Decode()`'s size/allocate/probe sequence (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:52-75`) against `DTIO_SIZE_OK`/`DTIO_Read64()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/dtio64.h:36-58,88-103`) and the selected DOS `Read()` implementation/contract (`rom/dos/read.c:27-43,59-75`). For file sizes 0–10 the adapter requests 12 bytes into a `size+1` allocation, accepts zero/short counts because it tests only `!= -1`, then calls external `heif_check_filetype()` with length 12; at size 11 the call fits the requested allocation but the twelfth byte is not file data. Traced entry through `HEIC_Import()`'s DTST_FILE branch and the support-process caller. Kept the downstream memory-read/fault consequence conditional because the external libheif helper implementation is not in this checkout. Reconfirmed the neighboring 20-byte MIME/full-file reads also accept partial nonnegative counts, but their short-read trigger is conditional on size changing or a nonstandard/short-reading provider after the initial size query; no extra finding is claimed. Expanded GD6308 detail and confidence limits in the report. No file, read, datatype, decoder, or build was exercised; source-only.


HEIC adapter error/ownership finding-detail expansion (GD6304–GD6307 fleshed out; no new IDs or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): rechecked the corresponding report entries against `heicclass.c:41-48,77-82,91-170,211,365-390` and the selected Picture `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` implementation (`pictureclass.c:1093-1210`). Expanded GD6304 with the dropped `heif_decode_image()` error and successful constructor return; GD6305 with Picture's concrete FALSE paths (including source-buffer allocation failure) and the discarded method result; GD6306 with the uninitialized image-handle output falling through after lookup error, keeping output-state consequences dependency-conditional; and GD6307 with the unmatched `AllocVec` input buffer/context allocations and no-copy buffer ownership. No additional IDs were created. Active `workbench-datatypes-complete` rules select the HEIC target; its external library implementation/build closure remains unreviewed. No decoder, Picture method, allocation failure, import, or build was exercised; source-only.


HEIC Picture-dimension and alpha-metadata finding-detail expansion (GD6309–GD6310 fleshed out; no new IDs or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): rechecked both direct dimension assignments in `heicclass.c:118-120,148-166` against `BitMapHeader`'s `UWORD` width/height (`compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:28-43`) and the selected Picture pixel-array and renderer paths. Expanded GD6309 with the unchecked narrowing before those dimensions are supplied as the pixel-array extent. For GD6310, confirmed Picture instance data is zeroed (`pictureclass.c:156-178`), HEIC switches to `PBPAFMT_RGBA` for alpha (`heicclass.c:123-127`) without setting `bmh_Masking`, and high-color alpha compositing requires `mskHasAlpha` (`pictureclass.c:603-660`); ordinary fallback blits are opaque. Kept low-depth alpha behavior separate under GD5527. External libheif dimension limits, oversized-image incidence and rendered output remain unverified. No image, decode, render or build was exercised; source-only.


**[GD14661](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14661) — Optional VMware SVGA offscreen bitmap byte-size multiplication wraps on 32-bit pc-i386 builds. A successful small allocation can back a bitmap that retains larger dimensions; source-only.**
**[GD14845](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14845) — Optional VMware SVGA cursor conversion buffer byte size wraps on 32-bit pc-i386 builds, so full-size conversion can exceed the allocated buffer. Full-size conversion exceeds the wrapped allocation; later clipped KMS read is not separately established. Conditional on a large custom bitmap and successful wrapped allocation; source-only.**
**[OD11345](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11345) — Nouveau output-poll cancellation can leave a timer armed.** A running poll callback can rearm delayed work after synchronous cancellation's timer deletion, allowing another connector poll after suspend/disable begins. Conditional on the callback overlapping disable and choosing to repoll. Source-only.
**[OD11346](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11346) — Concurrent first Vulkan calls can observe partially initialized loader state.** The loader marks initialization complete before publishing its OOP object and method base; simultaneous first calls can fail spuriously or dispatch with an unset method base. Conditional on use of the optional Vulkan loader. Source-only.
**[OD11347](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11347) — Vulkan instance creation discards the caller's create information.** `vkCreateInstance()` forwards a hard-coded application name/version and ignores requested API version, layers, extensions, flags and allocator callbacks. Conditional on use of the optional Vulkan loader. Source-only.
**[OD11348](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11348) — 32-bit Vulkan loader trampolines narrow non-dispatchable handles to pointers.** Vulkan handles are 64-bit integers in this mode, so calls can truncate handles and misread later arguments or array elements. Conditional on explicitly building the optional 32-bit loader. Source-only.
**[OD11349](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11349) — Vulkan device calls can switch GPUs after creation.** The HIDD reselects a preferred GPU on every call, and a successful device creation changes the use-count tie-break, so later operations may send that device handle to another GPU's callbacks. Conditional on multiple equal-priority GPUs in the optional Vulkan HIDD. Source-only.
**[OD11350](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11350) — Vulkan memory-budget queries return full heap size and zero usage.** Conditional on a backend advertising `VK_EXT_memory_budget` through the optional Vulkan HIDD; no in-tree provider was found. Source-only.
**[OD11351](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11351) — Enhanced Vulkan video-parameter retrieval can return trailing bytes beyond the data written.** The convenience wrappers size the vector from a preliminary query but do not trim it to the successful fill call's output size. Conditional on a size change between calls; optional video-encode support. Source-only.
**[OD11352](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11352) — Enhanced Vulkan pipeline-property queries pass a base-only output structure.** The API requires a larger identifier structure; the convenience and RAII overloads can supply too little storage. Conditional on use with pipeline-properties support; source-only.
**[OD11353](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11353) — Enhanced Vulkan latency-timing wrappers can return unused entries.** The convenience and RAII overloads allocate from the maximum queried count but do not trim to the number of records actually written. Conditional on use of `VK_NV_low_latency2`; source-only.
**[OD11354](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11354) — Vulkan-Hpp dispatchers erase the EXT fallback for `vkCmdEndRendering2KHR`.** Both dynamic and RAII initialization can leave the KHR slot null even after loading the accepted EXT equivalent. Conditional on driver entry-point availability; source-only.
15934:**[OD11355](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11355) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII display getters release display access they did not acquire.** Retrieval wrappers create a handle whose destructor unconditionally calls `vkReleaseDisplayEXT`. Conditional on platform-specific display APIs; source-only.
15935:**[OD11356](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11356) — Copying a Vulkan-Hpp RAII display mode drops its physical device.** Capability queries on a copied wrapper pass a null parent handle. Conditional on `VK_KHR_display`; source-only.
15936:**[OD11357](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11357) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII batch pipeline creation leaks successful outputs on partial failure.** Raw pipeline handles are wrapped only on overall success, despite Vulkan allowing mixed-success batches. Conditional on partial pipeline creation failure; source-only.
15937:**[OD11358](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11358) — Vulkan-Hpp acquisition helpers return an uninitialized image index on timeout/not-ready.** They return the index even when no swapchain image was acquired. Conditional on nonblocking or timed acquisition; source-only.
15938:**[OD11359](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11359) — Vulkan-Hpp display-timing helpers consume outputs on out-of-date.** With the out-of-date macro, one returns an unset counter and another compares an unset count. Conditional on swapchain timing queries; source-only.
15939:**OD11360 withdrawn — duplicate of [GD10226](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10226).** Both entries described `vulkan_raii.hpp` batch shader creation dropping non-null outputs on `eIncompatibleShaderBinaryEXT`; GD10226 remains canonical.
15940:**OD11361 withdrawn — duplicate of [GD10262](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10262).** GD10262 already includes the RAII pipeline-binary outputs dropped on accepted `eIncomplete` and `ePipelineBinaryMissingKHR` results; it remains canonical.
15941:**[OD11362](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11362) — Vulkan-Hpp micromap helper allocates one result regardless of count or stride.** Multiple micromaps, or one micromap with `stride > sizeof(DataType)`, request more output bytes than the local object provides. Source-only.


Vulkan-Hpp RAII video-format query error-path follow-up (GD10223 expanded; targeted only, no path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): the RAII `PhysicalDevice::getVideoFormatPropertiesKHR()` vector and `StructureChain` methods also leave `videoFormatPropertyCount` uninitialized before dispatch and read it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:19155-19181,19193-19228`). In no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled, an API error that leaves the output count undefined reaches resize/assert logic; the `StructureChain` method additionally indexes `structureChains` to that count (`:19225-19227`). This is the same GD10223 root cause, not a new finding. No Vulkan call or build was run; source-only.

**EK10864 — `catan()` returns a NaN imaginary component for large finite real inputs:** the unsafely squared components produce an `Inf/Inf` logarithm ratio. This is separate from EK10847's imaginary-axis guard; source-only. See [EK10864](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10864).
**EK10863 — `ccoshl()` and `csinhl()` can overflow a finite component before applying trigonometric scaling:** the distinct-long-double bodies overflow `coshl`/`sinhl` before multiplying by a small cosine. No in-tree callers found; source-only. See [EK10863](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10863).
**EK10862 — `cexpl()` can lose a finite component when `expl()` overflows first:** the distinct-long-double body multiplies the overflowing exponential by small trigonometric factors without scaling. No in-tree direct caller was found; source-only. See [EK10862](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10862) and the [range review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-distinct-long-double-complex-exponential-range-continuation-ek10862).
**EK10851 — `ctanl()` returns a NaN imaginary part for sufficiently large finite imaginary inputs:** the selected long-double body overflows `coshl(2*y)` and `sinhl(2*y)`, then divides `Inf/Inf`, although `tan(i*y)` approaches `i*sign(y)`. Applies to targets with distinct long double; same-precision configurations alias the double implementation. See [EK10851](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10851) and the [full-body `ctanl` review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#stdc-complex-circular-tangent-full-body-and-large-imaginary-input-review-ek10845-ek10851). Source-only.

**[EK10852](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10852) — AArch64 floating-point environment APIs report success but do not update flags or saved environment.** This makes status queries/restores ineffective, including `nearbyint()`’s attempt to suppress inexact. Default inline-header path only. Source-only.

**[EK10853](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10853) — AArch64 `fma()` and `fmal()` can return the next value above the correctly rounded result.** `fegetround()` returns `-1`, so both distant-product switches fall into their upward-rounding default even when hardware uses round-to-nearest. Default AArch64 inline fenv path. Source-only.
**[EK10854](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10854) — AArch64 binary128 `sqrtl()` can return a result one ULP below the correctly rounded value.** `sqrtl(11.0L)` follows the no-op fenv path and returns `0x1.a887293fd6f34168ef24f1987215p+1` instead of `...7216p+1` under round-to-nearest. Source-derived exact arithmetic trace; no build or runtime call.

15954:**[OD11363](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11363) — Vulkan-Hpp `ArrayWrapper1D<char, 0>` string construction writes past the zero-length array.** `N - 1` underflows and the helper writes a terminator unconditionally. Conditional on caller instantiation; no in-tree instance found. Source-only.

15955:**[OD11364](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11364) — Vulkan-Hpp `StridedArrayProxy` offsets wrap at 32 bits.** `end()` and `back()` multiply 32-bit count and stride before pointer arithmetic; affected only by caller-supplied ranges exceeding 4 GiB. No in-tree large-range caller found. Source-only.

15956:**[OD11365](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11365) — Vulkan-Hpp `ResultValue` marks a valid suboptimal image acquisition as having no value.** In no-exceptions mode, `has_value()` and dereference operators accept only `eSuccess`, although `acquireNextImageKHR()` returns a valid index with `eSuboptimalKHR`. Source-only.

15957:**[OD11366](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11366) — Vulkan-Hpp `DispatchLoaderDynamic` ignores the caller-supplied `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`.** Device commands are re-resolved through `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, breaking custom layer/loader dispatch chains. Conditional on passing an explicit resolver; source-only.

15958:**[OD11367](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11367) — Vulkan-Hpp dispatchers overwrite EXT/KHR alias fallbacks.** Four aliases in dynamic and RAII initialization (swapchain release, calibrated timestamps, and rendering end) can be reset by later null KHR lookups, breaking KHR wrappers with EXT-only exposure. Source-only.

15959:**[OD11368](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11368) — Vulkan loader marks initialization done before HIDD setup succeeds.** A transient first-use failure prevents retries; concurrent first callers can see missing dispatch state or a false Vulkan 1.0 fallback. Optional loader only. Source-only.

15960:**[OD11369](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11369) — Vulkan loader reports zero `VK_EXT_memory_budget` usage regardless of allocations.** It also reports full heap size as the budget, so callers can make memory decisions from false usage/budget data. Conditional on extension exposure/use. Source-only.

15961:**[OD11371](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11371) — No in-tree Vulkan GPU driver registers with the Vulkan HIDD.** Repository search finds the registration API and implementation but no driver caller; without an out-of-tree component the registry stays empty and instance creation fails. Candidate; optional Vulkan target. Source-only.

**[GD14849](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14849) — MUI text clients dereference failed parsed-text allocations.** Rectangle and Text fault during sizing after `zune_text_new()` fails; Register also faults during setup when title truncation is disabled. Conditional on allocation failure. Source-only.**
**[GD14850](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14850) — MUI text parser returns incomplete objects after internal allocation failure.** Line and chunk allocation failures are swallowed, and image-spec duplication can yield truncated literal text. Conditional on memory pressure. Source-only.**
**[GD14851](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14851) — MUI text parser mishandles a trailing or line-final HiCharIdx marker.** It reads past the buffer at string end, or consumes a newline and skips the next line’s first character. Source-only.
**[GD14852](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14852) — MUI Text constructor replaces failed copies of supplied strings with empty defaults.** Conditional on allocation pressure; construction can silently discard Contents or PreParse. Source-only.
**[GD14853](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14853) — Software cursor shape updates mishandle allocation failures.** Failed replacement can erase the old pointer; save-under failure can hide it during shape or target changes. Applies to inherited generic cursor methods in selected PC, OpenSBI, and AArch64 Pi framebuffer classes; source-only.
**[GD14854](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14854) — Generic cursor allocation products can overflow.** The ARGB-size wrap applies to selected i386-PC VESA; signed save-under overflow also applies to selected VESA, EFI, and AArch64 Pi framebuffer targets. Conditional on unusually large shapes and allocation outcome; source-only.
**[GD14855](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14855) — Generic software cursor narrows computed coordinates before clipping.** Conditional on signed position/hotspot/bitmap offsets exceeding WORD range and wrapping into visible framebuffer bounds. Source-only.
