**[GD14857](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14857) — Palette changes can leave the generic software cursor rendered with stale indexed colors.** On a mutable palette target, changing an entry used by a cursor pixel remaps it without recompositing the cursor; it remains visually wrong until the next redraw. Conditional and contract-sensitive; LinuxFB pseudocolor is an optional in-tree route; source-only.
**[OD11402](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11402) — AHI AbortIO reports success before queued reads become abortable.** A `CMD_READ` still on the unit port is not found in `ReadList`; the read proceeds, and AHI-Handler’s `ACTION_END` can wait for normal completion. Conditional queue/dispatch timing; source-only.
**[OD11403](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11403) — LinuxFB reports palette and gamma updates successful after ioctl failures.** It ignores per-entry `FBIOPUTCMAP` errors, so framebuffer colors can remain stale while software or MonitorClass records the new values. Conditional optional LinuxFB target; source-only.
**[OD11404](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11404) — LinuxFB gamma scaling collapses channels wider than 8 bits.** The channel step becomes zero; 9–15-bit channels load every entry from index 255, while a 16-bit table length wraps to zero and is not written. Conditional optional LinuxFB directcolor mode; source-only.
**[OD11405](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11405) — RP1 I²C inherits bus methods with no bit-banged implementation.** `Start`/`Address`/`Stop`/`ProbeAddress` reach generic pure-virtual GPIO bit methods; optional `i2cdw.hidd` clients cannot use these methods for valid transfers. Conditional optional module; source-only.
**[GD14858](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14858) — Palette updates race truecolor-to-palette conversion.** Concurrent conversion and `SetColors` can race on palette/cache state; two first conversions can also leak one duplicate cache allocation. Conditional on concurrent calls for one palette bitmap; source-only.
**[GD14859](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14859) — Sound.datatype leaks AHI cursor-timer resources on worker startup failure.** If the timer opens but the worker command-port allocation fails, the worker exits without closing/freeing its timer request and port. Conditional optional Sound.datatype path; source-only.
**[OD11406](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11406) — BTSerial zero-length reads wait for input.** The maintained `serial.device` has the same idle-buffer behavior; whether it violates the intended zero-length `CMD_READ` contract remains uncertain. Conditional optional BTSerial class; source-only.
**[OD11407](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11407) — Bluetooth AES S-box initialization lacks synchronized publication.** Concurrent first use across Bluetooth hardware tasks on ExecSMP can expose incomplete table state; conditional multi-unit configuration, medium confidence, source-only.

**[EK10855](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10855) — `system(NULL)` crashes in native POSIXC mode.** The early path-mode branch passes NULL to `strdup()`/`strlen()` before the documented shell-availability query. Source-only.
**[EK10856](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10856) — `system_no_sh()` dereferences failed path conversions.** With no shell, a rejected path or conversion-allocation failure reaches `strlen(NULL)`. Source-only.
**[EK10857](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10857) — `system_no_sh()` dereferences failed command-buffer allocations.** Failed `strdup()` or command-buffer `malloc()` results are used without checks. Source-only.

**[EK10858](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10858) — RISC-V64 OpenSBI does not handle vector first use or preserve vector state across task switches.** RV64 detects V and allocates per-task vector contexts, but illegal vector instructions are not enabled/retried and the scheduler has no vector save/restore. Source-only.

**[EK10859](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10859) — Unix-path `system(NULL)` reports a shell without checking for one.** NIX-mode callers receive `1` even when `bin:sh` cannot be locked, contrary to the documented availability query. Source-only.

**[EK10860](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10860) — `rmdir("..")` can reuse a freed path-conversion buffer.** The POSIXC wrapper converts the path, then delegates to `remove()`, which converts it again; terminal `..` expansion can force the second conversion to free its own input buffer. Conditional on a fresh buffer or at most three bytes of recorded capacity; source-only.

**[OD11408](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11408) — PCI xHCI grouped functions can mis-map root-hub ports.** If an earlier controller with a populated port count fails initialization and a later one succeeds, the failed controller still occupies the map prefix while the advertised count includes only successful controllers, shifting or hiding healthy ports. Even when all functions initialize, root-hub dispatch passes global indices as controller-local indices, so later functions can access the wrong port or exceed local arrays. Conditional on grouped multifunction PCI hardware; source-only.

**[OD3362](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3362) — PCI xHCI truncates variable root-hub bitmaps above 15 ports.** For 16–20 ports it advertises an 11-byte USB 2 hub descriptor where the two variable bitmaps require 13 bytes; Poseidon reads a power-mask byte as removable-port data for 17–20 ports. Downstream effect of the cached bitmap is unestablished; conditional on a high-port-count controller; source-only.


**[OD11409](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11409) — Generic PCI config subword writes use undefined signed shifts.** The byte-lane-3 mask and upper-word mask shift signed `int` values beyond their representable range. No checked-in caller was found to reach either lane; public/external PCI HIDD callers remain in scope; source-only.

**[OD11410](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11410) — PC/OpenSBI serial HIDD narrows data length before validation.** Direct HIDD values such as 261 pass as five bits and are truncated into the UART width field; selected serial.device uses UBYTE input, so no in-tree trigger is established. Conditional; source-only.
**[GD14866](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14866) — More mishandles Read errors on non-seekable inputs.** A negative Read result is used as an array offset and line-scan length, causing an out-of-bounds write and scan. Conditional on a non-seekable source read error; source-only.
**[GD14887](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14887) — More treats unsupported stream-seek responses as file lengths.** `CON:` makes it request at most one byte; the named pipe handler's zero status makes it treat the stream as empty. Conditional trigger in selected Workbench utility; source-only.
**[GD14888](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14888) — `Skip /BACK` ignores failed rewinds on non-seekable scripts.** `Execute` can read a console or named pipe stream; `Skip` consumes forward input looking for an earlier label. Conditional; source-only.
**[GD14889](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14889) — VMware SVGA LUT8 palette updates overrun the bitmap color cache.** `AllocBitMap()` initializes 256 colors through a backend array that holds 16; source-only, optional HIDD.
**[GD14890](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14890) — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap convenience construction sets usageCountsCount from the direct array only and can emit invalid dual pointers.** Optional beta API; no checked-in caller found; source-only.
**[GD14891](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14891) — Vulkan-Hpp reflection cannot compile for bit-field wrappers.** Optional `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` configuration; no in-tree macro definition; source-only.
**[GD14892](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14892) — Vulkan-Hpp tensor-copy helpers can emit mismatched dimension arrays.** Optional `VK_ARM_tensors` enhanced API; no AROS call site found; source-only.
**[GD14867](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14867) — More underallocates its line index after 32-bit size overflow.** A newline-dense file with about 358 million lines wraps the line-array size calculation on 32-bit builds; filling the index can overrun the allocation. Conditional on a large input and successful wrapped allocation; source-only.

**[GD14862](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14862) — AHI sound cursor time wraps after about 71 minutes.** Elapsed microseconds overflow 32-bit `ULONG` before widening, so the playhead jumps backward during long continuous playback. Conditional on optional AHI cursor-timer use; source-only.

**[GD14863](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14863) — More wraps long-line lengths before applying its display cap.** A 65,536-byte line wraps its UWORD source and rendered lengths to zero, truncating display, horizontal scrolling and search. Selected Workbench utility; source-only.

**[GD14864](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14864) — More overflows its title buffer for long AppWindow paths.** The drop path accepts up to 299 bytes, then `SetWinTitle()` copies/ formats into undersized 256-byte buffers. Selected Workbench utility; source-only.

**[GD14865](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14865) — More command formatting overflows its buffer for long paths.** Print/Save As combine paths in `s[256]`; the editor shortcut combines two inputs up to 299 bytes each in the same buffer. Selected Workbench utility; source-only.

**[GD14871](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14871) — ChunkyBM mode-change allocation failure leaves the new bitmap dimensions over its old owned buffer.** Reachable on the optional HeadlessGfx target, whose displayable HeadlessGfxBM inherits ChunkyBM’s owned buffer; requires a failed growth allocation. Source-only.
**[GD14872](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14872) — CursorFB direct access leaves a borrowed ChunkyBM buffer unprotected across a concurrent growth mode change.** On optional HeadlessGfx, a second task can replace/free the owned bitmap buffer while a Cybergraphics lock exposes its old address. Requires direct access plus an overlapping growth mode switch; source-only.
**[GD14870](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14870) — Generic 16-bit CopyBox accepts odd explicit row strides, then performs misaligned typed accesses on strict-alignment m68k.** Conditional on a direct HIDD client requesting an odd stride; source-only.
**[GD14869](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14869) — NVIDIA CopyBox shifts tall extents as signed integers.** Heights of 32,768 or more invoke undefined behavior in the packed GPU command fields. Explicit optional HIDD only; source-only.
**[GD14868](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14868) — Headless boot-driver replay retains a pointer to its caller's stack tags.** Disk-started HeadlessGfx queues its local HIDD attribute list for later replay, after the startup function returns; deferred construction then reads expired tag storage. Conditional on optional HeadlessGfx startup with no display registered; source-only.

**[EK10861](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10861) — OpenSBI FDT parser classifies any `memory*` root node as RAM.** A false secondary bank can be mapped and allocated on non-UEFI startup; with UEFI it can affect the primary heap only under the EFI-region size condition also described in EK9042. Conditional on an external RISC-V DTB; source-only.

**[OD11411](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11411) — PCITool vendor lookup skips the final vendor and overruns an empty index.** A nonempty `pci.ids` file with no parsed vendors underflows the index bound; a final vendor is never compared by the binary search. Conditional on the explicitly buildable PCITool utility; source-only.

**[OD3664](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3664) — Sam440 EMAC advertises gigabit but resolves negotiated speed as only 10/100.** The setup path then configures the bridge and MAC at the wrong rate. Conditional on a selected 1000BASE-T PHY/link; source-only.

**[OD2438](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2438) — EMAC uses uninitialized PHY values after MDIO read failures.** Autonegotiation setup and the initial status check ignore read failures, then consume unwritten local values and still report startup success. Conditional on an MDIO transaction failure; source-only.

**[OD2408](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2408) — EMAC Close takes a shared unit offline and leaves its opener count stale.** Closing any shared request resets hardware still used by other clients; the open count is never decremented. Conditional on multiple opens or an opener-allocation failure with an existing client; source-only.

**[OD2461](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2461) — EMAC resets and restarts autonegotiation on every successful Open.** A second shared opener disrupts the active link while the unit is reinitialized. Conditional on multiple clients opening one unit; source-only.

**[OD2462](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2462) — Overlapping EMAC starts reuse one queued timer request.** A second accepted Open can submit the unit’s already-queued timer message node again, corrupting timer queue state or stalling starts. Conditional on overlapping opens; source-only.

**[OD11412](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11412) — EMAC unit initialization waits forever if worker creation fails.** `CreateNewProcTags()` is unchecked and the parent waits for the worker's signal unconditionally. Conditional process-creation failure; source-only.

**[OD11413](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11413) — EMAC does not handle unit message-port allocation failures.** A missing input port is dereferenced by the worker; the write port is dereferenced during setup; other missing ports are later used by SANA-II queueing and interrupt processing. Conditional allocation failure; source-only.

**[OD11414](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11414) — FLAC encoder accepts metadata types above the format limit.** Codes above 126 pass validation and are truncated to seven bits when written, producing a different block type. Conditional on a direct encoder API client; source-only.

**[OD11415](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11415) — Serial reads larger than 65,535 bytes wrap their receive offset.** The interrupt callback uses a 16-bit destination index for a full-width request length, so a sufficiently large read can overwrite the start of its buffer and remain pending. Conditional on the explicitly buildable serial.device and a read above 65,535 bytes; source-only.

**[OD11416](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11416) — Hosted Ethernet can free its shutdown message before it is dequeued.** The I/O task posts its exit message then frees it; a lower/equal-priority Close task may consume the freed queue node. Conditional on receiver scheduling during shutdown; source-only.

**[OD928](AROS-other-drivers.md#od928) — EMAC can start without registered MAL interrupt handlers.** On the Sam440 PPC target, if the RX end-of-buffer handler cannot be allocated, the interface still starts without receive completion processing. Conditional on kernel interrupt-node allocation failure; source-only.

**[OD929](AROS-other-drivers.md#od929) — EMAC MAL initialization does not check descriptor or packet-buffer allocations.** On the Sam440 PPC target, a failed ring is dereferenced during setup; a missing shared packet-buffer slab leaves DMA descriptors with invalid low buffer addresses. Conditional on memory pressure; source-only.

**[OD2580](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2580) — EMAC dispatches both MAL RX channels to unit 0.** Unit 1's receive descriptors are not drained when its channel completes. Conditional on receiving traffic on unit 1; source-only.

**[OD2582](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2582) — EMAC enables MAC error interrupts but only logs them.** The callback neither reads nor acknowledges enabled status causes; repeated interrupts depend on hardware status semantics. Conditional; source-only.

**[OD3132](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3132) — EMAC reports CMD_FLUSH complete without flushing queued I/O.** Pending requests remain active after the successful flush reply. Conditional on queued requests and a direct CMD_FLUSH caller; source-only.


**[OD3180](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3180) — EMAC TX narrows request lengths before copying into fixed packet slots.** Oversized direct SANA-II writes can truncate or copy beyond a packet slot. Conditional on an oversized request and caller hook; source-only.

**[OD3181](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3181) — EMAC leaves queued writes dormant after its TX ring fills.** The write port switches to PA_IGNORE and TX completion does not restart it. Conditional on ring saturation; source-only.

**[OD3131](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3131) — SANA-II handlers read request fields after replying.** A reply consumer can reuse the request before the handler rereads `io_Unit` to release its semaphore. Conditional on reply-consumer scheduling; applies to the listed selected network drivers; source-only.

**[OD3133](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3133) — EMAC reports initialization success when a unit allocation fails.** Open later dereferences the missing unit. Conditional on unit-allocation failure; source-only.


**[EK10871](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10871) — `AddDosEntry()` returns duplicate-name failure without setting its documented `IoErr()`.** `IoErr()` can therefore remain zero or stale. Source-only; no DOS list operation was run.


**[EK10872](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10872) — `AssignAdd()` returns failure for `BNULL` without setting its documented `IoErr()`.** The C:Assign caller reports that stale value if reached. Source-only.


**[EK10873](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10873) — DOS `CheckSignal()` can erase a concurrently delivered signal on ExecSMP.** Local `Disable()` does not serialize a remote CPU's atomic signal delivery with the ordinary clear. Source-only; no task or signal was run.


**[EK10874](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10874) — DOS packet wrappers can return failure without updating `IoErr()` if packet or reply-port allocation fails.** POSIXC `F_SETFL`, `remove()`, and `readdir()` can then misreport the failure or treat it as end-of-directory. Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.


**[EK10875](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10875) — DOS packet helpers can send a NULL name BSTR after allocation failure on non-fast-BSTR builds.** The selected RAM handler dereferences it. Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.

**[EK10876](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10876) — `getpacketinfo()` leaks its name BSTR when device lookup fails on non-fast-BSTR builds.** Source-only; no lookup was run.


**[EK10877](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10877) — A rejected boot volume leaves `CliInit`'s current directory pointing at the lock it frees.** The old current-directory lock is also lost. Conditional on a bootability check rejecting a volume; source-only.


**[EK10878](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10878) — `NextDosEntry()` indexes outside its flag table for a corrupt DOS node type.** Conditional on prior DOS-list corruption; source-only.


**[EK10879](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10879) — `ExamineFH()` reports success for NIL handles, then converts the unfilled FIB as BSTR data.** The resulting memory damage depends on the caller's FIB contents. Source-only; no NIL handle was examined.


**[EK10880](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10880) — `ExAll()` fallback indexes before its size table for negative data types.** Conditional on invalid input and a nonempty directory on a filesystem without native ExAll. Source-only.

**[EK10881](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10881) — `ExAll()` fallback writes its overflow terminator beyond buffers smaller than the `ed_Next` field.** Conditional on an undersized buffer and a nonempty directory. Source-only.

**[EK10882](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10882) — Buffered `FRead()`/`FGetC()` can loop forever when a flush write returns zero.** Conditional on a handler reporting zero bytes for pending output; source-only.

**[EK10883](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10883) — stdc `fwrite()` loses completed elements after a later unbuffered write fails.** A selected RAMFS pool-exhaustion path can return a partial write after prior elements completed; the wrapper returns zero instead of the completed-element count. Source-only.

**[EK10884](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10884) — DOS `GetCurrentDirName()`, `GetProgramName()` and `GetPrompt()` treat zero or negative capacities as huge and write beyond the supplied extent.** Requires an invalid length argument; source-only.

**[EK10885](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10885) — `GetDeviceProc()` dereferences a failed nonbinding `AssignPath()` target lock.** Conditional on the assign target being unresolvable; source-only.

**[EK10886](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10886) — Retrying a root-relative `GetDeviceProc()` result with no DOS-list node dereferences NULL.** Selected `Lock()` and `Open()` loops can retry on a missing object; conditional on no current/home directory. Source-only.

**[EK10887](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10887) — `GetVar()` passes negative local-variable sizes to `CopyMem()`.** Requires invalid input and an existing local variable; source-only.

**[EK10888](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10888) — Binary `GetVar()` writes before the destination when a global read returns `-1`.** Selected stdc/POSIXC `getenv()` paths use this mode; conditional on a read error. Source-only.

**[EK10889](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10889) — `GetVar()` leaks an opened global-variable file when `ExamineFH()` fails.** Conditional on open succeeding and examination failing; source-only.

**[EK10890](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10890) — Non-m68k `Lock()` overwrites non-not-found `GetDeviceProc()` errors.** Conditional on a distinct lookup failure such as allocation failure; source-only.

**[EK10891](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10891) — Cross-volume soft-link resolution leaves a Process with no current directory at the target root.** Affects both `Lock()` and `Open()`; conditional on a null starting directory and cross-volume link; source-only.

**[EK10892](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10892) — Complex pattern matching follows an uninitialized link between backtracking marker blocks.** Conditional on more than 128 pending match states; source-only.

**[EK10893](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10893) — `MaxCli()` can read a task-number array after concurrent CLI creation frees it.** Conditional on a full array and concurrent process creation; source-only.
**[EK10894](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10894) — `NameFromLock()` can report the boot volume after duplicating a non-null lock fails.** Conditional on filesystem `DupLock()` failure; source-only.
**[EK10895](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10895) — `RemAssignList()` can leave a multi-directory assign's exposed device/unit metadata stale after removing its primary lock.** Consumer impact depends on reads of those legacy fields; source-only.
**[EK10896](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10896) — `RemSegment()` can race with resident-segment insertion when callers do not externally serialize the list.** The selected `Resident REMOVE` caller is protected; conditional external API path; source-only.
**[EK10897](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10897) — `Rename()` uses an unchecked `strcpy()` for long destination paths containing a parent reference.** Conditional on a volume-qualified path longer than 255 bytes; source-only.
**[EK10898](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10898) — `ScanVars()` returns without scanning global variables requested by its flags.** Selected in-tree callers use local-only; conditional external API impact; source-only.
**[EK10899](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10899) — `StrToDate()` can index outside its month table for an out-of-range numeric month and accepts impossible dates.** Conditional on invalid date input; source-only.
**[EK10900](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10900) — `SplitName()` treats a zero destination size as unbounded.** Conditional on a zero-size call; source-only.
**[EK10901](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10901) — `VFWritef()` ignores `FPutC()` errors and returns a success count.** Conditional on an output failure; source-only.
**[EK10902](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10902) — i386 Exec startup dereferences a missing optional boot command line.** Conditional on a Multiboot handoff without that tag; source-only.

**OD11417 consolidated into [OD11353](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11353):** duplicate report of the same Vulkan-Hpp `getLatencyTimingsNV()` stale-vector-length finding; both enhanced and RAII helpers are covered there.
**[OD11418](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11418) — Vulkan-Hpp display smart handles use incompatible/missing deleters.** `UniqueHandleTraits` selects `ObjectDestroy<PhysicalDevice>`, but display factories pass `ObjectRelease`; the generic destroy path also requires a nonexistent `PhysicalDevice::destroy(DisplayKHR, ...)`. Using the optional display smart-handle API therefore fails to compile. Source-only.
**[OD11419](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11419) — Vulkan-Hpp singular KHR/NV ray-tracing helper accepts multiple groups but supplies one-object output storage.** A count greater than one can overrun the local result; conditional on downstream enhanced-mode use; source-only.
**[OD11420](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11420) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII `DisplayModeKHR` copy operations omit the physical-device parent.** Copy construction leaves it null; assignment can retain an unrelated parent, so later plane-capability queries pass a mismatched handle pair. Conditional on downstream RAII `VK_KHR_display` use; source-only.
**[OD11421](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11421) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII physical-device enumeration does not shrink its vector to the second query's returned count.** If availability decreases between the two calls, it can return stale/default handles. Conditional on physical-device list changes during enumeration; source-only.
**[OD11422](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11422) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII `QueryPool::getResult<DataType>()` accepts a multi-query count with one-record storage.** Conditional on `queryCount > 1`; an implementation that writes all requested records can exceed the local result object; source-only.
**[OD11423](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11423) — Vulkan-Hpp RAII display-plane enumeration wraps the full first-query allocation after the second query reports fewer displays.** Conditional on the supported-display list shrinking between calls; source-only.
**[OD3172](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3172) — USB Audio registers a mode with no usable AHI sample rates.** Discrete rates can all exceed 64 kHz, or a continuous range can contain no listed common rate; the AHI requester and `AHIDB_MaxMixFreq` attribute path then query index -1 and get a bogus zero-frequency result; source-only.
**[OD11425](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11425) — USB Audio reads variable descriptor fields without checking `bLength`.** Conditional on a successful configuration transfer with a short class-specific descriptor; source-only.

**[OD11427](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11427) — Efika ATA architecture target calls an undefined IRQ helper.** The optional target has no checked-in `ata_HandleIRQ()` declaration or definition; its default boot-package edge is disabled. Source-inferred; no build was run.

**[OD11426](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11426) — RAII pipeline-binary creation drops handles on `VK_INCOMPLETE`.** Conditional on the driver writing one or more handles before returning incomplete; source-only.

**[OD3230](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3230) — USB Audio assigns unit numbers and mutates its shared unit list without cross-CPU synchronization.** Concurrent ExecSMP hub workers can claim the same unit number; overlapping AHI mode IDs can replace or remove another device's entries. Optional USB Audio target only; source-only.

**[OD4314](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4314) — VideoCore GPU free-memory queries include the 16-KiB hardware cursor allocation.** The optional BCM283x VideoCore HIDD leaves the cursor buffer counted as available; downstream sizing effects depend on callers. Source-only.

**[OD4317](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4317) — VideoCore HIDD initialization failure does not release acquired cursor, DMA, and IRQ resources.** Conditional on successful resource acquisition followed by an initialization failure; source-only.

**[OD11428](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11428) — Amiga keyboard HIDD passes a failed timer-request allocation to `OpenDevice()`.** The selected Exec implementation dereferences the null request before the driver's intended failure handling; conditional on memory pressure; source-only.

**[OD11429](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11429) — Enhanced and RAII Vulkan image acquisition returns an uninitialized index on timeout/not-ready.** Covers both acquire commands; source-only.

**[OD11430](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11430) — Vulkan out-of-date handling reads undefined counter/timing outputs.** Enhanced and RAII APIs; conditional on downstream clients defining `VULKAN_HPP_HANDLE_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_AS_SUCCESS`; source-only.


**[EK10904](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10904) — NewCLI does not refresh `pr_WindowPtr` after an AUTO console opens its window.** Conditional on an interactive AUTO console and a later requester; source-only.

**EK10905 withdrawn:** `LVF_IGNORE` is a local-variable node flag, not a separate global variable type; masking it out when `GVF_GLOBAL_ONLY` bypasses local lookup does not violate the API contract. See the [withdrawal review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek10905-withdrawal-review).

**[EK10906](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10906) — DOS `DateToStr(FORMAT_DEF)` ignores the current locale's date format.** Affects callers requesting `FORMAT_DEF` under a non-DOS locale; source-only.

**[EK10907](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10907) — Buffered DOS reads omit `IoErr()` when their first buffer allocation fails.** Conditional on allocation failure during a first buffered read; source-only.

**[EK10908](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10908) — NIX startup leaks the temporary default `PATH` buffer across repeated Shell commands.** The Shell runs loaded commands through `RunCommand()`; conditional on a `nix=yes` program, absent `PATH`, and configured CLI path entries. Source-only.

**[EK10909](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10909) — NIX startup ignores failures while constructing or storing the default `PATH`.** Conditional on allocation/storage failure followed by PATH-based execution; source-only.
**[EK10910](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10910) — `RXLIB` dereferences its Rexx message after initialization failure.** Conditional on the optional utility being explicitly built and the Rexx port or message allocation being unavailable; `main()` ignores `init()` failure, and message allocation failure also leaves its reply port uncleaned. Source-only.

**[EK10903](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10903) — Timestamped x86-64 `KrnBug()` can return a would-have-written count after truncating its debug buffer.** Conditional on `DEBUG_TIMESTAMP` and a message larger than the remaining 1,024-byte boot buffer; source-only.

**[OD11432](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11432) — Vulkan create-info equality forms end pointers from null empty arrays.** Conditional on downstream clients comparing empty create infos; source-only.
**[OD11433](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11433) — Vulkan-Hpp setters can leave mutually exclusive array representations active.** Conditional on downstream enhanced-mode micromap or descriptor updates; source-only.
**[OD11434](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11434) — Vulkan-Hpp fixed-size string comparisons can read past unterminated arrays.** Conditional on downstream comparisons of non-terminated `ArrayWrapper1D<char, N>` values; source-only.
**[OD11435](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11435) — Vulkan-Hpp comparisons trust counts for fixed-capacity arrays and compare heap padding.** Conditional on invalid wrapper counts or padding-sensitive memory-property equality; source-only.
**[OD11436](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11436) — Vulkan-Hpp present-info setters can desynchronize swapchain arrays.** Conditional on downstream enhanced-mode setters followed by present submission; source-only.
**[OD11437](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11437) — Vulkan-Hpp subpass setters can desynchronize color and resolve attachments.** Conditional on downstream enhanced-mode setters and render-pass creation; source-only.
**[OD11438](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11438) — Vulkan-Hpp platform handle constructors default to an incompatible FD type.** Conditional on platform-specific external-handle wrappers constructed without an explicit handle type; source-only.
**[OD11439](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11439) — Vulkan-Hpp enhanced array setters overwrite shared counts independently.** Conditional on enhanced setters being used with mismatched coupled array lengths; source-only.

**[OD11441](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11441) — Vulkan-Hpp empty array proxies form end pointers from null.** Conditional on a downstream client requesting `end()` from a default or null proxy; source-only.

**[OD888](AROS-other-drivers.md#od888-hosted-parallel-hidd-double-removes-failed-unixio-registration) — Hosted parallel HIDD repeats UnixIO cleanup after interrupt registration fails.** On non-Darwin hosted Unix, an `AddInterrupt()` fcntl failure removes the node and returns an error; constructor unwind closes the descriptor, then disposal removes and closes it again. Collateral impact requires concurrent UnixIO-list or descriptor reuse. Source-only; no failure or interleaving was induced.

**[OD11431](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11431) — ARM tensor stride setters can desynchronize the shared dimension count [conditional].** In enhanced Vulkan-Hpp, `setDimensions()` and `setStrides()` independently overwrite the count used for both arrays; mismatched lengths can make a downstream `VK_ARM_tensors` consumer overread one array or ignore entries. No in-tree caller or extension enablement was found. Source-only.

Related but distinct from EK10761, which covers stdc's fallback when the resource is unavailable. Source-only.

**[OD2142](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2142) — Envy24/Envy24HT AHI failed initialization expunges through a missing per-card array.** A matching PCI device followed by pointer-array allocation failure reaches cleanup that indexes the absent array; Envy24 also leaves its temporary discovery nodes allocated. Conditional on non-x86-64 native AHI `HAVE_ASMIO` builds and low memory. Source-only.
**[OD2491](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2491) — Envy24 AHI initialization dereferences unchecked vendor-table and matched-device-node allocations.** Conditional on allocation failure in the non-x86-64 native AHI build. Source-only.
**[OD2492](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2492) — Envy24 AHI driver does not free its vendor table during cleanup.** Allocated tables remain after no-card, later-failure, and normal expunge paths; conditional on `HAVE_ASMIO` selecting Envy24. Source-only.
**[OD2493](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2493) — CMI8738 AHI initialization dereferences unchecked vendor-table and matched-device-node allocations.** Conditional on allocation failure in the AHI `HAVE_ASMIO` build. Source-only.
**[OD2494](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2494) — CMI8738 AHI failed initialization expunges through a missing per-card array.** A matched device followed by pointer-array allocation failure reaches cleanup that indexes the absent array and leaves discovery nodes allocated. Conditional on `HAVE_ASMIO` and low memory. Source-only.
**[OD2495](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2495) — CMI8738 AHI driver does not free its vendor table during cleanup.** Allocated tables remain after no-card, later-failure, and normal expunge paths; conditional on `HAVE_ASMIO` selecting CMI8738. Source-only.

**OD3777 — EMU10kx card initialization failure leaves NULL slots or a missing card array for cleanup:** unchecked per-card setup results reach cleanup dereferences; failed setup can also retain a registered handler. Applies to selected EMU10kx AHI builds under the described failure conditions. See [OD3777](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3777) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.

**OD3778 — EMU10kx cleanup can leave later card interrupts registered:** the AROS wrapper uses one registration flag for every card, so freeing the first card disables removal of subsequent handlers before their card data is freed. Requires multiple matching cards. See [OD3778](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3778) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.

**OD4019 — EMU10kx AROS PCI enumeration can loop forever with two matching cards:** its finder alternates between two matches while `DriverInit()` counts with an unbounded loop. Applies to the AROS PCI wrapper when duplicate supported IDs are present. See [OD4019](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4019) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.

**OD4172 — EMU10kx AmigaOS4 PCI wrapper returns only the first matching card:** subsequent finder calls return NULL, so additional same-model cards are not counted or initialized. See [OD4172](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4172) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only.

**OD11227 — Native emergency console can dereference failed path or lock allocations:** unchecked temporary-path and `FileLock` allocations can fault while the optional emergency console handles DOS packets under memory pressure. See [OD11227](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11227). Source-only.

**OD1409 — OpenSBI PCIDT retains its MSI target page when virtual IRQ allocation fails:** bridge setup has already allocated/programmed the target page and enabled MSI, then loses the page when no IRQ range is available. See [OD1409](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1409). Conditional on the described FDT bridge and IRQ-allocation state. Source-only.

**OD1411 — OpenSBI PCIDT can advertise MSI after kernel controller registration fails:** failed `KrnModifyIRQA()` is ignored, leaving the bridge ready even though no controller entry services its interrupts. See [OD1411](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1411). Conditional on more distinct MSI bridges than the controller table supports. Source-only.

**OD1412 — OpenSBI PCIDT can assign the same MSI vector to concurrent clients:** allocation checks and marks the shared bridge bitmap without bridge-wide serialization. The reviewed selected xHCI and NVMe callers are serialized; the trigger remains conditional on other preemptible direct callers. See [OD1412](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1412). Source-only.


**[OD9851](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9851) — PCI ATA registers its IRQ before `HIDD_ATABus_Start()` installs the callback; a qualifying interrupt in that startup interval calls through the initially NULL function pointer. Selected i386-PC, x86-64-PC and Sam440 module targets; source timing is conditional. Source-only.**

**OD9870 — SM502 truecolor `SetColors()` updates its software colormap before returning `FALSE` for ranges beyond index zero.** In-tree callers ignore the status; external or future callers can observe a false failure. See [OD9870](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9870) and the [coverage trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sm502-truecolor-setcolors-returncaller-pass-od9870-added-2026-10-26). Source-only.

**OD3115 — Network-device Open can retain a unit freed by concurrent final Close:** the lookup and opener-count update race with final deletion in Prism2, Etherlink III, Realtek8180 and Rhine. Conditional on ExecSMP with LDDemon active; same-name Open/Open races are excluded. See [OD3115](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3115) and the [lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#lddemon-same-name-open-serialization-correction-od3115-narrowed-2026-10-31). Source-only.

**OD3972 — PCI network reset callbacks can outlive their unit:** callback removal does not wait for an in-flight callback before final Close frees its unit and hardware context. Conditional on ExecSMP with an explicitly built affected PCI driver. See [OD3972](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3972) and the [six-driver trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pci-network-reset-callback-in-flight-owner-race-cross-driver-comparison-od3972-expanded-2026-10-18). Source-only.
**[OD9567](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9567) — Nouveau PCI disable leaves bus mastering enabled.** Conditional on the optional Nouveau HIDD reaching probe rollback or removal after enabling bus mastering; source-only.

**[GD14898](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14898) — MUI gradient parsing narrows accepted angles to 16 bits.** Conditional on a caller supplying an out-of-range numeric angle; source-only.

**[GD14899](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14899) — Tall MUI gradients overflow signed intersection arithmetic.** Conditional on CyberGraphX truecolor rendering a custom-angle gradient at least 3,000 pixels high; source-only.

**[OD2515](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2515) — Unix timer options can produce a zero or unusable host timer interval.** Conditional on invalid frequency boot options or a valid positive high-rate pair; Linux high-rate case can leave SIGALRM timekeeping disarmed despite successful initialization. Source-only.


**[GD2346](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd2346) — Graphics initialization can leak its separately allocated ROM font after a later init failure.** Conditional on failure after ROM-font creation; the font allocation outlives the failed library base. Source-only.

**[GD4868](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4868) — Picture's IFF writer reports success after failed seeks or short writes.** The writer ignores helper failures and returns success; MultiView relies on that result when saving. Source-only.

**[GD10114](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10114) — SDL HIDD reports success when SDL could not apply a palette update.** Conditional on explicit indexed SDL bitmap use and an SDL palette update failure; no maintained indexed caller was found. Source-only.


**[OD11450](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11450) — Virtual Bluetooth L2CAP signaling handlers read fixed parameters without validating command lengths.** Conditional on malformed inbound ACL signaling to an explicitly built optional `vbthci.device`; short commands can be parsed from following bytes and final maximum-size commands read past the receive array. Source-only.


**[OD11451](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11451) — Virtual Bluetooth local CIDs can collide after the 8-bit allocator wraps.** Conditional on more than 256 channel allocations on one live link while an older channel remains open; later CID-based operations can hit the wrong channel. The virtual device is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.
**[OD11459](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11459) — Virtual Bluetooth emits reserved signaling identifier zero.** Conditional on the 128th accepted channel allocation on a live link; configure signaling uses identifier 0x00, which L2CAP reserves. The virtual device is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.
**[OD11460](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11460) — Virtual Bluetooth drops asynchronous completions when timed-event allocation fails.** Under memory pressure, inquiry can remain active or a connection can occupy a link slot without completing. The virtual device is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.




**[OD11453](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11453) — Virtual Bluetooth returns a fixed HID SDP record for every classic fake device.** Conditional on service enumeration of the virtual phone or searches for non-HID UUIDs; record class/PSM conflicts with the phone's advertised service UUID. The virtual device is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.

**[OD11454](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11454) — Virtual Bluetooth miscorrelates Configure Responses and treats them as success.** It compares the peer Source CID against the host CID, then falls back to the first configuring channel; overlapping transactions can advance the wrong channel, and non-success results are also accepted. The virtual device is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.

**[OD11455](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11455) — Nouveau MXMS iteration reads descriptor fields past declared record extents; the selected NV50 callback also loads 8 bytes from v2 output records declared as 6 bytes.** Conditional on inconsistent record extents or v2 DCB sanitization; source-only.

**[OD11456](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11456) — Nouveau ACPI/WMI MXMS validation checks the declared length without the returned buffer size.** Conditional on an undersized or inconsistent firmware response; distinct from the ROM probe issue OD11259. Source-only.

**[OD11457](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11457) — Nouveau voltage-map entries are decoded past their declared record stride.** Conditional on inconsistent BIOS entry lengths; decoded coefficients can reach the hardware voltage-setting path. Source-only.

**[OD11458](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11458) — GK104-family RAM cleanup traverses an uninitialized list after constructor failure.** Conditional on early RAM-constructor failure; teardown can fault instead of cleaning up. Source-only.


**[GD14900](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14900) — OpenWindow cleanup dereferences a failed BorderRPort allocation.** If a non-GZZ window layer is created but the subsequent BorderRPort allocation fails, cleanup passes NULL to `DeinitRastPort()`, which dereferences it. Conditional on memory pressure during window creation; source-only.


**[OD11461](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11461) — FDisk consumes an uninitialized FileInfoBlock after `ExamineFH()` fails.** The failed examine can corrupt reported geometry and write-protection state at startup or media reload. Conditional on an `ACTION_EXAMINE_FH` failure; source-only.


**[OD11462](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11462) — FDisk loops forever when a backing DOS write makes no progress.** AFS returns zero bytes with an error when its write-validity check fails; FDisk treats zero as progress and blocks that unit’s worker. Conditional on an AFS-backed image and a canceled write-protection/error path; source-only.

**[OD11463](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11463) — FDisk and hostdisk report success when media insertion fails.** Both ignore a backing-image reopen failure during `TD_EJECT` load and complete the request successfully, leaving media absent. Conditional on the configured image failing to reopen; source-only.
**[OD11464](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11464) — FDisk leaves `io_Error` stale for `TD_GETDRIVETYPE`.** The command writes `io_Actual` but leaves the previous request error untouched, which `DoIO()` returns. Conditional on reusing a request with nonzero `io_Error`; source-only.
**[OD11465](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11465) — hostdisk can report successful Open after worker message-port creation fails.** The parent publishes a unit with no request port or servicing task; later I/O or Close can fault or hang. Conditional on per-unit port allocation/signal failure; source-only.
**[OD11466](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11466) — MinGW hostdisk resident automount never discovers drives.** Its selected geometry-probe stub returns failure for every scanned `PhysicalDriveN`, so the shared automount hook creates no DOS nodes. Conditional on resident MinGW hostdisk initialization; source-only.
**[OD11470](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11470) — Virtual Bluetooth can dispatch continuation bytes after fragment overflow.** Overflow clears the buffered length but retains the expected PDU size; later orphan continuation data may be parsed as a new L2CAP PDU. Conditional on malformed raw ACL submissions to the virtual device, which is selected by the active Bluetooth aggregate on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64; source-only.
**[OD2362](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2362) — AHCI and VirtIO report successful `AbortIO` without cancelling the request.** The requests remain active and later complete normally; caller impact is conditional on a client relying on cancellation. Source-only.
**[EK699](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek699) — Console completion retains a writer task pointer after that task exits.** A later Tab/Shift-Tab completion can dereference the reclaimed task and its current-directory field; conditional on shared console handles and no intervening write refresh. Source-only.


**[GD14901](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14901) — ReAction Label can dereference a missing RastPort font after its fallback fails.** If a text-bearing label is drawn with a fontless RastPort and no default public screen can be locked, `SetSoftStyle()` dereferences `rp->Font`. Conditional on the optional label image's direct draw path; source-only.

**[GD14902](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14902) — FTManager publishes an incomplete grayscale preview after required allocation failures.** Failure of the pixel array or destination bitmap publishes a blank preview; failure of the row-work bitmap skips the glyph write into an uncleared destination. Conditional on grayscale preview and memory pressure; source-only.
**[GD14903](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14903) — FTManager publishes a blank monochrome preview after raster allocation failure.** The failed plane allocation is still passed to MUI, and the GUI replaces the previous preview with the empty bitmap object. Conditional on monochrome preview and raster allocation failure; source-only.
**[GD14904](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14904) — FTManager overflows its preview bounds when no character has a glyph map.** When every character lookup fails, sentinel extrema are subtracted as signed `int` values before the preview allocation checks. Conditional on a font/string pair with no drawable glyphs; downstream behavior after overflow is compiler-dependent. Source-only.
**[GD14905](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14905) — FreeType2 glyph retrieval dereferences a failed `GlyphMap` allocation.** If the per-glyph allocation fails for a mapped character, `GetGlyph()` still reads `ge->GMap->glm_Width`; FTManager is a confirmed caller. Conditional on memory allocation failure; source-only.
**[GD14906](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14906) — Planar image transfers misindex after an absent plane.** Generic planar and m68k AmigaVideo read/write loops skip NULL or constant planes without advancing the plane-array pointer; sparse `PlanePick` images can render incorrectly, and writes to sparse destinations can omit later-plane data. Conditional on sparse planes and applicable paths; source-only.

**[OD11468](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11468) — Nouveau NV50/G84 clock calculation leaks its HWSQ allocation on PLL errors.** A failed PLL calculation returns before the shared caller's success-only cleanup; later attempts overwrite the leaked buffer pointer. Conditional on a PLL parse/reference or target-calculation failure after script initialization; source-only.

**[GD14907](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14907) — Toggle-select buttons return an uninitialized gadget-up code.** With both toggle-select and release verification, ButtonGClass returns `GMR_VERIFY` without setting `gpi_Termination`; Intuition copies the uninitialized value to `IDCMP_GADGETUP.Code`. Source-only.

**[GD14908](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14908) — Custom gadget removal can race with post-dispatch input handling.** `GadgetLock` is released after the custom method but before Intuition processes its result; a concurrent `RemoveGList()` can unlink the gadget, leaving post-processing with a stale pointer or publishing an inactive gadget. Conditional on task interleaving; source-only.



**[EK8787](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8787) — Task notification callbacks deadlock if they change the hook registry.** Notification holds the hook list shared across callbacks; Add/Remove takes it exclusive, so a callback that mutates registration waits on its own shared hold. Conditional on an external or indirect callback; no selected in-tree mutating callback was found. Source-only.

**[EK10912](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10912) — `StartNotify()` scans beyond a relative filename when the process has no current directory.** The relative-name path gets a null lock from `GetDeviceProc()`, then the root-name logic scans until `:` without checking for NUL. The optional DOS notify test accepts a command-line filename but does not establish a null current directory; trigger remains conditional on that Process state. Source-only.



**[OD9566](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9566) — Nouveau NV04 nForce clock/arbitration paths dereference a NULL PCI bridge lookup.** The selected compatibility stub always returns NULL, and the config-read helper dereferences it. Scoped to affected nForce/nForce2 NV04 paths; the separate NV1A caller checks NULL. Source-only; no GPU or PCI access was exercised.

**[OD10284](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10284) — NV50/G94 Nouveau RAM programming discards HWSQ executor errors.** `nv50_ram_prog()` returns success regardless of `ram_exec()` status, so a failed memory-programming sequence is reported as completed. Conditional on HWSQ execution failure; source-only.

**[OD4135](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4135) — PPP submits a stack-local encoded packet to asynchronous serial I/O.** `SendBYTES()` returns after `SendIO()` while the serial request still points into `send_IP_packet()`'s local buffer. A deferred/partial write can outlive that buffer. Scoped to selected PPP plus serial-device paths; source-only.

**[OD4256](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4256) — PPP timer-open rollback aborts an unopened request.** `OpenTimer()` calls `CloseTimer()` after `OpenDevice()` failure, and cleanup unconditionally calls `AbortIO()` on the request whose device pointer was cleared. Conditional on timer.device open failure; source-only.

**[GD14909](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14909) — Vulkan-Hpp scalar property and ray-tracing helpers pass one-result storage for array counts.** Enhanced helpers forward multiple input structures/groups but provide and return storage for one result; optional-client misuse can issue invalid undersized-output calls. No in-tree callers found; source-only.

GD10227's batch unique-handle ownership-transfer finding also covers both `Device::createPipelineBinariesKHRUnique()` overloads (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:28687-28790`); optional pipeline-binary API, allocation-failure conditional, source-only.

**[GD14910](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14910) — Vulkan loader reads the output-only instance-version pointer.** `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion()` reads the caller's output value before dispatch when the HIDD object exists; a normal uninitialized output variable therefore triggers undefined behavior. Source-only.
**[GD14911](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14911) — Info dereferences a failed fallback `.info` path allocation.** If the original Workbench file match fails and allocating the appended `.info` path also fails, `sprintf()` writes through NULL. Selected Info target; source-only.

**[OD11469](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11469) — DiskImage XAD/XPK leak the reopened output handle when nested discovery rejects a successfully extracted zero-byte image. Conditional on decoder support for an empty output; optional explicit plugin targets only. Source-only.

HEIC Workbench target-selection correction (GD6304-GD6310; 2026-11-06; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked `workbench/classes/datatypes/mmakefile` and the complete aggregate chain. The active `workbench-datatypes-complete : workbench-datatypes-heic` edge selects HEIC; `workbench-complete` selects `workbench-datatypes-complete`, and the `AROS` target selects `workbench-complete` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:9-13`; `config/mmakefile.src:16-17`). Corrected the seven HEIC finding scopes and earlier ledger wording that called HEIC omitted/optional because of a commented parent edge. This establishes selection through the Workbench aggregate; external codec source fetch/build behavior, generated outputs and runtime decoding remain unverified. No dependency was fetched or built.

More Workbench target-selection correction (2026-11-06): active `#MM-` rules select More through `workbench-utilities`, `workbench-complete`, and `AROS`. Updated GD14799–GD14803, GD14863–GD14867 and GD14887 scopes and index labels; a specific generated image/runtime path was not verified. See the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

USB class aggregate/package selection correction (OD USB class scope; 2026-11-06; build-graph only, no source-body/path/LOC credit): traced `kernel-package-usb` through active `kernel-usb` and `kernel-usb-classes` rules. The shared class aggregate selects bootkeyboard, bootmouse, HID, mass-storage and common classes; x86-64 PC's USB package class list includes bootkeyboard, bootmouse, HID and mass-storage (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:10-14`; `rom/usb/mmakefile.src:7-22,52-62`). OpenSBI's BSP class list also includes bootkeyboard, bootmouse and HID (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:86-95,106-107`). Corrected bootkeyboard, bootmouse, HID and printer manifest rows that called active aggregate rules commented. Printer and USB Audio are selected by the common build aggregate but are absent from the checked x86-64 package class list; build selection is therefore distinguished from package/runtime inclusion. No build or image was produced.
**[GD14916](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14916) — LogView installs a failed pattern parse as its active filter [malformed pattern; x86-64 PC Workbench target].**
**[GD14917](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14917) — VMM stores and compares task patterns after parse failure [malformed pattern; optional target].**
**[GD14918](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14918) — ReqTools Select All matches an unvalidated pattern buffer [malformed user pattern; optional target].**
**[GD14919](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14919) — RequestFile frees ReadArgs-owned pattern strings as Vec allocations after parse failure.** Malformed pattern or pattern-buffer allocation failure leaves raw tag data for cleanup after `FreeArgs()`; conditional invalid free in the selected `workbench-c` target. Source-only.
**[GD14920](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14920) — Info reads before empty patterns and overruns its local buffer while normalizing long device patterns.** `DEVICES=""` passes parser validation then reads one byte before the pattern; a valid 31-character pattern writes its final NUL one byte past the 32-byte buffer during DOS-list filtering. Selected Workbench command; source-only.
**[GD6257](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6257) — Decoration publishes a failed screen-title pattern as the global decorator.** Parsed-pattern allocation or parsing failure leaves the global flag set; selected through the active Decoration dependency of `workbench-c`. Source-only.
**[EK641](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek641) — HPET enumeration omits the last comparator in every block.** The selected kernel registration uses unit zero; this limits resource visibility and does not establish a kernel timing failure. Source-only.
**[EK642](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek642) — HPET reports a fixed 10 MHz rate instead of the hardware rate [external caller conditional].** No in-tree `GetCSAttrsA()` caller found; source-only.
**[EK643](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek643) — HPET advertises periodic mode for every comparator [external caller conditional].** Per-comparator periodic capability is optional; no in-tree `GetCSAttrsA()` caller found. Source-only.
**[EK760](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek760) — HPET name attributes write one byte of a string pointer [external caller conditional].**
- **OD11473 — Vulkan-Hpp external-compute-queue data helper can undersize its output object:** `getData<DataType>()` provides one object without enforcing the device's required external data size. See [OD11473](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11473) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-external-compute-queue-data-size-od11473).
- **GD14921 withdrawn — duplicate of GD10257:** the same constructor/setter output-array mismatch is consolidated under [GD10257](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10257); the 2026-11-07 reconciliation is recorded in the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-swapchain-time-domain-output-pair-gd14921).
**[GD14922](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14922) — H.264 decode `setMaxStdPPSCount()` changes the SPS maximum instead of the PPS maximum.** Optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API; incorrect limits reach native video-session-parameter creation. No in-tree C++ caller found; source-only.
**[GD14923](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14923) — H.265 encode enhanced session-parameter constructor initializes the PPS pointer from the SPS proxy.** The incompatible record-pointer types should make enhanced-mode consumers fail to compile; optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API, source-only.
**[GD14924](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14924) withdrawn:** duplicate of canonical GD10223; the Vulkan-Hpp count/size instances checked in this pass are consolidated under GD10223.

**[OD2364](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2364) — VirtIO bus startup writes through a missing unit array after allocation failure.** A supported device can reach the bus start path; if allocating the unit array fails, unit publication dereferences NULL. Applies to selected i386 PC, x86-64 PC, and OpenSBI RISC-V VirtIO builds; source-only.

**[OD2390](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2390) — VirtIO accepts requests crossing the unit end.** A request whose start is valid but whose length extends beyond capacity is submitted without a full-range check; trigger requires a crossing request. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2391](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2391) — VirtIO publishes the available index without a hardware write barrier.** On selected OpenSBI RISC-V builds, the empty compiler barrier does not order descriptor/ring stores before the device-visible index update. Source-only; no device interleaving was run.

**[OD2392](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2392) — VirtIO discards block configuration-change notifications.** Capacity and geometry remain at their startup snapshot if the device later changes configuration; conditional on a configuration-change interrupt. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2393](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2393) — VirtIO dereferences PCI BAR addresses without mapping them for the CPU.** BARs in a selected backend's remapped window can produce an inaccessible register pointer. Conditional on x86-64 PC BARs above the identity range or OpenSBI RISC-V remapped-window BARs; source-only.

**[OD2446](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2446) — VirtIO ignores the negotiated per-segment `SIZE_MAX` limit.** A request larger than the device's limit is sent as one data descriptor; conditional on a smaller negotiated limit and oversized caller request. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2460](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2460) — VirtIO reports a read-only unit as writable.** `TD_PROTSTATUS` ignores the negotiated read-only flag, so filesystem callers may attempt writes that the device then rejects. Conditional on a read-only device; selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2604](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2604) — VirtIO and NVMe reinsert an already-linked change request.** SFS/NTFS reuse and free the request after removal, leaving stale unit-list links; later I/O can touch freed request links. Conditional on filesystem cleanup followed by unit reuse; source-only.

**[OD2704](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2704) — VirtIO reports the requested length after a short successful read.** It ignores the used length and marks all requested bytes valid; conditional on a successful short completion. Selected modern VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2805](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2805) — VirtIO miscalculates exported capacity for some negotiated block sizes.** When `blk_size / 512` is not a power of two, capacity division and the exported power-of-two block size disagree, hiding part of the device. Conditional on that device configuration; selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2842](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2842) — VirtIO reset polling reports success after its unsigned countdown wraps.** A nonzero device status at the polling limit wraps the counter and is accepted as reset success; conditional on a slow/stuck reset. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2589](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2589) — VirtIO reads block configuration without generation validation.** A config change during the multi-field startup read can produce a mixed capacity/block-size/geometry snapshot; conditional on a concurrent device update. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD3500](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3500) — VirtIO does not validate PCI capability offsets against BAR bounds.** Malformed capability/notify ranges can produce out-of-region MMIO pointers. Conditional on invalid device configuration; no conforming-device defect is claimed.

**[OD3205](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3205) — VirtIO reads used-ring entries without an acquire barrier.** On selected OpenSBI RISC-V builds, the CPU may observe the used index before the device-written completion element and status; no interleaving was run.

**[OD2396](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2396) — VirtIO truncates unaligned byte offsets to sectors.** An offset not divisible by 512 is rounded down when forming the device sector; impact requires a caller to submit an unaligned request. Selected VirtIO block builds; source-only.

**[OD2370](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2370) — VirtIO dereferences a failed storage-ID allocation.** After unit creation, a NULL result from `HIDD_Storage_AllocateID()` is used to read `ln_Name`; conditional on allocation failure during selected VirtIO bus startup. Source-only.

**[OD3012](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3012) — VirtIO failed bus startup leaves its worker or interrupt registration active.** Later startup failures do not stop the worker or remove an installed IRQ; a stale callback is conditional on subsequent controller teardown. Selected VirtIO builds; source-only.

**[OD11474](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11474) — econsole `AROS.boot` repeats the signature on every read packet.** Chunked/repeated readers do not advance; the in-tree bootability check reads the whole file once and is unaffected. Optional `kernel-econsole`; source-only.


**[GD14925](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14925) — Wanderer leaks prepared objects when IconWindow construction fails.** If the window's instance-pool allocation fails after construction resources are prepared, the NULL-window path leaks the menu strip, root-object tree, and optional backfill hook. Selected through the full Workbench aggregate and active MetaMake edge; source-only.
**[GD14926](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14926) — Wanderer leaks DiskObjects loaded during drawer settings operations.** Successful icon loads in both non-root window construction and snapshot settings saves are never freed or retained; repeated opens and snapshots leak the icon and layout allocations. Selected through the full Workbench aggregate; source-only.
**[GD14927](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14927) — Wanderer silently constructs windows without their IconList.** If IconList construction fails but the parent view/window succeeds, Wanderer opens an empty drawer/window instead of propagating the failure. Selected through the full Workbench aggregate; source-only.

**[GD14928](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd14928) — MiamiPanel can dereference a NULL interface message port during startup if `CreateMsgPort()` fails.** Conditional on allocation failure while app/window construction proceeds; limited to the explicitly buildable optional MiamiPanel module, not claimed in the default AROSTCP aggregate. Source-only.

**[OD11476](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11476) — USB HID and Bluetooth HID can divide by zero when a variable item's logical range has equal endpoints and its configured action scales or normalizes an analog-joystick value.** Conditional on the descriptor and action; USB HID is selected in x86-64 PC and OpenSBI USB package routes. Bluetooth HID is in the active Bluetooth class aggregate. Source-only.

**[OD11477](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11477) — USB HID configuration can free action nodes while its input worker traverses them on ExecSMP.** Conditional on concurrent report processing and GUI mutation; USB HID appears in the x86-64 PC and OpenSBI package class lists. Source-only.


**[OD3724](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3724) — Virtual Bluetooth pending-read and unit-port queue operations lack cross-CPU synchronization on ExecSMP.** A direct `AbortIO()` can overlap the unit task's queue operations; conditional on an external abort caller and concurrent scheduling. `vbthci.device` is selected on x86-64 PC and OpenSBI RISC-V64. Source-only.

**[OD11478](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11478) — Virtual Bluetooth acknowledges LE connection cancellation but later reports the pending connection as successful.** The selected host expects cancellation status `0x02`; conditional on cancelling a matching fake LE connection before its timer fires. Selected x86-64 PC/OpenSBI RISC-V64 Bluetooth aggregate. Source-only.
